The project applies the Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) approach and uses VCS standards and methodologies to a REDD voluntary carbon market. The project's geographical boundary comprises a parcel land named Matá-Matá (500,996 hectares), with 500,996 hectares of primary ancient and undisturbed areas of tropical rainforest. Thus, the project area comprises 476,995 hectares of dense lowland forest, 17,705 hectares of dense alluvial forest and 5,914 hectares of dense sub-montane forest. The parcel land is situated in the municipalities of Manicoré and Novo Aripuanã, southern State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project will generate GHG emission reductions from changes in land use caused by imminent deforestation and forest degradation. The emission of 43,973,073 tons of CO2e will be avoided with the 413 project, considering a lifespan of 30 years, with an annual average of 1,465,769 tons of CO2e calculated for the whole period (2021- 2050) and 34,615,467 for the first 10-year crediting period (2021-2030). The 413 Project seeks to be validated as Golden Level because exceptional climate measures will be undertaken to adapt the population to climate change. The baseline was conceived from the most-likely scenario, which is converting 20% of the forest to pasture for cattle raising. The conversion of forests to alternative land uses of up to 20% of private properties is permitted by the Brazilian Forest Code but the project proponent decided to protect forest and avoid deforestation and forest degradation, reducing CO2 emissions. In the planned deforestation approach, the conversion agent in the baseline is the owner of the area because he has the right to deforest under the current legislation.

vcs-2590: The Rice-Wheat-Maize system in North-West India accounts for a significant portion of the food supply in the country. Depletion of underground water, declining fertility status associated with multiple nutrient deficiencies, increased concentration of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in the atmosphere owing to soil methanogenesis from rice cultivation and burning of rice residues are some of the end results of the intensive system. Thus, there is a challenge to balance the food production and sustainability goals simultaneously. Recent advancements in regenerative agriculture methods improve environmental outcomes without negatively impacting yields. However, agronomic, and socio-economic factors such as access to agro-advisory and the cost of technology adoption remain a crucial barrier to adopting regenerative agriculture practices. By linking smallholder farmers to carbon marketplaces, this project aims to overcome these critical barriers to adoption by enabling additional income opportunities. The project will cover the states Punjab, Haryana, and the adjoining National Capital Region (NCR), and primarily focus on the Rice - Wheat - Maize cropping system, without excluding other crops, with regenerative agricultural practices that are known to reduce GHG emissions and thus generate carbon credits by way of CO2e and SOC. With a cash incentive, the smallholder farmers in the project boundary will adopt these practices more readily and contribute to sustainability and reduce GHG emissions. A voluntary carbon marketplace for carbon credits, for the first time will create income opportunities for smallholder farmers in India via this project.

vcs-2598:
Panguana is the oldest biological research station in Peru (founded in 1968) with a focus on studying the immense biodiversity of the Amazon rainforest. The research station is located on the western edge of the Reserva Comunal El Sira (RC El Sira), a national protected area established to protect the pristine montane rainforests of the Cordillera El Sira. The buffer zone of the RCS and its surrounding area is mainly populated by indigenous communities and small-scale farmers. Intensive deforestation in this area in favour of pastures has resulted in fragments of primary rainforests existing primarily as islands between pastures. In this respect, the private nature reserve of Panguana currently forms a peninsula with an intact connection to the untouched rainforests in the heart of the RC El Sira. Restoration of degraded pastureland and rehabilitation of secondary forests adjacent to existing old growth forests at Panguana presents the opportunity to conserve an important biodiversity corridor as well as an effective strategy for rehabilitation of degraded tropical forest across the region.
The project has the following main goals:
    • Restore natural rainforests on pastures within the area of the Panguana foundation (~140 ha)
    • Accelerate forest restoration by testing different approaches and developing best practices for local conditions
    • Introduce sustainable food and tree production systems (permaculture, aquaponics, tree nursery)
    • Only use inexpensive materials and methods, easily available in the region
    • Exchange knowledge and develop a sustainable landscape management together with local stakeholders (indigenous communities, small-scale farmers, local institutions)

It is expected that the project activities will lead to a mean annual removal of ~16 t CO2e per hectare during the first 20 years.

The major purpose of this grouped project activity is to use CNG Vehicles instead of fossil fuel powered vehicles in India. The usage of CNG powered vehicles instead of fossil fuel powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven. Project vehicles included are those sold directly or through authorized dealers. Only vehicles are counted where such an agreement has been signed. This is group project activity where the CNG vehicles can be added via instances throughout the crediting period. There are 30 CNG vehicles involved in the first instance of the project activity. Transport emissions have increased by almost a quarter since 1990 this means the transition to zero emissions will need to be swift and the importance of radical improvement through
fuel switching is growing. In this context there is an ongoing discussion about the role of methane in transport. Some stakeholders - often representing the fossil gas industry - claim the use of methane would contribute to decarbonizing transport in 2016, T&E published a study by Ricardo Energy & Environment that analyzed the role of methane in transport. The study found using fossil gas has no meaningful climate benefits compared to petroleum based fuels, whilst Biomethane cannot be produced in sufficient volumes to make a meaningful contribution.

In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, İzmir Harmandalı Solid Waste Disposal Site (SWDS) Rehabilitation and Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Utilization Project is being implemented by İzmir Novtek Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş.    

The proposed project activity is a Methane Gas Power Generating Plant and Mechanical Sorting Facility with the installed capacity of “39.690 MWe”. The project is built within the structure of Harmandalı Solid Waste Landfill Facility in İzmir province, as the third-largest SWDS in Turkey, and will be operated as integrated with the currently installed units. 

It is planned to rehabilitate the İzmir Harmandalı SWDS that receives around 4,500 tons of municipal waste coming from 23 different districts of İzmir province daily and to generate renewable electric power by capturing and utilizing landfill gas.

Whilst providing sustainable development benefits to the host communities and the host country, the proposed project activity will reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions mainly by 

•	preventing GHG emissions, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from waste at the Harmandalı SWDS that would be otherwise left to be decomposed;
•	replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid which is heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources, through generating renewable energy and feeding it to the grid.

The project has begun to generate electricity on October 29th, 2019, which is regarded as the project start date. 

This project adopts a fixed crediting period of 10 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 618,042 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 6,180,420 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its first crediting period.

The area of the project activity is 5856 ha, including 698 subcompartments spreading over Dengjia Town, Lijia Town, Litian Town, Lingdi Town, Longjin Town, Linshe Town, Shaqiang Town, Songkou Town, Songxi Town, Tianyuan Town, Wenjiao Town, Yupeng Town, Changxiao Town of Fujian Qingliu Forestry Co., Ltd. The Kuamut Rainforest Conservation Project (‘Kuamut Project’) aims to protect and restore 83,381 ha of tropical forest in Sabah, Malaysia. The project is located in the Tongod and Kinabatangan Districts of Sabah, Malaysia. The project area is part of a long-term approximately 1-million-hectare concession granted to Yayasan Sabah on a 99-year lease arrangement with the Sabah Forestry Department (acting on behalf of the State Government of Sabah). Yayasan Sabah is a State-owned para-governmental charitable foundation that was formed in 1966 with the aim of ‘improving the lives of Malaysians living in Sabah’. 
Prior to the start of the project, the project area was designated as production forest (Class II). The area had been repeatedly logged in the past and was designated for further commercial exploitation. Project additionality is explicitly demonstrated by preventing 84,000 hectares of commercial logging over 30 years. Had the project not intervened, the resulting carbon emissions over this period would have contributed 16 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) into the atmosphere. 
In addition to its contribution to preventing the release of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, the project is protecting an important biodiverse habitat, Despite its ex-logged state, the area is known to support very high populations of elephants, banteng and orangutan, and endangered bird species including Helmeted Hornbill, Bornean Peacock Pheasant and Storms Stork.

The project activity “Unitán Afforestation and reforestation of grazing land project” (hereafter, “Unitán project”) is an afforestation project on extensive cattle grazing pastures area and abandoned agricultural lands using native (Schinopsis balansae) and exotic species (various varieties of Eucalyptus including Eucalyptus gxc) aiming to produce, as a priority product, logs for tannin industry and secondarily, fuelwood. The afforestation with this species will prevent the use of timber from native forests in the future.

Unitán comprises 5 properties located in Chaco and Formosa province, in the NorthEast region of Argentina (the host country), on lightly degraded grassland as a consequence of many decades of extensive cattle grazing and abandoned agriculture land by previous owners. This degradation is expected to continue in the absence of the project. The area of grasslands to be effectively planted and to be included within the Unitán project boundary is then 2,403ha (72.1% of Unitán total area). The unplanted area remaining in part as grassland and native forest remains, become biological corridors used for flora and fauna conservation.

From September 2016 until the time of PDD elaboration, a total area of 939,3 ha of the project was effectively planted. In addition, there is an area of 1,464 ha of planned plantation for the period 2021 to 2025 (mainly in owned and a minor part in leased lands).  In total, the project will have a final scale of about 2,400 ha.

The project utilizes two main species: Schinopsis balansae, a native species, and Eucalyptus (different varieties: mainly gxc and cloeziana), occupying 36%, 64% of the total planted area, and with rotation periods of 40 years, 6 and 20, respectively.

Lingbi County wastewater treatment project is located in Suzhou City, Anhui Province, China. The whole aerobic process includes pre-treatment process,secondary biological treatment process, tertiary deep treatment process and sludge treatment process, with a maximum design influent flow of 120,000 m3/d, the influent and effluent COD concentration are 850 mg/L and 50 mg/L separately.
In the baseline scenario, village sewage and some industrial wastewater from the county would have been treated through a series of deep open anaerobic lagoons. The open lagoons are the best available low-cost solution for wastewater treatment, which is also in compliance with the environmental regulations. In the project scenario, the wastewater will be treated through aerobic biological treatment technology, which includes pre-treatment process, secondary biological treatment process, tertiary deep treatment process and sludge treatment process.
Emission reductions are generated by reducing methane emissions of the open anaerobic lagoons in baseline scenario. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the project activity is 67,302 tCO2e/year,

Jinjia Jiayi CMM Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located in Xiaochong Village, Pan County, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, People’s Republic of China.The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted coal mine methane (CMM) with a low concentration of methane to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. 

Six sets of CMM power generators are installed with a total installed capacity of 3.6 MW (6×0.6 MW). When all six power generators are in full operation, the Project is expected to export 17,280 MWh of electricity and destroy 7.2 million m3 (under normal conditions ) of methane every year. The generated electricity is supplied to the coal mines through the electricity distribution network in the Jinjia coal mine area; part of the electricity produced by the Project may also be exported to CSPG if there is any electricity surplus after the coal mine demand is fully met, thus displacing part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.

The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it reduces methane emissions by capturing and destroying methane which would have been directly vented into the air in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CSPG.

This project description document covers COMACO operations in Muchinga and Central provinces of Zambia. The COMACO Landscape Management Project (CLMP) promotes sustainable agriculture and forest management. The key objectives of the project are to increase smallholder farmer agricultural productivity, provide alternative livelihoods and reduce uncontrolled forest loss and degradation. Hence, the project comprises two components:
1. Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) component – which aims to promote widespread adoption of agricultural practices including conservation agriculture that increase food production per unit area and farmers’ income. The project promotes the adoption by farmers of legume-based alley cropping, residues management (e.g. mulching; cessation of residue burning), and reduced tillage among other SALM practices.
2. REDD+ (Avoided Unplanned Deforestation) component – which aims to reduce forest loss, and protect and expand areas under natural forest, and conserve biodiversity. This is achieved primarily through land use planning and creation of Community Conservation Areas (CCAs), coupled with sustainable non-extractive forest use, e.g. honey and mushrooms.  
The geographical area of the project stretches across sixteen (16) chiefdoms in nine (9) districts in the Central and Muchinga Province of Zambia, namely: Mulilo, Chikwa, Chifunda, Muyombe, Katyetye, Nkula, Chibale, Kabamba, Chitambo, Mukungule, Chikwanda, Mpumba, Kambombo, Lundu, Tembwe and Mubanga. It is a grouped project as defined in the VCS Standard (version 4.0); this project activity instance comprises 19,059 ha of agricultural land for the SALM component, and 131,491 ha for the REDD+ component. The potential project area for the SALM component is estimated to be about 81,500 ha of agricultural land, and for the REDD+ at 300,000 ha of forest.  
Prior to the project, poor farming practices such as residue burning, shifting cultivation and chitemene agricultural system (the cutting and burning of tree branches) led to rapid soil nutrient depletion and the traditional practices of collecting caterpillars (Lepidoptera), a butterfly/moth larva which is a traditional delicacy to the local people and largely consumed in urban areas of Zambia, involved cutting down trees or their branches leading to forest degradation. Uncontrolled and unregulated charcoal burning and cutting down of trees for wood fuel also contributed to deforestation and forest degradation. There was also a general lack of land use planning and forest management, undertaken in a participatory and coordinated manner – which led to destruction and fragmentation of the natural forests. The COMACO Landscape Management Project uses market incentives to promote adoption of SALM practices for forest and wildlife conservation. It uses land use planning with traditional leaders and communities to identify and zone areas for conservation and forest management known as Community Conservation Areas (CCA). A Community Conservation Plan (CCP) is developed and implemented for specific CCAs – including activities for sustainable forest management. These activities will result in increased and sustainable agricultural production, and forest conservation. Greenhouse gases (GHG) emission reductions will be generated through improved carbon storage on farms, and avoidance of mosaic deforestation from unplanned agricultural land conversion. The project activities will be supported by methodologies approved under a VCS approved GHG program to account for the project’s emissions reductions.
The annual average GHG emission reductions of the project are estimated at 147,925 tCO2-e, and total GHG emission reductions over 20 years are estimated at 2,958,500 tCO2-e. This estimate considers only the first 10 years of GHG emission reductions for the REDD+ component.

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Huishui County and Luodian County, Guizhou Province, where located in southwestern China with a total acreage of 19,066 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and emission reduction than the continuously flooded.
The project activity includes cement ditch construction, reservoir construction and necessary training for the farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. Controllable irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 2.80 tCO2e/ha is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 373,660 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 53,380 tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes.
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers.
- Provide more job opportunities, especially female workers.
- Use a proportion of benefits to improve the local children’s education.

Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and less methane emission reduction than the continuously flooded.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir construction and necessary training for the farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. Controllable irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (flooded state) In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 2.79 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 374,178 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 53,454 tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes.
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers.
- Provide more job opportunities, especially female workers.
- Use a proportion of benefits to improve the local children’s education.

Feitian 11 & Dabatian CMM Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located in Zhijin County and Nayong County of Bijie City, Guizhou Province, People’s Republic of China which involves two power plants which utilize low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mines and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus.

The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with a low concentration of methane to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM)  or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. CMM power generators with a total capacity of 6 MW are to be installed for Feitian 11 power plant, and 2 MW for Dabatian power plant, totaling to 8 MW for the Project. It is estimated that the two power plants will destroy a total amount of 17.1 million m3 (under normal conditions ) of methane and export 39,360 MWh of electricity every year, when all power generators are in full operation. The generated electricity is supplied to the coal mines through the electricity distribution network in the coal mine area, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from CSPG; part of the electricity produced by the Project may also be exported to CSPG if there is any electricity surplus after the coal mine demand is fully met, thus displacing part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.

The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it reduces methane emissions by capturing and destroying methane which would have been directly vented into the air in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CSPG.

The “Great British Sustainable Farming Project” (GBSFP) from One Carbon World (OCW) aims to raise farmers' awareness on the benefits of regenerative agriculture and how changes in agricultural practices can help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. In order to achieve this objective, the project activity consists of several regenerative agricultural land management practices to reduce and remove GHG emissions.

The project is developed as a grouped project within the United Kingdom (UK) boundaries. The project activity intends to add more instances over the upcoming years. The expansion of the project activity will depend on the allowance of the project validation and the project activities instances will have to follow the program eligibility criteria for its inclusion. The project implementation results in an increase of soil organic carbon and a reduction of GHG emissions. 

“Regenerative agriculture” refers to farming and grazing practices that aim to reverse climate change by rebuilding soil organic matter, sequestering carbon, improving degraded soil biodiversity, improving water cycle and restoring soil fertility. Regenerative agriculture does not imply only one practice, it is a combination of techniques. The project activity, based on this type of agriculture, consists of a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities that are carried out in the farms, these activities include but are not limited to:
- Reduce fertilizer application
- Improve water management/irrigation
- Reduce tillage/improve residue management
- Improve crop planting and harvesting (e.g. agroforestry)
- Improve grazing practices.

Balıkesir Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Utilization Project is being implemented by Landfill Enerji Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. within the boundaries of Balıkesir Solid Waste Disposal Site (SWDS) in Balıkesir province in Turkey.

The proposed project activity has the installed capacity of “14.14 MWe/h”. 

It is planned to rehabilitate the SWDS that receives around 1,200 tons of municipal waste generated at Balıkesir province per day and to generate renewable electric power by capturing and utilizing landfill gas.

Whilst providing sustainable development benefits to the host communities and the host country, the proposed project activity will reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions mainly by 

•	preventing GHG emissions, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from waste at the Balıkesir SWDS that would be otherwise left to be decomposed;
•	replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid which is heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources, through generating renewable energy and feeding it to the grid.

The project has begun to generate electricity on October 27th, 2019, which is regarded as the project start date. 

This project adopts a fixed crediting period of 10 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 185,502 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,855,020 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout the crediting period.

Three Nicaraguan forestry projects have gone together to get access to carbon credits as a mean to expand the planted areas and strengthen environmental and social components. The carbon project will be managed by Norteak Nicaragua S.A., whose plantations are located in the
departments of Boaco and Matagalpa and have a Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) certification issued
in 2015. Ekoteak S.A. is a Swedish capital company that has worked hand in hand with Norteak Nicaragua
S.A. in the exploitation and mechanized extraction of wood and whose plantations are in the Chinandega
department. Maderas Sostenibles S.A. (MSSA) is a Nicaraguan company formed in 2007 with the purpose
of reforesting pasture lands in the Pacific Region of the country. Currently, MSSA manages a farm owned
by Proyecto de Reforestación Limonapa S.A. in the Chinandega department, which is included as part of
the reforestation grouped project Norteak Nicaragua. Teak - Tectona grandis - is the central component in the first stage of the project, while local species are validated. Project activities are carried out and monitored according to approved project methodology AR-ACM0003
for a project period of 30 years. The project estimates to remove 6,357 tCO2e annually and 190,721 
tCO2e during its entire life. The companies involved in the project have as an objective to achieve a group
carbon certification of its forest plantations recovering 709.2 hectares (ha) from degraded grasslands in

and economic well-being of the local communities who derive livelihoods from the project area, by
providing employment, facilitating the access to the social security benefits, including health care, and

This project facilitates the decarbonisation of housing stock in the United Kingdom. Emission reductions are generated by reductions in fossil fuel and grid-connected electricity consumption in dwellings that are decarbonised compared to baseline consumption. The aggregated emissions from fossil fuel consumption of dwellings in the United Kingdom make up a significant component of greenhouse gas emissions; they also pose a significant opportunity to reduce real emissions.

This project is defined as a grouped project where the project proponent acts as a central administrator towards the objective of expediting the pace of housing decarbonisation. The project targets a range of individual dwellings all located in the United Kingdom. 

The project proponent collects, monitors, and aggregates data necessary to demonstrate additionality, quantify the resulting emission reductions and to originate voluntary carbon credits in conformance with the VM0008 Methodology.  The project proponent is responsible for overseeing validation and registration of the project with the Verra Registry and managing the verification and sale of the resulting emission reduction credits. 

The main project objectives are:

•	To gradually group together individual dwellings located in the United Kingdom inside a cluster, that will achieve together a significant reduction in real emissions during the project crediting period; 

•	To stimulate and reward dwelling owners for their efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions such as insulating, air sealing and improving the central heating system in existing dwellings and facilitating dwelling owners’ access to the internationally recognised voluntary carbon credits market; and

•	To overcome the inherent challenges of aggregating small scale decarbonisation activities, simplify third party auditing and control (monitoring) as well as undertaking centralised data collection activities paramount to the quantification of emission reductions.

For over five years, ecoTrees AG has been developing and managing Paulownia tree plantations located in Romania. The purpose is two-fold, to create an investment of fast-growing timber trees on previously unused land and reduce global CO2 emissions.

This project will sell wood production and carbon offsets.

Currently, ecoTrees AG manages more than 500 hectares of land in different sites around Romania. We have begun afforestation of 100 hectares with Paulownia trees with ecoTrees AG directly owning more than 60 hectares of Paulownia plantations with the continued expansion every year.

Moreover, we are offering our Swiss customers the chance to participate in our business model. We help them to set up a plantation with a complete management program that includes:
- Finding the land
- Planting the trees
- Managing the trees until harvesting
- Harvesting the trees
- Selling the wood for them

At this moment, we are already managing around 40 hectares for Swiss customers.

ecoTrees chose Romania because they promote afforestation efforts where all plantations use lands degraded and neglected agricultural areas. No new growth forests are touched.

The Paulownia tree is also known as the Kiri, Kaiserbaum, Emperor Tree, and Blue Bell. This wood’s properties have proven to be an excellent choice for noble wooden decks on boats, mouldings, skis, instruments, and furniture production.

The Paulownia tree hybrid we use thrives particularly well in the Central and Eastern European climate. The typical planting density is 700 - 750 trees per hectare. The plantations also help hold the soil and offer work for local inhabitants.

The massive size of the leaves helps trap carbon dioxide more than most tree species. One hectare of Paulownia absorbs about 50 tons of CO2 per year. We estimate that 100 hectares of Paulownia can absorb 5,000 tons of CO2 per year

KONYA Energy Biogas Plant is currently one of the largest biogas plants in Turkey with an operational license capacity of 12 MWe/h and became operational April 30th, 2020, with an installed capacity of 6 MWe/h. 

Located in Çumra district, Konya province, it is a biogas-to-energy project generating renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy. 

In its first phase, manure generated by animals at neighboring farms is collected daily through special sewage trucks and fed into the anaerobic digesters. In the baseline scenario, prior to the implementation of the project, manure was left to decay in anaerobic conditions without methane recovery at the farms.

With the project, manure coming to the plant biodegrades in anaerobic conditions. The biogas that is released during the biodegradation of organic wastes is used for electricity and heat production in the biogas unit. 

The proposed project has a total installed capacity of 6,004 KWe/h. The annual feed-in electricity is hence estimated to be 45,015,000 KWh. Whilst heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid. 

The project reduces GHG emissions mainly by preventing them, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from animal manure and replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. It is expected to generate 532,368 tCO2eq/y net emission reductions per annum.

Suzhou Landfill in Anhui Province Gas Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located within Suzhou Landfill at Qianfu Village, Suzhou City, Anhui Province, P. R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Suzhou Smart Energy Environmental Protection Power Co., Ltd.. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Suzhou Landfill and utilize it to generate electricity.
Construction of Suzhou Landfill started in 2005 and was finished in 2007, and the tipping of the waste at the site started in January 2008. The designed capacity of the site is 3.027 million tonnes. The average waste tonnage in 2008 is 405 tonnes/day and it increased by 5% each year, it is expected that the site will be closed for further tipping after reaching the full capacity of the storage 3.027 million tonnes, estimated in year 2022. 
The project involves the installation of a gas collection system and utilization system. The collected gas is utilized in gas engines with capacity of 2.060MW and generates power, and any excess gas is flared initially in an enclosed flare with a capacity of 1000 Nm3/h. 
Landfill gas has been extracted and combusted by flare since 01/01/2010. The construction of the grid connection was completed on 12 October 2012 followed by completion of engine commissioning on 25 December 2012. The project started to export power to the grid on 28 December 2012.
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Suzhou landfill for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid.

The project collects and utilizes LFG from Shenyang Daxin Landfill for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid.

The Inner Mongolia Moerdaoga Improved Forest Management Project  is located in northern part of the western side of Greater Khingan Mountains, Hulun Buir City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, P.R.C. It is implemented by Moerdaoga Forest Industry Co. LTD  to protect the once logging forest. 
The proposed project is implemented in Angelin, Fenglin, Hongqi, Shengli, Taiping, Xinqing, Yuliya and Hekou Forestry Centers, which is affiliated to Moerdaoga Forest Bureau. The project has 69,199.38 ha commercial forest with 21,045, 6,602, 3,862, 8,520, 6,808, 3,311, 8,220 and 10,831 ha in Angelin, Fenglin, Hongqi, Shengli, Taiping, Xinqing, Yuliya and Hekou forest center respective. The forest ages range from sapling, middle age to mature forest. Prior to the implementation of the project, the forest within the project area was designed and planted as commercial forest, and logged annually according to the timber production plan issued by Moerdaoga Forest Bureau. Since the project started in 2016, the commercial harvest has been cancelled and only tending and managing is allowed.
The project is expected to generate approximately 13,005,555 tCO2e during the 30 years’ crediting period, with the annual emission reductions of 433,519 tCO2e.
The project activity will significantly improve the forest management conditions within the project area, and benefit local ecological environment. The implementation of the project will not only achieve a reliable measurable carbon sequestration by reducing commercial timer, but also contribute to sustainable development of the local community.

vcs-2681: Jiaozuo Zhouliu MSW Landfill site LFG Recovery to Power Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in the south area of Zhouliu Village, Xiuwu County, Jiaozuo City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Shanghai BCCY New Power Industry Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Jiaozuo Zhouliu MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Zhouliu landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity. Zhouliu landfill site started operation in November 2008 with a total design capacity of 2,200,000 m3 and a daily municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 550 tons/d. The landfill is envisaged to be filled in by 2018 (closure of the landfill in 2019).  The project has a total designed capacity 2.5MW (5*500kW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The project started construction in January 2011 and started operation on 25-03-2011. The project collects and utilizes LFG from Zhouliu landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore, the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. Scenario existing prior to the start of the implementation of the project activity (the same as baseline scenario): LFG from Zhouliu landfill site is released into the atmosphere; Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the CCPG, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants. The total power generation from year 2011 to 2021 is estimated to be 45,917 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 31,755 tCO2e per year.

Luoyang Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Electricity Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Chanhe District, Luoyang City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Shanghai BCCY New Power Industry Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Luoyang landfill site and utilize it to generate electricity. No flare will be installed in this project activity.
Luoyang landfill site started operation in 2001 with a municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 1,300 tons/d and an operational lifespan of 18 years. The project involves the installation of a gas collection system, transmitting system, pre-treatment system and an electricity generation plant. Three sets of gas engines with the total installed capacity of 1.5MW (3*500kW) were installed. The gas engines combust the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The project started construction in December 2007 and started operation on 01-03-2009. 
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Luoyang landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore, the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid.
The total power generation from year 2009 to 2019 is estimated to be 87,750 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 114,743 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the CCPG.

The project introduces new animal waste management systems to treat the manure from 9 swine farms in Jiangxi Province. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one animal waste management system, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, most of the fertilizer is distributed to local farmers for free and only a small portion will be sold on the domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for electricity generation. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 1989 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. The biogas released during the biodegradation of organic wastes will be collected and used for electricity production. The annual electricity production is estimated to be 52,272MWh. Also, the generated electricity will be only used for daily operation of the AWMS and the 9 swine farms themselves and will not be connected to the region grid net or other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from power generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater.

The project introduces new animal waste management systems to treat the manure from 3 swine farms in Guangdong Province. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one animal waste management system, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then put into the homogenate regulating tank. After further hydrolysis and grit settling, all were put into the anaerobic digestion. The project adopts a fully mixed bag type anaerobic reactor, and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for power generation. After anaerobic fermentation, the fermentation liquid is separated by solid and liquid, and the biogas residue is put into the aerobic composting system used to produce solid organic fertilizer. The biogas slurry is used for agricultural irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 1,027 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. The biogas generated during the anaerobic process will be collected for electricity production. The annual electricity production is estimated to be 28,787MWh. Also, the generated electricity will be only used for daily operation of AWMS and 3 swine farms themselves and will not be connected to the region grid net or other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from power generation are neglected. The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater.

The proposed small-scale grouped project activity has already been registered as CPA 10484-P1-0006-CP1 under registered CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) 10484 titled:” SHINE – Distribution of LED Lightbulbs in India” which involves distribution of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) for domestic lighting in Uttar Pradesh. 
Uttar Pradesh has one of the lowest demand supply availability amongst the Indian States. The peak demand supply gap in 2016 stood at 12.5%. Post October 2016, the state has endeavored to provide 24 hours power to major towns and cities. However, the rural areas receive anywhere between 16 hours to 18 hours of electricity only. SHINE CPA 6 aims to reduce the peak demand requirement by distributing energy efficient LEDs to rural households.

The proposed small-scale grouped project activity has already been registered as CPA 10484-P1-007-CP1 under registered CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) 10484 titled:” SHINE – Distribution of LED Lightbulbs in India” which involves distribution of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) for domestic lighting in southern state of Andhra Pradesh. 
In Andhra Pradesh, peak electricity demand stood at 13436 MW in the year 2018-19. The government is working towards providing 24x7, reliable 3 phase supply to all domestic, commercial & industrial consumers, however this depends on availability of power. The government plans to achieve this by incremental energy procurement, supplemented by energy conservation efforts. Further, domestic lighting has been identified by AP Government as having second highest saving potential per annum after agriculture. With distribution of energy efficient LEDs, SHINE CPA 7 seeks to achieve this goal of reducing the burden on peak hour consumption.

The primary objective of the Juruena River REDD+ Project is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) of the 45,675.15 ha project area, consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest. The project area is located within 18 private properties, which are located in the municipality of Cotriguaçu, in the State of Mato Grosso, Southern Amazon. A Sustainable Forest Management Plan is also carried out in some of the properties.

Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities. The contribution to sustainability is being monitored through the application of the SOCIALCARBON® Standard.

vcs-271: The project activity consists of a renewable energy based power generation facility at Sangli district in the state of Maharashtra in India. The proposed project aims to remove GHG by implementing Sustainable livestock grazing management and controlled fire over multiple grasslands of different provinces in the host country Republic of South Africa. In the baseline scenario, the pastures are larger and the livestock movement less frequent, allowing for unrestricted and selective grazing of perennial grasses. Loss of perennial grasses in grassland ecosystems results in soil loss and erosion, soil carbon loss, reduced water filtration capacity, and reduced productivity of forage.  The Project Activity i.e. 'planned grazing and controlled burning' will increase the rest and rotation on pastures above baseline practices. Smaller pastures implemented by fencing with more rotations allow the recovery of perennial grasses, which foster greater carbon inputs, higher retention of carbon as lignin and cellulose, and greater belowground production. This results in the sequestration of GHGs from the atmosphere into the soil. 

The project has been designated as a ‘Grouped Project’ and plans to increase the number of project instances over a period of time. The first instance includes four land areas Kwazulu Natal
(KZN, 6866.2 ha), Eastern Cape (EC, 71546.64 ha), MPL (3810.4 ha) and “Free State” (11281.9 ha) and this first instance aims to recover around 93,505 ha of land degraded by unrestricted grazing and uncontrolled fire through the implementation of planned rotational grazing and controlled burning.  The overall purpose of this initiative is to develop soil carbon storage through improved grassland management and expected to result in significant removal of CO2 from the atmosphere, as documented using the VCS methodology, “VM0026 – Sustainable Grassland Management”.

The project is an innovative integration of industrial composting and increasing carbon stocks in soil. The proposed grouped project was implemented by Ambipar Environmental Solutions within the first instance located in the South of Brazil. The annual average estimation of carbon accrual is 2,337 tCO2e and 38,397 tCO2e of reduction.
Compost application in soil has the potential of contribution to the carbon cycle, where simple nutrients that return to the soil are converted by plants into organic compounds engaging sustainable agricultural land management. 
Soil carbon accrual per unit area is measured in both baseline and project scenarios based on the spatial coordinated sampling gathering data on soil carbon concentration with statistical rigor. The project activities were designed to improve soils, including changes to agricultural practices, compost application and enhance biodiversity in soils. The measurement of the stable SOC concentration was set up to quantify soil dynamics at depth. The soil layers up to 80cm were sampled to estimate changes in carbon stock, excluding the top-soil 20cm.
Prior to the implementation of this project, rural producers do not foresee regenerative agriculture due to the lack of knowledge and technical skills about how to switch to organic input, biological control of plagues and sustainable land management. The previous scenario within the project area outcome low productivity per area, soil degradation and no smart application of the compost provided through the waste management, which implied in deposition applications without potential reuse for climate change mitigation.
Nowadays, this waste gets into the circular economy by its smart reuse and social and environmental positive influence. Ambipar manages great volumes across Brazil for about 50 industrial customers. Built on the raised potential for inclusion of new project activity instances, this grouped project brings up attractive engagement for high carbon landscapes.

Huaibin MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Zhengying Village, Wangjiagang Town, Huaibin County, Xinyang City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Huaibin BCCY New Power Co., Ltd.. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Huaibin MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Huaibin landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
Huaibin landfill site is located in Zhengying Village, Wangjiagang Town, Huaibin County, Xinyang City, and started operation in 2008 with a total design effective capacity of 2,580,000 m3 and a municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 350 tons/d and an operational lifespan of 19 years. The project has a total designed capacity 2MW (4*500kW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The project started construction on 25/10/2019 and started operation on 01/04/2020. The operation period of the project will end in 2030.
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Huaibin landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. 
Scenario existing prior to the start of the implementation of the project activity (the same as baseline scenario) 
•	LFG from Huaibin landfill site is released into the atmosphere.
•	Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the CCPG, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants.   
Project scenario
•	LFG from Huaibin landfill site is partially used for electricity generation. 
•	4×500 kW LFG-generator sets  supply electricity to the CCPG.	
The total power generation during the operation period is estimated to be 128,835 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 59,196 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the CCPG.

The project is a run-of- the- river type with minimum environmental impacts. The technology or electricity generation process using hydro resources is converting the potential energy available in the stream flowing from higher altitudes into mechanical energy using hydro turbines and then to electrical energy using alternators. The project activity will provide and sell electricity to the state electricity utility (Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited (UPCL)) through NEWNE grid, thus reducing dependence on fossil fuels and thereby reducing CO2 emissions. Electricity shall be evacuated through 33 KV line to the nearest 33 KV sub-station at Hanuman Chatti Sub Station.
vcs-2740:
Dekang AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Sichuan Province introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 10 existing swine farms in Sichuan Province. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one AWMS. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, most of the fertilizer is distributed to local farmers for free and only a small portion will be sold on the domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for electricity generation. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that the daily treatment capacity of the AWMS is 2,232 tons of animal manure. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be collected and used for electricity generation and the Residual biogas (if any) will be flared. The total installed capacity of the proposed project is 9.5MW and the annual electricity generation is estimated to be 58,669MWh. Also, the generated electricity will be only used for daily operation of the AWMS and the 10 swine farms themselves and will not be connected to the region power grid or other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from power generation are neglected.

NIZIP Energy Biogas Plant project is a biogas-to-energy project that generates renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by NİZİP BIYOGAZ ELEKTRIK URETIM SANAYİ VE TİCARET ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, as the Project Owner, in NİZİP district, GAZİANTEP province, in Turkey. 

The project whose main feedstock is cattle and chicken manure generated at its neighboring farms provides an environmentally friendly solution to manure management problems that farms are currently facing. The project is supplied with manure generated by animals at neighboring farms daily which is fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site.
Within the scope of the project, the biodegradation of organic wastes coming to the Biogas Plant is taking place in an anaerobic environment. The biogas that is released during the biodegradation of organic wastes is used for electricity and heat production in the biogas unit. 

The proposed project activity currently will have three biogas engines installed at the biogas power plant, with a total capacity of 1,501 KWe/h each. Accordingly, the biogas generator system is designed with a total power of 4.503 MWe/h. Whilst heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 486,141 tCO2eq/y.

The Paraguayan Chaco Neem Reforestation Project is located in the dry savannah of the Gran Chaco, a region famous for its dry and hostile conditions. The region is traditionally used for livestock, having its vegetation cover suppressed over the years. Thus, the purpose of the present grouped ARR project is the
reforestation of a region within Paraguay’s Gran Chaco, in Boquerón. This will be achieved through the recovery of deforested and/or degraded forests, with the planting of native or exotic species.
vcs-2745:
Wuwei City Afforestation Project in Gansu Province (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Wuwei City, Gansu Province, People’s Republic of China. Wuwei is a prefecture-level city along the Hexi Corridor and the Silk Road where the Loess Plateau, the Tibetan Plateau and the Mongolian Plateau. The project activities involve the planting of trees and shrubs of native species on 28,817.73 hectares (or 432,234 Mu ) of deserts and other barren lands located in Liangzhou District and Gulang County administered by Wuwei City. The species include Picea asperata (Chinese spruce), Platycladus orientalis (Oriental thuja or Oriental arborvitae), Ulmus pumila (Siberian elm), Elaeagnus angustifolia (Russian olive) and Haloxylon ammodendron (saxaul). The project area was barren lands before the project and would continue to be so without the implementation of the project activities. 
The implementation of the project activity will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conditions, increase the forest cover and enhance local biodiversity; the project also generates social benefits including job opportunities and technical skills training for local communities and residents.
vcs-2746:
Guangzhou Eastern Solid Resource Recycling Center MSW Integrated treatment Plant Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is located at the Solid Resource Recycling Center, Fushan Village, Jiulong Town, Luogang District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, P.R China.
The purpose of the project is to treat MSW with anaerobic digesters and utilize recovered biogas for electricity generation. The project activity includes MSW collection, MSW pre-treatment system, biodiesel production system, anaerobic digester, biogas purification, electricity generation system and waste heat recovery. 
The fresh waste of the project is mainly kitchen and catering waste of the Guangzhou City and the design processing capacity of the project for the fresh waste is 2,040 tonnes per day. The biogas from anaerobic digestion will be used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators. The total installed capacity will be 10.34 MW included 4 generators with each 1.063 MW and 2 generators with each 3.044 MW. 
Before the implementation of the project activity, the fresh waste would be treated in a landfill site with a partial capture of the landfill gas (LFG) and flaring of the captured LFG. The project is to utilize the biogas produced by anaerobic digestion for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is supplied to China South Power Grid (CSPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations. 
In absence of the project, equivalent amount of electricity exported to the grid by the project would have otherwise been supplied by China South Power Grid (CSPG). Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions will be reduced by avoiding CO2 emissions from those fossil fuel-based power plants connected to the grid and by avoiding GHG emissions from venting LFG into atmosphere at the landfill site.
vcs-2748:
Zhangye Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Zhangye City, the northwest of Gansu Province and in the middle of Hexi corridor where the Qinghai Tibet Plateau and Mongolia Plateau meet. The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by seeding grass and building fence on the degraded grassland, increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local development by introducing sustainable grazing and management of grassland. 
The project covers Gaotai County, Shandan County, Mingle County, Sunan County, Ganzhou district and Shandan Racecourse. According to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, the grassland in the region has been facing serious degradation and even desertification due to the impact of climate change and human activities. 
Totally, 261,059.80 ha of degraded grassland have been managed scientifically by fence building and reseeding of local high-quality forage. In general, rest grazing and rotational grazing are implemented in slightly degraded areas (the total grass yield decreased by 30%-50% compared with that before degradation), and reseeding is implemented in severely degraded areas. Besides these main restoration measures, the project also alleviate soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area. The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 29,440,243 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 736,006 tCO2e.
vcs-2749:
DelAgua clean cooking project is a voluntary Grouped Project (“GP”) aimed at distributing fuel efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to local communities in Rwanda. The Improved Cooking Stove will reduce the firewood usage and the time & efforts required for cooking.

vcs-275: The project activity implemented by Rakesh Builders | Developers (RBD), is a renewable green power generation project by installation of 4 wind mills of 1.25 MW each in Tirunelveli District, TamilNadu India in two phases. The annual GHG reduction by this project activity is expected to be 11147 tonnes of Carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e). vcs-2750:
The tropical Andes are among the most vulnerable places on earth due to the dual impacts of climate change and human population pressures. With the intense and historic livestock activity in the area, deforestation in the valleys north and south have almost completely isolated the eastern forest. The remaining habitat is an oasis of biodiversity and one of Colombia’s many national treasures. The region also contains two important watersheds: the Río San Juan Antioquia, and Río San Juan Bravo Chocó.  These watersheds provide critical ecosystem services to communities living and working throughout the area and the forests are vital to protection of the headwaters of these important sources of fresh water to the surrounding communities. Without them, landslides, silting, and flooding threaten the health and safety of thousands of residents. 

As our planet’s climate systems continue to be altered, it is highly likely that some or many of the species found in cloud forests will be lost forever. The effects of climate change are already apparent here. As a result, many cloud forest species have started to migrate upslope to maintain a favorable climate. However, their routes are often blocked by a degraded and fragmented landscape caused by agriculture moving up the mountainside and penetrating deeper into the lowlands.   

Our goal is to create a large, protected area for endemic and threatened species to shield them from imminent threats, mitigate climate impacts, and prevent extinctions. Since 2017, we have worked closely with our local partner Fundación Colibri to create a vital connection across a narrow ridgeline. This ecological corridor will safeguard endemic and endangered wildlife and offers important protection for the headwaters of a major river, the primary source of fresh water for communities throughout the region.

vcs-2760: This REDD+ project is located in the province of Oro in Papua New Guinea. The Oro forests are among the most valuable natural resources. These forests support hundreds of rare and endemic species, making this place a “mega-biodiverse” district. These forests are also directly critical to the lives and well-being of most of our people, including the communities in this province. For decades, these areas are under tremendous stress due to logging, shifting agriculture, and plantations. The demand for unprocessed logs from these areas from the Asian market is the biggest cause of forest loss. However, for the past two decades, forest harvesting has occurred in a destructive and ecologically unsustainable fashion. Secondly, a large portion of the forests is being converted to permanent agriculture and long fallow shifting cultivation. In addition, the human population is been tremendously increased in these areas, and hence the dependence on forest resources increased. Due to the increase in the human population, the poverty among the rural areas is also increased, therefore the subsistence farmers respond to the growing needs of the population by various forms of agricultural intensification. This project is an Avoided Unplanned Deforestation and Degradation (AUD) activity. This initiative proceeds with promoting various activities to mitigate climate change and improving livelihoods.
vcs-2761: TheUS Beef CowCredit project (Multiple Instances of Project Activities and multiple US states) aims to involve the US Beef industry with the purpose to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector. The project activity introduces Mootral® natural feed supplement into beef diet aiming to reduce methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by direct inhibition of methanogens in the rumen. This process results in a substantial net reduction of GHG emissions, because of the avoidance of CH4 released into the atmosphere, which would occur under normal operating circumstances (“the business as usual”). Over the 10 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated annual average reduction of 300'000 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e).

Guizhou Xintian CMM Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) refers to a power plant which utilizes low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) for power generation to supply electricity to the Xintian coal mine and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG). The Project is located in Gantang Town, Qianxi County, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, People’s Republic of China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted low concentration CMM to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM)  or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. It was planned that CMM power generators with a total capacity of 17.6 MW would be installed for the Project. Based on ex ante estimates, the power plant will destroy a total amount of 35.2 million m3 (under normal conditions ) of methane and export 82,720 MWh of electricity every year, when all power generators are in full operation. The generated electricity is supplied to the Xintian coal mine through the electricity distribution network in the coal mine area; part of the electricity produced by the Project is exported to CSPG after the coal mine demand is fully met.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it reduces methane emissions by capturing and destroying methane which would have been directly vented into the air in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing an amount of electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CSPG.
vcs-2763:
3R Management (P) Ltd (hereafter referred as “project proponent”) is installing Composting at various locations across India as a grouped project activity. 3R Management (P) Ltd is looking forward to earn carbon credits under VCS mechanism for these composting projects
Composting is a process by which organic wastes are broken down by microorganisms, generally bacteria and fungi, into simpler forms. The microorganisms use the carbon in the waste as an energy source. The degradation of the nitrogen- containing materials results in the breakdown of the original materials into a much more uniform product which can be used as a soil amendment. Heat generated during the process kills many unwanted organisms such as weed seeds and pathogens. Advantages of composting include reduction of waste volume, elimination of heat-killed pests, and the generation of a beneficial and marketable material. Adding compost to soil increases organic matter content.
vcs-2765:
The Project “Improved Forest Management through Logged-to-Protected Forests and Reduced Impact Logging in UFA Ngombé, Republic of Congo (IFM - UFA Ngombé Project)” is designed to improve forest management in 583,326 ha of native Congolese forests legally designated for selective logging. The Project is situated within the UFA Ngombé forest concession which is attributed to and managed by the company Industrie Forestière de Ouesso (IFO), owned by INTERHOLCO AG (IHC). The UFA Ngombé forest concession is divided into four Forest Management Units for 1) the production of timber, 2) community development, and 3) protection and 4) conservation of biodiversity. The Project Area includes areas of High Conservation Value (HCV), including swamps and floodplains in connection with some of the largest peatland complexes in the world, the Cuvette Centrale and the Congo Basin peatland areas. These peatlands are essential for carbon storage, as peatlands store more carbon than any other natural terrestrial system. UFA Ngombé also borders the Ntokou-Pikounda National Park which is home to diverse wildlife, including one of the world’s largest western lowland gorilla populations.
The principle activities of the IFM - UFA Ngombé Project are 1) to implement Reduced Impact Logging (RIL-C) to reduce GHG emissions in one or more source categories (i.e., timber felling, skidding and hauling), and 2) to set-aside areas of Logged-to-Protected Forests (LtPF) to maintain and protect ecosystem services in forest production areas legally designated for selective logging. The Project will apply the VCS VM0035 and VM0010 methodologies to the respective RIL-C and LtPF Project Activities.

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Pinghu City under the jurisdiction of Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province of China, which have a total acreage of 12,545 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded. 
With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . Hence, this project activity is estimated to reduce 4.78 tCO2e/ha. 
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 419,489 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,927 tCO2e.

vcs-2772: The main purpose of this CPA is dissemination of the efficient improved cooking stove woody biomass-based ICS to the rural household of Madagascar. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, which will result in reduced firewood consumption, hence saving fuel. This will not only halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Madagascar but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood. Therefore, this will lead to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases, conservation of forests and woodlands as well as improved health conditions of ICS users due to improved indoor air quality.

This will not only halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Madagascar but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood. Therefore, this will lead to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases, conservation of forests and woodlands as well as improved health conditions of ICS users due to improved indoor air quality.

vcs-278: Henan Luoyang Huanghe Tongli Cement Co., Ltd. To effectively utilize the low temperature waste heat of the exit gases from Suspension Preheater (SP) and Air Quenching Chamber (AQC), the project entity intends to build one 9MW Waste Heat Recovery (WHR) captive power station for the 5,000t/d clinker production line. The total power capacity of steam turbine generator is 9MW.

vcs-2790:
The ARR Cerrado Carbon Project is located at the Cerrado Biome, in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. It is an AFOLU project, and therefore is classified within scope 14. More specifically, the project falls under the ARR category.
The ARR Cerrado Carbon Project’s purpose is to remove and reduce GHG emissions through an increase in forestry area and preservation of native vegetation in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, at the Cerrado biome, initially near the city of Ribas do Rio Pardo. The project also includes the management and implementation of various social activities at the local communities nearby. The carbon credits are a result of the change of land use in previous pasture areas, through the plantation of Eucalyptus species in an area of 38.708 ha (ARR category).
The plantation activities will be developed in accordance with good forestry practices, and in addition, the project proponents will also seek certification under sustainable programs, such as the FSC, which can confirm the implementation of such practices.
vcs-2791:
The project is located on the south-western slope of the Sarawaget Range in Morobe Province. It is comprised of three regions that are based on clan affiliations and is accessible from Lae. It consists of lower montane forest with small areas of lowland tropical rainforest and covers a total area of 226,843 hectares. The project comprises an initial area of approximately 226,843 hectares stretches from Tamigidu on the coast near Lae, all the way to the Morobe/Madang border in the Wantoat/Leron LLG area. It is located on the south-western slopes of the Sarawaget range in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea and is home to approximately 20,000 people.

Forests in the project area, however, have experienced a continued reduction in biomass due largely to illegal logging and to the establishment of crops, use of firewood, pastures, and settlements. These forests have historically been an important source of income for local families, who periodically harvest timber when the economic needs arise, or to generate income generation sources.

The climate objective of the Project is to avoid and prevent the unplanned deforestation in native forests of PNG, thus avoiding the net emission of 34,026,450 tCO2e through 30 years of Project crediting period.
vcs-2792: The objective of this project is to restore 1003 hectares of degraded lands in the Ayeyarwady Division of Myanmar. As per the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) category, the project falls under the ARR (Afforestation, reforestation and Revegetation) category. The project will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem in degraded lands belonging to Chaung Thar, Kangyi, and Bomie village tracts. Apart from the carbon sequestration, the project will address issues including natural disaster risk reduction, biodiversity improvement and poverty reduction with sustainable livelihoods in the coastal communities.

The purpose of the CPA is to combat climate change and contribute to sustainable development of Burundi, by reducing non renewable wood fuel consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of household users in rural and/or peri urban areas of Burundi by selling affordable Improved Cooking Stoves (ICSs) in replacement of traditional wood stoves. ICS combust wood fuel more efficiently, i.e. require less firewood than traditional stoves, reducing CO 2 emissions. It is assumed that in the absence of the project activity, the baseline scenario would be the projected use of fossil fuels to meet similar therm al energy needs as those provided by the project devices.
CPA implementer is Observatoire de l’Environnement et de la Nature « OBEN », the main technology supplier under the PoA, with the international assistance of AERA Group, leading carbon finance advisor in Africa. OBEN will run the project in compliance with the PoA requirements, disseminating estimated 250 ,000 affordable Improved Cooking Stoves (ICSs) in replacement of traditional wood fuel cooking stoves, such as 3 stone fires, resulting in an ave rage of 281,112 tCO2 avoided per year or 2 million tCO2 over the 7 year crediting period.
