Shandong Lijin Breeding Swine Farm Biogas RecoveryProject(hereinafter referred to as the Project) locates inLijin Huayu Breeding Swine Farm, Kongjiazao Village, Mingji Township, Lijin County, Dongying City, Shandong Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implementedby LijinHuayuBreeding SwineCo., Ltd.
The project is tointroduces anew anaerobic animal manure management system to treat manure waste (Breeding swine) from Lijin Huayu Breeding Swine Farm. This project uses USR(Up-flow Solid Reactor) to treat animal manure, and collect and destroy the generated biogas to avoid methane emissions.The generatedbiogas will be captured and sent to flaring withinthe project site. The residual waste from the USRdigesters will be sent outside of the project site for aerobic composting and then returned to the field as fertilizer.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the swinemanure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system at the LijinHuayu Breeding Swine Farmand generated methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 17,727tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 124,089tCO2e during the first 7-year crediting period.

Crop Zone Agro Forestry Limited (CZAFL) is proposing a grouped Afforestation, Reforestation and  Revegetation (ARR) in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Maharashtra state of India. CZAFL is the Project Proponent (PP) whereas EKI Energy Services Limited (Enking International) is providing 
carbon credit advisory services to the PP. The CZAFL has mobilized the farmers in the selected states of India to plant various tree species on their lands. These tree species range from fruit bearing trees like Indian blackberry, Guava, Mango to commercial species like Teak, Mahogany and Sandal. Simple 
tree cultivation techniques involving planting saplings in the pits with minimum disturbance to the lands have been employed. The lands selected for the project activity is fallow agriculture land. The PP has made contract with the farmers/land owners where they will be given tree saplings and technical support. In return, the PP will reap the benefits through sale of carbon credits. Initially, 501.7 hectares of land has been selected for the first project activity instance. Through carbon sequestration by the planted trees, the project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions of removals of 10,571 tCO2e.

The proposed mangrove restoration grouped project intends to generate GHG emission removals by restoring the ecosystems through the plantation of up to 16,000 hectares of mangrove. Within the first project instance of this project, the project activities will be carried out over an area of 7,020 hectares, by planting at least 35 million of new mangrove trees. The project area is located in Sine Saloum Delta and Casamance estuary in Senegal, being most of the project area within the boundaries of Protected areas. The plantation will be carried out in places previously selected due to their ecological conditions, together with the local communities, through a design that implies the active participation of communities involved in the project.
The goal of the project is to increase the mangrove area by planting a variety of species of native mangrove, which will increase the positive functions (ecosystem services) that mangroves provide to communities and biodiversity.  The location of the project contributes to the continuity of habitats and ecosystems, since the plantation areas are close to other reforestation project and inside the area of mangrove distribution in Senegal This project is expected to bring positive benefits for different species relevant for the communities as fishes, oysters and mollusks.
WeForest is the Project Proponent and the NGO Oceanium is the Project Implementer of the restoration activities. For the community and biodiversity activities WeForest is in charge and will perform those through other implementing partners and the subsequent agreement with them. WeForest´s fundamental goal is to create social value for rural communities and contribute to their food security through the restoration of their ecosystems. WeForest provides investors access to biodiversity friendly carbon credits that aid the rural communities through large scale and social impact projects.

The Central Europe CowCredit project (multiple instances of Project activity) aims to involve the dairy industry in Central Europe with the purpose to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector.  The project activity introduces Mootral® natural feed supplement into dairy cattle diet aiming to reduce methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by direct inhibition of methanogens in the rumen. 
The project activity includes Germany, Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Austria. It aims to add more instances over the 10 years of the first crediting period. The project implementation results in a substantial net reduction of GHG emissions, because of the avoidance of CH4 release into the atmosphere. Methane is a by-product of the enteric fermentation process and is expelled by the animal through belching. Prior to the start of the proposed project activity, there were no similar enteric methane reduction activities, therefore, this leads to CH4 released into the atmosphere (“the business as usual”).  Over the 10 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated annual average reduction of 600’000 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) and 6'000'000 tons over the 10 years of the first crediting period (from 01/07/2022 to 30/06/ 2032). The Project is quantified and will be monitored according to VCS methodology “VM0041 Methodology for the Reduction of Enteric Methane Emission from Ruminants through the Use of 100% Natural Feed Supplement” and falls under VCS Sectoral Scope 15, Livestock and manure management.
vcs-2842:
BlueMX Aztlán Blue Carbon is a large-scale mangrove restoration project in Nayarit, Mexico, led by and for local communities. 

The Project seeks to restore degraded mangrove ecosystems, mitigate climate change, enhance biodiversity and ecological resilience, and create improved livelihoods for local communities in the coastal areas of Nayarit, Mexico, in and around the Marismas Nacionales Biosphere Reserve.  

Known in the Uto-Aztecan tradition as “the place of the white heron”, the BlueMX Aztlán project area is rich in biodiversity, with more than 600 species of plants and animals recorded to date.  At full scale, BlueMX Aztlán Blue Carbon will aim to restore more than 22,000 hectares of coastal wetlands and build long-term ecosystem resilience by reconnecting tidal flows, improving hydrology, assisting natural regeneration with practices like elevated mangrove recruitment clusters also knows as “chinampas”.

The project employs hundreds of local people and supports social and environmental programs including handcraft, strengthening local fisheries, apiculture, mobile health clinics, environmental education and training, improved waste management and social security.
vcs-2843:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Qianxi City and Jinsha County, Guizhou Province, where located in southwestern China with a total acreage of 19,056 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emissions decrease than the continuously flooded.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir construction and necessary training for farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional flooded method. Controllable irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 3.11 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 412,713 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 58,959 tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes.
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers.
- Provide more job opportunities, especially female workers.
- Use a proportion of benefits to improve the local children’s education.
vcs-2844:
The project introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 11 existing swine farms in Nanyang City, Henan Province. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 1,759 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMSs and 3,531.53*104m3 of biogas can be produced annually. Also, the generated heat through biogas will be only used for daily operation of the AWMSs and the 11 swine farms themselves and will not be provided to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.

The project involves installing 3 composting plants respectivelly in Xianjia Industrial Park (Plant 1), Shuangmiao village of Mishui Sub-district (Plant 2) and zhangxinzhuang village of Liquan Sub-district (Plant 3), Gaomi city, Weifang city, Shandong Province in order to treat the manure from the chicken farms and Biomass waste residue such as Cassava residue and chaff in Gaomi city. Xinjiang Burqin Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Burqin County, Altai City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restoration of severely degraded land by replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term.
There are two main restoration measures in the project: 1) Grass seeding was implemented in 5,000 ha of the severely degraded grasslands where grass seeds of local high-quality forage was sowed under the condition of fencing enclosure for 2 years, and then the grassland should be used reasonably and sustainably according to the local approved livestock carrying capacity. 2) Imposing grazing prohibition measures and building fences on 60,000 hectares of degraded grassland in order to strengthen the protection and improvement of the grassland and to prevent excessive cultivation, grazing or human destruction. 
Besides these main restoration measures, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area.

In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 3.13 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 418,572 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 59,796 tCO2e.
This project aims to:

- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers
- Provide more job opportunities, especially female workers
- Use a proportion of benefits to improve the local children’s education

vcs-2860:
An anaerobic covered lagoon is a simple, effective and reliable technology to capture anaerobic lagoon produced biogas. The material used to cover the anaerobic lagoon is a synthetic high-density polyethylene (HDPE). The necessary materials used must be UV resistant, hydrophobic, tear and puncture resistant, non-toxic to bacteria and has a bulk density near that of water. HDPE is one of the most used geo-membranes used worldwide due to its UV, ozone and chemical resistance. This covering approach in the lagoon prevents methane emissions and reduces odour. This project activity will capture and combust methane gas produced from the anaerobic portion of an existing wastewater treatment system. 
The biogas lagoon is built in the form of an embankment lagoon by earth, the walls and bottom are compacted, lined with 1mm HDPE tarp, and all the surface is covered with 1.5 mm HDPE tarp. The biogas lagoon has a volume of 130,260m3, 151 m long, 136 m wide, 9m deep and is used for the main purpose of decomposing organic compounds in anaerobic conditions. 
To combust the excess biogas, an enclosed type of ground flare with fully automatic operation, including temperature measurement, has been installed. Flaring is fully automatic and continuous: starting when the biogas reaches an established high pressure setting and stopping when biogas pressure drops to an established low pressure setting. An automatic flare ignition system ensures methane is combusted whenever biogas is present at the flare. The flare includes thermocouples to monitor flare exhaust gas temperature, which is measured and recorded.

The project introduced a set of organic fertilizers production lines with an annual output of 31,500 tons to treat the manure from the chicken farms and Biomass waste residue i.e. straw in Xuancheng City, Anhui Prvince. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners and the biomass waste residue had been left to decay anaerobically in a solid waste disposal site (SWDS).
The proposed project was designed to treat the chicken manure and biomass waste residue such as straw, plant ash, rice husk in Xuancheng City to produce organic fertilizer. The proposed project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system, etc. It is estimated that approximately 75,000tons of manure and 18,750tons of biomass waste residue can treat annually, therefore total 93,750 tons of waste can be composted aerobically for this project. The final compost obtained will be sold to local businesses. The construction start date of the project is 01/05/2020 and was put into operation on 25/07/2020.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue. It is estimated that 51,261 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 512,613 tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixing crediting period.

Henan Shunhe CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located in Shunhe township, Yongcheng, Shangqiu City, Henan Province, China. The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted coal mine methane (CMM) with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved.
Ten sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 2.1MW (3*0.7MW), destroying 4.347 million m3 of methane annually. After the full operation of the Project, the expected annual exported electricity will be 11,320 MWh, which will be supplied to the coal mine first through the electricity distribution network in Shunhe coal mine area, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the CCPG and displace part of the electricity generated by CCPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the CCPG.

The CRIMA Predio Putumayo y Andoque de Aduche REDD+ Project seeks the conservation of
forests located in the indigenous territories of Andoque de Aduche Indigenous Reserve, in the
municipality of Solano and Puerto Santander; and in the areas of the indigenous communities of Puerto Zábalo y Los Monos, and
Monochoa that are part of the vast Great Predio Putumayo Indigenous Reserve and that are
located in Puerto Leguizamo, Puerto Alegría, La Chorrera
and Puerto Santander municipalities. The project area has a
total area of 1.260.222 ha at the beginning of the monitoring period. The project aims to
contribute to mitigate the effects caused by climate change by reducing 27.686.867 tCO2
emissions derived from deforestation and forest degradation during the 30-year crediting period.
The main activities during the Project lifetime focus in the development of productive activities compatible with
community well-being and nature conservation, providing food security, improving social
investment, strengthening land use planning and self-government structure, monitoring biodiversity and
forest conservation. These activities aim to control and reduce the incidence of deforestation
drivers such as wood extraction, mining and illegal productive activities.
The area is characterized by its high biodiversity along with social unrest and deforestation.
Among the activities carried out by the promoters of deforestation are moving the border of
farming activities (especially subsistence agriculture and livestock), mining, wood harvesting for
commercial and community use, illegal crops and colonization processes. The social problems
are triggered by the absence of the government, lack of sanitation infrastructure, education,
health programs and shortage of technological guidance for sustainable development.
This project focuses on the AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses) sectors. Inside
the category for Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation in developing
countries (REDD+). Its goal is to mitigate the effects caused by climate change through
reduction of CO2 emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, restauration of degraded
forest lands, promotion of the sustainable wood harvesting and carry out development activities
for the community well-being.

The project introduces new animal waste management systems to treat the manure from 7 swine farms in Nanyang City and Zhumadian City, Henan Province. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one animal waste management system (AWMS), and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for heat generation. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 1,637 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be collected and used for heat production. The heat production is estimated to be 657,340GJ. Also, the generated heat will be only used for daily operation of the AWMSs and the 7 swine farms themselves and will not be provided to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 321,663tCO2e emission reductions will be produced annually.

Binzhou Topigs Norsvin Breeding Swine Co., Ltd. Binhai Swine Farm Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project is located in Zhanhua District, Binzhou City, Shandong Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Binzhou Topigs Norsvin Breeding Swine Co., Ltd. Binhai Branch.
This project is to build an anaerobic animal manure treatment system to treat manure waste of breeding swine in the Binhai Breeding Swine Farm. The project uses the HDPE membrane enclosed anaerobic digesters to treat animal manure waste, and the biogas produced in this process will be recovered and utilized by the biogas heating system for heat supply during the heating period (October to April next year). During the non-heating period (May to September),the biogas will be burnt through the biogas flare system. The residual waste from the digesters will be handled aerobically to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system (uncovered open lagoon) at the Binhai Breeding Swine Farm and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. For conservativeness, the emission reduction from the biogas heating system is not considered. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 11,795 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 82,563 tCO2e during the first 7-year renewable crediting period.
vcs-2881:
The New Forests Company (NFC) was founded in 2004 in Uganda with the vision of creating a sustainable timber resource in East Africa amidst significant deforestation. From the start, the Company adopted a Shared Value approach to doing business that recognizes the need for the three C’s of Conservation, Community and Commerce in order to thrive and be sustainable. Furthermore, NFC has been FSC (Forest Stewardship Council) certified continuously in Uganda since 2009, demonstrating the Company’s commitment to responsible forestry practices that benefit the environment and local communities.
Within 5 years, NFC established three greenfield commercial plantations at Namwasa, Kirinya and Luwunga. Namwasa and Luwunga are government concessions within Central Forest Reserves (CFR) that were proclaimed in the 1930s, but management of the reserves weakened  after independence. The CFRs subsequently suffered from high levels of deforestation and encroachment of subsistence farming and charcoal production. The Kirinya plantation was established on an abandoned sugar cane farm that was established in the 1970s.

The Guangxi Fangcheng District IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Fangcheng District, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region of China by Fangchenggang Fangcheng District Jinsui Agriculture Investment Co., Ltd, the geo-coordinate of the  project is  107°27'E -108°30'E and 20°30'N - 22°00'N, the total area is 6238 km2, which includes  the  Improved  Forest  Management  (IFM)  of  the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 8263.71 ha, including 4,250 subcompartments spreading over Dalu Town, Dongzhong Town, Fulong Town, Huashi Town, Jiangshan Town, Maoling Town, Naliang Town, Nasuo Town,Tanying Township, Shiwanshanyaozu Township, Shuiying Street, Wenchang Street, Zhuhe Street of Fangcheng District. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned forests or collective-owned forests, and have the legal right to forest ownership. All the owners authorized the project proponent to access the project to their behalf. The species involved in the project are Pinus elliottii and Pinus massoniana. The forest of the project was older plantations under managing. Before the implantation of the project, the usual type of management was clearcutting.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 1,899,564 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 94,978 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 1,462,648 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 73,132 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to development.

Gansu Zhangye Grouped Afforestation Project (hereafter “the project”) is located in Zhangye City, Gansu Province of China. The project’s aim is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren lands. The grouped project combines multiple project activity instances into a single, combined project that adds new instances over time. The project proponent sets the geographic boundaries for the grouped project, including where new project activity instances may be added (Section 2.1.7), and establishes criteria for determining the eligibility of future instances (Section 2.1.21).
For the initial project activity instance, 11,011.93 ha of forest is to be planted by direct planting on barren lands in Zhangye City, and the planted trees and shrub are all native species which including Elaeagnus angustifolia (oleaster), Armeniaca sibirica (prumus armeniaca), Populus L. (aspen), Ulmus pumila L. (elm), Picea asperata Mast. (spruce), Pinus sylvestris (mongolian pine), Haloxylon ammodendron (synonym), Caragana korshinskii Kom (caragana microphylla) . It is expected that the scope of the project will increase. For the inclusion of new eligible areas as project instances willing to participate within the grouped project, the new areas shall meet the criteria listing in Section 2.1.21. According to the project design report, 53,000 hectares of new afforestation area is expected to be added from 2021 to 2027. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change; improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forests and bring income and job opportunities for local communities and residents.
vcs-2885:
The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Malawi. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 
Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Malawi. It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove, will be distributed. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Malawi, but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.
The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance which in turn is used for subsidising the price of ICS and for recovering project implementation costs.

The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Malawi. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 
Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Malawi. It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove, will be distributed. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Malawi, but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.
The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance which in turn is used for subsidising the price of ICS and for recovering project implementation costs.
vcs-2887: This project works with the ranchers of northern Mexico who raise livestock on individually owned or community-owned grasslands and enables those ranchers to adopt Improved Grassland Management (IGM). Ranchers in this region have traditionally followed practices such as continuous grazing, without any sustainable grazing or water management plans in place. This has resulted in overgrazing, leading to severe soil degradation, loss of vegetative cover and even desertification. When ranchers then become unable to sustain their livelihoods on their degraded ranches, they are sometimes forced to sell their land to farmers who convert the grasslands into croplands, resulting in further CO2 emissions and loss of natural flora and fauna. Through this project, ranchers are adopting new management practices, which include rotational grazing and a variety of water conservation measures. In rotational grazing, livestock are rotated between different sections of a pasture over the course of days, weeks, or months, while other sections of the pasture are allowed to rest. These sections are known as “paddocks”. This practice allows plants to recover and grow in the paddocks that are allowed to rest, and thus allows them to sequester carbon, gradually regenerating the land. In addition, for arid regions like northern Mexico, water conservation measures help increase the availability of water (which would otherwise be lost) for the growth of the biomass, contributing to the regeneration. The livelihoods of the communities utilizing these ranches are improved directly through the carbon credit payments, which provide an additional source of income, and indirectly through the increased productivity of their lands. The regenerated lands also become much less likely to undergo land use change, because the ranchers are better able to sustain their livelihoods. This in turn ensures that crucial habitats for the flora and fauna of the region are protected.

This project works with the farmers of southern and central India to help them adopt improved agricultural practices such as residue management and enhanced cropping practices that sequester carbon while increasing productivity. This region is largely composed of small and marginal farmers, with each farming just a few hectares of land. As a result, these farmers are highly susceptible to variabilities arising from markets and weather. 
Over the last century, agriculture in the region has undergone a dramatic shift towards intensification. Since the late 1940s, yields of all staple crops have seen a several-fold increase. This increase was necessary to feed a growing population, but at the same time, it led to an increase of 150kg/ha in the amount of synthetic fertilizer applied to farms, along with similar increases in other crop inputs. An intensive agricultural process focused on maximizing yields every year has led to a gradual degradation of the soils of the region, resulting in CO2 emissions from the lost soil carbon. 
In this context, improved agricultural practices provide the opportunity and the power to reverse this land degradation and return carbon to the soil, creating carbon removals while improving overall soil health. In this project, farmers adopt a variety of improved agriculture practices. These practices are proven ways to increase soil organic carbon, and also enable farmers to improve their productivity: increases in soil organic carbon improve the ability of soils to store moisture and nutrients, and thus also help to increase yields. This project works towards helping farmers to surmount their barriers, while working with partners to create feasible and sustainable solutions that effect grass-roots behavior change. Furthermore, the financial benefits from carbon credits will provide a direct boost to the livelihoods of these farmers, many of whom are small and marginal farmers.

Guizhou Jinyan CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located in Fengshan township, Dafang County, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, China. The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. 
Ten sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 4.8MW (8*0.6MW), destroying 8.7936 million m3 of methane annually. After the full operation of the Project, the expected annual exported electricity will be 24,816 MWh, which will be supplied to the coal mine first through the electricity distribution network in Jinyan coal mine area, and then to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG and displace part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG.

The project is located in one of the densest and most important forest areas in Cameroon, in the southern part of the eastern region, near the border with Congo and the Central African Republic. It is a state-owned forest granted in concession for the exploitation of wood resources, and like all neighboring areas, is of great economic interest due to the presence of high-value timber species. Since 2002, this forest unit has been managed by the company La Filière Bois (LFB), which harvests volumes of commercial timber from it, following the terms of the management plan that was drawn up at the start of management.
The VCS Improved Forest Management (IMF) - Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF) project aims to preserve a part of the forest from the exploitation of forest resources, which would anyway be used in the following years as foreseen in the documents approved by the Ministère des Forêts et de la Faune (MINFOF) - Ministry of Forests and Wildlife. The area that will be exempted from the work is approximately 44’413 ha for an estimated volume of 38 m3 /ha of forest not been harvested.
From the implementation of the Project, it is estimated that a net average of 325’885 tonnes of GHG emissions will be avoided from entering the atmosphere annually. Over the entire Project Crediting Period, it is estimated that a net total of 6’517’703 tonnes of GHG emissions will be avoided through the implementation of the Project.
vcs-290: Installation of a new 636 ton per day combustion unit at the Lee County Waste To Energy Facility in Fort Myers, Florida. The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Wuxing District and Deqing County under the jurisdiction of Huzhou City, Zhejiang Province of China, which have a total acreage of 12,019 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.
With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%1. Hence, this project activity is estimated to reduce 4.97 tCO2e/ha.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 418,257 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,751tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes;
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers;
- Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

The Ejido Felipe Carrillo Puerto (from now on “the Ejido”) is in the state of Quintana Roo’s central region, in southwestern Mexico. Declared a Forest Ejido in 1947 (U'yo'olché A.C., 2005). It is currently inhabited by 288 Ejido landowners and their families. The population of the site is mostly comprised of peninsular Mayans. Since its origins, the jungle has been exploited for the extraction of chewing gum found in the chicozapote tree (Manilkara zapota). 

The principal aim of this Project is the removal of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through activities that allow the identification, prioritisation, and execution of actions for the adequate management of dry tropical forest, the advancement of sustainable development, the establishment of local governance and the promotion of improved forest management activities.

The Project began in February 2018 and has an expected duration of 30 years; during this period, the removal of 6,459,222 CO2e is expected, this implies an average annual removal of 215,307 tCO2e.
This project will provide community benefits related to the strengthening of local governance and positive externalities to the management of forests. Meanwhile, maintaining sustainable community management practices for tropical forests, with a greater perception of the value of ecosystem services, as well as increasing employment opportunities. 

Finally, is also expected to use the CCB Program in conjunction with VCS to empower local communities and help protect endangered species.

The North Bandai Bamboo Reforestation Project is a reforestation project that is restoring 2,863 hectares of degraded forest lands within the Ashanti Region of Ghana, West Africa. It is a carbon financed project that integrates the reforestation of 1 million seedlings of sympodial bamboo with remnant standing trees, and areas set aside for biodiversity and conservation. The project area has suffered extreme historical deforestation and represents highly degraded lands that are prone to further loss of remaining tree cover in the absence of the reforestation activity. 

The project is managed alongside the adjacent Bandai Hills Bamboo Reforestation Project to represent a combined 10,681 hectare unique approach to forest landscape restoration.

vcs-293: Sukhbir Agro Energy Limited is producer rice in the region. The capacity of the rice mill is 50 TPD of paddy processing. Steam is a vital utility to perform number of operations during the manufacturing of rice. To meet the process steam requirement, SAELdecided to go for captive steam generation by setting up an in-house boiler. Considering the fact that rice husk is a renewable source of energy and use of rice husk would prevent use of coal, a carbon intensive fossil fuel, SAEL decided to install a rice-husk fired boiler to meet its process steam requirement. The project activity involves installation of a 6 TPH capacity rice husk firedboiler to meet the captive steam (heat) requirement. The project activity leads toavoidance of consumption of fossil fuel for the generation of process steam andconsequently contributes to GHG emission reduction and actively participate in the climate change initiative and contribute towards the sustainable development of the region.

The Hunan Cili IFM (conversion of logged to protected  forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Cili County, Zhangjiajie City, Hunan Province of China by Hunan Cili Jiangya Forest Farm, the geo-coordinate of the  project proponent is 110°27'E -111°20'E and 29°04'N - 29°41'N, the total area is 3480 km2, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest. The project avoids emissions by converting logged forests into protected forests.
The area of the project activity is 6993.48 ha, including 1,764 subcompartments. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned forests or collective-owned forests, and have the legal right to forest ownership. All the owners authorized the project proponent to access the project to their behalf. The species involved in the project are Broad-leaved tree Chinese fir and Pinus massoniana. The forest of the project was older plantations or natural forest under managing. Before the implantation of the project, the usual type of management was clearcutting.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 896,881 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 44,844 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 690,585 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 34,529 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

The Limeira Atlantic Forest Biodiversity Conservation Project is located in the state of Paraná, south of Brazil. Its area is located within the Atlantic Forest Biome, home of a great diversity of fauna and flora, including several endemic and endangered species, including the terrestrial tapir (Tapirus terrestrial), the largest terrestrial mammal, described as (endangered, IUNC, 2011) in the Atlantic Forest due to habitat loss ( (Medici et.al., 2011). The preserved forest is an important generator of ecosystems services such as water supply, climate regulation, tourism, energy, unique maintenance , beyond the environment with unique natural beauty. This hot spot on earth suffers a great risk of being converted to non-ecological uses, as 70% of the Brazilian GDP  is concentrated in it, only 12.4% of the original forest is left in Brazil, demonstrating that they cause a huge impact on this forest, which is limited by human development and agricultural.
The project area is the home to more than 50 headwaters, which flow into the São João River, an important water resource in the region. It is part of the only region of the state of Paraná with preserved native vegetation, being an important ecological corridor for the passage of fauna between two large National Parks. Areas such as the project are subject to intense risk every day, mainly due to degradation, which happens little by little, but causes a huge impact on this biome so fragile by human development.
This project extends itself through the territory of the municipalities of Guaratuba and Morretes, inside the rural area where the economy is based on agriculture and extractivism, being bananas and peach palm the main crops. The production and trade of these products is driven by the close Limeira state highways and by the Limeira street which passes through the project’s area from North to South, so it is considered th margins of this road, areas susceptible to deforestation.
vcs-2951:
Liaoning Xinwang Swine Farm Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project)  introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to a group of 10 swine farms in Kangping County, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province, China, which are owned by Kangping Xinwang agriculture and animal husbandry Co., Ltd (hereinafter called” Xinwang”). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater from the 10 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.

In this project, AWMS is built to replace the traditional open anaerobic lagoons, and each subsidiary swine farm installed one AWMS. The manure and waster will be collected into the anaerobic digesters and then biogas generated during the anaerobic treatment process will be captured and total 2500*104m3 biogas are expected to be generated annually. Biogas is then sent into biogas boilers for heat production. Every biogas boiler has been installed in each swine farms. All of the heat generated are used by AWMSs and the swine farms, while the rest (if any) will be burned. The sludge produced after fermentation is applied to corn fields as fertilizer, and the wastewater produced by anaerobic biogas digesters is used for agricultural irrigation.
Benefited from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMSs and 10 swine farms. 
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 201,850 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 1,412,950 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

The Not Hot Afforestation project  is designed to afforest non-used agricultural land (meadow)
with birch (Betula pendula) species native to the area. Part of the agricultural lands are not
managed (they do not use food product production). All this time, unmanaged land has brought
virtually no benefit to landowners or to the national economy. There are still about 300 kha of
non-forested agricultural land in Latvia, which meets the criteria of low-valued areas accessible
for afforestation. About 130 thousand ha of agricultural areas have organic soils. The potential for
reducing GHG emissions in such areas are particularly high. 1
This project is a grouped project, located in Latvia.
The Not Hot Afforestation Project will generate GHG removals through sequestration living
biomass and soil organic carbon. These credits are generated using CGM methodology AR-
ACM0003: Afforestation and reforestation of lands except wetlands (version 2).
Implemented activities in the project will remove an amount of 2,203 tons CO₂ in mineral soils
and 55 tons CO₂ in organic soils within 40 years. This means an average of 55 tons CO₂ yr⁻¹ in
mineral soils and 5.87 tons CO₂ yr⁻¹ in organic soils per year. A total area of 5.06 ha activities will
remove 2,438 tCO₂ within 40 years, which means an average of 60.9 tons CO₂ yr⁻¹.
Project will result in a significant contribution to sustainable development of Latvia, mainly
through: i) increased employment and quality of employment; ii) rural development
(decentralization); iii) increased gross value of production; iv) biodiversity preservation and v)
improvement and preservation of soil quality.

Wuhan Chenjiachong Landfill Gas Power Generation Project Phase II (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project located at Chenjiachong Landfill Phase II, Chenjiachong Town, Yangluo County, Xinzhou District, Wuhan City, Hubei province, People’s Republic of China. 
The purpose of the Project is to collect LFG from Chenjiachong Landfill Phase II and utilize it for power generation. The Project started construction in December 2019. Four power generators of 1.095 MW each, which add up to 4.38 MW, have been installed, and they were put into operation on 14-July-2020.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CCPG.
vcs-2958: The Lanao del Sur Bamboo Reforestation Project is a carbon financed landscape scale restoration project in the province of Lanao del Sur, on the island of Mindanao, Philippines. The project area covers 8,421 hectares of degraded montane landscapes. Project activities target the planting of 2.5 million clumps of native species of sympodial bamboo over a 3-4 year period. Bamboo reforestation activities are combined with the additional planting of 1 million trees of native species on areas not eligible for carbon accreditation, creating a biodiverse and holistic landscape. vcs-2964: Polatlı Enerbes Biogas Project is a biogas to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented  in Çanakçı village, Polatlı district, Ankara province, in Turkey. The project whose main feedstock will be cattle and chicken manure generated at farms in Polatlı, provides an environmentally friendly solution to this manure management problem. it is estimated that approximately 1,178 tons of cattle manure and 22 tons of chicken manure (totally 1,200 tons) generated at nearby animal farms will be collected daily through special sewage trucks equipped with close-tanks in order to prevent any odor and/or manure leakages and to be fed into the anaerobic digesters at the biogas power plant. The biogas that will be released during the biodegradation of organic wastes will be used for electricity and heat production in biogas unit. The proposed project activity has 3 biogas engines installed at the biogas power plant, with the total capacity of 4,500 KWe/h. Accordingly, the biogas generator system to be installed will be designed with a total power of 4.50 MWe/h. Whilst heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid. This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 529,993 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 3,709,951 tCO2eq emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

This savannah Land Afforestation Project on the Batéké Plateau north of Brazzaville aims to develop an alternative and renewable source of charcoal for urban use, based on the establishment of Acacia auriculiformis plantations. Furthermore, Acacia rows will be intercropped with lines of food crops (Cassava in particular), forming agroforestry plantations. 
We also know that another effective tool to combat global warming are 'carbon sink' plantations, i.e. plantations where trees are not harvested, in order to maximize greenhouse gas sequestration in the long term. Half of the project's area will therefore be dedicated to Acacia mangium plantations with the main objective of CO2 sequestration.
These plantations will be set up in anthropogenic savannahs, i.e. land with a biomass stock blocked at a very low stage due to recurrent bushfires. The savannahs are deliberately set to fire at frequent intervals (at least once a year) by villagers to facilitate agricultural, pastoral and cynegetic activities.
As a result, the Project will have several social and environmental benefits such as (1) CO2 sequestration on land that is currently non-forested and unused, (2) Less pressure on the surrounding natural forests, thanks to the production of charcoal from sustainably managed plantations, (3) Job creation in a territory heavily affected by unemployment, increased incomes. As such, the project acts as a driving force of local development and fights against rural exodus or (4) Increased farming production and productivity, contributing to the economic development of local communities.

In Mexico, the mangrove areas in Nayarit state are significantly impacted by deforestation. Among the major drivers of the forestation throughout the region, it is possible to identify land use changes altering the hydrology of the region, illegal logging, anthropogenic fires, and shrimp farming, among others.  According to a previous study made for the project proponent, the state of Nayarit had a deforestation rate of 1.03%/year for the period of 2005-2015.

The Project activity is a REDD+ grouped project that aims to address the unplanned deforestation of private and ejidos’ owned wetland areas in the state of Nayarit.  Until this PD version, the grouped project is comprised of 17 project activity instances, being that each one is a wetland area inside an ejido or privately owned land.  In the future, more project activity instances, in state-owned, private or ejidos’ lands, will be added to this grouped project.

Conservation activities include reestablishing canals, maintaining canal structures, soil rehabilitation, deforestation monitoring, cessation of illegal shrimp farming and monitoring of biodiversity.

The project proponent has been engaging with communities in ejidos and private lands since 2016 under a participatory and inclusive approach and will also include more properties as the project is developed.

BlueMX is also conducting strong outreach efforts, conducting capacity building meetings, providing supporting materials in order to empower communities to carry out the conservation activities under a participatory approach integrating cultural, social and gender equity safeguards and in strict respect and transparency to landownership and access to natural resources from the rightful owners of the land.

Among the major drivers of the deforestation in the region, it is possible to identify land use changes altering the hydrology of the region, illegal logging, and anthropogenic fires.  According to a study made for the project proponent, the deforestation rate for Laguna de Términos and Petenes is 2.62%/year for the period of 2005-2016.

Conservation activities include but are not limited to reestablishing canals, maintaining canal structures, soil rehabilitation, deforestation monitoring, and monitoring of birds and mammals.

The project proponent has been engaging with communities in ejidos and private lands since 2016 under a participatory and inclusive approach and will also include more properties as the project is developed. Conservation activities include reestablishing canals, maintaining canal structures, soil rehabilitation, deforestation monitoring, and monitoring of biodiversity.

Ozinga is a leading supplier of ready-mix concrete and other concrete products primarily in the Chicago area.  Ozinga operates 70 ready mix concrete plants across Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Michigan and South Florida.  Under this project activity, Ozinga will use a combination of CO2 injection and alternative materials to develop a concrete mix that has at least a 95% reduction in cement usage, which will result in a net reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.  The specific project locations are listed in Appendix I
This project activity will produce ultra-low carbon concrete through the use of high slag replacement hydraulic cement.  As a result of the use of this product, only a fraction of the amount of ordinary Portland Cement is required compared to what is typically found in concrete. Ozinga will be able to produce a concrete that virtually eliminates the use of Portland Cement and can be used under specific applications under ASTM C1157.
Ozinga’s goal is to produce up to 750,000 cubic yards per year from its production facilities in the Midwest.  That would yield an estimated 244,000 tCO2eq reduced per year.  Throughout the crediting period, the average level of emission reductions is estimated to be 128,114 tCO2eq (given the time needed to ramp up).  In the absence of this project activity, Ozinga would use conventional concrete, as it has always done, requiring much larger amounts of cement and thus all of the emissions associated with cement production.
vcs-2986: In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, Anatolia Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Utilization Project is being implemented by Uşak Yenilenebilir Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş. The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on rooftops of educational institutions in various states of India by SAEL Limited (Previously, Sukhbir Agro Energy Ltd). All the rooftop solar panel units involved in the project are implemented under RESCO model where SAEL acts as a RESCO (Renewable Energy Service Company). Being the RESCO, SAEL has developed, installed, financed, operates and owns the rooftop solar power units and supplies power generated from the project to the consumers on whose premises the rooftop SPV panels are set up. The building owners are the customers of the power generated from the rooftop solar panels who purchase the power from SAEL Limited under long term power purchase agreements signed for 25 years.

The purchased power by the customers is either consumed/utilized by the customers for in the buildings premises or injected to the grid of the Distribution Utility under the mechanism of net metering.

Under the concept of Net Metering, the customers are charged only for the net power that they consume from the electricity service provider that has accumulated over a specific period. In other words, if their renewable energy generating systems make more electricity than consumed, they may be credited or paid for the excess electricity contributed to the grid over the same period. Net metering is also a way to increase the energy in the power grid to keep up with increase in demand during peak power use times, and this is of particular interest to states facing power shortages.

The Blue Ocean Barns - Brominata Enteric Methane Demonstration Project (“the Project”) aims to reduce enteric methane emissions from beef and dairy production systems. Asparagopsis taxiformis, a type of seaweed, has been shown to reduce enteric methane production by up to 98% when fed to cattle and, in some instances, improve feed conversion efficiency (Roque 2019, Stefenoni 2020, Kinley 2020, Roque 2021a). Blue Ocean Barns proprietary feed additive, BrominataTM, is an Asparagopsis product that will be fed to cattle as the project activity on different farms throughout the United States.

This is a grouped project that will incorporate approximately three to four project instances (i.e. beef or dairy farms) in three to four states, tentatively including California, Kansas, and Vermont. Prior to implementation of the project, none of the project farms used a feed additive or supplement to reduce enteric methane emissions. Per the methodology and consistent with a conservative approach, this project will only claim tonnes due to the reduction of enteric methane production (not improvements in feed conversion efficiency and related emission reductions), and is anticipated to reduce enteric methane emissions by approximately 835 tonnes (average) annually.
vcs-2998:
The purpose of this project is to mitigate and recover animal effluent related Greenhouse Gas (GHG) by improving the Animal Waste Management System practices in the confined animal feed operations in the cities located at the Mato Grosso do Sul state, central Brazil, developed by BRASCARBON. In Brazil the agricultural operations related to the confined animals procedures are very wide and grow progressively and intensive to attend the worldwide food demand. There are three types of Confined Animal Operation for this project: finishing, breeding and nursery. 
The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity is the same as the baseline scenario, as follows: the confined animal wastewater, which consists of fresh water mixed with manure and urine that accumulates in pits under or beside the barns, is transported to one open lagoon for evaporation, fed by gravity pipeline systems. The organic material degraded in the primary treatment lagoon is digested, thereby producing significant amounts of methane. These systems emit methane (CH4) resulting from anaerobic decomposition process. The swine livestock operations create profound environmental consequences, such as greenhouse gas emissions, odour and water/land contamination that result of storing animal waste, where this operation is not sustainable due to its sever environmental pollution.
The Project Activity consists in the construction of a new covered in-ground anaerobic reactor (digester) that will utilize the organic material currently treated in the wastewater opened lagoon, of the confined animal operations to produce biogas. All manure will be sent daily directly to digester not exceeding 24 hours in the barns.

Andes has developed a carbon dioxide (CO2) removal solution based on the action of microorganisms interacting with plant roots, which accelerate the formation of minerals (bio-mineralization) in the soil.
The company is planning to first implement this biotechnology on row crops, including corn, soybean, and wheat, in the United States. In parallel, Andes is also planning to deploy its technology in Canada and South America.

vcs-3014:
The Patagonia Region Improved Grazing Project aims to remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere by implementing improved grazing management on multiple farms in Argentina. It is a grouped project.  The initial activity instances comprise 20,123 hectares that will generate on average an estimated 24,952 tCO2e of emissions reductions annually.  It is expected ultimately to comprise >500,000 hectares and generate on average an estimated 620,000 of emissions reductions annually. Improved grazing will increase the rest and rotation on pastures above baseline practices and reduce unrestricted grazing by livestock. Pastures will be grazed with higher livestock densities followed by longer periods of rest, increasing both plant productivity and soil carbon inputs relative to baseline conditions. This results in the sequestration of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere to the soil. 
Land operators are provided funding to increase fencing and water access needed to create more and smaller pastures and to provide the added labor needed to manage more frequent livestock movements. Project participants are required to manage for concentrated animal impact on small pastures with a focus on extended rest periods allowing for regrowth and recovery of leaf tissue, seed establishment, and replenishment of root reserves. In the baseline scenario, the pastures are larger and the livestock movement among pastures is less frequent. This allows grazing animals to select for preferred perennial species, which then become overgrazed and insufficient rest periods favor the encroachment by shrubs, annual grasses, and larger occurrence of bare ground.
The grouped project is on eligible grasslands of Argentina. The project area consists of grassland grazed by livestock on participating farms. Soils throughout the project area are primarily coarse-textured sand to sandy loam and have been losing carbon for over 100 years due to the continuous, selective grazing under the baseline scenario. Consequently, soils in the project area are modelled to have a high potential to store carbon under intensive, high rotation grazing management.
vcs-3015:

Planned grazing will increase the rest and rotation on pastures above baseline practices and reduce unrestricted grazing by livestock. Pastures will be grazed with higher livestock densities followed by longer periods of rest, increasing both plant productivity and soil carbon inputs relative to baseline conditions. This results in the sequestration of greenhouse gasses from the atmosphere to the soil.
Land operators are provided funding to increase fencing and water infrastructure needed to create more and smaller pastures and to provide the added labor needed to manage more frequent livestock movements. Project participants are required to manage for concentrated animal impact on small pastures with a focus on extended rest periods allowing for regrowth and recovery of leaf tissue, seed establishment, and replenishment of root reserves. In the baseline scenario, the pastures are larger and the livestock movement among pastures is less frequent. This allows grazing animals to select for preferred perennial species, which then become overgrazed and insufficient rest periods favor the encroachment by shrubs, annual grasses, and larger occurrence of bare ground.
The grouped project is on eligible grasslands and parts of Wyoming, Idaho, Washington, North Dakota, and South Dakota. The project area consists of grassland grazed by livestock on participating ranches. Soils throughout the project area are predominantly a mix of sandy and silty clay loams and have been losing carbon for over 100 years due to the continuous, selective grazing under the baseline scenario. Consequently, soils in the project area are modeled to have a high potential to store carbon under intensive, high rotation grazing management.
vcs-3016:
Guoyang MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Wangqiao Village, Chudian Town, Guoyang County, Bozhou City, Anhui Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Guoyang Baichang Renewable Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Guoyang MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Guoyang landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
Guoyang landfill site is located in Wangqiao Village, Chudian Town, Guoyang County, Bozhou City. The project has a total designed capacity 4MW (8*500kW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project started construction in December 2019 and started operation on 18/01/2021. 
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Guoyang landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. 
The total power generation during the crediting period is estimated to be 127,526 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 62,295 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the ECPG.
vcs-3017:
Jiangsu REO-ECO PET Recycling Project (hereafter referred to as the Project, or the proposed project) is located in No. 28, Nanhai Road, Hongze Economic Development Zone, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province, P.R. China. 
The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Jiangsu REO-ECO New Material Tech Co., Ltd (hereafter referred to as the Project proponents). The objective of the Project is to collect the waste plastic and utilize it to product Food-grade Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET).
In the Project, the Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) residues will be sorted, classified, washed with hot water, dried, compacted, pelletized, and then used as raw materials for production of PET. Prior to the implementation of the Project, the PET residues in municipal solid waste (MSW) were deposited in a disposal site.
The Project recycled PET from (MSW), and then process them into intermediate products, which displacing the production of virgin materials in dedicated facilities, thereby resulting in avoidance of energy use and the related emissions.
The total quantity of PET recycled during the operation period is estimated to be 30,000 tons per year. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the Project over the crediting period is 10,247tCO2e per year by avoiding energy consumption.
vcs-3018: A forest carbon credit project to create greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions and removals by converting privately owned operational forest lands to protected forest lands. The project will be implemented following the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VM0012 – Improved Forest Management in Temperate and Boreal Forests (LtPF), v1.2 methodology. This grouped project aims to reforest and restore degraded agricultural lands by planting Pongamia trees. Reforestation started in 2018, through the planting of 100 to 145 Pongamia  trees per acre (250 to 360 trees per hectare, approximately). The project aims to increase the Pongamia plantation area to 1,000 ha and certify carbon offsets for a period of 20 years following the small-scale afforestation and reforestation methodology (VCS - AR-AMS0007). 
Regenerative agriculture is a system of growing food that reverses climate change by revitalizing natural ecosystems and agricultural lands while improving water quality and soil biodiversity. It improves the health of soils capable of producing high quality, nutrient dense food. Currently, the project areas are in a high state of degradation due to intensive agriculture practices. Although the project represents an intervention on the ground, it favors the increase and recovery of land that enhances the possibility of connecting fragments of forest, reducing fertilization use and providing an additional source of income to the landowners.

vcs-3020: Dongyang Wastewater Treatment Plant Project is located in Dongyang City, Zhejiang Province, China. vcs-3021: The proposed project aims to reduce gas leaks from components through the implementation of an advanced Leak Detection and Repair Program in gas infrastructure systems operated by Titas Gas Transmission Distribution Company Limited (Titas) in the People’s Republic of Bangladesh. vcs-3023:
The Project BONOS DE LA RUTA SIAN KA'AN is situated in the Ejido Caoba (The Ejido) in the southern state of Quintana Roo State, Mexico. Ecology-wise, the Project is in the Central American portion of Mexico, bordering the country of Belize. This zone has an important tropical forest corridor. 
Ejido Caoba contains a significant forestry mass; its production area covers 30,000 ha of medium evergreen tropical forest, low evergreen tropical forest, savannahs, and deciduous tropical forest. From which 7,905 ha are destined for conservation and restricted use. Use of the tropical forest carried out by Ejido members dates back to the 19th century, and it is legally represented in the form of forestry concessions on national land, part of a whole organizational process linked to the sustainable use and management of tropical forestry resources. 
In 2013, Ejido Caoba was the first one in Mexico to obtain the International Certification for Good Practices and Operations in Forest Management and the Chain of Custody (CoC) Certification of Forest Stewardship Council (FSC). Today with the Project BONOS DE LA RUTA SIAN KA'AN, in English Carbon Credits of the Gate of Heaven, The Ejido aims to reach a new pivot point with its forestry management. Ejido Caoba decided to generate carbon credits through the removals of greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) by the VM0003 Methodology for Improved Forest Management through Extension of Rotation Age Version 1.2, Sectoral Scope 14. 
The Project began in October 2017 and will have an expected duration of 30 years; during this period, the removal of 20,835,260 tCO2e is expected through the implementation of activities related to four strategic lines: strengthening of governance, alternative productive projects, recovery and rehabilitation of tropical forest, and above-ground biomass monitoring.
vcs-3024:
Puwangzi Afforestation Project (hereafter refer to as “the project”) is located within Pu’an county, Wangmo county in Qianxinan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture and Ziyun county in Anshun city, Guizhou Province of China. It is an inland province, bordering Yunnan to the west, Sichuan to the northwest, Hunan to the east and Chongqing to the North. The province has a total population of 34 million. The project aims to plant native species on suitable land for forest  for GHG removal whilst contributing to local sustainable development goals.
25,901 ha (388,515 Mu ) of forest was planted on suitable land for forest in Pu’an county, Wangmo county in and Ziyun county which used to be poor sustainable ecological environment and karst rocky desertification. Prior to the project, the project area was suitable land for forest, there is no forestry management and the coverage by planting trees is low, and there has never been any activity affecting the local ecosystem . By checking the afforestation plan with the forestry bureau of Qianxinan and Anshun, it was confirmed that, a small number of trees have been planted in some project area before the project started, but the coverage by planting trees is low. So considering the low forest coverage, the forestry bureau of Qianxinan and Anshun determined that the project area is suitable for afforestation after investigation, then the local forestry bureau approved the supplementary planting without disturbing the existing trees in January 2019 to increase the vegetative cover.
vcs-3025:
CSD Wastewater Treatment Plant Project in Hebei Province is located in Hebei Province, China. The project includes five sewage treatment plants. The whole aerobic process includes pre-treatment process, secondary biological treatment process, tertiary deep treatment process and sludge treatment process, with a maximum design influent flow of 210,000 m3/d (The total amount of five sewage treatment plants), the influent and effluent COD concentration are 850 mg/L and 50 mg/L, separately. The wastewater is composed of industrial wastewater and some domestic wastewater within the service area. The project can reduce environmental pollution and destroy methane emissions from the open anaerobic lagoons in baseline scenario, the best available low-cost solution for wastewater treatment.
Emission reductions of this project are generated by reducing methane emissions of the open anaerobic lagoons in baseline scenario. The project started construction on February 2020 and put into operation in December 2020. The project put into test run from 18/12/2020 to 04/01/2021. The earliest official operational date of the five treatment plants is January 1, 2021, and the project began official operation on January 1, 2021.

vcs-303: Maharashtra faces a demand-supply gap which may be directly attributable to the growth in industrial activity as well as lack of investment in power projects.
