vcs-3045:
The proposed group project seeks to increase access of households and communities to improved cookstoves by disseminating high thermal efficiency and low greenhouse gas emitting cooking stoves known as Improved Cook Stoves (ICS) to the rural and urban households of Uganda. Their old low efficiency and high greenhouse gas emitting stoves would be replaced. The implementation of this group VCS project, through implementation of several instances, will result in the reduction of biomass/fuelwood consumption & consequent emissions from combustion leading to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases, conservation of forests and woodlands as well as improved health conditions of ICS users due to improved indoor air quality along with drudgery reduction in everyday cooking.
The individual households using ICS will sign an agreement/waive their carbon rights  with the project proponent acknowledging the inclusion of their stoves through instances under this group VCS project.
 
With respect to each instance, the implementer may potentially distribute information about the benefits of undertaking such group activity including its associated economic, social and environmental benefits. This will help in creating awareness amongst interested stakeholders.
PERSISTENTCLIMATE INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED, (herein after called “PersistentClimate”) is the project proponent (“PP”) for the project activity. Persistent Climate is a company registered in India and will facilitate the distribution of the ICS to households of Uganda.

Persistent Climate through its partner in Host Country will coordinate with the users of ICS directly or through local partners or its representative to ensure that all requirements with respect to project activity, such as assisting with validation and registration, record keeping, monitoring and survey of households at a regular interval are met.
vcs-3046: In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, Batman Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Utilization Project is being implemented by Anahtar Enerji Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi. The purpose of the project is to capture and utilize landfill gas for power generation.  The new gas extraction and utilization systems have been installed by the project owner. Before the implementation of the project activity, landfill gas that was captured and utilized by the project was emitted into the atmosphere directly. The project is located in Merkez District in the city of Batman, in southeast of Turkey. The waste deposition at the landfill in Batman is carried out since 2005.  The project activity is a Methane Gas Power Generating Plant with an installed capacity of 3,12 MWe. The project was commissioned  with generation of electricity from October 30th, 2020, which is regarded as the project start date. For the purpose of a sustainable waste management in which domestic wastes will be evaluated, it is planned to rehabilitate the Batman Solid Waste Disposal Site that receives around 127,750 tons/year, corresponding to an average of 350 tons per day of municipal waste coming from districts of Batman province and to generate renewable electricity power from landfill gas and the rehabilitation project was approved by the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization in Turkey. This project adopts a crediting period of 7 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 59,642 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 417,494  tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its first crediting period.
vcs-3047: The project introduces 6 sets of aerobic composting systems to treat the swine manure from Fangyuan swine farm, Liancheng swine farm, Longwang swine farm, Wangxin swine farm, Nanyang Zhuangzhuang Swine farm and Nanyang Pangpang swine farm in Fangcheng county, Nanyang city, Henan Province, China. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of swine manure.
vcs-3049: The primary objective of the Rio Preto REDD+ Project is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) of the 2,295 ha project area, consisting 100% of Amazon rainforest. The project area is located within 2 private properties in Nova Marilândia and Santo Afonso municipalities, in the State of Mato Grosso. The present REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 344.74 ha of deforestation, equating to 87,739 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (29-May-2019 to 28-May-2049), with an annual average of 2,925 tCO2e. Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities.
vcs-305: The project activity is a 4.5 MW wind power project consisting of 6 WEGs of 750 kW capacity each. The emission reductions from the project over the crediting period would be around 88,200 tonnes of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e).
vcs-3050:
Current research established nine planetary boundaries to define the environmental limits within which humanity can safely operate. Within those, two core boundaries — climate change and biosphere integrity — have been highlighted, each of which has the potential to drive the Earth system into a new state should they be substantially and persistently transgressed (Rockström et al., 2009; Steffen et al., 2015).
Inspired by a call of action, Maraui Program was designed to act upon the two wicked problems — Climate Change & Biodiversity Loss. Maraui Program intends to halt GHG emissions by avoiding ecosystem conversion while protecting Biodiversity. Furthermore, such a program aims to aid in a range of pressing issues, from preserving Freshwater Resources to improving Traditional Communities’ livelihood. 
The Program is a grouped project - as per VCS definition - located in the states of Piauí and Maranhão, Brazil. Owners of rich Biodiversity, Piauí and Maranhão states are home to one of the most intense agricultural frontiers of the country and are the most poverty-stricken states - the lowest average income in Brazil (IBGE, 2021). At the issuance of this document, one Project Activity Instance (PAI) has been instituted, Fazenda Boqueirão (27,458.29 hectares).
vcs-3052:
The proposed project aims at improving the quality of drinking water through dissemination of low green gas emitting safe drinking water purifier (SDWP) to provide clean drinking water for households in Kingdom of Cambodia. For this reason, this proposed project activity will avoid the use of thermal energy and/or low energy and associated emissions.
The project activity targets households in communities with no previous water purifiers access. The geographical boundary is in Cambodia. Water purifiers are distributed free of cost to user. Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company (SIPCO) financed the implementation of the project in full.
vcs-3053:
This project activity aims at the farmers and the farming communities to enable them adopt improved agricultural practices such as crop residue management for enhancing their crop productivity and sequester CO2 in the soil. The project activity is located in five different states of India – Bihar, Punjab, Maharashtra , Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh. 
The farmers involved in this project activity are small and marginal who are vulnerable from the impacts of climate change. A heavy dependence on chemical synthetic inorganic nitrogen fertilizers, post-harvest crop residue burning and disturbance of soil through intense tilling operations have led to severe degradation of the cropland soils. It has also made the agricultural system not only vulnerable to the impacts of climate change but also a major contributor to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions can be reduced.
vcs-3055: The ITAÚBA REDD+ PROJECT aims at protecting forests in one of the regions having the highest deforestation trends in the Amazon Biome, in the municipalities of Itaúba and Marcelândia. Both the municipalities are inside the “Arc of Deforestation” and since the colonization of the municipalities, besides the damage caused to natural ecosystems, several social conflicts have emerged from the dynamics of unsustainable land use, associated with the extensive deforestation and degradation activities. Throughout time, communities with livelihoods based on family-scale agriculture and forest resources were expulsed from the region and gave place to  large scale agricultural and pasture activities.  For the project period, the baseline scenario for the Project Area indicates that the historical patterns of change in land-use would be reproduced: extensive deforestation and systematic conversion from forest to soy crops and pasture areas for cattle ranching, far above the limits stablished by the Brazilian Forest Code. The project activities are designed to avoid the deforestation drivers that would realize the referred baseline in the without project scenario, with the long-term vision of restoring the relation of local communities of rural workers with the forest areas and contribute with the transition to socioeconomic scenario build on bioeconomy principles. With project activity approval, the proponents intend to improve the mechanisms of remote and in loco surveillance, as well as implement activities that will result in other climate, community, and biodiversity benefits.
vcs-3056:
The purpose of BRASCARBON Methane Recovery Project BCA-BRA-17 project is to utilize the effluent produced on a total of 7 pig farms in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, in Brazil, to capture methane and generate biogas. The projects have the potential to generate energy from waste using the biogas produced and captured. Energy derived from this process is used to power onsite electricity within each of these projects.
Before the project activity, local farmers considered waste as an externality in the pig production process. As such, minimal finance was allocated to this issue and wastewater was often treated in open water lagoons – frequently with profound environmental impacts. The projects demonstrate how the construction of a set of new, covered, in-ground anaerobic digesters can utilize the organic material from the animal operations to produce biogas and fertilizer, whilst reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The   basis   of   the   projects   is   the   anaerobic   digestion, whereby microorganisms break down biodegradable material in the absence of oxygen. As part of an integrated waste management system, anaerobic digestion reduces the emission of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and produces a rich biogas, suitable for energy production, which can be used to replace fossil fuels. The nutrient-rich solids left after digestion are used as fertilizer and the better wastewater management allows more water for irrigation.
vcs-3057:
In Mexico, the mangrove areas in the state of Veracruz are significantly impacted by deforestation.  Among the major drivers of the deforestation in the region, it is possible to identify illegal firewood harvesting, logging, dredging, and real estate development.

According to a previous study made for the project proponent, the average deforestation rate in the state of Veracruz is 1.07% for the period of 2005-2015, while in Alvarado region, within this same state, it was 1.5%/year for the same period.

The Project activity is a REDD+ grouped project that intents to address the unplanned deforestation of wetlands in the state of Veracruz.  Currently, there are 37 project activity instances, each one encompassing wetland areas within ejidos or private land.  In the future, more project activity instances, inside state-owned, private or ejidos’ lands, will be added to this grouped project.

Conservation activities include, but are not limited to, reestablishing canals, maintaining canal structures, soil rehabilitation, deforestation monitoring, and monitoring of biodiversity.

The project proponent has been engaging with communities in ejidos and private lands since 2016 under a participatory and inclusive approach and will also include more properties as the project is developed.  BlueMX is also conducting capacity building sessions and developing outreach and communication materials to empower communities to carry out the conservation activities.

The grouped project totals 4,903 hectares of wetlands and is estimated to reduce approximately 65,946 t CO2e per year.

The Project area is not covered by any jurisdictional REDD+ program.

BlueMX is also designing the project for certifying climate, community, and biodiversity benefits under the CCB Programme.
vcs-3058:
Jiayu MSW Landfill Site LFG Pollution Treatment and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Jiayu County MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Jiayu landfill site), in Danushan Village, Guanqiao Town, Jiayu County, Hubei Province, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Jiayu County BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd.
Jiayu landfill site started collecting and handling waste in 2014.
The project started to construct on 15/08/2021. The project has a total designed capacity 0.5MW (1*0.5MW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period will be 32,025MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reductions of the project is 19,169tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 191,691tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.
Scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project (the same as baseline scenario):
LFG from Jiayu landfill site is emitted to the atmosphere directly.
Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the CCPG, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants.
vcs-3059:
The purpose of this Grouped project “Replacement of ICLs with LED lamps in Gujarat, India” is to reduce fossil-fuel based electricity consumption in the Rural households of Gujarat by introducing more energy efficient LED lamps to replace incandescent lightbulbs (“ICLs”), This would result in reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. 

The overall penetration of LED in India is still at a nascent stage with rural India favoring conventional power guzzlers over CFLs and LED lightbulbs. Other barriers include reluctance to accept change, uncertainty about performance and lack of trust.
The ordinary incandescent bulb is extremely energy inefficient for lighting when compared to LED. An ICL bulb requires 60 watts of power to emit around 700 lumens of light whereas LED bulb can emit 700 lumen by consuming just 9 watts. About 95% of the energy in LEDs is converted into light, and only 5% is wasted as heat. Despite being inefficient, ICLs are the most preferred option. The Rwanda Riparian Restoration Project is restoring riparian buffer zones in key watersheds and catchment areas within the mountainous areas of Rwanda. These buffer zones serve a critical ecological function as the interface between sensitive upland areas and the water resources that they buffer. The project is using select species of sympodial (clumping) bamboos. These planted bamboo clumps have an intricate underground root system that binds fragile soils and reduces erosion and loss of top soil from sloping agricultural lands. In addition this root system reduces siltation, protecting water resources for downstream users. The multi-dimensional bamboo canopy further serves to reduce the rate and volume of flow of rainfall into rivers reducing flooding, and protecting river banks. 

The planted bamboo is purely for conservation and environmental purposes, while having high carbon emission removal benefits as a permanent and carbon rich ecosystem.

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in the southwest of Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, China, with a total acreage of 19,507 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase, and less methane emission reduction than the continuously flooded.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir construction, pumps and valves installation, training, etc. According to the needs of rice growth, farmers use pumps and valves to control irrigation and drainage, which not only saves water resources but also reduces methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions. Through the pumps and valves, the necessary water can be supplied to the rice paddies in time in the dry season, and the excess water can be drained from the rice paddies in the rainy season. In this case, the methane emission can be declined by an average of 48%. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction of 3.06 tCO2e/ha for rice.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 417,515 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,645 tCO2e. The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes, increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standards of local farmers and provide more job opportunities.

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, China, with a total acreage of 19,067 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline 
scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase, and less methane emission reduction than the continuously flooded.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir construction, pumps and valves installation, training, etc. According to the needs of rice growth, farmers use pumps and valves to control irrigation and drainage, which not only saves water resources but also reduces methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions. Through the pumps and valves, the necessary water can be supplied to the rice paddies in time in the dry season, and the excess water can be drained from the rice paddies in the rainy season. In this case, the methane emission can be declined by an average of 48%. Hence, with the proposed project activity, the estimated GHG reduction from rice is 3.09 tCO2e/ha.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 412,951 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 58,993 tCO2e. The project aims to reduce GHG and mitigate climate changes, increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standards of local farmers and provide more job opportunities.

The clean cooking project involves the distribution of improved cookstoves (ICSs) among local communities based in some areas of Ivory Coast, where currently several households still rely on inefficient and pollutant traditional cooking techniques. The project aims to replace the traditional cooking mechanisms used by local people (i.e. three-stone fire or rudimental stoves) with ICSs that require less fuel and decrease the biomass combustion’s emissions, with a consequent reduction of health hazard coming from the indoor smoke pollution. The introduction of more efficient stoves will help to limit the demand for woody biomass, reducing the unsustainable use of forests and halting deforestation that is progressing rapidly in the Country. The improved cookstoves’ deployment will also have a positive impact on women’ life, reducing the time they spend for collecting woody biomass and cooking the meals, giving them the possibility to invest their time in a more effective way.
Through the implementation of engagement and training processes dedicated to the local communities involved in the project, all the households receiving the ICS will be aware of the environmental improvements and the carbon finance benefit generated by their effective use of the stove.
This project will be developed in Ivory Coast. The areas of implementation will be the North-Central portion of the Country, considering in particular the districts of Savanes, Woroba, Vallée du Bandama, Zanzan, Sassandra-Marahoué, Lacs and Yamoussoukro.
The first project instances will be around 100.000 cookstoves delivered to the local communities, with an annual average emission reductions close to 110,000 tCO2e

India is one of the world's largest producers of rice and exporter of rice in the world. Rice cultivation is the most important agricultural operation in India, not only in terms of food security but also in terms of livelihood and plays a major part in the economy. It is a known fact that rice fields emit methane into the environment that contributes to global warming.
The project plans to promote improved water management practices in rice cultivation instead of using the traditional practice of continuously flooded irrigation. AWD/DSR are proven methods to reduce methane emission by as much as 48% compared to flooded conditions where large amounts of methane (CH4) gets generated because of anaerobic decomposition. This project is expected to generate important co-benefits of reducing water usage during rice cultivation, decrease pest and disease attacks, improve soil health etc. Further they are also beneficial for reduced cost of cultivation for small land holders.
In the first instance, the project is planned to be implemented in 8,112 hectares in Punjab and Haryana States.  During the project implementation, relevant technical training and advisory was provided for the farmers to help them conduct AWD/DSR during rice cultivation.
The total GHG emissions reductions due to the implementation of the project activity is estimated to be 380,225  tCO2e over 7 years.

The Foam Stabilized Base and Emulsion Asphalt Mixture Pavement Project (herein “project”) supports pavement designers across the United States in replacing hot mix asphalt (HMA) with foam stabilized base (FSB) and/or emulsion asphalt in pavement projects. Prior to implementing project methods, pavement designers often default to using energy-intensive mining, hauling, and high temperature material manufacturing practices associated with HMA. These industry standard activities unnecessarily destroy habitats, release carbon dioxide (CO2), and release volatile organic compounds (VOC).
This project reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting activities throughout the pavement application lifecycle. The project reduces dependence on the mining of virgin aggregate, reduces transportation of raw materials to mix plants, eliminates high-temperature asphalt manufacturing and, in the case of in-place pavement recycling, eliminates mix-plant to job-site transportation. The project replaces virgin aggregate with reclaimed asphalt pavement.
The project is conducted under VCS methodology VM0039, “Methodology for Use of Foam Stabilized Base and Emulsion Asphalt Mixtures in Pavement Application” and uses Pave Next, a web-based computer-aided-design (CAD) application, to help pavement designers compare carbon emissions between traditional and sustainable designs with similar structural properties. The project could reduce CO2 emissions by roughly 87 lb CO2 per ton of HMA replaced by FSB (or 39.46 kg CO2 per ton of material; Liu et al 2017). For example,  if a project uses 180,000 metric tonnes of FSB in place of HMA it reduces emissions for a CO2e savings of roughly 7,000 metric tonnes, or 7,000 Verified Carbon Unit (VCU) credits generated. Project instances will be added under a single Project Description as allowed by Verra. Other similar Project Descriptions may also be developed with other project proponents.

The proposed grouped project activity aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by distributing fuel- efficient Improved Cook Stoves in various districts Madagascar. Most of the people living are in region dependent on firewood and charcoal as source of cooking fuel. Forest provides around 92%12 of energy requirements in the form of firewood and charcoal. People in the rural areas collect firewood to meet the cooking energy needs nationwide. Most of the households in the city and some in rural area purchase their cooking fuel from the market. Burning firewood or charcoal not only leads to significant greenhouse gas emission but also leads to increased expenditure for buying the fuel and also increased time spent on collecting the firewood. In addition to this, firewood collection and charcoal production leads to increased deforestation and environmental degradation.
The access to clean fuel and technologies to the Malagasy households is around 0.91%34. Renewable energy usage for cooking still lies dormant in Madagascar with less than 1% of renewable energy available to the end users5 and fuel wood6 is mainly the source of fire for cooking at households. Around 82.2% of people in Republic of Madagascar are still dependent of firewood as fuel for cooking. With over 70% of people living in vulnerable situations firewood is the source of fuel to the rural households while charcoal stands as the source of most energy used in the urban regions of the country for cooking purposes7. 91% of the rural population still depends on firewood (using both purchased wood and wood picked up) against 45% in urban areas. As for the baseline scenario on how the fuel is being used, large proportion of the households in the country depend on traditional cookers, viz., “3- stones or triangle iron” or “toko”. The target population continues the use of non- renewable wood fuel to meet their thermal energy needs which includes cooking also. The project aims to replace old traditional cookstoves

The main goal of this project is changing continuously flooded irrigation to intermittent flooded irrigation in rice cultivation in Wuhua County, Meizhou City, Guangdong Province of China. Wuhua County is located in east of Guangdong Province. The project includes 8 towns, namely Hengpo Town, Guotian Town, Shuanghua Town, Anliu Town, Mianyang Town, Meilin Town, Huayang town and Longcun town, with total double-cropping rice area is approximately 14,252 ha. Since lack of financial support, it is very difficult to change irrigation method by local farmers. Therefore, the baseline scenario should be recognized as continuously flooded irrigation situation. Due to the anaerobic decomposition, a large amount of CH4 will be produced during continuously flooded irrigation. In contrast, rice paddies intermittently submerged and dried so that the upper soil layers switch from anaerobic to aerobic conditions several times during the crop growing season in intermittent flooded method. Moreover, the intermittent flooded method brings many benefits, such as the higher rice yield production, the higher methane removal rate, etc.
In project area, every farmer who owns rice paddy field is regarded as an individual unit. With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation. During intermittent flooded irrigation, the controllable irrigation and drainage system will be applied, which can not only save water resources but also reduce methane emission in anaerobic condition (in flooded phase).

The Project is a biogas-to-energy project that generates renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by Babil Biyogaz Enerji Sistemleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi, as the project owner, Eyyübiye district, Şanlıurfa province, in Turkey.

Cattle and chicken manure which are generated at farms and left to decay in anaerobic conditions, are collected daily through special sewage trucks equipped with close tanks to prevent any odour and/or manure leakages and to be fed into the anaerobic digesters at the proposed biogas power plant. 

The project has received Electricity Generation License (EGL) issued by the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EMRA) in Turkey on October 22nd, 2020, for the maximum operational licensed capacity of 4.68 MWe/h.

The project has become operational by starting to generate electricity and feeding it directly to the Turkish national grid on October 31st, 2020. 

The manure which is supplied to the proposed project plant is coming from around 50,000 cattle and 1,800,000 chicken living at the farms daily which are fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site.

The project has obtained the approval of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) issued by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization, and Climate Change in Turkey on September 17th, 2020. 

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 417,287 tCO2eq/y.

vcs-3137: The main goal of this project is changing continuously flooded irrigation to intermittent flooded irrigation in rice cultivation in the south of Wuhua County, Meizhou City, Guangdong Province of China. Wuhua County is located in east of Guangdong Province. The project includes 4 towns, namely Mianyang Town, Meilin Town, Huayang town and Longcun town, with total double-cropping rice area is approximately 7,127.43ha. Since lack of financial support, it is very difficult to change irrigation method by local farmers. Therefore, the baseline scenario should be recognized as continuously flooded irrigation situation. Due to the anaerobic decomposition, a large amount of CH4 will be produced during continuously flooded irrigation. In contrast, rice paddies intermittently submerged and dried so that the upper soil layers switch from anaerobic to aerobic conditions several times during the crop growing season in intermittent flooded method. Moreover, the intermittent flooded method brings many benefits, such as the higher rice yield production, the higher methane removal rate, etc. In project area, every farmer who owns rice paddy field is regarded as an individual unit. With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation. During intermittent flooded irrigation, the controllable irrigation and drainage system will be applied, which can not only save water resources but also reduce methane emission in anaerobic condition (in flooded phase).

The WARG Project is an initiative led by Carbon Credits Consulting SRL and a group of landowners in the state of Acre to protect multiple parcels of precious native forest. The project gives landowners with small and medium sized properties the opportunity to participate in a REDD+ project which will bring biodiversity, community, and climate benefits to their land.
The project areas are in the region known as the Amazon deforestation arc and are located in a region of high conversion rates from original forest habitat to pasture and/or large areas of agricultural crops. 
The Brazilian economy in the south of the Amazonian regions, has been based based on native forest clearing to allow cattle-ranching, often without appropriate management technologies. Considering the infertile soil in the Amazon Forest, its exposure to the weather, and to little improvement in agricultural technology the region is hampered by low productivity, leading to increasing deforestation to ensure profitability. 
The WARG project intends to deliver significant improvements in the area’s monitoring, with remote sensing technology implementation to identify any signs of modification in the Project Area and surroundings, in addition to training staff for field monitoring. The project will also be implementing satellite wildfire detection systems and teams of fire fighters to detect fires early before they reach an unmanageable size.
The project is expected to avoid the emission of 3,620,766 tCO2eq in the first 10 years. The actual project area is 60,000 ha of native forest divided in 22 properties, with an ambitious target for continuous expansion to a total area of 500,000 ha.
Finally, the project has been protecting the Brazilian Big Five which include the giant anteater, the giant armadillo, the maned wolf, the puma, and the jaguar on top of a multitude of other endangered animal and plant species.

Mozambique hosts some of the largest intact mangrove forests in Africa, with more than 60% located along the coastal stretches of Zambezia and Sofala provinces. Over the past three decades, however, more than 30,000 hectares have been lost, primarily due to anthropogenic pressures. This degradation has led to soil erosion, reduced coastal protection, declining fish stocks, and significant biodiversity loss. In response, the MozBlue project aims to restore over 30,000 hectares of degraded mangroves across Zambezia and Sofala.

Phase 1 of MozBlue, developed by Blue Forest in collaboration with Removall and financed by Removall and Sumitomo Corporation, will restore 5,116 hectares, with an estimated carbon sequestration potential of 2.64 million tons of CO₂ over a 60-year period.

Restoration sites have been identified through remote sensing and validated through ground-truthing, and will be implemented in line with Wetlands Restoration and Conservation guidelines. The project will mobilize local restoration experts to plant native mangrove species and engage surrounding communities to monitor and maintain restored areas throughout the project’s lifetime.

vcs-3155: This is the first Blue Carbon Project of Niger Delta Mangroves. It is a grouped project whose expansion region includes all the mangrove forests present in the Niger Delta in Nigeria. This project is aiming at restoring and sustainably managing the Niger Delta mangroves. Niger Delta mangroves together with the creeks and rivers are a major source of food and livelihood for about 30 million people, which represents more than 17% of Nigeria's population. Other ecosystem services provided by this unique environment are flood control, ground water re-fill, reservoir of biodiversity, fuel wood, cultural values etc. This ecosystem also plays important role in climate change mitigation because of its high blue carbon sequestration potential. Mangroves constitute important nurseries for fishes, crustaceans, sponges, algae and other invertebrates, and also acts as a sink, retaining pollutants from contaminated tidal water. Mangroves are also used as shelter and breeding grounds by small mammals, shore birds, reptiles, and insects. Unfortunately, this unique ecosystem is on the decline and at the verge of been totally lost. Mangrove forests are converted to farmlands and the trees are cut for timber, fuel, house construction and so on. Consequently, many coastal communities in the Niger Delta are losing their lives and primary livelihoods due to increased vulnerability to floods as a result of the disappearance of mangroves which usually serve as defense in times of coastal flooding. They are also now exposed to the high intensity of sunlight and heat waves as the land lay bare of trees to regulate sun rays. There is an urgent need to restore/conserve the mangroves of Niger Delta region. Hence the main objective of the project is sequestration of greenhouse gases (GHGs) through planting activities.

Yantai Xinhao Swine Farm Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to swine farms in Yadi village, Muping District, Yantai City, Shandong Province, China, which are owned by Yantai Xinhao agriculture and animal husbandry Co., Ltd (hereinafter called” Xinhao”). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater from the swine farm to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
In this project, AWMS is built to replace the traditional open anaerobic lagoons, and swine farm installed one AWMS. The manure and waster will be collected into the anaerobic digesters and then biogas generated during the anaerobic treatment process will be captured and total 1,450*104 m3 biogas are expected to be generated annually. Biogas is then sent into biogas boilers for heat production. Every biogas boiler has been installed in each swine farms. All of the heat generated are used by AWMSs and the swine farms, while the rest (if any) will be burned. The sludge produced after fermentation is applied to corn fields as fertilizer, and the wastewater produced by anaerobic biogas digesters is used for agricultural irrigation. 
Benefited from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMSs and the swine farm. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system, and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed. 
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 105,655 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 739,585 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

Before 2018， they were all forests which the trees could be logged and sold once reached the cutting rotation age based on a timber harvest plan. After 2017, they are all converted to protected forests. The Hangzhou Chaoteng Energy Technology Co., Ltd is in charge of applying VCS project.
The project activity is to protect the previously harvested forests. Community residents can become our employees, and their job is to protect the forest. The local forestry bureau can supervise the implementation of the project and ensure that there is no commercial logging in our project. In addition, organizations in the community and all sectors of society can supervise our project and make complaints and suggestions through the risk control department.
The purpose of strata is to improve accuracy and reduce the sampling cost. The strata are usually based on the tree species, age and canopy density, but it does not mean all these factors should be considered for all projects, more strata mean more workload and cost. For this project, the factor of species for strata could reduce the variation within the same stratum and reach the accuracy level of 90% under certain degree of freedom. So the strata are reasonable and feasible. All the subcompartments are divided into 3 strata based on the tree species.

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Changlinyan within Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province of China, with a total acreage of 20,012 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction than the continuously flooded.
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results in not only large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method, which shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%1 . Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 2.92 tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 409,493 tCO2e in the first 7 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 58,499tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes;
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers;
- Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by replacing continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, this method can reduce the flooded time of rice in the whole growth cycle and the methane (CH4) emissions, and is more beneficial to production increase than the continuously flooded as well. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario

vcs-3195:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Jinyujie within Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province of China, with a total acreage of 20,027 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction than the continuously flooded.
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results in not only large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method, which shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%1 . Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 2.92 tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 409,794 tCO2e in the first 7 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 58,542tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes;
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers;
- Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.
vcs-3196: The Paracel ARR Carbon Forestry Project (ID 3196) in northeastern Paraguay combines afforestation, reforestation, and native ecosystem restoration to generate high-quality Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) while promoting biodiversity and social development. The project rehabilitates lands degraded by agriculture and cattle ranching, establishing eucalyptus plantations for kraft pulp alongside the restoration of Cerrado savannas and degraded forests. Paracel manages 195.548 ha, with the first project activity instance (PAI-1) covering 35.764 ha, of which 23.827 ha are eligible. From 2019–2021, 8.382 ha were planted and verified, achieving 192.219 tCO₂e removals after buffer deductions. Over its 50-year crediting period, PAI-1 is expected to remove 7,16 million tCO₂e and issue approximately 2,54 million VCUs. Beyond climate benefits, the project generates more than 1.100 jobs, supports local communities with health, water, and infrastructure initiatives, and actively restores ecosystems, including up to 15.800 ha of savannas and 66.000 ha of degraded forests. By integrating productive forestry with conservation and social investments, Paracel offers a landscape-scale model for sustainable development in Paraguay.
vcs-3197: The project will donate high efficiency Jiko Kisasa improved cookstoves to local residents in Kenya. The improved cookstove will replace the low efficiency three stone or traditional stove, which will contribute to lower GHG emissions and better indoor air quality. The project will also save wood fuel for decreasing the deforestation and protecting the biodiversity in Kenya.
vcs-3198:
The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Burundi. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 
Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Burundi. It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. Each household will receive up to 2 ICS per household. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Burundi but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.
The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance which in turn is used for subsidising the price of ICS and for recovering project implementation costs.

vcs-32: Luara Ceramic is a small and prototypical red ceramic, located in the southeast of Brazil, which produces primarily blocks and other structural ceramic devices, for the market in Campo Grande of the Mato Grosso do Sul state. The industry possesses one Round kiln and one Paulista kiln to produce approximately 550,000 ceramic devices per month. In order to supply the heat necessary to cook its products, it maintains a temperature of 900ºC for 24 hours in both kilns. The fuel that was used was native wood extracted from the nearby Cerrado forest. The practice has led to the deforestation of this very crucial biome that is located in the southern region of Mato Grosso do Sul. This area is geographically limited to the southeast by São Paulo and the remaining Cerrado forest in the same region of the ceramic that is located in the surrounding area of Panorama.
vcs-320: The objective of the project is construction and expansion of compost production facility for Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) located at Tikri in Delhi. The project involves adopting improved and scientific method for aerobic decomposition of Bio-Degradable component of MSW at Tikri. The Project comprises measures to avoid production of methane from biomass and other organic matter which would otherwise have been left to decay in Solid Waste Disposal Site (SWDS) without methane recovery. Due to the project activity, decay is prevented through aerobic treatment by composting and proper soil application of the compost. Hence the project will provide replicable model for environment friendly and economically viable MSW processing.

The Soil Carbon Project aims at promoting Sustainable Agriculture practices that increase soil organic carbon. In the project the farmers will adopt practices that increase capacity of the soil to sequester increased carbon they will reduce the use of synthetic fertilisers, increase activities that improve soil productivity like increasing the use of organic fertilisers, incorporate residue management, and reduce tillage thereby reducing overall greenhouse gas emissions.
In the proposed project area farmers cultivate corn, peanuts, soybeans, and rice in a no-till manner in June each year and harvests them in October of the same year. Wheat is planted by the no-till method after peanut harvest. After the corn, soybean, and rice harvest, the land will be tilled with less tillage or traditional tillage, including deep ploughing and deep loosening (vertical rototilling). After crop harvest, straw and root stubble will be returned to the land to improve soil organic matter input and enhance soil fertility. In this process, organic fertilizers will replace part of the synthetic chemical fertilizer. At the same time, no-till activities will reduce the consumption of fossil fuels when farmland is tilled.
Through these activities, the project will rebuild the organic matter of the soil, improve its properties and reduce GHG emissions from the implementation of activities such as reducing the use of N fertilizers and fossil fuel. The practices will also restore soil fertility and sequester carbon from the atmosphere, mitigating climate change.
The main objective of this proposed project is to raise farmers awareness and prove to them that there is a way to practice farming methods that are sustainable and positively impact climate change. Such practices can also be profitable to the farmers. The farmers will be assisted with technical advice on how to implement these activities, which will transition throughout the years into a sustainable farm system.
vcs-3202: The Henan Runan Agricultural Land Use Management Project belongs to the type of VCS Agricultural Land Management (ALM) project activities and seeks to increase the capacity of soil organic carbon (SOC) to sequester carbon and enhance nutrients through tillage management, application of organic fertilizer, and straw application. The proposed project has strived to implementing sustainable management practices which not only reduce and remove greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions but also achieves socioeconomic development of the project areas. The project area is 18500 ha. The selected towns for the project are located in Runan county of Zhumadian city in Henan province of Central China.
vcs-3204:
The intention of the grouped project activity involves the installation of low greenhouse gas emitting safe drinking water purifiers (SDWPs) to provide clean drinking water to the households of Laos. The grouped project activity reduces the use and demand for fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass that would have been used to boil water as a means to purify water in the absence of this project activity. This directly leads to reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it  can be helpful to user`s health. 
The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project is the actual baseline scenario which is equal to the existing common practice by the households i.e. in absence of the project activity the equivalent amount of thermal energy generated using firewood in three stone open fires to meet the boiling water demand.  

The grouped project will distribute water purifiers to households who use the traditional cookstove for boiling water. The annual estimated emission reductions for the grouped projects are 655,210 tCO2e/annum.

vcs-3207: This project activity will capture waste CO2 which would have otherwise been emitted into the atmosphere, or atmospheric CO2 which would otherwise be in the atmosphere, and utilize that gas as a feedstock in the production of concrete. These project activities reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sequestering CO2 via the production of concrete. This manufacturing process has the additional benefit of requiring less Portland cement, which further reduces emissions, because the cement production process is highly energy and carbon intensive. The project activity will take place at the location where the concrete is first manufactured (mixed with cement, water, aggregates, etc.).  At its peak, this project activity will result in approximately 366,400 metric tons of CO2 reduced over the crediting period, the average annual emission reductions being 52,342 tCO2eq.
vcs-3208: The Wheatbelt Biodiversity Carbon Credit Project (WBCC) (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is a carbon sequestration project developed by Decarbonology Pty Ltd. This Project focusses on ecosystem restoration of the project site and the Wheatbelt of WA more broadly. It aims to support existing primary forest patches via afforestation of matrix areas between fragments to increase native habitat area, connectivity and ecosystem functions. Plantings will consist of a mix of over 20 native species local to the region.

vcs-3210:
The purpose of the REDD+ Bajo Atrato project is to reduce GHG emissions from deforestation and forest degradation activities, envisioning that the efforts of the communities inhabiting and owning the territories where it is located are materialized in actions that lead to forest conservation and the improvement of living conditions. The project is located in the northwest of Colombia, in the Department of Chocó, between the municipalities of Riosucio and Carmen del Darién, in the lower basin of the Atrato River, which is part of the Darién area. In the area of the project’s first instance, the following Afro-descendant communal lands are grouped: the Quiparadó River Basin Community Council, the Curbaradó River Community Council, the Salaquí River Basin Community Council, the Cacarica River Basin Community Council, the Truandó Medio La Teresita Community Council, the Bocas de Taparal Community Council, the Dos Bocas Chintado Community Council, the La Nueva Truandó Community Council, and the Clavellino Community Council.
The actions that will make possible to reduce deforestation and forest degradation in the project area are aligned with the needs and purposes  identified during the first meetings with the communities and while conducting the prior, free and informed consent process. These actions are aimed at achieving four major purposes: strengthening of governance and community management; improvement of community welfare; provision of social and community infrastructure; and boost of sustainable livelihoods and environmental protection, basic sanitation and aqueducts. The lands in the project area include tropical pluvial forests with transition to cold and very humid tropical forests. There, forests, grasslands, secondary vegetation, swampy areas and agroecosystems are found. In these areas, deforestation is associated with wood extraction, agricultural frontier expansion, illicit crop cultivation, and unplanned infrastructure construction.

vcs-3213: This Project is intended to promote a range of agricultural management practice changes targeted at increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and reducing net emissions of CO2, CH4, and N2O from farms across North-Western Europe. Indigo Ag helps farmers to implement climate-smart practices through an integrated system of extension and outreach, modeling, agronomy support, and digital data collection tools. vcs-3214:
Caglayanlar Biogas Plant project is a biogas to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by ÇAĞLAYANLAR BİYOGAZ ELEKTRİK ÜRETİM SANAYİ VE TİCARET LİMİTED ŞİRKETİ, as the Project Owner, in Mucur district, Kırsehir province, in Turkey.
Project activity has three biogas engines installed at the biogas power plant, with 4.503 MWe/e. The manure produced by 625 dairy cattle and 76,200 non-dairy cattle located on neighboring farms is collected and fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site.
The project began to generate electricity on October 16th, 2020According to Electricity Generation License, The biogas generator system has the maximum operational capacity 9.006 MWe/h. The annual feed-in electricity is estimated to be 67,545,000 kWh. While heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid.
vcs-3215:
The ASATIQ Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project is located within the area of the Association of Traditional Indigenous Authorities of Querarí (ASATIQ), which is part of the Great Eastern Indigenous Reservation of Vaupés in jurisdiction of the municipality of Mitú, in the department of Vaupés, Colombia. ASATIQ’s territory is located in the Colombian Amazon biome. The objective of the ASATIQ Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions coming mainly from deforestation and degradation of the Amazon Forest.
Potential activities to reduce deforestation include forest protection and monitoring, the intensification and improvement of agricultural productivity in local communities, planting of fruit and timber trees (including those used for firewood), planting of other species used as construction materials, the creation of jobs as an alternative source of income (for example, in forest monitoring) and the improvement of health and education conditions of the communities in order to offer non-extractive work options.
At the same time, actions in the medium and long terms have been defined to support the territory’s self-governance principles, as well as to promote the development of local traditional practices and ancestral education. The proposals made are framed aligned with the general action lines of the ASATIQ Life Plan.
On the other hand, between 40% and 60% of recent IDEAM deforestation early warning bulletins come from the Amazon, and the department of Vaupés appears in the first five ranks of alert. Under these circumstances, the without-project scenario presents an unplanned use of forest resources with extractive logging activities and the expansion of the agricultural frontier through subsistence crops and itinerant mining, which are being developed progressively putting at risk the ecosystem balance of the forests and the cultural traditions of the communities.
The duration of the project is proposed from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2047.
vcs-3216:
The ASATRIZY Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project proposed to be implemented in the Great Eastern Reservation of Vaupés is in the Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD+) category. Development of the REDD+ project is based on the VM0009 Methodology, v3 of the VCS. This methodology is applicable to this project and is being used for other REDD+ projects in the region. It has also been used by Wildlife Works, having two types of areas of application.  The first, corresponding to the Project Area (PA) and the second to the Project Accounting Area (PAA). The PAA is the area with forest cover, where the project would implement activities to prevent deforestation and whose results would be used to calculate carbon credits.
According to the territory conditions, this is a standalone project that respects ASATRIZY’s autonomy. In the without-project scenario, the forest ecosystems in the department of Vaupés and in particular those in the territory of ASATRIZY are located in life zones of tropical humid forest. This area has been recognized as one of the most biodiverse in the country and the whole continent, being characterized by its endemic species.
The forest monitoring carried out by the Colombian Government and coordinated by IDEAM has shown a national annual deforestation average between 177,764 ha and 219,552 ha for the 2016-2017 period, with the Amazon biome representing 70% of the total deforestation. In addition, between 40% and 60% of recent IDEAM deforestation early warning bulletins come from the Amazon, and the department of Vaupés appears in the first five ranks of alert.
According to this scenario and based on data obtained from the Amazonian Scientific Research Institute (SINCHI) and through field visits carried out by WWC, it was possible to identify the unplanned use of forestry resources as the main driver of deforestation in the project area, consisting of “slash-and-burn” activities in the jungle to expand the chagras.
vcs-3217:
The Project is located in the Amazon biome in southwestern Colombia, in the municipalities of Puerto Leguizamo (Putumayo), Solano (Caquetá) and Puerto Alegría (Amazonas), in the territory of the communities grouped in the Association of Traditional Authorities and Councils of the Indigenous Peoples of the Municipality of Leguízamo and Alto Resguardo Predio Putumayo - ACILAPP.
Prior to the development of the Project, according to monitoring of the country's forests led by IDEAM, an annual average of deforestation at the national level of 145,943 ha for the period 2000 - 2017 was found, where the Amazon biome presents 56% of the total deforested, with an annual average for the same period, of 82,332 ha. The data does not show a trend of decreasing change or stabilization, confirming the problem of deforestation is recognized as one of the most critical environmental liabilities for the country. Based on data obtained from the Instituto Amazónico de Investigaciones Científicas SINCHI and through field visits conducted by WWC, the main driver of unplanned deforestation affecting the project area is the clearing and burning of forest for extensive cattle ranching, accompanied by the construction of unplanned road accesses. Other identified causes of deforestation are illicit crops (coca, etc.), illegal mining, and illegal timber extraction.
As a result of the work with the community, activities aimed at reducing deforestation and forest degradation were identified, such as: protection and monitoring of the forest, intensification of Eco-Friendly agriculture, substitution of firewood, generating alternatives to meet the demand for construction materials, creation of jobs (Alternative Income), in addition the community is interested in strengthening the governance of the territory, as well as developing initiatives to generate wellbeing in the community associated with educational, health, cultural and sports projects.
vcs-3218: The Atrato-Baudó REDD+ Project aims to reduce GHG emissions from deforestation of natural forest. It is expected to achieve this through implementation of community actions framed in conservation, protection and sustainable management of the forest, which lead to improvements in living conditions in the territories. The area of the project’s first instance is located in the Tumbes-Chocó-Magdalena bioregion, in the municipalities of Alto Baudó, Quibdó, Lloró, Bagadó, Tadó, Río Iró (Santa Rita) and Cértegui, in the department of Chocó. The project is designed as a grouped project, initially made up of the collective territories of the following Afro-descendant communities: Community Council of San Isidro, Community Council of Villa Conto and Major Community Council of the Alto Atrato Popular Peasant Organization (COCOMOPOCA).  The project activities are aligned with the community needs and purposes identified during the process of relationship and free and informed prior consent developed with the communities. These actions are aimed at achieving four major purposes, which are: Governance and community management; social and community infrastructure; sustainable livelihoods and environmental protection, basic sanitation and aqueducts. Currently, the forests in the project area include areas of very humid tropical forest with transition to Tropical Rainforest. These ecosystem characteristics potentiate the habitat conditions of both flora and fauna, being cataloged as one of the most biodiverse areas of the country and the continent, characterized by endemism.  Deforestation that occurs in the project area are the result of a combination of complex socioeconomic and historical factors, associated with extractive processes that have directly affected biodiversity and ecosystem services. The project, as an alternative to conversion, aims to maintain carbon stocks through sustainable forest management, promoting improvements in the living conditions of local communities.
vcs-322: The project activity promotes a fuel switch at Lara Ceramic, which is a small and prototypical ceramic industry that produces structural ceramic units like bricks, destined for the local market of Vale do Paraiba. The project consists on switching the non-renewable fuel such as heavy oil, which was a common practice in the region, by a renewable biomass to feed the kiln.  Lara Ceramic utilized a fossil fuel (heavy oil) to feed their kiln, however it made adaptations to change the fuel, and become to use renewable biomass such as sawdust and rice husk to supply of the kiln. Lara Ceramic receives sawdust, wood residues, and wood chips, which are all turned into sawdust inside the ceramic and then mixed with rice husk to feed the kilns.
vcs-3220:
The purpose of the project activity is to install and operate a run-of–river, greenfield 1.49 MW hydroelectric plant at Mbakaou Carrière and electrify neighbouring communities through an isolated mini-grid. At least 75% of the clients in these communities will be households. 
The project developer and operator is IED Invest Cameroun, which aims is to develop and operate a small scale hydro power project at Mbakaou. 
By providing electricity to rural communities located around Mbakaou through a network of off-grid mini-grids, IED invest Cameroun aims to bring clean energy to the communities and thereby reduce greenhouse gases (GHGs). 
The operating mode of the particular case of the Mbakaou Quarry site can be assimilated to a low waterfall type installation with water available all year round, thanks to water regulation by Djerem dam. The turbines will harness the kinetic energy of the water and convey the energy to a generator and transformer.

vcs-3223: The project is a grouped project that aims to generate greenhouse gas emission removals and reductions through mangrove reforestation and avoided degradation, including wetland restoration and conservation activities. The project area covers the entire mangrove landscape (both intact and degraded areas) of The Gambia, covering more than 100,000 ha, and project activities will be included gradually on the basis of appropriateness for rehabilitation and avoided degradation of mangrove, community involvement and financial resources available. The project area covers all mangrove regions of The Gambia. The regions are: - West Coast Region (WCR) - Lower River Region (LRR) - Greater Banjul Area (GBA) - North Bank Region (NBR) - Central River Region (CRR). vcs-3225:
Yingkou MSW Incineration and PowerGeneration Project (hereafterreferredto as the project) is located at Industrial Park of Metallurgy, Chemical Industry andHeavy equipment, Yantian District, Yingkou City, Liaoning Province, P.R.China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Yingkou Canvest Environmental Power Company Limited. (hereafter referred to as the project owner).
The purpose of the projectis to treat fresh MSW with two750t/d MSW combustion lines and utilize recovered waste heat for electricity generation. The MSW treatment system is composed of two 750t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched withtwo sets of 15MW steam turbine and two sets of 15MW generators. The project will process 547,500 tons of MSW every year, and consume 120 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion lines will work
8,000 hoursand generate 204,800 MWh electricity every year, of which 167,940 MWh will be exported to the Northeast China Power Grid (NECPG).
By combusting MSW thatwould otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the project avoids the emission of methane that would be generated under landfilling condition. Meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the MSW treatment system, the project could generate electricity to displace equivalent electricity supplied by NECPG which is dominated by fossil fuel-fired plants. The baseline scenario of the project is the sameas the scenario priorto the
implementation of the project, namely that the landfill gas is vented to atmosphere directly and the equivalent power is supplied by the NECPG.

The Padang Tikar Landscape project is located in the Padang Tikar Landscape of the Batu Ampar subdistrict, Kubu Raya district, West Kalimantan province, Indonesia. The project consists of 10 'Village Forests', covering 76,370 hectares (ha), 58,672.7 ha of which is eligible for the reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD) project. The Village Forest of Padang Tikar is the largest 'Village Forest' permit in Indonesia and is divided
into three types of forest: protected forest (69,299 ha), limited production forest (1,985 ha), and convertible production forest (5,086 ha). The Padang Tikar Landscape project is a microcosm of the country as it has comprehensive forest ecosystems, ranging from inland forests to swamp forests (including mangrove forests and peatlands).

The project aims to reduce a large amount of greenhouse gases (GHG) by changing the water regime from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. The project is conducted in Suibin County, Hegang City, Heilongjiang Province of China, and involves a total acreage of 19,365ha for single-cropping rice. 
Currently, the farmers in the project area are using the continuously flooded method during the rice cultivation. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches and technical support to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, which is also the baseline scenario. Within the project boundary, every farmer’s household owning the paddy fields is regarded as an isolate unit. With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method.  As the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, after the implementation of the project, the period of flooded condition will be shortened, which will have negative impact on the methane production. It means that controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements during rice cultivation, can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, CH4 emission during the cultivation can be declined significantly. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 2.66~2.98  tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 559,218   tCO2e in the 10-years crediting period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 55,922 tCO2e.
vcs-3228:
Brick making in Nepal is energy and labor-intensive process and is regarded as one of the most polluting industries. Nepalese brick kilns use mainly coal and a small fraction of sawdust and firewood as energy source for firing bricks. A 2011 study by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) estimated coal consuming industries contribute eight percent of black carbon (BC) emission in Nepal and the brick industry, the second largest industry in Nepal, is responsible for most of it.  
In good brick manufacturing system, bricks are manufactured without burning fossil fuel and it instead utilizes soil (90%), cement (9.8%) and soil stabilizer (0.2%). This technology is highly productive, eco-friendly and labor-friendly. Good bricks system hardens and cures bricks using soil stabilizers instead of baking bricks in kiln, reducing production time significantly. This shall reduce air pollution and facilitate the abatement of greenhouse gas emissions. Carbon revenues shall enable the project proponent to meet the project management cost, provide financial incentives to the brick kiln owners under each project activities to undertake this good brick system on a wide scale by providing the soil stabilizer in subsidized cost, thus helping the proposed programme to achieve its potential to encompass the entire sector on a national scale. 
The project will be located in Panchkhal Municipality, Ward no:12, Kavre Palanchowk. This installation reduces about 2037 tCO2e annually through substitution of fossil fuels (mainly coal).
vcs-3229: The project is in north of Kaiping City, Jiangmen City, Guangdong Province, which is located in southern China, including 6 towns, namely Dasha Town, Longsheng Town, Cangcheng Town, Magang Town, Shatang Town, Yueshan Town. The main goal of this project is changing the irrigation method from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded during rice cultivation. In 2019, the average annual income of each local household was only 20,703 RMB CNY and rice cultivation is the main way for local farmers to survive. In this case, they lack of financial support to build ditches for implementing intermittently flooded method. Therefore, traditional continuously flooded method still used for rice cultivation, which means there is constant pond water maintained in the field until the harvest drainage. The organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition.  In contrast, rice paddies intermittently submerged and dried so that the upper soil layers switch from anaerobic to aerobic conditions several times during the crop growing season in Intermittently flooded method. Moreover, the intermittently flooded method brings many benefits, such as the higher rice yield production, the higher methane removal rate and etc. The project aims to achieve GHG mitigation goal （sustainable development goals）in project zone by utilizing intermittent flooded irrigation method. There is totally 7,359.19ha of rice paddies are switched from continuously flooded method to implementing intermittently flooded irrigation method in this project.

vcs-3238:
Paddy fields are the most dominant anthropogenic sources of methane to the atmosphere (5-20% of the total emission from all anthropogenic sources ). Anaerobic decomposition of organic material in flooded rice fields produces methane, which escapes to the atmosphere primarily by transport through the rice plants. The annual amount of CH4 emitted from a given area of rice is a function of the number and duration of crops grown, water regimes before and during the cultivation period, and organic and inorganic soil amendments. Soil type, temperature, and rice cultivar also affect CH4 emissions. This CH4 emission-intensive cultivation method will be targeted by the proposed programme, that will involve the implementation of the technology/measures that result in reduced anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in rice cropping soils and thus reduced generation of methane.
The project activity comprises of grouped projects of rice fields implementing the following methods:
 (a) Rice farms that change the water regime during the cultivation period from continuously to intermittent flooded conditions and/or a shortened period of flooded conditions;
(b) Alternate wetting and drying method (AWD)
(c) Rice farms that change their rice cultivation practice from transplanted to direct-seeded rice (DSR).
Thus, the measure will consist of AWD and/or DSR in combination with adjusted water management system in rice cultivation.

vcs-3240:
The Core Carbon Program intends to distribute Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) to rural households in India. The project activity is developed by Core CarbonX Solutions Private Limited and is targeted to be implemented in rural areas located in all the districts in the states of India.
This project seeks to increase access of households and communities to improved cookstoves by disseminating high thermal efficiency and low greenhouse gas emitting cooking stoves. This will in turn reduce deforestation as less firewood would be utilised for cooking. It will also avoid soil erosion and nutrient loss from degradation of forests.
The improved cook stoves to be distributed would provide co-benefits to users in the form of reduced exposure to health-damaging indoor air pollutions due to the burning of firewood in traditional inefficient cook stoves, and create decent work for local people leading to a sustainable source of income.
Gathering of firewood and cooking are major tasks undertaken primarily by women and young girls especially in rural communities. The time saved from gathering firewood and cooking can be spent on productive, educational and income earning activities.
The location of the project
The project location is in the state of Odisha and Jharkhand in India initially and will expand to other states of India. The project location for Initial Project Activity Instances i.e., Project Instance 1 in Odisha and Project Instance 2 in Jharkhand, India and also planning 38 future instances details are provided in Section 1.12 of the VCS PD Document

Guangdong Huidong Afforestation Project  is located in Huidong County, Huizhou City, Guangdong Province, in the southeast of Guangdong Province and the east of Huizhou City. The project’s aim is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on suitable lands  for forestation, and there has never been any activity affecting the local ecosystem. 
An area of 7,950.86  ha, which belongs to the villagers and the village committees manage the lands on behalf of villagers, have been planted on more than 600 parcels of lands since 2015. All the trees planted in the project zone are native species, including Schima superba, Castanopsis fissa, Elaeocarpus sylvestris, Liquidamba formosana, Camphor tree, Cinnamoummum bumannii, Michelia macclurei, Acacia rachii, Castanopsis hystrix, Casuarina equisetifolia Forst., Pinus elliotti, China fir. No invasive alien species or genetically modified organisms are involved.
The implementation of the project would generate GHG emission removals and improve local environment by planting trees, enhance biodiversity conservation and climate change adaptation, improve soil and water conservation in project zone, strengthening the live skills of local communities and residents by providing their relevant technical skills, training and create more permanent job opportunities for local women and increase income for local communities.
