Agrisolero farm is located in Solero e Quargnento, Alessandria in Northern Italy. The coordinates are attached as a KML file.  Several agricultural practices will be implemented or modified on the land. Taken together, the goal is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by this farm and raise the carbon stored in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. 

To do so, the following methods will be applied on site; reduced amount of inorganic fertilizers,an improved fertilizer application, reduced tillage, application of organic digested fertilizer, improved water management, the use of cover crops and a reduced use of fuel.

The sectoral scope 14 – Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) is applicable to the project. Within this sector, this project has been developed under the scope of the methodology for improved agricultural land management (VM0042 VCS methodology).

The project has been found eligible under the scope of the VCS program as it meets all requirements established by the program. 

The crediting period chosen for this project is of 33 years, renewable 3 times. The period lasts from the 1/6/2022 to the 1/6/2055. We estimated that 55tCO2/year will be stored in the soil or not emitted.

Rice cultivation is the most important agricultural operation in Telangana State, not only in terms of food security but also in terms of livelihood and plays a major part in the economy and employment. The agriculture sector is backbone of the rural economy in Telangana. In Telangana State Paddy cultivated is 52,51,261 acres in Vanakalam and 51,71,916 acres in Yasangi and total cultaivated area for the year 2020-21 is 10.423 Million acres . The total production of rice in Telangana was 145.68 lakh tonnes in 2020-21. The district of Suryapet is one of the major producers district of rice.  
The aim of this project activity is reducing the CH4 emissions by switching traditional rice cultivation to AWD technique. 
The project activity comprises of grouped projects of rice fields implementing various water management practices located at different areas within the geographical area of India.
The proposed project activity instances involve the implementation of the various water management practices to mitigate methane emission from rice fields in regions in Suryapet District  in Telangana state, India.
vcs-3244:
This Grouped project is to reduce fossil-fuel based electricity consumption in households of The Socialist Republic of Vietnam (hereafter called “Vietnam”) by introducing more energy efficient LED lamps to replace incandescent lightbulbs (“ICLs”), which would result in reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.
The ordinary incandescent bulb is extremely energy inefficient for lighting when compared to LED. Only 10% of the energy used by an incandescent bulb is converted to light; the other 90% is lost as heat while LEDs use 90% less power than incandescent lights, are ecologically friendly, have zero UV emissions or mercury, and are very durable. Despite being inefficient, ICLs are the most preferred option because of its cheaper cost for replacing the broken ones that is about four times lower than LED lightbulbs. The replacement of ICLs with energy efficient LED bulbs will reduce energy consumption, thus resulting in less GHG emissions.
The grouped project will distribute freely 6,000,000 LEDs to households who are using incandescent lightbulbs for lighting. All the project instances to be included in this grouped project will be from within Vietnam only. The estimates of annual average GHG emission reductions of the grouped project activity is 598,293 tCO2e/annum.
vcs-3245: The project activity aims to replace the commonly used inefficient wood fired mud stove technology, with efficient biogas based cook stove, which is clean and sustainable. The project activity involves bundling household biogas plants located in the state of Kerala and Bihar, India.
vcs-3248: The project is a VCS ARR Gro up project where various horticulture species and coffee shrubs are planted. Plantation activities are done in the first 6 years (20 17 2022) as part of the first project instance . In the first project instance Coffee shrubs have been planted along with shade trees like Silver oak on 6390.9 hectares. The total project area of first instance is 6824.7 hectares where several other tree species are also planted in the remaining area. The planting activities are done on abandoned croplands and barren lands in 13 Mandal's of Vishakhapatnam district in Andhra Pradesh state. By reforesting these areas , the project instance is expected to sequester 342277 tCO2 annually. Plantation activities are done on the barren land parcels owned by tribal communities living in these area. These land parcels are pre provided to them by state as individual Plattaland's. Community were able to do only subsistence farming in a small patch of their lands because of investment constraints. Rest of the land were abandoned leading to land degradation. PP identified these land areas and plantation activities have been done here with the consent of land owners.

Through this project, the distribution and installation of ICS will be undertaken for households and communities/non-household. It is intended that under this project high thermal efficient cook stoves will be distributed. The present project promotes the distribution and utilization of the clay made Chitetezo Mbaula (CM) cookstove in Malawi. The efficient CM cookstove will replace the traditional open air three stone cooking method that is most popularly used. The CM cookstove is significantly more efficient than the traditional open fire three stone cooking method. The project will thus help reduce wood consumption by more than half in each household and therefore preserve the local forests and their biodiversity, as well as reducing greenhouse gas emissions resulting from unsustainably sourced wood. The end user will be informed in advance that the use of CM stoves generates carbon finance which in turn is used for subsidizing the price of CM stoves and for recovering project implementation costs.
The CM cookstove has further benefits such as avoiding hazardous open flame systems and reducing the quantity of harmful smoke in the local rural village households. Local families and women also benefit significantly through a reduction in time spent and distance walked in collecting wood. The project does not consist in a fuel switch as locally available wood is still being used. 
The project will be implemented in two districts (Machinga and Zomba) located in the Southern Region of Malawi. This region is the most populated one with around 45% of the total national population. The first CM cookstove was implemented on 26 March 2021. Up to 60,000 will be distributed in total.
The baseline scenario is the continued use of non-renewable wood fuel by the target population to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves in absence of project activity. It is estimated that this project will reduce about 128,199 tCO2e  per year on average. Over the 10 year life span of the project, this project is expected to reduce 1,281,189 tCO2e.

vcs-3270: The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Guiping City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, where is located in southwestern China with a total acreage of 12,588 ha for double-cropping rice. The project area contains the project fields of rice merely, and the data of total area is confirmed by the Agricultural Bureau of Guiping City. The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by replacing continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, this method can reduce the flooded time of rice in the whole growth cycle and the methane (CH4) emissions, and is more beneficial to production increase than the continuously flooded as well. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario.

Germany's image as an industrialized country is dominated by vehicle and machinery manufacturers as well as producers of chemical products. The agricultural use of more than 50% of the country's land area is usually overlooked, although here too, successful industrial cultivation is predominant. Technical progress in fertilizers and pesticides, agricultural machinery, and cultivation methods, as well as advances in breeding and the yield-oriented transformation of agricultural landscapes have increased yields many times over in the last 100 years. However, an accompanying effect of this growth is a significant impact on the environment and the climate.

To reduce this impact while maintaining high yields, the Future Soils and Sustainable Farming Initiative aims to promote IALM (improved agriculture land management) practices in Germany. Designed as a grouped project under the VCS, the initiative’s purpose is to encourage interested farmers to participate who meet the requirements. As its initial instance, the initiative starts with a farm located southeast of Berlin in the state of Brandenburg.

By applying regenerative practices, the participating farmers do not only support the global efforts to mitigate climate change by reducing and removing GHG, but also make their own soils more resistant to upcoming challenges such as longer periods of droughts or extreme weather phenomena. Furthermore, a significant contribution is made to the conservation and promotion of biodiversity.
vcs-3279:
Bangladesh is an agricultural country with majority of the population residing in rural areas. Solid 
fuels accounts for 90% of Bangladeshi households’ energy needs with fuelwood being used in 
around 84% households for cooking purposes. Cooking by rural households is predominantly done 
in traditional stoves using fuel wood. Burning solid fuels for cooking releases emissions of carbon 
dioxide, methane, black carbon, and other short-lived climate pollutants, some of the most 
important contributors to global climate change, along with deforestation and unsustainable wood 
harvesting. In addition, incomplete combustion of biomass fuels in inefficient traditional stoves 
produces Household Air Pollution (HAP) resulting in negative health impacts, particularly for 
women and children. In Bangladesh, about 145 million people are exposed to HAP and this 
contributes to 46,000 casualties per annum1
. Despite efforts by various organizations to introduce 
cleaner and more efficient cooking solutions since the 1980s, only 3-5 percent of households have 
access to an improved cookstove (ICS) in Bangladesh.

vcs-3280:
The Carpathia Forest Carbon Project aims for the restoration and full protection of forests in the south-eastern Carpathians Mountains in Romania. Through land purchase and conservation agreements, the project seeks to protect primary and secondary forests in five Natura 2000 network sites and regenerate areas affected by clear cuts, spruce monocultures, and degraded riparian habitats along the mountain rivers.
The Carpathia Forest Carbon Project would create GHG emission reductions by avoiding the release of carbon associated with timber harvesting, road building and other forestry operations that would be expected to be carried out in the baseline (business-as-usual) scenario. Thus, the project includes improved forest management (IFM) practices that convert the logged forests to protected forests through conservation management activities with low level of timber removal for ecosystem/habitat enhancement and risk management in the wider Făgăraș Mountains (Natura 2000 designated site), the Piatra Craiului National Park and the Leaota Mountains. 
The broader vision of this project is to establish the foundations of a new National Park that can be recognized as the European Yellowstone Park (in reference to the Yellowstone National Park in the United States), encompassing the Carpathian Mountains; from the Olt Valley in the West to Piatra Craiului Mountain in the East.
The project area involves the lands owned by Fundatia Conservation Carpathia (FCC) as well as those managed by them and owned by their partners Wildland Ltd, Romfor Sustainable Forestry SRL, Almimax Natura, Dante International and Sanatate & Natura. The forest properties to be considered include 36 forest management plans (FMP). The total project area is 23,404 ha, of which 14,541 ha are eligible for the development of the IFM activities.
vcs-3281:
Andrade Sun Farms REDD+ Fazenda Santa Rita promote forest conservation and the reduction of potential greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, based on an economic development model. place that values forest preservation through a mosaic of activities associated with the organic production of Tahiti lime (Citrus latifolia).

The Project area is located in Cerrado biome vegetation, the second largest Brazilian biome, after the Amazon, where thousands of species of animals and plants that only exist in this region live. More than 14 million people also inhabit the Cerrado, many of whom depend on agriculture and livestock to survive and help the economy grow. The “Brazilian savannah” is also the country’s water tank: it concentrates the main springs and some of the most important tributaries of the three largest hydrographic basins in South America (Amazonas, Paraguay and São Francisco).

With the approval of the REDD+ Project and the consequent issuance of carbon credits, the values measured in their sale will be destined to optimize the management directed to forest areas, both legal reserve and forest surplus, to promote high productivity in these areas. ensuring a decrease in deforestation and GHG emissions. Such actions will be linked to sustainable management of production areas.

The proposed project involves the establishment of a municipal solid waste (MSW) processing plant in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. The project involves aerobic decomposition of biodegradable components of municipal solid waste.
The waste processing plant would have an aggregated capacity to process 400 tonnes per day (TPD) of waste.
The purpose of the project is to avoid methane emission through Processing of municipal solid waste in a compost plant that uses controlled aerobic decomposition in a windrow composting process. The process of composting would result in the production of compost that will be supplied to the local agricultural farms
vcs-3283: Asya Lale Biogas project is a biogas to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented in Karatay, İsmil district, KONYA province, in Turkey. The project began to generate electricity on October 22nd, 2020. According to Electricity Generation License, the biogas generator system has the maximum operational capacity of 6 MWe. The annual feed-in electricity is estimated to be 45,030,000 kWh. While heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid. This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for 21 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 411,705 tCO2eq/y.
vcs-3284: This REDD+ project is an Avoided Unplanned Deforestation and Degradation (AUD) activity. The REDD+ project area covers parts of four provinces namely, East Sepik, Gulf, Madang and Southern highlands in Papua New Guinea .The rainforests in the project area are among the most valuable natural resources. The forests support hundreds of rare and endemic species, making this place a “mega-biodiverse”. These forests are also directly critical to the lives and well-being of most of our people, including the communities. These areas are under tremendous stress due to logging, shifting agriculture, and plantations for decades. The major causes for forest loss in these areas are due to demand for an unprocessed log from the Asian market and, a large portion of the forests is being converted to permanent agriculture and long fallow shifting cultivation. Besides, the human population has been immensely increased in these areas which leads to poverty escalation, thus the subsistence farmers respond to the growing needs of the population by various forms of agricultural intensification. This initiative proceeds with promoting various activities to mitigate climate change and improving livelihoods.
vcs-3285: The proposed group project activity aims to ameliorate the lifestyle of people living in rural and semi-urban households of Gujarat and Rajasthan States of India. The grouped project activity will reduce greenhouse gas emission by disseminating fuel-efficient cookstoves (ICS) in Gujarat and Rajasthan in India. The objective of the project activity is to diminish the consumption of fuel-wood which will ultimately lead to forest conservation and make better the health condition of the ICS users by reducing the smoke emissions. The proposed grouped project activity aims to replace traditional cookstoves with better ones which are called as ‘Improved Cookstoves.’The estimated annual average GHG emission reduction for the project activity is 197,687 tCO2e and the total GHG emission reduction estimated for the entire crediting period for the proposed grouped project activity is 1,976,870 tCO2e
vcs-3286: The project activity involves promotion of purified water to the people of socially deprived community in India states. The project intends to avail the households with clean water solutions; thereby, displacing the firewood which were using by households to boil the water for drinking purpose. Replacement of the firewood will reduce the exposure of the family members, specifically women, to the indoor air pollution and therefore result in saving of health related expenses.
vcs-3287:
The proposed project involves the establishment of a Biogas Plant at Village Pij, Taluka Vaso, District Kheda, Gujarat-387230, India. The project involves anaerobic and aerobic decomposition of biodegradable components of organic waste.
The waste processing plant would have an aggregated capacity to process 240 tonnes per day (TPD) of waste.
The main purpose of the project is to incorporate competent biogas technology and implementation to support in the country by setting up to field scale biogas plant; to be located based on the continuous availability of raw materials. Anaerobic digestion is the prominent technology used for degradation of biodegradable organic waste.
vcs-3288: The project activity is an organic waste anaerobic digestion bio-refinery; the purpose of the project activity to recover and treat various types of organic wastes (including livestock manure) to convert them into biogas under an anaerobic process and then to produce Compressed Biogas (CBG) via “Bio-methanation process for further application in transportation sector. The total capacity of the bio-refinery has been proposed to be 250 Tons of waste per day; the proposed waste types under the project shall primarily include animal manures, agri-wastes and a nominal quantity of other mix wastes as well. The wastes to be considered under the project activity would have been otherwise openly decayed, leading to a significant quantity of methane emission in absence of the project activity. Additionally, the project proposes to have an off-grid solar unit within the project boundary to meet the captive power requirements of the plant leading to reduction of GHG emissions against grid power at baseline. Further, the by-products of the refinery shall be used for soil application to replace nitrogen based fertilizers which further reduces GHG emissions. Thus, the project aims to combine multiple baseline to achieve a high level of GHG emissions and thereby leading to sustainability. Due to high level of environmental and social involvement the project activity shall cater to various positive impacts which are related to more than 5 SDG indicators. The project is currently at pre-commissioning stage, expected to achieve commissioning during the last quarter of this year.
vcs-3289: The intention of the grouped project activity (“hereafter “proposed project activity”) involves the installation of energy efficient Improved Cooking Stove (ICS) devices in the households (hereafter “users”) of Zimbabwe for cooking households. For this reason, this proposed project activity aims at reducing the wood-fuel consumption of traditional stove users by installing ICS to households. By reducing the consumption of wood-fuel, it can contribute to improving public health problems. Furthermore, this proposed project can contribute to climate change mitigation measures in Zimbabwe and sustainable development. The project activity targets households with no previous ICS access. The geographical boundary is in Zimbabwe.
vcs-329: The project activity is the grouping project of Nova Dutra, São Silvestre and Vila Nova Ceramics, which are three small and prototypical ceramic industries that produce structural ceramic devices like bricks destined for the regional market of the state of Rio de Janeiro. The activity of this grouping consists of utilizing wood from afforestation and woody residues such as pallets, other industries residues wood and elephant grass, which are renewable biomasses, to feed the kilns rather than using a non-renewable fuel like heavy oil. Such a switch was a pioneering practice in the region. Usually companies in the ceramic sector do not take into consideration the effects that they have on the environment, but this is not the case with these three ceramics. These ceramics worked hard to create a good working system and are perfectly within the boundaries of the regulations imposed by the Brazilian Government.
vcs-3290:
Project activity will target peri-urban and rural households in the Western region of Kenya, who typically cook on traditional open fires or inefficient charcoal stoves . These are extremely inefficient and demand a lot of inefficient biomasses, resulting in high CO2 emissions, deforestation, and exposure to indoor air pollution. The project stoves will displace the inefficient baseline technology – traditional open fires and inefficient charcoal stoves – by providing an improved cookstove which will reduce CO2 emissions by reducing wood or charcoal use.  

The Mukuru Stove is designed and manufactured by women from the local communities in Western Kenya and has a lifespan of 3 years. The factory is in Kalandin, Siaya County in the Western region of Kenya (approximately 318km from the capital city of Nairobi).

As well as reducing greenhouse gas emissions, the Project will provide various benefits to the end user households and communities whilst helping to meet the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Benefits include improved health through reduction in indoor air pollution, providing women with more time to put towards educational and income-generating activities, empowering women through establishing partnerships with women micro-entrepreneurs to be sales agents of the clean stoves in their communities, and reducing the income expenditure on fuelwood for stove recipients. The Project will monitor and report on the positive impacts that clean cooking has on women and gender equality.
vcs-3291:
This project encompasses the Pampas grasslands (known as La Pampa in Spanish and Os Pampas in Portuguese), which are vast grassland plains spread across the South American lowlands of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay over 750,000 sq. km. These are natural grasslands where livestock production is the key livelihood activity in the region. These grasslands are subdivided into 3 distinct ecoregions: the Uruguayan Savanna, the Humid Pampas and the Semiarid Pampas. Like other grasslands across the globe, these grasslands are under tremendous pressure from anthropogenic activities such as overgrazing and unsustainable grassland management activities. Grasslands in this region are also declining steadily due to changes in land use - the conversion of grasslands to croplands. Overgrazing and land use change has resulted in the decline of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) across the grassland region. 
The project promotes sustainable grassland management activities that will both improve SOC in the soil and improve the livelihoods of the communities utilizing these ranches, directly through the carbon credit payments, which provide an additional source of income, and indirectly through the increased productivity of their lands. The regenerated lands also become much less likely to undergo land use change, because the ranchers are better able to sustain their livelihoods. vcs-3294: The Muskitia Pâsa Klîn Nâka (Muskitia – a source of fresh air) project is a regional community initiative, which seeks certification of actions related to the reduction of carbon emissions due to unplanned deforestation and the conservation of mangrove, broadleaf, and coniferous natural forest in about 5,000, 200,000 and 70,000 ha respectively. Under the Uttarakhand Forest Resource Management Project (UFRMP), Uttarakhand Forest Department (UKFD) has tackled forest degradation in over 800 Van Panchayats across the state. VPs were treated in Ranikhet Soil Conservation Forest Division. Out of these Van Panchayats, 18 Van Panchayats have 
been selected for developing carbon finance project.
Anthropogenic pressures such as unsustainable extraction of fuel wood, overgrazing of cattle,anthropogenic forest fire, and unsustainable extraction of Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) are responsible for forest degradation and deforestation in these Van Panchayats. These activities include assisted natural regeneration, protection through fencing, soil and water conservation, alternative livelihood development including other better forest management practices like fire management and forest patrolling.

The 70 MW solar PV plant is the largest in West Africa and the first renewable energy facility in the country. This plant which is located in Blitta, will supply reliable, clean electricity to hundreds of thousands of homes and businesses in the country and save more than one million tonnes of CO2 emissions through its lifetime.

The current capacity of the plant is 50 MW. An additional 20 MW expansion is expected to be operational by 2023/2024 bringing the total to 70 MW.
The village of Blitta-Losso is part of the canton of Blitta village and is surrounded from north to south and from east to west by the villages of Blitta kotokoli, Boufouli boko losso, Doufouli and Oranyi.

The Blitta area has an average monthly direct normal radiation of 5.14 kWh/m²/day and an average annual solar irradiation of 1,876 kWh/m².
The project will advance the Togolese national clean energy strategy to increase the share of renewables in electrification to 50 per cent by 2025 and 100 per cent by 2030.

The project activity, which has a lifetime of 25 years, is expected to produce more than 88,000 MWh of electricity annually. The total estimated emission reductions of the proposed project are 464,040 tCO2e during the first crediting period. The ex-ante emission reduction calculation shows that the project will avoid  66,291 tCO2e on average, annually.

The project will not only reduce the GHG emissions but is expected to achieve many social benefits such as improving social services to targeted social groups and generating job opportunities. The jobs created are intended to promote sustained, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all. The project is also crucial in ensuring that all learners acquire the knowledge and skills needed to promote sustainable development, including, among others, through education for sustainable development and sustainable lifestyles, human rights, and gender equality.
vcs-3299: The project “Serra do Sudeste” is a grouped project, falling under the Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) category and targeting the following Verra certifications: Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standard (CCB). vcs-3303: Methane emissions through flooded rice cultivation is one of the largest sources of methane into the atmosphere. Tibet Ngari Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as 'the project') is located in Ngari Region, Tibet Autonomous Region, China. The objective of the project is to restore the 'black soil beach' and degraded grassland ecosystem through reseeding native grasses and grazing management, such as rest grazing and grazing prohibition, increase carbon sequestration, and promote local development.
Totally, 373,467.02 ha of degraded grassland in Ngari have been managed sustainably including rest grazing and grazing prohibition by fence building and seeding of local high-quality forage.There are three main restoration measures: rest grazing, grazing prohibition and black soil beach restoration.

vcs-3321: Mount Kenya Regenerative Agroforestry Project is a reforestation and afforestation  initiative designed and funded by Dutch Green Business. The Project aims to increase tree cover in Kenya through two distinct strategies: 1) restoring degraded or deforested areas in Kenya Forest Service lands with native species, and 2) planting agroforestry crop trees on individual farms where smallholders wish to benefit from the income that perennial nuts and fruits can provide. In both cases, site-appropriate tree species will be contributing to regional wildlife habitat or corridors, improving water infiltration, controlling erosion, and sequestering carbon, among other ecosystem services. Prior to project implementation, thousands of hectares of Kenya Forest Service land have been degraded or deforested over time, without the financial resources to restore them. In some cases, reforestation efforts have been attempted, but without the dedication of enough funds to guarantee the survival of these trees when threats like livestock grazing must be constantly warded off through employed patrols. The Project aims to change this dynamic by bringing in external up-front investment made possible through the anticipated sale of Verified Carbon Units generated through project activities. Similar financial barriers are faced by individual farmers, many of whom rely on annual crops like cabbage or potato, and do not have the resources to invest in trees that they are interested in. Their farms are currently lacking in canopy cover, with perhaps a few trees on the property boundaries that are cyclically harvested for fuelwood or timber.
vcs-3322: Beyaz Piramit Biogas project is a biogas to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by BEYAZ PİRAMİT TARIM HAYVANCILIK ENERJİ EĞİTİM VE DANIŞMANLIK A.Ş., as the Project Owner, in Çumra district, KONYA province, in Turkey. From a socio-economic perspective, agricultural activities and animal husbandry have historically been primary household income sources for those living in Cumra Region. it is estimated that approximately 550 tons of cattle manure generated at animal farms will be collected daily through special sewage trucks equipped with close-tanks to prevent any odor and/or manure leakages and to be fed into the anaerobic digesters at the proposed biogas power plant The proposed project activity has two biogas engines installed at the biogas power plant, with 3.002 MWe. The manure produced by 12,650 dairy cattle and 2,110,000 hens located on neighboring farms is collected and fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site.The expected average annual emission reductions are 354,263 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,479,844 tCO2eq emissions reduction during the first crediting period and 7,439,533 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its three crediting periods for a total of 21 years.
vcs-3324: The primary objective of the IPOÁ REDD+ Project is to avoid gross baseline emissions of 2,719,762 tCO2e (averaging 90,659 tCO2e/year), corresponding to 4,200 hectares of avoided deforestation over the 30-year project lifetime (being an average of 140 ha/year). The project operates within private areas totaling 17,386 hectares, 17,329 hectares of which are eligible for REDD+ activities, located in Amazonas State, municipality of Novo Aripuanã. The latter ranks 15th for highest deforestation rates of the municipalities within the Amazon biome according to the Brazilian national deforestation monitoring program (PRODES) as, between 2016 and 2021, it displayed an average deforestation rate of 160km²/year. Long-term, high-impact benefits for communities and biodiversity will be provided by the Ipoá project, which are duly quantified and monitored through the CCB methodological standard. The definition of the actions to be implemented was carried out through a collaborative participatory consultation with community stakeholders. The activities fall into multiple activity scopes including: healthcare, education, occupational health and safety, communication and electrification, employment, and training, within the Community Pillar; fauna and flora research and conservation activities, as well as those addressing high conservation values, in the Biodiversity Pillar; and forest conservation activities articulated under Carbonext’s Forest Integrity Plan in the Climate Pillar. These initiatives will begin as soon as possible to project start in 2022 – 2023, Monitoring Period 1 (“MR1”), and continue along the project lifetime, through MR30 in 2052.
vcs-3325:
The project aims to reduce a large amount of greenhouse gases (GHG) by changing the water regime from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. The project is conducted in Nehe City, Heilongjiang Province of China, and involves a total acreage of 20,245ha for single-cropping rice. 
Currently, the farmers in the project area are using the continuously flooded method during the rice cultivation. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches and technical support to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, which is also the baseline scenario. As the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, after the implementation of the project, the period of flooded condition will be shortened, which will have negative impact on the methane production. In this case, CH4 emission during the cultivation can be declined significantly. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 2.87 tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice is expected per year during the 10-yr fixed crediting period.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 580,676 tCO2e in the 10-years crediting period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 58,067 tCO2e. This project aims to sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes, save water resources; increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers and provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Indonesia. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 
Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Indonesia. It is intended that under this project two types of single pot portable stove will be distributed, which are SSM S32-X stove and Baldwin stove. Each household will receive up to 2 ICS per household, it could comprise of same or different types of ICS. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Indonesia but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

vcs-3331: U.S. Farmers and Ranchers represent one of the most scalable and cost-effective solutions to draw down greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and address climate change. Arva Intelligence is a producer-first, B Corporation that uses machine learning (ML) and precision agriculture to optimize sustainable practices and profitability for landowners. Arva was founded on the principle of helping farmers and their suppliers make data-informed agronomic decisions, resulting in improved environmental stewardship for the buyers and an increased efficiency in grower operations. Limited access to data and financial risk concerns have been common barriers to adopting regenerative land management practices in the U.S., and the Arva Carbon Ready USA project will bring tools to farmers and ranchers to help them overcome barriers to adoption. Arva provides solutions through its measurement, monitoring, reporting, and verification platform and will provide its cloud-based, ML-enabled software to collect, integrate, and validate data from the adoption or expansion of on-field regenerative agricultural practices. Access to low-cost, scalable, agricultural carbon offsets is limited by the industry’s disaggregated digital infrastructure. Arva’s established Carbon Ready program allows farmers to upload field boundaries and run scenarios to determine the GHG emission values for practice changes that result in GHG avoidance/reduction and soil organic carbon sequestration. A project goal is to help growers identify the practices and seed best suited for their land and to overcome scalability challenges. To facilitate the collection of soil carbon measurements and verify location, Arva will utilize its newly developed mobile app. The project is designed as a grouped project within the USA. Arva estimates that this project will result in the removal and/or avoidance of 1,000,000 tons CO2e annually by 2023. Total GHG ERRs after the first 20 years of the project are estimated at 17,020,002 tons CO2e.
vcs-3332: The SIMFlor (Systematic Implementation of the Brazilian Forest Code) Programme 2, hereinafter known as “SIMFlor2”, is a grouped project located in the arc of deforestation within the Amazon biome. SIMFlor2 will provide carbon finance to promote native forest conservation in areas under threat of deforestation for the expansion of extensive cattle ranching thereby promoting compliance with the Brazilian Forest Code.
vcs-3333: The purpose of the project is to Reforest/restore degraded or severely degraded mangrove habitats and Afforest grassy land accretions within degraded mangrove habitats along the coastline of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar, resulting in increased area under mangroves. The proposed project aims to establish mangrove plantations in suitable locations within currently degraded costal/ intertidal mangrove habitats in Myanmar.
vcs-3334: The Marajó REDD+ Project has been designed for the protection of forests and rich biodiversity in the Amazon. It is part of the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) project category. Specifically, the project is of the “Avoided Unplanned Deforestation & Degradation” (AUDD) project category.
vcs-3335: The Project consists of forest protection and emission reduction activities in the Tiger Reserve. About 45522 ha (Project Area) area comes under REDD (Reducing Emission from Deforestation and Forest Degradation). The main effect of this project activity is reducing carbon emissions by preventing the conversion of forest lands with high carbon stocks to non-forest lands with lower carbon stocks.
vcs-3336:
Eastern Yan’an Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as ‘The Project’the project”) is located in Yanchang County, Yanchuan County, Yichuan County and Zichang City  in eastern Yan’an City, Shaanxi Province, People’s Republic of China. The project aims to increase carbon sequestration and improve the local ecological environment by means of forest planting activities on degraded lands suffering from severe soil erosion.
The project activities involve the planting of trees and shrubs on 58,423.59 hectares (or 876,354 Mu ) of degraded lands located in Yanchang County, Yanchuan County, Yichuan County and Zichang City under the administration of Yan’an City. The species include Robinia pseudoacacia (black locust), Platycladus orientalis (Oriental thuja or Oriental arborvitae), Pinus tabuliformis (Chinese red pine), Armeniaca sibirica (Siberian apricot) as well as Hippophae rhamnoides (sea-buckthorn). All of them are native species except for Robinia pseudoacacia, which is native to North America; it is not considered as an invasive species in China (refer to Section 5.2 for details). The project area was degraded lands with little vegetation before the project and would continue to be so without the implementation of the project activities. 
The implementation of the project activity will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conditions, increase the forest cover and enhance local biodiversity; the project also generates social benefits including job opportunities and technical skills training for local communities and residents.
vcs-3337:
Central Yan’an Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as 'The Project') is located in Ansai District, Baota District, Fu County, Ganquan County, Huangling County, Luochuan County and Zhidan County in central Yan’an City, Shaanxi Province, People’s Republic of China. The project aims to increase carbon sequestration and improve the local ecological environment by means of forest planting activities on degraded lands suffering from severe soil erosion. 
The project activities involve the planting of trees and shrubs on 67,473.46 hectares (or 1,012,102 Mu ) of degraded lands located in Ansai District, Baota District, Fu County, Ganquan County, Huangling County, Luochuan County and Zhidan County under the administration of Yan’an City. The species include Robinia pseudoacacia (black locust), Platycladus orientalis (Oriental thuja or Oriental arborvitae), Pinus tabuliformis (Chinese red pine), Armeniaca sibirica (Siberian apricot) as well as Hippophae rhamnoides (sea-buckthorn) and Xanthoceras sorbifolium. All of them are native species except for Robinia pseudoacacia, which is native to North America; it is not considered as an invasive species in China (refer to Section 5.2 for details). The project area was degraded lands with little vegetation before the project and would continue to be so without the implementation of the project activities. 
The implementation of the project activity will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conditions, increase the forest cover and enhance local biodiversity; the project also generates social benefits including job opportunities and technical skills training for local communities and residents.
vcs-3338:
Yan’an Wuqi Afforestation Project (hereafter 'The Project') is located in Wuqi County, Yan’an City, Shaanxi Region, China. The project aims to increase the carbon sequestration and to contribute to local sustainable development through planting the trees on the barren land or barren mountain.
45,661.91 ha of forest is to be planted by direct planting on barren land and barren mountain in Wuqi county, there are 4 species selected as designated tree species, they are Robinia pseudoacacia, Armeniaca sibirica, Prunus davidiana and Pinus tabuliformis, the planted trees are all native species. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and improve the Wuqi county’s local environment, about 3,791,500.00 ha enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing them with relevant technical skills and training and increase local biodiversity as a result of establishing a forest of native trees.
vcs-3339:
Yan’an Aerial Seeding Afforestation Project (hereafter 'The Project') is located in Yan’an City, Shaanxi Region, China. The project aims to increase the carbon sequestration and to contribute to local sustainable development through directly aerial seeding on the barren land and barren mountain. 
Aerial seeding is a method of afforestation in which forest seeds or seed pellets are scattered on the woodlands (i.e., sown areas) by aircraft. Planting afforestation by airplane is a modern afforestation method, which has the advantages of high speed, high efficiency, saving labor and great effect. In the sparsely populated, inconvenient transportation, labor shortage of large areas of barren mountains, sand and cutting, afforestation by aerial seeding is an effective way to speed up afforestation.
31,049.40 ha of forest is to be established by direct aerial seeding on barren land and barren mountain in Yan’an city, there are 2 species selected as designated sowing seed species, Platycladus orientalis (Giant cedar) and Pinus tabuliformis (China pine), which are all native species. The implementation of the project will generate GHG emission removals and improve the Yan’an local environment, about 3,703,054.05 ha enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing them with relevant technical skills and training and increase local biodiversity as a result of establishing a forest of native trees.
vcs-334: Animal methane capture and power generation.  Agricultural operations have been shaping the landscape and the way of life in the Dutch Provinces of North Brabant and Limburg for several hundred years. Until today, this is a mostly rural region with relatively little heavy industry, where agro-swine industry still plays the significant role. Indeed, these provinces house the majority of swine farms in Holland. This concentration of livestock has already led to a situation in which the complete manure cannot be disposed off on fields in the region any more due to the reached nitrogen absorption limit of the soil.
vcs-3340: This project helps pastoralists in deploying practices that contribute to the sustainable development of the Savanna grasslands of East Africa. The pastoralists of this region have largely resorted to implementing traditional grassland management methods on their lands. The grazing of grasslands by both livestock and wildlife is widely prevalent, and degradation of land due to overgrazing is a prominent issue. In this context, the opportunity to introduce improved grassland management practices, including sustainable grazing practices, will significantly help the grasslands of the region and restore carbon to their soil, creating carbon removals while improving overall soil health. In this project, pastoralists will be mobilized to take up a variety of improved grassland management practices. These practices are proven ways to increase soil organic carbon, prevent further degradation of the grasslands, and enable pastoralists to improve their productivity.
vcs-3341: The Samkos REDD+ Project (SRP) is an initiative designed to promote climate change mitigation and adaptation, maintain biodiversity and create alternative livelihoods under the United Nations scheme of Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation (REDD+). Phnom Samkos Wildlife Sanctuary and Southern Cardamom National Park are significant protected areas in Cambodia because they maintain an intact and sizeable area of primary evergreen forest in the region. Their landscapes are also home to over 59 IUCN Red Listed globally threatened species such as, the Asian elephant, Malayan sun bear, Asiatic black bear, Siamese crocodile, Irrawaddy dolphin, fishing cat, and the pangolin.
vcs-3342:
The XiCO2e: Mexican Reforestation Project is a grouped project for the afforestation, reforestation and/or revegetation (hereafter referred to as “ARR”) of lands in the states of Tabasco and Tamaulipas in Mexico. The main goals of this grouped project are:
●	To restore degraded areas through the plantation of Gmelina arborea. The project activity will prevent further deterioration of already degraded areas and address soil erosion by providing protection through vegetative cover.
●	To mitigate climate change by removing greenhouse gases (GHG) through biomass growth.
The first project activity instance of the XiCO2e project includes planting 1,014.82 hectares in the state of Tabasco and 204.18 hectares in the state of Tamaulipas, located in southeast and northeast Mexico, respectively. This totals 1,219.01 ha during the monitoring period from 2017 to 2022.
The project will achieve greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reductions through carbon sequestration by pools via the reforestation with Gmelina arborea. The estimated annual average is 3,726 tCO2e, and the estimated total GHG emissions reduction and removals amount to 111,781  tCO2e. Monitoring activities for the first verification period started on January 11, 2017 and concluded on July 30, 2022.
The scenario before the project's implementation involved degraded lands, with the previous land uses being grassland and agricultural lands, currently abandoned and degraded.”
The project proponents are ALA BOOL ALA BOOL TRUST SA DE CV and FORLIANCE GmbH. The project implementor is PROXYLO S.A.P.I DE C.V.
vcs-3343:
The XiCO2e: Mexican Peninsula Forest Project aims to increase carbon removal through Improved Forest Management activities in communal-land properties (ejidos) located in the Yucatán Peninsula in the southeastern state of Quintana Roo, Mexico. The project is developed under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) methodology VM0003 v1.3 - Methodology for Improved Forest Management Through Extension of Rotation Age (IFM ERA).
The Project Area covers 70,246 hectares and is comprised of semi-evergreen tropical forest with broad species diversity, having as its primary target commercial species such as mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla), Spanish cedar (Cedrela odorata), Sapotilla (Manilkara zapota), Fiddlewood (Vitex gaumeri), Tsalam (Lysiloma bahamensis), Ramon (Brosimum alicastrum), Katalox (Swartzia cubensis), Shaving bush tree (Pseudobombax ellipticum), Copperwood (Bursera simaruba), and Chechen (Metopium brownei), among several other tropical commercial species.
The common practice of harvesting in the ejidos consists of selection cuts of tropical species in management units during the established rotation period. The project will extend the rotation cycle by +5, +4, and +2 years. Additionally, the project aims to implement a monitoring procedure to systematize and centralize information related to forest practices. The project is expected to remove 4,599,024 tonnes of CO2e over 30 years, with an annual average of 170,334 tonnes of CO2e.
vcs-3344:
The Last Habitat REDD+ project is located in the Ucayali region, in the central zone of the Peruvian Amazon, one of the regions with the highest rates of deforestation in Peru (31,543.29 ha in 2021). The project area is comprised by two private estates belonging to the project proponent, BAM: the properties of Nuestro Señor Jesucristo with 8,049.87 ha and Selva Maestra with 14,176.13 ha, a total area of 22,226 ha mainly of primary floodable forests.

Located near the city of Pucallpa (Ucayali) and surrounded by deforestation pressures from agriculture, urbanization and others, the project area harbors an extraordinary ecological wealth, being the last habitat or refuge for various species of flora and fauna and a green island of outstanding ecological value. In addition, the are includes several types of valuable forest, among them the aguajales, which are the wetlands with the greatest carbon sequestration capacity in the Amazon, making this an essential ecosystem to conserve.

The Last Habitat REDD+ project is designed under the avoided planned deforestation methodology as this area was originally sold to the project proponent with the authorization to  convert the forested areas in agrarian production lands (camu camu, palm oil, piñon, and cattle ranching). Despite having the legal authorization to carry out traditional productive activities, BAM, with its own resources, has promoted the conservation of these valuable forests and its biodiversity over the years by implementing different strategies and activities such: territorial supervision with technical and legal support, forest surveillance activities, permanent work with communities for improving their capacities in sustainable forestry management, among others. Such conservation efforts will only be feasible and sustainable over time with the support of carbon revenues from the proposed REDD+ project.
vcs-3346: The project intends to generate additional income to the small holder farmers of Indo- Gangetic plain region for adopting improved agricultural practices such as zero till farming, cover cropping, crop diversification, farm residue incorporation, optimizing fertilizer application and efficient water management which provide a potential to not just prevent emissions into the atmosphere but also create carbon sinks through sequestration of carbon back into the soil. The project will be a grouped project. Starting with rice-wheat cropping system, the project will be further expanded to maize-wheat, sugarcane, and cotton-wheat/cotton cropping systems. Pulses and Mustard are cover crops widely interspersed in these cropping systems. The project considers 2019 as the baseline year in which the interventions started. Starting with 12 thousand hectares (~28000 Tonnes CO2 Eq. per annum) in 2019, the area will be stabilized at 2 million hectares (~7.0 million Tonnes CO2 Eq. per annum) in 2027 and maintained until 2038.
vcs-3347: Tiger Reserves are the storehouse of ecosystem services and a majority of rural population depend on forest resources for their day-to-day livelihood. This dependence is in the form of collection of a variety of Non-Timber Forest Produce (NTFP) and collection of firewood and fodder for subsistence and livelihood purposes. Due to this dependence on forest resources and lack of sufficient infrastructure, the local communities venture in the forest areas resulting in degradation of pristine forest and causing human wildlife conflicts. This results in loss of human lives, and wild animals in a retaliatory process. Hence, there is a need to develop a dedicated finance mechanism which shall help in mitigating the conflicts in an efficient way and lead to coexistence and harmony amongst forest fringe communities and wildlife. This project will result in enhancing carbon sequestration by reducing pressures on forests from unsustainable collection of firewood through sustainable firewood management and exploring energy efficient technologies and alternative fuel in and around Periyar Tiger Reserve, Kerala.
vcs-3348: Huizhou Landfill Gas Power Generation Phase III and IV Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is invested and owned by Shenzhen PhasCon Technologies Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the project owner). The project captures the landfill gas that would have been released to the atmosphere in the absence of the project and generates electricity with the landfill gas (LFG). The electricity is supplied to the China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) to replace the electricity generated from coal-fired power plants of CSPG.

The carbon credits are a result of the change of land use in previous pasture areas, through the plantation of Eucalyptus species in an area of 14,427 ha, considered as the first project activity, as well as a result of the recovery of sandy areas, through the plantation of native vegetation most adequate for each case in an area of 999 ha, considered as the second project activity, both classified under the ARR category.
vcs-3351: The CIBO Initiative for Scaling Regenerative Agriculture is a holistic effort to provide financial and technical support to US commodity crop growers that results in their adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and, consequently, greenhouse gas emissions reductions and removals. CIBO’s proprietary remote sensing technologies and process-based crop and soil model (SALUS), combined with technical and financial support from both CIBO and other enterprise partners, provide the incentives, safety net, and guidance that growers across the midwestern Corn Belt region of the United States need in order to overcome the barriers to widespread adoption of improved agricultural land management practices.
vcs-3352: This project activity will use smart thermostats installed in homes to reduce the heating and cooling usage.  The thermostats are manufactured by ecobee which also has developed a thermostat optimization software platform to control these devices remotely in a manner that deepens the levels of energy savings beyond what would have occurred in the absence of this enhanced functionality.  The energy efficiency optimizations resulting from this platform generate no additional revenue for ecobee but do represent a significant cost.  This approach reduces both electricity and natural gas usage in air conditioning and heating units in residential homes. The project boundary will include the United States, and the project will be grouped by climate and equipment type as detailed in Appendix D.  This project activity will result in approximately 3,825,927 tons of CO2 reduced over the crediting period, the average annual emission reductions being 546,561 tCO2.
vcs-3353:
The proposed Xeset 2 Extention Hydro Power Project identified and developed by Electricite Duo Laos is located on Xeset river in the vicinity of Ban Baktheung village, Laongam district, Saravane province, Lao PDR. The proposed project activity is a run of river project has created a small reservoir for smooth operation of the project activity.

The nominal installed capacity of the project is 10 MW (the actual installed capacity is 10.454MW comprising 2 turbines with individual installed capacity 5.227MW each), with estimated annual power generation 34.38 GWh. The generated electricity from the project activity will be supplied to the regional grid consisting of Thailand power grid and the Lao power grid.

The purpose of the project activity is to produce renewable energy using hydro power for supplying to grid. In the absence of the project activity equivalent amount of electricity would have been generated by the operation of grid connected fossil fuel based power plants. The Project activity thus reduces the anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in to the atmosphere associated with the equivalent amount of electricity generation from the fossil fuel based grid connected power plant.

The baseline scenario is that the electricity delivered to the grid by the project activity would have otherwise been generated by the operation of grid-connected power plants and by the addition of new generation sources into the grid The estimated annual average and the total CO2e emission reduction by the project activity over the first renewable crediting period of 7 years are expected to be 19,347 tCO2e and 135,429 tCO2e respectively.
vcs-3354:
The TERRRA Santa project of Improved Agriculture Land Management (IALM), according to the VM0042, will implement sustainable practices in all the project sites in order to reduce and remove GHG, support the local community, increase farmer’s income, and improve biodiversity and natural habitat – important pillars of sustainability.
The existing scenario prior to the implementation of the project was aquaculture with the use of on-land fishponds, producing fish for sale in Israel. This has been a common case in Kibbutzim (collective communities, traditionally based in agriculture) in the last 4-6 decades and currently becoming less profitable due to tax removal and cost increases, therefore some fishponds are not productive and left inactive. In addition, fishpond aquaculture makes use of technologies and practices that have large impacts in terms of, for instance, carbon footprint. 
The project will convert fishponds following rewilding concepts to increase biodiversity and vegetation growth using the earth’s “Muscle Memory”.  The project’s GHG removals will focus mainly on: 
I.	Aboveground biomass that will grow back after each harvesting.
II.	Belowground biomass, which is expected to have a high initial removal rate and small continuous increase.
III.	Soil carbon that accumulates continuously as biomass and sediments are added into the soil. 
Through this project, in collaboration with TERRRA, the Kibbutz farmers will be able to utilize the same fishpond areas to grow vegetation. These will mainly be Common Reed (Phragmites australis), Elephant Grass (Arundo donax), Castor (Ricinus communis), and/or other crops, to be harvested and used as fodder and source for renewable energy.
The IALM project is located in North Israel; it includes a portfolio of assets with a total area of around 500 hectares, which are estimated to reduce and remove 22,704 tons of GHG annually and a total of 454,080 tons over a 20 years period.
vcs-3355: The proposed project activity is a grouped project activity promoted by Himadri Energy International Pvt. Ltd. (hereinafter also called as ”HEIPL”). As number of existing solid waste disposal near metros and urban/semi urban cities in host country, HEIPL envisage to promote legacy waste biomining activity for cleaning old sites and free the land used for such purpose to be used for other developmental work. HEIPL envisage to contribute towards sustainable development and helping to meet the host country targets to increase MSW treatment penetration level. The estimated annual average and the total CO2e emission reduction for the first project instance over the fixed crediting period of 10 years are expected to be 7,569 tCO2e and 75,690 tCO2e respectively.
vcs-3356:
SD Environmental Projects Inc is a social enterprise focused on reducing deforestation in megadiverse hotspots and changing the lives of the most vulnerable communities by improving household economics, health, gender equality and overall quality of life. These vulnerable communities, often residing in areas most exposed to the risks of climate change and deforestation are disproportionately threatened by their impacts.  

The Philippines being severely deforested countries and amongst the most vulnerable countries to climate change is the host country.. The project targets primarily households (with a particular focus on indigenous people) in the Philippines, with no previous ICS access.  The project provides high efficiency biomass cookstoves, replacing existing inefficient open fire cooking methods. By providing the tools and education, project households are able to dramatically reduce their biomass fuel consumption; greatly reduce indoor air pollution including harmful particulate matter, reduce the emission of greenhouse gasses associated with burning biomass fuel; and free-up significant time for more productive uses such as employment or education that would otherwise be spent collecting fuel wood/cooking. 

SD Environmental Projects Inc and Climate Secure India Private Limited will manage the implementation, operation, and ongoing support of the project as the project implementer. 

Thus, the CLiC-Philippines project will bring a positive change to the livelihood of communities vulnerable to climate change by creating sustainable energy access and dependence.
vcs-3357: The project includes restoration of degraded mangrove habitats through the planting of 4,500,000 mangrove seedlings in discrete parcels of land on a total area of 1000 hectares across the island of Sri Lanka. The objective of this project is to initiate a long-term community-based conservation and management programme to increase the extent of tropical mangrove forests and local biodiversity in Sri Lanka.  This project will also provide forest goods and services to the local community members in a sustainable manner.

vcs-3361: The objective of the project is to restore degraded mangrove ecosystems in the estuarine islands of several rivers in coastal Karnataka, including the Aghanashini, Sharavathi and Kali rivers, and their tributaries. The three rivers form an integral part of the coastal ecosystem of Uttara Kannada District of Karnataka, India.The project objective is to restore the degarded mangrove habitats through plantation of several, diverse native mangrove and mangrove associated species, including several species which had disappeared from the region following degradation and deforestation of the mangrove habitat.
vcs-3363: A forest carbon credit project to create greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions and removals by converting privately owned operational forest lands to protected forest lands.   The grouped project will be implemented following the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VM0012 – Improved Forest Management in Temperate and Boreal Forests (LtPF), v1.2 methodology. The project is located throughout Germany.
vcs-3364: The Grouped Project Activity (GPA) intends to generate Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) through the charging of electric vehicles (EVs) through EV charging systems, including their associated infrastructure, whose GHG emission reductions are achieved through the displacement of emissions from conventional fossil fuel vehicles used for passenger and freight transportation as a result of the electricity delivered by the project chargers. The usage of electricity powered cars instead of fossil fuel powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven.
vcs-3365: The project will reduce CO2 emissions by taking appropriate preventive measures for drivers and curbing forest degradation. vcs-3366:
Shanxi Qinyuan Afforestation Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Qinyuan County, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province of China. The aim of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and to contribute to the local sustainable development by planting the trees and shrubs on the barren mountains and barren land.
4,949.40 of forest is about to be planted by direct planting on the barren mountain and barren land in Qinyuan County, and the planted species are all native species including Pinus tabuliformis (Chinese pine), Fraxinus L. (white wax), Prunus davidiana. (wild peach), Acer truncatum (Mono Maple), Armeniaca sibirica (apricot), Quercus Liaotungensis (oak), Forsythia suspensa (Forsythias Fructus) . The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forest, and bring income and job opportunities for local communities and residents.
vcs-3368:
Orizon’s CarbonCrop Programme supports and incentivizes South African farmers/landowners in the transition towards more sustainable agricultural practices by paying out a majority share of the carbon credit revenues resulting from emission reductions and carbon sequestration on our participating project fields. Together with our partners, we support our farmers by providing tailored financial and practical advice, building online tools to assist farmers in their transition, hosting information sessions/webinars and contributing to local research on sustainable agriculture.
The program, with its project boundaries being the geographic boundaries of the Republic of South Africa, will be registered as a grouped project under VM0042 - Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management. Each project activity will be carried out and monitored according to this methodology and its supporting methodologies, standards, and tools. Over time this project will include various types of farming practices /land types by adding instances that meet the additionality and applicability conditions as per the methodology.
Our vision is to be a comprehensive partner for our current and future farmers in their regenerative journey, support further research and investment into Regenerative Agriculture (“RA”) and to ultimately help drive a national shift to improve soil health and productivity to secure the long-term future of agriculture in South Africa.
vcs-3369:
The project installs new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to a group of 4 existing swine farms in Liangshan Yi Autonomous prefecture, Sichuan Province. The purpose of the project is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The project replaces the current open anaerobic lagoons with new AWMSs, and each subsidiary swine farm will install one AWMS. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated solid are treated in aerobic composting system to produce fertilizer and part of the fertilizer will be distributed to the surrounding farmers free of charge to improve the life condition of farmers and the others will be sold to the market. The separated liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to the power generation equipment, the power generated are all used by the operation of AWMSs and the swine farms, which was provided by the region power grid. And other surplus biogas is destroyed through the flaring system (if any).
After anaerobic digestion. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the separated solid and the effluent will be used as a liquid organic fertilizer for the irrigation of agriculture.
It is estimated that total 5,063.52*104m3 biogas are expected to be generated annually and each generator is installed in each subsidiary swine farm, total installed capacity of the project is 7.4MW and the annual electricity generation is estimated to be 65,824MWh.
vcs-3371:

(hereafter referred to as “Improved Cookstoves” or “ICS”) in Uganda. Each CPA will support the project
goals of reducing fuel consumption, improving health, and reducing deforestation in Uganda
vcs-3373: The proposed grouped project activity seeks to reduce greenhouse gases emissions by disseminating the high energy efficient solar water pumps for agricultural activities to Indian farmers who were using the inefficient electricity pumps in baseline scenario. The proposed grouped project activity seeks to increase access of solar water pumps which are zero greenhouse gas emitting being operated on the solar energy. Their old low efficiency and high greenhouse gas emitting electricity pumps would be replaced. The implementation of the project activity, will result in the reduction of consumption of grid electricity and DG sets & consequent emissions from combustion leading to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases by promoting the renewable solar pumps to the farmers.
vcs-3377: Huilong Area Deqing County Methane Emission Reduction in Rice Cultivation Project (hereafter referred to “the project” or “project”) is located in Huilong area, Deqing County, Zhaoqing City, Guangdong Province, China. The project activity consists of the implementation of an intermittent irrigation system to replace the traditional continuous flooding method in double-season rice cultivation in order to improve water management and reduce methane emissions from the paddy fields. The project utilizes cement ditches, pumps and vales to enable farmers to switch from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded conditions for the rice cultivation paddy fields. The intermittent irrigation also contributes to enhancing the grain yield and conserving water resources thus improving the sustainability of the cropland production. The project involves a total cultivated agricultural area about 5,428 hectares in Huilong Area, Deqing County.
vcs-3378:
Animal Manure Management System (AMMS) GHG Mitigation Project In Huoqiu county Anhui province is located at Shidian Town, Huoqiu County, Lu’an City, Anhui Province, P.R.China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Huoqiu huizhao Renewable Energy Technology Co., Ltd.. The project will introduce a new waste management system to treat animal manure from 8 livestock farms in Huoqiu County to replace the current open anaerobic lagoons. The treated manure is collected by tank trucks from the livestock farms to the project and the collected material is subsequently treated. 
By treating the manure with closed anaerobic digesters, the project avoids the emission of methane that would be generated from animal manure in current
open anaerobic lagoons. The biogas generated during the treatment process will be partly used for electricity generation and the rest will be supplied to
users nearby for heat generation. The electricity generated will be supplied to East China Power Grid (ECPG) to displace equivalent electricity from ECPG
dominated by fossil fuel-fired plants. The fermented sludge from the closed anaerobic digesters will be treated in aerobic composting system and used as
fertilizer. Wastewater from the treatment system will be used for agriculture irrigation.

In the baseline scenario, farmers in Yueyang County use continuously flooded method in rice paddies with the straw on field as the organic amendment inputs, which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Yueyang County changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. The PlanTogo project aims to establish 120.230 hectares of forest plantations in Maritime , Plateaux and Centrale Regions of Togo, over a period of 10 years (2021 2030). The main forest species to be planted are eucalyptus , khaya and gmelina , the project also considers the planting of other species such as bamboo and cashew .
T he purpose of these plantations is to restore degraded lands in the short term and the sustainable production of goods an services in the medium and long term, while contributing to local development and fight against climate change by sequestering CO2.
The project developer is Sequoia Plantations Togo ( who will implement the plantations under two modalities: i) on their own lands and ii) on communal or smallholders lands to who S PT will provide seedlings and technical assistance. Sequoia Plantations Togo is responsible of project monitoring through the entire crediting period.
SPT is a Grouped Project, and project areas are selected considering the land eligibility requirements of the VCS, that is, on lands where there have been no native ecosystems in the last 10 years and without forest at the beginning of the plantation activities. The areas identified for the first instance are constituted by grasslands and shrublands, and current land use is extensive agriculture or cattle grassing. SPT will allow intercropping in the first years of the plantations.
The reforestation activities proposed by Sequoia Plantations Togo will generate a switch in land covert from non-forest to forest and it will lead to the creation of a carbon stock in biomass and in the soil greater than that existing under current conditions. The Net GHG emission removals expected in 20 years is 1 45 690 569 tCO2e (7 284 528 tCO2e/yr)
vcs-3397: The Kruger to Canyons Rangeland Restoration Project is a grouped project located in the globally significant Kruger to Canyons Biosphere Reserve. The area has lost soil carbon due to unrestricted animal movements and high grazing intensities leading to low productivity and bare ground, while this is exacerbated by unfavorable herd structures. Unrestricted grazing is occurring due to a ‘tragedy of the commons’ where communal areas are over-utilized for livestock grazing and knowledge of sustainable grazing practices have lapsed. The project aims to reverse historic rangeland degradation on communal rangelands by introducing rotational grazing through herding and improved animal husbandry, and removing and reducing Greenhouse Gases in the process. Furthermore, project participants will benefit from improved access to livestock markets.

Initially the project activity plans to reforest up to 13,939 hectares of riparian areas currently occupied by unmanaged grassland along the banks of ten hydropower reservoirs in the State of São Paulo, Brazil, with native forest species. However, the project faces financial difficulties to maintain the reforestation along the years. It’s important to remember that the market of carbon credit ten years ago was worse than now. Considering this, a new objective was set and the project plans to reforest approximately 6,400 hectares of riparian areas until 2030.
 The objectives of the project activity are to:
•	Restore the structure, function, and ecosystem services of riparian forests located along the borders of ten hydropower reservoirs.
•	Enhance the biodiversity of degraded riparian areas and contribute to the creation of ecological connectivity along the rivers.
•	Increase carbon sequestration in riparian forests.
•	Improve water recharge in the reservoirs and control soil and water erosion.
•	Contribute to stop and reverse land degradation processes in the State of São Paulo, with special focus on riparian ecosystems; and,
•	Provide employment and recreational opportunities for local residents in the vicinity of the reservoirs.
From 2001 to 2021, AES Tietê reforested around 4,696 hectares of non-contiguous lands along the reservoirs. AES Tietê initiated these activities in 2001 to protect and reforest riparian areas bordering its reservoirs by testing and observing the results of different afforestation/reforestation practices. Those tests were conducted by (1) planting native species in protected areas, which had not demonstrated spontaneous natural regeneration; and (2) including between 80 and 126 native species for completing reforestation of the areas. The results of those tests demonstrated that these protected areas will only regenerate natural forest cover through human reforestation activities and will not naturally regenerate.

The project utilizes cement ditches, pumps and vales to enable farmers to switch from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded conditions for the rice cultivation paddy fields. The intermittent irrigation also contributes to enhancing the grain yield and conserving water resources thus improving the sustainability of the cropland production. The project involves a total cultivated agricultural area about 6,975 hectares in Wencun area.
