The proposed ARR-VCS project is a large-scale grouped project centered on the reforestation of degraded lands in Spain. According to the country’s National Action Plan for the UNCCD, approx. 74% of Spain is at risk of desertification and 18% of the land is at high risk of becoming irreversibly desert. This grouped project aims for the long-term restoration of Spain’s forests, achieved through native, mixed-species reforestation that reverses the impact of land degradation, prevents the loss of flora and fauna and improves biodiversity. The planting employs the latest technologies and planting techniques to support the permanent establishment of native forests in predicted bioclimates that may benefit rural communities in time. The long term resilience of forest and vegetation composition will be monitored by an extensive monitoring system to track the effectiveness and resilience of project activities.
The project is managed by Land Life, a tech-driven reforestation company that plants trees at scale to restore degraded ecosystems globally in hubs like Europe, the US and Australia. In Spain, Land Life’s local team based in Burgos ensures the boots-on-the-ground and maintains a close collaboration with local partners and authorities. 
Project activities are implemented and monitored according to approved large scale project methodology AR-ACM0003, with more project instances to be added over the coming years (up to 10,000 ha expected). The first set of project instances covers 167.46 ha of degraded land in Spain, at 4 distinct planting sites: Campos, Pancorbo, Villapadierna and Grisel. To date, a total of 147,369 native trees have been planted in the project areas and these will sequester approximately  49,792 tCO2e over a project crediting period of 60 years. Within this time frame, 40 years are accounted for in each project instance due to land agreement contract terms. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals is 1,245 tCO2e.

vcs-3420: The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in Baoshan City, Yunnan Province, China, with a total acreage of 22,853 ha of single-cropping rice. Without the project, there would be no ditches, pumps, valves, and reservoirs to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario in which rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the paddy soil under flooded conditions, a large amount of methane can be released, so the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to saving water, improving rice yield and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.

Junshan District, which is located on the north of Dongting Lake, is one of the major rice producing districts in China, has a population about 246,516, and annual household income of farmers is only CNY 35,932. The project is located in East of Junshan District, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China, with a total acreage of 7,925.01 ha for double-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in East of Junshan District.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Junshan District use continuously flooded method in rice paddies with the straw on field as the organic amendment inputs, which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Junshan District changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.

The Project Activity is planting trees to restore the area, improve biodiversity, improve livelihoods of the local communities around the degraded forests and join the fight against climate change which has become a threat of global warming to the planet. The project will increase the sequestration capacity of carbon dioxide and other Greenhouse gases by increasing the forest and vegetative cover.
The project will contribute to the removal of GHG from the atmosphere. Through the plantation of teak, which is a wood biomass, its implemented on degraded forest reserve. Which without human influence and financial support will remain degraded, especially due to rapid depletion on and off-reserve stocks. This would lead to loss of carbon sinks and the negative climatical conditions will be evidence, impacting the social and economic activities of the region.
The carbon project will be managed by Private Afforestation Developers Organisation (PADO) which is an umbrella Organisation of private forest plantation developers in Ghana. They are the legal owners of the plantations located in Ghana; Kumasi at Kwamisa Forest Reserve located at Offinso Forest District within the Ashanti Region of Ghana. The reserve lies midway between Kumasi-Techiman and the Kumasi–Sunyani Road about 35 miles north of Kumasi.
The ARR activities are carried out and monitored according to approved project methodology AR-ACM0003 (Ver 2.0) for a project period of 40 years. The project expected to remove 26,281 t/CO2e annually and 1,051,223 tCO2e during its entire life.  The project has an goal to achieve forest plantations recovering 3010 hectares (ha) from degraded forest reserve in a total project zone of 5225 ha. The area was a degraded land Prior to the project implementation caused by a serious fire disaster in 1983 which engulfed Ghana and led to   massive forest degradation and severe hunger crisis.

The project includes both revegetation techniques in and around agricultural land, on different lands of the Republic of South Africa, providing resilient systems to protect the agricultural land from extreme weather events. The project proposes both the IALM and ARR methodologies together, at different GIS delineated areas on each project instance (land), the agricultural methodology will incorporate regenerative agricultural practices as well as circular use of by-products from the farm, as well as neighbouring farms. 
The ARR compartment of the project will include revegetation of native flora around the farm, facilitating ecological resilience to the project instance and sustaining pollinators throughout the year. This will be scaled to vegetation unit specific revegetation activities and regenerative agricultural practices as applicable per the Improved Agricultural Land Management methodology of the Verified Carbon Standard. This project intends to look at the system instead of looking on how to apply a methodology onto the land, a larger look at biota and their interaction in applied stewardship.
The first project instances occur in the Western Cape province, Southern Cape area of Knysna where a matrix landscape of Fynbos (ever-green shrubland, indicative of Mediterranean climates) and Temperate Forest was found historically.

This project activity targets the restoration and conservation of 30,000 hectares of degraded and deforested lands in the highlands of eastern Tigray. The project area is located inside the Desa’a State Forest which is a dry Afromontane forest and lies between the Tigrinian plateau and the Afar lowlands (elevation between 3100 and 900 m a.s.l.), stretching along the Western edge of the Great Rift Valley escarpment of Ethiopia. The fragmented forest covers about 154,071 ha and is the largest Afromontane remnant forest in Tigray. The restoration project consists of active planting, assisted natural regeneration and conservation activities. In addition to the forest establishment and protection activities, soil and water conservation activities are implemented, including stone check dams, hill side stone terraces, trenches, small ponds and micro basins. 
It is a community-oriented project, which means that a participatory and inclusive approach is taken with the aim to improve the livelihoods of local communities. The degradation of the ecosystem in the project area is the result of unsustainable use and management over a longer period. These practices of overexploitation were mainly driven by grazing, firewood collection and timber extraction in a context of insufficient law enforcement and resource use planning. The drivers of deforestation are being addressed through a combination of providing alternative livelihood opportunities and improving management and law enforcement capacities. The recovery of the forest will restore the carbon stocks in the vegetation and the soil. A vital component of the project is the conservation and enhancement of biological diversity and the promotion of assisted natural regeneration. The project will result into an estimated GHG removal of in total 4.746.785tCO2-e over a period of 50 years.

Juruá REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Amazônia Agroindústria EIRELI, in order to foster forest conservation and the reduction of potential greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions based on a local economic development model that values the “standing” forest through the integration of non-timber forest product management and trading of environmental services.

Juruá REDD+ Project is located at Seringal Valparaíso property, in the Alto Juruá region, between the municipalities of Cruzeiro do Sul and Porto Walter, including an area of 24,076 hectares. Juruá River basin is formed by four micro-basins: the micro-basin of Igarapé do Meio, the micro-basin of Igarapé Primeiro de Março and the Igarapé Grande micro-basin, in addition to the Valparaiso river basin (micro-basin) itself, which is the main drainage network of the rubber plantation region.

The purpose of the project is to reduce GHG emissions from activities regarding to conserve the forest and its natural resources, as well as to maintain carbon stocks, through activities that promote the reduction of deforestation in the region, such as the improvement of patrimonial vigilance, the monitoring of land use change and land cover using satellite images and strengthening the management of non-timber forest products. The performance of activities allied to a good project management, with continuous monitoring and evaluation of activities and results, will allow the Project to reach the expected goals and effects.

Therefore, it is expected that Juruá REDD+ Project prevents, by curbing deforestation, about 413,927 tCO2e by reducing GHG emissions throughout 30 years of the project. All the proposed activities to curb deforestation will become economically feasible if the management of non-timber forest products is combined with the trading of carbon credits through REDD+ carbon crediting mechanisms.

Guiyang Afforestation Project (hereafter refer to as “the project”) is located at Guiyang City.
10,158.2 ha (152,373 Mu ) of forest was planted on suitable land for afforestation in Guiyang City where used to be poorly sustainable in terms of ecological environment and suffer from karst rocky desertification. Prior to the project, the project area was suitable land for forest, there is no forestry management and the coverage by planting trees is low, and there has never been any activity affecting the local ecosystem . By checking the afforestation plan with the Guiyang Forestry Bureau, it was confirmed that a small number of trees have been planted in the project area before the afforestation project. However, the forest coverage rate is relatively low. Therefore, considering this situation, the Guiyang Forestry Bureau determined that the project area is suitable for afforestation after investigation, then the Forestry Bureau approved the supplementary planting without disturbing the existing trees to increase the vegetative cover. The forest farm and Guiyang Forestry Industry Development Co., Ltd implement the afforestation project, and Guiyang Forestry Industry Development Co., Ltd is authorized to apply for carbon sink projects on behalf of the forest farm, and to implement management activities such as monitoring.
The project is to plant without disturbing the existing trees, and only the trees actually planted in the project were monitored. The carbon credit of the original trees in the baseline scenario will not be monitored or counted in the actual net GHG removals by sinks.

The Lomphat Wildlife Sanctuary (LWS) belongs to Eastern Plain Landscape (EPL) was established in 1993 by the Cambodia royal government, covering an area 250,000 hectares within the provinces of Ratanakiri (accounting for approximately 80%) and Mondulkiri (20% of the area). Most of Lomphat land areas are dominated by dry deciduous forest and followed by semi-evergreen and evergreen forest, grassland, traditional crops, ponds, streams and Repos River that are reliable for thousands of endangered, vulnerable, and rare species. LWS has also been marked in recent years with significant impacts of human activities including: deforestation, mining, land conversion for agriculture, forest encroachment, new road construction, hunting and trapping, resettlement and increasing population. To ensure the effective protection of the EPL-LWS, conservation actions need to promote the significance of forests while helping to address and support sustainable livelihood development of the local population.
From 2010 to 2018, the loss of forest cover in LWS has increased by 16.4% or 41,659.30 hectares, resulting in the loss of biodiversity and greater pressures on endangered species. BirdLife International Program in Cambodia (BirdLife) in close collaboration with the Ministry of Environment (MoE) and NGO partners, has supported and lead conservation activities in the region with the focus on capacity development for law enforcement, forest monitoring, preservation of endangered species and facilitating local community participation. In 2018, the project expanded its strategic approach for LWS to incorporate carbon finance, specifically REDD+, which have been defined as the most appropriate mechanism for addressing financial sustainability, refining activities for natural resource management and providing key benefits for community development and livelihoods. This initiative is also contributes to the 3rd strategic direction of Cambodia's Climate Change Strategic Plan (CCCSP).

vcs-3449: Forest plantations in Brazil make up around 1% of the country's area, and are responsible for 91% of all wood production for industrial purposes. Located in the department of Meta, Cabuyaro is a municipality whose surface equals to 832 kilometers square, with a population of 5,432 inhabitants, and an altitude of 151 meters above the sea level (DANE, Censo Nacional de Poblacion y Vivienda, 2018). The project is located in Guayabal, a small town in Cabuyaro composed of 204 inhabitants who mainly work the land, growing a variety of crops such as plantain, cassava, papaya, passion fruit, corn, soy, and cacao which are mainly sold in the local market of Villavicencio.
This is a grouped project, the first area to be verified, consists of a total of 2,258 hectares composed of degraded pastures in majority and conservation areas, at the baseline. Of which 1,764 hectares will be established in an agroforestry system, with cacao being the perennial crop planted with other trees for shading purposes (Gliricidia sepium) and boundary purposes (windbreakers -Cariniana pyriformis). This agroforestry system has the goal of increase the soil organic carbon, as well as the aboveground and below ground biomass, and will recover the soil health and fertility through time. Other relevant agricultural practices that will be implemented are proper residue management as crop/tree materials that are periodically pruned are left in the soil for decomposition to build organic matter, processing of the cacao husks to produce organic fertilizer to be applied back in the field, as well as planting cover crops in bare soil areas, irrigation,  and planting boundary trees to prevent erosion and reduce wind damage to the cacao.
The rest of the project area, 491 hectares, corresponds to other uses such as drainage channels, internal roads, and conservation areas which included native forest species, called morichales, riparian zones, and secondary forests. The total project area is divided into two properties, Espejuelos (1,258 hectares) and Primavera (1,000 hectares).

The primary objective of the Harpia Grouped REDD+ Project is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) of the Amazon rainforest and, as a grouped project, offers the possibility to expand the conservation to other areas in the future. The first instance is composed of 3 properties, with a project area of 18,700.24 ha, located in Cotriguaçu, State of Mato Grosso.

Besides the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities. The contribution to sustainability is being monitored through the application of the SOCIALCARBON® Standard.

The present REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 3,681 ha of deforestation, equating to 1,552,613 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (09-December-2019 to 08-December-2049), with an annual average of 51,753 tCO2e.

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in the southern part of Jining City, Shandong Province, China, with a total acreage of 19,030 ha of single-cropping rice. Without the project, there would be no ditches, pumps, valves, and reservoirs to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario in which rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the paddy soil under flooded conditions, a large amount of methane can be released, so the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to saving water, improving rice yield and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir construction, pumps and valves installation, training, etc. According to the needs of rice growth, farmers use pumps and valves to control irrigation and drainage, which not only saves water resources but also reduces methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions. Through the pumps and valves, the necessary water can be supplied to the rice paddies in time in the dry season, and the excess water can be drained from the rice paddies in the rainy season. In this case, the methane emission can be declined by an average of 48%. Hence, with the proposed project activity, the estimated GHG reduction from rice is 3.06 tCO2e/ha.

Linxiang District is a county-level city in Hunan Province, is managed by Yueyang City. Linxiang located in the northeast of Hunan Province, is known as the Gateway to Northern Hunan, is one of the major rice producing districts in China, has a population about 541,864, and annual household income of farmers is only CNY 35,511. The project is located in South of Linxiang District, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China, with a total acreage of 8,155.00 ha for double-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in south of Linxiang City.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Linxiang District use continuously flooded method in rice paddies with the straw on field as the organic amendment inputs, which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Linxiang District changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.

vcs-3475: The ACABA REDD+ Project is located in the General Community Council of the Baudó River and its Tributaries (ACABA) on the Pacific coast of the department of Chocó. The Project contains very humid tropical forest with transition to tropical pluvial forest, and has unique habitat conditions for both flora and fauna. It is considered an invaluable region at the national and international level and is classified as one of the of the most biodiverse hotspots on Earth, characterized by the presence of endemic species. Significant and exponential deforestation has occurred in the region over time, which according to the IDEAM forest monitoring report for the 2010-2017 period was 10,559 ha. This scenario is the caused by a lack of territorial planning, which in turn results in processes associated with wood extraction, the expansion of the agricultural frontier, the establishment of crops for illicit use, unplanned infrastructure, the construction of new road accesses, and itinerant open-pit mining. The project uses a standalone approach and an annual average of 208,556 tCO2e are expected to be reduced with a total reduction of 6,465,226 tCO2e over the project’s lifetime of thirty years. With the implementation of the REDD+ project, the community will achieve the reduction of emissions resulting from deforestation and forest degradation, and thereby environmental and social benefits will be generated. Additionally, economic resources will be available to be invested in the creation of productive opportunities aimed at improving the living conditions of the inhabitants, in alignment with the ACABA ethno-development plan. The Project is eligible under the VCS Program and uses the VM0009, v3 Methodology. The project will have a AUDD activity type baseline scenario, using Colombia’s national Forest Reference Emissions Levels (FREL). The project will generate GHG emission reductions by reducing unplanned deforestation, covering activities within the scope of the VCS Program.
vcs-3476: The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Jharkhand, India. The project is being conducted in the spread across all the districts of Jharkhand. CCX entered into carbon offset agreements with individual farmers of various districts of Jharkhand state for the provision of carbon credit advisory services to them. The individual farmers are the owners of the lands on which trees are being grown to sequester carbon and reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the atmosphere. CCX has mobilized the farmers in the selected states of India to plant various tree species on their lands. These tree species range from fruit-bearing trees like Indian blackberry, Guava, and Mango to commercial species like Teak, Mahogany Sandal, etc. The selected farmers have employed simple tree cultivation techniques involving planting saplings in the pits with minimum disturbance to the lands.

vcs-3479: The Amigos de Calakmul Community Forest Conservation Program (ACAC Program) is focused on protecting the forests and preventing land use change in the Calakmul Biosphere Reserve in Mexico. The program works with local communities called ejidos that reside in the reserve's buffer zone and area of influence. Instead of timber harvesting, participating ejidos receive conservation payments and social program support. Phase 1 of the program covers 10 ejidos and 95,077 hectares. The ejido members in the program area have limited livelihood options, and timber harvesting can be a significant economic activity, both legal and illegal. The Yucatan Peninsula has experienced significant forest and timber harvesting in the area leading to forest degradation, human access, and biodiversity loss. The program also focuses on diversifying income sources and improving livelihoods through productive projects, emphasizing community participation and input gathering. It was developed under the methodology VM0010 under VCS and will also be validated under the CCB.

Core CarbonX Solutions Private Limited (CCX) is a carbon management consultancy company with registered office in the state of Odisha. CCX is the Project Proponent (PP) of the carbon offset project called “Core Carbon Vanam (Sericulture) in Odsha State”. CCX entered into carbon offset agreements with individual farmers of various districts of Odisha state for provision of carbon credit advisory services to them. The individual farmers are the owners of the lands on which trees are being grown to sequester carbon and reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the atmosphere. CCX has mobilized the farmers in the selected states of India to plant various tree species on their lands. These tree species range from trees like Asana, Arjuna covering Sericulture sector. Simple tree cultivation techniques involving planting saplings in the pits with minimum disturbance to the lands have been employed by the selected farmers. 
The villages under the project area predominantly have an agrarian economy where most of its population depends on agriculture. The major agroforestry plantation in these project districts (Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj & Sundergarh) are Asana, Arjuna etc . The planation was done by the farmers and utilized the subsidies to avail the saplings. The saplings do the sequestration of carbon dioxide at faster pace and ultimately reduces GHG emissions. 
The Project Activity will lead to considerable carbon sequestration in the project areas and will contribute strongly to the sustainable development of rural villages involved in the project.
Initially, 6,300 hectares of land has been selected for the first project activity instance. Through carbon sequestration by the planted trees, the project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions or removals of 62811 tCO2e.

The purpose of this grouped project (Program) is to replace the traditional practice of flooded irrigation (baseline) with System of Root Intensification (SRI) technique in rice cultivation (project). SRI is an intermittent wet and dry technique of cultivation which induces positive socio-economic and environmental impacts by reducing water consumption and increasing crop yield compared to baseline. This also results in reduced GHG emission emissions associated with energy use in water pumping and methane avoidance associated with standing water in farm fields compared to the baseline. Increase in yield and reduced water and energy consumption also yields socio-economic benefits to the farmers.  
The first project activity instance (VPA) under the program is located in the state of Odisha in India. In the baseline, farmers were using traditional agriculture practice of rice cultivation and replaced it with SRI in the project activity. The area covered in this VPA is up to 500 hectares. In the project activity, emission reductions happen due to methane avoidance from the farm fields and reduced electricity consumption. However, emission reductions due to methane avoidance alone, are being claimed under the program. It is estimated that 60,000 tCO2e of emission reductions will be generated per annum.
vcs-3505: The proposed project El Espinillar is located in the Northwestern part of Uruguay and covers nearly 2,956 hectares. The project region has a long history of sugar cane production for the beverage market in Uruguay.  Ancap Beberage and Alcohol Company (Compañía Ancap de Bebidas y Alcoholes S.A – CABA) was a Uruguayan company dedicated to the manufacturing and marketing of alcoholic beverage and liquors. The project region El Espinillar supplied the value chain with irrigated sugar cane production on Government-owned lands. In the early 90s, due to national economic reforms, the land was sold to several private owners with the aim of diversifying and boosting regional productivity. After that, coarse crop (e.g. maize) production with furrow irrigation and livestock farming activities were the main activities in the region. However, these activities were done under unsustainable practices leading to soil degradation. Following the aim to restore the soil, sequester carbon from the atmosphere and increase the yields per hectare, the project was established in 2019, with the focus on planting trees that produce high-value crops such as citrus fruits (lemon, mandarins, oranges, persimmon caqui), avocados, nuts (pecan, macadamia, almonds), and essential oil crops (e.g. eucalyptus). Through the photosynthesis of the newly planted trees, the project generates GHG emission removals up to 4,400 tons annually, while delivering ecological and socio-economic benefits at the same time. To ensure the success of the project activity, the project proponent seeks to establish irrigation systems, implement conservative measures to recover the degraded soil and achieve climate-neutral production. The project area also counts with a small extension of native riparian forest which will remain protected. The project will deliver economic, social, and ecological benefits to the local communities while making a significant contribution to the battle against climate change on a global scale.

vcs-3535:
Andhra Pradesh has been historically called the Rice Bowl of India and continues to be the country's largest rice producer. The agriculture system forms the backbone of economic development and contributes 32.79 % of the total State Domestic Product.
The proposed Natural Farming in Andhra Pradesh activity is practised by individual farmers practised by about 5,00,000 farmers and organic grower cooperatives covering 6,41,230 hectares of cropland in the state of Andhra Pradesh to be implemented in the first phase. The project aims at increasing the capacity of soil to sequester carbon, enhance the carbon sequestration by agroforestry practices such as planting of trees, reduce emissions from the use of synthetic fertilizers and reduce emissions from burning of crop residue by application of VCS methodology: VM0017 Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM). Several SALM practices and technologies have been proven to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and prevent climate change by enhancing carbon storage in soils, preserving existing soil carbon, and reducing carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide emissions. Those practices include conservation tillage, cover crops, enhanced crop rotations, residue retention, agroforestry and avoidance of crop residue burning. The project holistically aims at achieving sustainable management practices which improve soil health, reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and develop the socio-economic status of the project area. The project aims to reduce and sequester carbon leading to estimated GHG emission reductions or removals (tCO2e) of 4830706 tCO2e / year. This project's climate benefits include emissions reduction or removals of approximately 193228248 tCO2e over the lifetime of the project.
vcs-3538: Alternate-wetting and drying (AWD) has been identified as one of the promising water management technologies that can correct the inefficient water use in irrigated rice ecosystem, hence conserving water for irrigating more rice fields.  It uses a simple tool called an observation well, which guides farmers on the timing and depth of irrigation water to apply. This can save irrigation water up to 30% at the field level without yield penalty. The periodic (or intermittent) aeration of the subsoil also reduces methane emission emanating from decomposing organic matter that occur in flooded rice fields. Emission reductions are sold to then provide a basis for rewarding farmers for their commitment to the Project with a financial incentive to supplement their income. Thus, AWD allows rice farmers to adapt to water scarcity and mitigates methane emissions in parallel. The Project represents the first stage of a nationwide program in which the next stage will be the UPRIIS irrigated system in Luzon.

Gansu Xiaolongshan Afforestation Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in the suburbs of Hui County, Liangdang County, Li County of Longnan City, suburbs of Qinzhou District, Maiji District, Qingshui County, Wushan County of Tianshui City, suburbs of Min County, Zhang County of Dingxi City, Gansu Province of China, whose aim is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren or degraded lands. The project is implemented by Gansu Xiaolongshan Forestry Conservation Center. 
3,738.23 ha (56073.4 Mu) of forest is to be planted by direct planting on barren lands in Tianshui City, Longnan City and Dingxi City, including seven suburbs and two counties: Qinzhou District, Maiji District, Qingshui County, Wushan County, Hui County, Liangdang County, Li County, Min County and Zhang County. All the project sites were previously barren lands. There is no natural renewal and afforestation before the project.
The implementation of the project would generate GHG emission removals and improve local environment through growing of the trees, increase income of local residents by offering job opportunities from the project, enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing their relevant technical skills and training, and increase local biodiversity as a result of establishing a forest of native trees (Styphnolobium japonicum, Robinia pseudoacacia, Pinus, Picea)
The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 2,721,683 tCO2e in 60 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 45,361 tCO2e.

The proposed project is located a 170-acre plot of land approximately 7km South East from the town centre of Mymensingh City, Bangladesh. The electricity generated from the project will be supplied to Bangladesh National Power Grid, which is owned and operated by Power Grid Company of Bangladesh Ltd. (PGCB). vcs-3546: The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in Changshou District, Chongqing City of China. Changshou District is located in the centre part of Chongqing, with a total acreage of 15,727 ha for single-cropping rice. Without implementing this project, which provides ditches to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 865,564 tCO2e in 21 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 41,217.3 tCO2e.
vcs-3549: “Community Forest Plantation in India” is a combined Afforestation and sustainable development project carried out by farmers with the help of a project implementer. Farmers received training from the project implementer for plantation and the project implementer (Greenovation) is providing plantation material (saplings, manure) to the farmers and further assistance in maintaining the required survival rate of the plantation. Carbon credits generated from this project will help in maintaining the survival rate of planted trees and support farmers. The total area expected to be covered in the project is around 10,000 hectares. The current plantations have been covered to plant 4,400 hectares in the country.The project participants are using the afforestation approach and planted thousands of trees on the land across the project boundary. In case of the absence of this project activity land would be continued to be less productive land or degraded land. The project will help in mitigating climate change for the next 40 years by sequestrating/removing the carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and creating a carbon pool. The project activity will result in an annual average of 1,40,882 tons of GHG removal and total removal of 56,35,266 tons of CO2 over the 40 years of the period.

“Community Forest Initiative in India” is an sustainable afforestation development project carried out by the local farmers with the help of a local NGO. The farmers plant trees on the abandoned wasteland allotted to the communities and retain ownership of the trees, produce, from forestation. Project activity has been planned for helping farmers in developing forest for which they have received plantation material, Irrigation technology and other training received from NGO to establish and maintain the planted forest. NGO empowers the large group of poor communities in West Bengal and Odisha states of India to create & manage the forest on degraded abandoned land to increase forest cover by planting fruit-bearing species. Apart from above, the NGOs helps in managing and sustainably harvesting the NTFPs (Non-Timber Forest Products) for participating farmers. 
The carbon credits from this project activity will also create a new ‘virtual’ cash crop for the participants, who gain all the direct benefits of growing trees and receive benefits based on the GHG benefits created by their efforts (as a result-based payment approach). The maturing trees and conservation activity will provide additional sustainable benefits such as income in form of the carbon payments, climate change mitigation self-resilience and sustainable. . The project will help in mitigating climate change for the next 40 years by sequestrating the carbon from the atmosphere and creating a natural biomass carbon pool. NGO has estimated that this project will result in an annual average of GHG removal of 1,45,278 tonnes/annual and total removals of 58,11,102 tonnes of CO2 for 40 years of project duration.
vcs-3553: Grouped Reforestation Project on Degraded Land and Fallow Agricultural Land is located within the borders of India. The project plans to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. The project activity was implemented in 125824 hectares. The Jutaituba REDD+ Project is a partnership between the Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Martins Agropecuária, belonging to the Martins Group and aims to promote forest conservation and mitigate climate change by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from changes in land use. In addition to climate benefits, the Project also aims to generate socio-environmental benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and the improvement of the well-being of surrounding communities, while preserving the culture and tradition of local peoples.
The Project Area has 129,417 ha of Amazon rainforest and is located almost entirely in the mesoregion of Marajó, in the State of Pará, covering the cities of Bagre, Portel, Baião and Oeiras do Pará. It is located near BR 422, known as the Transcametá highway, and near the rivers Pacajá, Jacundá and Tocantins. Communities that are directly or indirectly influenced by the Project were identified, either because they provide labor to Fazenda Jutaituba or are geographically close to the Project Area and depend on the forest resources present in the area, such as nuts and medicinal herbs.
The region has great relevance in relation to its biodiversity, being an ecological corridor that makes it possible to connect Conservation Units (UCs) that are nearby. The predominant vegetation is the Dense Ombrophilous Forest with a high density of medium and large trees, as well as woody and epiphytic lianas. It houses at least 24 species of fauna and flora with some degree of threat according to the IUCN Red List, some of which are endemic to the region.
Thus, the Jutaituba REDD+ Project hopes, in addition to climate impacts, to improve the well-being of communities and generate exceptional benefits for local biodiversity.
vcs-3591: The Mayas Project aims to protect and restore a 33,747 hectare area of peat swamp forest in Ketapang District, West Kalimantan Province, Republic of Indonesia. At the time of the project’s intervention the area was in the process of being drained, selectively logged and partially converted to industrial tree plantation in line with a government approved management plan. This would have resulted in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions averaging over 2m tCO2e per year, irreversible loss of globally important biodiversity and a negative impact on the livelihoods and wellbeing of people living around the project area. MPK will fully protect the remaining peat forest areas (now named The Mayas Project) and restore those areas already affected by fire, land clearance and drainage. In parallel the Mayas Project will work in close collaboration with the communities surrounding the area to ensure benefits derived from the project area (no permanent settlements exist within the project area) are used to improve rural livelihoods and wellbeing and to develop greater resilience to climate change. The project will also fully protect the globally important biodiversity of the project area, including a population of Critically Endangered Bornean Orangutan estimated to be between 813 and 1,204 (around 2% of the global population) and significant populations of at least eight other critically endangered or endangered species. At this stage the project is not validated and is not trading carbon. The project remains committed to aligning operations with the Government of Indonesia’s developing legislation on carbon projects.

This is a grouped project, with the initial Project Activity Instances make up a initial Project area of approximately 140,000 hectares of forest at risk that have the potential to reduce emissions from deforestation and degradation (REDD+) and non-forest areas with the potential to plant 60,000 hectares of afforestation/reforestation primarily for agroforestry systems. The Project Activities instances are in State Reserves which are managed by Agro-Industrie Développement SA (AID–SA) under a 30-year contract. AID-SA has been running piloting programs for local communities, working with Mali-Folkecenter Nyetaa, a national NGO) to promote sustainable income streams. However, the funding and project activities have not been able to fully address the on-going pressure on forests nor finance the full potential for new tree-based (agroforestry) income streams. The Project Activity Instances are among the last remaining stands of contiguous mature and fairly intact forests in Mali and are being threatened by various anthropogenic deforestation drivers.

The objective of the Project is to conserve and restore these forests by working with the local communities in and around these threatened forests to provide environmental education and awareness, delineation and protection of forests, development of alternative fuel wood and timber supplies, as well as alternative sustainable income generation and farming techniques for crops and non-timber forest products.  There is also the potential to expand to additional areas within the geography to potentially increase the size of this grouped project over time.

Col La Paz is implementing an Afforestation/Reforestation Project in degraded grasslands in Colombia. The Vichada Department is home to vast tropical grasslands, which have been subject to unsustainable grazing causing ecosystem degradation. La Paz Farm is an extensive forestry plantation with multiple introduced species, mainly planted with Acacia mangium which is undergoing the process of soil regeneration. This productive ecosystem will produce several timber products for construction materials and charcoal to sustainably meet the needs of a growing population. 
La Paz applies practices such as low agrochemical use and regenerative agriculture. It employs a total of 37 workers who benefit from long-term contracts, free meals three times a day, and comfortable accommodation.
The project serves as a biodiversity corridor for many species. Conservation efforts include wildlife protection, spring preservation, and stream conservation. The initiative brings climate benefits by preventing erosion and enhancing carbon sequestration. Col La Paz follows social and environmental policies, aiming for verified emission removals under the Verified Carbon Standard and the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity Standard. 
The estimated annual emissions and removals are 15,705 tCO2e, and the total anticipated emissions and removals are 698,014 tCO2e over 40 years, accounting for future planned harvesting events

The project is located on the northern region of Guatemala (km. 268) on the route to the Lanquin Municipality, Department of Alta Verapaz. The farm’s rolling hills, and occasional low altitude mountains, surrounded by valleys originate moderate to steep slopes. This is a multifunctional and biodiverse cocoa and coffee agroforestry project. Additionally, it produces cardamom, lemons, and rubber; diversifying revenue streams and increasing landscape connectivity.

Currently, Finca Chimelb is the largest cacao farm in Guatemala with a total of 470.5 hectares of cocoa crop, and a major producer of arabica coffee, with a total of 573 hectares of specialty coffee. Likewise, in the next few years, it will become a leading producer of rubber and cardamom. The farm also has an area of eucalyptus and other tree species, plus natural forest within the property which are protected and managed. 

This grouped project has a Project area which initially has Project Activity Instances of 4,805 hectares. Out of this total area, approximately 2,740 hectares are cropland, while most of the remaining land is covered with forest. In the project area, crops are grown under regenerative agriculture principles including practices such as agroforestry, crop diversification, cover crops, and no-till. The farm’s elevation ranges from 400 meters to 1,150 meters above sea level. Thus, productive areas are distributed according to the altitude, soil’s conditions, and vegetation types. Between 400 and 900 meters above sea level, cocoa, cardamom, and coffee (Robusta) are planted in an agroforestry system under the shade of tress such as rubber, and pine. And between 900 and 1,150 meters above sea level, Arabica coffee is grown. 

The project area includes the Sepalau Lagoon and other smaller water sources that cover approximately 48 hectares of the project area. In terms of infrastructure 105.7kilometers of internal roads has been built to facilitate production activities among the plantation.

Yunxi District is located in the northeast of Yueyang City and the south bank of the middle reaches of the Yangtze River. Rice cultivation is an important agricultural operation in Yunxi District, not only in terms of food security but also in terms of livelihood and plays a major part in the economy. Yunxi District has a population about 178,400, and annual household income of farmers is only CNY 42,507. The project is located in south of Yunxi District, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China, with a total acreage of 8,059.19 ha for double-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in south of Yunxi District.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Yunxi District use continuously flooded method in rice paddies with the straw on field as the organic amendment inputs, which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Yunxi District changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.
vcs-3598: Through this project activity, Pivot Bio will evaluate the impact of replacing synthetic nitrogen fertilizer with an in-season nitrogen source that fixes and supplies nitrogen to the roots corn and other cereal crops. One such source is nitrogen-fixing microbes which that convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia, a plant available form of N, supplying N to the plant during the most critical stages of growth. This treatment offers unique advantages over synthetic nitrogen fertilizer, including consistency (microbes do not leach or volatilize during weather events), accessibility (biological nitrogen fixation occurs on the root of the crop, making N readily available to the plant), and resiliency (microbes produce nitrogen throughout the growing season, matching N availability to crop needs).  Microbes can replace synthetic nitrogen fertilizer by fixing and supplying N to cereal crops in-season, allowing growers within the project boundary to apply less synthetic nitrogen on the field.  Lower applications of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer have the well-documented impact of reducing nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions, and in certain cases, growers may also see a reduction in additional GHG emissions from reduced equipment use. In total, the GHG emission reductions from reduced synthetic fertilizer use will be used to generate credits.

The proposed grouped projects aim at improving the quality of drinking water through dissemination of zero greenhouse gas emitting safe drinking water purifier (SDWP) to provide safe drinking water for schools and institutions throughout Viet Nam. In this grouped projects, the schools include Kindergartens, nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, high schools. Institutions or/and community homes are home for disabled, orphanage, nursing home, mental home. For this reason, this proposed project activity will avoid the use of thermal energy and/or low energy and associated emissions.
The grouped project activity will minimize the use of non-renewable biomass or fossil fuel utilized for boiling water as a means purification to achieve safe drinking water quality in the absence of this project activity. This directly leads to reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it can be helpful to user’s health.
The project activity targets schools/institutions with no previous safe drinking water access. The geographical boundary is in Viet Nam. Water purifiers are distributed free of cost to schools. R. China. The Proposed Project aims to plant trees in Nalinhe Forest Farm, managed by the Stated-Own Wudinghe Forestry Field in the Wudinghe Town, Uxin Banner, Ordos City, sitting on the south edge of Ordos Desert in the Inner Mongolia Plateau. 
In the absence of the Proposed Project, all the project sites are barren land covering by a few of grasses. Without its implementation, all the sites might keep the same circumstances with no natural reforestation within the project area due to shortage of water and soil nutrition. The Proposed Project is a mixed stand with Pinus sylvestris var. Mongolica, Picea asperata, Populus alba, and those that do not survive will be removed and replanted in time. 
The GHG removals generated by afforestation activities is calculated ex-ante in accordance with AR-AMS0007 v03.1 developed under the UNFCCC Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) for Afforestation/Reforestation (A/R) Small-scale Methodology, which is recognized and applied by the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS).
vcs-3601: The CAAPII REDD+ PROJECT aims to protect the Amazon Forest present in properties inserted in the municipalities of Paragominas, Ipixuna do Pará and Tomé- Açu in the Pará State, in Brazil. This region has historically high rates of deforestation, especially associated with conflicts of land tenure, and the high value of activities of other land-use such as livestock and soybean production. The illegal exploraration of timber and other illegal activities such as hunting affect the forest, the biodiversity , the climate and consequently the local population as well. The conservation of 33,766.64 hectare of Ombrophilous Dense Forest  with the CAAPII REDD+ Project will reduce more than 14 millions tCO2e of GHG emissions and bring positive impacts to the region with the project activities. The actions have as goals the preservation of the forest, as well as the improvement of the well-being of the communities, biodiversity and climate regulation. A socioeconomic diagnosis on each community involved in the project conducted the design of the project activities in order to encourage the growth of environmental awareness and the sustainable development, aligned with the conservation of the forest and fauna and flora species. With  the approval of the CAAPII REDD+ Project, the forest areas inside the properties can be protected and the project activities can be implemented aiming to bring climate, community, and biodiversity benefits.

Udzungwa Corridor Limited will reforest 7500 ha of bracken fern thicket on the Eastern Slopes of the Udzungwa Mountains in Tanzania by planting over 100 native tree species.

The project area is largely fallow farmland on steep slopes with no road access. Natural regeneration in the project area is prevented by a dense thicket of bracken fern, occasional cultivation, and hot fires when the bracken burns. The project is signing 30-year leases with the small holder farmers and village councils that own the project lands. The project covers all the costs associated with tree nursery establishment and tree planting and employs hundreds of local community members in the process. To ensure that the planted trees survive, the project is weeding around the planted seedlings 3 times a year for 3 years, clearing fire breaks around the planted areas, and employing firefighting teams.

The project is a 30-year project and will remove approximately 5,322,834 tCO2e over the project lifetime.

The project will greatly improve the local economy in the participating villages through reliable payments for leased land, creating hundreds of well-paying jobs, the provision of avocado seedlings and improved bean seed outside the planting area and funding village development projects. With 30 years of funding already secured by the project, the economic opportunities created by the project will be much more reliable than farming and thus help communities adapt to uncertain climate conditions. 

The project is located in the Eastern Arc Biodiversity hotspot and will create a forest corridor that will reconnect the Udzungwa Scarp and Kilombero Nature Reserves. The corridor will increase habitat connectivity for the endangered Sanje Mangabey, vulnerable Udzungwa Red Colobus Monkey, and several other endangered and vulnerable species. Additionally, the project is planting vulnerable tree species, thereby directly increasing the population of vulnerable species in the area.

Jiangsu Lisaike PET Recycling  Protect (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) aims to produce PET flakes by recycling and processing post-consumer PET bottles, to replace the same amount of PET products produced from raw materials. It is planned that 80,000 tons of post-consumer PET bottles per year will be recycled into 65,000 tons of PET flakes at maximum production capacity. The project located in  Xuyi Country, Huaian City,  Jiangsu, China and is developed and operated by Jiangsu Lisheco Environmental Protection Material Technology Co., Ltd.(hereafter referred to as “the project proponent”).
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of PET flakes was produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well.
The estimated annual average GHG emission reduction is 59273 tCO2e and the total estimate GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period is 414911 tCO2e.

The Jiangxi Ruijin Improved Forest Management Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Ruijin City (county-level city), Ganzhou City, Jiangxi Province, P.R.C. The geo-coordinated of the project proponent is 115°55′E, 25°49′N, total area is 13,316 ha. It is implemented by Jiangxi Tianye Biotechnology Limited (hereafter PP) to protect the once logging forest. 

Prior to the implementation of the project, the forests in the project area were harvested following the guidelines in Timber Harvest Plan approved by the local forestry bureau. In order to protect the forest ecosystem, improve the ecological environment, increase carbon sinks, reduce GHG emission reductions and slow down climate change, the project proponent decided to implement this improved forest management project activities from January 2020 to December 2049. And from the Project Start Date, PP has stopped the commercial logging in the project area. 

This project aims to protect 13,316 ha commercial forest from logging. The Forest Conservation Project activities will be focused on forest resource supervision and monitoring. In order to supervise and monitor any disturbances that may affect the whole forest, PP has established a ranger team that monitors the state of the forest with regard to diseases, illegal logging, hunting, fires etc. This ecosystem will then continue to provide its services to all the communities and entities that depend on it.

The project reduces greenhouse gas emissions and increase carbon sinks by preventing logging, avoiding any kind of commercial harvest and other linked to logging activities,.

The project is expected to generate approximately 3,471,067 tCO2e with buffer deduction during the 30 years’ crediting period, with the annual emission reductions of 115,702 tCO2e.

The project activity will significantly improve the forest management conditions within the project area, and benefit local ecological environment, address globle climate change.

Mutlular Biogas Animal Manure Methane Recovery and Utilization Plant (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighboring animal farms with vacuum trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units for heat and electricity generation. The thermal energy is utilized for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is both used for internal electricity requirements and supplied to the national grid. 

The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emission from fossil-fuel based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 527,342 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 3,691,394 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

The Recycling Roadways for Carbon Emission Reductions - Midstate Reclamation and Trucking Project (herein “project”) supports Midstate Reclamation and Trucking in replacing hot mix asphalt (HMA) with foam stabilized base (FSB) and/or emulsion asphalt in pavement projects across the United States. Prior to implementing project methods, pavement contractors often default to using energy-intensive mining, hauling, and high temperature material manufacturing practices associated with HMA. These industry standard activities unnecessarily destroy habitats, release carbon dioxide (CO2), and release volatile organic compounds (VOC).

This project reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting activities throughout the pavement application lifecycle. The project reduces dependence on the mining of virgin aggregate, reduces transportation of raw materials to mix plants, eliminates high-temperature asphalt manufacturing asphalt at high temperatures and, in the case of in-place pavement recycling, eliminates mix-plant to job-site transportation. The project replaces virgin aggregate with reclaimed asphalt pavement.

The project is conducted under VCS methodology VM0039, “Methodology for Use of Foam Stabilized Base and Emulsion Asphalt Mixtures in Pavement Application” and compares carbon emissions between traditional and sustainable designs with similar structural properties. 

Project instances will be added under a single Project Description as allowed by Verra. Other similar Project Descriptions may also be developed with other pavement contractors.

The project is located in Hefeng district of Huarong country, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China, with a total acreage of 8,192.02 ha for double-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in Hefeng district of Huarong country.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Huarong country use continuously flooded method in rice paddies with the straw on field as the organic amendment inputs, which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Huarong country changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.

vcs-3627: The Eastern Cape Restoration Project is a revegetation project, aimed at the landscape restoration of the native Albany thicket, within a biodiversity hotspot that has undergone extreme degradation and ecosystem loss. A multi-year drought, combined with a multiple decades of over grazing have led to a scenario whereby vast areas of land can no longer support either economic or ecological functions. The project restores ex-grazing lands with a native species, Portulacaria afra, which shows unique ecological features adapted to the semi-arid project area. Planted at high density and subsequently protected from grazing, the restoration activity facilitates a microclimate and dense canopy cover that subsequently allows for the return of the high floral biodiversity endemic to the project area. The project is a grouped project covering the sub-municipality of Makana and is implemented hand in hand with the Eastern Cape Restoration Project, South Africa - Somerset East, and the Eastern Cape Bamboo Forestry Project, for the creation of a holistic restoration strategy.

Located in the extreme east of the province of Misiones, in San Pedro, the field of native forest where the project is located has 22,878.5 hectares and immersed in the Green Corridor. In this area, controlled logging has been carried out since the 1960s and will decrease as the NIDEPORT project progresses, with harvesting expected to be completed by the end of 2021. The project activity is improved forest management with areas that will be enriched and regenerated by planting more than 250,000 native species individuals annually and others managed to increase forest productivity (bambuacea´s control, and others). 
Although there is not any community, individual or group of people living in the project area, GS1 has been subjected to situations of intrusions and illegal occupations, with burning for planting or deforestation for rudimentary construction, there are numerous cases where the land has been colonized or exploited for agriculture or livestock, where the land is left with high levels of degradation and contamination. 
The project zone, encompassed in an area with population under poverty line, expects to work together with the community identifying risks, HCV areas and needs, in order to implement mitigation actions together. In this line, first meetings with communities have already helped to identify both biodiversity and community´s HCVs, and possible projects regarding housing improvement, health care, among other needs to be identified during the project lifetime.
The climate benefits of the project are defined as the reductions or removals of GHG emissions resulting from forest regeneration, these are expected to reach 3,106,582 tCO2e during the crediting period, averaging 103,553 tCO2e per year.

Project seeks to address the issue of deforestation in the Amazon biome on a local level at the state of Acre, Brazil . The IACO REDD+ Project is an AFOLU project, and therefore is classified within scope 14. More specifically, the project falls under the Avoided Unplanned Deforestation and Avoided Planned
Deforestation (categories). If this REDD+ project is implemented, 60,805 hectares of Amazon rainforest will be conserved over the first 30 years, avoiding the emission of 26,040,427 tons of CO 2 into the atmosphere. Under the social sphere, the project also brings benefits for the region . The IACO REDD+ project proponents recognize the essential role of the participation of project area residents and neighbors in the success of this project.
vcs-3632: South Africa's Eastern Cape has suffered over a century of land degradation, through a combination of clearance of the original ecosystem for livestock production, over intense grazing, and extended periods of drought. Such land degradation has gone hand in hand with increased levels of unemployment and poverty, with poverty in the province representing the highest in the country. Over the past ten years EcoPlanet has pioneered the use of a naturalized species of sympodial bamboo, Bambusa balcooa, as a tool for restoration of these degraded lands setting the framework for expansion. The proposed project activity uses a landscape approach to afforest extremely degraded farms that can no longer support agricultural activity, in a mosaic fashion. The project provides carbon removal benefits, enhanced ecosystem services, and long term job creation within a sub-municipality that current has >80% unemployment. The project is designed and managed hand in hand with the Eastern Cape Restoration Project, providing a holistic approach to restoration.
vcs-3633:
The aim of the project is to facilitate the roll-out of conservation agriculture in regions of South Africa where it is not prevalent. The intention is to at a minimum, assist farmers to replace conventional cultivation practices with the three essential components of CA – no till, cultivating a variety of species and the maintenance of organic cover through the year. 

To facilitate the initial adoption as well as long-term maintenance of these essential components and potential additional activities, a broad set of activities are required that are centred around three themes or goals:
1. To address the lack of regionally specific awareness, knowledge, evidence and models. 
2. To build regional technical support programmes and peer networks based on trust and evidence, and
3. To create an attractive financial incentive package to sustain implementation over the long-term. 

In terms of a broad strategy, a bottom-up participatory approach will be followed working with existing programmes, farmer study groups, farming organisations and institutions to increase awareness and knowledge of the opportunity in an effective and efficient manner. In a similar manner, regional expertise and research will be drawn upon to develop the supporting science, monitoring methods and financial models. Such an approach not only improves the viability of the underlying activities, but creates the trust required to sustain implementation over the full project period.  

This approach is based on the proven concept of farmer innovation platforms where the engagements and interaction are farmer centred.  Farmers are seen as the principal restoration agents and practitioners.  

A grouped project approach will be taken where the intention is to add project instances over time that meet all eligibility criteria. The initial set of identified farms are expected to lead to GHG emission reduction and removals of approximately 106,000 tCO2e per year or 3,180.000 tCO2e over a 30 year project.

Agoro Carbon USA Cropland Program is a grouped VCS project implemented by Agoro Carbon Alliance. The program will implement a package of regenerative agricultural land management activities such as but not limited to reduced and zero tillage, cover cropping, improved nitrogen management as a means to reduce GHG and decarbonize agriculture. The implementation of these practices will lead to increases in carbon sequestration rates in the soil, reduced soil disturbance and soil erosion, improved crop residue and water management, as well as potentially reducing the total usage of fossil fuels. 
The main objective of the program is to provide the financial, agronomic and educational support needed for growers to adopt new farming practices that not only produce agricultural products in a sustainable and profitable way, but also have a positive impact on climate change.

The APD REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 1,289 ha of deforestation, equating to 302,439 ton CO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 10,081 ton CO2e.

vcs-3645:
The aim of the climate protection project is to increase soil organic matter content in arable soils and simultaneously reduce agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions via a broad scale-up of regenerative agriculture. Therefore the project intends to motivate as many farmers as possible to convert from conventional farming, the most common type in Germany, to regenerative agriculture practices. This is done through financial support and in-depth knowledge transfer using digital platforms (company-owned web application & mobile application). 
Today, conventional agriculture is the predominant agricultural practice in Germany, with dramatic consequences for the overall soil fertility and the soil carbon stocks. Therefore, one focus of the project is to reduce CO2 by increasing the SOC stock. But at the same time the project considers the reduction of CO2, CH4 and N2O emissions from agricultural management activities, such as fossil fuel consumption, fertiliser use or livestock production. This enables a holistic view on the development of GHG-emissions related to regenerative management methods. Other positive side-effects of large scale project application can be taken into account, such as an overall improvement of the soil fertility and health  including i) an increase in water storage capacity, thus providing a higher drought resilience, ii) an increase in anion retention capacity of the soils, thus reducing nitrate leaching rates to aquifers and iii) an improvement of the soil structural stability and infiltration rates, thus minimising the risk of soil erosion events. The project aims to be validated according to the Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management (VM0042).

Tianjin Dahanzhuang LFG Power Generation ProjectⅠ(hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located at the Dahanzhuang landfill site in Balitai town, Jinnan District, Tianjin city, P.R China.The purpose of the project is to capture and utilize landfill gas for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is supplied to North China Power Grid (NCPG). The new gas extraction and utilization systems have been installed by the project. Before the implementation of the project activity, the landfill gas that was captured and utilized by the project was emitted into the atmosphere directly. Equivalent electricity was provided by North China Power Grid (NCPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations. This is the scenario that existed prior to the implementation of the project activity and is also the baseline scenario.

Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions will be reduced by avoiding CO2 emissions from those fossil fuel-based power plants connected to the grid and by avoiding GHG emissions from releasing LFG into the atmosphere from the landfill site.
vcs-365: The primary aim of the project is to Implement a high efficiency biomass residue based cogeneration project at a green field sugar plant and export the surplus electricity to grid. A new cogeneration project activity has been implemented along with it to effectively utilize the bagasse generated in-house. The purpose of the proposed activity “CPA1 - Man and Man Enterprise Improved Cooking Stoves Programme in Ghana (Brong-Ahafo region)”, hereafter referred to as ‘CPA1’, is to combat climate change and contribute to sustainable development of Ghana.
In the baseline scenario, households continue to using non-renewable biomass in traditional cooking stoves. An ICS combusts wood fuel more efficiently, i.e. requires less charcoal than a traditional stove. This reduces CO2 emissions.
CPA1 thus aims to reduce non-renewable wood fuel consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of households (hereafter also “end-users”) in the urban and peri-urban Brong-Ahafo region of Ghana by selling about 200,000 affordable Improved Cooking Stoves (ICSs) in replacement of traditional charcoal cooking stoves, so-called coal pots, resulting in 174,201 tCO2 emission reductions per year on average or 1,219,411 tCO2 over the 7-year crediting period.
The CPA implementer is Man and Man Enterprise, a Ghana-based ICS producer and seller. The ICS distributed under CPA1 is the so-called Jiko-type ICS. It is also known as the “Holy cook”, which is the brand name of the Jiko-type ICS produced by Man and Man Enterprise. Compared to coal pots, which have an efficiency of 15%-18%, Holy Cooks have an efficiency of about 30% while providing the same service. This allows better heat retaining, i.e. quicker heating-up and longer cooking times with less wood fuel (and combustion fumes). ICSs work on a simple but mature technology for efficient energy conversion of biomass to heat. As ICS is relatively more expensive than traditional stoves, most households can’t afford to buy ICSs. In order to implement this program, stove subsidy and operational cost support are vital. Ecoeye Co., Ltd., and other Korean Companies have financed all improved cooking stoves distributed to the households until April 2021.
vcs-3651: Ege Biogas project (hereafter referred to as the project) is a biogas to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by EGE BİYOGAZ ELEKTRİK ÜRETİM ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, as the Project Owner, in Çapaklı quarter, Salihli district, Manisa province, in Turkey. In the project's final environmental impact assessment report, it is estimated that approximately 400 tons of cattle manure and chicken hens generated at animal farms will be collected daily or every two days through special sewage trucks equipped with close-tanks to prevent any odor and/or manure leakages and to be fed into the anaerobic digesters at the proposed biogas power plant. The proposed project activity has two biogas engines installed at the biogas power plant, with 3.120 MWe. The manure produced by 40 neighboring farms is collected and fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site. The project began to generate electricity on April 23rd, 2021, which is the date of gas engines had implemented. According to Electricity Generation License, the biogas generator system has the maximum operational capacity 3.120 MWe. The project has obtained the approval of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) issued by the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization in Turkey on January 9th, 2020, and the Electricity Generation License (EGL) issued by the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EMRA) in Turkey on December 10th, 2020. This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for 21 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 322,680 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,258,762 tCO2eq emissions reduction during the first crediting period and 6,776,286 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its three crediting periods for a total of 21 years.
