Xinxiang MSW Incineration Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Xinxiang City, Henan Province,  P.R. China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Xinxiang Capital Environment Energy Co., Ltd.
With two 750t/d MSW combustion production lines, the project will treat 1,500 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of two 750t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 35MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 547,500 tons of MSW every year, and consume 284 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work 8,000 hours every year, generating 218,830 MWh electricity, of which 179,411 MWh will be exported to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The implementation of the project will meet the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment.
By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the project activity avoids the emission of methane that would be generated under landfill condition. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can produce steam to generate power to replace the electricity that would otherwise be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants which are connected to the CCPG. Before the implementation of the project, the local MSW was usually disposed of at nearby landfill, where no landfill gas capturing system erected and the landfill gases are released to atmosphere directly. The equivalent power generated by the project was supplied by the the CCPG. The baseline scenario identified is the same as the scenario existing prior to the start of implementation of the project activity.
It is estimated that in the first crediting period of the project (from 19 November 2020 to 18 November 2027), the average annual GHG emission reduction will be 132,263 tCO2e.
vcs-3654:
The proposed grouped project activity aims to reduce Greenhouse gas (GHG) emission from the atmosphere by disseminating fuel efficient wood stoves in Rwanda of sub-Saharan African region. 
The main objective of the project activity is to distribute new and efficient cookstoves to the target population, that is, rural/urban households who use, using traditional, unimproved firewood/charcoal based cookstoves and open fires for cooking in Rwanda. The traditional stoves will be replaced by wood-based improved cookstoves, the distributed ICS will have an average lifespan of at least 5 years with thermal efficiency of at least 25%. 
A typical project instance under the project activity will replace either conventional firewood/charcoal stoves with higher efficiency ICS models by leveraging resources provided by the project activity in rural/urban areas. ICSs are more efficient than conventional stoves as they reduce heat loss and improve heat transfer and combustion efficiency. The ICS models are fuel efficient, resulting in a decrease in fuel use in comparison to conventional pre-project stoves while also reducing particulate matter and carbon emissions. Design considerations have also incorporated ergonomics and safety.
The project activity will deploy state-of-art technology options with goal of providing the high performing, affordable and locally appropriate technologies to the local environments. The proposed project activity will use following improved cooktoves under the grouped project activity
vcs-3655: The project plans to promote improved water management practices in rice cultivation instead of using the traditional practice of continuously flooded irrigation. AWD/DSR are proven methods to reduced methane emission by as much as 48% compared to flooded conditions where large amounts of methane (CH4) gets generated because of anaerobic decomposition. This project is predicted to generate important co-benefits of reducing water usage during rice cultivation, decrease pest and disease attacks, improve soil health etc. Further they're also beneficial for reduced cost of cultivation for small land holders
vcs-3656: Agoro Carbon USA Pastureland Program is a grouped VCS project implemented by Agoro Carbon Alliance. The program will implement a package of regenerative land management activities in pasturelands, these include nutrient management, increasing species diversity, rotational grazing and other regenerative practices. The implementation of these practices will lead to an increase in carbon sequestration rates in the soil, increase in forage quality, overall animal and soil health and improved water management. The main objective of this program is to provide financial, agronomic and educational support to ranchers to implement the aforementioned practices. During the project lifetime, enrolled ranchers will be assisted by the Agoro Carbon agronomic team to implement improved agricultural management practices from their current system standard to a system that capitalizes on sustainable, regenerative production.
vcs-3657:
MoEVing Urban Technologies Pvt Ltd. (from here onwards MoEVing) is implementing commercial electric 2 wheeler, 3 wheeler and 4 wheeler instead of fossil fuel powered vehicles. MoEVing provides solutions to top e-commerce, e-grocery, FMCG, logistics and D2C companies to optimize their logistics costs and meet their goals of reducing carbon emissions. At the same time MoEVing works with OEMs, driver cum owners and financial institutions to helps address various constraints that are coming in the way of EV adoption. It was founded in Jan 2021. As of August 2022, the company's fleet of vehicles includes the Ampere, Ather, Hero, Okinawa, Revolt, 2 wheelers and Alti green, ETO, E-Trio, EULER, Omega, Piaggio 3 wheelers. 
Project activity is replacing fossil fuel (Petrol, Diesel and CNG) powered vehicle from baseline. The usage of electricity powered vehicles instead of fossil fuel powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven. This is proven in the respective ER calculations. Included Project vehicles are implemented by MoEVing those were owned by MoEVing or operating on lease. Based on lease agreement carbon credit rights are owned by MoEVing, thus avoiding issues of double counting. Only vehicles are counted where such an agreement has been signed.
vcs-3658:
The project activity intends to mainstream clean cooking practice through dissemination of fuel efficient improved biomass cookstoves in the rural areas of Maharashtra amongst socially and economically deprived households (households belonging to below poverty line )). The objective of project activity is to reduce anthropogenic emission of greenhouse gases to the atmosphere as well as reduc e environmental degradation and health risk of women and children subjected to indoor air pollution.

Transition to improved cook stoves usage from use of inefficient bi omass fired traditional cook stove is contribut ing towards reduction of greenhouse gas emission by reducing consumption of non renewable biomass in compared to the baseline scenario . Successful operation of the project activity and the health benefits the project has rendered to has also encourage d rural residents to shift from traditional cook stoves usage to improved cook stove usage.

Since the beneficiaries selected under the project activity belongs to socially deprived and economically marginalised ho useholds (households belonging to below poverty line ), therefore investing on improved cookstoves has never been a choice . . Moreover, the beneficiary households have lower level of awareness pertaining to health impact of traditional cookstoves usage.
vcs-3659: This Nesa Solar PV Grouped Project consists of the commissioning of new, small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) installations in the Republic of South Africa. The PV installations provide a clean, renewable source of electricity. In addition, the PV facilities increase the security of electricity supplies in South Africa. This is primarily because the national utility, Eskom, is currently unable to provide consistent electricity supplies due to aged and failing infrastructure. The quantity and duration of power cuts in 2022 is expected to be the highest since load shedding was initiated in 2007.
vcs-366: The purpose of the project activity is to utilize rice husk as a source of energy to generate clean electricity and heat. This Project involves the construction and operation of a rice husk-fired power plant in Ubonratchathani Province, in Northeast Thailand. The project owner, Kaona Power Supply Co., Ltd. (a private entity hereafter referred to as the project owner), is part of the Kaona Group, an agro-industry company that produces quality chicken and exports frozen chicken products.
vcs-3660:
The objective of this project is to reforest degraded mangroves sites in Kwale, Kilifi, and Tana River counties, in Kenya. The project will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem in degraded lands, starting by planting 220 ha in Shirazi, Bodo, Munje, and Funzi Island, in Kwale county.
The main components of the project are to provide a variety of ecosystem services, climate change mitigation, economic considerations, and active participation of the local community. Without the project, carbon stocks in the project area will continue to decline, as the mangrove ecosystems in Kenya suffer a strong degradation process resulting from anthropogenic (e.g., deforestation for wood consumption) and natural causes (e.g., sea tides).
Under this grouped project, degraded mangroves on the Kenyan coast are restored and replanted. In the first project activity up to 196.000 mangroves will be planted. The species selected for this reforestation project are indigenous and local, namely Rhizophora mucronata, Ceriops tagal and Avicennia marina.
The project will monitor soil conditions to measure changes in soil carbon content and maintain soil nutrient levels to improve water quality compared to the baseline scenario. Mangrove restoration will further increase fish populations, improve biodiversity, and provide other important ecosystem services. To measure the positive impact on biodiversity, annual biomonitoring will be conducted using eDNA.
The empowerment of the population is also central to the project. The labour requirement for the project will be fulfilled with local employment. Therefore, most of the budget for labour and an additional 50/50 share of carbon credit revenues will remain in the country. The project will promote a working family model where more than 50% of women can actively participate in the project. People are shown alternative livelihood opportunities that allow them to acquire and grow high-value crops, and invest in beekeeping or ecotourism.
vcs-3661: Agroforestry Practices as an alternate to fulfil the rising demand for timber and other non-timber forest produce is promising in long term as it provides both wood and food. Agroforestry can help to conserve and rehabilitate the ecosystem, along with providing better livelihood opportunities to the rural community. The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India.
vcs-3662: Nam Hinboun Downstream Hydropower Project is developed by Rasita Power Co., Ltd. in Songhong village, Hinboun District, Khammouane province, Lao PDR. Total installed capacity of the project is 15MW, provided by two (2) bulb turbine of 7.5MW each. Project is commissioned on 01/02/2021. The expected annual electricity generated from the project is 79,740 MWh. The electricity generated from the project replaces the grid electricity and thereby avoids associated CO2 emission.

vcs-3664: Huinan County Afforestation Project is located in Huinan county, Tonghua city, Jilin province of China. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren or degraded lands. Prior to the start of the project, the land in the project area was barren, no forest or wetland except some scattered shrub and grass. Under the project, an area of 13,784ha of barren land in Huinan county was planted with trees of native species, mainly including Korean pine, spruce, larch, Fraxinus mandshurica, Juglans mandshurica, etc. The implementation of the project will generate greenhouse gases (GHG) emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conservation and forest cover, enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forests, increase competence and capability of local residents by providing them with relevant technical skills and training, and create more permanent job opportunities for local residents especially women and increase income for local communities.  The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 19,001,754 tCO2e in 60 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 316,696 tCO2e.
vcs-3665: Holocene Ecosolutions Private Limited (HCE), is in the process of implementing grouped project activities to convert Poultry litter to compost i.e., chicken manure with an annual output of 170 tons per day at different locations across various States & UTs in India. HCE are pioneers in up cycling organic residues from various Agro-processing centers using the Black Soldier Fly (BSF), Hermetia illucens, (Diptera: Stratiomyidae) in India. The primary objective of the project is to effectively demonstrate the use of BSF larva to not only generate feed, but also achieve an environmentally friendly way of managing waste.
vcs-3666:
The primary objective of the Xingu-Araguaia Grouped REDD+ Project is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) in a 10,004.42-ha project area, consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest. The project area is in São José do Xingu and São Félix do Araguaia, in the State of Mato Grosso, Southern Amazon.

Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities. The contribution to sustainability is being monitored through the application of the SOCIALCARBON® Standard.

The present REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 4,312 ha of deforestation, equating to 1,421,408 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (15-October-2020 to 14-October-2050), with an annual average of 47,380 tCO2e.
vcs-3667: This project is to build a composting plant which is designed to treat manure waste from the Beichen Breeding Swine Farm to produce organic fertilizer. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting manure.
vcs-3668:
The project introduced a set of organic fertilizers production lines with an annual output of 32,500 tons to treat the manure from the chicken farms in Zhucheng City, Shandong Province. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners. The proposed project was designed to treat the chicken manure in Zhucheng City to produce organic fertilizer. The proposed project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system, etc. It is estimated that approximately 98,000 tons of manure can be composted aerobically annually for this project.
vcs-3669: The Western Kenya Soil Carbon Project promotes the adoption of a range of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management technologies including reduced tillage, mulching, cover crops, green manure, composting, soil & water conservation, integrated pest management, and agroforestry on croplands and surrounding areas for watershed restoration and protection. It is implemented western Kenya in three counties: Bungoma, Kakamega and Siaya. Due to its more favourable agroecology, the region is densely populated, and the lands are extensively cultivated with limited natural vegetation. Farmers practice subsistence agriculture, characterized by low inputs, low yields, and continuous loss of soil fertility. The project is managed by Soil-Carbon Certification Services Ltd (SCCS), a non-for-profit company. SCCS is contracting implementation partner (IPs) to support farmers in their land restoration efforts. The project’s main goals are improved yields, food and incomes for farmers, increased resilience to climate change, and climate change mitigation via increased carbon sequestration in soils and plant biomass. The project activities will generate carbon credits that will be certified under the VCS program and monetized and invested in the project activities to ensure sustainability of the project goals. It is a grouped project covering 32,000 ha, with total VCUs 1.87 million tCO2. Participating smallholders are organized in farmer groups for efficient extension services delivery. The groups sign agreements to be project participants after due process of local stakeholders’ consultations and are then entitled to all extension services and support from the project. The group agreements oblige them to adopt and implement SALM technologies on their lands, support project monitoring, and transfer emission reduction units to the project. The project has a 20-year crediting period and applies the VCS Methodology VM0017 Adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management, Version 1.0.
vcs-367: The Kitroongruang Biogas Energy Project (hereafter, the Project) developed by Thai Biogas Energy Company Ltd (hereafter referred to as TBEC, or the Project Developer) is an anaerobic digestion project, which treats wastewater from the cassava processing factory owned by Kitroongruang Tapioca Factory Limited Partnerships (hereafter referred to as the Facility) in Rayong, Thailand. In the baseline scenario, the wastewater flows from the factory through a series of 9 low-maintenance anaerobic and aerobic lagoons. As the wastewater flows through the lagoons, organic material is broken down and resulting methane is released to the atmosphere.
vcs-3670: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Meioeste UniCarbo landfill gas to energy project” encompasses the promotion at the Meioeste landfill site of destruction and/or utilization and/or supply to consumer(s) of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosedopen flare(s), utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 5 MW) and a predicted supply of upgraded  LFG to consumer(s) with an LFG processing and supply infrastructure of combined installed capacity of 5,000 Nm³/h.
vcs-3671:
Project Chaco Vivo will be developed under the Verified Carbon Standard and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standards (VCS – CCBS) as an avoided planned deforestation (APD) REDD+ project. Chaco Vivo will help conserve an area of over 1,800 km2, encompassing over 187,000 hectares (464,000 acres) in Paraguay's Gran Chaco ecosystem. Despite the Gran Chaco’s regional and global significance, the region is one of the most deforested on earth, losing over 1,000 hectares (2,471 acres) of tree cover per day. Project Chaco Vivo will mitigate deforestation pressures in the region and protect this important yet critically threatened ecosystem, which provides habitats to more than 3,400 plant species, 500 bird species, 150 mammals, 120 reptiles, and approximately 100 species of amphibians - including numerous endemic and IUCN red list vulnerable, threatened, and endangered species. 

Chaco Vivo is a People Project at heart with numerous communities living within the Project's Area of Influence (AOI), including Indigenous communities of the Maskoi - an ethnolinguistic group of people of Lengua-Maskoi. The Project Area encompassed by Chaco Vivo is a High Conservation Value Area (HCVA) since it consists of natural habitats of outstanding significance and/or of critical importance due to the special biological, ecological, social, and cultural values. 

Key to Chaco Vivo is a robust social program called the L.I.F.E. Program™ (Land-use Initiatives & Forest Enterprises Program). The L.I.F.E. Program™ will provide a tangible system of socio-economic enrichment programs to improve the livelihoods of marginalized populations. The key objectives of the L.I.F.E. Program™ are to directly impact the U.N. SDGs, but also to foster community engagement, project integration, collaboration, and self-sustaining sustainable enterprise creation for generational impact, or G-Impacts™.
vcs-3673:
Sagri Co., Ltd is going to decrease the usage of Nitrogen Fertilizer in India and Thailand by using the soil detect technology by satellite images. Indian farmers are over-applying chemical fertilizers. However, the rising price of chemical fertilizers has put small-scale farmers' farming operations in a critical situation. In addition, excessive application of nitrogen fertilizers is bad for the environment for the following reasons. First, excessive nitrogen fertilizer applied to the ground causes excessive denitrification. In the process of denitrification, N₂O, a greenhouse gas with a greenhouse effect about 300 times greater than CO₂, is emitted. In addition, excessive application of synthetic nitrogen fertilizers can cause water pollution. Excess nitrogen that runs off into rivers and streams and enters people's bodies through drinking water and aquatic products poses a health hazard. Therefore, by applying the appropriate amount of nitrogen fertilizer to the soil, the amount of nitrogen fertilizer applied can be reduced, helping farmers to operate their farms, preventing global warming, and reducing health hazards to people.
Sagri is engaged in the business of solving global issues related to agriculture and the environment by combining satellite data and AI machine learning technology, and is promoting its core technology, AI Polygon, which uses image technology with AI to analyze high-resolution satellite data and automatically plot farmland in Japan and overseas. Sagri is also developing a technology to analyze soil chemical indices on farmland after plowing, using wavelength data obtained from satellite data and AI-based machine learning.In this project, Sagri will use this technology to analyze soil chemical indices to determine the appropriate amount of fertilizer to be applied, and will receive carbon credits for encouraging farmers to use variable fertilizer application.
vcs-3674:
The Veracruz Mangroves for Life Project aims to restore the ecosystems of mangroves and floodplain forests in the Alvarado lacunar system, Veracruz (ALS) contributing to its adaptation to climate change, the conservation of biodiversity and the reduction of GHG emissions. The Alvarado Lagoon System is a 267,000 h ectares wetland complex formed by the estuaries of the Papaloapan, Acula, Blanco and Limón rivers. ALS is home to tremendous biodi versity and provides a bounty of ecosystem services to the c. 130,000 people living in the area. In recognition of its high conservation priority, it is registered as a RAMSAR site and listed as an Important Bird Area.
This ecosystem has faced ALS severe historical degradation, ever since the establishment of Spanish colonizers in the 16th century who first undertook to convert its natural ecosystems into pasture and sugar cane plantations.
The project is a grouped project and will restore 2,101 hectares. This objective will be a chieved thanks to the work of different stakeholders. The project proponent (Livelihoods) will implement the project together with the local communities and the Mexican ONG Pronatura Veracruz (PNV).
The entire project area (2,101 ha) will sequester 50 902 tCO2e per year. Based on this ex ante estimate, the project will sequester 1, 2 7 2, 561 tCO2e over 25 years.
vcs-3675: The project activity is an 'Alternate wetting and drying (AWD)' activity that is a water saving strategy in irrigated rice production. The main objective of the project is to switch from continuously flooded rice fields to fields that alternately encompass flooded and non-flooded phases which can save significant amount of irrigation water. Thus, the project activity has been designed to change from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation which is conducted in different blocks in the district of Bhopal, Hoshangabad, Raisen and Sehore of the state of Madhya Pradesh, in India. A total of 8,085 hectare for single-cropping rice has been covered under the project activity. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can save water resources, and also at the same time will also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). Additionally, in the project activity compost will be used for soil application in the rice fields and thus replace the application of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer. It is estimated that about 58,722 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually across the crediting period.
vcs-3676: The main objective of the grouped avocado agroforestry project is to be a regional GHG emissions reduction and removal initiative, pioneer in the concept of combining sustainability activities with agricultural activities for avocado planting. To our knowledge, it is an unique initiative in Israel. All projects are located in Northern Israel. The four projects currently included in the grouped project are located at the following locations; Galed, Ramat Menashe, Ramat Yohanan and Yodfat. Agricultural practices by farmers in Kibbutz in Israel have traditionally involved open field activities such as corn, cotton, and wheat crops mostly with sprinklers (for more details refer to 3.4. Baseline scenario). This situation led the land to being occupied only for a few months each year (seasonal crops) with high levels of soil erosion and energy and water inputs. The proposed grouped project activity involves replacing seasonal crops with permanent avocado plantations, changing the entire ecosystem through the implementation of regenerative agricultural practices and boosting carbon sequestration by avocado tree planting.
vcs-3677: The Ecobase Europe Afforestation Project (hereafter the “Project”) is an Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) project, using the CDM AR-ACM0003 methodology V.2.0. The proposed VCS project activity consists of afforestation of agricultural land/other land, low productive agricultural land, and any other project eligible land across the geographical area of the European Union (all 27 member states), all EFTA member states, the United Kingdom and European EU candidate states (Ukraine, Moldova, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia).
vcs-3678:
Chia Tai AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Guangdong Province (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 15 Existing swine farms in Zhanjiang, Guangdong Province, which are owned by Guangdong Zhanjiang Chia Tai Swine Industry Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The specific treatment process of this newly constructed project is as follows: All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, which will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The waste water enters an anaerobic treatment system (enclosed) for reaction and biogas generates. The biogas is captured for electricity generation, with surplus biogas destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge would be produced from anaerobic digestion and the effluent is supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation as organic fertilizers together with other fermentation wastes produced in the project. The electricity generated are all used by the AWMSs and the swine farms, and hence the GHG emission reductions generates from the avoidance of methane emissions from the enclosed treatment system and the electricity generation.
vcs-368: The Project is a peak regulation power plant including installation of two sets of 175 MW air-cooling gas steam combined cycle power generation equipments which use natural gas to generate electricity. Annual consumption of natural gas by the Project is 247.8 million Nm3. It is estimated that the feed-in electricity to the North China Grid from the Project is approximately 1,196 GWh per year via two 220 kV outlet circuits.  The Project clearly fits into the development priority of China. It will support China in stimulating and accelerating the technology development. It will therefore help reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from the high-growth, coal-dominated business-as-usual scenario.
vcs-3680:
The objective of the project is to provide a fuel-efficient cookstove termed as Improved Cook Stove (ICS) to the rural parts in the state of Gujarat in India. The use of Improved Cook Stove for daily cooking activity will reduce the greenhouse gas emissions. The project will replace the traditional cook stove primarily used in the rural households which consumes huge quantity of wood in cooking. The ICS is manufactured in such a way that it has significantly high thermal efficiency which will lead to the low fuel wood consumption and thus less greenhouse gas emissions would occur. 

The project activity will also positively impact the health and daily lifestyle of the rural people. ICS is proven to produce less smoke and thus it will reduce the respiratory heath issues which happens in the traditional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS beneficiaries will have to spend less time to collect the firewood and this saved time they will use in taking care of their family, kids and other productive work. 
The cookstove is also a safer equipment as it is closed from all sides hence users and their family will be in a safer environment. Climate Detox Pvt Ltd and Siddhant Energy Consultants are the project participants for this project. The distribution of ICS will be done in the rural areas under the supervision of an equipped team. All the ICS will be supplied by an experience manufacturer. ICS has been tested in the reputed laboratory for thermal efficiency.

In the absence of project activities, the baseline scenario is that the target population continues to consume non-renewable wood fuel to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves.

Under this project activity, project participant has planned to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in the rural area of India. The estimated annual average greenhouse gas removal from the project is 368,478 tCO2e.
vcs-3681: The technology of solid state anaerobic digestion (SSAD) or dry digestion is being introduced in India by Cities Innovative Biofuels Private Limited. Based on this technology, an anaerobic digestion plant using rice straw (and other lignocellulosic biomass), cattle dung and poultry litter as substrates is proposed to be set up near the city of Patiala, Punjab. The plant will have an input capacity of 80 tonnes per day (TPD) of biomass, with minimal need for water and no effluent. BioCNG (3,600 kg/d) and sterile compost (50 TPD) will be the end products and sold locally to dedicated farmer through long term agreement . It will provide a viable solution to the problems of crop residue burning an d disposal of cow dung and poultry litte r in and around urban areas in N orth India. The project is the result of an exclusive collaboration between Cities Innovative Biofuels Private Limited and a Swiss company, Renergon International AG.
vcs-3683:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Yuyao City1 , under the jurisdiction of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province of China, which have a total acreage of 12,155 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.
With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%2. Hence, this project activity is estimated to reduce 4.93 tCO2e/ha.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 419,888 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,984 tCO2e.

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Xiuzhou District under the jurisdiction of Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province of China, which has a total acreage of 12,085 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.
With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%1. Hence, this project activity is estimated to reduce 4.96 tCO2e/ha.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 419,531 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,933 tCO2e.

Xinjiang Burqin Improved Grassland Management Project Phase II (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Burqin County, Altai City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term.
The main restoration measure of rest and rotational grazing were implemented in 68,333.33 ha of degraded grassland. For the first five years, grazing was strictly forbidden and then, sustainable grassland management methods will be applied, such as rotational grazing in different pastoral areas, limits the time and number of grazing in the project area to protect the natural grassland resources, curb the deterioration of the ecological environment of the natural grassland. It requires that the grazing time shall be halved by dividing grasslands into seasonal grazing land according to the livestock carrying capacity of the grassland by fence building. Then based on specified grazing order, grazing cycle and zoning grazing time, the grassland is grazed area by area and used in turn. 
Besides these main restoration measures, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area.

The objective of the project is to distribute fuel-efficient cook stoves termed as Improved Cook Stove (ICS) to the rural parts in the state of Gujarat in India. The daily usage of Improved Cook Stove for cooking purposes will reduce the greenhouse gas emissions from burning of fuel wood. The project will replace the traditional cook stove primarily used in the rural households which consumes huge quantity of wood in cooking. The ICS is designed in such a way that it has significantly high thermal efficiency, which will lead to the low fuel wood consumption and thereby reducing the greenhouse gas emission. The project activity will also positively impact the health and daily lifestyle of the rural household. ICS is proven to produce less smoke and thus it will reduce the respiratory health issues which occurs in the traditional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS beneficiaries will have to spend less time to collect the firewood and this saved time they will use in taking care of their family, kids and other productive work. The cookstove is also a safer equipment as it is closed from all sides hence users and their family will be in a safer environment.

The purpose of project activity is to provide a safer and efficient cooking medium to the rural population, which will further result in reduction of greenhouse gas emissions to the atmosphere and conservation of forests.

In the absence of project activities, the baseline scenario is that the target population continues to consume non-renewable wood fuel to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves.

Under this project activity, project participant has planned to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in the rural area of India. The estimated annual average greenhouse gas removal from the project is 368,478 tCO2e.

The proposed project activity under VCS will mobilize resource-poor farmers to raise tree plantations on vacant farmlands. It proposes to link resource poor farmers and end users of wood products in order to optimize the land use and to facilitate the co-ordination of wood producers, agronomists, industry, social enterprises and non-governmental organizations to improve the livelihood opportunities of rural households. Various environment friendly technology-based agroforestry practices and Natural Climate Solutions (NCS) will be adopted to help climate change adaptation and mitigation as part of sustainable land management.

This project will optimise the land use and generate Emission Reductions (ERs). The amount of carbon sequestered through the project activity will be measured, quantified with reference to a baseline to determine the Emission Reductions (ERs) generated. The DRC REDD+ Carbon Credit Harvesting Project, located in central DRC, Africa, is a group project that will protect 13,586,379 hectares of forest from industrial logging, unsustainable fuel wood extraction and slash and burn agriculture. Carbon validation will be undertaken by the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS). The project is developed and managed in a joint venture by forest carbon leaders GEC Communities II, Inc. as General Partner to R.E.D.D. Carbon Credit Harvesting LP (GEC-C) and Global Treaty Corporation (GTC). This project will utilize the methodology, 'Methodology for Avoided Deforestation' approved by the VCS in October, 2012. 

The project will be developed as a REDD+ project with validation planned under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS). The VCS methodology used for this project will be Wildlife Works’ VM0009 ‘Methodology for Avoided Deforestation’ v2.0, originally validated with VCS in January, 2011 (Version 1.0) with the revised version (version 3.0) receiving validation from VCS in June, 2014.

The DRC REDD+ Harvesting Project falls under VCS sectoral scope 14 - Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU), under project category Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) and most specifically under the activity Avoiding Planned Deforestation (APD). The project falls into this category by the definition provided in the VCS AFOLU Requirements Document Version 3 published 1 February, 2012, by virtue of the fact that it prevents emissions that otherwise would have taken place under a legally commissioned logging concession.

Shagang Town is located in the central and southern part of Hubei Province, located in the hinterland of Jianghan Plain .The project is located in Shagang Town,Jiangling County, Hubei Province, China, with a total acreage of 13061 ha for single-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in Shagang Town.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Shagang Town use continuously flooded method in rice paddies , which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Shagang Town changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.
Emission reductions of this project are generated by reducing methane emissions of continuously flooded during rice cultivation in baseline scenario. With the project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 4.49 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the project activity is 58,608 tCO2e/year, the total GHG emission reductions are 410,256 t CO2e in the first 7 years crediting period.

vcs-3715: Taihe County Biogas Power Generation and Organic Fertilizer Project is located at ShuangXing Village, Shuang fu Town, Taihe County, Fuyang City, Anhui Province, China.This project builds a new livestock and poultry manure management system and collects organic wastes such as manure from many farms to produce biogas power generation and organic fertilizer. Fermentation raw materials are managed by unified collection and transportation. Agricultural waste resources (ie, livestock and poultry wastes in this project) undergo pretreatment and anaerobic fermentation, and the generated biogas is desulfurized and then enters the generator to generate electricity. The waste heat of the generator is used to increase the temperature of the material in the homogenization tank and the fermentation tank. The mud produced by anaerobic fermentation is transported to the nearby farmland through the pipeline network to form an organic ecological cycle industry. The residue is used to produce solid organic fertilizer. The electricity generated is fed into the East China grid, reducing methane and other greenhouse gas emissions. It also avoids the CO2 emissions generated by the power generation process corresponding to the replacement of electricity, thereby achieving greenhouse gas emission reduction.The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of manure. The project adopts a 10-year fixed crediting period, It is estimated that 62,834 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 628,338 t CO2e in the crediting period.

The growing threats to the forests of the Peruvian Amazon, such as migratory agriculture, land trafficking illegal logging and illegal gold mining, are causing the alarming degradation of forests; the loss and in some cases the disappearance of the most important flora and fauna in the territory; and the general pollution - deterioration of the country’s most valuable ecosystems. Specifically, illegal (gold) mining have caused tragic damage to part of the Peruvian Amazon. Rivers, streams and soils have been contaminated due to this cause to such degree that it will take many years to remediate and recover -to some extent- their initial state. One of the most affected areas in Peru in terms of deforestation, and specifically due to illegal mining, is the buffer zone of the Tambopata National Reserve and the forests located on the right bank (towards Cusco) of the Interoceanic highway in the region of Madre de Dios.

REDD+ Amazon Guardians purpose is to reduce and avoid deforestation within the conservation, reforestation/afforestation, and ecotourism forest concessions located in the buffer zone of the Tambopata National Reserve and adjacent areas which are highly threatened by illegal mining and traffickers who use these areas for illegal crops. REDD+ Amazon Guardians has been designed and developed with the purpose of protecting these valuable forests and their biodiversity, generating environmental services that allow the capture of CO2 and providing opportunities to improve the quality of life for the communities that live and depend on these areas. 

The project is implemented by Bosques Amazonicos SAC (BAM) in partnership with the concessionaire families in the area, grouped in the Federation of Concessionaires of Madre de Dios, FECOMAD.
vcs-3727: The Corridors for Life ARR Grouped Project aims at mitigating climate change through planting of native trees that will remove carbon from the atmosphere, environmental and biodiversity conservation through the formation of ecological corridors that promote connectivity between the remaining forest fragments and protect the soil, and the generation of employment and income through training and acquisition of products and services from local companies of the reforestation chain. With this, the project has the potential over its 50 years lifetime to reforestate 75,000 hectares and remove 29,213,780 tons of CO2e, generate at least 600 jobs, benefit at least 180 women and contribute to the conservation of 8 endangered species according to the IUCN Red List.

vcs-3730: The proposed project is located in Bokpyin Township, Kawthong District, Tanintharyi Region, along Myanmar's 2800 km of coastline. As a result, Worldview International Foundation (WIF) planned to develop a project to restore degraded mangroves and stimulate socioeconomic development in the Tanintharyi coastal region. Objective of the project is to restore 12,000 ha of degraded mangrove areas in the region. The restoration areas under the project belong to Htaung Ka Met, Noet Ngwar, Han Ka Phyu and Kawt Ba Mar village tracts of Bokpyin Township in Kawthong District.
vcs-3731: The project of Yicheng -1 Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation is conducted in Yicheng City within Xiangyang City, Hubei Province of China, with a total acreage of 13,187 ha for single-cropping rice. Anaerobic decomposition of organic material in flooded rice fields produces methane, which escapes to the atmosphere primarily by transport through the rice plants. The target of this project is to solve problems of large amount of methane (CH4) emissions and low rice productivity caused by excessive water used during rice cultivation through replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method to shorten the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. Without the implementation of this project that provides technology/measures to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method would continue to be used and thus the baseline scenario is rice cultivated by continuously flooded method. Soil organic matter under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, therefore the intermittent flooded method is beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction compared to continuously flooded. With the project activity, the estimated amount of GHG emission reduction is 4.52 tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice. The total GHG emissions reductions is collectively expected to 417,237 tCO2e in the first 7 years with an average annual GHG emission removal of 59,605 tCO2e. This project aims to: - Reduce greenhouse gas emission and mitigate climate changes; - Increase rice productivity to improve living standard of local farmers; - Provide more job opportunities, especially for women workers; - Use a proportion of benefits to fund education for local children.

The project encompasses 15,000 acres of commercial plantations, based on species like eucalyptus globulus, eucalyptus nitens, radiata pine and others.
vcs-3735: Rivian's EV charging network project consists of the installation and operation of L2 & DCFC electric vehicle chargers, across the United States. Emissions reductions from the electrification of vehicles reduces greenhouse gas emissions below fossil fuel vehicle levels.
vcs-3736:
Deykoh Dairy Cows Manure Composting Project (hereinafter as “the project”) employs aerobic composting systems on dairy farms in Dengkou County, Bayan Nur City, Inner Mongolia, China. The avoidance of methane emissions could be achieved with treatments of aerobic composting, which replaces the baseline scenario where the dairy manure would undergo an anaerobic decomposition conditions.
In this project, the collected dairy manure after a solid separation will be utilized through a fermentation composting process. After the fermentation, both solids and wastewater are then treated by a fertilizer production system, of which can produce organic fertilizers used for application to lands. Without this project, the farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere. 
During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 117,000 tons of dairy manure would be treated and composted, with 30,000tons of organic fertilizer generated per year. Besides, the GHG emissions is expected to reduce 59,553 tCO2e per year and 595,530 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.
vcs-3738:
The Triunfo do Xingu Grouped REDD+ Project (hereinafter also referred to as “TdX”) is composed by seven rural properties located in the Municipality of Altamira, in the south region of the State of Pará. According to the geo-referencing data, the total area of the project is established at 10,636.02 ha. This project aims to be registered under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) to avoid unplanned deforestation (AUD), combating the decreased carbon stock in the Brazilian Legal Amazon. 
The crediting period of the project is 30 years. The start date is on August 31, 2022 and, therefore, the crediting period is expected to end on August 30, 2052. The baseline scenario developed is going to be used for the first six years of the project, since, according to VCS requirements, these six years are the maximum period until a baseline scenario reassessment needs to be done. The present analysis, that will be employed in the project validation and future project verifications, is going to be done in a conservative approach, keeping the project consistent.
The TdX aims for the following objectives: environmental benefits through a successful monitoring system; economic benefits resulting in regional development through investments in local communities. To execute the installation of this project and to achieve its objectives the VCU generation is very important. A baseline reduction of 1,565,285.35 tCO2e of GHG is expected over six years, associated with the avoided deforestation of 6,167.07 ha.
vcs-3739:
The Selva de Urundel REDD+ Project, seeks to enforce the protection of the native forest and the biodiversity of the Urundel forest located in the Province of Salta, Department of Oran, in northern Argentina. 
The Project started in January 2021 and is expected to reduce emissions by 3,513,643.40 tCO2eq in the first 10 years through 9,647 hectares of avoided deforestation, at an average of 351,364.34 tCO2eq per year. 
The project is expected to generate emission reductions through the reduction of deforestation and forest cover loss by implementing several activities that include the prevention and control of fires, the control of illegal activities occurring in the property (hunting, logging, grazing), the training and capacity building, as well as the cooperation with different institutions to promote alternative activities in the property including among others ecotourism and scientific research. 
This project is particularly relevant as it aims to preserve a territory which is part of the Yungas Biosphere Reserve, included in UNESCO’s Man and Biosphere Program (MAB) thanks to the arrangement of the Yungas mountain ranges which present a discontinuous and insular distribution that creates conditions for the coexistence of great biological diversity.
vcs-374: The project activity involves enhancement of the power generation capacity with the installation of a new 3MW turbo generator. The captive energy requirements of the KCP SICL sugar mill are taken care of by the already existing 4.25MW bagasse based cogeneration system. Now that the additional 3MW system is in place, it opens up the possibility of export of renewable based electricity to the grid.  The new 3MW turbine is of backpressure type and the extracted steam is used for process requirements. The existing 3MW and 1.25MW turbines cater the steam and power demand of the sugar mill, whereas the surplus power generated by the new 3MW turbine is fed to the grid. As a result of the project activity, the net electricity generation on site has increased enabling the export of electricity to the regional grid.  The project activity has been registered with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) as a CDM project activity (Reference No. 1571) on 13th June, 2008.
vcs-3740:
The carbon sequestered and stored in the coastal wetland ecosystems; mangroves, tidal marshes and seagrass meadows are called blue carbon. Sri Lankan coastline consists of blue carbon ecosystems predominating by mangrove ecosystems. The Puttalam lagoon is the second largest lagoon with the largest mangrove extent in Sri Lanka. The heaviest destruction of mangroves also exists in the Puttalam lagoon. As a response to the mass degradation of mangroves, the conservation and restoration process has been activated in this area. The GMSL together with Arinma Holdings commenced a pilot operation to rehabilitate 6000 mangrove plants in selected plots in Anawasala lagoon. The project was done in two phases, phase one we decided that the Rhizophora species was suitable. The number of plants available from both nurseries was 1300, and those plants were used for first round planting in March 2021. Phase two, the fishing community suggested that it would be better to plant propagules, therefore it was confirmed that 3000 plants will be purchases. Those 3000 plants were planted in zone A. After the commencement of the project A dedicated individual was appointed to look after the planted plants for two months. As the two months were coming to an end, the president of the village fishermen's association volunteered to take care of the plants. As of now information given by the Fisheries Society, states the plants planted have grown successfully thus far. 
Objectives:
• As a member of the United Nations global compact, Arinma holdings wishes to align with UN’s SDG hence promote life under water. This project adapted being to our company goals “under Water Stewardship” in order to mitigate climate change.
• Monitor carbon secretion by mangrove eco-systems and to find supporting data for future use.
• It is an untouched topic of research; hence it gives the students at the university the opportunity to engage in research.
• Provide the community with lively hood and food security.

Smart Power India (SPI), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Rockefeller Foundation, extends clean and reliable electricity to those without sufficient access, with the goal of ending energy poverty and transforming the livelihoods of the underserved. 

SPI is implementing distributed solar power solutions across India mainly by different modes – 1) mini grids for catering to the power needs of households, shops and small commercial applications in rural areas, 2) rooftop solar in commercial and industrial establishments and 3) off-grid solar for anchor loads such as telecom towers.

This grouped activity covers distributed renewable energy installations across states of India.
vcs-3743: The Grouped Project aims to implement forest restoration activities throughout the Brazilian Atlantic Forest Biome (hereinafter referred to as the project zone), primarily by replacing exotic grasslands formerly used for cattle raising. The project zone encompasses 17 states within Brazilian territory and is located in climatic and edaphic conditions suitable for plant growth. It also includes a region of high value for biodiversity conservation.The initial objective is to restore approximately 88,400 hectares of forest cover within the project zone and to facilitate the subsequent sequestration and storage of carbon in various carbon pools, including aboveground biomass, belowground biomass, litter, dead wood, and soil organic carbon. Net greenhouse gas removals are estimated at approximately 48,346,689 tCO2e over 100 years, equivalent to the annual removal of 483,467 tCO2e. The reduction of greenhouse gases (GHGs), specifically CO2, through the project’s activities is achieved via biological sequestration through plant photosynthesis. This potential is enhanced by implementing a continuum of human-induced forest restoration activities, ranging from assisted natural regeneration to full planting. In some cases, the process includes the use of commercial timber species native to the region to trigger the initial restoration process. In the absence of the project, the project areas would remain dominated by degraded pastures with low carbon stocks as a result of unsustainable anthropogenic activities. The project’s first instance (PAI-001) encompasses 345 hectares, is located in the municipality of Eunápolis, Bahia, Brazil, and is expected to generate 194,712 tCO2 over 50 years, equivalent to 3,894 tCO2/ha/year. The project’s second instance (PAI-002) covers 1,278 hectares, is located in the municipality of Potiraguá, Bahia, Brazil, and is expected to generate 743,324 tCO2 over 50 years, equivalent to 14,866 tCO2/ha/year.
vcs-3745: The Enexor Impact USA Project is a grouped project that generates emissions reductions through the deployment of Enexor’s Bio-CHP™ systems at client facilities across the United States. These modular, on-site systems convert organic and non-recyclable plastic waste into renewable electricity and thermal energy. Leveraging Enexor’s proprietary Bio-CHP™ technology, the project simultaneously addresses two major emissions sources: fossil fuel-based energy generation and landfill methane emissions. System performance and emissions reductions are continuously monitored through remote data systems and a secure cloud-based platform, ensuring accurate tracking and verification. Overall, the project represents a distributed infrastructure model for decarbonization, transforming waste liabilities into energy assets while generating verifiable carbon credits at scale.
vcs-3746: The project “NaturAll Carbon Program – Conservation Agriculture and Land Management in Brazil” belongs to NaturAll Carbon Limited and is located in Brazil, South America. The area is located in 23 states, covering a total area of 414.8 million hectares. The extension of the project covers four Brazilian biomes, Caatinga, Cerrado, Atlantic Forest and Pampa. It is very important to highlight that in order to preserve forests and swamps, lands from Amazon and Pantanal biomes will not be part of this project. As the leading causes of high GHG emissions and agricultural soil degradation have already been identified and are linked to inadequate management practices. But, although there are several studies and research data from all over Brazil, until now, there has been no efficient program to raise awareness and support rural producers in the transition to conservationist soil management on their agricultural property. Adopting conservation practices in the areas of agricultural and livestock activities, the goal will be to help reduce and remove GHG from the atmosphere, increase Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), avoid soil degradation (physical, chemical, and biological), improving soil fertility and productivity, creating a better resilience to extreme weather events, providing food security and preserving natural resources and their ecosystem services. The choice of instances inserted in the project will be based on implementing one or more regenerative or conservationist practices from November 1st, 2019, which are not common in the region, and there is additionality. The project intends to expand over time and reach multiple instances, and a range of agriculture and livestock activities in the four Brazilian biomes described previously to help drive resilient and sustainable agropastoral systems in these locations.
vcs-3748: The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in the north of Hongze District, Huai’an City, Jiangsu Province, China, with a total acreage of 12,843 ha of single-cropping rice. A total of 3,672 households (16,157 farmers) were involved in the project. Without the project, there would be no ditches, pumps, valves, and reservoirs to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario in which rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the paddy soil under flooded conditions, a large amount of methane can be released, so the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to saving water, improving rice yield and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.

The “Olive Groves for Carbon Farming” Project consists in new super-high-density organic trees crop plantations in Centre and South of Italy for olive cultivation with the implementation of innovative precision organic agriculture practices as Climate Change adaptation and mitigation Natural Based Project.
The Project activities take place in several Italian farms of Central and Southern Regions which are located in the Mediterranean Climate Area. Since “The Mediterranean region is a hotspot for highly interconnected climate risks” (IPCC 2021) and for this area it is expected a faster warming with respect to global temperature average rise (UN environment program 2020), The Project builds new resilient crops contributing to the climate mitigation through carbon reduction and removal, securing in the long-term food production and cultural identity.
The Project consists of crop change on agricultural land, from annual crops to perennial organic tree plantations with a super-high-density of 1,200/1,600 olive trees per hectare, with respect to traditional olive groves density of less 200 trees per hectare.
The Project involves changes and improvements of traditional and local common agriculture practices as: improved water management with new water dripline irrigation system, tillage reduction, fertilizer reduction, cover crops implementation like green manures and precision farming by vegetation monitoring with satellites and drones.
The Project started in 2019 in some farms, it was then implemented in others and its accomplishment is expected for all the remaining farms by 2025 for a total estimated area of around 2,500 hectares.
vcs-3762: The project recovers the Landfill gas of the landfill site to generate electricity. The project is constructed by 2 phases, with total capacity of 5MW. Gansu Ganzhou Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) locates in Mingyong Town, Ganzhou District, Zhangye City, Gansu Province, P.R China.The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects manure waste (dairy cow and sheep) from surrounding livestock farms in Ganzhou district. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. The recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation at the project site. The electricity generated by the project will be delivered to Northwest China Power Grid (NWCPG). The residual waste from the CSTR digesters will be used to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. In addition, the electricity generated from the biogas will be delivered to NWCPG to replace equivalent electricity generated by the fossil fuel fired power plants connected to the grid.
vcs-3767: MicroEnergy Credits – Microfinance for Solar Lamps in Kenya is a voluntary Grouped Project (GP) aimed at reducing fossil-fuel based electricity consumption by distributing Solar Lighting Systems (SLS) to local communities in Kenya. This project aims to help farmers deploy improved cropland management and regenerative agricultural practices in the croplands of Kenya. Over time, these croplands have undergone severe degradation due to anthropological factors, environmental conditions, and recurring natural calamities.

Around 75% of the population of Kenya is dependent on agriculture, and the sector supports a majority of the country’s food requirements. However, since agricultural production is largely rain-fed and around 80% of Kenya’s geography comprises arid and semi-arid regions, the occurrence of erratic rains and frequent droughts has imposed constraints on its productivity and stability.

In addition to natural disasters like droughts, degradation of land is greatly accelerated by unsustainable land use and management practices. Furthermore, in several parts of the country, soils are deficient in nitrogen, phosphorous and potassium, thereby resulting in poor vegetation cover. In this context, the opportunity to introduce improved cropland management practices will significantly help the croplands of the region and restore soil organic matter to their land, creating carbon removals while improving overall soil health.

The project activities include the adopt of practices such as no-till or reduced tilling, mulching with crop residues, reduced synthetic fertilizer application, using organic manures, water management, improved crop planting and harvesting methods, and agroforestry activities. These practices are proven ways to increase soil organic carbon, preventing further degradation of croplands and their soils, and enabling farmers to improve their productivity.

This grouped project consists of afforestation and reforestation activities, with an innovative silvopastoral system design taking place in Uruguay. The project activity involves the inclusion of exotic and native trees on grassland, which is in a degraded state due to a long history of overgrazing. Trees are introduced at a low density with a unique plantation frame so that both livestock grazing and forestry activities are integrated without displacing any previous activity. Some instances also include a novel intensive grazing management. 
The main aim is to sequester atmospheric carbon through photosynthesis, to be stored in aboveground and belowground tree biomass, as well as dead wood, litter, and soil organic carbon pools. The most common tree species will be Eucalyptus grandis (W.Hill), however alternative species including various native species will be included as part of the project.
This system is an alternative to the conventional high-density, large-scale plantations for pulp or sawn wood that are the most common forestry activities in the country. Despite the numerous barriers for its implementation, management, and harvesting, it is an option for farmers who want to include trees as shelter and shadow without leaving behind animal husbandry and replacing the native grass cover. Because of the low volume of production, normally the labor during planting and forest management is done by local people and the timber is sold to nearby small-scale sawmills, contributing to the local communities by providing a source of qualified jobs in the primary and secondary sectors. 
This project does not only contribute to the local and regional economy but also has a net positive impact on social and environmental aspects. With the utilization of native species, new job positions will be created in existing or new-to-exist nurseries, among other social benefits.

The proposed grouped project “SCALA 2 Laos Agroforestry Project’ is seeking carbon credits for carbon removal within an area of 31,500 ha in Nakathing-Nongkapath and Phou Talava Production Forests Areas (PFA) in Lao PDR.  These areas present a dynamic landscape consisting of a mosaic of settlements, agricultural land, regenerated or fallow forest and remnant forest ranging from high altitude mountainous areas to riverine valleys. The first instance, called ‘SCALA Laos Agroforestry Project 2.1 - Phase 1’ will be implemented in an area of 4,713 ha.  The remaining area will be implemented in subsequent project instances. 

The reforestation project aims to establish eucalyptus plantations consisting of ~90% of plantations with the remaining ~10% set aside for conservation management. The project follows a participatory approach to identify suitable areas for plantations including frequent consultations with the communities according to the FPIC principle. The Plantation Model is based on agroforestry systems allowing for agriculture crops to be grown between the tree rows. The project areas have been heavily impacted by logging and shifting cultivation. The area is also heavily impacted by use of defoliants, carpet bombing and chemical spraying during the American-Vietnam war, causing degradation of forest landscapes. The project will make productive use of degraded land and provide significant local and regional employment opportunities across operations. Plantation establishment will require UXO clearance which will provide community health and safety benefits over large areas and unlock the land for use beyond the life of the project. 

The project will increase carbon sequestration and reduce GHG emissions by establishing forest cover in degraded land areas. It is estimated that over a crediting period of 30 years, the project will generate  9,229,270 tCO2e of removals, with an estimated  1,386,148 tCO2e removals from the first project instance.

Foumbouni-Mitsamiouli solar farm involves the construction and operation of two solar photovoltaic parks of 4 MWp each in Foumbouni and Mitsamiouli, respectively in the south and north regions of the island of Ngazidja, Comoros. The solar power plants are equipped with 10,080 modules of 405 Wp each mounted on tracker single array, with a backtracking system. They are coupled with 1 MW / 2 MWh batteries that allow the solar farm to operate under 2 modes: hybridization and islanding to export power to the national grid.
The bundled project is the first solar power plant on the island and its power generation is off-taken and distributed by SONELEC (national power utility company) that was prior to the implementation of the project activity only relying on fossil fuel fired power plants. Therefore, the clean and renewable energy produced by the power plant is substituting to the grid electricity and cut down GHG emissions from baseline fossil fuel intensive grid mix. Apart from emission reductions, the benefits of the project comprise, among others, improvement of energy self-sufficiency of the country, as well as creation of local employment.
Today, electricity in the Union of Comoros is produced mostly by diesel generators. Besides its use of fossil fuels, this system fails in providing the local population with electricity: energy access remains below 60 %. Thus, the project’s 12.7 GWh/plant/year power generation will result in global emissions reductions of 9,384 tons CO2eq per year on average.

Regenerative farming practices are attracting significant interest within Australia's tree crop industries. Practices that are being trialled and introduced include: Reduced reliance on chemical fertilisers and pesticides, cover cropping, improved water use efficiency, establishment of new permanent tree crops, revegetation of areas surrounding orchards and adoption of carbon improvement management programs.
Implementing such practice changes are challenging as it requires up-front investment with considerable delay in financial return. This is particularly the case in: Non producing orchards during the establishment phase, where no or little income is generated for the first seven years and producing orchards in an environment of falling prices and rising input costs.  
This programme aims to provide additional economic support to farmers to fund, implement and maintain new regenerative farming practices that would alternatively not have been implemented, scaled up or maintained if it was not for this additional financial support. 
This programme is designed as a grouped project, focussing on tree crops in Australia, with the specific aim to generate carbon offset revenue from non-producing and producing orchards to finance regenerative agricultural practices.  These practices will improve SOC levels, but also lead to a reduction of chemical and energy inputs per unit of production. 
The potential of these practices is not being realised, as there is not a clear cost-benefit proposition, which this programme now aims to address. 
This project will also account for the additional biomass carbon generated in qualifying orchards established after the project start date, in accordance to the guidance under this option in VM0042.
Pilot assessments have shown that implementing the practices listed above can generate significant improvements in soil carbon levels. These improvements could amount to approximately 20 tonnes of CO2e reductions and removals/ha/year

The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice
cultivation is conducted in Jintang County within Chengdu City, Sichuan Province of China,
with a total acreage of 12,776 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of
this project, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice
was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic
matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4)
because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to
water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction than the
continuously flooded.
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which
results in not only large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity
by replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method, which
shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. In this case, the CH4
emission can be declined by an average of 48%1. Hence, with the proposed project activity,
an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 4.44 tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice is
expected. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the project activity
is 56,664 tCO2e/year, and the total GHG emission reductions are 566,640 tCO2e during the
fixed 10 years crediting period.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes;
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers;
- Increase the number of local individuals who have relevant skills due to diversified
educational opportunities from trainings;
- Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.
