This is a VCS-large scale project class implemented to protect the Chirisa Safari Area in the Midlands province of Zimbabwe. The project area of 144,796 hectares is owned by the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority (ZPWMA) and is leased to Carbon Green Africa (CGA) and Carbon Green Investments (CGI) for the purposes of establishing and running a REDD+ project. The partnership of CGA and CGI, hereinafter Carbon Green, is the project proponent. The main objective of the agreement is to establish a REDD+ project, with the aims of:
●	REDD+ carbon credit generation
●	Contribution to sustainable conservation in Zimbabwe
●	Development of a strategy for invasive species management
●	Fire and roads management
●	Game, water and habitat management
●	Strengthening antipoaching law enforcement
●	Wildlife population management
●	Promoting wildlife tourism and related activities
●	Community livelihoods enhancement 
The project proponent works in partnership with ZPWMA and adjacent communities in 12 wards across the surrounding 3 districts of Gokwe North, Gokwe South and Binga in a REDD+ scheme. Together the protected Safari Area and surrounding communal land make a project zone of 490,710 Ha. The project zone forms part of the last remaining corridor for animal movement and migration. 
The project aims to generate GHG emission reductions through 4 main strategic approaches:
1.	Direct forest and wildlife conservation to stop clearing and cutting of wood and wildlife poaching by implementing standard monitoring activities such as patrols
a.	Training to support law enforcement.
b.	Regular forest monitoring and carbon accounting will be done through aerial (remote sensing) and ground methods.
c.	Biodiversity assessments will be done via aerial methods supported by ground transects-based observations and citizen science. 
2.	Engagement and capacity building with key community and government stakeholders to willfully participate in one climate change mitigation goal
3.	Distribution of performance-based benefits to project zone communities delivered through local institutions 
4.	Implementation of sustainable alternative livelihood activities identified through a robust gender and inter-generationally sensitive participatory rural appraisal process
a.	Livelihood activities will include both subsistence and entrepreneurial initiatives in the fields such as agriculture, small scale, high-intensive controlled environment growing systems (greenhouses) 
b.	Vocational training on manufacturing of products for export
The baseline (without-project) scenario is unplanned deforestation due to the continual clearing of land for small-scale agricultural expansion and land degradation caused by overgrazing of cattle, driven by increasing populations and decreasing yields. The livelihoods of communities continue to decline, increasing the threat on the already declining biodiversity of the project zone due to erratic weather conditions. 
The project's clear CCB objectives are:
Climate – Avoided emissions of 14,280,937 tCO2e over a 30-year period at an average of 476,031 tCO2e per year, and in the process assist the human and wildlife population of the project zone to adapt to climate change impacts through income diversification, climate smart agricultural techniques, and habitat protection. 
Community - Alleviate poverty for more than 21,000 households, total of more than 90,000 individuals, specifically targeting women, vulnerable, and marginalized people. The project will also improve health, education and general social and infrastructure services within the project zone.
Biodiversity - Enhancement of the population of plant and wildlife species by conserving and maintaining vulnerable, threatened, and endangered species through habitat protection, controlled law enforcement, as well as rehabilitation and wildlife restocking.

The Painted Forest Carbon Project creates GHG offsets and forest health benefits through the purchase and management of 59,846 ha (147,882 acres) of private forest land, located in the District of Algoma near Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, Canada. The property is in a unique geographic location that will contribute to landscape level forest connectivity between the already established Lake Superior Provincial Park and Algoma Headwaters Provincial Park. The project avoids GHG emissions that would occur from harvesting the existing forestland. In the project scenario, significant carbon stocks are retained and sequestered through the preservation and continuing growth of the forest, creating substantial net benefits for Ontarians, and providing biodiversity benefits from the conservation and management of the area’s forest ecosystem.

The project scenario is improved forest management, wherein PFLP undertakes the forest carbon project and associated ecosystem protection and enhancement activities. The project scenario includes a low level of timber harvesting as part of forest management activities for the purposes of forest health, incidental infrastructure, ecosystem resilience, biodiversity and other conservation objectives.
vcs-3813:
The Motor Verde Forestry Carbon Project – Grandas de Salime (Spain) consists in the reforestation of 86.94 ha in Grandas de Salime, Principality of Asturias, Spain. 
The land over which reforestation is set to occur is part of the “Sierra de la Cuesta and Villarpedre” communal forest and is owned by the Grandas de Salime City Council. The area was affected by two wildfires in April and October 2017 that devastated the forest. Since then, no-human induced measures to restore the forest have been implemented. Furthermore, natural regeneration has been and continues to be impeded by the shrubland that now covers the area, thereby preventing natural regeneration.
Being an area with steep slopes and shallow soils, the land has been devoid of any forest vegetation since the fire and rainfall is now causing soil loss due to surface runoff. The hillside on which the works were carried out is located on the banks of the Salime Reservoir, which pours its waters directly into the Navia River.
The reforestation work consisted in extracting the burned material by using either the walking excavator felling head or a chainsaw. The burned material was then moved to the forest/logging trail and then a clearing was made using the felling head coupled to the walking excavator, whilst digging was underway. Then, the plots were treated, and seedlings planted by hand. A 10-metre wide strip adjacent to the clearing was made to serve as an auxiliary strip for fire-fighting purposes.
The project will remove a total amount of 50,370 tCO2 over a 100-year period, which works out at an average reduction of 504 tCO2 per year.
The project is part of Motor Verde initiative (see below). In Grandas de Salime, by means of recovering the forest that was lost in April and October 2017, the project will yield economic, social and environmental benefits. It will sequester carbon, it will restore ecosystems, and it will provide the local population with training and subsequent employment.
vcs-3814:
The importance of American forests to the global ecosystem and climate is central to the work of Chestnut Carbon, LLC, a US-based company that seeks to conserve and restore functional forestland throughout the United States for the primary purpose of increasing carbon sequestration. By the year 2030, Chestnut Carbon anticipates conserving up to 500,000 acres of land using long-term carbon management. This ambitious plan contrasts with regional common practice among the sellers of these lands: extractive timber harvesting to compensate for decreasing revenues from adjacent agricultural and ranching operations over time due to soil compaction and degradation. By extending rotation ages on these at-risk forests, the project increases carbon storage relative to the baseline case, as well as increases biodiversity and diversity in forest structure. 
To extend rotation ages across the project area, the project activity includes transitioning forestland into sustainable, uneven-aged silvicultural systems, where appropriate. These transition activities include the application of special silvicultural treatments that accelerate the recruitment of trees into standing dead wood, among other treatments. Estimated average GHG emission reductions are 221,312 tons CO2 equivalent per year, with total reductions over the first project crediting period of 5,532,801 CO2e. PAIs will be located across the contiguous United States and southern Alaska. To ensure sustainability in management, Forest Carbon Works requires PAI forestland to be certified by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) prior to commercial harvesting under the group certificate managed by Forest Carbon Works (SCS-FM/COC-009247). Approved management plans shall meet both FSC requirements and the requirements specified by the management policies of Forest Carbon Works related to the promotion of even-aged management, biodiversity, water quality and wildlife habitat.
vcs-3815: The Boutili Afforestation and Agroforestry Project (B2A Project), located northwest of the capital in Central African Republic (CAR), is made up of a mosaic of more or less wooded savannas and gallery forests. The human activities are traditional: slash-and-burn subsistence farming, collection of firewood, pastoralism. Their impact is increasing due to the proximity of the capital, Bangui. For many years, and the phenomenon is accelerating, these activities have been consuming forest areas faster than they are regenerating, leading to deforestation and degradation of wooded areas. The B2A Project aims to place local communities at the heart of a vast sustainable development program, aimed at revitalizing the socio-economic fabric of the region while restoring the forest cover.
vcs-3816:
The project will be developed in the municipality of Apuí, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil - within the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) category. The project will conserve 71,822.56 hectares of native Amazon Rainforest in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to pasture activities, part of which will be designated to Avoiding Unplanned Deforestation (AUD) (56,349.96 ha), other to Avoiding Planned Deforestation (APD) (14,158.28 ha) and the remaining hectares corresponding to water resources (314.32 ha). For the total area (AUD+APD) and by the end of the project, it is estimated a total avoided emissions of 23,452,633.10 tons of Greenhouse Gases (tCO2e). 
The project will follow the CCB Standards, with benefits for Climate, Community, and Biodiversity. As benefits for climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adaptation to the impacts caused by climate change, such as changes in rainfall regime, as the area presents a dense hydrographic network that contributes to the provision and quality of water in the Amazon River basin.
As quantifiable benefits for Communities, the project will implement groundwater collection and distribution systems, installation of solar panels for electricity generation and provision of satellite internet service in  low-income's extractive communities residences. 
The maintenance of forest cover ensures the conservation of biodiversity, the maintenance of ecosystem functioning (e.g., nutrient cycling) and of ecosystem services provisioning (e.g., carbon sequestration) performed by living organisms. It is noteworthy that the project includes a high priority area for biodiversity conservation, in compliance with the vulnerability criteria of the CCB Gold Level, as it presents species classified as Critically Endangered (CR) and Endangered (EN) according to the IUCN.
vcs-3818: The project will restore the areal extent of 3600 hectares in total along the Gulf of Mottama over the Myanmar coast, including 940 hectares in Yangon Region, 1500 hectares in Bago Region, and 1160 hectares in Mon State. The total GHG emission reductions and removals from this project is estimated as 5,037,323 tCO2e for a period of 20 years with an annual emission reduction of 251,886 tCO2e.
vcs-3819:
Flooding conditions in rice fields emit the most CH4, while intermittently flooded rice fields create a high quantity of N2O. Emissions of GHGs from rice fields can be reduced by modifying irrigation patterns, regulating organic additives, and using suitable rate and quantity of Nitrogen fertilizer. Irrigation practice such as Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) method has been observed to reduce GHG emissions in comparison to the traditional method 
of flooding. The time intervals between dry and wet conditions help in the transition from aerobic to anaerobic soil conditions, thus alternate wetting, and drying method leads in a significant reduction in methane generation1. Thus, the project employs AWD method to reduce the CH4 emissions. This will also lead to reduction in the water consumption, thus decreasing the input cost of the farmer. Before implementation of the project activity, the farmers were following the traditional flooding method, leading to the emissions of methane in the atmosphere. The project proponent conducted training programs and meeting with the farmers to make them aware about the benefits of adopting AWD, followed by the distribution and installation of AWD pipe in the fields of enrolled farmers. The first instance of the project is located in Haryana state covering an area of 4973 hectares. Furthermore, as it is a grouped project, the project activity will be implemented in other rice growing states of India in the future instances. Annual average emissions from the project are 48,853 tCO2eq.
vcs-382: The objective of this grouped VCS project is to reduce emissions of 10,970 tCO2eq annually by replacing 5,211,522 litres of furnace oil used for generating heat with 39,760 tonnes of sustainably grown fuel wood in two rubber factories at Seethawaka and Biyagama in Sri Lanka. by installing 3 Thermic Fluid Heaters in rubber glove manufacturing plants generating 9.5 kcal/hr of thermal energy. Out of these three thermic fluid heaters, 2 heaters are with capacity of 2.5kcal/hr each and are located in the Seethawaka Industrial park and the third heater with a capacity of 4.5kcal/hr is situated at the Biyagama Export Processing Zone.

vcs-3821:

According to CEA’s (Central Electricity Authority) Load Generation Balance Report 2018-19, actual demand supply gap in the Southern Region was -0.2% while the peak deficit was -0.4% during the year 2017-18. In Karnataka, the actual demand supply gap was -0.2% and the peak deficit was -0.5% during the year 2017-18. Trend shows that there has been a steady increase in peak demand in Karnataka while supply has not been able to match up to this demand. This project activity could have a positive impact on the demand supply gap by introducing energy efficient light bulbs thereby reducing peak hour demand of power in residential areas.

Considering this, in this section and elsewhere, wattage of baseline lamps has been referred to as 60 or 100 Watts. vcs-3822:
The grouped project “Reforestation program for multiple purposes as a means of sustainable development”, also known as “Plante com a Klabin” (Plant with Klabin), has as its stated goal the promotion of sustainable reforestation in Southern Brazil, specifically in the states of Paraná and Santa Catarina, aiming to achieve net removals of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere. 
The land use that has historically predominated in these states is agriculture and cattle raising. The project proposes a change in the traditional land use of this region, promoting reforestation practices as a sustainable alternative, either to produce wood for multiple purposes based on rapid-growth species (for example, Pinus.spp or Eucalyptus.spp), and/or to restore areas based on native species. 
Through an integrated approach, the project has established a set of incentives to make reforestation activities more attractive, with the aim to achieve important synergies between production and restoration, contributing to the strengthening of the low carbon economy and promotion of sustainable development.
vcs-3823: Partanna is developing a type of concrete that completely eliminates conventional Portland cement, a significant environmental advantage over conventional concrete. vcs-3824:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice
cultivation is conducted in Dujiangyan City within Chengdu City, Sichuan Province of China,
with a total acreage of 12,532 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of
this project, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice
was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic
matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4)
because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to
water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction than the
continuously flooded.
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which
results in not only large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity
by replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method, which
shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. In this case, the CH4
emission can be declined by an average of 48%1. Hence, with the proposed project activity,
an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 4.47 tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice is
expected. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the project activity
is 56,045 tCO2e/year, and the total GHG emission reductions are 560,450 tCO2e during the
fixed 10 years crediting period.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes;
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers;
- Increase the number of local individuals who have relevant skills due to diversified
educational opportunities from trainings;
- Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

vcs-383: The project activity under consideration entails generation of clean power by harnessing wind energy – a non-conventional renewable energy resource and export of the electricity generated to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board (TNEB) on the basis of Power Purchase Agreements. The electricity exported from the project to the grid thereby replaces an equivalent amount of power generation at the grid connected power plants which are primarily fossil fuel based. vcs-3830: The project is located at west of Huaiyin Village, Dayu Town, Jiyuan City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is owned and implemented by Jiyuan Weiheng Cow Breeding Co., Ltd.. vcs-3831:
The proposed grouped project activity seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by disseminating fuel-efficient wood and charcoal stoves in the host country Zambia of sub-Saharan African region. 
The lack of access to clean cooking remains very acute in sub-Saharan Africa with access increasing only slightly from 15% in 2015 to 17% in 2018. Since 2015, only 25 million people have gained access to clean cooking in the region, meaning that the number of people without access has increased to over 900 million in 2018 as population growth outpaced provision efforts. Sub-Saharan Africa is the only region where the number of those without access continues to rise significantly, highlighting the urgent need for action. The vast majority of people in sub-Saharan Africa thus rely on gathering biomass for cooking, particularly in rural areas, which dramatically damages health and impairs productivity improvements. 
‘SDG13 Ventures Pte Ltd’ (hereinafter called as “SDG”) is the project proponent (“PP”) for this project. SDG is a company registered in the Republic of Singapore. SDG, through its representative in Host Country will coordinate with the users of ICS directly or through local partners or its representative, to ensure that all requirements with respect to project activity, such as assisting with validation and registration, record keeping, monitoring and survey of households at a regular interval are met.
vcs-3832: The grouped project aims to install state of the art solar irrigation systems in India to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and assist farmers adapt to these changing climate conditions. vcs-3842:
Sarkisla Biogas Power Plant (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a biogas-to-energy project that involves methane capture through anaerobic digestion and utilization of methane for thermal energy and electricity generation via cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighboring animal farms with vacuum trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units for heat and electricity generation. The thermal energy is utilized for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is both used for internal electricity consumption and supplied to the national grid. 

The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 48,493 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 342,600 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

Dongxing Waste Incineration Plant leachate biogas Harmless Treatment and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Dongxing Waste Incineration Plant, in Zhongmu County, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Henan BCCY Environmental Energy Co., Ltd.in Zhongmu project City.
Before the implementation of this project, Zhengzhou (East) environmental Protection Energy Project invested by Zhengzhou Dongxing Environmental Protection Energy Co., Ltd. incinerates domestic waste with a daily treatment capacity of 4000t /d. Leachate will be produced during the storage and fermentation process in the garbage bin. The supporting treatment system of the factory is pretreatment +UASB+ secondary A/O-MBR aerobic system + nanofiltration NF+STRO treatment process. A large amount of biogas is produced in the anaerobic treatment section of UASB. This project collects the biogas generated by the anaerobic treatment section of leachate to generate electricity and connect to the grid, which can effectively utilize biogas resources.
The project started to construct on 30/11/2021 and started operation on 21/01/2022. The project has a total designed capacity 3MW (3*1MW) and combusts the leachate biogas, which contains nearly 65% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period will be 118,470MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reductions of the project are 66,089tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 660,899tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.
vcs-3852:
The project is to change from continuously flooded regimes to intermittently flooded regimes during rice cultivation in Wanzhou District, Chongqing City, China, with a total acreage of 18,723 ha of single-cropping rice. A total of 8,466 households (36,234 farmers) were involved in the project. Without the project, local villagers would not have access to intermittently flooded technology and intact facilities to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario in which rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the paddy soil under flooded conditions, a large amount of methane can be released, so the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to water efficiency, improving rice yield and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.
The implementation activities of the project include promoting intermittently flooded technology, technical training for the farmers, facility repair and replacement, etc. According to the needs of rice growth, farmers use pumps and valves to control irrigation and drainage, which not only saves water resources but also reduces methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions. Through the pumps and valves, the necessary water can be supplied to the rice paddies in time in the dry season, and the excess water can be drained from the rice paddies in the rainy season.
The project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions by 414,785 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,255 tCO2e. The project aims to reduce GHG and mitigate climate changes, increase rice productivity resulting in higher living standards for local farmers and provide more job opportunities.

The project is to change from continuously flooded water regimes to intermittently flooded water regimes during rice cultivation in Changshou District, Chongqing City, China, with a total acreage of 18,842 ha of single-cropping rice. A total of 8,774 households (38,255 farmers) were involved in the project. Without the project, local villagers would not have access to intermittently flooded technology and intact facilities to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario in which rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the paddy soil under flooded conditions, a large amount of methane can be released, so the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to water efficiency, improving rice yield and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.
The implementation activities of the project include promoting intermittently flooded technology, technical training for the farmers, facility repair and replacement, etc. According to the needs of rice growth, farmers use pumps and valves to control irrigation and drainage, which not only saves water resources but also reduces methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions. Through the pumps and valves, the necessary water can be supplied to the rice paddies in time in the dry season, and the excess water can be drained from the rice paddies in the rainy season.
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by 416,423 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,489 tCO2e. The project aims to reduce GHG and mitigate climate changes, increase rice productivity resulting in higher living standards for local farmers and provide more job opportunities.

Pingyuan Landfill Gas Power Generation Phase I Project (hereafter referred to as the project) captures the landfill gas that would have been released to the atmosphere in the absence of the project and generates electricity with the landfill gas (LFG). The electricity is supplied to the China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) to replace the electricity generated from coal-fired power plants of CSPG. 
Pingyuan landfill site is located in Dazhe Town, Pingyuan County, Meizhou City, Guangdong Province, P. R. China.
The purpose of the project is to use LFG, which consists mainly of methane, for electricity generation. It includes LFG collection system, LFG pre-treatment system and electricity generation system. The project started to construct on 19/08/2020 according to the contract of construction. The total installed capacity of the project is 2MW. The project consists of 2 sets of 1000kW generators which were was operated since 08/02/2021. LFG collected is used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators to generate about 61,489MWh supplying to CSPG during the first 7 years crediting period. The project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CSPG. vcs-3867:
In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, Vega-Hereko Istanbul Waste to Energy Project is being implemented by Vega Hereko Enerji Üretim Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi. The project activity is a methane gas power generating plant with a license capacity of 18.012 MWe. 
The project was commissioned with the generation of electricity from April 3rd, 2021, which is regarded as the project start date. The project's lifetime is 16 years, according to the EMRA Generation License. Also, the facility has a mechanical separation plant with 9,000 tons/day capacity. The sorting facility distributes the waste into organics. The separated organic fraction is taken for controlled anaerobic digestion (biological treatment tanks) together with the organic waste received by the facility. The methane recovered from digestion will be combusted through gas engines and the electricity is fed into the grid. Main objective and aim of the project is to take the separated organic fraction to controlled anaerobic digestion process and recover methane from the organic waste. The methane recovered from digestion is combusted through gas engines and the electricity is fed into the grid. The wastewater is re-used in the digesters, then will be sent to ISTAC wastewater treatment plant near the project area. The project is located in In Karakiraz Village, Sile District, in Istanbul /Turkey. This project adopts a crediting period of 7 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 320,042 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,240,299 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its first crediting period.
vcs-3868: Fangchenggang Mangrove Afforestation Project is located in Gangkou District and Fangcheng District of Fangchenggang City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting mangroves in degraded mangrove habitats. The project proponent is Fangchenggang Xinggang Agricultural Development Co., Ltd.The purpose of the project is to restore the degraded local mangrove ecosystem and increase forest cover by planting a variety of species of native mangrove, and establish a healthy local ecological and economic system by involving residents in the implementation of the projects directly. Totally 221.9 ha of mangroves have been planted with 5 native mangrove species (such as Avicennia marina, Kandelia candel, Aegiceras corniculatum, Rhizophora stylosa, Bruguiera gymnorrhiza). The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals, improve the local environment, enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing them with relevant technical skills. In addition, the project has restored the degraded mangrove ecosystem and increased forest coverage, provided a suitable habitat for animals, especially for endangered birds which mainly live in mangroves. The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 111,592 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 2,789.8tCO2e.

Future Green Carbon Project is an AFOLU initiative to be implemented in the Central West
region of Brazil, specifically in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul (MS). It is a voluntary action of
Eldorado Brasil Celulose S/A, aiming at the reforestation of more than
100,000 hectares with new and additional eucalyptus plantations , established exclusively on
non forested and anthropized areas . In addition to the creation of carbon stocks through
reforestation activities for production purposes , the project will also enable the recovery and
conservation of carbon stocks based on native species for conservation purposes. Even tho ugh
the restoration of such areas will be enabled by the project, resulting in direct climate benefits,
VCUs will not be claimed for such activities.
vcs-3877:
The grouped project “Reforestation of land for multiple uses” is a voluntary action to promote
sustainable tree planting in the Central-West region of Brazil, specifically in the states of Mato
Grosso (MT), Mato Grosso do Sul (MS) and Goiás (GO), on non-forested lands. Its objective is to
generate net removal of greenhouse gases through converting traditional land use in the region
– e.g. non-forested/agricultural areas – into reforestation actions, based on the engagement of
investors and independent rural producers. Also, the project proposes the restoration of nonforested
lands with the purpose of enhancing carbon stocks of native vegetation, including
protected areas, i.e. Permanent Preservation Areas, Legal Reserves, and other
lands, as applicable to each case.
vcs-3878:
The project's goal is to supply improved cook stove (ICS) in the rural areas of the Indian state of Rajasthan. ICS is an innovative cookstove that uses less fuel. The emissions of greenhouse gases will be decreased if improved cook stoves are used for daily cooking. The initiative will replace the conventional cook stove, which is mostly utilized in rural communities and uses a significant amount of wood to prepare food. The ICS is built with a remarkably high thermal efficiency, which will result in a minimal need for fuel wood use and less greenhouse gas emissions.
The project activity will have a good effect on the rural residents' daily lives and health. It has been demonstrated that ICS produces less smoke, which will lessen the respiratory health problems that result from using a conventional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS recipients will spend less time gathering firewood, and they will use that time to care for their families, children, and other productive tasks. Additionally, because the cookstove is completely enclosed, users and their families will be in a safer environment. The baseline scenario assumes that in the absence of project activities, the target population will continue to use non-renewable wood fuel to satisfy thermal energy needs comparable to those met by project cookstoves. The project participant intends to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in India's rural areas as part of this project activity. The project will remove 368,478 tCO2e of greenhouse gases on average each year. The project participants for this project are Climate Detox Pvt Ltd. And Siddhant Energy Consultants. Under the direction of a prepared team, ICS will be distributed in rural areas.
vcs-3879:
The Guangdong Huaiji IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Huaiji County, Guangdong Province of China by Huaiji County Weizhou Construction Investment and Development Group Co., Ltd, the geo-coordinate of the project is 23°28′07″N～24°23′30″N, 110°52′09″E～112°30′49″E, the total area is 355,661.39 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 14,870.98 ha, including 3,561 subcompartments. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned forests or collective-owned forests, and have the legal right to forest ownership. All the owners authorized the project proponent to access the project to their behalf. The species involved in the project are Pinus massoniana, Chinese Fir and Pinus elliottii. The forest of the project was older plantations under managing. The age of Pinus Massoniana was 20-31, Chinese Fir was 21-39, Pinus Elliottii was 21-38. Before the implantation of the project, the usual type of management was clearcutting.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 2,123,753 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 106,187 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 1,635,281 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 81,764 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

vcs-3880: The common practice for the swine farm owners to manage the manure is to have uncovered anaerobic lagoons/ponds at their farms in the region. i.e., Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in uncovered open lagoon and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility. In China, the uncovered anaerobic lagoons are a manure treatment method recognized by the state1. In addition, since there is no legal regulation to mandate the farm owners to implement anaerobic digestion, aerobic or other biological treatment techniques and to capture and/or utilize methane generated at these lagoons, therefore the continue of this common practice to treatment the manure i.e., uncovered anaerobic lagoons is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.
vcs-3881:
This project aims to reduce carbon emissions and other greenhouse gases by distributing our fuel-efficient, improved wood burning cookstoves (ICS) to rural households in West Africa. These will replace far less fuel-efficient three-stone fires. 

Cookstoves are manufactured in rural Togo, providing infrastructure, economic growth, and employment for the local community.  

The project aims to reduce the time burden of cooking and collecting firewood, which disproportionately falls to women. By reducing the amount of wood required for cooking, women will have more time to spend on educational and income-generating activities.

By providing a family with a fuel efficient cookstove, the indoor air pollution within their home will be reduced, improving health conditions and reducing smoke related illnesses. 

Alongside reducing the amount of GHG in the atmosphere, the reduced need for wood for cooking will help stop rapidly progressing deforestation. 

The project will work towards 8 sustainable development goals creating environmental, health and economic benefits for the end users as well as more employment especially for women.
vcs-3884:
The purpose of this Grouped project “Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in Sub Saharan Africa by BURN” by BURN Manufacturing Co. is to reduce the rate of deforestation in the remote areas of Sub-Saharan Africa along with indoor air pollution. The project will reduce the time spent by women in collecting fuel wood from large distances. 
Approximately, 3.2 million people die every year prematurely from illness attributable to the household air pollution caused by the inefficient use of fuels for cooking . 
Only 18% of population in Sub Saharan Africa have access to clean cooking fuel technology.  The Improved (ICS) cookstoves has a better combustion process due to which indoor air pollution along with GHG emissions is significantly reduced compared to traditional three stone cooking method. The beneficiaries will be the households in 9 countries of sub-Saharan Africa namely Kenya, Somalia, DRC, Mozambique, Tanzania, Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, and Ivory Coast. The geographical location of the project is the above mentioned 9 countries.
The baseline scenario is continued use of traditional method of open fire or three stone cookstoves using firewood as fuel in rural areas and charcoal as fuel in urban, semi-urban areas to meet the energy demand for cooking purposes.
This Grouped project deploys highly efficient Improved cook stove (ICS) models, known as ‘Jikokoas’ and ‘Kuniokoas’ reducing charcoal and woody biomass consumption for urban, semi-urban and rural households in the 9 countries mentioned in section 1.12 respectively
vcs-3885:
The objective of this project is to restore degraded mangrove sites in Kafoutine in Senegal. The project will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem in degraded lands.
The components of the project are reforestation, providing important ecosystem services, climate change mitigation, socio-economic improvements, and active participation of the local community.
Under this grouped project degraded mangroves are restored and enriched. In the first project activity, up to 1.9 million mangroves will be planted in an area of 750 ha, starting in 2023. The species selected for this reforestation project are indigenous and local, namely Rhizophora mangle and Avicennia germinans.
Training and awareness-raising of the local communities are crucial for the success for the project. From the start of the project, stakeholders potentially affected by the project have been involved in the process. This included providing information on all project activities and teaching basics on forest management, monitoring, forest protection activities, climate change, and carbon sequestration. Depending on the given conditions, up to 3,500 seedlings per hectare will planted. The project will sequestrate an estimated 355,000 tCO2 in the 750 ha over a period of 20 years.
The empowerment of the communities is central to the project. The labor requirement for the project will be fulfilled with local employment. Therefore, most of the budget for labor and an additional 50/50 share of carbon credit revenues will remain in the country. The project will promote a working family model where more than 50% of women can actively participate in the project.
Mangrove restoration will further increase fish populations and improve biodiversity. To measure the positive impact on biodiversity, annual biomonitoring will be conducted using eDNA.
Over the 20-year period, the project team will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem, improve the socio-economic status of the community, and foster climate change mitigation.

vcs-3890: Elmadag Biogas Power Plant (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a biogas-to-energy project that involves methane capture through anaerobic digestion and utilization of methane for thermal energy and electricity generation via cogeneration units. vcs-3891:
“Enteric fermentation emissions‘ reduction program of Uruguay” is taken place in a country where livestock farming covers a total area of 12,9 million hectares which represents 70% of the total national area (DIEA, 2021). This sector accounts for 57% of national net emissions, of which more than half correspond to methane emissions from enteric fermentation of livestock. This project will comprise approximately 100,000 animals per year, starting with a feedlot of 1,500 animals. In this system animals enter a feedlot with a weight of 415 kg and finish after 110 days with 590 kg. The breeds involved in the feedlot systems are Angus, Hereford and their crossbreeds.
The project will result in a reduction of methane emissions from enteric fermentation in beef cattle and dairy cows by providing a natural additive of composed by essential oils, flavonoids, and tannins: Anavrin. Anavrin® is a product that has been tested in recent years at the universities of Milan, Sassari, Santa Maria in Brazil, and at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of UdelaR in Uruguay. In addition, tests have been carried out in other parts of the world, where it was highlighted that the correct use of Anavrin® also improves the animal's daily production, around 70 g, and 1,5 l daily milk gain per capita. This a grouped project that starts with a farm located in the department of “Flores” near its capital city, The project start date is 1st April 2022. New instances (farmers) will be part of the project, benefiting from the use of the product itself but also from the generation of carbon credits, which will be seen as a reduction of the purchase price of the product. In 10 years, the project will be generating 100.000 tCO2, based on the preliminary estimations done by yet to be published papers. The project will monitor the emissions reductions according to VM0041 methodology by direct measurements.

vcs-3898: Guizhou Jinsha CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located in Taoyuan community, Liutang town, Jinsha County, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, China. The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. Twenty sets of CMM power generators are installed with a total installed capacity of 18MW, destroying 27.2 million m3 of methane annually. After the full operation of the Project, the expected annual exported electricity is 94,656 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Guiyuan coal mine area, and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG and displace part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG.

The project activity includes capture and utilization of landfill gas (landfill gas (LFG) contains approximately 50% methane and is a potent greenhouse gas (GHG)) for power generation, that would have been vented to the atmosphere in the pre-project/business as usual scenario. vcs-39: The project's purpose is to reduce the factory's greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions that result  from the combustion of fossil fuels for energy generation. A part of the textile manufacturing  process requires energy in the forms of steam and heat, which are provided by steam and  thermal oil boilers respectively.  There are two steam boilers (one main and one back-up) and  four oil (heat) boilers (two main and two back-up). Prior to the project activity, the textile  factory’s boilers operated solely on heavy fuel oil that is delivered to the factory in large  trucks. The factory has been operating since 1971 and since 1990 has used low-sulphur  heavy fuel oil (HFO)1 to fuel its steam and heat boilers. The project retrofits Offis' main  steam and heat boilers to operate on landfill gas by replacing the boilers' burners. The  landfill gas (LFG) will be delivered by a pipeline from the Hiriya Landfill, which is located  approximately 2 km away from the Offis plant.
vcs-390: The project activity is generation of electricity by utilizing waste heat. Waste gas coming out of the copper smelter at a temperature of 1044oC is allowed to pass through a waste heat recovery boiler. By utilizing the waste heat, the recovery boiler with operating pressure of 70 bar and temperature 285oC would generate 45TPH of steam. The temperature of steam is further increased to 485oC in the super heater, by utilizing furnace oil. The steam generated is used to drive turbine with 11.2 MW rated capacity.  Thus project activity utilizes the waste heat recovery technology to generate electricity. The electricity generated by the project activity displaces grid import. Thereby, reducing the green house gas emissions from the grid connected fossil fuel based power plants.

La Gioia farm is located in La Gioia, Alessandria in Northern Italy. The coordinates are attached as a KML file.  Several agricultural practices will be implemented or modified on the land. Taken together, the goal is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by this farm and raise the carbon stored in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. 

To do so, the following methods will be applied on site; Reduction of the inorganic fertilizer application, change of irrigation system, Incorporation of crops residues into the soil, Tillage reduction, Cover crop implementation, Reduction of the fossil fuel use, Switch from crops to woody biomass

The sectoral scope 14 – Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) is applicable to the project. Within this sector, this project has been developed under the scope of the methodology for improved agricultural land management (VM0042 VCS methodology).

The project has been found eligible under the scope of the VCS program as it meets all requirements established by the program. 

The crediting period chosen for this project is of 25 years, renewable 4 times. The period lasts from the 01/06/22 to the 1/6/2047. We estimated that 211,7 tCO2/year will be stored in the soil or not emitted.

The project activity “Creation of Biodiverse Forests for Land Restoration and Community Development” (referred as “the project”) is located in 5 districts in the Maharashtra state of India. The project works with individual farmers and community members across 5 districts of Maharashtra to help them afforest or reforest land that is fallow, unused or deforested thus helping to bring back lost biodiversity and creating green employment and income opportunities for community members. 

Forest plantations on unused or abandoned agricultural land are not only a great mitigation strategy, but also a great adaptation strategy. Biodiverse forests, as compared to traditional agriculture, are extremely resilient to extreme weather events like cyclones, drought, hailstorms and pest attacks. They thus can help provide a reliable source of supplemental income to the agrarian and tribal communities in India that are facing declining yields and income loss due to climate-change induced erratic rainfall and extreme weather events. 

The project involves planting of over over 120 different species of trees, shrubs, grasses and creepers to create small carbon-sequestering pockets of land with about 1000 trees / hectare that can provide a source of fruit, leaf, bark and oilseed harvest for community members, while also bringing back lost soil carbon onto the land and attracting a wide variety of pollinators like birds and bees to the area. Along the boundary of the tree plantation two to three different species of bamboo will be planted that community members can harvest in a sustainable manner for timber. The project is expected to create 30 labour days of rural employment per hectare to plant and maintain the trees every year.

The grouped project aims to provide individuals with intermediate improved cookstove (ICS). The stoves will be commercialized into several countries in Africa, starting with Togo as a first instance. Stoves will be distributed for free. 
The ICS distributed through this project will encourage households to replace the prevailing inefficient three-stone fireplace or traditional charcoal cookstoves such as charcoal clay cookers and charcoal iron stoves that are predominantly used across the region. The ICS provides for an efficient use of the thermal energy generated though the combustion of biomass while cooking and there is a more efficient transfer of this thermal energy to the cooking pot. There is thus a resultant reduction in both biomass consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
In addition to the reduction of biomass consumption (and associated reduction in expenses to purchase wood or charcoal – or reduction in time gathering firewood), there will also be an economic benefit in that the ICS will be produced locally in the region and will create jobs which will have a large proportion of female employees.

In order to protect the forest ecosystem, improve the ecological environment, increase carbon sinks, reduce GHG emission reductions and slow down climate change, PP decided to implement this IFM project activities from March 2020 to March 2050. And from the Project Start Date, PP has stopped the commercial logging in the project area.

The Forest Conservation Project activities will be focused on forest resource supervision and monitoring. This ecosystem will then continue to provide its services to all the communities and entities that depend on it. 

The project reduces greenhouse gas emissions by preventing logging, avoiding any kind of commercial harvest and other linked to logging activities, as decomposition of harvested tree, bark burning, emissions due to carbon fraction sequestered from wood products over time.

The project activity will significantly improve the forest management conditions within the project area, and benefit local ecological environment. The implementation of the project will not only achieve a reliable measurable carbon sequestration by reducing commercial timer, but also contribute to sustainable development of the local community, host country.

vcs-3925: Symbrosia's natural seaweed feed additive, SeaGraze™, reduces enteric methane emissions in ruminants by 80%. SeaGraze™ is made from the red seaweed Asparagopsis taxiformis (A. taxiformis). 9 peer-reviewed studies from institutions including The Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), UC Davis, and Penn State University have shown that replacing just 0.4% of a cow’s feed with A. taxiformis can reduce the amount of methane the cow produces by up to 98%. During this project, Symbrosia will collaborate with producers, academic researchers, and corporate partners throughout the United States to integrate SeaGraze™ into the diet of beef and dairy cattle and closely monitor the reduction of enteric methane emissions that is created. Initial project instances will be livestock operations located in Hawaii, California, and Oregon. Prior to the implementation of this project, in the baseline scenario, none of these operations supply any methane-reducing feed additive to their livestock. During the seven years of the project’s first crediting period, the project is expected to generate an average of 141,121 tonnes of CO2e reduction per year.

The regenerative livestock farming carbon project in Colombia is developed by the project developers Sosty S.A.S and Carbono Local+ GmbH. The project titled “Regenerative Livestock Carbon Project with a Participatory Approach in Colombia” is a comprehensive initiative developed by the project developers encompassing a variety of activities aimed at improving grazing practices, restoring soil health, and enhancing the resilience and well-being of farmers.
 
The primary objectives of the project are to reduce overall emissions through carbon sequestration in the soil while simultaneously improving farm productivity and conserving biodiversity in grazing areas. These goals will be achieved by enhancing livestock production practices, specifically by ceasing 
grassland burning and implementing adaptive multi-paddock grazing. The project will also 
promote the diversity of forages rather than the monoculture of pastures. This includes the 
management of native savannahs and introduced pastures, incorporating nitrogen-fixing species, 
and integrating silvo pastoral systems. The grouped project is developed within the Colombian agricultural frontier (located in five different eco-regions), which is the delimited area defined by the government, where livestock husbandry and agricultural activities are allowed to be developed. The project’s start date is 20.01.2020 and its crediting period goes on to 40 years. The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice
cultivation is conducted in Southern Pengzhou City within Chengdu City, Sichuan Province
of China, with a total acreage of 12,437 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the
implementation of this project, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the
scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario.
Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of
methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is
more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction
than the continuously flooded.
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results
in not only large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by
replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method, which shortens
the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. Hence, with the proposed
project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 4.55 tCO2e/ha for singlecropping
rice is expected. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the
project activity is 56,539 tCO2e/year, and the total GHG emission reductions are 565,390
tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes;
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers;
- Increase the number of local individuals who have relevant skills due to diversified
educational opportunities from trainings;
- Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

The project involves dissemination of the Changu Changu Moto high efficiency biomass cook 
stoves to approximately 19,000 households in Nkhata Bay District, Malawi. The project is being 
developed under the small scale CDM methodology AMS- II.G. Energy efficiency measures in 
thermal applications of non-renewable biomass, version 5.
The Changu Changu Moto is a low cost, high efficiency biomass fired cook stove developed 
through extensive trials with the local communities and is specifically designed for local Malawian 
conditions. The stove is constructed from locally available materials and does not require specialist 
construction skills or equipment. The stove design is a brick rocket stove, constructed using 26 
mud bricks and a mud mortar mix. The Chichewan name Changu Changu Moto translates to “Fast 
Fast Fire”, and reflects one of the main benefits of the improved cook stove in reducing cooking 
time and saving wood fuel.
The Changu Changu Moto improved cook stove will replace the low efficiency 3-stone fire stove, 
which is the dominant firewood end-use system for cooking within Malawi. Emission reductions are 
achieved through improving household energy efficiency and thus reducing the consumption of 
non-renewable woody biomass

Gansu Hui County Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduces a new Animal Waste Management System (AWMS) to treat manure from this existing pig farm in Hui County, Longnan City, Gansu Province, which belongs to Xingjiang Muge Co.,Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. The estimated lifetime of project is 15 years.
First, all manure and wastewater will be collected and then solids and liquids will be separated. The solid manure will be processed in an aerobic composting system and organic fertilizer will be produced, and the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers free of charge. The liquids will be treated by anaerobic digestion and the biogas produced during the treatment process will be captured and sent to a boiler to generate heat, with the excess gas being destroyed through a combustion system (if available). The sludge produced after fermentation is applied as fertilizer to nearby fields, and the wastewater from the anaerobic digester is used for agricultural irrigation.
With the help of the above-mentioned model, a harmless and ecological use of pig manure can be achieved. It is estimated that approximately 900 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. Also, the generated heat through biogas will be only used for daily operation of the AWMSs and the swine farms themselves and will not be provided to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 68,384 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 478,688 tCO2e in the crediting period.

Zhejiang Jia’ao Biodiesel Production Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located at No.416 Desheng Road, Industry District, Zhouquan Town, Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province, China. The Project is designed to produce 150,000 tonnes biodiesel BD100 (hereafter referred to as “the biodiesel”) annually made from the feedstock of waste oil/fat. The biodiesel produced will be supplied to consumers to substitute diesel used for car fuel.
The Project produces biodiesel based on waste oil/fat from biogenic origin to substitute petroleum diesel for the use as fuels. Biodiesel is a fuel which produce lower GHG emissions when combusted, hence the GHG emissions will be reduced resulting from such displacement.
vcs-3969:
Hebei Handan Damingchang Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) locates in Cao Ren Village, Dangtou Township, Daming County, Handan City, Hebei Province, P.R China. The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects manure waste from dairy cows from Daming farms in Daming County. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. The recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation at the project site. The electricity generated by the project will be delivered to North China Power Grid (NCPG). The residual waste from the CSTR digesters will be used to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. In addition, the electricity generated from the biogas will be delivered to NCPG to replace equivalent electricity generated by the fossil fuel fired power plants connected to the grid.
vcs-397: Dodhia Synthetics Limited initiated the project activity based on renewable energy to partially displace the GHG emission that would have taken place had an equivalent quantity of power as generated in the project activity been met out of combustion of fossil fuels. The project activity consists of a renewable energy based power generation facility at Sangli district in the state of Maharashtra in India. The project activity harnesses the kinetic energy of wind to produce electrical power in a Wind Turbine Generator (WTG) with a rated capacity of 0.6 MW. The power generated is sold to the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL). The power generated is evacuated through HV transmission lines to the facility’s switchyard and from the switchyard up to the state grid (NEWNE grid) substation.

vcs-3971:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in Nanchang City， Jiangxi Province of China. Anyi County is located in the west part of Nanchang, with a total acreage of 6949.6 ha for double-cropping rice. Without implementing this project, which provides ditches to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded. 

This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results in not only a large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by replacing the continuously flooded method with the intermittently flooded method, which shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . 

The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 1,603,490 tCO2e in 21 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 76,356.6 tCO2e.

vcs-3973: The Involtor Future Agriculture East-Europe is a grouped project gathering under the same program major agricultural areas from Romania and aiming at the scientific implementation of modern agricultural practices that helps preserve the Planet's climate, increase the resilience of agriculture and food security to climate change. The project provides a wide range of support for farmers, aiming for a safe transition to regenerative agriculture by implementing effective practices that sequester carbon in the soil, reduce / remove the emissions of CH4, N2O, CO2 that agriculture emits today in significant quantities, and in exchange for the performance monitored by this Project, farmers will receive income from verified carbon credits. vcs-3975: The refugees crisis in South Sudan, led to hundred thousands of households moving from their country to Uganda. In August 2022, the total number of refugees was 1,525,197  persons (382,778 households). This flux increased strongly the deforestation rate in the regions where refugees are installed. A study  conducted in 2029, showed that between 2014 and 2018, there was 34,11é ha of tree cover loss and 29,604 ha of degradation. The sudy also highlighted that in the 14 targeted refugees settlements the demand of cooking fuel was equivalent to 345,000 tons. Which is 4 times the quantity of tree growth within the settlements and the 5 km buffer zone. A joint assessment conducted by FAO and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in one settlement (Bidibidi) in March 2017  concluded that the aboveground biomass (AGB) stock within the settlement area could meet the needs of the population for only three years, in the absence of any intervention.
vcs-3976:
The Palma Development Foundation created the Rovuma Belt project with the objective of supporting the economic security  of the Cabo Delgado province in Mozambique through the development of sustainable social, economic, environmental protection and reforestation projects in the Palma and Mocimboa da Praia Districts. The vision is to redefine these districts as key producers of biomass for carbon sequestration as well as construction materials. Sustainably produced and harvested biomass, on scale, will greatly contribute to the preservation and re-establishment of natural habitats, reduce deforestation, reduce carbon dioxide emissions, augment carbon dioxide sequestration, as well as provide sustainable livelihoods for thousands of people.
The project consists of creating a “bamboo belt” between the communities of Palma, Mocímboa da Praia and Awasse. In each community, the FPDP will develop a 50 hectares area for the bamboo plantation and train a local association of 50 families, whereby each family becomes the owner of 1 hectare (ha) of bamboo production. Furthermore, the area will be intercropped with locally consumed produce, and a water system will be installed. Farming tools, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and income support will be provided for the beneficiary families in the 1st year, together with fit-for-purpose training, follow-up and monitoring by an experienced agronomist. In each community, the FPDP collaborates with a local leadership group, including the leader and other local influential individuals, that will represent the community in the target geography and beneficiary selection processes.
vcs-3977:
Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in West of Fuling District in Chongqing City (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that changes the water regime during the rice cultivation period from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded on rice paddy fields located in the West of Fuling District in Chongqing City, China. The project involves 16,472.7 hectares of single cropping rice within the project boundary.
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by reducing the flooding time during the rice cultivation period. Since soil organic matters emits a large amount of methane (CH4) under flooded conditions because of anaerobic decomposition, when the flooded time of rice fields in the whole growth cycle is reduce, CH4 emissions are hence reduced; in addition, it provides other benefits such as creation of job opportunities, water saving, and yield increase compared to the traditional continuously flooded cultivation.

vcs-398: Heilongjiang Huanan Hengdaishan West Wind Power Project (hereafter refers to the proposed project) is to build and operate a 45.05 MW grid connected wind farm, located in Hengdaishan, Huana District, Jiamusi City, Heilongjiang Province, P.R.China. vcs-3980:
Xinjiang Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 3 existing swine farms in  Xinjiang Province, which are owned by AKSU Xingjiang MUGE food Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
In this project, AWMS is built to replace the traditional open anaerobic lagoons, and each subsidiary swine farm installed one AWMS. The manure and waster will be collected into the anaerobic digesters and then biogas generated during the anaerobic treatment process will be captured and total of 3.7 million m3 biogas is expected to be generated annually. Biogas is then sent into biogas boilers for heat production. Every biogas boiler has been installed in each swine farm. All of the heat generated is used by AWMSs and the swine farms, while the rest (if any) will be burned. The sludge produced after fermentation is applied to cornfields as fertilizer, and the wastewater produced by anaerobic biogas digesters is used for agricultural irrigation.
Benefiting from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMSs and 3 swine farms. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed. The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 415,544 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 2,908,811 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

This group project activity (GPA) intends to replace motorcycle with internal combustion engines (ICE) which use petrol fuel sources, by electric motorcycles. Therefore, the GPA will replace fossil fuel powered motorcycles by electric motorcycles, thus leading to emissions reduction
In sub-Saharan Africa, the transport sector account for 14.5% of total energy combustion  representing 69 millions metrics tons of oils equivalent. This consumption is expected to grow to 10.1 quadrillon BTU by 2040 with an increase of 3.1%  per year. 
The transport sector is also the second largest source of emissions in Africa, accounting for 28% (348 Mt CO2)   of the total emissions of the continent.
The sector is also one of the main causes of urban pollution. It is estimated that 90% of urban air pollution is attributable to vehicles emissions, and according to the World Health Organisation, 176,000 deaths per year in Africa are due to outdoor air pollution .
The purpose of this grouped project (the project) is to tackle these issues by the dissemination of 753,300 of electric motorcycles 2 wheelers in different countries across Africa by 2026.
The first instance of the grouped project is the distribution of 67,746 e-motorcycles in Togo by 2026. The second instance is the distribution of 111,554 e-motorcycles in Benin by 2026.
The global CO2 emissions of Togo was 2,6 GtCO2 in 2018, with transport representing more than 77% of the total emissions .
This first instance in Togo may lead to emissions reductions of 460,644 tCO2e over the first crediting period, or on average 65,806 tCO2e/year.
The second instance in Benin may lead to emissions reduction of 754,247 tCO2e over the first crediting period, and 107,750 tCO2e/year on average.

The VCS Milopri project - Precision Management Systems for Sustainable Avocado Orchards, is the flagship project of We-Agri’s Regenerative Carbon Credit Network (RCCN) initiative - an intelligent platform designed to provide a holistic solution to endorse commercial fruit orchards and vineyards around the world. 

Fruit trees have great structural characteristics (e.g., long-life cycle; permanent organs such as the trunk, branches, and roots; minimum soil tillage; high quality and yield) which allow them to accumulate a significant amount of carbon (Sharma et al. 2021). Hence, the motivation to establish a sustainable agricultural system in orchards and vineyards that can further minimize emissions and is capable of efficiently sequestering carbon within the atmosphere.

This is a pioneering project that follows the SCOVY (i.e., Sustainable Carbon Orchards and Vineyards) methodology, which is currently being developed by We-Agri. This methodology will be the object of future works that will encompass different fruit crops. The main goal is to shift commercial fruit orchards into sustainable agricultural systems endorsed for the issuance of high-quality carbon credits by implementing smart-climate agricultural practices.

The Milopri grouped project is situated within the western Galilee region in the northern part of Israel. The project location has an overall area of circa 3,000 hectares which are owned by 25 different Israeli agricultural cooperative villages. These farms are consolidated into one Centralized packhouse & logistic center - Milopri Agricultural Cooperative. 

The project activities aim at increasing the capacity of soil to sequester carbon and reducing nitrogenous fertilizer-related greenhouse gas emissions. The project also holistically aims at achieving sustainable management practices which not only improve soil health and productivity but can also achieve socio-economic development in the project area.
