Sichuan Huashun PET Recycling Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) aims to produce PET fibers and PET particles by recycling and processing post-consumer PET bottles, to replace the same amount of PET products produced from raw materials. The total production capacity is about 60,000 tons of recycled polyester (PET) products per year. The project is located in Pengxi Country, Suining City, Sichuan, China and is developed and operated by Zhejiang Zhongwei Carbon Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “the project proponent”).
Before the project implementation, the same amount of PET product was produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well.
It is estimated that the Project will achieve annual GHG emission reductions of 59506 tCO2e and total emission reductions of 416,542 tCO2e over the first crediting period.
vcs-3992: MEM OSB-1 SOLAR POWER PROJECT includes installation of rooftop solar photovoltaic systems with the objective of generating clean energy (electricity) for the purpose of inhouse/captive consumption in the commercial facilities of the project owners. Consumption of clean electricity generated in the project activity by harnessing renewable energy (solar) resources has resulted in avoidance of grid power that was used by the project facility/project owner in the pre-project scenario. The project activity has therefore resulted in curbing emission of greenhouse gas, which would have been emitted from generation of equivalent amount of electricity in the grid tied power plant, that has been avoided due to the project activity. The project activity encompasses a rooftop solar power project with the capacity of 10.3 MWe. The proposed project activity deployed in Turkey by MEM Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi. The project is expected to result in an average annual supply of 8,974 MWh/year. The average annual emission reduction from the project is estimated to be around 5,822 tCO2e/annum and a cumulative emission reduction of 40,753 tCO2e for the entire crediting period of 7 years.
vcs-3993:
The project intends to include producers dedicated to extensive agriculture (corn, soybeans, wheat, sunflower, cotton, and other crops), and extensive cattle ranching, mostly cattle and grazing grasslands, pastures, agropastoral, and silvo-pastoral. Given the characteristics of the country, farm and ranch  production dates from no more than 200 years ago.
During most of the 20th century, the farms were managed in a rather extensive manner and with aggressive tillage systems, which caused widespread declines in the organic matter content of the soils. This lasted until the end of that century, when for different reasons the producers adopted zero tillage systems, which are what predominate today (more than 90%).
The projects to be implemented are expected to mitigate climate change both by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and by capturing atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) and storing it as stable carbon in the soil, which must be recarbonized. The greatest efforts to reduce GHG emissions will be due to the adoption of better nitrogen fertilization technologies, which include alternative sources of nitrogen and variable rate fertilization that reduce nitrous oxide (N2) emissions from fertilized soils, the intensification of agricultural rotations with greater incorporation of winter crops, nitrogen fixing species and cover crops, and improved grazing management in livestock, which increase carbon stocks and with improvements in digestibility that reduce methane (CH4) emissions due to enteric fermentation. 
It is estimated that with these improvements, which are not currently widespread even among producers, it will be possible to reduce between 0.5 and 3 tons of CO2e/ha/year. Obviously, the total amount will depend on the area committed by the producers. This area is expected to reach more than 160 thousand hectares. If this is so, it is expected to mitigate almost 2 million tons CO2e at the end of this project.
vcs-3994:
Hubei Jinnonggu AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to the two swine farms in Shilong Town, Jingshan City, Hubei Province, China, which are owned by Hubei Jinnonggu Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Technology Co., Ltd. The project activity aims to treat the manure and wastewater from the 2 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
The common practice for the swine farm owners to manage the manure is to have uncovered anaerobic lagoons/ponds at their farms in the region. As per “technical specification for sanitation treatment of livestock and poultry manure[ https://oss.baigongbao.com/2020/12/14/MRyhTKQcWC.pdf]”, In China, the uncovered anaerobic lagoons are a manure treatment method recognized by the state. In addition, since there is no legal regulation to mandate the livestock farm owners to implement anaerobic digestion, aerobic or other biological treatment techniques and to capture and/or utilize methane generated at these lagoons, therefore the continue of this common practice to treatment the manure i.e., uncovered anaerobic lagoons is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.
Benefiting from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMS and the swine farm. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed. 
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 65,470 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 458,290 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

The Family Forest Carbon Program (FFCP), administered by the Family Forest Impact Foundation (FFIF), is an innovative, incentive-based program engaging private family and other non-industrial private forest landowners throughout the United States in improved forest management practices, promoting forest health, carbon sequestration and storage, and other environmental conservation and protection practices. 

Through its grouped project design, the FFCP is able to engage and achieve economies of scale with smaller non-industrial forestland owners, reaching ownerships that have been largely unrepresented in voluntary carbon markets. The FFCP solves challenges to small forest holdings participation in carbon projects, by reducing cost and complexity of participation. 

FFCP provides incentive payments to forest landowners to implement climate-smart practices that increase sequestration and storage of carbon. The FFCP further connects enrolled landowners with technical assistance from local consulting foresters, helping family landowners transition to long-term, sustainable forest management. 

The first project activities implemented in the FFCP program (directed towards the U.S. Central Appalachia region) include: Growing Mature Forests (GMF) –20-year, renewable agreement to limit timber harvest (with imposition of minimum residual basal area and riparian buffers and prohibition on high-grading/diameter limit cuts), thereby increasing net growth. The GMF practice, compared to common practice high-grading in the region, is expected to generate net emission reductions of ~1.6 t CO2e/acre/year. total GHG emission reductions and removals.

The project activity instance locations of this project disclosed in the public kml file correspond to the centroids of the counties where the project's activities are located. Specific details of the project activities’ locations can be requested at datarequest@forestfoundation.org
vcs-3997: The project activity is a Landfill Gas Power Generating Plant. Electricity production will be done by burning the landfill gas. Landfill gas will be burned in gas engines and electrical energy will be obtained from the ends of the generator coupled to gas engines. Electrical energy to be taken from the ends of the generator will be increased to medium voltage level in transformers and given to the interconnected system. Whilst providing sustainable development benefits to the host communities and the host country, the project activity reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions mainly by preventing GHG emissions, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from waste at the solid waste disposal site that would be otherwise left to be decomposed; and by replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid which is primarily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources.
vcs-3998: The project aims to address widespread land and agro-ecosystem degradation and climate-change related hazards across the landscapes of Rulindo and Bugesera districts in northern and eastern provinces of Rwanda respectively. The project will undertake a number of activities including: 1) planting of around four million functional tree species on both smallholders’ farm plots and public suitable lands to restore degraded ecosystems, protect watersheds, sequester carbon, conserve biodiversity, and provide farmers with a diversified income streams, e.g., from fruits and timber; 2) establishing seedling nurseries to provide quality materials for tree planting 3) provide trainings to enhance knowledge to a wide range of key stakeholders, including farmer groups, the youth, community advisors, Community Extension Officers, nursery managers, project’s staff, etc. 4) promoting specific livelihoods activities, e.g., horticulture package, livestock husbandry, Village-based Savings & Loan Associations (VSLA), local investments, etc.; 5) facilitating market access for farmers products/produce by encouraging farmers to organize into cooperatives/ other community structures, and when possible, entering into supply agreements with off-takers; 6) engaging farmers in sustainability agreements - committing them to sustain the implementation of the project activities for the long-term, beyond the project’s crediting period (≥20 years). The project activities aim to address this land and agro-ecosystem degradation and directly contribute to climate mitigation through increased carbon storage in tree biomass and in soils within the agricultural landscapes. The new VERRA’s Verified Carbon Standard carbon methodology called Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation Projects will be used. The ex-ante annual average GHG emission reductions of the project are estimated at 70,470 tCO2e, and total GHG emission reductions over 20 years are estimated at 1,414,808 tCO2e.
vcs-3999:
The project “Zambia Agroforestry Grouped Project” is comprised of the cashew plantation execution started as of January 2020 to 2021 for 5.5million of cashew nuts seedlings in the total of 72,000 hectares in ten districts (Mongu, Limulunga, Lukuku, Metete, Kalabo, Sikongo, Nalolo, Senanga, Sioma and Shangombo) in Western Province in Zambia. The project at the beginning initiated under the contract with CIDP in Western Province, in partnership with the Empowering Farmers Foundation, it is our intention to develop our project areas into a voluntary carbon project through the GHG emissions removals by such planting activities, which should in turn allow to perform regular gap filling, continue the plantations, thereby expanding the planted areas significantly.
We intend to perform a comprehensive environmental study, covering the feasibility of expanding the cashew plantations beyond the current project areas potentially to Eastern Province, in collaboration with ETG group companies and partners.
In the Eastern Province in Zambia, EFF had also executed 1 million (1.043.425) of cashew seedlings plantation in six districts namely: Nyimba, Petauke, Sinda, Chadiza, Mambwe, Lundazi.
vcs-4: The purpose of this project is to mitigate and recover animal effluent related GHG by improving AWMS practices.  The proposed project activities will mitigate and recover AWMS GHG emissions in an economically sustainable manner, and will result in other environmental benefits, such as improved water quality and reduced odour.
vcs-40: The project is located in Langxiang Town, Yichun, Heilongjiang Province of China. The project is a wind power plant. The proposed installed capacity is 28.05 MW consisting of 33 0.85MW turbines. The details of the turbines with respect to their numbers, type and model of the machines have been verified /4/ to be as per details provided in the PDD. The electricity generated is supplied to CNPG (which is dominated by coal-fired power plants) under Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)/5/. The project has accounted for emission reductions generated by the proposed project from 29 March 2007 to 17 May 2007. The projects emission reductions are determined by multiplying the net amount of electricity generated by the project by an estimated ex-ante fixed grid emission coefficient of 1.0985CO2e/MWh.
vcs-400: Zhejiang Provincial Energy Group Zhenhai Natural Gas Power Generation Co., Ltd.’s NG Power  Generation Project (the proposed project) is located in Zhenhai Power Plant, Hongqiao Village, Zhenhai District, Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province. The proposed project is the construction and operation of a new natural gas fired grid-connected power plant owned by ZheJiang Southeast Electric Power Co., Ltd. It will install two sets of gas-steam combined cycle for power generation units with the total rated output of 795.6MW. The generated electricity will be sold to the East China Power Grid (ECPG), which covers Shanghai, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Anhui and Fujian provincial grids.
vcs-4000: The Grouped Project activity “DelAgua Clean Cooking Grouped Project in The Gambia” aims at distribution of Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in the Least Developed Country The Gambia. The program is reducing the usage of firewood as fuel used for cooking at household level, thereby reducing the GHG emissions arising out of the burning of fossil fuels. This reduction in the firewood usage at the household level will be achieved by the usage of project ICS for cooking, as it has a higher thermal efficiency, therefore, consuming lesser amount of fuel and time in cooking a specific amount of meal.
vcs-4001:
The proposed VCS biochar grouped project aims at adopting improved waste handling and disposal (WHD) practices to remove carbon from atmospheric carbon pools across multiple biochar project instances. The grouped project is expected to reduce atmospheric greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions concentrations through the removal and subsequent storage of carbon dioxide (CO2) following the steps below:
• Sourcing of waste biomass that would have otherwise been left to decay or be burned for purposes other than energy use.
• Stabilization of carbon by converting waste biomass into biochar through a thermochemical process, where organic material is thermally decomposed to elementary carbon under the absence of oxygen.
vcs-4003: The project involves the installation of bundled Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) power plant with a cumulative capacity of 9.51 MW primarily to meet the captive demand of the premises owners and export of surplus power to the grid through the mechanism of net metering. All the solar panel units involved in the project are implemented under the DBFOT model, i.e., Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Transfer. The premises owners are the customers of the power generated from the solar panels which purchase the power under long-term power purchase agreements signed for 25 years. Before installation of the rooftop solar units, the Kochi Metro premises, Subros Ltd., SECI rooftop premises owners used to meet the electricity demand from the national grid of India. The project thus replaces fossil fuel-dominated grid electricity thereby reducing the equivalent amount of GHG emission.
vcs-4004: The objective of the Native Ecosystem Restoration in Nicaragua Project is to reforest an area of around 20,000 hectares, starting with the acquisition of 6,000 hectares of unused or under-used, degraded land in Nicaragua currently managed as abandoned or cattle pasture grazed at very low densities, and restore this ecosystem with native trees in order to sequester carbon dioxide. The degraded land will thus be rehabilitated with native tree cover, and over time biodiversity and local hydrology will be restored. The grouped Project will control erosion, regenerate soil health, and increase water infiltration, consequently improving ground water levels in the area, as well as provide local employment opportunities. Most land being considered is in the Central and Pacific regions of Nicaragua, but all regions of the country with degraded cattle pasture are eligible.
vcs-4005:
The “Macaúba as a Productive Second Floor” is a VCS AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use) grouped project, Scope 14, and, specifically, it falls under the ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation) category. 
The project works with local farmers to implement integrated systems in previously degraded pastures and/or croplands. The main project activity consists of the planting of Macaúba trees. This will be done considering two possible arrangements: (i) Macaúba intercropped with pasture (silvipastoral) or (ii) macuaba intercropped with agriculture (agrisilvicultural).
Through the planting of Macaúba trees the project will contribute to an increase in carbon stocks and associated GHG removals. The project activity will also improve the livelihood of local farmers and provide other ecosystem services, such as: maintaining the local microclimate, preventing erosion, conserving soil and moisture.
vcs-4008: The project activity “Terraligna Afforestation over degraded grasslands” is an afforestation project over extensive cattle grazing pastures areas using exotic species (mostly Eucalyptus dunnii) aiming to produce biomass for energy and/or pulp. The Terraligna project eligible for the VCS standard is circumscribed to 4,282 ha effectively planted after the trust fund operation starting date, carried out in 8 properties (7 entire plots and 90% of the effectively planted area of the 8th). The area corresponding to the other 19 of the trust fund properties (5,896 ha) will not be presented as part of the project as it does not meet the requirements of the VCS Standard boundaries. The project activity is carried out on degraded land as a consequence of many decades of intensive cattle grazing. This degradation is expected to continue in the absence of the project. The project utilizes 2 species: mostly Eucalyptus dunnii and Eucalyptus smithii in a lesser extent, 95.9% and 4.1% of the planted area, respectively. The project sequesters CO2 through forest plantation in grassland areas, generating net anthropogenic removals by sinks. The long-term average GHG benefit (LTA) is determined by averaging the expected total GHG benefit for the length of the project (100 years: from 21/12/2019 – until 21/12/2119). The total GHG benefit for the length of the project is 1,112,972 tCO2e, when divided by 100 years results in 11,130 tCO2e.
vcs-401: The proposed project activity is implemented at Roi Et Flour Company Limited, which at present has a full production capacity of 800 tonnes of native starch per day. The proposed project activity involves the installation of an anaerobic wastewater treatment facility adopting the Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket technology, at the existing tapioca processing plant.
vcs-4010:
Agriculture is the mainstay of rural economy in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh and is the single largest employment generator. Of the total population of 25.5 million, 70% of the population is engaged in Agriculture of which 80% belonging to small & marginal category (around 3.746 million farm families) 1 with limited investment capacity. Poor irrigation
coverage, inability of the small farm holders to opt for irrigation has in turn forced small and margi nal farm holders towards subsistence and monocropping practice thereby narrowing farm sector income, declining interest in farming and farm investment, and triggering concerns over food security.
vcs-4011:
Qinghai Taiheyuan Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to the two swine farms in Huzhu County, Haidong City, Qinghai Province, China, which are owned by Qinghai Taiheyuan Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd. The project activity aims to treat the manure and wastewater from the 2 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
 All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
Benefiting from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMS and the swine farm. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that
93,501 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emissionreductions are 654,507 tCO2e in the first crediting period.
vcs-4012: The project activity involves installation of a 8 MW installed capacity of WTE power project in Phon Sawang Sub-District, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai province, Thailand. The electricity generated from the projects supplied to grid and thereby avoids CO2 emission associated with grid-based electricity generation.  The project also avoids methane emissions from waste management as the project avoids the organic waste going to landfill which would result in methane emission in the baseline senario.
vcs-4014: Sinop Landfill Gas to Electricity Project is located at Sinop Landfill Site in Hacioglu Neighborhood, Central District, Sinop Province Turkey. The project is owned by Biokütle Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş. The facility started operation on 29/06/2021 and the feed-in electricity is estimated to be 21,210 MWh / year  at full capacity during the 7-year crediting period. The project is expected to reduce 30,789 tCO2e/y annually in the first 7-year crediting period between commission date of 29/06/2022 and ending date of 28/06/2028.
vcs-4015:
The Sanergy Composting Group Project is located in Kenya and produces compost and compressed fuel briquettes from various organic and biomass waste sources. These waste sources include food waste, wood dust, sugarcane bagasse, slaughterhouse waste and human sanitation waste. The processes also entail a pre-treatment step with the use of black soldier fly (BSF) insect larvae, which valorize some of the organics in an aerobic process and leave behind a residue which is called frass. The frass is then mixed with other types of organic waste aerobically composted into organic fertilizer for local farmers. Furthermore, the frass can be mixed and compressed into biomass briquettes which are in part used on site, and the residual briquettes are sold to local industry as a renewable fuel for industrial boilers generating heat and steam. 

The first project activity instance is located in Nairobi, Kenya. Sanergy Limited is the owner of the facility located in Nairobi and is the Project Developer for the Sanergy Composting Group Project. Circular Impact is the project proponent.
vcs-4016: The Amazon Biome Conservancy Grouped REDD+ Project (hereinafter also referred to as “ABC”) has as its main objective to contribute to the preservation with the biggest tropical forest of the world in the Brazilian territory, while providing significant improvements in the social interface. The project for this validation process has only one project activity instance located in the Itacoatiara municipality, state of Amazonas near its capital of Manaus. According to the geo-referencing data, the total area of the project is established at 5,140 ha, which is composed of native Amazon Rainforest vegetation, without the existence of secondary vegetation since the land has not been cleared of native ecosystems within the last 10 years before the project start date. The project area consist of the ABC project is equivalent to the 20% of the landowner property area that he could legally suppress, according to the Brazilian forest code (Law 12.651, 2012). This project will be eligible under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) category, using the VM0007 methodology for Avoiding Planned Deforestation (APDD). The crediting period of the project is 30 years. The start date is on 19/11/2022 and the crediting period is expected to end on 18/11/2052. To execute the installation of this project and to achieve its objectives the VCU generation is very important. A reduction of 2,605,773.23 t CO2-e of GHG is expected over the next ten years for the first baseline developed and presented in this Project Description - PD (average of 260,577.32 t CO2-e per year).
vcs-4018: This project activity will capture waste CO2 which would have otherwise been emitted into the atmosphere, or atmospheric CO2 which would otherwise be in the atmosphere, and utilize that gas as a feedstock in the production of concrete. These project activities reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sequestering CO2 via the production of concrete. This manufacturing process has the additional benefit of requiring less Portland cement, which further reduces emissions, because the cement production process is highly energy and carbon intensive. The project activity will take place at the location where the concrete is first manufactured (mixed with cement, water, aggregates, etc.). At its peak, this project activity will result in approximately 542,500 metric tons of CO2 reduced over the crediting period, the average annual emission reductions being 67,813 tCO2eq.

vcs-402: The project involves the installation of power generator modules (or gensets) at the Jiang Cun Gou Municipal landfill (hereon referred to as “the landfill”), to allow the increasing volumes of landfill gas from the incoming waste to be captured and utilized for power generation. The landfill is in the city of Xi’an, in Shaanxi, China. It is the only operating landfill in Xi’an city and serves an important role in managing the environmental cleanliness of a city with 2.7 million people.  The Project aims to enhance the landfill gas collection system by installing new power generators and new gas collection wells. The landfill gas will then be combusted in landfill gas reciprocating engines to produce electricity. The produced renewable energy will be exported to the Chinese national grid.  The implementation of the project will bring about environmental and social benefits to the residents of the city, and technology transfer to better manage the environment.

vcs-4021: The project activity promotes sustainable agriculture practices among cotton farmers in order to reduce the usage of synthetic fertilizer and biomass burning. The project activity aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the agricultural fields which mainly source from the stubble burning, excess use of fertilizer and as a result excess water requirement for irrigation etc
vcs-4022: The AgreenaCarbon Project aims to reduce agricultural GHG emissions through the implementation of activities that are central principles of regenerative agriculture. The Project intends to help farmers transition to regenerative agriculture by applying sustainable agricultural land management practices (ALM) in order to maintain yields while ensuring long-term viability of their farms and land. Regenerative agriculture describes holistic farming practices that improve the soil fertility and enhance the storage of soil organic carbon (SOC) and ‘focuses on the regeneration of living soil, improved micro hydrology, and conserving biodiversity at all levels while enhancing inputs use-efficiency and ecosystem system services.’  The AgreenaCarbon Project assists farmers in the transition from conventional, intensive farming practices to ones that avoid soil disturbances and increase the amount of organic soil amendments all while reducing the use of synthetic fertilisers. The focal point of these practices is reducing tillage to reduce soil disturbance with the addition of the other activities as a combined suite of activities that contribute to soil fertility. The Project facilitates the transition through a carbon payment programme which provides economic incentives to change existing agricultural practices, described as project activities. The programme is located across Europe and is based in temperate climates.
vcs-4025: The fragile ecosystem of the upland tribal regions in Keojhar and Mayurbhanj districts of Odisha have been affected by deforestation and rampant shifting cultivation practices causing extensive soil erosion, reducing the capacity of land to rejuvenate and affecting natural vegetation and water resources.In order to address some of the issues of the communities it becomes pertinent to adopt interventions based on improved land use planning, soil-moisture conservation measures and improved farming based agroforestry practices. This will not only strengthen the agrarian livelihoods of the tribal households, but also increase their food and nutritional security.The proposed project in the two districts of Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj is aimed at improving the livelihoods of the tribal communities by restoring 4000 hectares of barren uplands through plantation of forest and fruit tree species mostly in private lands. Additional components include land development, soil-moisture conservation, crop diversification and intercropping and promoting organic farm and pest management practices. The project will be implemented in 4000 hectares covering 3 blocks of Keonjhar district (Harichandanpur, Jhumpura and Champua) and 2 blocks of Mayurbhanj district (Udala and Khunta). The project aims for economic upliftment of the small holder famers through improved land use planning, increase in production and productivity, social empowerment of women along with enhancement of the carbon sequestration potential through such interventions.
vcs-4026:
The proposed project activity aims to generate renewable electricity through a 25MWp photovoltaic power plant located in Caraculo, Nambibe province, in Angola Southern Region, which currently relies mainly on diesel thermal plants for electricity production. The project is implemented by Solenova, a company jointly owned by Sonangol and Eni Angola.
This project activity represents the first phase of a larger photovoltaic project having a total capacity of up to 50 MWp. The overall project is implemented in following phases as requested by the Rede Nacional de Transporte (“RNT”) as the sole offtaker, taking into consideration the current load and the need to ensure the full dispatchability of the energy produced.
The area identified for the project is located 2 km west from Caraculo village (Namibe Province), adjacent to the EN 280 road and the South Transmission Grid. The area covers about 165 ha and was proposed for this initiative by the Province Authorities.
The scope of Caraculo project is to ensure a reliable production of electrical renewable power to be dispatched into the Southern Transmission Grid of the Country, which currently relies mainly
on diesel thermal plants for its supply. The expected annual average energy production over the 24 years project technical lif etime is up to 59 GWh/year. The scope of works also includes the construction of a MV/HV substation inside the project area.
The project first phase implementation (25 MWp) will permit a diesel consumption reduction of about 18.000 m3/year. The average annual GHG emission reduction expected with the implementation
of the project activity is around 50,000 tCO2e per year.
vcs-4027: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Guamá landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) at the CPTR Guamá landfill through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare and utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of about 2 MW).
vcs-4029: The Electric Vehicle Charger Premier Aggregation Project (Project) project is proposed for registration under the Verra Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VCS Standard, Version 4.2, 20 January 2022 (Standard) and associated Program Guide, Version 4.1, 20 January 2022 (Guide). The Project is an Aggregate Project, consisting of multiple Project Activity Instances (Instances), and is proposed to be submitted following VCS Methodology VM0038, Methodology for Electric Vehicle Charging Systems, Version 1.0, 18 September 2018 (Methodology). The Project will generate GHG emission reductions through the displacement of fossil fuel powered vehicles across the included fleet categories as detailed below) with grid-connected electricity. The existing scenario prior to Project implementation (Baseline Scenario) is the operation of comparable fleets (as defined in the Methodology) that would have been used to provide the same transportation service in the absence of the project. Namely, the comparable fleets in the baseline comprise fossil fuel driven vehicles. As such, the energy generated by direct combustion of fossil fuels and release of emissions at the tailpipe of vehicles in the Baseline Scenario is equivalently displaced by less fossil-fuel intensive grid-connected electricity in the Project Scenario.
vcs-403: The project is a combination of five GHG reduction projects located in five different cement manufacturing units of SCG Cement Co.,Ltd, in Thailand. All project activities in this group involve partial replacement of fossil fuels by alternative fuels or less carbon intensive fuels, including biomass, in kiln processing of cement manufacture. In order to implement the project activities a complete system for receiving, storing, and feeding alternative fuels and less carbon intensive fuels needs to be introduced.
vcs-4030:
220MWDC Minbu Solar Power Plant (hereafter simplified as “the project”) is a newly built grid-connected photovoltaic power plant with an installed capacity of 220MWp, which is located in Minbu
District, Magway Region, Myanmar. The project is divided into 4 phases with a capacity of 50WMp
for phases 1-3 and 70MWp for phase 4. Currently, phase 1 has been operated since 27 September
2019 while phase 2 is under construction with an expected COD in 2024. Phase 3 and
4 are expected to complete 1 and 2 years respectively from phase 2 COD’s date (2025-2026).
The project is ultimately owned by Green Earth Power (Thailand) Co. Ltd which the company hires
GEP (Myanmar) Co. Ltd (its subsidiary)The project is to develop and operate. by Green Earth
Power (Myanmar) Co. Ltd (it's subsidiary).
The existing scenario prior to the implementation of the project is the electricity being generated
by the Ministry of Electricity and Energy, Electric Power Generation Enterprise (EPGE), and the
baseline scenario of the project is the same as the existing scenario
The purpose of the project is to generate electricity by using renewable solar energy, and the
electricity generated by the project will be delivered to EPGE for 30 years period ending on 26
February 2049 to replace equivalent electricity generated by fossil fuel-fired power plants
connected to the EPGE.
vcs-4031: The proposed ARR VCS project intends to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale traditional farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the states of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Uttarakhand, India. This project will help in increasing tree outside forest (TOF) that will add in mitigating climate change. The project shall also enhance the income of farmer communities along with biodiversity conservation and improvement of soil health.
vcs-4032: This project aims to reduce the CH4 emissions through improved water management practices involving alternate wetting and drying (AWD) of the paddy lands instead of the traditional continuous flooding method. Along with reduced water usage by implementing AWD, the project also aims to improve soil health without any yield penalty.
vcs-4034: The Agropalma REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Agropalma Group and its purpose is to promote forest conservation, maintenance of carbon stocks and mitigation of climate change through the reduction of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from land use change. In addition to the climate benefits, the Project also intends to generate social benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and improved well-being of the surrounding communities, as well as environmental benefits through actions aimed at the conservation of local flora and fauna. The Project area covers 50,519 hectares of Amazon forest and is located almost entirely in the northeastern mesoregion of Pará State, including the municipalities of Tailândia, Moju, Tomé Açu and Acará. The region has great relevance in relation to its biodiversity, since it is located in the Belém Center of Endemism (CEB), a place with a large concentration of rare and endemic species. The predominant vegetation is Dense Ombrophylous Forest with a high density of medium and large trees, besides woody lianas and epiphytes.
vcs-4035:
The project activity focuses on the development of Bamboo as a key resource for catalyzing an inclusive green economy. In this project, different types of bamboo species will be planted to restore degraded lands. It will help the local communities and farmers generate income by involving them in different livelihood activities like making of bamboo handicraft and furniture. In addition, it will help to sequesters atmospheric carbon dioxide, which aids in climate change mitigation, as well as improving soil in the project area through conservation practices. 

The project activity will be implemented across states of India. This is a grouped project.

First project activity instance:
The Konkan Bamboo & Cane Development Centre (KONBAC) is a not-for-profit company, facilitated by the International Network for Bamboo and Rattan (INBAR) through the Centre for Indian Bamboo Resource and Technology (CIBART). 

The KONBAC organization planted bamboo species with the collaboration of local farmers in 24 districts (Ahmednagar, Akola, Amravati, Aurangabad, Beed, Bhandara, Buldhana, Chandrapur, Dhule, Jalna, Kolhapur,	Latur, Nagpur, Nanded, Nandurbar, Nashik, Palghar, Parbhani, Pune, Sangli, Satara, Solapur, Thane & Wardha) of Maharashtra, India. The area covered in the project is about 595.5 hectare.

The techniques used for the plantation are vegetative propagation, rhizome & the seedlings. This seedling are sourced from the various designated nurseries and planting from various empty and barren locations in the project.  KONBAC provides hands-on training to farmers in the scientific processes of propagation, cultivation and harvesting.

The first VPA is estimated to sequester average 26,292 tCO2e annually.
vcs-4036:
26MWp Solar Photovoltaic Power Plant in Bavet City, Cambodia (hereafter referred to as “the 
project”) is a solar power project with total installed capacity of 26MWp, located in Monourom 
village, Bavet City, Svay Rieng Province, the Kingdom of Cambodia. The project is invested by 
Green Sustainable Ventures (Cambodia) Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “the project owner”).
The purpose of the project is to utilize the solar energy at the project site to generate and supply 
electricity to Electricite Du Cambodge Grid (EDC) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the electricity delivered to the grid by the project 
activity would be generated by the operation of grid-connected power plants and by the addition 
of new generation sources into the EDC. This is the scenario that existed prior to the 
implementation of the project activity and is also the baseline scenario.
The project is a renewable energy project and is expected to supply an annual average of 37,085
MWh of zero-emission electricity to EDC during the whole project lifetime of 25 years, which 
replace the power generation of those fossil fuel-fired power plants delivered to the EDC under 
the baseline scenario. 
The project started construction on 13-Apr-2021 and commissioned on 27-Jan-2022. The 
expected total emission reductions are 185,314 tCO2e during the first crediting period from 27-
Jan-2022 to 26-Jan-2029, with average annual emission reductions of 26,473 tCO2e.
vcs-4042:
The Cauaxi REDD+ Grouped Project (hereafter called GPD) aims to conserve forests in several private properties located in northeast portion of Pará, close to the border with Maranhão. The Cauaxi River, which gives the project its name, is one of the tributaries of the Capim River, located in the central portion of the project's reference region, at Paragominas municipality.
The GPD aims to create positive economic incentives for landowners to conserve rainforests in private areas that are vulnerable to degradation and deforestation, while contributing to net positive climate impacts as well as benefit to traditional communities and conserve biodiversity. By joining BRcarbon (hereafter known as BRC), forest owners can access funds from the carbon voluntary market to develop conservation and monitoring efforts in their forests. A partnership between BRC and landowners will result in the legal protection of forests, forest monitoring using satellite images, biodiversity inventory (including fauna e flora species), and forest biomass inventory in a broad scale, using 
a upscaling approach based on field collection, drone-borne and satellite sensors such as LiDAR (light detection and ranging). In addition, we will involve surveillance of property, wildfire monitoring, fire prevention and fighting, threatened species protection and social activities with traditional communities. 
As a result, BRC expects to enhance the climate impact of carbon projects, helping communities and biodiversity. The Cauaxi REDD+ Grouped Project is part of the company's initiative to promote forest conservation using the financial flows of the carbon market. This project is related to climate-positive impacts caused by the reduction of emissions 
caused by deforestation and avoided degradation (REDD+).
vcs-4043:
Adoption of agroforestry approach is a viable alternative solution for the local communities in India to increase the fertility of their land and create livelihood opportunities to overcome extreme poverty. It is a system that can provide both food and income sources while preserving and rehabilitating the ecosystem. The proposed ARR VCS project aims to support tribal communities of ASR district in Andhra Pradesh, India. For the first project instance, approximately 12,500 hectares of area under agroforestry has been considered. The different species included in the proposed ARR project activity includes mango, silver oak, teak, jackfruit, cashew, and several other local tree species. The project area is located in 22 Mandals of ASR district in Andhra Pradesh state. The project activity involves the distribution of improved cookstoves (ICSs) among local communities based in some areas of Mozambique (Country), where currently several households still rely on inefficient and pollutant traditional cooking techniques.
The project aims to replace the traditional cooking mechanisms used by local people (three-stone fire or rudimental stoves) with ICSs that require less fuel and decrease the biomass combustion’s emissions, with a consequent reduction of health hazard coming from the indoor smoke pollution. The introduction of more efficient stoves will help to limit the demand for woody biomass, reducing the unsustainable use of forests and halting deforestation that is progressing rapidly in the Country. The improved cookstoves’ deployment will also have a positive impact on women’ life, reducing the time they spend for collecting woody biomass and cooking the meals, giving them the possibility to invest their time in a more effective way.
Through the implementation of engagement and training processes dedicated to the local communities involved in the project, all the households receiving the ICS will be aware of the environmental improvements and the carbon finance benefit generated by their effective use of the stove.
This project will be developed in the Republic of Mozambique. The areas of implementation will be the Central portion of the Country, considering in particular the provinces of Sofala and Manica.
The average annual GHG emission reduction expected with the implementation of the improved cookstove distribution project in the Country is around 120,000 tCO2e per year.

Mangrove habitats are substantial and dynamic carbon sinks, contributing significantly to the global carbon cycle and having the ability to reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide levels. India accounts for about 4740 sq. km, or around 3 percent of the world's mangrove cover. Andhra Pradesh state on the East coast of India has two major mangrove patches with an area of approximately 550 sq. km. The project is being developed in the Krishna and Coringa Wildlife Sanctuaries and the reserve forest areas of Andhra Pradesh. The project activities include Habitat management and Eco-development activities. Local community members are proposed to be engaged in the implementation of different REDD+ activities. This will provide an alternate livelihood opportunity for the local communities and eventually enhance their economic conditions/status as well as reduce the biotic pressure on the mangrove ecosystem. Thus, the project activities empower the local communities and improve the quality of mangroves. Additionally, female members of the fisher community will also be involved in the nursery development and other plantation related activities, thereby empowering the women as well.
Location: Krishna and Coringa Wildlife Sanctuaries and the Reserve Forest areas of Andhra Pradesh
Average annual Emission Reductions (ERs): 239,250
Total GHG emission reductions: 4,785,000
Along with the conservation and improvement of mangrove ecosystems and community development, the project will also help in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) like SDG 1 (No poverty), SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 15 (Life on land), SDG 16 (peace, justice and strong institutions) etc.
vcs-4046:
The project area is in Nepal which is a home to a plethora of flora and fauna which spread across Terai to the middle to mountain of the country. Around 5962.03 (000 ha) of land was under forest cover in 2020. Forest Act 1993 recognizes two essential kinds (national and private) and five auxiliary kinds of forest beneath national forest (Government Managed, Community Managed, Protected Forests, Leasehold Forest, Religious Forest, and Private Forest). Deforestation, degradation and fragmentation of natural habitat of wildlife are a serious threat to forests of the country which alarm the need for protection of biodiversity. Adopting agroforestry practices is the best possible solution as this system can avail basic needs of an individual and rehabilitate the lost ecosystem. The primary objectives of agroforestry are to produce food, fodder, fuel-wood, and/or timber. There can also be co-benefits such as carbon sequestration, water quality enhancement, soil protection, and biodiversity conservation. 
Agroforestry system in Nepal is a traditional and ancient practice. Farmers in the hills have expanded the number of agroforestry trees on their farmland in response to forest degradation and deforestation, to meet their immediate demand for fodder, fuelwood, and small-sized timber products. The agroforestry systems deliver several forest products, agriculture products and ecosystem services which may enhance social well-being of the local farmers, national and global community. The small and marginal farmers are almost unaware of the scientific importance (economic and environmental aspects) of agroforestry, short- and long-term benefits, and technical requirements. There awareness efforts to educate farmers on the benefits of agroforestry practice in their farmlands.

Household air pollution is a global crisis and India is not unaffected by the problem. There is significant dependence on polluting traditional chullahs (fuelwood stoves) for cooking in rural and semi-urban households in the country. Household pollution can cause diseases and women are particularly affected due to their direct exposure to cooking fires and involvement in daily cooking. Combustion of the non-renewable fuels and release of greenhouse gas emissions in the environment adds to global warming problem. 
The proposed project will be addressing this problem by providing access to improved cooking solutions (ICS) in the form of energy efficient cookstoves. This is a voluntary initiative by Tata Communications Limited (Project Proponent). PP will be collaborating with local implementation partners to provide improved cooking solutions for marginalized households living in rural and semi-urban areas in India. 

The baseline scenario is the continued use of non-renewable fuelwood by the target population in absence of project activity. 

Under the grouped project, three project activity instances are being implemented in the states of Meghalaya, Odisha and Jharkhand. Over a period a total of 20,000 ICS shall be deployed.

Shangqiu Weijie Agricultural Development Co., Ltd Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to swine farms in Hanying Village, Hedi Township, Sui County, Shangqiu city, Henan Province, China, which are owned by Shangqiu Weijie Agricultural Development Co., Ltd (hereinafter called” Weijie”). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater from the swine farm to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. In this project, a closed anaerobic lagoon was constructed to replace the traditional open anaerobic lagoon, for this project, animal waste management system (AWMS) refers to this closed anaerobic lagoon. The manure and waste will be collected in the anaerobic lagoons and the biogas produced during the anaerobic treatment will be collected, which is expected to produce 435 *10^4 m^3 of biogas per year. The biogas will then be used in the pig farm's electricity and heat generation system, and the electricity and heat generated will be used in the daily production and staff life of the pig farm. All the electricity and heat generated a reused by the pig farm, while the rest (if any) will be burned. The sludge produced after fermentation is applied to the corn fields as fertilizer, while the wastewater from the anaerobic
digester is used for agricultural irrigation.
Benefited from the “waste biogas fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMSs and the swine farm. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system, and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed.

Jiangxi Zhenghe Livestock Manure Treatment Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Jiangxi, China, which is operated by Jiangxi Zhenghe Ecological Agriculture Co., Ltd. The proposed project is an animal manure management system, which utilize livestock wastes from nearby farms, to produce biogas and organic fertilizer through an anaerobic digestion process. 
The raw material (i.e. livestock waste) from neighboring farms was collected and transported to each biogas plant by the principle of proximity. Continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units for heat and electricity generation. The thermal energy is utilized only for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is both used for internal electricity requirements and supplied to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The slurry produced by anaerobic fermentation is transported through pipe networks and utilized in nearby farmland to create an ecological recycling industry. The residue waste is used to produce solid organic fertilizer.
Before the implementation of the project, manure from livestock farms was treated by uncovered anaerobic lagoons without biogas recovery, and CCPG provided the same amount of electricity. This is also the baseline scenario for the project. The successful implementation of the project not only reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions but also develops clean biomass energy. The project utilizes waste resources and achieves sustainable development of the agriculture industry.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of manure. It is estimated to deliver totally   640,129  tCO2e emission reduction during the 7 years’ crediting period, at an average amount of  4,480,903  tCO2e per year.

The project activity is implemented on the degraded farmlands or lands used for rainfed subsistence agriculture. 
Various environment friendly technology-based agroforestry practices and Natural Climate Solutions (NCS) will be adopted to help climate change adaptation and mitigation as part of sustainable land management.

This project will optimise the land use and generate Emission Reductions (ERs). The amount of carbon sequestered through the project activity will be measured and  quantified with reference to a baseline to determine the Emission Reductions (ERs) generated. The ERs will be calculated through quantifying  Above Ground Biomass, Below Ground Biomass and Soil Organic Carbon. In the absence of the project, the lands would have remained degraded and the resource poor farmers would have continued to practice subsistence agriculture. 

The participation of small and marginal farmers as part of the VCS project makes this initiative unique in contributing to their land use choice, improvement of livelihood opportunities and in promoting their capacity to organize and implement climate change mitigation initiatives.

The project implements reforestation on 13,500 ha of degraded private lands in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Orissa. The reforestation activities under the project were initiated after 1 April 2020. 

The project is estimated to generate 94,200 credits / year on average over a period of 20 years.
vcs-4053: The “D.LIGHT’S IMPROVED COOKING PROJECT IN AFRICA” is a Grouped project that aims dissemination of energy-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to replace existing traditional Cookstoves in domestic households and communities throughout Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, and Uganda. Rice is the country's most significant agricultural product; it is grown on 43.86 million hectares in India and contributes to more than 20% of world rice output (158.2 Tg in 2013).
Rice is farmed in practically every state in India, and its production is directly related to the country's food security. Additionally, it is a significant source of income and employment. Rice production, on the other hand, is a substantial source of critical and long-lasting GHGs such as CH 4 and N 2 O, posing a huge threat to sustainable agriculture. Rice fields provide approximately 30% and 11% of total agricultural CH 4 and N 2 O emissions, respectively. According to early US-EPA study, paddy in India produced around 37.8 Tg CH 4 per year. GHG emissions from rice fields may be minimized by changing irrigation patterns, managing organic additions, and utilizing the appropriate rate and amount of nitrogen fertilizer. Irrigation practices such as alternate wetting and drying (AWD) have been shown to lower GHG emissions when compared to typical flooding methods. The time intervals between dry and wet circumstances aid in the shift from aerobic to anaerobic soil conditions,
resulting in a considerable reduction in methane output. As a result, the project adopts the AWD approach to minimize CH 4 emissions. This will also result in a reduction in water use, lowering the farmer's input costs. Prior to the execution of the project activity, the farmers used the traditional flooding approach, which resulted in methane emissions into the atmosphere. The project proponent along with local implementation partner held training sessions and meetings with farmers to educate them on the benefits of using AWD, which was followed by the distribution and installation of AWD pipe in the fields of registered farmers. Location: The first instance of the project is located in Madhya Pradesh (Hoshangabad, Raisen, Sehore and Bhopal districts). The annual average emissions is 53,369 tCO 2 eq.
vcs-4064: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in West of Wanzhou District in Chongqing City (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that changes the water regime during the rice cultivation period from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded on rice paddy fields located in the West of Wanzhou District in Chongqing City, China. Heilongjiang Nehe Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities (conventional tillage with synthetic fertilizer) to no tillage or straw returning with organic fertilizer application in fields located in Nehe city in Heilongjiang province, China. The project involves 60,360 ha corn field and 82,341 ha soybean field.
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by no tillage and applying organic fertilizer, since no-tillage can reduce soil disturbance and reduce the loss of soil organic carbon (SOC) compared to conventional tillage. And applying organic fertilizer can reduce nitrous oxide emission compared to synthetic fertilizer. Moreover, the project is expected to increase SOC by straw returning, since straw contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, returning straw to the field can effectively increase soil organic matter (SOM). Straw returning to the field also can improve soil physical and chemical properties, enhance soil aggregate structure, and increase soil permeability.

This project will support the transition of 11,000 ha towards Regenerative Agriculture in Brittany, France with C.100 farmers. The farming model thrilling soil health is called conservation
agriculture and has locally bee n proof tested for 20 years by an innovative group of pioneer farmers and Livelihoods Venture is willing to scale up to local farmers, including young settlers,
with the support of local public authorities. The farming model is called conservation agriculture because it conserves and restores soil organic matter by protecting the soil micro and macro organism habitats. It builds on three main practices: permanent soil cover, diversified rotations and low soil disturbance Therefore, this project is expecting to generate GHG emission reductions and removals mostly through soil organic carbon storage. Conventional agriculture in Brittany is the most common scenario existing on local farms, prior to the implementation of the project. Be tween two main cash crops cycles, land is not producing and soil remains uncovered for weeks, increasing risks of run off and topsoil erosion. Those risks are amplified by the common use of tillage, as the main “soil preparation” practice. By implementing this project, we estimate a total GHC emission reductions and removals of C.370, 000 t CO2e over a 20 year period To estimate the carbon potential of the project, we
designed a set of assumptions embedding agronomic specifications, recruitment pace, and the success rate of farmers’ practices adoption. To assess the carbon inputs, we have set a range of
10 typical baseline rotations and 10 regenerative agriculture rotations that we have combined with 3 soil types, till age, low tillage and no tillage options. Carbon pools generating credits is the
increase of carbon soil stocks (91%), the reduction of fuel consumptions (5%), the decrease of nitrogen fertilizer upstream (3%) and nitrogen field impact (1%).

vcs-41: The Chao Khun Agro Biogas Energy Project developed by Thai Biogas  Energy Company Ltd  is an anaerobic digestion project, which treats wastewater from the cassava processing factory owned by Chao Khun Agro Products   in Saraburi, Thailand.     The Covered In-Ground Anaerobic Reactor (CIGAR) will remove the organic material in the  wastewater, thus reducing the Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) and subsequent fugitive CH4  emissions. Biogas produced in the CIGAR will be used in the Chao Khun Agro Products factory to dry the wet starch cake to the final dry starch product, thereby displacing the fuel oil currently  employed to dry the starch product.  Surplus biogas, where produced, will be flared rather than  released to the atmosphere.
vcs-410: The project activity under consideration entails generation of clean power by harnessing wind energy and export of the electricity generated to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board and Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) on the basis of Power Purchase Agreements.The project activity is a bundled wind energy project with total capacity of 6.85 MW, comprising of six Wind Turbine Generators (WTG‟s) of varying capacities, commissioned in the period between 09/01/2008 and 29/09/2008.The electricity exported from the project to the grid thereby replaces an equivalent amount of power generation at the grid connected power plants which are primarily fossil fuel based. vcs-4102: Damao Banner Sustainable Grassland Management Project is located in Darhan Muminggan Joint Banner, Baotou City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. vcs-4103:
The lack of a safe drinking water supply is one of the primary issues in Indonesia. The size of the population paired with an increase in clean water demand poses an enormous challenge to water provision. The poor quality of the existing water sources leaves the citizen with no choice but to rely on alternatives such as bottled and boiled water. The high reliance on non-renewable biomass and fossil fuels for typical household water boiling could contribute air pollution, deforestation, increase public health risks, and many more.

The grouped project will install low greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting water treatment facilities to provide clean drinking water to communities that previously had no access to a public distribution network supplying safe drinking water (SDW) within the host country, the Republic of Indonesia. The Project serves as an open platform for various water treatment technologies, which are eligible under the methodology AMS-III.AV (Version 08.0). 

Through the installation of water treatment facilities, the project reduces the use and demand for fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass that would have been used to boil water to purify water in the absence of the grouped project. Primarily, the operation of a water treatment facility reduces greenhouse gas emissions of around 21,475 t/CO2et per year along with various other environmental, social, and economic benefits. This project is thus designed for the long-term improvement of the living conditions of people in the Republic of Indonesia.
vcs-4105:
Paddy fields are the most dominant anthropogenic sources of methane to the atmosphere (5-20% of the total emission from all anthropogenic sources ). Anaerobic decomposition of organic material in flooded rice fields produces methane, which escapes to the atmosphere primarily by transport through the rice plants. The annual amount of CH4 emitted from a given area of rice is a function of the number and duration of crops grown, water regimes before and during the cultivation period, and organic and inorganic soil amendments. Soil type, temperature, and rice cultivar also affect CH4 emissions. This CH4 emission-intensive cultivation method will be targeted by the proposed programme, that will involve the implementation of the technology/measures that result in reduced anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in rice cropping soils and thus reduced generation of methane.
The project activity comprises of grouped projects of rice fields implementing the following methods:
 (a) Rice farms that change the water regime during the cultivation period from continuously to intermittent flooded conditions and/or a shortened period of flooded conditions;
(b) Alternate wetting and drying method (AWD)
(c) Rice farms that change their rice cultivation practice from transplanted to direct-seeded rice (DSR).
Thus, the measure will consist of AWD and/or DSR in combination with adjusted water management system in rice cultivation.
The Project Activity Instances will be implemented in Kamareddy district in the state of Telangana.  Each instance will be of 5000 Hectares will be implemented in Kamareddy, Telangana State.

Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in South of Enyang District in Bazhong City (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation in conduction in south of Enyang District in Bazhong City with a total average of 11,282 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.
Within the project boundary, every farmer’s household owning the paddy fields is regard as an isolate unit. With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, controlled irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic condition (in the flooded state). 
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 506,190 tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 50,619 tCO2e.
The project aims to Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes、Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers and Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

vcs-4117: The REDD Carbonflor is a multi-activity grouped project, located in Brazil, in the Amazon and Cerrado biomes. The project is classified in scope 14 - AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses) and falls into the category Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) in the scopes of planned (APD) and unplanned (AUDD) deforestation. vcs-4118:
Regenerative farming practices have been proposed as a means to reduce the climate impact and carbon footprint of agriculture by, inter alia, enhancing the ability of agricultural soils to store carbon, buffering food production systems from environmental changes, improving water and nutrient use efficiency, and removing CO2 from the atmosphere. 
For this project, which encompasses regenarative orchards in Australia, GHG reductions and removals will be achieved by the implementation of a combination of the following practice changes: 
•	Reduce the intensity of agricultural practices, specifically reducing the use of synthetic fertilisers by incorporating organic amendments, and reducing the use of chemical pesticides via improved integrated pest management 
•	Cover cropping, including promoting inter-row biomass generation and the establishment of multi-species cover crops
•	Establishment of new permanent tree crops and associated canopy growth
•	Promote specific regeneration of soil and the increase of soil organic carbon (SOC)
•	Reduce water consumption and energy use through improved irrigation management 
•	Promote carbon sequestration in the above ground biomass
•	Improved crop residue management by re-incorporating prunings and crop waste into the soil
The undertaking of this project will support a number of United Nations Sustainable Development Goals in the project area, local communities, surrounding environments, and in the supply chain. The project will contribute towards SDG 2: Zero Hunger, SDG 3: Good Health and Wellbeing, SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, SDG 13: Climate Action, SDG 14: Life Below Water, and SDG 15: Life on Land.
vcs-412: The project under consideration is set up to produce clean power from the wind electric converters.
