7,045.27 ha of forest is about to be planted by direct planting on the degraded mountain and degraded land in Ulan County, and the planted species are all native species including Tamarix chinensis (Chinese tamarisk), Populus (aspen), Caragana korshinskii and Artemisia desertorum. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forest, and bring income and job opportunities for local communities and residents.
vcs-4122:
Siziwang Banner Improved Grassland Management Project aims to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through grass-planting and grazing management in the project zone. This project locates in Siziwang Banner , Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. It covers the entire grassland area of Siziwang Banner, including 13 minor administrative districts under the jurisdiction of the banner. By introducing sustainable grazing measures and managing the plants properly, this project is expected to increase local carbon sequestration and contribute to the development of the local ecosystem. 
Specifically, this project anticipates scientific management of 1966396.34 ha of degraded grassland in total to mitigate and reverse the degradation. Three main restoration measures are adopted, including rotational grazing, rest grazing and grassland reseeding.
This project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 54,091,628tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 1,352,291 tCO2e.
The objectives of this project include bringing benefits to three main aspects, climate, community, and biodiversity.
vcs-4123: The 1MT Nation Uganda Bamboo Planting project -the Project is an AFOLU project, located in Uganda. The project is located on depredated land - grassland, not used for many decades and/or land that has been heavily farmed for many decades, following the clearing of the native ecosystem many decades ago. An afforestation project has been designed to plant and maintain selected species of giant clumping bamboo. The Project is a grouped project, located in Uganda. Using native bamboo species, the Project aims to restore 10,000 hectares of degraded lands that were cleared of their native ecosystem more than 10 years ago.
vcs-4124:
BUYUKSISMANLAR BIOGAS ENERGY PLANT is a biogas-to- energy project that involves methane capture through anaerobic digestion and utilization of methane for thermal energy and electricity generation via cogeneration units. The chicken manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighbouring chicken farm with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. The thermal energy is used mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but also used for auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function.

The project is being implemented by BÜYÜK ŞİŞMANLAR YUMURTA VE GIDA MADDELERİ TİCARET LİMİTED ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, in Kalecik district, Ankara province, in Turkey.

The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 42,289 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 296,026 tCO2eq emissions reduction during the first crediting period.
vcs-4125:
As Koç Kırşehir Biogas Power Plant is a biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Thermal energy is used mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but also used for auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function.

The project is being implemented by AKYURT ELEKTRİK SANAYİ VE TİCARET ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, Kırşehir province, in Turkey.

The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 256,351 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,794,457 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.
vcs-4126: Community Restoration of Native Ecosystems in Ghana is a landscape-scale reforestation project designed by Three Trees and Climate Investment Partners that aims to increase tree cover in various regions of rural Ghana by planting native species on degraded communal lands or forest reserves. This reforestation will contribute to wildlife habitat or corridors, improve water infiltration, control erosion, and sequester carbon, among other ecosystem services. This grouped project is targeting a scale of up to 50,000 hectares.
vcs-4127:
The project activity involves distribution of improved cook stoves (ICS) to households in Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) by C Quest Capital Stoves Asia Limited (CQC). 

The distribution of improved cook stoves would displace the use of non-renewable biomass to meet similar thermal energy needs for cooking in households. Presently, the households use traditional cookstoves with very low efficiency, which leads to consumption of copious amount of firewood for preparing meals. 

The project activity was pursued as a component of the PoA “Household energy appliance programme” (ref. 10030) under CPA title “10030 P1 0003 CP1 Household Appliance Distribution in Lao PDR CPA003” 1 with Differ Cookstoves AS as the CME and is now being transitioned to VCS. First stove under this project activity was installed on 11 January 2018, and the project has accrued issuances under CDM until 31 December 2020.

Ecoeye Co., Ltd. (Ecoeye) will be responsible for financing the cost of production, distribution and maintenance of the stoves distributed under this project.

The project will facilitate the adoption of energy efficient ICS. This, in turn, will curb deforestation and forest degradation in Lao PDR by encouraging people to use energy efficient stoves and improve the quality of life of communities in Lao PDR by reducing drudgery, time and money spent in fuel wood collection and purchase, while also decreasing indoor air pollution. Worldwide, the effort will also lead to the reduction in GHG emissions into the atmosphere.
vcs-4128: The proposed VCS project activity titled “EcoParque Maceió landfill gas project” encompasses the promotion at the Ecoparque Maceió landfill site of destruction and/or utilization and/or supply to consumer(s) of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare(s), utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 7.13 MW) and supply of upgraded  LFG to consumer(s) with a LFG processing and supply infrastructure of combined installed capacity of 2,500 Nm³/h.
vcs-4129:
PROJECT SATHYA is an Improved Cookstoves and Livelihood project (hereafter referred to as “the Project” or “Project Sathya”) that aims for the sustainable development of the poor and marginalised communities residing in the core, buffer and fringe areas of the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, a protected area in Erode District, Tamil Nadu State, India (hereinafter referred to as “STR”).  Key activities of Project Sathya include:
1)	Installation and maintenance of 7500 Sarala brand improved cookstoves (“ICS”), which are fuel-efficient in-situ cookstoves with a chimney, that are constructed inside homes. This reduces fuelwood usage, air pollution, deforestation, human-animal conflict, health risks, poverty, and gender inequality.  
2)	Creating awareness about the advantages of clean cooking practices and ongoing maintenance of devices to ensure continued health and economic benefits.
3)	Training of people from the community, primarily women, as cookstove makers to provide skilling, additional livelihood, supports higher adoption of devices and improves ongoing maintenance and usage.
4)	Training of community members in digital literacy, surveys, monitoring, project management, collaboration, and related skills to improve livelihood opportunities and reduce inequalities.
5)	Opening of bank accounts for members in the community to support financial inclusion and increase financial independence for women.
6)	Sourcing raw materials for cookstove making and installation from local micro, small and medium-sized enterprises to support economic development and employment opportunities in the region.
7)	Upgrading school infrastructure by supplying water filters, utensils, etc to support continued education and better health.
8)	Solar lighting in the villages to improve safety, reduce human-animal conflict and improve access to clean lighting.
This Project supports SDGs 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15, and 17.
vcs-413: The objective of Hebei Yuxian Kongzhongcaoyuan 49.5MW Wind Farm Project is to generate renewable electricity using wind power resources and to sell the generated output through Hebei Southern Power Grid to the North China Power Grid. The project activity will generate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions by avoiding CO2 emissions from electricity generation by fossil fuel power plants that supply the North China Power Grid.
vcs-4130:
The project, Giresun Solid Waste Management Facility and Electricity Generation Facility (4.353 MWm / 4.242 MWe) is in Giresun Province, Görele District, Çavuşlu neighbourhood, and owned and operated by Biotrend.
Giresun LFG plant has been granted the generation license from EMRA on 24/12/2020. As per the generation license, the annual expected generation is 31,815,000 kWh/year. The first unit was commissioned on 02/04/2021. Accordingly, project activity start date is 02/04/2021.
This project adopts the renewal crediting period of 7 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 52,207 (tCO2e).
vcs-4131:
Future Carbon Methane Capture Grouped Project is a grouped project. A centralized manure management plant operated by the International Center for Renewable Energy – CIBIOGAS serves as the first project instance. Such plant was designed to generate renewable electricity from the captured biogas and avoid environmental impacts due to inadequate treatment of swine manure. The plant is located in the municipality of Toledo, State of Paraná, in the South Region of Brazil and will replace animal waste management systems (anaerobic lagoons) from fourteen swine confinement farms located in the same city.

The project was developed to reduce methane emissions and adequately treat the waste produced by small and medium-sized swine and cattle farms in feedlots. The project activity involved the installation of a centralized waste treatment plant (Biodigesters or bioenergy plants), with the capture of biogas that will be used to generate energy in biogas generator systems. This will replace anaerobic lagoons, which are considered the baseline scenario for livestock farms.

Based on its first instance, this project is expected to reduce 93,085 tCO2e for its first crediting period, ranging from 01-March-2023 to 28-February-2030. Incremental emission reductions might be achieved with the inclusion of new project instances.
vcs-4136:
Wetlands along the Yangtze River and Dongting Lake Restoration Project in Junshan (hereafter as “this project”) is an initiative to promote climate change mitigation and adaptation, maintain biodiversity, and create improved livelihoods, well-being, and employment for wetland-dependent communities in the Project Zone. The Project Zone is an area of 13093.19 ha located in the northeast of Junshan District, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China. By sowing grass, cutting down invasive poplars, planting native vegetation, and digging ditches, this project is expected to increase local carbon sequestration and contribute to the development of the local wetland ecosystem.
This project anticipates mitigating or reversing the degraded wetlands and rewetting the drained wetlands in the 1,297.76 ha of wetlands in the project area. The invasive species Populus Canadensis, which may damage the wetlands, is also expected to be eliminated during the project’s lifetime.
This project anticipates the sequestration of an estimated 498,492tCO2e over its lifetime of 50 years at an estimated average of 9,774tCO2e annually.
The objectives of this project include bringing benefits to three main aspects including climate, community, and biodiversity. It will meet the Gold Level criteria for both climate change adaptation and biodiversity as demonstrated in the PD Report.
vcs-4137:
The “Productive Second Floor with Macaúba” is a VCS AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use) grouped project, Scope 14, and, specifically, it falls under the ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation) category. 
The project works with local farmers to implement integrated systems in previously degraded pastures and/or croplands. The main project activity consists of the planting of Macaúba trees. This will be done considering two possible arrangements: (i) Macaúba intercropped with pasture (silvipastoral) or (ii) macuaba intercropped with agriculture (agrisilvicultural).
Through the planting of Macaúba trees the project will contribute to an increase in carbon stocks and associated GHG removals. The project activity will also improve the livelihood of local farmers and provide other ecosystem services, such as: maintaining the local microclimate, preventing erosion, conserving soil and moisture.
vcs-4138:
The Brusque landfill is a well-managed landfill site located in the municipality of Brusque in Santa Catarina State (Southeastern region of Brazil). The landfill started its operations in year 2009. This landfill site was designed and has been operated by the host-country project proponent and project owner and project proponent Recicle Catarinense de Resíduos LTDA.
The proposed VCS project activity titled “Brusque Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare and utilization as gaseous fuel in a set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 4.56 MW).  
As per its design configuration, combustion of collected LFG occurs in the following methane destruction device(s): 
-	1 high temperature enclosed flare;
-	3 engine-generator sets  of an electricity generation infrastructure (in which collected LFG will be utilized as gaseous fuel for electricity generation), that will be installed in 2024.
-	Possibility of future increase of the number of engine-generator sets, maintaining a total combined nameplate capacity up to 10 MW.
vcs-4139: The project serves the purpose of producing clean electrical energy in a sustainable manner. The project activity involves implementation of 2 turbines of 9.51 MW Mai Beni Hydropower Project (MBHP) and 6.2 MW Lower Jogmai Khola Hydropower Project (LJKHP) which utilize potential energy available for power generation. Therefore, no fossil fuels are involved for power generation in the project activity. The proposed project activity will also reduce the anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere by avoiding business as usual operation of existing fossil fuels-based power plants to produce equivalent amount of electricity
vcs-414: The objective of Hebei Haixing 49.5MW Wind Farm Project is to generate renewable electricity using wind power resources and to sell the generated output to the Hebei Southern Power Grid. The project activity will generate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions by avoiding CO2 emissions from electricity generation by fossil fuel power plants that supply the Hebei  Southern Power Grid, which is an integral part of the North China Power Grid.
vcs-4141:
The Itamarati Grouped REDD Project is initially formed by 4 properties  located in the municipalities of Nova Olímpia, Denise, Barra dos Bugres, Salto do Céu and Reserva do Cabaçal in the State of Mato Grosso, Brazil. Instance 1 is located in the Amazon and Cerrado biomes. The total area of the properties is 69,207.15 ha. The project aims to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) within the 22,753.36 ha project area, consisting of 64% Amazon rainforest and 36% Cerrado. The present REDD project is expected to avoid predicted 4,861 ha of deforestation, equating to 1,264,521 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 42,151 tCO2e.

In addition to the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, aiming at the propagation of environmental awareness, generation of alternative sources of income and environmental education actions.
vcs-4142:
The Serenity Valley REDD Project is located in three different municipalities in a private propert in the State of Pará, Brazil: Cumuaru do Norte, Santana do Araguaia and Santa Maria das Barreiras consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest. The project aims to avoid the unplanned deforestation(AUD) within the 52,644.73 ha project area. The present REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 19,220 ha of deforestation, equating to 6,251,508 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 208,384 tCO2e.

In addition to the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, aiming at the propagation of environmental awareness, generation of alternative sources of income and environmental education actions.
vcs-4143:
The project area is located within 6 private properties, located in the municipality of Vila Rica, inthe State of Mato Grosso, Brazil , inserted in an area of transition from Cerrado to Amazon biome. The project aims to avoid unplanned deforestation (AUD) in a project area of 13,351 ha. The AUD REDD project is expected to avoid predicted deforestation of 6,214.13 ha of deforestation, equating to 2,309,793 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (01-February-2021 to 31-January-2051), with an annual average of 76,993 tCO2e.

Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities.
vcs-4144: The present project promotes the distribution and utilization of locally made Chitetezo Mbaula (CM) stoves in Malawi. The CM stove is significantly more efficient than the traditional three stone open fire and therefore contributes to reducing wood consumption, preserving local forests and reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from unsustainably sourced wood. The CM stove also has further health and social benefits such as reduction of smoke produced during cooking or reduction of time required to collect wood.
vcs-4145:
Chanzi are a protein rich, animal feed producing company, located in Tanzania, and with expansions in place for Kenya as well. Their high protein animal feed is produced through the farming of Black Soldier Flies, and the use of their larvae either in whole form, or dried crushed form. 

The Black Solider Fly (BSF) is a particular species of fly that is commercially farmed around the world, for its ability to be converted into an insect-based animal feed. Its name comes from the color of the adult flies, which are black with metallic reflections. The commercialization of farming BSF’s came from the large demand for animal feed around the world and the concerns that fish meal and/soy-based meal (animal feed) would in the long term not be a sustainable solution.

The larvae are fed organic food waste, which come from a variety of sources, i.e. pre-consumer and post-consumer at industrial and household levels. This organic waste would have otherwise been sent to landfill, thus ensuring recovery for beneficiation of this waste. This diverting of organic waste from a landfill leads to the avoidance of carbon emissions and can therefore potentially be registered as a process which generates carbon credits.
vcs-4148: Agroforestry practices as an alternate to fulfil the rising demand for timber and other non-timber forest produce is promising in long term as it provides both wood and food. Agroforestry can help to conserve and rehabilitate the ecosystem along with providing better livelihood opportunities to the rural community. The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India.
vcs-4149:
The High Impact Soil Carbon Program of Lithuania is a joint initiative between UAB Heavy Finance (HF) farmers within the Lithuanian Republic borders. The program utilizes private capital to implement, and adopt improved agricultural land management for a long-term period, thus changing the mindset and establishing climate change mitigation and biodiversity-friendly practices.  						
It is a first-of-its-kind program in Lithuania and the Baltics. It aims to assist farmers in overcoming barriers that prevent adopting sustainable land management practices by providing scientific knowledge, training, and technical and financial support to adopt mitigating climate activities successfully. The program is designed to expand over time and cover a range of conservational farming practices in Lithuania to help drive the change from the current conventional agriculture toward resilient and sustainable agrifood systems.
vcs-415: The project activity involves recovery of fugitive methane emissions using a UASB system and utilizing the biogas thus produces as a fuel, thereby replacing the fossil fuel earlier used by the project participants. The project has a thermal generation capacity less than 45 MWth and will generate emission reductions less than 60 ktCO2e per year.
vcs-4150: ‘DelAgua clean cooking grouped project in Rwanda’ is a voluntary Grouped Project (GP) aimed at distributing fuel efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to households in Rwanda. Under the GP, DelAgua will distribute the project technologies to individual households and communities within the host country Rwanda. The GP will follow the VCS Methodology from Sectoral Scope 3 - VMR0006 “Methodology for Installation of High Efficiency Firewood Cookstoves”, version 1.1 for ER calculations. The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity would be usage of 3-stone fire and traditional stoves, which have a very low thermal efficiency, and therefore consume a higher amount of firewood as fuel for cooking. With DelAgua stove, people will be able to save time consumed for cooking, collecting fuel, and save the fuel itself. The primary benefit of the project cookstoves will be that the health risks 1from the smoke coming out of baseline stove will be reduced to a significant extent.
vcs-4151: The goal of the proposed project is to distribute improved cookstoves (“ICS”) in the households/small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) in Sub Saharan Africa, with the initial host countries being Rwanda, Malawi, Nigeria, Mali, Madagascar, Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia and Uganda (with a possibility of expansion to other countries e.g., Mozambique, Cameroon, Somalia/Somaliland, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Kenya, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Togo, Burundi, Ghana, Benin, Burkina, Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Zimbabwe and Namibia in Sub Saharan Africa in future).
vcs-4153:
This project is designed to support the livelihoods of at least 3,250 smallholder coffee producers from which at least 1,000 are women, in the State of Oaxaca, Mexico , by increasing the resilience of their coffee production systems after the impact caused by coffee rust. These producers are affi liated to the 45 cooperatives of CEPCO, The project will help CEPCO pursue and accelerate its efforts to restore coffee landscapes by focusing in areas with best potential for high adoption and technical success, around 4 main planting systems: New shade grown coffee systems set up on good potential plots (2,062 ha). Increased shade in existing coffee plots (3,300 ha). Productive forest set up (timber) in degraded land (1,031 ha). Diversification pilots on cocoa and maize/fruit trees intercropping (100 ha)
The 45 cooperatives members of CEPCO represent a total of 142 communities organized in 6 clusters: Cañada, Costa, Istmo. Mixteca, Papaloapam, Sierra Norte, Sierra Sur distributed in
several landscapes in Oaxaca state. Project beneficiaries will be farmers members of CEPCO and their families, who will join on a voluntary basis. It will consider a gender approach in which specific needs for women and youth will be identified and incorporated as much as possible in the activities and project tools. Plots will be selected in degraded and open lands, for new plantations of shaded coffee and timber plots. 3,300 hectares will be areas with already established in coffee plantations with some shade w h ere 50 trees per ha will be added to enrich the tree cover.
The Project activities are carried out according to the approved project methodology AR ACM0003 for the crediting period of 20 years. The project aims to remove ACM0003 for the crediting period of 20 years. The project aims to remove an estimated 54.675,24 tCO2e annually and 1,093.504,78 tCO2e during the crediting period.
vcs-4155:
The Malawi Bamboo Afforestation Project will distribute seedlings of giant bamboo, Dendrocalamus asper, to individual agricultural homesteads in rural Malawi. The project will also provide educational support and outreach for the long-term care of bamboo clumps. 

The project is located within the political boundary of the Republic of Malawi.

The project will generate GHG emission reductions by sequestering carbon in live above- and belowground biomass. When individual bamboo clumps reach the end of their lifespan, they will be replaced by a new clump, ensuring carbon remains sequestered over the project lifetime.

Smallholder agricultural homesteads are widespread across Malawi. A variety of trees are grown on farms, in gardens, and around homesteads to serve as fuel, timber, and other uses. However, fast-growing giant bamboo is not grown in Malawi at a large scale. 

Estimated annual average GHG emissions reductions: 174,301 tCO2e
Total GHG emission reductions: 5,054,739 tCO2e
vcs-4157:
The project activity includes the distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Tanzania. The ICS distributed through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves i.e., three-stone fire or conventional open fire.

An approximately 100,000 ICS through this project will be distributed and installed in the households of Tanzania. It is intended that under this project activity single or double pot TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. The ICS burns wood more efficiently due to its higher thermal efficiency, hence saving fuel. As a result, deforestation will be slowed in Tanzania and will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will spend less time gathering firewood.

The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance to the project proponent which in turn is used for recovering the price of ICS and project implementation costs.

Each ICS is the project activity instance that will substitute the current practice of using the three stone fire or a conventional device with no improved combustion air supply or flue gas ventilation, that is without a grate or a chimney. Fuelwood is burnt more efficiently with the ICS because its thermal efficiency is higher, resulting in a reduction in fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

The baseline scenario is the continued use of three stone fired or a conventional cook stove without a grate or a chimney by the target population burning non-renewable wood fuel to meet similar thermal energy needs in the absence of project activity.

The average annual GHG emission reduction from the project is expected to be 285,339 t CO2e. Total GHG emission reduction from the project is expected to be 2,853,391 tCO2e over the entire crediting period of 10 years.
vcs-4158:
The project is under development. The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Chad. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 

Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Chad. It is intended that under this project single pot, Total Land Care Rocket Stoves, henceforth referred as TLC-CQC Rocket StovesTLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. Each household will receive up to 2 ICS per household. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Chad but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

The ICS will substitute the currently common cooking on open fire. The ICS burns wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

The baseline scenario is the continued use of non-renewable wood fuel by the target population to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves in absence of project activity.

The average annual GHG emission reduction from the project is expected to be 2,075,549 t CO2e and total 20,755,493 tCO2e over the entire crediting period of 10 years.

vcs-4163: Otog Front Banner Sustainable Grassland Management Project is located in Otog Front Banner, Ordos City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restoration of severely degraded land by replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term. Totally, 100,297.9 ha of degraded grassland has been managed scientifically by including by fence building and reseeding of native grass species.
vcs-4164: The proposed grouped project activity is a step towards supporting the implementation and installation of solar rooftop and ground mounted projects in the premises of Lahore, Pakistan. The main goal of project activity is to implement renewable energy projects in the country and the significant importance of revenues from sale of Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) to achieve this goal forms the basis of the implementation of this project activity. The project activity is a voluntary action and each SPV will be the Project Proponent for their project activity.
vcs-4165: The Seringueira Project is implemented in the municipality of Ipixuna, Amazonas State, Brazil. It falls under the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU) sector within the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) category The project will conserve 2,773.79 hectares of native Amazon rainforests in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to pasture activities, designated to Planned Avoided Deforestation (APD). For the total area and by the end of the project, it is estimated a total avoided emissions of 1,100,000.00 tons of Greenhouse Gases (tCO2e). The project will be developed considering the CCB Standard, with benefits for Climate, Community and Biodiversity. As benefits to the climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adapting to the impacts caused by climate change, such as changes in the rainfall regime, as the area presents a dense hydrographic network that contributes to the provision and quality of water in the Amazon River basin. As benefits to the communities, the project will implement systems of underground water collection, installation of solar panels for electricity generation, provision of satellite internet service, construction of toilets with septic tanks, training of fire brigades, training of women in entrepreneurship, provision of assistance in the formation of community associations, and construction of a school. Project activity is carried out in Mexico City, operating under a Ride Hailing platform. Electric vehicle recharge is carried out in six charging HUBs located in “Lomas Verdes”, “Aleph”, “Miyana”, “Artz”, “Puerta Polanco” & “Monumento a la Madre”, exclusively for VEMO’s fleet vehicles, where charging infrastructure is located. Each operational shift is 9.5 hours long, and each vehicle is meant to cover two shifts each day. Therefore, the vehicles are also charged twice a day. In these chargers, is where emission reductions are effectively carried out, given that electricity is energizing the vehicles, rather than conventional petrol fuels, which are less efficient and produce more emissions per kilometer traveled.

Fleet operation is monitored in real time through telemetry devices installed in each vehicle, being capable of monitoring key operation parameters such as depth of discharge (DoD), state of charge (SoC), battery temperature, mean speed, odometer, charging power, etc. Information is available in a vehicle database that can be accessed from different devices to carry out data analysis on electric vehicle operation, allowing VEMO to use real time information to carry out electric vehicles emissions tracking. Also, the operational information of the vehicles is used to calculate the emissions a conventional vehicle would have produced, had it been used to carry out the operation (baseline emissions).

The advantage of this system lies in information liability, being generated automatically as vehicles operate. If the vehicles do not operate, emission reductions are not carried out and thus, no carbon credit can be emitted. Vehicle and energy accounting become more liable because the information is gotten directly from operation and no estimations are done regarding travelled distance.

Emission reductions are a result of the difference generated between real electric vehicles emissions, & the emissions that would have occurred if the vehicles were ICEVs.

The project uses livestock and poultry excrement resources generated by local farming as raw materials, and uses biomass residues, straw and other wastes generated in local agricultural activities as auxiliary materials for aerobic composting treatment. 
The annual feces treatment capacity is 80000 tons of swine manure, 18000 tons of cattle manure, 55000 tons of chicken manure, 12000 tons of sheep manure, 36000 tons of biomass waste residue, and produce approximately55000 tons of organic fertilizer every year. This REDD+ project, titled “Reducing Emissions from Deforestation Due to Slash-and-Burn Corn by Introducing Cacao Farming in Gorontalo Province, Indonesia” is located in Gorontalo Province on northern Sulawesi Island in Indonesia. The Project Area is 43,014 ha of forest area in Gorontalo Province, consisting of dry land primary forest and dry land secondary forest. prices practiced by corn intermediates. In the last two decades, deforestation in Gorontalo Province has been observed at a rate of 0.65% per year. The “slash-and-burn” farming of corn is known to be the main factor contributing to deforestation in Gorontalo Province. In short, the main driver of deforestation is the socio-economic condition in this area. Decreasing deforestation will be achieved through a series of activities that are designed to improve the livelihoods of local people. The principal project activity is introducing improved cacao production as an alternative source of income to the slash-and-burn farming of corn. The Project is community-based and consists of the implementation of activities in conjunction with local people. The implementation of the management structure and activities addressing deforestation drivers began on, as well partially after, 2020, together with associated investments. The Improved Forest Management (IFM) project activity is located in Lushi County, Sanmenxia City, Henan Province of China. The annual average temperature is 12-13.4 ℃ and the annual average precipitation is 692.9 mm.
The project activity includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forest in 17 compartments spreading over Zhuyangguan Town, Hengjian Town, Shahe Town, Guandaokou Town, Panhe Town by the conversion of logged to protected forest. All the compartments had the legal right to harvest issued by local forest bureau before the implementation of the project activity. Before 2020, they were all forests which the trees could be logged and sold once reached the cutting rotation age based on a timber harvest plan. After 2020, they are all converted to protected forests. The Hangzhou Chaoteng Energy Technology Co., Ltd is in charge of applying VCS project.
The project activity is to protect the previously harvested forests. Community residents can become our employees, and their job is to protect the forest. The local forestry bureau can supervise the implementation of the project and ensure that there is no commercial logging in our project. In addition, organizations in the community and all sectors of society can supervise our project and make complaints and suggestions through the risk control department. The purpose of strata is to improve accuracy and reduce the sampling cost. The strata are usually based on the tree species, age and canopy density, but it does not mean all these factors should be considered for all projects, more strata mean more workload and cost. For this project, the factor of species for strata could reduce the variation within the same stratum and reach the accuracy level of 90% under certain degree of freedom. So, the strata are reasonable and feasible. All the compartments are divided into 2 strata based on the tree species.The Improved Forest Management (IFM) project activity is located in Lushi County, Sanmenxia City, Henan Province of China.

COD Biogas Energy Manure Treatment Plant is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, via anaerobic digestion and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration unit. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighbouring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane rich biogas. Waste heat from gas engines is utilized for heating anaerobic fermenters. The electricity generated by the two installed biogas engines with the capacity of 1,501 KWe each is not only supplied to the national grid, but also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taken place at the project site are distributed to neighbouring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by COD ENERJİ ÜRETİM SANAYİ TİCARET ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, as the Project Owner, in Pınarbaşı district, Kayseri province, in Turkey. The start date of the project and of the first crediting period is determined as June 28, 2021. 
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project also reduces CO2 emission from fossil-fuel based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 189,969 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,329,783 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

The proponent of the project is Hainan University.
The project is located at Danzhou Bay and Xinying Mangrove National Wetland Park, a hotspot of mangrove biodiversity and conservation in China. After years of protection and management, Danzhou Bay and Xinying Mangrove National Wetland Park has retained the largest area of continuous mangrove forest in western Hainan, and, through many years of popularization of science, the local people's awareness of mangrove wetland protection has increased significantly, creating a good foundation for the project to be implemented. 
The objective of this project is to reconstruct the mangrove ecosystem from previously abandoned aquaculture ponds, enhance biodiversity, increase carbon sequestration of mangroves, and mitigate risks of marine disasters to the coastal communities. The restoration of the pond to its original state will expand the area of mangroves and the mangrove forest belt in Danzhou Bay, creating a complete mangrove shelterbelt. This will also establish a complete vegetation sequence along the coastline, including sea surface, tidal flat, mangrove, semi-mangrove, and terrestrial plants, thereby enhancing the structure and function of the mangrove ecosystem. This will improve the habitat of birds and marine organisms. The mangroves will play a crucial role in maintaining the coastal ecological function and biodiversity, as well as protecting the lives and property of the villagers residing around the bay.

vcs-4196: MicroEnergy Credits - Microfinance for Efficient Lighting Product Lines - India is aimed at reducing fossil-fuel based electricity consumption by distributing Light Emitting Diode (LED Inverter Bulbs) to local communities in India. vcs-4197:
Sanli Biogas Power Plant is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Waste heat from gas engine is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but is also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taken place at the project site are distributed to neighbouring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by ŞANLI BİYOGAZ ENERJİ VE SANAYİ ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, Şanlıurfa province, in Turkey. The start date of the project and the first crediting period is determined as June 30, 2021. 
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 311,544 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,180,808 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.
vcs-4198:

The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting duck manure.
The project comprises of solid-liquid separation system, composting system, and fertilizer packaging system. It is estimated that approximately 47,413.5 tonnes of duck manure can be treated annually, and the annual organic fertilizer production is 15,000 tonnes. Part of the organic fertilizer will be distributed to nearby farmers for free and most of it will be sold to local businesses. The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting duck manure.
vcs-42: Nong Bua Farm Ratchaburi Biogas Project (“the project”) involves the capture of methane (CH4) rich biogas produced during the treatment of swine barn flushing wash-waters and its combustion power generation at Nong Bua Farm in the Ratchaburi Province of Thailand.  With the swine rearing capacity of 65,000 fattening swine, Nong Bua Farm has recently invested in a high-rate continuous flow closed anaerobic treatment reactors to treat 100% of all barn flushing effluents produced from their swine rearing operations.  Nong Bua Farm has constructed these facilities to replace low-rate open anaerobic lagoon barn flushing effluent treatment systems.
vcs-420: The project activity is a Wind energy based power generation project of capacity 13.75 MW comprising of 11 Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) of 1.25MW each. vcs-4201: The Carbon Farming Program of Lithuania is a joint initiative between UAB Heavy Finance (HF) and farmers within the Lithuanian Republic borders. The Program aims to reward farmers for the positive results of fostering improved agricultural land management practices by sharing the revenue obtained from the sale of VCUs generated through the verified greenhouse gas emissions reductions and removals projects. Project activities are helping farmers to reach the balance in the triple bottom line - economic, environmental, and social. Improved agriculture land management refers to the techniques that focus on soil health and fertility by storing and increasing organic carbon, reducing anthropogenic gasses from excessive use of chemical fertilizers in the context of the offered program, accelerating changes to pre-existing agricultural management practices, and adopting regenerative methods.

Feicheng Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) installs a set of organic fertilizers production lines with an annual output of 50,000 tones to treat the manure from the dairy cow farms and biomass waste residue i.e., straw in Zhangling Village, Feicheng City, Shandong Province, China. The project is invested and owned by Taian Jinliyuan Fertilizer Technology Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass waste residue.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable, and reasonable option for livestock farm owners, and the biomass waste residue was left to decay anaerobically in a solid waste disposal site (SWDS).
This project was designed to treat the dairy cow manure and biomass waste residue (straw) to produce organic fertilizer. This project comprises a fermentation system and a fertilizer production system. An estimated 130,000 tons of manure and 5,000 tons of biomass waste residue can be treated annually, so a total of 135,000 tons of waste can be aerobically composted for this project. The final compost product obtained are sold to local businesses and farmers. The construction start date of the project is 01-June-2020 and was put into operation on 01-January-2022.
The project activity will reduce the amount of GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting manure and biomass residue. It is estimated that 59,122 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, with a total of 591,217 tCO2e over the 10-year crediting period.

vcs-4209:
The primary objective of the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project Activity is to avoid greenhouse gases emission by the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill through landfill gas capture, purification and injection in a distribution grid, while contributing to the environmental, social and economic sustainability by minimizing global climate changes and local air pollution.
The proposed Project Activity consists of capturing the landfill gas (LFG) generated by the landfill using an active LFG capture system and injecting it into a natural gas distribution network (after a purification process), displacing the use of natural gas. Any LFG excess will be flared.
Applying the state-of-the-art on LFG capture technology, a collecting system is installed to avoid the free emission of methane to the atmosphere. The LFG captured is sent to the upgrading facility before being injected to the natural gas distribution grid.
This type of project, i.e., upgrading of landfill gas to natural gas and injection into a natural gas distribution grid is not usual in Brazil.The Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project Activity has a substantial positive impact in terms of sustainable development as it is one of the first projects that purify the LFG and injects it to a network distribution grid being developed in Brazil that, as consequence, directly displaces natural gas.
An environmental benefit with the implementation of the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project is the destruction of methane that otherwise would be emitted to the atmosphere, increasing the impact on global warming.
The project invests on training engineers and operators to the qualification level required by these new activities. Oeste de Caucaia makes use of the experience of its own shareholders as well as its international consultants to train and qualify the human resources necessary for the implementation and operation of the magnitude of the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project.
vcs-421: Jiangsu Qidong Dongyuan Wind Power Project (hereafter referred as the proposed project) is located in Dongyuan Town, Qidong City, Jiangsu Province, East China. vcs-4216:
Wen County BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd landfill gas direct combustion utilization heating project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Wen County MSW landfill site, Baofeng Village North, Zhaobao Town, Wen County, Jiaozuo City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed, and operated by Wen County BCCY New Energy CO., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the project owner). The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Wen County MSW landfill site and utilize it to generate hot steam for the nearby factories.
Wen County MSW landfill site started collecting and handling waste in 2008 with a total design effective capacity of 590,000 m3 and a calculated operational lifespan of 25 years. The project has a total designed capacity 3.5t/h (1*3.5t/h) gas type boiler that combusts the LFG that contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate hot steam and export it to the nearby food industries. The project started to construct on 20/11/2020 and started to operate on 01/09/2021. The operation period of the project will end on 31/08/2031.
The LFG from Wen County MSW landfill site is greenhouse gas. In the absence of the project activity, the LFG would have released to the atmosphere, hence contribute to the global warming. Furthermore, the biogas utilized in the boiler replaces the fossil fuel that utilized in the food industries’ boilers. The gas boiler uses LFG will generate heat which will replace the Fuel-Gas type boiler and the biogas type boiler in the food industries. Therefore, the project activity significantly contributes to the reduction of GHG emission. 
Total heat supplied to the food industries by using the LFG in the crediting period will be 396,767t. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the diesel oil displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reductions of the project are 39,676tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and the removals are 39,676tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.

The project involves distribution of 60,000 domestic fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Zambia. The ICS distributed through this project will replace the prevailing inefficient three-stone fires, or traditional pot supports . The ICS combusts wood more efficiently and improves thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

This is the fifth CPA implemented under the CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) titled “Distribution of Improved Cook Stoves in Sub-Saharan Africa”. C-Quest Capital Malaysia Global Stoves Limited (CQC) is the Coordinating / Managing Entity (CME) for the PoA in which this CPA is to be included. Ecoeye Co., Ltd. (henceforth referred as Ecoeye) provide all implementation cost for all ICS under this CPA, so that affordable clean technology can be made available to the participating households. Ecoeye will also make available all operation and maintenance costs along with ICS production and distribution cost. Total LandCare (TLC) Zambia will implement this project, manage and coordinate activities of local partners, the promotion and installation of the ICS and also provide all necessary marketing and promotion assistance to partners. TLC is also responsible for monitoring activities of this project.

It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. In this grouped project, each ICS constitutes a single project activity instance which is in line with its definition stated in VCS Program Definitions version 4.2

The end user will be informed that carbon finance is being generated by the use of the ICS, and this finance is in turn used to facilitate the access to ICS (eg. subsidize the price of the ICS) and helps to cover project implementation costs.

vcs-4221: The Seringueira II project will be developed in the municipality of Ipixuna, Amazonas State, Brazil. It falls under the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU) sector within the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) category. The project will conserve 23,851.88 hectares of native Amazon rainforests in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to land use conversion activities from forests to pastures aimed at raising livestock. The project area (16,483.02 ha) will be allocated to Avoided Unplanned Deforestation (AUD), and it is estimated that at the end of the project the emission of 591,917.73 tons of Greenhouse Gases will have been avoided. The project will be developed considering the CCB Standard. As benefits to the communities, the project will implement systems of underground water collection, installation of solar panels for electricity generation, provision of satellite internet service, construction of toilets with septic tanks, training of women in entrepreneurship, provision of assistance in the formation of community associations, and construction of a school. These measures will enable water security and access to information to minimize the impacts caused by climate change in traditional, low-income extractive communities. As benefits to the climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adapting to the impacts caused by climate change as the area presents a dense hydrographic network that contributes to the provision and quality of water in the Amazon river basin. The maintenance of forest cover also ensures the conservation of biodiversity, the maintenance of ecosystem functioning and of ecosystem services provisioning performed by living organisms. It is noteworthy that the project includes a high priority area for biodiversity conservation with species classified in the categories Endangered (EN) and Critically Endangered (CR) according to the IUCN red list.
vcs-4222: The afforestation project is a vital initiative that combats climate change by promoting the plantation of bamboo with landowners and communities. vcs-4223: The “D. LIGHT’S IMPROVED COOKING PROJECT IN KENYA” is a large-scale project that aims dissemination of energy-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to replace existing traditional Cookstoves in domestic households and communities in Kenya. Traditional cooking methods prevalent across host country, contribute to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions due to inefficient combustion of unsustainably sourced, non-renewable biomass (NRB) fuel. Furthermore, the use of solid biomass fuels (e.g., wood) in inefficient traditional stoves and/or open fires releases large amounts of particulate matter (PM), creating hazardous levels of indoor air pollution (IAP). The ICSs disseminated under the project are designed to improve fuel combustion and heat transfer. The ICS results in the reduction of fuel consumption and improvement in levels of Indoor air pollution for project users (reducing smoke, black soot, and particulate matter (PM) emissions). The reduction in consumption of cooking fuel also reduces equivalent greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions attributed to the use of non-renewable biomass. In the absence of this project, the project activity beneficiaries would cook primarily using traditional inefficient stoves for meeting their thermal energy needs, perpetuating environmental and health degradation. The project activity intends to access carbon finance to mitigate one of the main barriers (price) for end users towards adopting clean cookstoves.
