The “Improved cropland management project in Anyang” is aimed to raise farmer's awareness on the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change the agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objectives of the project is to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage, in order to achieve these, a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried out, the specific activities are the following:
A. Reduce fertilizer (organic or inorganic) application;
B. Reduce tillage/improve residue management; and
C. Improve crop planting and harvesting.
vcs-4236:
The Anew Agri-Carbon Project Aggregation 1 enables the adoption of regenerative
agricultural practices on continental United States row crop land through financial incentives and
technical support. Participants in the Project are individual farmers and field managers who have
implemented one or more practice changes on their farm that will increase the deposition of soil
organic carbon, reduce nitrogen fertilizer losses in the form of N 2 O, or reduce on farm energy
consumption.
vcs-4237:
The project involves demand side energy efficiency measures in public lighting infrastructure through the replacement of existing luminaires with more efficient technology, including “Light Emitting Diodes” (hereinafter referred to as “LEDs”) lightings in urban area of the municipality of Feira de Santana, state of Bahia (Instance 1) and Aracaju, state of Sergipe (Instance 2) in Brazil.
The project covers activities such as installation, maintenance, expansion, replenishment, operation and management of all the public lighting infrastructure in the municipality of Feira de Santana and Aracaju (Brazil).
This grouped project (Instances 1 and 2) will install 118,636 luminaires The public lighting infrastructure based on inefficient sodium mercury luminaires was the scenario prior to the implementation of the project.
vcs-4238: Hefei Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Feidong County, Hefei City, Anhui Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Hefei Modern Energy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner). The project is to collect methane from manure treatment at Modern Farming Feidong Farm in Feidong County, Hefei City, Anhui Province. The project treats the raw manure from 18,000 dairy cows annually by anaerobic digester, and uses the biogas generated during the treatment process for power generation. The electricity generated by the project will be transmitted to East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project is expected to produce 42,400 m3 biogas per day. All the manure is collected and transferred to the anaerobic digester. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is sent out and used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmlands.
vcs-4239: Wuhe Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Wuhe County, Bengbu City, Anhui Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Modern Energy Wuhe Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner). The project is to collect methane from manure treatment at Modern Farming Wuhe Farm in Wuhe County, Bengbu City, Anhui Province. The project treats the raw manure from 18,000 dairy cows annually by anaerobic digester, and uses the biogas generated during the treatment process for power generation. The electricity generated by the project will be transmitted to East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project is expected to produce 80,500 m3 biogas per day. All the manure is collected and transferred to the anaerobic digester. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is sent out and used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmlands.
vcs-424: The project activity under consideration entails generation of clean power by harnessing wind energy – a non-conventional renewable energy resource and export of the electricity generated to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board, Hubli Electricity Supply Company Limited (HESCOM) and Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company Limited (GESCOM) on the basis of Power Purchase Agreements. The electricity exported from the project to the grid thereby replaces an equivalent amount of power generation at the grid connected power plants which are primarily fossil fuel based. Therefore the project activity results in an equivalent amount of CO2 emission reduction which otherwise would have resulted from fossil fuel combustion related to electricity generation at the grid.
vcs-4240:
Guinan Grassland Sustainable Management Project (hereafter“the project” ) is located in Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China. The project aims to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem through fence construction, degraded grassland improvement and pest control on the degraded grassland to increase carbon sink capacity, and contribute to local development by the adoption of rational grazing and sustainable management of grassland over a long time.
Totally,107,326.16 ha of degraded grassland has been managed sustainably by seeding grass, pest control and fence construction. The project implements fence construction mainly containing rotational grazing and rest grazing in the degraded grassland to achieve sustainable grassland management. Degraded grassland improvement  has been managed sustainably by the implementation of seeding, reseeding, applying fertilizer and Black soil beach management. And,the project also implemented pest control to restore degraded grassland and improve soil carbon storage.
vcs-4241:
GAZIANTEP BIOGAS POWER PLANT is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Waste heat from gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but is also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taking place at the project site are distributed to neighboring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by GAZİ BİYOGAZ ÜRETİMİ A.Ş., the Project Owner, Gaziantep province, in Turkey. The commissioning date of the project is June 30, 2021. However, there are some technical problems with digesters and there is neither electricity generation nor methane capture until April 22, 2022. The project's start date and the first crediting period are thus defined as April 22, 2022, the date on which the technical problems were resolved, and as a result, the project started capturing methane and began generating GHG emission reductions with electricity generated from animal manure. 
This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 185,910 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,301,372 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.
vcs-4242: Under this project activity, BTR will work with EV OEMs to help accelerate the adoption and optimal use and charging of EVs and, through the collection of accurate and precise data, measure the GHG impact of those EVs’ charging relative to an assumed baseline of comparable-model ICE vehicles. Using an existing proprietary technology platform (the BTR Bridge platform), BTR will aggregate EV telematics data from participating EV OEMs to measure miles driven and kilowatt-hours charged and thus GHGs reduced. BTR’s technology enables the precise and accurate measurement of the GHG impact because the EV’s telematics systems collect data on the location, time, and amount of charging, which BTR then uses to determine the carbon intensity of the relevant grid during each charging event compared to the baseline of a comparable-model ICE vehicle. BTR intends to relay this information back to the EV OEMs and the EVs and thereby inform drivers about the GHG intensity of their charging and encourage them to optimize charging by shifting it to times when the grid is cleanest. BTR will act as the project proponent for this grouped project and undertake all of the monitoring and data collection required under VM0038. The carbon offsets representing the emissions reductions are generated by the charging data collected by the EV OEMs from the EVs, and ownership of the offsets has been contractually transferred from the EV OEMs to the project proponent. During the course of the crediting period, BTR estimates that 2,508,916 tons of CO2 will be reduced or an annual average of 250,892 tCO2. In the absence of this project, fewer EVs would displace the sale and use of ICE vehicles, fewer EV drivers would be informed about the GHG intensity of their charging and, therefore, fewer EV drivers would optimize their charging for GHG reductions.
vcs-4243: The project activity is an afforestation project on multiple farms of extensive grazing lands. The overreaching goal is to promote innovative afforestation management activities on degraded lands. By combining native and exotic species to produce high-quality wood and other non-woody products and, in the long term, to generate new patches of managed native species forests. The grouped Project is located in Corrientes Province, in the Northeast region of Argentina (host country) and could include areas in the contiguous south of Misiones Province.  In this region, grazing and agriculture lands have different levels of degradation due to a long history of use without sustainable management. The activities proposed in the Project could stop the degradation processes and enhance the regional environmental conditions. For the design of the plantations, specific local conditions are considered to determine where species will be planted to promote facilitation strategies between them. Exotic species have favorable competition conditions over native ones (e.g., in standing flooded areas), but in return, they help native species with their development, protecting them from frosts, wind, and high radiation. Through forest plantation of native and exotic species, the Project sequesters CO2 by generating net anthropogenic removals by sinks that can be measured, monitored, and verified with known tools and approaches, contributing to the country's sustainable development.The initial activity instance comprises 2,331 hectares of degraded grassland generating an estimated average (long-term average) of ≈775.509 tCO2e net GHG emissions reductions and removals, implying a total GHG benefit for the environment of approximately ≈19.387. tCO2e per year for the length of the project (40 years).
vcs-4245:
EKI Energy Services Ltd. is in the process of implementing grouped project based on biogas from cattle manure at different locations across various States and Union Territories in
India. The primary objective of the project is to effectively demonstrate the use of anaerobic biogas digesters to generate biogas based renewable energy connected with off grid. Thus, project will achieve an environment friendly way of managing wastes and renewable power generation by utilizing the wastes
vcs-4246: The objective of the project is to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through the sustainable grassland management practices, such as increasing the rotation of grazing between summer and winter pastures, limiting the grazing days on degraded pastures, and replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term, thereby increasing carbon sequestration, and promoting local development. Totally, 326,819.9 ha of degraded grassland will be restore in Subei Mongilia Autonomous County, Jiuquan City, Gansu Province, China.
vcs-4247:
HISAR BIOGAS POWER PLANT is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Waste heat from gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but is also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taken place at the project site are distributed to neighbouring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by HİSAR BİOGAZ TARIM VE HAYVANCILIK A.Ş., the Project Owner, Eskişehir province, in Turkey. The project began to collect animal waste from
neighbouring animal farms and generate electricity on July 06, 2021. Thus, the start date of the project and the crediting period is determined as July 06, 2021.
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 210,728 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,475,096 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.
vcs-4248: Haishang Shaoyang Composting Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Sanxing Village, Jinchengshi Town, Shaoyang County, Shaoyang City, Hunan Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Shaoyang County Haishang Ecological Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner).
vcs-4249:
In order to provide an environmentally friendly and sustainable municipal solid waste management system, Ordu Landfill Gas to Electricity Project is being implemented by Ordu
Yenilenebilir Enerji Elektrik Üretim Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi The project is built within the premises of the Ordu Landfill Facility in the Çaybaşı district of Ordu province . The Solid Waste Landfill Site is located on a total area of 132,84 37 m 2 1 The project start date is 24 June 2021 , and w ithin the crediting period between 24 June 2021 and 23 June 202 8 landfill gas is extracted, and electrical energy is obtained. The project activity includes capturing and utilizing landfill gas (landfill gas contains approximately 50 % methane and is a potent greenhouse gas) for power generation, which would have been vented to the atmosphere in the pre project/business as usual scenario. It has been determined that an average of 300 350 tonnes/day of waste will be stored in the landfill . The waste composition that the project receives has 7 8.4 2 organic materials.
vcs-425: The project activity was implemented at Sahamitr Tapioca Chonburi factory in 2005. The production capacity of the plant is 100 tons of native starch per day which generates approximately 1000 m3 of wastewater for every production day. Before the implementation of proposed project, the wastewater from the starch plant was treated in 12 cascading open anaerobic lagoons, with a retention time of more than a year. The minimum depth of these ponds is more than 2 m. from water surface and the average atmospheric temperature in the region is 28 degree Celsius1 . This consequently leads to methane generation from the organic content (characterized by chemical oxygen demand or COD) of the wastewater.
vcs-4250:
The proposed project aims at reducing the fuel wood consumption in traditional cook stoves by disseminating improved cook stoves (ICS) at a highly reduced cost of 200 INR. The transition from traditional to improved cookstoves will help in achieving significant firewood consumption that will enable climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objective of the project is to improve the lives of the rural women by providing them with efficient cooking technology. This project will not only empower women, but also decrease fuelwood consumption at household level which will enable reduction of carbon emissions at a global scale. The project will ensure that just sources of renewable biomass are used that are in line with the requirements according to Glossary of CDM terms v 11.0.
The existing scenario prior to the implementation of the project activity involves the usage of traditional mud cookstoves with poor ventilation, causing excessive indoor air pollution (IAP) and has been a serious health risk for women and children who spend several hours in the kitchen. The State of Meghalaya has an abundance of forest reserves and the ethnic communities rely on firewood for cooking. The state has three hill regions of the united Khasi and Jaintia Hills and Garo Hills. Garo Hills comprises of five district and the communities rely on traditional cooking practices and sources firewood from nearby forests. Penetration of modern cooking mediums like LPG gas, electric induction etc. have remained out of bound for most households in the region. The project activity is aimed to implement 20,000 cookstoves in the Meghalaya state of India. The Project activity had started distribution of Improved Cookstoves from 19th October 2022. The estimated annual emission reductions for this crediting period are 8,05,612 tCO2e and 1,15,087 tCO2e/year.
vcs-4251:
In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, Vega Diyarbakir Waste to Energy Project is being implemented by Vega Diyarbakır Atık Yönetim ve Enerji Üretim Sanayi Ticaret ve Anonim Şirketi. The project activity is a methane gas power generating plant with a licensed capacity of 14.509 MWe. The project was commissioned with the generation of electricity from June 11th, 2021, which is regarded as the project start date. The project's lifetime is 15 years, according to the EMRA Generation License.  
For sustainable waste management where municipal waste is utilized, the rehabilitation of the Diyarbakır Solid Waste Disposal Site, which receives approximately 1,500 tons of municipal waste from different districts of Diyarbakir province on a daily basis, and the generation of renewable electricity from landfill gas was planned and the rehabilitation project was approved by the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization in Turkey.
The main goal and objective of the project in the near future is the rehabilitation of the Diyarbakir Solid Waste Disposal Site and the generation of renewable electricity from landfill gas, as well as the introduction of the organic fraction separated by the planned separation unit and digester units into the controlled anaerobic digestion process and methane recovery from organic waste. Methane recovered from the digestion and landfill site is combusted through gas engines and the resulting electricity is supplied to the grid. The project is located in Yukarıakdibek, Baglar district city of Diyarbakir, in Turkey.
The expected average annual emission reductions are 182,826 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,279,780  tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its first crediting period.
vcs-4252: The proposed group project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by distributing fuel efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to households in Kenya and Uganda. The goal of the project is to replace traditional cookstoves with the ICS, which are designed to burn wood more efficiently and save fuel by distributing approximately 200,000 ICS to households. The improved cook stoves will replace 3-stone fire, which is the predominant stove in the project area. By using the ICS, fuel consumption will be reduced, thereby reducing the time required for wood collection or reducing costs for firewood for households purchasing wood. The improved efficiency of the stove will also lead to reduced indoor air pollution, thereby improving the health situation especially of women and children.
vcs-4254: Tianjun County Sustainable Grassland Management Project is located in Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China. The project aims to restore degraded grasslands in Tianjun County, through degraded grassland improvement (including grass reseeding, fertilization, fence construction), sandy grassland management, rest grazing, rotational grazing and harmful weed control. As a result, 89,123 hectares degraded grassland has been managed sustainably.
vcs-4255: The Rewilding Maforki grouped project aims to recover low intensity and unproductive grasslands in Port Loko District, in the Northwest Province of Sierra Leone. Strategic activities to restore and conserve the areas will include tree nursery, tree planting , care and management of the tree plantation, prevention of pest and illegal activities within the project areas. The project will generate GHG removals by the plantation of indigenous species.
vcs-4256:
This project is a step towards supporting disposal and comprehensive utilization of animal waste in Hebei Province, one of the agriculture production bases in North China. This project has installed an environmentally friendly manure treatment solution: a system to produce bio-natural gas through plug-in dry fermentation treatment of manure collected from local livestock farms. Solid bio-organic fertilizer and liquid fertilizer are the by-products. The bio-natural gas is to be used in the transportation sector to displace traditional fossil CNG. 
Prior to the implementation of the project, manure is stored at individual livestock farms in uncovered anaerobic lagoons over a retention period of a couple of months before they were used for agriculture application as fertilizer, directly without any treatment. Significant amount of Greenhouse Gases (GHG), such as methane could be emitted directly into the atmosphere. 
From the perspective of bio-CNG produced by this project, without the project the fossil origin CNG would be continuously used by the transportation applications. 
The successful implementation of the project prevents GHG emissions, methane in particular, as well as generate a clean renewable energy that displaces fossil fuel CNG.
vcs-4259: The objective of the proposed VCS Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) project activity aims to transition the farmers into practicing more sustainable cultivation practices in sugarcane production. The SALM project is expected to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions or increase sequestration of carbon in soil and biomass.These sustainable practices will improve the soils of the farmers and enhance their resilience to climate change

vcs-4260:
Guizhou Zhongzhichang CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Zhongzhichang coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mine where the Project is located and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus. The Project is located in Hongguo Town, Panzhou City, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. Seven sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 6.4MW (2*0.7MW+5*1MW), destroying 12.1 million m3 of methane annually. At the first operation year, it is expected the installed capacity will be 3.4MW (2*0.7MW+2*1MW). After the full operation of the Project after the second operation year, the expected annual exported electricity will be 32,998 MWh, which will be supplied to the coal mine first through the electricity distribution network in Zhongzhichang coal mine area, and then to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG and displace part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
vcs-4261:
The Aksaray Solid Waste Management System and Electricity Generation Facility (hereafter named as “ the Aksaray LFG”) (1.414 MWe) is situated in the province of Aksaray, in the Merkez District, and is owned and operated by Biotrend. The facility is designed to process municipal waste from Aksaray province, classified as type-2 sanitary landfill, and serves a total of 8 districts. The facility consists of four key areas: a sanitary landfill, a mechanical separation facility, a compost facility, and an electricity generation facility. 
The Aksaray LFG plant has obtained a generation license from EMRA, with an expected annual generation of 42 420 .00 0 kWh/year. The project's first crediting period is set at 7 years, with expected average annual emission reductions of 29,019.74. Through this project, waste is stabilized, waste storage is minimized, electricity is produced, and negative environmental impacts are eliminated.
vcs-4262: Solid Waste to Energy Production Facility Sharjah UAE project (hereinafter referred as “the Project”) is invested and operated by SHARJAH ENVIRONMENT COMPANY LLC 1st Floor Lagoon Tower, Corniche Road, Sharjah UAE P.O. Box 20248 Sharjah. The purpose of the project is to dispose the municipal solid waste through incineration, and simultaneously utilizing the residual heat for power generation.
vcs-4263:
The primary objective of the Sepoti REDD Project is to avoid unplanned deforestation (AUD) of a region within the municipalities of Novo Aripuanã and Borba. The first Project activity instance has 26,062 ha project area, which is within one private properties in Novo Aripuanã, consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest.

It is expected that, with the carbon project, it will be possible to expand the monitoring of the area, hiring new professionals to work on the farms. In addition to the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, aiming at the propagation of environmental awareness, generation of alternative sources of income and environmental education actions.

The present REDD project is expected to avoid predicted 1,888 ha of deforestation, equating to 782,072 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 26,069 tCO2e.
vcs-4264: The Hainan Grassland Sustainable Management Project is located in Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China, with a total area of 184,352.04 hectares. The local grassland environment had already been deteriorating because of overgrazing and climate change before the project was put into action. By reseeding grass and using sustainable grassland management techniques including rest grazing, rotational grazing, hazardous plant control, and insect control, the project aims to restore the local damaged grassland ecosystem. The project enhances the grassland covering, boosts carbon sequestration, and contributes to local development. With an average yearly GHG emission removal of 534,995 tCO2e, the project is expected to produce GHG emission removals of 21,399,792 tCO2e in 40 years.
vcs-4265:
The REDD+ Café Apuí Agroforestry (CAA) project aims to expand the production chain of agroforestry coffee in southeastern Amazonas and avoid deforestation of native forests on rural properties in the municipalities of Apuí, Manicoré and Novo Aripuanã, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. In the absence of the project, forests on the participating properties would be cleared for agricultural activities, especially pastures, for income generation.

REDD+ CAA is a 30-year grouped project that will have periodic membership of new participants over the first ten years. The initial project's participants are 42 family farmers (Project Activity Instances – PAI) that totalize a PA of 3.696 hectares around the town of Apuí (50km) in Amazonas State/Brazil. The project has a defined geographical area within which instances of project activities are located, totalling 19,874 km2. This area is composed of native forests and agricultural areas, mainly planted pastures, in addition to some enclaves of non-forest pioneer formations.

The project is based on long-term (30-yr) agreements with landowners to avoid deforestation in their areas in exchange for performance-based payment for avoided deforestation. In addition to monitoring, reporting, verification, and leakage mitigation activities, VCU revenues will be invested in agroforestry implementation, technical assistance, organic certification processes, administration, and marketing of coffee and other agroforestry products. The project aims to expand agroforestry coffee production using agroecological techniques and trained personnel in organic production promoted since 2012 in the region.

The project intends to generate climate, community and biodiversity benefits under CCB standard. The payment for avoided deforestation, investment in the agroforestry coffee chain, and support for the structuring of new agroforestry product chains offer an alternative sustainable income to producers while maintaining conserved forests.
vcs-4266: Cattle ranching is one of the main pillars of Botswana’s largely agrarian society: livestock is the primary source of subsistence and income for two-thirds of rural households.  Furthermore, Botswana’s urban population is rapidly growing, increasing demand for food, land and fuel. This growth has taken place in tandem with threats to natural resources in the form of  rangeland degradation, loss of grazing habitat, and the over-exploitation of wildlife. The KALAHARI GRASSLANDS PROJECT (KGP) is a grouped project located in the heart of Botswana’s Kalahari, a semi-arid grassland and shrubland ecosystems. Since 2016, Botswana has lost over 800,000+ hectares of Wildlife Management Areas (GH10, GH11, SO2, and KW6) partly due to the ongoing cycle of land degradation and encroachment into nearby areas. The central piece of legislation regulating designated land use on protected wildlife areas is the Wildlife Conservation and National Parks Act of 1992, § 3(15)(2) and enables the President to rezone and/or modify WMAs. Currently, most ranchers across Botswana operate an average ranch of 5 hectares with a few head of cattle and lack an understanding of carrying capacity resulting in overgrazing. The lack of enforcement mechanisms to prevent encroachment past communal grazing lands into WMAs coupled with Big-Agriculture interests converting rangeland into commercial cattle operations has resulted in the degradation of over 91,000 km² or 15.5% of Botswana. The KGP program was launched to provide an alternative to land conversion for landowners and game ranchers located in high-risk areas adjacent to WMAs and other wildlife corridors. By leveraging the voluntary carbon market the KGP protects both the biodiversity and sequestration potential of these critical areas. The main agents of conversion, private landowners, forego their legal right to convert native grasslands, and in doing so avoid GHG emissions totaling over 2.23M mt/CO2e over 10 years.
vcs-4267: The AFOLU Carbon project focuses on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from cotton cultivation through a variety of measures and technologies The project will engage with medium, small and marginal farmers and promote managing the use of synthetic fertilizers, reduce the use of fossil fuels in cotton cultivation by promoting more efficient ways for irrigation and encourage the implementation of agroforestry practices.
vcs-4268: Family forests make up over one-third of America’s 765 million acres of forestland, according to a 2021 Congressional report. This fact puts management decisions providing clean water, recreation, and other valuable resources in the hands of everyday American families. The importance of American forests to the global ecosystem and climate is central to the work of Forest Carbon Works, PBC, a US based company that seeks to conserve and restore family-owned tracts of forestland throughout the United States. Forest Carbon Works is acutely aware of vulnerabilities particular to family forest owners. Without an alternative form of income, families face pressures to liquidate their timber to cover unforeseen expenses. By the year 2030, Forest Carbon Works anticipates protecting 500,000 acres of land owned by many individuals with durable agreements of permanent carbon storage. The project longevity shall be at minimum 60 years with possible extension to 100. Extending rotation ages on these at-risk forests increases carbon storage relative to the baseline case, as well as increases biodiversity and diversity in forest structure. Estimated average GHG emission reductions from the project are 845,991 tons CO2 equivalent per year, with total reductions over the first 25-year project crediting period of 21,149,786 tCO2e.  This is a grouped project. The geographic area of the entire project shall encompass is the contiguous United States and southern Alaska. To ensure sustainability in management, Forest Carbon Works requires enrolled forestland to be certified by the Forest Stewardship Council ® (FSC®) under the group certificate SCS-FM/COC-009247 prior to the commencement of any harvesting activities.
vcs-4269:
A large percentage of the total populations in India draw income from the agriculture. These populations reside in the rural area commonly addressed as farmers were performing the
conventional farming i.e., use of fertilizers, use of synthetic fertilizers, using machinery’s for tillage, and residue burning across the year which would result in emissions all the year round. In this proposed project the PP intends to promote activities organic and/or natural farming where farmers are encouraged to produce the manures in their farm land, control pest infestation using natural ingredients, practice low or no tillage, avoid or stop residue burning, enhance the soil organic carbon & sequestration, and establish market for premium price covering 6500.00 ha of cropland in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Goa and Karnataka in states of India. Several research in the past (Jarvan et all., 2017 and Chahal et all., 2020) shows that such practices are boon for the farmers as well for the environment.
vcs-427: The project activity involves recovery of fugitive biogas from the wastewater released from tapioca starch processing plant. The recovered biogas is used in a boiler to generate heat for the starch drying process and used to generate electricity in order to meet the power requirement of the starch processing plant and may later be supplied to  national-owned grid. After satisfying the above demands, surplus biogas is flared for safety purpose. The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by applying the conservation agriculture management. The conservation agriculture refers to a sustainable agricultural technology that can reduce farmland soil erosion, protect farmland ecological environment and achieve coordinated development of ecological benefits, economic benefits and social benefits through comprehensive supporting measures such as less tillage, no tillage, irrigation water management, residue management, surface covering and rational planting. Since the conservation agriculture can reduce soil disturbance and reduce the loss of soil organic carbon (SOC). Refloresta Portugal, Forestry Carbon Project (Central Region I) consists of the implementation of reforestation projects located in burned areas in Portugal. This project is part of Motor Verde, an offsetting initiative promoted by Fundación Repsol, based on Mediterranean forest reforestation and regeneration aiming for a triple goal social, environmental and economic. 
The project proponents of this single project are Grupo Sylvestris and Fundación Repsol. Sylvestris is a forestry consultancy located in Madrid, Spain, specialised in forestry restoration, rural development and environmental consulting, Spain; and Fundación Repsol is the fund responsible for Repsol’s social responsibility vocation. Both entities are connected by the fund's shareholding in Sylvestris. The project counts on Metsä, the project implementing partner, a local forestry consultancy located in Abrantes, Portugal, close to the affected areas to be restored.
The project intends to establish approximately 56,51 ha of Mediterranean forest. Plantations are being established in private-owned land located in the mid-centre of Portugal. These lands have been burned by 2017 and 2019 fires, where natural regeneration is inexistent. 
The project will generate GHG removals by the plantation growing, using native species such as Quercus suber and Pinus pinaster, among others. A total amount of 16,566 tonnes of CO2e are expected to be generated by the implementation of the project, equivalent to an average of 414 tonnes of CO2 per year, taking into account that this amount varies annually depending on the corresponding compensation.
Economic, environmental and social benefits are expected: 
-	recovering burned ecosystems with native species
-	creating jobs in the implementation areas,
-	contributing to minimise the risk of depopulation,
-	investing in natural resources, that allows a sustainable business development,
-	promoting the innovation and research for new technologies application in forestry

The purpose of BRASCARBON Methane Recovery Project BCA-BRA-18 project is to utilize the effluent produced on a total of 7 pig farms in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, cities of Jarei and Gloria de Dourados, Brazil, to capture methane and generate biogas. The projects have the potential to generate energy from waste using the biogas produced and captured. Regardless this potential, energy will not be a part of this project activity.
Before the project activity, local farmers considered waste as an externality in the pig production process. As such, minimal finance was allocated to this issue and wastewater was often treated in open water lagoons – frequently with profound environmental impacts. The projects demonstrate how the construction of a set of new, covered, in-ground anaerobic digesters can utilize the organic material from the animal operations to produce biogas and fertilizer, whilst reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The   basis   of   the   projects   is   the   anaerobic   digestion, whereby microorganisms break down biodegradable material in the absence of oxygen. As part of an integrated waste management system, anaerobic digestion reduces the emission of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and produces a rich biogas, suitable for energy production, which can be used to replace fossil fuels. The nutrient-rich solids left after digestion are used as fertilizer and the better wastewater management allows more water for irrigation.

Yongji MSW Incineration Project is located between the Xiachao Village of the Chengbei Street and the Gucheng Village of the Kaizhang town, Yongji City, Shanxi Province, P.R. China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Yongji Huaxinda Cleaning Energy Co., Ltd.. 
With two 300t/d MSW combustion production lines, the project will treat 600 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of two 300t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 12MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 250,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 130.3 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work 8,000 hours every year, generating 72,748 MWh electricity, of which 59,972 MWh will be exported to the North China Power Grid (NCPG). The implementation of the project will meet the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also helps reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil-fuel fired plants and MSW treatment at landfill.
By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the project avoids the emissions of methane that would be generated under landfill condition. In the meanwhile, the proposed project can produce steam to generate power to replace the electricity that would otherwise be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants which are connected to the NCPG. The baseline scenario of this project is the same as the scenario prior to the implementation of the project, namely the landfill gas is vented directly and the equivalent power is supplied by the NCPG.
It is estimated that during the 10-year fixed crediting period of the project (from 30 June 2021 to 29 June 2031), the average annual GHG emission reductions will be 63,176 tCO2e.

This project description document covers COMACO operations in part of the Central province (Mumbwa and Shibuyunji districts) and part of Southern province (Itezhi-Tezhi district) of Zambia. The COMACO Landscape Management Project – South (CLMP-South) promotes sustainable agriculture and forest management. The key objectives of the project are to increase smallholder farmer agricultural productivity, provide alternative livelihoods and reduce uncontrolled forest loss and degradation. Hence, the project comprises two components:
1. Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) component – which aims to promote widespread adoption of agricultural practices including conservation agriculture and agroforest that increases the food production per unit area and farmers’ income. The project promotes the adoption by farmers of legume-based alley cropping, residues management (e.g. mulching; cessation of residue burning), use of organic fertilizers such as composite and animal manure, and reduced tillage among other SALM practices and the intercropping of Gliricidia Sepium as part of Agroforestry to restore soil quality and sequestrate carbon.
2. REDD+ (Avoided Unplanned Deforestation) component – which aims to reduce forest loss, and protect and expand areas under natural forest, and conserve biodiversity. This is achieved primarily through land use planning and creation of Community Conservation Areas (CCAs) for protection of natural forest, coupled with sustainable non-extractive forest use, e.g. honey and mushrooms. The creation of CCAs and the enforcement of by-laws to protect them promotes the protection of ecosystems and biodiversity within and around the CCAs.

The Project is aligned with the Moroccan Ministry's goal to transition one million hectares to Zero-tillage by 2030, the project operates with a 10-year crediting period under the VCS-approved Methodology VM0017. The Transformational Regenerative Integrated Biodiverse Agriculture for Livelihoods (TRIBAL) Project is a landscape approach that aims to make it viable for small and marginal farmers to live off their land in a sustainable and profitable manner. 
The project will promote agroforestry and sustainable farming practices across within the Araku Valley in Vishakhapatnam District, Andhra Pradesh, India. Planned agroforestry and sustainable farming practices that will be promoted by the project include agroforestry utilizing both fruit and multi-purpose tree species, shade coffee systems, intercropping of pulses and millets, green manuring, mulching and organic composting. These activities will improve the livelihoods and well-being of the tribal landowners by achieving multiple objectives such as improved soil fertility, increased revenue generation, food security, reduced drudgery for women and increased biodiversity. Through this positive impact on climate, communities, and biodiversity the TRIBAL project aims to achieve both VCS and CCB Gold certification. 
This grouped project is being initiated in Paderu and Pedabayalu Mandals of Paderu Division in Vishakhapatnam District, with the intention of expanding to up to 11 Mandals within the Araku Valley landscape in future. The tribal people of this region were traditionally hunters and gatherers, relying on the forest for sustenance. The practice of shifting cultivation came in at the turn of the century. As the- forest began to get depleted, the tribal communities gradually become engaged in agriculture. Now, subsistence agriculture is the primary livelihood for nearly 99% of the tribes within the project region, with over 80% of the landholdings being less than one hectare in size.
vcs-4306: The SALM project in Bangladesh aims to address the negative impacts of conventional farming practices on the environment, particularly greenhouse gas emissions. The project includes a range of measures and technologies designed to reduce emissions by promoting regenerative and sustainable farming practices.The activities include efficient use of irrigation water, mulching, reduction of chemical fertilizer and pesticide use through the use of organic amendments, applying green manure, and alternative pest control methods, avoidance of crop residue burning, and minimum tillage.

The project intends to include producers dedicated to extensive agriculture (corn, soybeans, wheat, sunflower, cotton, and other crops), and extensive cattle ranching, mostly cattle and grazing grasslands, pastures, agropastoral, and silvo-pastoral. Given the characteristics of the country, farm and ranch  production dates from no more than 200 years ago.
During most of the 20th century, the farms were managed in a rather extensive manner and with aggressive tillage systems, which caused widespread declines in the organic matter content of the soils. This lasted until the end of that century, when for different reasons the producers adopted zero tillage systems, which are what predominate today (more than 90%).
The projects to be implemented are expected to mitigate climate change both by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and by capturing atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) and storing it as stable carbon in the soil, which must be recarbonized. The greatest efforts to reduce GHG emissions will be due to the adoption of better nitrogen fertilization technologies, which include alternative sources of nitrogen and variable rate fertilization that reduce nitrous oxide (N2) emissions from fertilized soils, the intensification of agricultural rotations with greater incorporation of winter crops, nitrogen fixing species and cover crops, and improved grazing management in livestock, which increase carbon stocks and with improvements in digestibility that reduce methane (CH4) emissions due to enteric fermentation. 
It is estimated that with these improvements, which are not currently widespread even among producers, it will be possible to reduce between 0.5 and 3 tons of CO2e/ha/year. Obviously, the total amount will depend on the area committed by the producers. This area is expected to reach more than 160 thousand hectares. If this is so, it is expected to mitigate almost 2 million tons CO2e at the end of this project.

The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 

The first instance under this grouped project, will be implemented within the state boundary of the eastern states of India i.e., West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Jharkhand etc. It is envisaged that a combination of improved cook stoves (ICS) shall be provided to end user communities to completely replace baseline stoves. The overall effect is reduced emission of carbon dioxide and smoke, improving air quality within the household as well as the quality of life of women folk. At present the total stove distribution under this project activity is set at 3,500,000 out of which 3,000,000 will be Baldwin stoves and 500,000 Dinabandhu stoves for end user households. Each home will receive either a single Dinabandhu Cookstove or two Baldwin Cookstoves as part of the distribution of the stoves. This is to ensure that the end user is not forced to go back to using baseline stoves on account of one project stove not being able to cater to complete requirements of the household.

The Northern Plains Landscape REDD+ project (NPL REDD+), in Cambodia’s northern province of Preah Vihear, operates initially within three established protected areas: parts of Kulen Promtep Wildlife Sanctuary (KPWS), Chhaeb Wildlife Sanctuary (CWS) and Preah Roka Wildlife Sanctuary (PRWS), with plans to add Phnom Tbaeng Natural Heritage Park (PTNHP) at a later stage. The protected areas are under the jurisdiction of the Royal Government of Cambodia’s Ministry of Environment, the NPL REDD+ project proponent. The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) serves as the main technical and implementing partner. The project recognizes the local communities in and around the borders of the protected areas as critical stakeholders upon which the project’s success depends.  
The Northern Plains support globally important fauna and flora, with 84 globally threatened wildlife species and 48 nationally protected species, including Asian elephants, wild cattle and the critically endangered giant and white-shouldered ibises. The project contains a mosaic of different forest types and wetlands that are under severe threat due to illegal logging, clearing of forest for agriculture, and infrastructure development. Large economic land concessions (ELCs) and social land concessions (SLCs) have progressively encroached on the protected areas’ forest. An active illegal wildlife trade in the region also severely impacts the area’s biodiversity.
The NPL REDD+ project, since 2018, endeavors to better maintain the forests for the benefit of the climate, as important habitat for wildlife, and to support the livelihoods of the local communities living in the area. Project interventions include improving incentives for conservation through payment for environmental services (PES), strengthening forest law/protected areas law enforcement activities through upgraded patrolling systems, and improving livelihoods through increased tenure security, diversification, and sustainable community development.

B. Reduce tillage/improve residue management; and
C. Improve crop planting and harvesting.
vcs-4319: The C-SA Carbon Project focusses on this opportunity to restore subtropical thicket, sequester carbon and to deliver a broader range of social and ecological outcomes. The C-SA property includes a primary conservation area (in which the Kwandwe eco-tourism operation is located) as well as several severely degraded properties that have been acquired over time. The additional areas of at least 4,000 hectares were previously goat and ostrich farms and have been left in a degraded state, largely clear of vegetation and especially Portulacaria afra. The intention is to implement a landscape-scale rehabilitation project that includes the propagation and planting of Portulacaria afra as well as other species, combined with the long-term management of planted propagules and herbivory pressure. Such planting and management has led to the successful restoration of carbon stocks elsewhere in the biome. The outcome will extend beyond carbon sequestration to the delivery of further ecosystem services and a source of employment and income for local residents (in a region where such opportunities are rare). In an area that is predicted to become significantly warmer and drier over time, enhancing the resilient provision of water services to downstream communities and economies is of significant importance. Through direct restoration of over 4,000 hectares, the project is expected to sequester at least 1,078,000 tCO2e over a 40-year period or an average 26,950 tCO2e per year.

This project will promote tree-based wild silk production (sericulture) outside traditional forests by utilizing privately owned degraded lands that smallholder farmers currently do not significantly utilize for productive purposes. It will undertake host tree planting for the Tasar silkworm and silkworm rearing value chain development in two states in India: Jharkhand and West Bengal. Traditionally, the tribal communities in these areas depend significantly on forests for their livelihoods and have a long history of silk production from natural forests –silk is second to agriculture as a source of income/livelihoods. However, production from the forests have become uncertain due to government regulation of forest access rights and instability in the silk market. Yet there are large areas in these regions that are severely degraded, fallow, etc. that would benefit from restoring their productive capacity and biodiversity through profitable tree planting investments. Therefore, this project will undertake tree planting for Tasar production on an estimated 3,000 ha of such lands. 
The project is implemented by the Non-Governmental Organization (NGO): PRADAN - Professional Assistance for Development Action – which has a long-standing experience (50 years) in the area. It will involve the participation of ~4,000 households in 117 villages, grouped into two clusters. The project has a crediting period of 20-years renewable, and will employ the new VERRA ARR Methodology ”Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation Projects”. Its estimated annual average and total GHG emission removals are 89,847 and 1,796,931 t CO2e respectively.

vcs-4329: The Conservation and Restoration of Classified Forests in Côte d’Ivoire project (“CRCF”) is being developed by Eni S.p.A. and Eni Côte d’Ivoire LTD and aims to implement both forest conservation and restoration activities in 14 classified forests for a total area of 156,000 ha spread across the districts of Lagunes and Comoé. The overall project aim is to preserve each classified forest targeted, restore the deforested and degraded areas through reforestation, agroforestry and assisted natural revegetation activities and develop a sustainable management of the forest resources.  The targeted forests have been heavily deforested and degraded over the years. The main direct causes of deforestation and forest degradation are: (i) the significant expansion of extensive slash-and-burn agriculture and monoculture plantations (e.g. cocoa, rubber, palm oil etc.); (ii) the uncontrolled exploitation of forests; iii) population growth and urban expansion; (iv) bushfires (related to agriculture and/or hunting); v) mining, including illegal gold panning; and vi) political and military crisis. To this end, the implementation of the CRCF project is critical to ensure the preservation and restoration of the remaining portions of natural forests, to reduce the greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) from the conversion of natural forest and to restore the biodiversity across the project area. The project will actively involve local communities and will produce significant socio-economic benefits through the creation of alternative livelihoods and economic opportunities. The project is in line and will support the Government’s strategy to reduce the deforestation and related GHG emissions and increase its forest surface. The project has a 30-year crediting period and applies the VCS approved VM0007 REDD+ Methodology Framework (REDD+ MF). The estimated annual average is approximately 273.524 tCO2e and the total net greenhouse gas emission reductions/removals are around 8.205.724 tCO2e.

The grouped project activity is carried out by Zhejiang Green Intelligent Link (hereafter Green Intelligent Link or Intelligent Link), which is a platform supplying environmental transport capacity and smart vehicle networking, to provide rental services of electric delivery vehicles in China.
In China, commercial vehicles sold out 3 million in 2022, including 2.893 million trucks. Most commercial vehicles burn fossil fuels. As one kind of commercials vehicles, the sales of pickup trucks were 519,000. By fuel, the sales of gasoline pickup trucks and diesel ones were 120,000 and 397,000 respectively. The new energy vehicles used for distribution in urban accounted for 8% of all new energy vehicles till 2020. 168,000 new energy vehicles were sold in 2021, with a penetration rate of 3.5%. Due to problem like lack of supporting infrastructure, and high price of power batteries, the fuel vehicles were commonly used in commercial transportation services.
In this project, project vehicles of the proponent, Intelligent Link, are divided into 2 categories, truck and van. They are all electric vehicles (hereafter EVs). EVs are driven by pure electric provided by energy stored in batteries. The project scenario is EVs instead of fuel-driven vehicles delivering goods in urban area of China. As an EV runs on electricity instead of fossil fuel (diesel and gasoline), the vehicle emits no exhaust from a tailpipe, which leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven.
The project contributes in a significant manner to sustainable development, which are below: 
•	Project activity is generating employment for local drivers;
•	Project reduces the per capita negative environmental impact of cities within project area, especially the air quality improvement due to reduced vehicle exhaust emission;
•	Project reduces GHG emission reduction due to implementation of EVs and reducing fossil fuel-based vehicles.

Guangxi Nanning animal waste management systems project installs total 9 sets of new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure on site for 9 existing swine farms owned by four subsidiaries of Muyuan Foods Co., Ltd. in Nanning city in Guangxi, i.e. one set for each swine farm. The purpose of the project is to treat the waste produced in swine farms by adopting AWMSs to avoid GHG emissions generated in the uncovered anaerobic lagoons of baseline scenario.
The treatment process employed by the newly built AWMSs consist of 3 steps: solid-liquid separation, anaerobic digestion, and aerobic composting. All manure and urine collected from swine farms are separated first. Solid components separated are then treated in aerobic composting system to produce organic fertilizer. And the liquids flow into anaerobic digestion process to generate biogas for utilization for energy. Excess biogas (if any) is destroyed through the flaring system. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion process are treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent is supplied to the farmers living around for free for agriculture irrigation.

Zhenyuan Swine Farm AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduces 1 new animal waste management system (AWMS) to treat the manure from the existing swine farm in Zhenyuan County, Guizhou Province, which are owned by ZHENYUAN XINMU Agricultural Development Co., Ltd (hereinafter called the project owner). Each subsidiary swine farm will install one AWMS. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The common practice for local swine farm owners to manage the manure is to have uncovered anaerobic lagoons/ponds at their farms in the region. As per “technical specification for sanitation treatment of livestock and poultry manure ”, in China, the uncovered anaerobic lagoons are a manure treatment method recognized by the state. In addition, since there is no legal regulation to mandate the livestock farm owners to implement anaerobic digestion, aerobic or other biological treatment techniques and to capture and/or utilize methane generated at their lagoons, therefore the continue of this common practice to treatment the manure i.e., uncovered anaerobic lagoons is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.
It is estimated that approximately 388.64*104 m3 of biogas will be produced annually. The biogas will be captured and utilized for heat generation, the heat will be only used for the daily operation of the AWMS and the swine farm and will not be produced to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 32,028 tCO2e emission reductions will be produced annually.

vcs-4372: The mangrove areas of the Democratic Republic of Congo (fall under the global category grouping of Central African mangrove eco-region. They are found within the Central Congo Province occupying an area of 23,684 hectares.Mangrove forests of DRC are crucial because of its importance in provision of goods and services which are unique to this type of forest such as shoreline protection and being a feeding and breeding ground of commercially important fisheries due to the location of these forests at the tidal estuaries ecosystems of River Congo as well as supporting a wide range of biodiversity. Despite these uses, the DRC Mangrove Forest has seen degradation and deforestation over the years. The threats facing these mangroves include the encroachment of the areas by the nearby communities leading to conversion of forest land to settlement and other land uses that is linked to population increase over the years, coupled with unsustainable harvesting for wood and firewood for varied purposes. Additionally, the loss of mangroves leads to the release o f the carbon stored by the ecosystem back into the atmosphere, thereby accelerating climate change. Through the implementation of the mangrove REDD+ project in the area the project proponents aim to conserve the mangrove areas by addressing the drivers of deforestation leading to a potential emission reduction of 689,274 tCO2e/year. Furthermore, the project proponent also aims to restore the already degraded and deforested area of 1161 ha during the project lifetime that will lead to additional emission reductions of 33,379 tCO2e/yr along with other benefits such as shoreline protection and biodiversity conservation. Thus, this REDD and RWE project is expected to avoid unplanned deforestation and degradation, along with restoration of the already degraded areas on an area of 23,684 ha equating to 21,691,891 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30 year project lifetime with an annual average of 723,063 tCO2e.

The project activity aims to provide individuals with improved cookstove (ICS). The stoves will be availed for free in all the districts of Benin: Alibori, Atacora, Atlantique, Borgou, Collines, Couffo, Donga, Littoral, Mono, Ouémé, Plateau, and Zou. The ICS distributed through this project will replace the prevailing inefficient three-stone fireplace or traditional charcoal cookstoves such as charcoal clay cookers and charcoal coal pots that are predominantly used by households across the region. The ICS provides for an efficient transfer of the thermal energy generated through the combustion of biomass towards the cooking pot. There is thus a resultant reduction in both biomass consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
In addition to the reduction of biomass consumption (and associated reduction in expenses to purchase wood or charcoal – or reduction in time gathering firewood), there will also be an economic benefit in that the ICS will be produced locally in the region and will create jobs which will have a large proportion of female employees.
The actual situation for cooking practices in Benin shows that only 4% of population have access to clean cooking . According to a recent World Bank report on Benin’s forest note, at present, one of the main drivers of deforestation is the use of the forested area as fuelwood which provides 46 percent of the energy consumed in the country. 
The project seeks to distribute up to 640,000 ICS to households across Benin. Thanks to carbon finance, the cookstoves will be distributed at a 100% subsidy to users. The project aims to avoid on average 616,777 tCO2e per year and 4,317,441 tCO2e over the first crediting period.
