Geothermal is a non-polluting, renewable and clean energy compared with traditional fossil energy such as coal, oil and natural gas. According to the Plan for Clean Heating in Winter in Northern China (2017-2021) (Development and Reform of Energy resources (2017) No. 2100)  , the proportion of clean heating in northern China is low, especially in some areas, where bulk burning coal is used in winter and air pollutant emissions are high, so it is urgent to promote clean heating.
At present, there is no municipal central heating system in the urban area of Lankao County, so a new central heating source is needed to ensure the heating demand. The purpose of the project activity is to introduce geothermal energy-based space heating system to realize heat supply to a series of residential buildings in Lankao County over winter season, which will displace heat supply from isolated coal-fired boilers as a business-as-usual scenario in the project area.
The project owner is Lankao Green Energy Clean Energy Co., Ltd. It can supply geothermal heat to 3,736.1 thousand m2 of newly built residential buildings with a total heating load of 112.08 MW. The scenario prior to the implementation of the proposed project activity is that heat supplied to the building areas in winter would be provided by isolated coal-fired boilers.
vcs-4384: The Jaji ARR Project is the first ARR based CCB-VCS project to be developed in Kaduna State, Nigeria and amongst the first CCB-VCS projects of its kind in Nigeria. The goals of the project are; the reforestation of degraded abandoned farmland and the sustainable management of the reforested area for the lifetime of the project in order to sequester emissions, enhance land resources and their ability to support life on land, positive social/community impact for the improvement of livelihoods and conditions of communities around the project area, empowerment of marginalized segments of the rural population and the promotion of biodiversity in the project area and zones.
vcs-4385: The proposed group project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by distributing fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to households in Tanzania. The goal of the project is to replace traditional cookstoves with ICS, designed to burn wood more efficiently and save fuel, by distributing approximately 400,000 ICS to households. The improved cook stoves will replace the 3-stone fire, which is the predominant stove in the project area. By using the ICS, fuel consumption will be reduced, thereby reducing the time required for wood collection or reducing costs for firewood for households purchasing wood. The improved efficiency of the stove will also lead to reduced indoor air pollution, thereby improving the health situation especially of women and children.
vcs-4386: The proposed group project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by distributing fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to households in Ethiopia. The goal of the project is to replace traditional cookstoves with ICS, designed to burn wood more efficiently and save fuel, by distributing approximately 400,000 ICS to households. The improved cookstoves will replace the 3-stone fire, which is the predominant stove in the project area. By using the ICS, fuel consumption will be reduced, thereby reducing the time required for wood collection or reducing costs for firewood for households purchasing wood. The improved efficiency of the stove will also lead to reduced indoor air pollution, thereby improving the health situation especially of women and children.
vcs-4387:
The REDD+ Project Pacha Prometida is a grouped initiative that takes place in indigenous communities San Pedro (located in the Ixiamas municipality), Cachichira and Tres Hermanos (located in the San Buenaventura municipality), in Abel Iturralde province of La Paz Department, in Bolivia. Initially, it seeks to protect 11,500 hectares of primary Amazonian forest, which is strongly threatened by planned agricultural expansion and sugarcane planting activities, through:
• Reducing the threat of deforestation on the forests of the communities Cachichira, San Pedro and Tres Hermanos and, therefore, avoid the issuance of around 4.3 million of tCO2 during the first 20 years of the Project life cycle (on average 215,000 VCUs annually).
• Promoting of the social development actions to improve the quality of life of the families of the communities Cachichira, San Pedro and Tres Hermanos.
• Protecting biological diversity in flora and fauna, especially habitats of endangered wild species, found in the territories of the communities Cachichira, San Pedro and Tres Hermanos.
• Conserving and improving the focal areas where High Conservation Values are found that are identified.
vcs-4388:
Jiangsu Jiangyan Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities (conventional tillage without straw incorporation) to conventional tillage with straw incorporation in fields where rice and wheat are rotated and the project located in Jiangyan district in Jiangsu province, China. The project involves 26,666 ha field where wheat and rice are rotated.
The project is expected to increase SOC by straw incorporation, since straw contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, straw incorporation to the field can effectively increase soil organic matter (SOM). Straw incorporation to the field also can improve soil physical and chemical properties, enhance soil aggregate structure, and increase soil permeability.
vcs-4389:
The bundled project consists of the construction and operation of two greenfield solar power plants, Zano for 24MWc and Souri for 18MWc. Zano is located near the town of Tenkodogo, in Bougou region, Center- Eastern Burkina Faso and will be operated by Quadran Burkina Faso, when Souri is located near Dedougou, in the Mouhoun region, Western Burkina Faso and will be operated by Dédougou Solaire. Both involve the setting up of photovoltaic (PV) panels for a total installed capacity of 42MWc which will capture solar energy and produce electricity to be exported to the West African Power Pool.
Access to clean and inexpensive energy is a priority of Burkina Faso's Ministry of Energy, which aims to increase the national and rural electrification rates by 45% and 19% respectively by 2025. To this end, the Government of Burkina Faso has signed a concession agreement with Quadran International (now rebranded Qair), Syscom Network (the sponsors) on one hand, and Quadran Burkina Faso and Dedougou solaire on the other hand (the project SPV’s) to build and operate Zano and Souri respective solar power plants during 25 years. 
The project is a type I project activity under sectoral scope: 1, Energy Industries (renewable and non-renewable sources). The methodology ACM0002 (Version 21.0) is applied since its purpose is the installation of a new grid-connected renewable power plant (Greenfield) as the “electricity delivered to the grid by the project activity would have otherwise been generated by the operation of grid-connected power plants.” 
The average power generation of the project for the next 7 years is estimated at 80 GWh per year, resulting in emissions reductions of 45,316 tCO2e emission reductions per year and 317,217 tCO2e of emission reductions over the 7 years crediting period.
vcs-439: The purpose of this proposed project is to collect all of the waste stream of HFC23 from HCFC22 production process, and decompose it almost completely by an incinerator to be installed in Yingpeng Chemical Co., Ltd. HFC23 will be decomposed to carbon dioxide (CO2), hydrogen chloride (HCl), and hydrogen fluoride (HF) etc., with high temperature and low pH value, and be further processed by the cooling and de-acid process before being emitted to the atmosphere.
vcs-4390:
Jiangsu Guanyun Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities (conventional tillage) to conservation agriculture management (conservative tillage) in Guanyun county, Lianyungang city, Jiangsu province, China. 
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by applying the conservative tillage. The conservative tillage refers that: through straw returning to the field, minimum tillage, no tillage, reduction of chemical fertilizers and pesticides application and other agriculture management measures. The conservative tillage is a sustainable agricultural technology that can reduce farmland soil erosion, protect farmland ecological environment and achieve coordinated development of ecological benefits, economic benefits and social benefits. 
Since the conservative tillage can reduce soil disturbance and reduce the loss of soil organic carbon (SOC). Moreover, the project is expected to increase SOC by applying crop residue management, since the crop residue contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Mulching crop residue into soil can maintain soil moisture, reduce soil temperature, increase soil microbe amount and eventually increase soil organic matter (SOM).
vcs-4391:
The project area is located within 3 private properties, located in the municipalities of Vila Rica, inthe State of Acre, Brazil, inserted in an area Amazon biome. The project aims to avoid unplanned deforestation in a project area of 58,487.50 ha. The REDD+CCB project is expected to avoid predicted deforestation of 10,354,998 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (Dec 01,2022-Nov 30,2052), with an annual average of 345,167 tCO2e.
The objective is to originate- with characteristics of a REDD+CCB initiative, following the Project Cycle of the VM0015 Methodology for Avoided Unplanned Deforestation, v1.1 Methodology. Thus, such VCUs may, in the future, be accounted for in Brazil's Nationally Determined Contributions Emission Reductions efforts, within the framework of the Paris Climate Agreement, as they are negotiated between different parties, within the framework of the voluntary markets for carbon credit negotiations.
Since the proiect will originate from the characteristics of a REDD+ initiative, it will contribute to efforts to reduce deforestation of the Amazon Biome in Brazil, resulting in the preservation of biodiversity in one of the most important tropical forests on the planet and in the restoration and preservation of the conditions of Climate Regulation of the Earth. It is therefore important that the Project is added to the methodological efforts provided for in the CCB Program- so that the VCUs eligible for the validation of the methodological quality are also valued considering the methodological efforts validated by the CCB Program.
The project's social engagement creates a support base to ensure preservation and sustainable use of the forest. Social engagement at all stages is important so the actions to be developed are inclusive and transparent, in processes that allow communities and stakeholders to actively participate to ensure that the project generates legacies with positive social and environmental impacts.
vcs-4392: Jinhui sustainable grassland management project is located in Tianjun County, Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province of China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem and black soil beach through sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals among rotational grazing plots, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and reseeding with native grasses on severely degraded grassland and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term, thereby increasing carbon sequestration, and promoting local development. Totally, 297,781.30 ha of degraded grassland has been managed scientifically through rest and rotational grazing by fence building and reseeding of native grass species.
vcs-4394:
The Jatobá project will be developed in the municipality of Boca do Acre, state of Amazonas, Brazil, within the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) category. The project will conserve 94,090.42 hectares of native Amazon rainforests in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to land use conversion activities from forests to pastures aimed at raising livestock. The project area (18,017.19 ha) will be allocated to Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), and it is estimated that at the end of the project the emission of 5,440,804 tons of Greenhouse Gases (GHG) (tCO2e) will have been avoided. 
The project will be developed considering the CCB Standards, with benefits for the Climate, Community and Biodiversity. As benefits to the climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adapting to the impacts caused by climate change.
As benefits to the communities, the project will enable water security and access to information to minimize the impacts caused by climate change in traditional, low-income extractive communities.
It is noteworthy that the project includes a high priority area for biodiversity conservation, as it is located within a Key Biodiversity Area (KBA), harboring species endemic to the Brazilian Amazon and species classified as Vulnerable (VU), Critically Endangered (CR) and Endangered (EN) with extinction according to the IUCN.
vcs-4395: WABIO Technology Holding Ltd. builds and operates its own biogas power plants for third-party companies wishing to gain access to renewable energy sources. Alter Biogas ll Project is one of those projects, which will be located on cadastral parcel no. 2906/11 in cadastral municipality of Nova Crnja, Serbia. Prior to the development of this Alter Biogas ll Project, the manure and straw from the farms is stored in open manure lagoons where it is allowed to decay anaerobically, generating greenhouse gas emissions and other negative impacts on the farm environment through soil pollution. Alter Biogas ll Project will use cow manure and corn straw as feedstock for anaerobic digestion and production of biogas. Electricity will be generated from the 999 kWe generator within the plant.
vcs-4396:
The purpose of this project is to provide safe drinking water to the people in Viet Nam through carbon finance. Several low greenhouse gas emitting water purification technologies in accord with the CDM approved methodology AMS-III. AV. may be applied in the project such as water filter, ultraviolet disinfection and chemical disinfection.
In the absence of the Grouped project , the fossil fuels and biomass could have been used to boil water in Viet Nam as a means of water purification. As the consumption of fuel wood will be reduced by project activities, it can contribute to improving public health problems.
TAB is the coordinating/managing entity (CME) of this project. TAB is a company registered in the Republic of Korea which will provide all implementation cost for all the VPAs of the Grouped project and make them financially sustainable through carbon market.
vcs-4397:
Jilin Zhenlai Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) implements conservation agriculture (crop residue addition and no or reduced tillage) in 60,000 hectares (or 900,000 Mu  ) of monocropping corn fields located in villages under the administration of Zhenlai County, Baicheng City, Jilin Province, China.
The project is expected to replace conventional farming practices and promote conservation agriculture, which entails incorporating crop residues in the field after the harvest and applying no or reduced tillage prior to sowing. No or reduced tillage minimizes soil disturbance; crop residues incorporated in the fields contribute to soil organic matter increase and avoid greenhouse gas emissions which would otherwise occur due to burning or other management measures.
vcs-4398:
Jilin Dehui Improved Crop Management Project (hereafter as 'the project') aims to increase soil carbon storage and decrease current carbon emissions from participating farms. By switching from the previous agricultural management practices (conventional tillage to conservational tillage), the chosen measures will also help to improve crop yields and soil health.
The project is located in Dehui City, Jilin Province of China, covers 15 towns and 2 street committees. Dehui City is a county-level city under the jurisdiction of Jilin Province, is managed by Changchun City, located in the northern part of Jilin Province and the hinterland of Songliao Plain, with an area of 3,322.24 square kilometres, and the geographic coordinates between 125°14’ and 126°24’ East longitude, 44°02’ and 44°53’ North latitude.
The conservational tillage method will be used in the project, which is projected to reduce GHG emissions. The term 'conservational tillage' refers to an environmentally friendly agricultural technique that, with the help of a variety of supplementary practices like straw return  and minimal or no tillage, can reduce soil erosion on farms, safeguard the ecological environment on farms, and achieve coordinated development of ecological, economic, and social benefits. Due to the fact that conservational tillage can lessen soil disturbance and soil organic carbon (SOC) loss. Additionally, returning straw to the field can efficiently use organic fertilizer resources and increase soil organic matter (SOM), as straw contains a significant amount of organic matter and trace elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
vcs-4399:
Heilongjiang Shuangcheng Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Shuangcheng District in Helongjiang Province, China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices including returning straw in fields and applying organic fertilizer, and to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land.
Since straw contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, returning straw to the field can effectively use organic fertilizer resources and increase soil organic matter (SOM). Straw returning to the field also can improve soil physical and chemical properties, enhance soil aggregate structure, and increase soil permeability. Applying organic fertilizer can reduce nitrous oxide emission compared to synthetic fertilizer.
vcs-44: The Jiratpattana Biogas Energy Project (hereafter, the Project) that was developed by Thai Biogas Energy Company Ltd (hereafter referred to as “TBEC, ”or the Project Developer) is an anaerobic digestion project, which treats wastewater from the cassava processing factory owned by Jiratpattana Agriculture Limited (hereafter referred to as the Facility) in Kalasin, Thailand. In the baseline scenario, the wastewater flows from the factory through a series of 9 low-maintenance anaerobic and aerobic lagoons.  As the wastewater flows through the lagoons, organic material is broken down and resulting methane is released to the atmosphere.
vcs-4400:
The “Improved cropland management project in Moqi” is aimed to raise farmer's awareness on the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change the agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objectives of the project is to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage, in order to achieve these, a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried out, the specific activities are the following:
A. Reduce fertilizer (organic or inorganic) application;
B. Reduce tillage/improve residue management; and
C. Improve crop planting and harvesting.
vcs-4401:
The Hunan Miluo IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Miluo City, Hunan Province of China by Hunan Carbon Technology Co., Ltd. The geographic coordinate of project is 112°51′~113° 27′ E and 28°28′~29°27′ N, the total area is 156,200 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.

The area of the project activity is 1879.76 ha, including 80 subcompartments spreading over Sanjiang Town, Dajing Town, Changle Town of Hunan Carbon Technology Co., Ltd.  All these departments are 100% owned by forest farmers and have the legal right to forest ownership. They all singned commissioning contracts with Hunan Carbon Technology Co., Ltd. The species involved in the project are Chinese Fir, Masson pine, Broad-leaf trees and other pine. These are common local tree species.

Prior to the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged annually according to a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 708,630 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual emission reduction is 23,621 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 552,731 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 18,424 tCO2e.

The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.
vcs-4402:
The proposed project was designed to treat chicken manure in Shanglin Country to produce organic fertilizer. The project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system, etc. It is estimated that approximately 80,000 tons of chicken manure can be treated with 30,250 tons of organic fertilizer generated per year. Without this project, the farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere. 
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting biomass waste. It is estimated that 54,726 t CO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 547,260t CO2e in a 10-year crediting period.
vcs-4403:
CEKEREK BIOGAS POWER PLANT (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that aims to methane capture through anaerobic digestion and utilization of methane for thermal energy and electricity generation via cogeneration units. The cattle and animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Waste heat from gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but also used for auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. 
The project is being implemented by ÇEKEREK ENERJİ VE GÜBRE ÜRETİM A.Ş., the Project Owner, in Çekerek district, Yozgat province, in Turkey. The start date of the project and of the first crediting period is determined as June 29th, 2021.
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 50,727 tCO2e/yr. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 285,369 tCO2e emissions reduction during the first crediting period.
vcs-4404:
ELAZIG BIOGAS POWER PLANT (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that aims to captures biogas from animal manure, cattle, and chicken manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate electricity through cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighbouring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas.  Waste heat from gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The electricity generated by the installed biogas engines with the total capacity of 3.002 Mwe/ 3.080 MWm is not only supplied to the national grid, but also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products, by-products of biogas generation processes, are distributed to neighbouring agricultural farms as fertilizer free of charge. 
The project is being implemented by ELERJI ENERJI GUBRE URETIM SANAYI TICARET A.Ş., as the project owner, Cevizdere district, Elazığ province, in Turkey. The start date of the project and the of the first crediting period is determined as June 30, 2021.
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emission from fossil-fuel based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 84,101 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 588,706 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.
vcs-4408: Trees for the Future (TREES) is developing The Lake Victoria Watershed Agroforestry Carbon Project. This project uses VERRA methodology VM0042 with CCB to develop and monitor VCUs with smallholder farmers on 75,000 hectares of land in the counties of Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori and Siaya along the shores of Lake Victoria in Kenya. This project will involve training and implementing sustainable agroforestry practices with farmers to transform mono-cropped land into nature-based carbon sinks with above and below ground biomass and improved soils. Currently this cropland is under low yield cultivation of grain crops and is an area designated by the Kenyan Government as a target region for agroforestry development on cropland. In addition, to creating VCUs, the sustainable agroforestry techniques and extension services provided to farmers will ensure diversification of cropping systems including horticulture crops and fruit and fodder trees. The projects aims to improve nutrition, increase income and resilience, develop the sustainable growing capability of the land, and enhance biodiversity in the region. The restoration effort will generate an estimated 20.7 million Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) and help farmers adapt to the impacts of climate change.
vcs-4411:
Xinzhou Echeng Afforestation Project (hereafter as “the project”) locates in Echeng County, Xinzhou City, Shanxi Province of North China. It aims to address climate change and promote sustainable development in the region. The project involves planting trees on barren mountains to increase carbon sequestration, which can help mitigate the effects of climate change by removing CO2. Aside from the environmental benefits, the project can also have positive economic impacts on the local community by providing employment opportunities for residents and contributing to local economic development. The project was implemented by the project proponent Jingle County Sailing Carbon Sink Development Co. Ltd.
A total of 39,589.87 ha of forest will be planted through direct planting on previously barren lands in Echeng County. The project will cover 6 towns,6 townships and 223 administrative villages. The project sites have not undergone any natural renewal or afforestation prior to the implementation of the project. 
The project is expected to generate GHG emission removals of 19,966,354 tCO2e in 60 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 332,773tCO2e.
vcs-4412: The project activity uses scraper system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated solid will be treated in aerobic composting system to produce fertilizer. The separated liquid will be treated through UASB or USR anaerobic digestion, and the biogas generated in the UASB or USR anaerobic digestion process is collected as boiler fuel to produce hot water or generate electricity for the swine farm, and the residual biogas will be flared by internal combustion emergency flare (closed flare) if there is any surplus biogas. Almost no biogas is produced in the aerobic digestion process. The sludge produced by digestion is treated with aerobic composting together with solids, and the effluent is used as liquid organic fertilizer for agricultural irrigation.
vcs-4413: The consumption of non renewable biomass firewood for household purposes in the rural areas is one of the main causes of deforestation in the surrou nding areas of the state of Assam, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Sikkim and West Bengal and others states of India and has several implications in the environmental and health aspects of such communities. The Project activity aims to replace the commo nly used inefficient wood fired mud stove technology with efficient bio gas based cook stoves, which is clean and sustainable. In view of the same, National Diary Development Board (NDDB), a body corporate constituted an ACT of Parliament called, “The National Diary Development Board Act, 1987” and Sustain Plus Energy Foundation, a Non Profit company incorporated under Section 8 of companies Act 2013, has planned to implement a project which is clean, convenient and efficient energy can be accessed by the rural households.
vcs-4414: The purpose of the project activity is to treat the sugarcane press mud generated from nearby sugar factories. It aims to convert the press mud into organic manure, develop and market organic manure. . Generated biogas is compressed after purification and supply to nearby market as a substitute of Diesel or Petrol. This acts as a solution to reduce pollutions by avoiding fossil fuel burning like Diesel or Petrol and achieve reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
vcs-4416:
The Improved Cookstove Grouped Project in Papua New Guinea is a grouped project activity that involves the distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Papua New Guinea (PNG). The ICS disseminated through this project will replace open-fired wood-fueled cooking methods at no cost to the local community. 
The project activities included in this grouped project activity will occur in geographically defined regions within the project boundary of Papua New Guinea, starting first within the Western, Eastern Highlands Provinces, Southern Highlands Provinces, and Jiwaka Province.
vcs-4417: M/s Shree Gaushala Samiti, Operates a Cowshed at Padampur, District- Shriganganagar, Rajasthan, India and desires to generate off-grid electricity by using biogas generated from cattle dung and use the electricity for captive purpose. The cowshed is a non-profit organization. They are providing shelter to animals and treatment to sick animals. They are taking mass awakening program to prevent animal cruelty.

vcs-4419:
Colombia has approximately 60 million hectares of forest. Of these, 66% is located in the Amazon biome. The Forest and Carbon Monitoring System (SMByC) of the Institute of Hydrology, Meteorology and Environmental Studies (IDEAM), identified that in 2021, 174,103 ha of forest were deforested.
The name given to the Conservation Project is Project MATANI REDD+ DIOS MAYOR DE LOS PUEBLOS CABILLARI CONSERVACION ANCESTRAL, Matani is the Greatest God of the communities that make up the Association of Traditional Indigenous Captains of Vaupés (ACTIVA), made up of the communities of Altamira, Buenos aires, Cachiporro, Mutanacua, Villagladys, Cananari, Morroco, Reforma, Villareal. The Project MATANI REDD+ is located in the Department of Vaupes, corresponding to the Amazon biome of Colombia. Due to its biophysical conditions, this biogeographic zone is strategic for regulating the climate, sustaining biological cycles, conserving soil and water resources, capturing greenhouse gas emissions, and conserving the biological diversity of the region. Amazon region.
Therefore, the indigenous communities linked to the project seek, through their territorial autonomy and their right to free self-determination, to carry out conservation processes framed in sustainability criteria that have to do with the protection of natural forest areas, rescue and protection of their cultural identity and promotion of productive practices that promote the protection of biodiversity and the environmental richness of their territory.
Characteristics that are directly linked to the purpose of REDD+ projects, with the desired sustainable local development, as well as with the purpose of reducing emissions generated due to deforestation and forest degradation. The project MATANI REDD+ DIOS MAYOR DE LOS PUEBLOS CABILLARI CONSERVACION ANCESTRAL constitutes an area of 812,491 hectares.
The main objective of the project has been is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) in the Amazon rainforest.
vcs-442: The Project involves the capture and destruction of landfill gas from the Sussex County Landfill via an expanded gas collection and flaring system. The project is owned and operated by the Sussex County Municipal Utilities Authority (SCMUA). A pre-project landfill gas collection system was installed in Phase 1 of the Landfill in 1996 and expanded into Phase 2A in 2004. This system included on-site gas wells and piping, with landfill gas being delivered to a 1MW power generation plant located off site. The power generation plant is currently owned and operated by Lafayette Energy Partners LP (Lafayette), with whom SCMUA has had a gas sales agreement since January 2007. Landfill gas collected using the pre-project system and transported off site to generate electricity is not included within the scope of the Project.
vcs-4420:
MIR Global Enerji A.Ş. has constructed the Kayseri Biogas Plant Project. The aim of the project is to produce and supply electrical energy to the Turkish national grid.
By means of reducing dependency to the fossil fuels, environmental pollution is significantly reduced. Also, clean energy is generated by using animal manure as a source for biogas facility.
Within the scope of the project, MIR Global Enerji A.Ş constructed a biogas facility in Kocasinan District, Kayseri Province, Turkey. The facility has a capacity of 80,000 cattle, a slaughterhouse with a daily slaughter capacity of 500 and a biogas facility. The cattle manure processing capacity of the biogas plant is 2000 tons/day. Based on the applied tool, the project boundary is considered as the National Electricity Grid of Turkey. The baseline scenario refers to the energy generation from the fossil fuels.
The project includes 3 units in total as (3 x 1.540) MWm / (3 x 1.501) MWe with a total of 4.620 MWm/ 4.503 MWe. 
The first commissioning date of the project is 29/06/2021 for the first unit of 1.540 MWm / 1.501 MWe. The second commissioning date of the project is 27/04/2022 for the units 2 and 3 with the same capacities of 1.540 MWm / 1.501 MWe with a total of 3.080 MWm/ 3.002 MWe.
The total commissioned capacity is 4.620 MWm / 4.503 MWe
By avoiding the use of fossil fuels and using biogas as an energy source instead, greenhouse gas emission reductions can be achieved. Total annual electricity generation is 33,750 MWh for the installed units. As a result, total of 236,250 MWh electricity will be generated in a 7-year span between 30/06/2021 to 29/06/2028 with an average value of 33,750 MWh/year. According to this, the emission reduction is estimated around an average of 102,204 tCO2e annually. For the entire crediting period, total of 715,425 tonnes of CO2 is expected to be reduced in a total of 7 years
vcs-4421:
Within the scope of the project, Novantek Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş constructed a biogas facility in Odunpazarı District, Eskişehir Province, Turkey. Within the scope of the planned project, Organic wastes that will come to the Biogas Facility will be biodegraded in an anaerobic environment. The biogas that will be released during the biodegradation of organic wastes will be used for electricity, hot water and heat production in the cogeneration unit. The scope of the project will also include an organic fertilizer production facility with a capacity of 200 tons/day.
Based on the applied tool, the project boundary is considered as the National Electricity Grid of Turkey. The baseline scenario refers to the energy generation from the fossil fuels.
The project includes 2 units in total as (2 x 1.540) MWm / (2 x 1.501) MWe with a total of 3.080 MWm/ 3.002 MWe .
The first commissioning date of the project is 30/06/2021 for the first unit of 1.540 MWm / 1.501 MWe. The second commissioning date of the project is 11/08/2022 for the 2nd unit with the same capacities of 1.540 MWm / 1.501 MWe. These two commissioned units combine for a total of 3.080 MWm/ 3.002 MWe.
By avoiding the use of fossil fuels and using biogas as an energy source instead, greenhouse gas emission reductions can be achieved. Total annual electricity generation is 22,515 MWh, and a total of 157,605 MWh electricity will be generated in a 7-year span between 01/07/2021 to 30/06/2028. According to this, the emission reduction is estimated around an average of 64,670 tCO2e annually. For the entire crediting period, total of 452,688 tonnes of CO2 is expected to be reduced in a total of 7 years.

vcs-4423:
NEW HOPE AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Anhui Province (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduces 3 new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 3 existing swine farms in Bengbu City, Anhui Province, which are owned by WUHE NEW HOPE LIUHE ANIMAL HUSBANDRY Co. LTD (hereinafter called the project owner). Each subsidiary swine farm will install one AWMS. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The specific treatment process of these AWMSs are as follows: All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the organic fertilizers are distributed to local farmers for free, the rest will be sold in the local market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for heat generation, with surplus biogas destroyed through flaring systems (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around for free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 1216.08*104 m3 of biogas will be produced annually. The biogas will be captured and utilized for heat generation, the heat will be only used for the daily operation of the AWMSs and the 3 swine farms and will not be produced to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.

Investancia Brasil Ltda  (Investancia) is undertaking a Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) grouped reforestation project, known as Reflorestamento de Impacto no Brasil Project. The Project is planting pongamia (Pongamia pinnata) and other tree species in degraded pastures across Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil in areas that were cleared of native forests more than ten years prior to the projects’ start date. 
Investancia is developing a business model to establish pongamia as a regional commodity in a region where agriculture, other than cattle-ranching, is extremely difficult to make work. The focus of Investancia’s business is four-fold:

1) Production of reforestation oil;
2) Maintaining cattle or hay on silvopastoral lands with improved pastures;
3) Providing protein (i.e., feed) for cattle from the pongamia seedcake; and
4) Sequestering carbon dioxide in the pongamia trees (i.e., generate carbon offset credits).

To date, Investancia has established a nursery, explored the suitability of pongamia in the region, developed protocols, assessed various genetic strains of pongamia, and spoken with numerous local landowners about leasing land. The Reflorestamento de Impacto no Brasil Project will sequester carbon dioxide and generate GHG emission removals in the planted pongamia trees and in the soil following the reforestation of degraded pasture.
vcs-4435: The Cobram Estate Olives Regenerative Farming Project, developed by Carbon Friendly, is a pioneering initiative aiming to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the agricultural sector through the adoption of regenerative farming practices. vcs-4452:
The Asaga Amazonas REDD+ project is located in the state of Amazonas and is comprised of 470504 hectares , near the Apuí Conservation Unit Mosaic and the Campos Amazônicos National Park, as well as being surrounded by other settlement projects, reserves, and indigenous territories and at least one other REDD+ project. This diversity provides a great opportunity for the conservation and socioeconomic development of the region.

The Apuí Conservation Unit Mosaic is composed of nine conservation units, including four state forests (Sucunduri, Aripuanã, do Apuí, and Manicoré), two state parks (Guariba and Sucunduri), two sustainable development reserves (Bararati and Aripuanã), and the Guariba Extractive Reserve. Regarding the Campos Amazônicos National Park, it presents one of the most significant Cerrado enclaves within the Amazon Forest biome. One of the reasons it has great scientific potential is the presence of endemic species.

Due to the high density of biodiversity and the many unique species of flora and fauna, the conservation of this wild habitat is extremely important. Nevertheless, the involved municipalities rank high in deforestation and wildfires, as well as facing pressure from agricultural expansion, illegal logging, mining, construction of hydroelectric plants, roads, and land grabbing. 

The region has a variety of habitats, including upland forests, flooded forests, rocky fields, and savannas, as well as waterfalls and rapids that occur along the rivers, with a great diversity of species and landscapes.
vcs-4453:
The “Regenerate Outcomes Farming Project” developed by Regenerate Outcomes Ltd aims to support farms to transition away from intensive conventional modes of food production towards regenerative production systems via a mentoring and farm data services programme. As a result, the participating farms of this project implement several regenerative land management activities which reduce and remove GHG emissions.

Regenerate Outcomes Ltd (Regenerate Outcomes) is a registered company in the United Kingdom. Regenerate Outcomes is part of a global network bridging the gap between the finance and farming sectors. Regenerative agriculture presents opportunities to improve soil, plant and animal health, wider ecosystem processes, and the fundamental economics of farming.

“Regenerate Outcomes Farming Project - ROFP” is a grouped project with a project boundary of the UK; the project initially consists of 10 farms located in Northumberland (UK) seeking to move towards regenerative food production and better pasture and agricultural land management. The farm types range from upland (livestock only) to lowland mixed (arable and livestock) and arable-only. The project was inspired by the Environmental Impact Bonds (EIBs) pioneered in the US, such as the Forest Resilience Bond and Quantified Ventures’ Water Outcomes Funding in Washington and Ohio. 

The project seeks to provide four essential services to participating farms: 
i)	Data management, including baselining and monitoring of activities and ecological change, 
ii)	Funding support for capex requirements such as fencing and water infrastructure,
iii)	Mentoring and education from regenerative agriculture advisors, and 
iv)	Marketing and sales of environmental outcomes such as carbon bio-sequestration, biodiversity enhancement, and water quality improvements to downstream beneficiaries (payors). 

The project is developed as a grouped project.

The project of Kitchen and catering waste Disposal Phase II in Wuchang area (hereinafter
referred to as the Project), constructed by Wuhan Carbon Ring Ecology Co., Ltd. Biogas is
produced by anaerobic digestion of organic kitchen waste from MSW(municipal solid waste).
generating sets and boilers are used to generate electricity and steam, and a large amount
of waste heat is generated during operation, which can be used to heat the plant's
production process and also for heating the living area. The electricity generated will be
used for the electricity needs of the site, reducing the running costs of the project, and the

after approval by the relevant authorities, and the surplus electricity will be integrated into

replaces the equivalent power supply from the fossil fuel power plant-based power grid in

objective of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

vcs-4456: Agroforestry is a land use management system combining trees with crops or livestock on the same land. It is used for food production and environmental services. The project is located in Bangladesh and Chapainawabganj, Nogaon, and Rajshahi districts of Bangladesh are considered in the first instance. As we move forward, the benefits of horticulture-based agroforestry ecosystems will also be brought to other parts of the country. The main aim of the project activity includes the plantation of fruit-bearing trees on the farmlands of smallholder farmers. The agroforestry systems deliver several forest products, agriculture products, and ecosystem services which may enhance the social well-being of the local farmers and national and global community. The primary activity of the project is to onboard farmers who are practicing agroforestry plantations on their farmland. vcs-4457: The Tramontana ICS-01 project involves the distribution of up to 400,000 heavy-duty, energy-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS), free of cost through carbon finance, to indigenous communities across rural India that currently use traditional stoves such as mud clay and three-stone stoves. The project aims to directly and immediately enhance the health, well-being and livelihoods of these communities, and particularly of the women and children who are the most affected. vcs-4461: The REDD+ Tauari Forest Conservation Project is a partnership between Mata Nativa BR and MyCarbon and deals with the preservation of the Amazon rainforest in line with the traditions of local populations and the sustainable development of the region, through activities that will reduce greenhouse gas emissions that contribute to the increase of global warming. The project area is located in the northern region of Brazil, more specifically in the municipality of Tarauacá, state of Acre. The 126,157.8211 ha of tropical forests that are part of the project area are located in the Amazon biome. Avoiding a scenario of logging in 85% of the area, a truly sustainable economic activity was sought, which discards the suppression, even if authorized, of the existing vegetation, and also preserves the existing biodiversity in the glebe, with the cooperation of the local populations, through this project. The activities designed here aim to ensure that forest areas belonging to the project are preserved, continuing the important work of generating ecosystem services there, such as climate regulation, protection of water sources, maintenance of biodiversity and genetics heritage, among others, and also ensuring that 119,812,777.36 tons of CO2 are not released into the atmosphere.
vcs-4462: Forestal RioAquidaban (FRA) is a small-scale agroforestry reforestation project in Paraguay, combating deforestation by combining cattle keeping and sustainable timber production. It converts degraded grasslands into forests, halting soil and land degradation. Prior use of the area was extensive cattle farming.
vcs-4463:
The proposed ARR-VCS project is a large-scale grouped project centered on the reforestation of degraded lands in Australia. In the last 200 years, approximately 40% of Australia’s native forest cover has been lost due to human-induced land conversion. Today, much of the remaining native vegetation is highly fragmented. This grouped project aims for the long-term restoration of Australia’s forests, achieved through a mixture of direct seeding and seedling planting techniques to re-establish native flora and fauna, build ecological connectivity and reverse the deleterious impacts of land degradation. 

The project is managed by Land Life, a tech-driven reforestation company that plants trees at scale to restore degraded ecosystems globally in hubs like Europe, the US and Australia and maintains an on-the-ground presence in Australia, and collaborates closely with local partners and authorities. Local partner Cassinia Environmental brings on-the-ground expertise in forestry and conservation, supporting Land Life’s team of reforestation specialists in managing and implementing quality projects in Australia.

Project activities are implemented and monitored according to approved large scale project methodology AR-ACM0003, with more project instances to be added over the coming years (up to well over 10,000 ha expected). The first set of project instances covers 706.65 ha of degraded land across Australia, at 4 distinct planting sites: Morrl Morrl (Victoria), Moolagundi (New South Wales), Killongbutta (New South Wales), and Hillridge (South Australia). The project expects to establish 474,407 trees and to sequester at least 196,837 tCO2e over a project crediting period of 100 years. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals over the first 43 years is 4,578 tCO2e.
vcs-4464: The proposed project will divert approximately 27,713 tonnes of food waste and 24,910 tonnes of brown waste from Mwakirunge landfill over a seven-year period. These volumes of waste would collectively emit an estimated 38,000 net tonnes CO2e from methane emissions over a seven-year crediting period if they were to decompose in Mwakirunge landfill. Instead, Biobuu Kenya, Ltd. (“Biobuu”) will contract with local markets, hotels, port operators, and waste collection companies to transport the waste to its facility in nearby Mawamba, Kenya (about 22 km north of Mombasa). Biobuu will feed the food waste to Black Soldier Fly (“BSF”; Hermetia illucens) larvae over several days before processing the larvae processed into animal feed. Greenhouse gas emissions from BSF feeding and growth are assumed to be de minimis by enterologists. Any brown waste included in the food waste (e.g., mango pits) is then composted in windrows on-site, along with the separately collected brown waste. Both the animal feed and the compost are sold to farmers. In addition to creating valuable agricultural products, the project activities will avoid the 38,000 net tonnes CO2e in methane emissions.
vcs-4467:
TSH Grouped Biogas Recovery Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is a grouped project which consists of biogas recovery projects located in Indonesia. The project is owned by TSH Resources Sdn Bhd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner), and implementation of the projects are by the individual plant operators of each PAI (project activity instance).

The purpose of this Grouped Project is to recover the biogas generated from the wastewater (with or without sludge) treatment process which would have otherwise, be emitted into the atmosphere resulting in GHG emissions. 

The recovered biogas is expected to be utilized for (a) electricity generation for own consumption, and (b) upgrading of biogas for transportation, and/or (c) upgrading of biogas and bottling for distribution to end user, and/or distributing to natural gas distribution grid, and with the option of flaring for any excess quantity.
vcs-4468: The proposed project adopts composting to treat organic waste. Composting is a process by which organic wastes are broken down by microorganisms, generally bacteria and fungi, into simpler forms. The microorganisms use the carbon in the waste as an energy source. The degradation of the nitrogen- containing materials results in the breakdown of the original materials into a much more uniform product which can be used as a soil amendment. Heat generated during the process kills many unwanted organisms such as weed seeds and pathogens. Advantages of composting include reduction of waste volume, elimination of heat- killed pests, and the generation of a beneficial and marketable material. Adding compost to soil increases organic matter content. This, in turn, improves many soil characteristics and allows for the slow release of nutrients for crop use in subsequent years.
vcs-4469: Zonguldak Landfill Gas to Electricity Project is located at Zonguldak Landfill Site in Sofular Neighborhood, Central District, Zonguldak Province Turkey. The project is owned by Arel Yenilenebilir Enerji Teknolojileri ve Elektrik Üretimi Ltd. Şti. vcs-447: The project activity under consideration entails generation of clean power by harnessing wind energy – a non-conventional renewable energy resource and export of the electricity generated to the Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) and Hubli Electricity Supply Company Limited (HESCOM) on the basis of Power Purchase Agreements. The electricity exported from the project to the grid thereby replaces an equivalent amount of power generation at the grid connected power plants which are primarily fossil fuel based. The project activity is a bundled wind energy project with total capacity of 12.5 MW, comprising of Ten Wind Turbine Generators (WTG’s) of varying capacities.

vcs-4473:
Karidja project consists in restoring 70,000 ha of the Haut Sassandra gazetted Forest (102,400 ha) in Côte d’Ivoire. This forest has lost over 95% of its original cover in less than 30 years.
Restoration activities are based on both assisted natural regeneration and plantation of a very diversified mix of native species, the overall aim is the permanent re-establishment of a largely natural and largely intact tropical rainforest.
Agroforestry schemes are implemented around the restored forest (over 30,000 ha) to ensure sources of sustainable livelihoods to local populations, contributing to the long-term success of the project.
Karidja project includes an important package to support sustainable economic transition, social infrastructures improvement and trainings for locals to provide long term social co-benefits.
vcs-4474:
The “Santa Nicolasa North Patagonia Regenerative Grazing Project” aims to stop and reverse the historic soil degradation process of the region by implementing regenerative grazing technics by restoring the ecological condition of ~70.000 hectares of rangeland soils on Santa Nicolasa farm. Regenerative grazing activities can increase SOC concentrations, improve natural growing grasses, decrease bare soil, and improve water infiltration, among others. An average amount of 0,4% of Soil Organic Matter, is expected to increase, which results in a net GHG emissions reduction and removals of ~ 1,400,000 tCO2e in the SOC pool, with an annual average of 71,000 tCO2e in 20 years of the project. 
In general terms, the regenerative grazing activities restrict the cattle to relatively small paddocks to generate intensive grazing in short periods, followed by long grazing resting periods. As a result, a homogeneous disturbance on all the forage species is generated, avoiding the selectivity of the cattle for the most palatable plants. This technique requires the installation of new fencing and watering infrastructure and a significant adaptation of management practices. 
The project contributes to sustainable development by promoting an integrated management scheme with the ecosystem in privately owned land, avoiding carbon emissions and restoring native ecosystems from a degradation process together with the continuity of sustainable food production; promoting sustainable practices along the region, generating labor demand from the local population, and making improvements in infrastructure; generating knowledge on current SOC concentrations data and monitoring the effects of regenerative grazing management in the region; developing and improving a new mechanism to finance projects in the sustainable livestock production sector; the conservation of a unique ecosystem, that despite the severe degradation, still conserves the original land use and the natural ecosystem structure.
vcs-4475:
Kijani Forestry is a social enterprise founded in 2019, located in Uganda. Kijani’s mission is to empower smallholder farmers to generate income and combat climate change through the establishment of sustainable wood lots. As of 2022, Kijani has planted over 5 million trees with over 8,000 farmers throughout northern Uganda. Kijani works in partnership with local communities, government agencies, international non-governmental agencies, universities, and other stakeholders to implement sustainable land use practices and agroforestry management systems. Through these partnerships, Kijani aims to build capacity and establish a foundation for sustainable development in Uganda through growing trees that provide income-generating opportunities for farmers. 
Kijani works through a network of thousands of organized small groups across Uganda to establish small-scale nurseries, train farmers in nursery management, and mobilize farmers to establish fuelwood lots on their private land. Kijani’s unique approach addresses many of the barriers faced by rural farmers who wish to plant trees; Kijani provides all inputs needed for a productive tree nursery, including properly sourced seeds, potting bags, equipment for maintenance, and materials needed to care for seedlings. Kijani’s field staff are stationed in the communities full-time, and provide regular training to groups on nursery establishment and maintenance, seedling care, pest management, agroforestry practices, and fuelwood lot establishment and management. At any given moment, a Kijani staff member is no more than a bicycle ride away from a Kijani nursery. Kiiani’s continuous presence, and strong relationships, in the community is critical to the long-term success of the project. In addition to its reforestation efforts, Kijani provides training and support to communities to help them establish sustainable forest management practices and create economic opportunities through various forest products.
vcs-4476: The Grouped Project Sul da Bahia falls under the Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) category and targeting the following Verra certifications: Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standard (CCB). The project aims to restore forest formations that are diminished due to the expansion of other land use practices such as overgrazing on extensive cattle ranches, intensive agriculture and silviculture systems. The grouped project is located in the Atlantic Forest biome in the state of Bahia (Brazil). Restoration is attained through forestation activities using native and non-native species. Project activities also include harvesting and establishing agroforestry systems to diversify and maximize project benefits for all parties and communities involved. The overarching goal of the project is to create a biodiverse forest cover that combines carbon capture, biodiversity and community impacts with a diversity of economic functions such as sustainable production of crops and forest products.
vcs-4477:
The proposed project activity aims to reduce the electricity consumption by replacing sodium vapor street lamps with energy efficient LED street lights. The implementation of the proposed project activity will reduce the energy required for street lighting network in various areas of municipality Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh State of India. The proposed project activity will be implemented by Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam and will install energy efficient LED street lights in
Ghaziabad.
The sodium vapor street lights consume comparatively more electricity as they need heat to glow. Also, sodium lamps have the worst color rendering of any bulb as they produce dark yellow glow which is generally a very low-quality light. On the other hand, LED street lights can provide an incredibly better variety of high color rendering index options. The implementation of the proposed project activity will thus enable the municipality to consume considerably less amount of electricity dur to better energy efficiency of the LED lamps.
vcs-4478:
The project activity is a grouped project activity promoted by Nagar Nigam Ghaziabad (hereinafter also called as “NNG”). As number of existing solid waste disposal near metros and urban/semi urban cities in host country, NNG envisage to promotes the waste treatment using alternate method that is composting. NNG envisage to contribute towards sustainable development and helping to meet the host country targets to increase MSW treatment penetration level. The project instances under the grouped project will be located in Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, India.

The NNG has planned to establish composting facilities in various location within Nigam, the 4 composting plant already commissioned with installed capacity 735TPD and rest are under commissioning.
vcs-4480: The Bajo Baudó Mangroves REDD++ Project is in the Pacific region in the department of Chocó, Colombia. It limits to the north with the municipality of Nuquí, to the south with the municipality of Medio Baudó, to the east with the municipality of Atrato and to the west with the Pacific Ocean. The project area is collectively owned by 5 Community Councils, which are Cuevita (R 2701/Dec 21, 2001), Pavasa (R 2695/Dec 21, 2001), Villa María de Purrichá (R 1129/May 23, 2000), Virudó (R 2698/Dec 21, 2001) and San Agustín de Terrón (R 3369/Dec 21, 2000). Although the total titled area for the 5 councils is 73,611 ha, the project area is 62,212 ha, which overlaps 51% with the DMRI Encanto de los Manglares del Bajo Baudó Management District, created through the agreement 008 of 2017. The (DRMI) is a Protected Area category that decentralizes the power of the environmental authority and allows decision-making by the communities that inhabit it. With the management of the area, new models of social and environmental territorial management have been created, however, there are several challenges in terms of governance and conservation of ecosystems. Through the DMRI declaration, sustainable management agreements have been reached with the communities and joint restoration and monitoring actions have been developed with the participation of other key institutional actors. The project area overlaps with two important ecosystems, mangrove forest (19.88% of the total project area), with an estimated average reserve of 800 tCO2e/ha, and Basal humid forest (80.12% of the total project area), with an estimated average reserve of 604 tCO2e/ha. The drivers of deforestation in the baseline have been due to the implementation of coconut crops, subsistence crops, crops for illicit use, and livestock; the drivers of degradation have been selective logging, illegal mining, fishing, and indiscriminate housing. The main objective of the project is: Reduce GHG emissions due to forest degradatio.
vcs-4481:
The Restore Africa: Restoring trees and livelihoods project in Kenya aims to restore the land and livelihoods of vulnerable small-scale farming households on private land and community-owned conservancies in the Kitui and Baringo counties in Kenya . This initiative, using appropriate, sustainable agriculture, forestry and agroforestry practices will enhance the sequestration of carbon and result in greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions. The integration of livelihood interventions, landscape restoration, and carbon sequestration will support climate-vulnerable communities to build resilience and adapt to climate change.
The proposed project activities will encompass afforestation, reforestation and revegetation, including direct (e.g., manual planting, broadcast seeding) and indirect (e.g., herbivory exclosures, coppicing, pollarding) activities that facilitate natural regeneration. The project will facilitate sustainable food production, enhance the functioning of ecosystems and to increase carbon storage in the landscape through the scaling up of nature-based restoration activities, including the establishment and regeneration of approximately 2.1 million trees. This will improve the livelihoods and resilience of estimated 30,000 households while restoring about 32,500 hectares in Baringo and Kitui counties. Any project intervention or activity will not compromise but rather enhance livelihoods of individual and community land holders. These activities are expected to sequester at least 1,300,000 tCO2e over a 30-year period. The Global Evergreening Alliance (GEA) program will work.
The Global Evergreening Alliance acts as project proponent. The lead implementing organisation is the International Centre for Research in Agroforestry working together with implementation partners Self Help Africa and Adventist Development and Relief Agency.
vcs-4482:
Lushan MSW Incineration Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in the industry park of Lushan County which is located in the West side of Guogou Village, Zhangliang Town, Lushan County, Pingdingshan City, Pingdingshan City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Lushan Capital Environment Energy Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the project owner).
The project will treat 600 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of one 600t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 12MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 219,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 130 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work 7,446 hours every year, generating 77,934.1 MWh electricity, of which 63,905.9 MWh will be exported to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The implementation of the project will meet the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also, the project fits the priority development sector of integrated utilization of resource and energy saving of China, and helps reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil-fuel fired plants and MSW treatment at landfill.
The project started construction in 08 July, 2019 and put into operation on 07 October 2021. It is estimated that during the 10-year fixed crediting period of the project (from 07 October 2021 to 06 October 2031), the average annual GHG emission reductions will be 60,883 tCO2e. The total amount of emission reductions is expected to be 608,829 tCO2e during the 10-year fixed crediting period.
vcs-4483: Inner Mongolia Hinggan League Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Horqin Right Front Banner and Jalaid Banner  under the administration of Hinggan League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China. The project aims to restore 42,330.93 hectares (or 634,964 Mu) degraded grasslands by adopting a variety of measures including seeding, fencing and sustainable grazing management. The project will increase carbon sequestration, reverse grassland degradation, contribute to local development and preserve cultural traditions.
vcs-4485: Forest conservation at the BRArbo property, located in the municipalities of Juruá, Jutaí and Carauari, State of Amazonas. Forest conservation will be achieved through a combination of sustainable forest management in an area of 130,641 ha and surveillance in the remaining area of the project, of 543,721 ha. vcs-4486: The proposed project activity is a greenfield, grid connected solar PV based electricity generation project, located in the Least Developed Country (UNCTAD) of Malawi, Africa. The purpose of this project is to provide clean energy to the local power grid as per design specifications and bolster renewable energy penetration in the relatively remote areas of Malawi, thereby improving energy access. It is configured as a single instance of project activity and is not a grouped project.
vcs-4487:
Guangxi Baiduoshou Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) introduced a set of organic fertilizers production lines with an annual output of 25,050 tons to treat the manure from the chicken farms and Biomass waste residue i.e., straw in Tiandeng county, Chongzuo city, Guangxi Province. The project is invested and owned by Guangxi Baiduoshou Biotechnology Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass waste residue. In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.
This project was designed to treat the chicken manure and biomass waste residue (straw) to produce organic fertilizer. This project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system. It is estimated that approximately 80,000 tonnes of manure and 10,500 tonnes of biomass waste residue can be treated annually, therefore total 90,500 tonnes of waste can be composted aerobically for this project. the collected chicken manure will be utilized through a fermentation composting process. After the fermentation, both solids and wastewater are then treated by a fertilizer production system, of which can produce organic fertilizers used for application to lands.
vcs-4488: The project aims to address widespread land and agro-ecosystem degradation and climate-change related hazards across the landscapes of Rulindo and Bugesera districts in northern and eastern provinces of Rwanda respectively. The project will undertake a number of activities including: 1) planting of around four million functional tree species on both smallholders’ farm plots and public suitable lands to restore degraded ecosystems, protect watersheds, sequester carbon, conserve biodiversity, and provide farmers with a diversified income streams, e.g., from fruits and timber; 2) establishing seedling nurseries to provide quality materials for tree planting 3) provide trainings to enhance knowledge to a wide range of key stakeholders, including farmer groups, the youth, community advisors, Community Extension Officers, nursery managers, project’s staff, etc. 4) promoting specific livelihoods activities, e.g., horticulture package, livestock husbandry, Village-based Savings & Loan Associations (VSLA), local investments, etc.; 5) facilitating market access for farmers products/produce by encouraging farmers to organize into cooperatives/ other community structures, and when possible, entering into supply agreements with off-takers; 6) engaging farmers in sustainability agreements - committing them to sustain the implementation of the project activities for the long-term, beyond the project’s crediting period (≥20 years). The project activities aim to address this land and agro-ecosystem degradation and directly contribute to climate mitigation through increased carbon storage in tree biomass and in soils within the agricultural landscapes. The new VERRA’s Verified Carbon Standard carbon methodology called Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation Projects will be used. The ex-ante annual average GHG emission reductions of the project are estimated at 117,565 tCO2e, and total GHG emission reductions over 20 years are estimated at 2,351,302 tCO2e.
vcs-4489:
Riwne Oblast Forest Preservation Project (Conversion of logged to protected forest) (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Rivne Oblast by “Denmak” TOV, the geo-coordinates of the project are latitude 50.971019 and Longitude 27.027294, the total project area is 13,374.21
ha, which is the area in which the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests was implemented in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The forest in the project consists of coniferous forest, the predominant tree species is Pinus Sylvestris.
If it were not for the implementation of the project activity, the trees would be logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber harvest and management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity conserves the carbon stock in the protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions by about 8,930,874 tCO2e over the span of 30 years. The average annual emission reduction is 297,696 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 6,787,464 tCO2e over 30 years, while the average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 226,249 tCO2e.
The project activity contributes to the preservation and protection of the natural environment (biodiversity conservation and soil erosion control), thus contributing to the sustainable development goals of the United Nations.
vcs-449: The proposed project activity involves the installation of an anaerobic wastewater treatment facility with methane capture, based on the Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket (UASB) technology. vcs-4490:
Maodeng Pasture Improved Grassland Management Project (hereinafter as “the project”) is located in Xilin Hot City, Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China. The Xilin Hot City geographic coordinates of the project zone are 115 °16′~117°13′E and 43°02′~44°52′N and borders Abaga Banner in the west, Zhenglan Banner in the south, Xiwu Banner and Chifeng City in the east, and Dongwu Banner in the north.
The main objective of the project is to implement sustainable grassland management measures for 10,533.33 hectares of degraded grassland through seeding, grazing prohibition and fertilization. These measures improved grassland productivity, restored vegetation, significantly increased vegetation coverage, improved biodiversity in degraded grasslands, increased the proportion of superior pasture, improved soil fertility, and enhanced the stability of grassland ecosystems.
According to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, due to the impact of climate change and human activities, the grassland in this area has been facing varying degrees of degradation, sandification, and sparse vegetation.
The total scale of the project is 10,533.33 hectares. Strictly ban grazing on all plots within the project area for the first five years after the completion of the project and, after five years, adopt sustainable grassland management methods according to the actual grassland restoration situation, such as rotational grazing in different pastoral areas, limits the time and number of grazing in the project area to protect the natural grassland resources, curb the deterioration of the ecological environment of the natural grassland.
vcs-4492:
Qixian MSW Incineration Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Dongguan Village, Chengguan Town, Qixian County, Kaifeng City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Qixian Capital Environment Energy Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the project owner).
The project will treat 600 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of one 600t/d mechanical grate incinerator,   matched with one set of 12MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 219,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 150 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work 7,446 hours every year, generating 74,534.5 MWh electricity, of which 61,118.3 MWh will be exported to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The implementation of the project will meet the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also, the project fits the priority development sector of integrated utilization of resource and energy saving of China, and helps reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil-fuel fired plants and MSW treatment at landfill. By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the project avoids the emissions of methane that would be generated under landfill condition.
