The project started construction on 18 December, 2019 and put into operation on 08 December, 2021. It is estimated that during the 10-year fixed crediting period of the project, the average annual GHG emission reductions will be 53,361 tCO2e.
vcs-4493: Varanasi Smart City Bio-Conversion Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is a Biogas recovery and utilization project, collects manure waste of dairy cow from surrounding livestock farms, as well as press-mud from nearby agricultural lands by building a centralized anaerobic waste treatment system and utilizes animal manure and press-mud as ferment material to produce biogas. Gobardhan Varanasi Foundation SPV (hereafter referred to as the project proponent) has set up biogas plant in village Shahanshahpur of Varanasi district In Uttar Pradesh State of India. The project is expected to produce 90m3 biogas per day. The biogas produced is recovered and combusted in the auxiliary equipment of the project’s anaerobic waste treatment system and the organic fertilizer plant. The residual waste from the CSTR digesters is used to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
vcs-4494: This project focuses on diverting a significant amount of different paper grades from landfills throughout California through recycling. For this project specifically, the focus is carboard, or OCC (old corrugated carboard). Our company consistently recycles 120,000 tons of OCC per year on average. As a result, this large quantity of tonnage is not ending up in landfills across California.Trees absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as they grow, a process called carbon sequestration and when they’re cut down that carbon is released back into the atmosphere. Per EPA standards, by recycling 120,000 tons of paper per year, we save 2,040,000 trees (17 trees saved per every ton of paper recycled). Not only that, but we also save 6,072,000 gallons of oil, 64,129,200 hours of electricity and 192,150,000 gallons of water per 120,000 tons of paper we recycle which is further beneficial for the environment. Moreover, recycling one ton of paper on average eliminates 3.3 metric tons of carbon dioxide from being released into the atmosphere. Our estimate is that by recycling 120,000 tons of paper per year, we are eliminating 396,000 tons of carbon dioxide from being released into the atmosphere. Additionally, we are preventing 3,060,000 tons of carbon dioxide from being released into the atmosphere through the tree saving efforts associated with paper recycling. Therefore, we estimate that in total, we prevent 3,456,000 tons of carbon dioxide from being released per year. Prior to the implementation of our project, millions of metric tons of carbon dioxide were being released into the atmosphere which we have since eliminated.
vcs-4495:
Working Trees grows trees where the interests of farmers and the climate overlap. 

The agricultural benefits of incorporating trees into active pastureland or hayland –, known as “silvopasture” or “alley cropping”,  respectively; collectively referred to as “silvopasture” –, include reduced livestock mortality, minimized heat stress, improved soil health, increased hay yield, improved water retention and infiltration. At the same time, planting trees on pastureland or hayland has been identified as the largest agricultural climate solution for carbon sequestration.

Despite these benefits, adoption has remained low due in part to high up-front costs and the multi-year delay between planting and benefits. Revenue from carbon credits presents an opportunity to overcome this imbalance. Financing from carbon markets affords farmers the opportunity to profit from sustainability enhancements and environmental services.

However, the methods used today for tree-based sequestration have mainly been accessible to large landowners. In the United States this means small landowners – who own 90% of farms and 50% of farmland – get left behind in the green economy. 

Working Trees innovative new approach to carbon-credit-supported silvopasture allows landowners of all sizes to start planting trees and reap the benefits of this practice through three key strategies: 
1. Streamlined eligibility and carbon measurement through a phone application
2. Guaranteed offtake of the generated carbon credits
3. Target geography spanning the Eastern US

The project activity aims to treat the manure and wastewater from the 2 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.

The objective of the Amazon Partners (AP) 20 Project is to originate -with the characteristics of a REDD+ initiative (Reduction of Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation), following the Project Cycle of the VM0015 Methodology for Avoided Unplanned Deforestation, v1.1 Methodology. Thus, such Verified Carbon Units (VCU) may, in the future, be accounted for in Brazil's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) Emission Reductions efforts, in the framework of the Paris Climate Agreement, as much as they are negotiated between different parties, within the framework of the voluntary markets for carbon credit negotiations.

The Project will avoid Greenhouse Gas Emissions at the Territory of Indigenous Peoples of the Shawadawa Association, in the municipality of Porto Walter, in the State of Acre, Amazon Biome of the Brazilian Territory. Liyang 15 MW Low-concentration CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Liyang coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the North China Power Grid. Waste heat
generated by the gas power generators will be utilized for heat supply to the coal mine. The Project is located in South Liyang Village, Liyang Township, Heshun County, Jinzhong City, Shanxi Province, China. The project owner is Beijing Yonder Environmental Energy Technology Co., Ltd. Prior to the implementation of the Project, Liyang coal mine was equipped with CMM extraction facilities and all extracted CMM was vented into the atmosphere directly; equivalent amount of electricity was provided by all power plants connecting to NCPG and the heat was provided by gas-fired boilers. The baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. 24 sets of CMM gas generators and one set of steam turbine generator will be installed to generate with a total installed capacity of 15MW （20*0.6MW+4*0.5MW+1MW), destroying 25.5 million Nm3 of methane annually. After the full operation of the Project, the expected annual exported electricity will be 77,550 MWh, which will be supplied to the NCPG. The waste heat from generators is recovered by waste heat boilers, and saturated steam from waste heat boilers will be supplied to the steam turbine to produce electricity, surplus saturated steam will be supplied to the coal mine to replace part of the heat generated by the gas-fired boilers. To be conservative, emission reductions will not be claimed for heat supply. It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the Project (from 01-March-2022 to 29-February-2032), the expected average annual GHG emission reductions will be 484,446 tCO2.

This grouped project consists of planting Macaúba trees (Acrocomia aculeata) within agrosilvopastoral systems on non-forestland (primarily degraded pastureland) in the Vale do Paraíba region in São Paulo State, Brazil. 

Macaúba is a native palm tree that is drought and disease tolerant and uses 70% less water than the common commercial African palm, while still producing fruits that can be processed into commercial palm oil products (e.g. pulp and kernel oil, livestock fodder, biofuel, and fertilizer). 

The Vale do Paraíba region, located within the Atlantic Forest biome, is characterized by abundant biodiversity and endemism in its original form. However, due to extensive land-use changes that occurred over the centuries, it now exists in a fragmented state. Extensive low-productivity cattle grazing is currently the dominant land management regime in the project region. Cultivating Macaúba on those lands has the potential to slow soil erosion, store carbon in tree biomass, regulate the micro-climate, and promote biodiversity. The integration of Macaúba palm trees with cattle grazing and cropland will diversify and increase  income to local farming and ranching communities without displacing commercial or subsistence activities.  Whenever possible, the plantings will connect forest fragments to create ecological corridors that promote flux of genes through migration, dispersal, linkage and interrelation of populations of wild flora and fauna, all of which are important to biodiversity.

This project has the potential to remove on average 42,396 tCO2e annually throughout the project crediting period, with an estimated total of 847,925 tCO2e over the twenty-year crediting period in the form of aboveground and belowground tree biomass and soil organic carbon.
vcs-451: The project activity consists of the construction of a new small hydro power plant with 29.3 MW total installed capacity and a reservoir of 2.87 km². The plant is being installed in the Midwest region of Brazil, in Rio do Sangue (river). Small hydro in Brazil must have installed capacity between 1 MW and 30 MW and reservoir area less than 3 km², or, if the area is between 3 km² and 13 km², it should have a minimum environmental impact. The Carbon Program by AGROROBÓTICA aims the recovery of degraded pasture and crops by adopting and maintaining several climate-smart agriculture practices and considering the specificity of each Brazilian biome: Amazon Forest, Cerrado, Caating, Atlantic Forest, Pampa, and Pantanal. In advance, it is expected to increase the sustainability of this sector and raising the life standards in rural areas. The reductions and removal of GHG emissions expected to be achieved would not have taken place without it. As this is a grouped project, as defined by the VCS standard, it includes multiple growers with multiple enrolled fields. The estimate is that the project could promote a GHG emission reduction and removal of up 2,624,400 tCO2eq promoted by more than 2,000,000 ha, in the next 20 years. The carbon credit payments will provide an additional source of income to help farmers to implement sustainable practices and improve the livelihoods of their communities.
This project is an agricultural GHG emission reduction and removal project using the methodology “VM0042: Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management”, v. 2.0 and the AGLIBS ® Artificial Intelligence (AI) Platform, which is specifically addressed to fulfil the need for a high-integrity and cost-efficient monitoring system (MRV- measurable, reportable, and verifiable) through the emerging technology LIBS.  The overall objective will be achieved by supporting farmers to adopt and maintain climate-smart agricultural practices through agronomic support and the monitoring of soil carbon stock change inside the farm boundary. The primary goal is to promote a range of regenerative agricultural land management practice improvements targeted to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and reduce net emissions of CO2, CH4, and N2O from grower operations and degraded pasture area, increase farm resilience to extreme weather and climate change, and enhance yield, improve soil quality, and reduce GHG emissions.

The current geographic area is composed of 11 private forest parcels located in the counties of, Buzău, Dâmbovița, with future instances to be located in Arges, Prahova, and Teleorman. vcs-4513:
The Project aims to protect the native forest socio-ecosystems of the Argentine Gran Chaco ecoregion. The Grouped Project will seek to reduce planned deforestation and unplanned deforestation and degradation pressures by encouraging landowners granted with large-scale agricultural and livestock production deforestation permits to set aside their land for conservation and forest regeneration. It will also implement a combination of environmental and social activities aimed at improving the livelihoods of community members living in the vicinity of the project area as well as the enhancement of the forest and biodiversity.
In Argentina, deforestation has accelerated over the past 40 years as the country's agricultural frontier has expanded, resulting in one of the highest deforestation rates in the world. This expansion of the agricultural frontier is having a major impact on native ecosystems and their biodiversity. At the same time, deforestation and land enclosure have altered the livelihoods of many indigenous and/or peasant communities who use large areas of the Forest for their activities.
For the first Project Activity Instance the project proponent, VISTA Energy, purchased part of the El Chaguaral farm (4.892 hectares) in the current boundary of the agricultural frontier. The former owner of the property had a clearing permit to transform the land for agricultural and livestock purposes. VISTA will not make use of that permit. The activities to achieve this include fencing, hiring responsible field staff to monitor the property, and developing and implementing a biodiversity conservation plan together with an action plan for fire prevention, warning and response will be implemented. Also assisted natural regeneration and enrichment planting activities will be implemented.The initial activity instance is estimated to generate ≈ 983,460 tCO2e net GHG emissions reductions and removals (≈49,173. tCO2 e per year for 20 years)
vcs-4514: M/s S&P Feeders Pvt. Ltd., Maharashtra is setting up a 20 TPD Poultry Litter to Energy plant at Thengode village, Nashik District in Maharashtra. The proposed project activity is a step towards supporting the implementation of poultry waste to Energy production facility in India, through the production of Biogas. The project site is home to approximately 175,000 birds, resulting in a daily production of around 22,000 kg of poultry litter. The close proximity of the proposed land to the farm eliminates the need for transportation, ensuring a continuous and uninterrupted supply of raw material. The poultry litter is treated anaerobically in the KVIC Floating Dome Digester, producing about 1,400 m3 of biogas per day with a calorific value of 4,700 to 5,400 kcal per cubic meter. The high-efficiency biogas engine and generator installed will generate 175 kWh of electricity per hour, while also yielding a bio-organic slurry/manure with high NPK content, totaling 55,000 liters or 6,600 kg per day

The Qitai Shuifa Improved Grassland Management Project is located in Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture is located at the northern foot of the Tianshan Mountains and the southeastern edge of the Junggar Basin. Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture borders Hami City to the east, Shihezi City to the west, Turpan City and Bayingolin Mongolian Autonomous Prefecture to the south, Tacheng and Altay Prefecture to the north, and Mongolia to the northeast. The project aims to restore local degraded grassland ecosystems by rest grazing on degraded grasslands, increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local development by introducing sustainable grazing and managing grasslands.
Totally, 64,391.13 ha of degraded grassland have been managed scientifically by rest grazing. Rest grazing requires that adopting sustainable grassland management methods, such as rotational grazing in different pastoral areas, limits the time and number of grazing in the project
area to protect the natural grassland resources, curb the deterioration of the ecological environment of the natural grassland.
In general, rest grazing is implemented in slightly degraded areas (the total grass yield decreasedby 30%-50% compared with that before degradation). In addition to this main restoration measure, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restores grassland vegetation through grassland management measures to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity, supplemented by daily management measures of other protection projects, such as grassland fire prevention and rodent control, so as to ensure long-term sustainable management of the project area. project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 5,400,253 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 180,008 tCO2e.

vcs-4524:
ARC Ride is implementing a Carbon Credit project based on the VCS methodology VM0038, which focuses on EV charging systems. Electrify Africa tracks CO2 emissions avoided, through the use of ARC Ride’s eMCs instead of petrol MC equivalents. The project focuses on the charging of ARC Ride's eMC batteries through a network of L2 Battery Swap Charging Stations in Africa, starting in Nairobi, Kenya.

ARC Ride's charging stations are designed to accommodate up to 11 batteries at a time and operate as 6.8 kW chargers using 240-volt grid electricity. The EC by the charging stations is measured through on-site metres, while the distance travelled by the eMCs is tracked using telematics systems, providing real-time primary data for monitoring and verification. The batteries are rechargeable at the dedicated charging stations and can only be swapped between eMC clients, enhancing mobility.

The project incorporates design features to prevent the use of batteries' kWh for non-transportation purposes, but applies conservative measures regarding the kWh sourced from external charging locations not owned by ARC Ride. Only kWhs sourced from ARC Ride's battery swap charging stations are included in the carbon credit calculations.

The project demonstrates eligibility for carbon credits in the LDV sector and utilises L2 chargers for the eMCs. Kenya's low market penetration of eMCs and EVs overall justifies the geographic additionality of the project. Customised factors for the MPG baseline are developed, taking into account peer-reviewed studies on fossil fuel motorcycles' MPG in Nairobi.

ARC Ride's charging stations are associated with on-site renewables, and the emission factor is calculated as a weighted average of the Kenyan national grid EFkw and the zero-carbon EFkw from on-site renewables. The project incorporates smart metering and telematics systems to measure kWh consumption and estimate baseline emissions accurately.

The Republic of the Congo Improved Forest Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “The project”) is located in UFA Djua-Ikié, The Republic of the Congo. It is implemented by Société d’Exploitation Foresrière Yuan Dong (hereinafter referred to as “SEFYD”) as the project proponent. The project is to protect the forest that was planned to be logged.
UFA Djua-Ikié is located in the Souanké and Semé Districts of the Sangha administrative Province. The project is designed to improve forest management in 338,589 ha of native Congolese forests legally designated for logging. By avoiding previously planned logging and implementing improved forest management and conservation activities, this project will increase the carbon stock through protecting the forest.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the forests in the project area were harvested following the guidelines in Timber Harvest Plan approved by the local forestry authority. In order to protect the forest ecosystem, improve the ecological environment, increase carbon sinks, reduce GHG emission reductions and slow down climate change, the project proponent decided to stop the logging and implement this improved forest management project activities from 01-August-2020 to 31-July-2040.
The project is expected to generate approximately 53,140,400 tCO2e during the 20 years’ crediting period, with the annual emission reductions of 2,657,020 tCO2e.
The project’s climate, community and biodiversity objectives:
⚫ Reduce GHG emissions and mitigate climate change; and
⚫ Improve soil and water conservation and contribute to sustainable development; and
⚫ Provide experience of forest management and risk prevention and control for local stakeholders; and
⚫ Improvement of the biodiversity and ecological environment of the project area and its surrounding area; and
⚫ Increase employment opportunities and raise the income level of local residents; and
⚫ Protect the local tree species from being cutting down.

The proposed project will introduce and adopt Trinetra as an organic waste decomposer to treat animal manure and agricultural waste. The proposed project is intended to solve environmental issues brought on by improper disposal of these wastes. The project activity will help reduce greenhouse gas (methane) emissions by controlled, aerobic decomposition of agricultural wastes, focusing on cow dung and agricultural residues in this phase. The project thus generates carbon credits from controlled, aerobic treatment of animal (cow) dung and agricultural waste. The project locations are in the state of Gujarat. The project will sell around 1,139 tonnes of Trinetra over a ten-year fixing crediting period, leading to an emission reduction of about 2.42 million metric tCO2e. The electricity generated by the proposed project will than dis-place part of the electricity generated by North West China Grid which is dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants: an annual average emission reduction of 764,452 tCO2eq is therefore estimated to occur with the proposed project.
vcs-4530: MatchBack Systems Inc. is a SAAS (software as a service) company that has built its own proprietary software allowing us to record, track, and verify a logistic company’s moves. Having the load information on any given inland container move allows MatchBack Systems Inc. to calculate the emissions savings through fuel consumption, freight weight, total trip mileage, commodity, and more. The project location will initially take place at major east coast ports and rail terminals including: Norfolk, Baltimore, Savanah, Charleston, Atlanta. Jacksonville, Memphis, Dallas, Houston, New York. The freight will be either an import headed from the port of origin to the destination (which would be an inland location) or an export headed from an inland location to the designated port. As we grow along with our customer base we plan to expand across the United States, completing street turns out of all major ports and terminals.  Customers use our cloud-based system to match pickups and deliveries within their own network or digitally connect with other parties collaborating on our neutral portal. Our solutions help companies to identify, plan and execute street-turns (matchbacks), enabling them to unlock cost and emissions savings as well as operational efficiencies that were previously unattainable. A matchback occurs when an import container move is matched with an export booking inland to eliminate the transportation of empty containers to and from the port. Reducing the amount of empty container moves and trucks on the road vastly reduces carbon emissions.
vcs-4531: The proposed project aims to reduce gas leakages from components in the natural gas transmission and distribution system operated by Hududgaz Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited across Uzbekistan. The project activity will reduce natural gas leakage in the transmission and distribution network of Hududgaz in the project area through the implementation of advanced leak detection and repairs (LDAR) procedures using advanced leak detection and measurement technology such as HiFlow Samplers. Leak Measurement Devices and Gasurveyors. The project activities will include inspection and leak measurements, as well as repair works at components in the natural gas above ground distribution system using advanced repair materials.
vcs-4532: THE PROJECT AIMS TO IMPLEMENT ALL FORMS OF IMPROVEMENT IN AGRICULTURE FROM THE CUTTING OF FERTILIZERS TO NO GRAZING AND TO USE AGRICULTURAL LANDS WHERE POSSIBLE AS EVERGREEN MEADOWS OR BETTER PERMANENT GRASSLANDS
vcs-4533:
Tech-Bank Animal Waste Management Systems (AWMS) GHG Mitigation Project in Fuyang (hereafter referred to as “the project”) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMS) to treat the manure from 5 existing swine farms at Linquan County, Fuyang city, Anhui Province, which are owned by Tech-Bank Food Co., Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm installs one AWMS, and the manure is treated on-site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All manure and wastewater will be collected and then the next step will be solid-liquid separation. The solid manure will be processed in an aerobic composting system and organic fertilizer will be produced. The liquid will be treated by anaerobic digestion and biogas produced during this treatment process will be captured and sent to an on-site torch and destroyed. The biogas residue produced after fermentation is applied as fertilizer to nearby fields, and the wastewater from the anaerobic digester is used for agricultural irrigation. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from power generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce GHG emissions in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from the anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. The annually emission reduction is estimated as 211,574tCO2e, and the total emission reductions are estimated as 2,115,740tCO2e throughout the crediting period.
vcs-4534: The Project Activity involves the decarbonization and implementation of energy efficiency measures in Dwellings in the UK. The Project Activity will achieve net Greenhouse Gas emission reductions through the implementation of energy efficiency measures which will have the effect of reducing the overall requirement for energy in Dwellings primarily through improvements to the building fabric and removing fossil fuel boilers and replacing them with more efficient electricity-based alternatives such as heat pumps

vcs-4536: The Esteros y Manglares REDD+ Project reduces deforestation and forest degradation, and protects mangrove ecosystems within eight (8) community councils in the municipalities of Mosquera, Olaya Herrera, La Tola, El Charco and Tumaco, in the department of Nariño in an area of 117,998.7 hectares. Within the limits of the project, actions are implemented from the social, cultural, environmental and economic fields that allow improving the living conditions of the communities, which is based on fundamental pillars such as governance of the territory, conservation of forests and biodiversity, territorial development and development of sustainable economies; which is aligned with the sustainable development objectives and the socio-environmental safeguards that protect the communities involved.
vcs-4538:
The proposed project aims to provide fresh and clean drinking water in remote villages in Western Zambia.  Contaminated water is responsible for a large percentage of sicknesses and diseases globally, with Sub -Saharan Africa being the most vulnerable. This is particularly the case in Western Zambia where a majority of the population lives in remote villages with no access to good, clean water sources. 
The project involves the construction of water wells to access clean groundwater, reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by minimizing the need for fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass in water purification. The selected groundwater will undergo testing according to CDM methodology AMS-III.AV. 
In the absence of the project, the baseline scenario would involve water scarcity, widespread sickness, declining living conditions, and continued reliance on fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass for water purification, resulting in significant greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. However, by providing access to clean drinking water the project not only reduces GHG emissions but also promotes more efficient lifestyles, enabling advancements in vital areas such as personal hygiene, gender equality, and sustainable agriculture.
In total, approximately 100 wells will be built annually to provide clean and safe drinking water to over 100 000 people during the project lifecycle. The average annual GHG emission reduction of the project is 24 000 tCO2e. The project expects a crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable to a total of 21 years.
vcs-4539: In Sierra Leone, mangrove forests are under severe threat from the pressures of subsistence-based harvesting for construction material and fuelwood for cooking and smoking fish. The health of mangrove ecosystems is directly tied to the social and economic well-being of local communities that depend on them for sustaining their traditional livelihoods in fishing and shellfish harvesting. Communities further depend on the mangroves for preventing erosion, which threatens coastal villages. Through a community-based and livelihood driven approach, and in collaboration with the Government of Sierra Leone, this grouped project will generate greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals through avoided deforestation and reforestation of mangrove ecosystems in the Bonthe and Moyamba districts, identified as global hotspots for biodiversity and home to some of the most marginalized communities in Sierra Leone. The project will begin with the conservation of 10,624 ha of mangroves on Sherbro Island, expanding in subsequent instances to include conservation activities in a combined total of over 74,000 ha of mangrove forests. Restoration activities will similarly expand from an initial 50 ha to an estimated total of 2,000 ha of degraded mangrove areas that are now threatened by erosion or abandoned due to saltwater intrusion.
vcs-454: The project activity under consideration entails generation of clean power by harnessing wind energy, a non-conventional renewable energy resource and export of the electricity generated through the Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited (in the state of Karnataka, India) on the basis of Power Purchase Agreements signed for each of the individual wind-mills with the respective state authorities. The project activity is a bundled wind energy project with total capacity of 9 MW comprising of six Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs), each having a capacity of 1.5 MW.
vcs-4540:
The Nagaland 4 Change is proposing an AFOLU Project under REDD+ Category in Peren district of Nagaland, North-eastern India. Nagaland is one of the few states of India having forest cover more than 50% of its geographical area. The forests provide multiple goods and services to the local Naga communities, such as fruits, seeds, medicines and recreation. Moreover, Nagaland state is located in the Indo-Burma Biodiversity Hotspot Region, which is among the 36 most biodiverse regions of the Earth. Some of the rare and endangered species, such as Spotted Linsang (Prionodon pardicolor), Clouded Leopard (Neofelis nebulosa), and Black Softshell Turtle (Nilssonia nigricans). In addition, forests of Nagaland protect the fragile hilly ecosystems of the state by preventing soil erosion and landslides.
   
However, specifically forests in Peren are gradually reducing in size. As well as the forests are also becoming increasingly prone to the fires during the dry summer months (April, May and June). Because of high anthropogenic pressures, the forests are also under extreme stress as a result of firewood collections. Therefore, Nagaland 4 Change, the Project Proponent is proposing a forest conservation project through funding from carbon financing under Verra VCS Mechanism. The main aim of the projects are as follows:
1.	Conservation of existing forests by protecting the forest cover.
2.	Increasing the forest cover as well as increasing density of the vegetation in forests.
3.	Enhancing the capacity of carbon storage of the forests, therefore generating carbon credits revenue out of it.
4.	Monitoring and reporting of the rare and endangered flora and fauna living the forests.
5.	Providing livelihood improvement to the local Naga communities through various interventions such as improved cookstoves, clean drinking water, etc.
vcs-4541: The Sundari Mangrove Restoration Project is a grouped project that aims to protect and restore 4.343 hectares of degraded urban mangroves located in the Sundarbans, West Bengal, India, by planting local species and rebuilding hydrological connectivity in the area. The first instance of the grouped project will be implemented in Sagar Island and Namkhana of South 24 Paraganas, and it will concern 417 ha. This project is a one of a kind, with a holistic approach ensuring successful restoration and conservation of the largest mangrove forest in the world. This project will be generating GHG emissions reductions by conserving and restoring degraded mangroves, as well as generating removals by increasing the biomass by planting millions of mangrove trees in the project area. The project is planned for an initial duration of 20 years and 4.1 million tCO2e are estimated to be removed over the crediting period, corresponding to an average of 209k tCO2 per year. Regarding the first instance of the grouped project, approx. 654K tCO2e are estimated to be removed over 20 years. Sundari aims to lower the pressure on the mangrove due to a high dependency of the populations on the mangrove forests for fuelwood collection and fishing. The project seeks to reduce these threats by conducting capacity building with local communities and improving sustainable local livelihoods to ensure the permanence of the carbon as well as the ecosystem services provided. Sundari is entirely community-based and was designed in close relationship with the local communities. The project developer, Meensou India Private Limited, is a local limited company implanted in the region with extensive expertise in mangrove ecology and carbon projects. EcoAct will act as co-project owner of the Sundari project and will oversee/help with the project validation and verification as well as administrate KPIs.
vcs-4542:
The Amazônidas REDD+ AUDD Grouped Project (hereafter called GPD) aims to avoid unplanned deforestation in private and public properties at Amazonas State. The scalability area of the GPD was defined based on the Brazil regional division by IBGE of 20171, as the sum of the Tefé, Parintins, Manaus, and Lábrea intermediate geographic regions in the Amazonas state, excluding the immediate geographic regions of Coari, Tefé, and Tabatinga. This region has long been recognized for its alarming rates of deforestation within the Amazon biome, and its forests face an escalated risk of deforestation. Initially, the present GPD is composed of thirty-five properties with 251,706.41 hectares of forest cover, split into four municipalities: Itacoatiara, Itapiranga, Silves and Presidente Figueiredo. The climate benefits brought with this GPD are directed related to the emission reduction of 124,528 tCO2e in average per year, calculated with a 6-year jurisdictional baseline.
The actions involving the implementation of Amazônidas REDD+ AUDD GPD are complementary to the grouped projects developed by brCarbon. Through these projects, in accordance with current federal and state environmental laws, brCarbon seeks to promote integral forest conservation actions in rural properties with remaining vegetation, promote solutions based on nature in its regions of influence, generating co-benefits not only for the climate (reduction and removal of emissions), but also communities and local biodiversity. Furthermore, the Amazônidas REDD+ AUDD GPD aims to create positive economic incentives for landowners to conserve rainforests in areas that are vulnerable to degradation and deforestation, while contributing to net positive climate impacts as well as benefit to traditional communities and conserve biodiversity.
vcs-4543:
The project developer is Sequoia Plantation Gabon who will implement the plantations under the modalities of lease of 20 years and renewable by 10 years, Sequoia Plantation Gabon will oversee project monitoring through the entire crediting period. The PlanGabon project aims to establish a total of 96,954 hectares of forest plantations across four initial farms. The project envisions transforming the degraded areas of these farms into forested landscapes, contributing to biodiversity conservation and the reforestation process. To achieve this goal, the project has set a specific target of establishing an average of 3,000 to 4,000 hectares of plantations per year over a duration of six years, this highlights the intended scale and pace of the establishment process over a period of 20 years (2023-2043). 
The project has five main goals. Firstly, it aims to transform non-forest areas into reforested areas. Secondly, it seeks to enhance the environmental and social conditions of rural areas, creating healthier and more sustainable communities. Thirdly, the project is dedicated to improving the income of local communities and ensuring the long-term viability of farmers by generating sustainable sources of income. Additionally, it actively contributes to mitigating climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting carbon sequestration. Lastly, the project addresses the issue of erosion, implementing measures to prevent soil erosion and protect the cover of natural forest present in the project areas. These goals collectively represent the project's commitment to forest reforestation, community development, climate resilience, and environmental conservation.
These plantations have a purpose: to restore damaged lands, produce wood sustainably, support local development, and combat climate change. They aim to revive depleted areas, ensure responsible wood production, boost local economies, and reduce carbon dioxide in the atmosphere by sequestering CO2.
vcs-4544:
Al Multaqa Landfill Gas Recovery Project (hereafter referred to as “the proposed project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project developed by Oman Environmental Services Holding Company S.A.O.C (be’ah). The proposed project is located in the Al Mulqata Landfill of the Al Amerat city, Muscat Governorate, the Sultanate of Oman, and the landfill is the first engineered landfill in Oman which began its operations in early 2011. 
The proposed project started operation in November 2021, and it is to capture LFG from the landfill and utilized the gas to generate electricity. At the time of requesting VCS registration, only cell 1 (half of the landfill) is closed and LFG from this cell has been captured and flared. After the closure and the installation of gas capture system of Cell 2 (the rest half of the landfill), gas engine(s) will be installed and fed with the LFG to generate electricity. The rated capacity of the engine is estimated to be 0.5MW.
vcs-4545: Ejin Banner Improved Grassland Management (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Ejin Banner, Alashan League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the time and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restoration of severely degraded land by replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term. The project proponent is Inner Mongolia Chengyao Grassland, Forestry and Animal Husbandry Ecological Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Project Proponent or PP).
vcs-4546:
The Recycling Roadways for Carbon Emission Reductions – Recycling & Stabilizing Association of California Project (herein “project”) supports RSA-California in replacing hot mix asphalt (HMA) with foam stabilized base (FSB) and/or emulsion asphalt in pavement projects across the United States. Prior to implementing project methods, pavement contractors often default to using energy-intensive mining, hauling, and high temperature material manufacturing practices associated with HMA. These industry standard activities unnecessarily destroy habitats, release carbon dioxide (CO2), and release volatile organic compounds (VOC).
This project reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting activities throughout the pavement application lifecycle. The project reduces dependence on the mining of virgin aggregate, reduces transportation of raw materials to mix plants, eliminates high-temperature asphalt manufacturing asphalt at high temperatures and, in the case of in-place pavement recycling, eliminates mix-plant to job-site transportation. The project replaces virgin aggregate with reclaimed asphalt pavement.
The project is conducted under VCS methodology VM0039, “Methodology for Use of Foam Stabilized Base and Emulsion Asphalt Mixtures in Pavement Application” and compares carbon emissions between traditional and sustainable designs with similar structural properties. 
This is be a grouped project and other similar Project Descriptions may also be developed with other pavement contractors.

vcs-4548: Tech-Bank Animal Waste Management Systems (AWMS) GHG Mitigation Project in Bengbu, Anhui (hereafter referred to as “the project”) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMS) to treat the manure from 4 newly-built swine farms in Chuzhou City and 2 newly-bulit swine farms in Bengbu City, Anhui Province, respectively, which are owned by Tech-Bank Food Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. vcs-455: The project activity is the project of Maracá Ceramic, which is a red ceramic industry localized in Ituiutaba municipality, in the state of Minas Gerais, region known as Triangulo Mineiro, southeastern of Brazil. The ceramic industry produces bricks and roof tiles, destined mainly for the regional market in Minas Gerais, but also for Mato Grosso and Goiás, which are boundary states. The fuel utilized in the baseline scenario to fire the ceramic units was native wood from the Cerrado biome, which is a pioneer practice in the region. This type of wood is considered a non- renewable biomass, once it is not originated in areas with reforestation activities or sustainable management activities.

The Hubei Badong IFM Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Badong County, Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Hubei Province of China by Hubei Yangfan Tourism Development Co., Ltd and Guangzhou Guotan Assets Management Co., Ltd, the geo-coordinate of the  project proponent is 110°04'E -110°32'E and 30°28'N - 31°28'N, the total area is 3348.75km2, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 5944.83 ha, including 750 subcompartments spreading over Bashan Forest Farm, Chadianzi Town, Dazhiping Town, Dongrangkou Town, Guandukou Town,Lvcongpo Town, Qingtaiping Town, Shuibuya Town, Xinling Town, Yanduhe Town, Yesanguan Town, Jinguoping Township, Xiqiuwan Township of Hubei Badong. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned or collective-owned, and have the legal right to forest ownership. The species involved in the project are Chinese Fir, Coniferous Broad Mix and Coniferous Mix.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 704,532 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 35,226 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 542,478 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 27,123 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.
vcs-4552:
The Uákiry REDD+ Grouped Project (hereafter called GPD), aims to avoid unplanned deforestation in private properties at Acre State. The area of deforestation involving three states in the north of Brazil has increased significantly in recent years, where before it was well preserved, the region known by the acronym AMACRO (where the states of Amazonas, Acre and Rondônia are located) has literally become no man's land. The lack of control caused cases of land grabbing and other crimes linked to the expansion of the agricultural frontier to explode. The region came to be known as the new Deforestation Frontier.
Initially the first four project activity instance is composed by four properties with 84,220 ha of forest cover, located in the Iaco River margins, one of Purus River affluents, in the Amazon basin. Through these projects, BrCarbon (hereafter known as BRC) and Yaco2 Gestão e Comércio de Carbono (Yaco2) seeks to promote integral forest conservation actions generating co-benefits not only for the climate (reduction and removal of emissions), but also communities and local biodiversity. At the validation, the climate benefits are directed related with the emission reduction of 215,021 tCO2e in average per year.
By joining BRC forest program, landowners can access funds from the carbon voluntary market to develop conservation and monitoring efforts in their forests. A partnership between BRC and landowners will result in the legal protection of forests, forest monitoring using satellite images, biodiversity inventory (including fauna e flora species), and forest biomass inventory in a broad scale, using an upscaling approach based on field collection, drone-borne and satellite sensors such as LiDAR (light detection and ranging). In addition, we will involve property surveillance, wildfire monitoring, fire prevention and fighting, threatened species protection and long-term social activities with local communities.
vcs-4554: The BiodeS biogas recovery and electricity generation project (hereafter, the “Project”), developed by Agro de Souza (hereafter, also referred as the “project proponent”), consists in the implementation of an anaerobic manure management system  for methane recovery and energy generation.
vcs-4555:
Hunan Fufeng Composting project (hereinafter as “the project”) employs aerobic composting systems on organic fertilizer factory in Miluo City, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China. The project is owned by Hunan Fufeng fertilizer Co., Ltd. The avoidance of methane emissions could be achieved with treatments of aerobic composting, which replaces the baseline scenario where the swine manure would undergo an anaerobic decomposition condition.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners, and methane would emit to the atmosphere.
The project introduces the aerobic composting system to treat livestock manure produced around Miluo City, the project was designed to produce 42,000 tons of organic fertilizer by treating 14,000 tons of livestock manure and 50,000 tons of straw. The organic fertilizer produced will be sold to local farmers and businesses. Without this project, the farms in project
areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere. 
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment of organic waste. During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 41,213 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total 412,130 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.

vcs-4557: The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. The project is being conducted in five divisions of Bareilly Forest Circle of Uttar Pradesh, namely Bareilly Social Forestry Division. vcs-4558: The project activity uses scraper system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated solid will be treated in aerobic composting system to produce fertilizer The separation liquid is treated by anaerobic digestion, and the biogas generated in the anaerobic digestion process is collected and utilized. Biogas is used as fuel for producing hot water and cooking for pig farms, which eliminated most of methane production and realized methane reduction. and the residual biogas will be flared by internal combustion emergency flare (closed flare) if there is any surplus biogas. The sludge produced by digestion is treated with aerobic composting together with solids, and the effluent is used as liquid organic fertilizer for agricultural irrigation.
vcs-4559:
Anhui Zhujixi CMM Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) utilizes the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Zhujixi coal mine to generate hot air to dry coal slime provided by Zhujixi coal mine. The Project is located in Hetuan Town, Panji District, Huainan City, Anhui Province, China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to generate hot air to dry the coal slime. The project applies flameless oxidation process. Four sets of regenerative thermal oxidizers (RTOs), each with a treatment capacity of around 30,000 Nm3/h  are installed, able to destroy 10.368 million Nm3 of methane annually and dry 400,000 tonnes of wet coal slime ideally.

The Ajinomoto Co., Inc. grouped project aims to introduce feed additives to dairy farms in United States, Japan, EU, Australia, New Zealand, Chile, Costa Rica, and South Korea to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector. Methane is a by-product of the enteric fermentation process in cattle and is mainly expelled by the animal through belching. The Agolin® Ruminant feed additive used in this project reduces methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by changing the microbial population in the rumen; it also increases milk production efficiency.

A VCS-grouped project combines multiple project activity instances into a single, combined project which adds new instances (farms) over time. The project instances of this grouped project are located in United States, Japan, EU, Australia, New Zealand, Chile, Costa Rica, and South Korea and will implement the Agolin® Ruminant in the cattle’s diet, starting from September 01, 2023.

The dairy farms included in the grouped project have not previously engaged in enteric methane reduction activities similar to those in the proposed grouped project activity and have otherwise been releasing CH4 into the atmosphere (“the business as usual” scenario). 

In the seven years of the first crediting period, when the project activities will be implemented, the project will organize the addition of a natural feed blend to the dairy cattle feed and to subsequent feeding to generate estimated emission reductions of 0.45 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) per cattle per year, with an estimated total reduction of 231,518 tCO2e in the first crediting period, depending on the continuing success of enrolling more farms. The Project is quantified and will be monitored according to the VCS methodology “VM0041 Methodology for the Reduction of Enteric Methane Emission from Ruminants through the Use of Feed Ingredients”. It falls under VCS Sectoral Scope 15, livestock and manure management.

Shandong Zhucheng ALM Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Zhucheng City, Weifang City, Shandong Province of China. The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by the farms taking part to the project and raise the carbon storage in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. The project was implemented by the Shandong Herong Agricultural Technology Group Co., Ltd. and Hainan icarbon Ecological Development Co.,Ltd. (hereafter “the project proponent”).
The project is located in the Zhucheng City, which covers 3 Streets and 10 towns. Zhucheng City is located in the southeast of Shandong Peninsula, at the junction of Taiyi Mountain Range and Jiaowei Plain. The total area of Zhucheng City is 2182.7 square kilometres, with the geographic coordinates between 35°42′23′′ and 36°21′05′′ north latitude and 119°0′19′′ and 119°43′56′′ east longitude.
The proposed project is aimed to prevent the soil degradation through adoption of the improved crop land management practices (collectively referred to conservational tillage) to replace the conventional cultivation mode.
Main activities about conservational tillage adopted in the project include： 
Organic fertilizer application (reduce inorganic fertilizer application): 54,398.5 ha of cropland have reduced the use of chemical fertilizer.
Straw incorporation (Improve crop residue management): straw in 54,398.5 ha of cropland have been buried and returned, with the depth of 30 cm.
A total of 54,398.5 ha of farmland has been managed under conservation tillage, The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 3,471,463 tCO2e from 01-Jan-2021 to 31-Dec- 2040, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 173,573 tCO2e.
vcs-4562: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Içara Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature open flare(s) and utilization as gaseous fuel in engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure, and a LFG upgrading plant that produces biomethane for thermal use.

Allcot Blue Carbon Mangrove Restoration project in Senegal (ABC Mangrove Senegal) is a grouped project for the reforestation and conservation of mangrove ecosystems in Senegal. Through the restoration of at least 7,000 ha of mangroves, the project aims to:
o Strengthen the vegetation cover in the mangrove ecosystems.
o Improve the production and income of vulnerable groups.
o Strengthen the capacity of vulnerable groups to use land resources sustainably.
Involving the local communities since the beginning is one of the most important steps in the project. This includes providing information on all project activities and teaching basic concepts on climate change, and 
carbon sequestration projects. The project promotes a functioning family model where both women and 
men can equally participate in the project. People will show alternative livelihood opportunities that allow them to acquire and grow high-value crops, beekeeping, or ecotourism among other potential possibilities, 
which also reduces pressure on mangrove forests. An improvement of the basic infrastructure for rural communities is targeted as well.
The Project location is the Saloum Delta and the Casamance estuary respectively located in two regions (Fatick and Casamance) and 5 departments (Fatick, Foundiougne, Ziguinchor, Bignona, Oussouye), implemented in bare land, and at the end of the crediting period, the net emissions reductions are 2,241,960 tCO2 e.
vcs-4564: The main purpose of this project activity is to generate clean form of electricity through waste to energy-based power generation. The plant utilizes the Refuse-Derived Fuel (“RDF”) as feedstock derived from the separation and sorting of Municipal Solid Waste (“MSW”) excluding the recyclable or potentially hazardous materials from the waste stream. The MSW is sourced from the Jamnagar City and the project will utilise about 311 ton of RDF per day and generate electricity with the installed capacity of 7.5 MW. The project avoids CH4 emission from avoidance of waste going to landfills and also avoids CO2 emission by replacing grid electricity.

Muyuan Huainan AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Anhui Province (hereafter referred to as the project) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from swine farms in Huainan City, Anhui Province, China, which are owned by Muyuan Foods Co.,Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm shall install one AWMS, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 359.022 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMSs. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 336,687 tCO2e emission reductions will be attained annually.

Grow Indigo is implementing a project in Maharashtra and Gujarat to boost smallholder farmers' income through the adoption of regenerative agriculture, resulting in reduced greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and positive environmental and economic outcomes.
The proposed project in Maharashtra and Gujarat addresses the GHG emissions caused by traditional agricultural practices in crops such as cotton, sugarcane, rice, wheat, maize, or soybean, without excluding other crops. Intensive agriculture practices in the project area have posed threats to land sustainability and contributed to increased GHG emissions.
The project aims to promote regenerative agricultural practices, such as optimized fertilizer management, cover cropping, zero- or reduced-tillage, improved water management/ irrigation, crop rotation, and agroforestry, to restore soil health, enhance biodiversity, and improve productivity.
The project takes an integrated and science-backed approach, including agricultural extension, outreach, agronomic support, digital data collection, and biogeochemical modeling.
The project will initially target 40,000 hectares in the project area and cover diverse cropping systems with regenerative agricultural practices that are known to reduce GHG emissions (N2O, CO2e, and SOC) and thus generate carbon credits.
The project also aims to link smallholder farmers to voluntary carbon markets, providing them with additional income opportunities and incentivizing the adoption of regenerative agriculture. With a cash incentive, smallholder farmers in the project boundary will adopt these practices more readily and contribute to sustainability and reduce GHG emissions.
Through these efforts, the project seeks to contribute to sustainability, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and improve the overall livelihoods of smallholder farmers in the project area.

AS KOC POLATLI BIOGAS POWER PLANT (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that aims to captures biogas from animal manure, dairy cattle and other cattle manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate electricity through cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas.  Waste heat from two gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The electricity generated by the installed two biogas engines with the capacity of 1.501 MWe each and a total capacity of 3.120 MWe is not only supplied to the national grid, but also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products, by-products of biogas generation processes, are distributed to neighboring agricultural farms as fertilizer free of charge.

Prior to the project activity, livestock farms supplying animal manure to the project were, in the baseline scenario, storing the animal manure generated at their farms in uncovered anaerobic lagoons as Animal Waste Management System (AWMS) in a retention period of 2-3 months and then, generally applying to land, as fertilizer, directly without any proper treatment. In addition, untreated animal manure is an important source of methane which is one of the most potent GHGs. 
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes.
vcs-4577:
Grouped ARR Project in Telangana is an Agroforestry, Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation project being jointly developed by Tapovanam Organic Farming Systems (hereinafter referred as Tapovanam) and ClimeTrek Limited (hereinafter referred as ClimeTrek) in fallow agricultural, and wastelands owned by individual farmers and communities with low plant cover (hereinafter referred as project activity). The entire project lies within the geographical boundaries of Telangana state in India. In the first instance, the project activity is limited to the district of Nalgonda. Being a grouped project, more farmers and communities belonging to other districts of Telangana will be added as ‘future project instances. The project activity involves planting oil palm trees along with some cash crops like turmeric and groundnuts. In the first project instance, around 1,100 Ha will be covered in Nalgonda district in three years.  Future instances will cover 15 other districts of the state of Telangana. All project instances within this grouped project activity will consist of afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR) primarily involving oil palm plantations with intercropping of turmeric and groundnuts. Based on ex-ante estimates the project will sequester around 1,073,817.9 tCO2e over 30-years (tree/ shrub biomass carbon and soil carbon) and an annual emissions reduction of 35,793.9 tCO2e.
Tapovanam is the coordinator for all the participating farmers and provides training to the farmers regarding the technologies/measures involved in the project activity. Tapovanam will have the right to carbon credits without any violation of farmers rights. The revenue after expenses from sale of carbon credits will be shared with the participating farmers. Clime Trek is the Carbon Project Developer. As per the agreement between Tapovanam and Clime Trek, the rights to carbon credits from the project will be transferred to ClimeTrek.Tapovanam and ClimeTrek are project pp.
vcs-4578:
This project activity is a voluntary initiative by WeAct Pty Ltd in the Sangareddy district, in the state of Telangana in India. WeAct is a carbon asset management and carbon financing entity from Australia who deals in such GHG projects globally to address the concerns of climate change and ensures long term sustainability. The project activity uses Low technology production facilities to produce Biochar from biomass wastes in the project region. The project includes mainly soil-pit methods and box-kiln method which are two common low-tech approaches that can serve as a starting point for small-scale production, experimentation, and community-level initiatives. Under the facilities, the biomass undergoes pyrolysis process. The project activity mainly targets to include “Cotton Stalk” as a single type of waste biomass used as feedstock to produce biochar and the resulting biochar to be utilized for soil application. In the absence of the project activity, the cotton wastes would have been mainly combusted without any utilization for purposes and not utilized for producing biochar for either soil or non-soil application. 

The project activity is expected to generate an annual average of 22,376 tCO2e emission reductions which is estimated based on a projected generation of biochar from cotton stalks as feedstock during each harvesting season in each year. The project contributes to sustainable development by promoting various aspects including (but not limited to) environmental conservation, resource efficiency, rural development, climate change mitigation, and the transition towards a circular economy. It aligns agricultural practices with the principles of sustainable development, fostering a more resilient and equitable agricultural sector.
vcs-4579:
The project basically consists of the application of regenerative agriculture techniques and strategies on different farms in Spain, to promote a more sustainable agronomic management, and as a result increasing the amounts of atmospheric carbon fixed in the soil.
Regenerative agriculture promotes practices such as the reduction or absence of tilling the soil, the presence of plant covers, the non-use of synthetic chemical products, organic fertilization, the optimization of water use, the improvement of by-products or waste management, and crop rotation, among others.
The project is national scope and will be carried out on all those farms within the boundaries of the Spanish State that adopt the commitment to improve their agronomic management and that meet the established requirements.
Regenerative agricultural management is focused on improving the soil’s properties and promoting conservation practices. The implementation of these measures will help to improve the health and fertility of agricultural soils which translates into an increase in the amount of organic matter (OM) in those soils. Carbon is one of the main components of OM, so increasing its percentage in soils is equivalent to increasing the amount of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC).
Each of the regenerative strategies proposed in the project has a direct or indirect effect on the reduction of Green-house Gases (GHG), either by reducing emissions or by increasing its fixation in the soil.
Although it is gaining ground in recent years, regenerative agriculture is not a common practice in the Spanish territory. Most farms are managed according to the principles of conventional agriculture, in which the soil is considered a mere support which generally has very little organic life and therefore, the amounts of OM and C are well below the levels that they could potentially contain.
The Sustainable Farming Carbon Project in Spain will be developed as a grouped project.

The Myanmar Kindar Solar Power Plant Project is the construction of a new solar photovoltaic power plant project located in the south of Mandalay Division and 56km northeast to the Meiktila town, Mandalay Division, Myanmar. 
The project scenario consists of the installation of 74,592 pieces of 540Wp polycrystalline silicon PV module, providing a total capacity of 40.28MWp. The expected net annual power supply to the grid is 62,015.75MWh. The expected full load operating hours are 1,540h annually, and the plant load factor is 17.58%. The power generated by the project will be routed via an on-site step-up station to 132 kV and then connected to the Myanmar Power Grid.
By displacing fossil fuel fired power generation within the Grid by clean renewable energy, the project leads to the reduction of CO2 emissions into the atmosphere. Total annual Green House Gases emissions reduction is estimated to be of 22,402 tCO2e annually. The total emission reductions during the renewable 7-year crediting period will be 156,814 tCO2e.
