Total annual Green House Gases emissions reduction is estimated to be of 23,339 tCO2e annually. The total emission reductions during the renewable 7-year crediting period will be 163,373 tCO2e.
vcs-4583:
The Myanmar Satoketayar Solar Power Plant Project is the construction of a new solar photovoltaic power plant project located 76km northwest from the capital city of Magway Division, Myanmar. 
The main purpose of the project is to generate power from clean renewable solar power and supply electricity to the Myanmar Power Grid while contributing to the sustainability of power generation of the Myanmar Power Grid.
The project scenario consists of the installation of 74,592 pieces of 540Wp polycrystalline silicon PV module, providing a total capacity of 40.28MWp. The expected net annual power supply to the grid is 63779.85MWh. The expected full load operating hours are 1,583 h annually, and the plant load factor is 18.08%. The power generated by the project will be routed via an on-site step-up station to 66 kV and then connected to the Myanmar Power Grid.
By displacing fossil fuel fired power generation within the Grid by clean renewable energy, the project leads to the reduction of CO2 emissions into the atmosphere. Total annual Green House Gases emissions reduction is estimated to be of 23,014 tCO2e annually. The total emission reductions during the renewable 7-year crediting period will be 161,098 tCO2e.
vcs-4584:
A-Thermal has a pyrolysis process plant for the destruction of hazardous and general wastes in South Africa. The plant has a lower CO2e footprint than other current waste disposal methods that are both legal and lower cost  i.e., landfill. Further, the process captures and fixes carbon from the waste feed in the carbonized residue by-product.
The project meets the methodology requirements for avoidance of methane production from the waste going to landfills.
The plant has been in operation since 2009 and is fully permitted.
vcs-4585:
The project aims to distribute 100 000 fixed improved cookstoves to all eligible households in the district of Rusizi in Western Rwanda over the next 4 years. 
Those single-pot cookstoves will be built in-situ into domestic kitchens. Kiasi Energies will disseminate fixed Improved Cookstove Solutions (ICS) in Rwanda that will drastically increase community access to clean cooking solutions by providing, installing, and maintaining energy efficient and smoke reducing cookstoves. Those improved cookstoves will be distributed for free and the materials (bricks, clay, ...) needed for installation will be collected by the households themselves. 

The aim of the project is to reduce the emissions of greenhouse gases incurred by high wood consuming cooking practices. Indeed, in the district of Rusizi, a large part of the population is still cooking with a three-stone fire. The distribution of these stoves directly improves energy access and reduces wood fuel consumption, thus slowing down deforestation. It is expected to prevent the emission of 150kt of CO2eq per year, on average. It also benefits the local population with several other socio-economic matters addressed by the Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, such as improved health for the households, gender equality, reduced poverty, and others.
vcs-4587:
The Boreal Wildlands Forest Carbon Offset Project creates GHG reductions and removals through the 
purchase and management of 145,173 ha of private forest land, located in the Ontario Boreal shield 
forest, by The Nature Conservancy of Canada (NCC) for the creation of a conservation-based forest 
carbon project.
vcs-4588:
Nam Houng - 1 Hydro Power Project is developed by Simoung Group Co., Ltd in Xayabouly province, Lao PDR. The primary purpose of the project is to generate electricity to the Lao Power Grid. The project activity is a run-off river hydro power project with a total installed capacity of 15 MW. The project is promoted by Simoung Group Co., Ltd. Project is expected to commission on 01/10/2023 with a expected net annual generation of 87,280 MWh.
The baseline scenario of the project is continuation of the present situation, i.e electricity supplied from the power grid. By displacing part of the power generated by thermal power plants, the project is therefore expected to reduce equivalant CO2 emissions from he grid connected power plants.
vcs-4589: The proposed project activity involves methane recovery through controlled anaerobic digestion of animal waste (cow dung) and utilization of recovered methane (biogas) for thermal energy and electricity generation in the dairy plant. The project plans to install two centralized anaerobic bio-digesters having capacities of 2000m3/day each, a total of 4000 m3/day and two number of 125KVA capacity biogas-based electrical engine.  The proposed plant will treat about 100 MT/day of animal manure per day sourced from nearby farmers or aggregators. The project is being built, and is owned and operated by Dudh Utpadak Sahakari Sangh Limited (DUSSL). Project activity is located at Chandauli district of Uttar Pradesh state in India.
vcs-459: Hubei Jiugongshan Wind Farm CDM Project, a grid-connected renewable energy project, is located in Tongshan County, Hubei Province, Centre China. The objective of the proposed project is to generate electric power from local wind resources, and supply to the Centre China Power Grid. The implementation of the proposed project will achieve CO2 emission reduction by replacing electricity generated by fossil fuel fired power plants in the Centre China Grid. The proposed project installed 16 sets of 850 KW wind turbines in Jiugongshan Mountain, for a total installed capacity of 13.6 MW. It is estimated that the annual power supply to the grid of the proposed project will be 28.05GWh, with 2059 hours of installed capacity utilization. As a result, 31758 tonnes of CO2 emission reduction will be generated each year.
vcs-4591: Piantagione di rimboschimento con messa a dimora di piante bambù gigante nella regione Piemonte.
vcs-4592:
The Symbiosis Continuous Cover Forest Project is a reforestation project, proposed by Symbiosis Investimentos e Participações S.A., a company focused on the restoration of degraded land through the sustainable commercial reforestation of the Atlantic Rainforest native species.
The Atlantic Forest Biome (Mata Atlântica) is the most degraded in Brazil, with less than 12.4% left of its original area and very fragmented. The degradation started in the 16th century in the State of Bahia. Today, the same pattern of destruction is seen in the Amazon Biome, which started in the 70’s after the Atlantic Rainforest resources were depleted. In addition, plant breeding with the Atlantic Forest native species has not been implemented before.
The project is designed as a grouped project, with an initial instance at “Fazenda Novo Horizonte”, in Trancoso District of Porto Seguro municipality, Bahia State. It is situated in close proximity to Symbiosis headquarters, where seedlings are produced and where research and development activities take place. Novo Horizonte has a total area of 669.28 ha, from which 236.50 consist of the initial project area. Symbiosis expansion plans for the grouped project are focused on the South of Bahia, with projected 50,000 hectares of mixed species reforestation, in addition to 15,000 hectares of ecological restoration and 5,000 hectares of agroforestry with cocoa (also a relevant product of the region).
The land use in the region is predominantly focused on pasture, which is also the prior condition of all of the regions where the grouped project is intended to occur.
The project is designed for a 40-year crediting period, in which 27,499,184 tCO2e will be reduced/removed
vcs-4593: The main objective of the project Cycling the Change Latin America is to promote the sustainable mobility at the cities  covered by the grouped project through the implementation of new bicycle sharing programs with sharing stations. Beyond that the program aims at the expansion of the existing parking areas, expansion of existing bikes and introduction of e-bikes.
vcs-4596:
According to information from the Ministry of the Environment of Japan, total GHG emissions from the agricultural sector in Japan in 2018 were about 32.3 million t-CO2eq. Of these, emissions from rice cultivation were the largest, at approximately 12 million t-CO2eq. , accounting for 38.2% of total emissions. The implementation of this project will reduce emissions by tCO2eq. per year and contribute to the reduction of GHG emissions from these agricultural activities.
At this project, we use VM0042 to reduce CH4 by using no pesticides, no fertilizers, and by drying the soil in the middle of the year. As for environmental impact, the absence of chemical fertilizers reduces most of the nitrous oxide generated from the soil and the carbon dioxide produced during the production and transportation of fertilizers, and the absence of animal-based fertilizers eliminates concerns about methane emissions from the fertilizer production process.
vcs-4597: The project activity involves setting up and operation of a Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) to Torrefied Charcoal Pellets manufacturing facility by NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Ltd (NVVN) in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh State, India. MSW collected from local Varanasi Municipal Corporation will be used to manufacture the Torrefied Charcoal Pellets; which shall then be supplied via Onward sale agreement to nearby operating coal fired power plant as replacement substitution for coal. The project will dispose of 600 TPD Fresh MSW to convert to 400TPD of Torrefied Charcoal for further use as fuel in power plant.
vcs-4598:
The projected ARR VCS initiative aims to help farmers in Gujarat, India, by providing them with additional income via the sale of carbon credits created by agroforestry tree crops on their land.
Shri Hari Bhujal Vikash Mandal (SHBVM), the project's co-proponent, has supported farmers in providing quality planting material for agroforestry species. They also provide on-site help to farmers who have registered with them for plantation maintenance. The project is being implemented in six Gujarat districts: Chhota Udepur, Mahisagar, Vadodara, Bharuch, Aravalli, and Panchmahal. Roughly 15 million seedlings will be planted on an area of around 4,000 hectares.
vcs-46: The Wahei Hydroelectric Project (hereafter, the Project) is being developed by Sichuan Mabian  Xianjiapuhe Power Generation Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the Project Developer), a county-level private company. The purpose of the Project is to utilize the hydrological resource of the Wahei River in a diversion type hydro power scheme to generate zero carbon emission electricity for the Central China Power Grid. The project will generate Certified Emission Reductions (CERs) by displacing electricity generation from grid connected fossil fuel-fired power plants that would otherwise be generating the electricity needed.
vcs-460: The Gansu Datonghe Tiecheng Hydropower Station Project involves the construction of a run-of-river hydropower station at the main stream of the Datong River in Yongdeng County of Lanzhou city in Gansu Province, China. The main objective of the project is to generate power from clean renewable hydro power in Gansu Province and contribute to the sustainability of power generation of the North West China Grid. The hydropower station will install 4 Francis turbines with a total installed capacity of 51.5 MW.
vcs-4600:
The FST solar project consists of the installation of solar photovoltaic power plants with a capacity of 9.98 MWp, located in Kamphaeng Phet Province, Thailand. 

Petroleum exploration and production required significant amounts of electricity use, baseline technology to produce electricity generate large amount of greenhouse gas (GHGs) emissions such as fossil-fuel power plant which use natural gas, diesel, and other fossil fuels used to generate electricity. The displacement of fossil fuel with solar power generation will generate GHGs emission reductions by replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy sources such as solar power. The project involves the installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) panels, which generate clean electricity without emitting GHGs emissions. In contrast, the use of fossil fuels for power generation produces significant GHGs emissions that contribute to climate change.  

Moreover, the excess solar energy generated will be stored in batteries, reducing the reliance on fossil fuel-based power generation. This will further reduce GHGs emissions associated with power generation. 

Overall, the replacement of fossil fuels with solar power generation projects will generate significant GHGs emissions reductions, contributing to fight against climate change. 

The annual emissions reduction is 13,061.87 tCO2e/annum.
vcs-4601: The project recovers biogas from the wastewater generated in citric acid, corn flour, and protein production process and use the biogas to generate electricity and heat for TTCA Co. The project site includes two connected areas. The east area includes two generators, and the west area includes four generators.
vcs-4602:
Tropical rain forests with their rich fauna and flora are threatened worldwide from deforestation and forest degradation. In Argentina, deforestation rates are particularly high, caused mainly by conversion of forests to expand soy and beef production. Wintershall Dea AG, VisionNetZero GmbH and Banco de Bosques have joined forces to develop REDD+ carbon projects to conserve large forest patches with a high biodiversity in the Northwestern region of Argentina. 
The project intends to protect and conserve 24,154 hectares that are part of the Yungas forests in northwest Argentina. The main project activity is taking the property off the market to prevent agricultural development and conserve its high carbon values, rich biodiversity, and critical ecosystem functionality by avoiding planned deforestation and forest degradation. Therefore, the project intends a joint certification with CCB Standard.
The project will deliver significant carbon as well as non-carbon benefits by conserving the natural forest ecosystems of the Yungas, one of the most biodiverse natural systems in Argentina and home to nearly 50% of the country's biodiversity. Through the income of carbon revenues, forest areas with high conservation value can be purchased and conserved by donating and integrating them into national or provincial protection systems.
The development of REDD+ carbon projects contribute to climate change mitigation by reducing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) from forest loss and forest degradation. The number of generated credits is estimated based on the comparison of the projected baseline and the effectiveness of the project activities targeting the drivers of deforestation and degradation. In the project area that would be protected, the weighted average of tons of carbon dioxide per hectare (tCO2/ha) is 884 tCO2/ha. On that basis, up to 1.8 Mio. VCUs can be expected within the duration of the project (30 years).
vcs-4603: BATIKIPAS BIOGAS PLANT is located in Söke district of Aydın, Türkiye. The proposed project activity includes installation of anaerobic wastewater treatment plant to  generate biogas from wastewater of the paper mill. Installed capacity of project is planned to be 6.168 MWm.
vcs-4605:
Hubei Longshen Composting project (hereinafter as “the project”) employs aerobic composting
systems on organic fertilizer factory in Jianli City, Jingzhou City, Hubei Province, China. The
project is owned by Hubei Longshen fertilizer Co., Ltd. The avoidance of methane emissions
could be achieved with treatments of aerobic composting, which replaces the baseline scenario
where the swine manure and chicken manure would undergo an anaerobic decomposition
condition.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic
lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners, and
methane would emit to the atmosphere. The project introduces the aerobic composting system to treat livestock manure produced
around Jianli City, the project was designed to produce 14,000 tons of organic fertilizer by
treating 140,000 tons of livestock manure and 10,000 tons of straw. The organic fertilizer
produced will be sold to local farmers and businesses. Without this project, the farms in project
areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of
GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere. The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions through
controlled aerobic treatment of organic waste. During the implementation of the project, it is
estimated that about 59,514 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total
595,140 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.
vcs-4606: Qinghai Gangcha Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Haibei Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China. The project aims to restore 64,200 hectares (or 963,000 Mu) degraded grasslands in Gangcha by adopting a variety of measures including grass seeding, rotational grazing and rest grazing. The project will increase carbon sequestration, reverse grassland degradation, contribute to local development and preserve cultural traditions.
vcs-4607:
The proposed Project activity intends to restore degraded mangrove habitats in the Indian Sundarbans region.  The project activity plans to restore up to 3,000 hectares of degraded mangrove ecosystems in phased manner through the plantation of diverse native mangrove tree species. The project activity is being implemented in the Indian part of Sundarbans delta situated in the West Bengal state of India. The project is implemented by the proponent in collaboration with the project implementing partner organization, site specific ground partners, and the local communities. The project activity will ensure the active participation of women in various stages of project implementation and post implementation management of the project interventions

By restoring the degraded mangrove land with the native tree species, the project activity will remove atmospheric carbon dioxide through biological carbon sequestration in the tree biomass and in the soil there by avoiding the equivalent amount of GHG emissions which would have not been occurred in the pre-project scenario as the land remains degraded land with no carbon sequestration.
vcs-4608: One Earth Fund BEC-2022 will reduce emissions and reduce landfill inputs through composting residential and commercial food waste.
vcs-4609:
The Hainan Jinhua IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project is implemented in Hainan Province of China by Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd. 
In recent years, Hainan has been promoting the construction of tropical rainforest national parks and increasing the ecological restoration of tropical rainforests. In order to support Hainan's tropical rainforest protection and biodiversity conservation, since 01-Sep-2020, Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd has taken the initiative to incorporate part of the company's forest land into the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park. Since the launch of Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park, logging has been stopped in the protected area to achieve forest protection. The area of forest land allocated to Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd is about 14,600 ha, including two tree species,  eucalyptus and Acacia mangium. Of these, the Acacia mangium forest land is involved in the the Improved Forest Management (IFM) project of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 4863 ha, including 126 subcompartments spreading over Baisha, Baoting, Changjiang, Ledong, Lingshui, Qiongzhong, WuzhiMountain. All these departments are 100% owned by Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd and have the legal right to forest ownership. The specie involved in the project is Acacia mangium. This is common local tree species.
Prior to the implementation of the project activity, Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd harvested trees in the project area in accordance with a valid timber management plan approved by the government.
The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 3,187,713 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual emission reduction is 106,257 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 2,486,416 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 82,881 tCO2e.
vcs-461: Veerachai Farm Ratchaburi Biogas Project  involves the capture of methane (CH4) rich biogas produced during the treatment of swine barn flushing wash-waters and its combustion for heat and power generation at Veerachai Farm in the Ratchaburi Province of Thailand. With the swine rearing capacity of 120,000 fattening swine, Veerachai Farm has recently invested in a high-rate continuous flow closed anaerobic treatment reactors to treat 100% of all barn flushing effluents produced from their swine rearing operations. Veerachai Farm has constructed these facilities to replace low-rate open anaerobic lagoon barn flushing effluent treatment systems.
vcs-4611:
The project activity is a combination of several waste management activities with purpose to valorize the coconut husks waste. The coconut husks waste biomass is fed into a gasification system to produce electricity and biochar. While the electricity is supplied to the coconut factory at the same location, the biochar is sold as soil enhancer for the surrounded coconut plantations. Through these activities, the project will avoid emitting CH4 to the atmosphere, producing renewable energy, and remove carbon through application of biochar as soil enhancer.

The new biomass gasification plant project will generate 1 MWe for its coconut processing plant in West Halmahera, North Maluku. The proposed project involves installing a gasifier unit and two internal combustion engines with a 1.0 MW installed capacity. Considering 24 hours of operation per day and 350 days of operation per year, the expected annual power generation is 8.400 MWh of electricity which will be absorbed by the coconut processing plant. The gasification process will produce biochar as the by-product, distributed as soil enricher for the farmers.

The Project Proponent plans to upgrade the coconut plant capacity to 200.000 coconuts per day after four years of stable production with increasing product demand. Following the plant capacity increase, biomass gasification would be upgraded to 2 MWe.
vcs-4612: Weiyuan Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) installs a set of organic fertilizer production lines with an annual capacity of 50,000 tons to treat swine manure from swine farms and biomass waste residue (straw) in Weiyuan County, Neijiang City, Sichuan Province, China. The project is invested and owned by Sichuan Zhengwei Industry Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass waste residue. This project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system. It is estimated that approximately 102,000 tonnes of manure and 35,000 tonnes of biomass waste residue can be treated annually, therefore total 137,000 tonnes of waste can be composted aerobically for this project. A portion of the organic fertilizer obtained is sold to the local government for improving the quality of local high-standard farmland, and another portion is sold to local farmers, farmer cooperatives and businesses. The construction start date of the project is 21 July 2020 and was put into operation on 1 January 2022. The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue. It is estimated that 59,518 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 595,175 tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixing crediting period.
vcs-4613:
The primary goal of this project is to contribute to the removal and reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the atmosphere by planting agroforestry species on farmlands owned by individual farmers. In contrast to traditional agriculture, agroforestry systems have a high potential in raising yield, improving soil fertility, generate economic revenue, and improving carbon sequestration. The agroforestry systems deliver several non-timber forest products, agriculture products, and ecosystem services which may enhance the social well-being of the local farmers, national, and global communities. The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation.
The Project Proponent along with the local implementation partner will implement the project activity including plantation, capacity building, and training programs. The species selected for agroforestry plantation include Mango, Guava, Citrus, Pomegranate, Carissa carandas, and other fruit species. The project aims to cover 50,000 hectares of total agroforestry area and for the first instance, 17,500 hectares have been considered. The implementation of the project would generate GHG emission removals and improve the local environment by growing trees, increasing the source of income, and enhancing the capabilities of farmers. The project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions or removals of 531,212 tCO2e.
vcs-4614:
GER Recycled PP Project (hereinafter called “the Project”) aims to recycled PP plastic particles by using waste PP products (like packaging bags, sheeting, pipes, household daily necessities etc.) and to replace the same PP produced from the raw materials. The Project located at Fengcheng Circular Economy Park, Yichun District, Fengcheng City, Jiangxi Province, China and is developed and operated by Jiangxi Green Recycling Co.,Ltd. (hereinafter called “The Project Proponent”).
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of PP particles would be produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas) which is also the baseline scenario of the project. Therefore, the GHG emission reduction will be generated through the implementation of the project by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and reducing related energy consumption as well. The project has started constructed since 03/2021, and the date of production line putting into operation is 31/12/2021.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through an avoiding extraction of raw materials and production of virgin materials. It is estimated that the project will result a total of 137,200 tCO2e emission reductions in the first crediting period of 7 years and with annual average of 19,600 tCO2e emission reduction in the 1st crediting period.
vcs-4615: The Panãma REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Investimentos Ambientais S.A.  Fundação Jari and Jari Celulose, with the purpose of promoting forest conservation and reducing potential greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) based on a model of local economic development that values the “standing forest” through the integration of Sustainable Forest Management activities and the commercialization of environmental services. The Project is located in three municipalities: Almeirim, in the State of Pará, and Laranjal do Jari/Vitória do Jarí, in the State of Amapá. There is a very important role in this region as it serves as a home for many rural families and as an ecological corridor, with several Conservation Units (CUs) in its vicinity. It has a very rich biodiversity, its vegetation includes ten forest and non-forest formations and species of extreme ecological and social importance.
vcs-4616:
Shunfeng Erhai Composting project in Yousuo (hereinafter as “the project”) designed to construct an organic fertilizer factory in Songqu Village, Yousuo Town, Eryuan County, Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China. The project is owned by Dali Erhai Biological Fertilizer Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners, and methane would emit to the atmosphere.
The project is designed to treat livestock manure collected from Niujie Town, Sanyin Town, Zhibi Lake Town, Fengyu Town, Yousuo Town and Dengchuan Town to produce organic fertilizer in Songqu Village. The proposed comprises of composting system and fertilizer packaging system. It is estimated that about 168,088 tons of cattle manure, 127,688 tons of swine manure, 8,842 tons of chicken manure and 66,960 tons of straw will be treated to produce 200,000 tons of organic fertilizer annually. The organic fertilizer produced will be sold to local government, farmers and businesses. Without this project, the manure produced in these farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment of organic waste. During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 57,435 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total 574,350 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.
vcs-4617:
This afforestation project, set up in anthropogenic savannahs on the Batéké Plateau east of Kinshasa, aims to develop carbon sink plantations, i.e. plantations where wood is little or no harvested, in order to maximize greenhouse gas sequestration in the long term. The majority of the project's area will therefore be dedicated to forest plantations with this main objective. Another objective of these forest plantations will be the timber production: some trees will be cut down very selectively in order to maintain the constant volume of the forest stand over time, while sustainably a local timber sector, replacing informal logging of natural forests. We also know that another effective tool to combat deforestation is an alternative and renewable source of charcoal for urban use and agricultural products, based on the establishment of agroforestry plantations (trees rows will be intercropped with lines of food crops).
As a result, the Project will have several social and environmental benefits such as (1) CO2 sequestration on land that is currently non-forested and unused, (2) Less pressure on the surrounding natural forests, thanks to the production of charcoal and timber from sustainably managed plantations, and the sensitization of local populations to agroforestry, that is more sustainable and productive than slash-and-burn agriculture or (3) Job creation, increased incomes and local development in a territory heavily affected by unemployment.
In this project, we account for the removals of GHG that occurred through the creation of the plantations: we use the UNFCCC AR-ACM0003 CDM methodology and the VCS Guidance AFOLU Guidance: Example for Calculating the Long-Term Average Carbon Stock for ARR Projects with Harvesting (Version of the 8 March 2011). The project plans to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. The first accreditation period is 30 years. The sequestration of GHG is estimated at 5,000,075 tCO2-e.
vcs-4619:
Ñangareko Forest Reserve, is an AFOLU REDD+ project, under the VCS + CCB standard, located in the province of San Cristobal, which is developed within the Estancia Marangatu, Paraguay, whose objective is the conservation of the Sub-Atlantic Tropical native forest in conjunction with the social development of meliponiculture and ecotourism associated with this activity, as a factor for forest growth and improvement of the economic conditions of the most vulnerable nearby communities in the province.
Its proponents: Zero Carbono SPA developing the project for SEMON SRL, seeking the highest standard of international certification, as well as the highest degree of integrity for its carbon credits, seeking transparency and traceability in all its processes, as well as a clear governance and the participation of local communities as an integral part of the project, seeking to fully comply with the 10 basic principles of carbon.
With 1,592 hectares of native forest, the project is the only real tropical Sub-Atlantic forest reserve in the region, it has a great ecosystemic wealth in terms of flora and fauna, so its protection is of vital importance for the region, considering that Paraguay today has only 12% of its total territory's forests.
The project also has the support of the Paraguayan government, becoming an ITO to follow for those private owners of forests that still maintain them in conservation.
vcs-462: The Sinohydro Inner Mongolia Ximeng Honggeer Wind Power Project (hereafter refers to as the “proposed project”) is to utilize wind resources for electricity generation through the construction of a wind farm with a total capacity of 49.5MW and a 220KV substation in the border area of southeast Abaga Qi and south XilinHot City, Xilinguole League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, P. R. China. The proposed project is invested by Sinohydro Renewable Energy Co. Ltd. The electricity generated from the project will be sold to Inner Mongolia Power Grid, an integral part of the North China Power Grid. The estimated annual net electricity output and emission reductions of the proposed project are 131,970MWh and 141,932tCO2e, respectively. The proposed project is a grid-connected renewable energy project.
vcs-4620:
The project activity is 14MW Waste to Energy Power Plant located at Moshi Kachara Depot, Pimpri, Pune, India. The plant utilizes Refuse-Derived Fuel (“RDF”) as feedstock derived from the separation and sorting of Municipal Solid Waste (“MSW”) excluding the recyclable or potentially hazardous materials from the waste stream. The MSW will be sourced from the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipality area as per the concession agreement with Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.
The main purpose of this project activity is to generate clean form of electricity through waste to energy-based power generation. The project will treat about 700 ton of RDF per day and generate electricity with the installed capacity of 14 MW. The project activity helps to avoid methane emissions from open dump site iand generate renewable electricity, which displaced part of the electricity otherwise supplied by grid connected power plants. The expected average emission reduction from the project is 65,318 tCO2e annually.
vcs-4621:
Shandong Ju County ALM Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Ju County, Rizhao City, Shandong Province of China. The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by the farms taking part to the project and raise the carbon storage in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. The project was implemented by the Ju County Urban Construction Investment Group Co.,Ltd. and Hainan icarbon Ecological Development Co.,Ltd. (hereafter “the project proponent”).
The proposed project is aimed to prevent the soil degradation through adoption of the improved crop land management practices (collectively referred to conservational tillage) to replace the conventional cultivation mode.
Main activities about conservational tillage adopted in the project include： 
Organic fertilizer application (reduce inorganic fertilizer application): 53,422 ha of cropland has reduced the use of chemical fertilizer.
Straw incorporation (Improve crop residue management): straw in 53,422 ha of cropland has been buried and returned, with the depth of 30 cm.
A total of 53,422 ha of farmland has been managed under conservation tillage, The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 2,684,200 tCO2e from 01-Jan-2021 to 31-Dec- 2040, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 134,210 tCO2e.
For the project the validation date and the specific date of the first monitoring period of this project has not been determined, and will be supplemented in the latest PD.
vcs-4622:
Grupo Transportes Monterrey S.A.P.I. de C.V (GTM) is a company in the road freight transportation sector in Mexico, where the baseline scenario is the situation where, in the absence of project activity, the fleet used for freight transportation in the different routes does not change in technology or type of fuel. Throughout the project, cargo is transported using less GHG-intensive modes of transport.
The baseline considers a fleet growth of 12.5%. The existing fleet has 94% Diesel vehicles and 6% compressed natural gas (CNG), which is maintained throughout the period. According to the methodology, the average tons transported annually, and the total distance traveled are considered.
The project includes re-newing vehicles from the existing fleet, with vehicles with better technology in both fuel efficiency and emission control, maintaining the CNG-Diesel vehicle composition and the annual growth of the baseline.
According to the methodology, the project boundary includes the following: Fleet to which low-emission vehicles are introduced:
a)	The geographical area in which these vehicles operate.
b)	Auxiliary facilities such as fueling stations, workshops, and service stations that are used by vehicles.
The conditions which govern the operation of the fleet (e.g., tariffs, regulations) should be homogeneous within the project boundary. The origin and end points of the routes carried out, where complete coverage is observed in Mexico, reaching the 32 states.
Baseline emissions are calculated as per the consolidated Methodology AMS III.S version 04.0.
The annual estimated emission reductions are 67,775 tCO2/yr. The total emission reductions for the period of 10 years of crediting years are 677,553 tCO2.
vcs-4623:
The objective of the REDD+ Mwali Project is to tackle deforestation on the island of Moheli, in the Union of the Comoros. Emissions reductions are to be obtained by preventing or avoiding conversion of forested lands into no-forest lands. The island of Moheli exhibits a complex mosaic of nine different ecosystems. Some of these zones are valuable for the number of species they harbor, or for the proportion of rare species that are supported in suitable living conditions. Others play an essential role in the regulation of water cycles or protect other ecosystems from the effects of climate events. The forest zone located along the ridge in the center of the island is home, among others, to Livingstone's fruit bat (Pteropus livingstonii), a species which is endemic to the Comoros islands and emblematic of the Moheli primary forest. This species, also known as the Comoro flying fox, is threatened with extinction. The agroforestry zones on the park's slopes provide shelter to many species of animals, including birds, reptiles, and a few mammals (Lemuridae (Eulemur mongoz). Coastal vegetation is the habitat of the coconut crab (Birgus latro), also an endangered species. This vegetation also serves to protect the coastal zone where green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas) commonly reproduce. The green sea turtle population in Moheli is one of the largest in the world. This configuration of interdependent natural areas led Comoros to create the Moheli National Park (Parc National de Moheli, PNM), and now the entire island is recognized as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve (UNESCO, 2021).
The Moheli forests have been steadily shrinking since the 1950s. This trend has persisted over the 2007-2019, the baseline period of the project, with an annual deforestation rate of 1.65%, according to project analysis. Habitat loss then represents one of the most serious threats to local species, many of which are endemic.
vcs-4625:
Gauthans are village-based cow-dung processing premises that have emerged as multi-activity centres supporting vermicomposting production and livelihood-based activities for Self-help groups in the Chhattisgarh state of India. The avoidance of methane emissions is achieved with treatments of aerobic composting with the help of Worms, which replaces the baseline scenario where the manure would undergo anaerobic decomposition conditions. 

In this project, the collected cattle manure is utilised through a composting process with the help of Worms. Worms convert the cattle manure aerobically into vermicompost used for application to lands.  Without this project, the farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere.

Utilising cattle manure for vermicompost preparation has the primary benefit of reduced methane emission along with secondary benefit of replacing fertilisers in farm inputs which contribute for emission reduction. During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 117,000 tons of dairy manure would be treated and composted, with 30,000tons of organic fertiliser generated per year. Besides, the GHG emissions are expected to reduce 59918 tCO2e per year and 419424 tCO2e in a 7-year crediting period.
vcs-4626: The Regeneration Meghalaya Project is a grouped project under ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation) category that aims to increase tree cover through planting a majority of indigenous trees that are suited to local conditions of the bioregion. The project is located in the Khasi, Ri Bhoi Jaintia and Garo Hills regions, in the Northeastern state of Meghalaya, India. Regeneration Meghalaya will plant trees across up to 30,000 ha of wasteland. The project aims to plant up to 40 - 64 million trees sequestering up to 23 Million tonnes of CO2e in Meghalaya. In addition, the project aims to reach a significant number of beneficiaries over a period of 35 years. The GHG (greenhouse gas) removals in the project would be created by improving the land though planting new trees and plants in the eligible project areas. The project’s broader aims are to restore ecological integrity, reduce soil erosion, improve ecological functions, increase biodiversity and improve livelihoods. In this regard, the project will monitor and report on the co-benefits for climate adaptation, biodiversity and people through the climate, community and biodiversity standard (CCB). The project taps into and is led by indigenous knowledge custodians to accelerate landscape restoration and sustainably develop both tree-based and non-tree based products to create value chains and grow sustainable livelihoods. The project goals are aligned to the local needs and existing land use systems, farmer-led species selection that prioritise indigenous and naturalised species, and customised solutions to challenges identified by local stakeholders. The project area is home to the Khasi, Jaintia and Garo tribes, and the majority of the land is held under private / clan ownership, with some community control and management.
vcs-4627: The objective of the project is to increase the tree cover outside forest (ToF) areas through ARR activities on privately owned lands of farmers who belong to the local communities. Some plantation is also undertaken on common lands under the village or Gram Panchayat if the GP wishes to include the same. Apart from ARR activities, the project also works closely with the communities to address livelihoods. The project aims to secure the financial security of the local farming and other communities through planting of farmer friendly trees to support traditional crop-based agriculture systems and through support through supplementary community-based interventions. The PP implements the project through service providers, who work closely with farmers to assess willingness to participate in the project, engage them in project activities and undertake project activities with high levels of participation from the local communities. The project team on the ground are employed from the local community, and care is taken to ensure participation of women and other marginalized members of the community.
vcs-4629:
Heilongjiang Lishu Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Lishu County, Jilin Province, China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices including no tillage/reduced tillage，returning straw in fields and applying organic fertilizer, and to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land.
Since straw contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, returning straw to the field can effectively use organic fertilizer resources and increase soil organic matter (SOM). Straw returning to the field also can improve soil physical and chemical properties, enhance soil aggregate structure, and increase soil permeability. Applying organic fertilizer can reduce nitrous oxide emission compared to synthetic fertilizer.
The project plans to implement no tillage/reduced tillage practice, straw returning and organic fertilizer application in 15,385 ha of agricultural land in the first crediting period to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) and reduce nitrous oxide emission. The project proponent not only introduced more efficient and appropriate tillage method with Lishu County Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau to the farmers, but also provide technical training and support to the farmers.
The scenario existing prior to the project’s implementation is primarily conventional tillage without straw returning, which cause greater soil disturbance and increase the loss of SOM.
During the first crediting period from 20-Nov-2022 to 19-Nov-2042, the project is expected to generate GHG emission removals of 1,110,180 tCO2e, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 55,509 tCO2e.
vcs-463: CNG, LNG or biogas powered heavy duty vehicles (HDVs) emit less greenhouse gas emissions per unit of service in comparison to the same type of diesel powered HDVs, that represent the baseline vehicles (with a market share of 99%).  The project activity includes CNG and LNG HDVs operating in fleets located in various countries worldwide sold as entire new vehicles by Westport Innovations or its joint ventures.  The average annual greenhouse gas emission reductions over the crediting period of 10 years is estimated ex ante as 1,065,146 tCO2eq.  Baseline and project emission calculations as well as leakage and monitoring are based on the approved CDM methodology AMS III.C Emission reductions by low greenhouse gas emitting vehicles.  The start date of the crediting period is 01/01/2009.
vcs-4630: The project is an initiative of various NGOS for the plantation activities. IICare Foundation is the aggregator and would act as the project proponent. The plantation activities are based in India. Project aims to plant 1 million trees which will contribute in carbon sequestration and promote the message of ‘green living’ among local community. The project plans the introduction of trees to farms and other landscapes for multiple productive purposes which could play a key role in climate change mitigation and adaptation and help increase tree cover at the selected sites. The project started in August 2020. The project encompasses scattered parcels of land measuring about 800 hectares distributed in 14 Indian states namely Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Rajasthan and Haryana with over 60% on aggregate basis in just two western states of Maharashtra and Gujarat.
vcs-4631: Located in the municipality of Las Gordas in the Maria Trinidad Sanchez province of Dominican Republic, the Ambrosia coconut farm set across 2,132 hectares. The project aims at rehabilitating the established coconut palm plantation back to full productivity and to establish additional 800-hectares of organic cocoa plantation inter-cropped with coconut palms. Ambrosia farm also has 843 hectares of natural forests that are and will continue to be protected, which will ensure the provision of important ecosystem services such as natural pest control, wind protection, and water flow regulation, while preserving wildlife corridor, key species habitat protection. The Project Area applies organic agricultural practices to produce premium cocoa for export and a range of premium-quality coconut products, such as virgin coconut oil, coconut water and sugar, which are sold domestically and abroad.  In Ambrosia, the promotion of agroforestry system has the goal of increasing the soil organic carbon, as well as the aboveground and below ground biomass, while recovering the soil health and fertility through time. Other relevant agricultural practice under implementation is referred to cover crop planting in bare soil areas. Regarding social impacts, the Project currently provides full-time employment to a total of 34 local people and over 70 seasonal workers, who live in the surrounding communities of the project area. Employees have financial security due to a fixed steady income paid according to legal labor legislation that guarantees the access to the Dominican Republic legal benefits. On the biodiversity aspects, the Project maintains conservation areas where species have made their habitats. Also, the project has established and reinforced a non-hunting policy, to prevent this practice in the project area. As a supporting measure, biodiversity studies are planned to be conducted periodically to make sure population and numbers of present species are maintained.
vcs-4632:
On the eastern Caribbean coast of Panama lies Cuango Project, an area of 1,471 hectares between a production and forest area. Cuango is transforming degraded grasslands into a long-term producing perennial agroforestry system applying regenerative agricultural practices such as integrated pest management, implementation ofa planting system that mimics the natural growth of combined native and exotic plants. Additionally,the farm applies a rationale use of herbicides and fertilizers, intercropping of crops such as plantains, andtemporary nitrogen fixing trees (Madre cacao -Gliricidia sepium, pigeon peas – Cajanus cajan) and timber trees (Almendro - Dypterix panamensis, Zapatero - Hieronyma alchorneoides, Cedro - Cedrela odorata, Mayo - Vochysia ferruginea), plant species that act as wind and rain breakers, providing sustenance for pollinators and insects, and nutrients to the soil. On the forest area the farm also has 660 hectares of natural primary and secondary rainforests, playing an important role as biological corridors of natural rain forests, which have been put aside for wildlife conservation and the provision of ecosystem services. By reforesting degrading pastures through agroforestry, Cuango Farmexpects to enhance landscape connectivity and increase wildlife populations on the farm while promoting carbon removals. The farm’s environmental policy is based on national, local and community environmental regulations, focused on the care and enhancement of natural resources, and the prevention and mitigation of negative impacts.
The farm also employs a total of 200 workers who benefit from long-term contracts, workers are divided into two main groups, one from local project zone communities and one group constituted of indigenous people from Bocas del Toro. The Project seeks to create verified emission reductions/removals under the Verified Carbon Standard and the Climate, Community and Biodiversity Standard.
vcs-4633: The Fortaleza Ituxi II REDD+ Project aims at protecting private forests located in one of the regions having the highest deforestation rate in the Amazon Biome: the municipality of Lábrea. The south region of the municipality of Lábrea has already been reached by the “Arc of Deforestation”: for the last 10 years, Lábrea has been one of the most deforested municipalities in the Amazon Biome. Besides the damage caused to natural ecosystems, the land-use changes have provoked severe social conflicts through processes of land-grabbing and installation of agriculture and cattle ranching activities, contributing to the expulsion of family-scale forest extractives from that region. The primary objective of the Fortaleza Ituxi II REDD+ Project is to avoid planned (APD) and unplanned (AUD) deforestation in an area of 69,185.87 ha of Amazonian forest. The APD REDD project area is expected to avoid a predicted 5,153.00 ha of legal deforestation, equating to 1,721,301 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, an annual average of 57,376 tCO2e. The AUD REDD project area is expected to avoid a predicted 64,023.44 ha of illegal deforestation, equating to 16,066,567 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 535,552 tCO2e.
vcs-4634:
Muyuan Bengbu AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Anhui Province (hereafter referred to as the project) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from swine farms in Bengbu City, Anhui Province, China, which are owned by Muyuan Foods Co.,Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm shall install one AWMS, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 266.590 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMSs. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 240,368 tCO2e emission reductions will be attained annually.

The project generates power at 11 kV which is recorded and stepped down to 440 V for the usage of the company

vcs-4644: The Scarcies Mangrove Rewilding Project is a smallholder mangrove reforestation project in the Scarcies estuaries, northern Sierra Leone. The grouped project area covers four chiefdoms in the Kambia and Port Loko districts. Approximately 270,000 people live in these four chiefdoms . The Project will generate GHG emission removals through mangrove reforestation in abandoned rice paddies (VCS AFOLU project activity categories Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR), and Restoring Wetland Ecosystems (RWE)). The Project will be validated and verified under the VCS and CCB standards.
vcs-4645:
Wudi Lvhe Composting project (hereinafter as “the project”) installs a set of organic fertilizersproduction lines with an annual output of 50,000 tones to treat the manure from the cattle 
farms in Wudi Country, Binzhou city, Shandong Province, China. The project is owned by WudiCounty Lvhe Organic Fertilizer Co., LTD. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane
emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and microbial strains.In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic 
lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.In this project, the collected cattle manure will be utilized through a fermentation composting 
process. After the fermentation, both solids and wastewater are then treated by a fertilizer production system, of which can produce organic fertilizers used for application to lands. Without 
this project, the farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere.
During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 165,000 tons of cattle manure would be treated and composted, with 50,000 tons of organic fertilizer generated per 
year. Besides, the GHG emissions is expected to reduce 57,116 t CO2e per year and 571,160 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.
vcs-4646: Since its inception in 1999, over 170,000 participants organized into over 26,000 TIST Small Groups have planted over 25 million trees in Tanzania, India, Kenya, and Uganda - accomplishing GhG sequestration through tree planting, creating a potential long-term income stream, and developing sustainable environments and livelihoods. Kenya 011 is a subset of the TIST project in Kenya and applies to 12,892 Small Groups, 79,089 Participants, 53,357 active Project Areas, and 23,747 hectares.  TIST farmers use a mosaic restoration approach, planting on thousands of individual farms spread across the landscape. The individual farms are found throughout Kenya and concentrated around Mt Kenya.
vcs-4649: The purpose of project activity is extraction and capture of methane enriched bio-gas generated from treatment of waste water. The captured biogas is treated further to remove impurities and bottled as compressed biogas to supply to oil company for replacing fossil origin natural gas used in vehicles for transportation. In case any shutdown of CBG plant excess methane gas will be flared in controlled manner in an open flare.
vcs-465: The project activity is being undertaken by Bajaj Hindusthan Ltd at its 9,000 tonnes of cane per day (tcd) Thanabhawan sugar factory. The project activity involves installing of a new power plant next to an existing power plant, at the sugar factory in Uttar Pradesh, India. The power plant will use biomass, bagasse, a renewable biomass material that is produced from the milling of cane to generate electricity for supply to the grid.
vcs-4650:
The project activity aims to improve municipal solid waste (MSW) management through the
installation of an anaerobic digestion system to generate Compressed Biogas (CBG) in the city
of Indore, Madhya Pradesh in India. The installed capacity of the project is to treat 500TPD of
segregated MSW to generate approx. 42,500 N-m3/day of CBG. CBG generated is purified and
processed for various thermal applications such as use in vehicles use for transportation or
bottled for use in Industrial energy applications. Technical details of the equipment installed
in the project are provided in section 1.11 of this PD.
The project is implemented by Indo Enviro Integrated Solutions Private Limited (IEISL). The
project is commissioned on 22-May-2022 and is in operation since.
In the absence of the project activity, MSW would be left to decay in the landfill site without
any controlled treatment and such decay would lead to methane emission, a greenhouse gas,
into the atmosphere. CBG generated in the project is a direct replacement of fossil fuels (e.g.
CNG) used in the baseline. CNG combustion in the baseline would have resulted into CO2
emissions.
vcs-4651: The New Zealand Indigenous Forest Regeneration Project is an Improved Forest Management, Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF) project located in New Zealand that was developed using the VM0012 methodology. The project is a grouped project, with the project area encompassing both the North and South Islands of New Zealand, with project instances geographically dispersed throughout. Project instances predominantly include properties of Pinus radiata plantations that were established with the objective of harvesting the timber for commercial purposes. New Zealand Forestry Removals Limited (an entity within the New Zealand Carbon Farming Group) will either own or have a legal right to control, such properties in order to convert the plantations into protected forests, with the long-term goal of transitioning them to permanent native forest.
vcs-4654:
Hengyang Peike Animal Manure Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is a centralized manure treatment plant established in Hengyang County using aerobic composting system. The project collects and composts swine, chicken, and duck manure produced by livestock farms in Hengyang County to produce organic fertilizer.
The project introduces the aerobic composting system that is designed to treat swine, chicken, and duck manure from livestock farms in Hengyang County to produce organic fertilizer. The project comprises of pretreatment system, composting system, and fertilizer packaging system. It is estimated that approximately 50,000 tonnes of manure can be treated annually, and the annual organic fertilizer production is 30,000 tonnes. Part of the organic fertilizer will be sold to nearby farmers and most of it will be sold to local businesses.
vcs-4655:
The Improved Grazing management in Mosaic Forest-Grasslands Landscapes in the centre-north of Argentina aims to remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere by implementing regenerative grazing practices across different properties of the northern-central region of Argentina. The fundamental axis of this approach is the division of large pastures into smaller paddocks, implementing rotational grazing, which allows periods of rest and recovery for the land.
The grouped project area covers 1,212,583 km2 in the north-center of Argentina. The region is dominated by grasslands with varying degrees of tree or shrub cover, ranging from savanna ecosystems characterized by sparse tree density to mosaic landscapes of grasslands and patches of native forests. These types of ecosystems, which integrate trees, forages, and livestock, can create significant synergies that improve soil health, while sequestering significant amounts of carbon from the atmosphere.

Developing these regenerative grazing activities in areas with remnants of native trees or forests also plays and important role in the conservation of natural habitats. These productive systems mitigate climate change without the need for a change in land use, thereby safeguarding habitats that support a rich diversity of native flora and fauna. On this basis, the Project will in the future develop plans for biodiversity conservation and integration of the communities involved in each socio-ecosystem. In this way, conservation will be integrated into productive systems, encouraging landowners to change their paradigms about non-productive areas of ranches.

The first Project Activity Instance is being carried out in the “La Alicia” property, located in the province of Santa Fe. The values obtained for this PAI determined that the project activities can result in a net GHG emissions reduction and removals of ~ 231,829 tCO2e in the SOC pool, with an annual average of 11,590 tCO2e in 20 years of the project.
vcs-4656: The Guangdong Foshan Improved Forest Management Project is implemented in Gaoming District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province of China by Foshan Gaoming District Forestry Research Institute. The total area is 1760.4ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) in the conversion from logged to protected forest.
vcs-4657: This small scale PoA involves the distribution of energy efficient cooking stoves to households in The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. The majority of households in rural areas of The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia cook over open fires1, and this leads to a very significant consumption of wood, as well as a major health risk. To combat this problem, this PoA will distribute low cost, high efficiency stove designs that use considerably less wood than conventional open fires. Users are households who previously used inefficient, traditional open fireplaces. Deforestation and degradation have become a major concern in rural areas of Africa, as wood demand for household energy largely exceeds the available renewable woody biomass. By reducing the fuel wood consumption, the project activity hence reduces greenhouse gas emissions stemming from the use of non-renewable biomass. More information on the project can be found at CDM Project ID 9769: https://cdm.unfccc.int/ProgrammeOfActivities/poa_db/5TE6HLP1Z4KOABSDI873YQCFGXW2RM/view?cp=1
vcs-4658: The Lavardin IFM (Improved Forest Management) project aims to sequester carbon through improvements in the management of commercial Eucalyptus plantations in the southeastern and central-eastern region of Uruguay. The project will implement changes in the current plantation management regime, which includes two scenarios (A and B). Scenario A involves a current management of Eucalyptus globulus plantations with a 10-year harvest cycle for pulp production, covering a total planted area of 9,436 hectares. Scenario B covers a total planted area of 5,543 hectares and involves the current management of E. globulus and E. maidenii plantations with a commercial thinning at 10 years and a final harvest for high-quality wood at 20 years. The Lavardin IFM project will be implemented following the Verra Standards and is designed to have the same environmental and social impacts as all the carbon projects presented in the VCS, which sequester carbon through commercial plantations in Uruguay. Through a substantial capital investment, Lavardin will implement a unique management regime for the region (regime C) to sequester more atmospheric carbon dioxide. This new regime involves changing the species planted, selecting new ones which will increase productivity, and adjusting the rotation ages to maximize carbon sequestration and manage forests sustainably
vcs-4659: The One Mara Carbon Project (OMCP) is an ecosystem-level conservation initiative that aims to protect ecological resources and provide economic and social co-benefits for communities by incentivizing conservancy formation and grassland restoration in the Maasai Mara landscape in Kenya. The goal of OMCP is to restore the degraded rangelands through improved grazing management and prevent further loss of grasslands by providing alternative livelihoods for communities, build resilient conservancies, ensure biodiversity conservation, and enhance tourism. This region is world-renown for the expansive rangelands where agropastoralists and wildlife co-exist. However, historical land sub-division into small, fenced land parcels and long term extensive grazing by livestock has led to land degradation, including the gradual loss in soil organic carbon (SOC). Communities living within the ecosystem depend on the condition of the grasslands to provide livelihoods that will meet their socio-economic needs. Implementing climate change mitigation measures and halting land degradation are vital to ensuring the longevity of this world-famous conservation area.
vcs-466: The project activity occurs in expansion cells at the McCommas Bluff landfill. Although the landfill is required under NSPS requirements to collect and destroy landfill gas, expansion cells are not required to install a gas collection system until five years from the date on which they initially accept waste. The project activity consists of the voluntary installation of a gas collection system prior to the effective date of NSPS requirements in expansion areas of the landfill. Gas collected is purified in Dallas Clean Energy’s processing plant at the landfill and injected into a pipeline distribution network or flared.
vcs-4660: PotlatchDeltic Corporation (PCH) is developing a nature based services project, titled the Legacy Forest Climate Initiative (Legacy), to generate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions and removals by converting privately owned operational forest lands to protected forest lands. The project area includes non-contiguous lands owned and operated by PCH located in Alabama, Arkansas, Georgia, and South Carolina, USA. Legacy will contribute to sustainable development as defined by and tracked against the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The project will contribute to (at a minimum) SDGs 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), 13 (Climate Action), and 15 (Life on Land).
vcs-4661: Through this program, we plan to reduce green house gas emissions and enhance livelihood of rural and tribal communities in the project area by equipping them with improved cook stoves, generating employment opportunities, and increasing awareness on both GHG emissions. This community-engaging program will introduce clean cooking practices, reduce Household Air Pollution (HAP), and lower health risks through our own specially designed and manufactured high-energy efficient improved cookstoves - Shri Stoves.
