vcs-4667:
TTCA Organic Composting Project in Attapeu province, Laos was constructed to produce organic fertilizer with an annual output of 34,000 tons from the treatment of cattle manure from livestock farmers in Attapeu province and from biodegradable waste residue such as Crotalaria spp. (a nitrogen fixation belonged to legume family which is used for rotation in sugarcane plantation), bagasse, mud and ash from a sugarcane processing factory in the site. The project is invested in and owned by TTC Attapeu Sugar Cane Sole Co., Ltd. The project aim is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic decomposition in a windrow composting process of cattle manure, Crotalaria spp. waste and sugarcane processing waste (mud, ash, bagasse) in a landfill site.
The aerated composting process will avoid methane emissions and will also result in compost as a product that can be utilized as organic fertilizer for agricultural purposes. With financial support from the carbon credit, this project will demonstrate that the carbon credit finance mechanism can catalyze environmentally sustainable and financially viable waste management practices.
Its operation will be made sustainable by covering the installation and operation cost through sale of compost and revenue from CDM. The CDM benefits would act as a means of subsidizing the cost of compost production to ensure the project’s financial sustainability. 
The final compost obtained will be sold to organic sugarcane plantations in the province which lateral supply sugarcane to processing factory. The construction start date of the project was 28/01/2021 and was put into operation on the 16/11/2021. 
It is estimated that an average of 10,823 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 108,230 tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixed crediting period.
vcs-4668: Alxa Left Banner Improved Grassland Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Alashan Left Banner, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. The project is aimed to improve the rotation of grazing animals, limit the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restore degraded land by replanting with grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term. The project proponent is Inner Mongolia Cili Agricultural Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Project Proponent or PP).
vcs-4669: Energon Renewables (BD) Limited (ERBL) is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) formed by Orion Group is implementing a 100MW solar PV plant near Moidhara village of Bagerhat district in the Khulna division of Bangladesh. The proposed project is a greenfield project activity. The project will achieve the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions through the displacement of grid electricity which is mainly fossil-fuel dominated, by electricity generated through solar power which is a renewable source. In absence of this project activity equivalent amount of electricity would have been delivered to the grid by existing fossil fuel-based power plants or by addition of more fossil fuel based power plants. The baseline scenario of the proposed project is the same as the scenario prior to the start of the implementation of the project activity.
vcs-467: The project activity involves recovery of fugitive biogas from the wastewater released from tapioca starch processing plant. The recovered biogas is used in a boiler to generate heat for the starch drying process as well as used in gas engines to generate electricity. The produced electricity will be used to meet the power requirement of the starch processing plant and may later be supplied to national-owned grid in the future. After satisfying the above demands, surplus biogas, if any, is flared for safety purpose. The project has a total electrical generation capacity of less than 15 MWel and will generate emission reductions less than 60 ktCO2e per year.
vcs-4670:
The project’s goal is to remove greenhouse gas (GHG) by implementing sustainable grazing management and controlled burning phases across the Limpopo - Lipadi (L-L) reserve. The baseline scenarios include loss of perennial grasses and destruction of indigenous trees and shrubs from wildlife grazing leading to erosion, soil carbon loss, water runoff and reduced wildlife carrying capacity. The project type that corresponds to the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) is “Improved Grassland Management (IGM)” of the project category of “Agricultural Land Management (ALM)”. The project aims to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) through adjustment of burning and controlled grazing. 

The L-L wildlife conservation reserve covers an area of 20,712 hectares with all land units assembled from a contiguous group of traditional Botswana former cattle farms in the Tuli Block region. This area would establish phase 1 of a project that can incorporate further farms and common areas within the locale. A proposed phase 2 would see the project activities expanded to nearby cattle farms and game reserve areas, with the Limpopo-Lipadi team organizing the implementation of grassland management and/or controlled grazing techniques. 
Prior to the land becoming a wildlife conservation area, the farm was used for cattle ranching and limited cropping. There is overwhelming evidence of over grazing and the land when it was assembled in 2004 was severely degraded. This was compounded by drought and the conservation reserve had reached a tipping point in recent years, leading to further soil erosion and grassland degradation, to the detriment of the resident wildlife and ecosystem.
vcs-4671: The ANGELIM REDD+ Project protects 21,261.02 hectare of Amazon rainforest from deforestation in Aripuanã, Juína and Castanheira municipalities of Mato Grosso State – Brazil. This project estimates a total GHG emissions reduction of 3,303,261 tons of CO2eq during 40 years of project by avoiding unplanned deforestation of 8,915 ha, with an average annual emissions reduction of 82,582 tons of CO2eq. The project consists of four farms: Continental, União, Recanto do Sinuelo and Cachoeirinha.
vcs-4672:
Jiangxi Jinwang Waste Aluminum Recycling Project(hereafter referred to as the project) aims to produce the aluminum product by reprocessing the waste aluminum products (like disassemble aluminum from scrap cars, scrap the motorcycle disassembles the aluminum, scrap aluminum wire and cable, used cans etc.) and to replace the same aluminum product produced from the raw materials. The total production capacity is about 180,000 tons of aluminum product per year, Among them, 15,500 tons of waste cans are used every year. The Project located in  Yujiang County, Jiangxi Province, China and is developed and operated by Jiangxi Jinwang Aluminum Co., Ltd. (hereinafter called the Project Owner).
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of aluminum alloy was produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well.
The first crediting period of the project is from 28-March-2022 to 27-March-2029. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions are 58,871 tCO2e and the total estimated GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period are 412,097 tCO2e
vcs-4674:
The Selva Norte Conservation project (CSN+) is a grouped REDD+ initiative developed by Projet Café Selva Norte Eleva Finca Inc and ECOTIERRA, supported by Café Selva Norte SAC, and financed by URAPI Sustainable Land Use Fund. CSN REDD+ is pioneering and unique in its kind, working with farmer communities, local governments, conservation organizations and private forest owners to enable them to access climate finance tools and consolidate their conservation efforts.

The project aims to reduce GHG emissions related to deforestation, over 200 000 ha in the department of Amazonas, Cajamarca and San Martin, in the north of Peru. The project will also contribute to consolidate an important conservation corridor and protect key ecosystems in the region.

Over the life of the project, we aim to diversify the income of more than 20 local organizations or communities. Currently, small and medium-scale conservation areas have little investment capacity and low or no income, a situation that can influence deforestation and forest degradation, thus generating loss or reduction of carbon stocks. CSN+ will make use of technical and financial tools available for conservation to generate greater benefits and create a diversified portfolio of activities, with the objective of creating a sustainable model for conservation.

CSN+ will enable the creation of a strong partnership between the communities, URAPI  and ECOTIERRA with the objective of reducing forest degradation and deforestation processes, introducing high productivity agricultural systems, ensuring the sustainable development of value chains; empowering producers, cooperatives, associations and the community in general; creating mechanisms for enforce conservation; and increase environmental awareness of the communities.
vcs-4675: Huoshengyuan Composting Project in Mianyang City (hereafter referred to as the project) installs a set of organic fertilizer production lines with an annual capacity of 50,000 tons to treat manure (cow and swine manure) from livestock farms and biomass waste residue, i.e.straw, in Santai County, Mianyang City, Sichuan Province, China. The project is invested and owned by Sichuan Huoshengyuan Biotechnology Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass waste residue straw. This project was designed to treat the cow, swine manure and biomass waste residue (straw) to produce organic fertilizer. This project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system. It is estimated that approximately 117,000 tonnes of manure and 32,000 tonnes of biomass waste residue can be treated annually, therefore total 149,000 tonnes of waste can be composted aerobically for this project. A portion of the organic fertilizer obtained is sold to the local government for improving the quality of local high-standard farmland, and another portion is sold to local farmers, farmer cooperatives and businesses. The construction start date of the project is 6 August 2019 and was put into operation on 1 January 2022. The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue. It is estimated that 58,686 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 586,856 tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixing crediting period.
vcs-4676: This IFM project is roughly 3,800 acres and is projected to generate 152,000 credits by extending the rotation age of a mixed hardwood stratum and a planted pine stratum.
vcs-4677:
Jinshan Songlin Market Swine Manure Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Wanchun Village, Langxia Town, Jinshan District, Shanghai, P.R China. The project builds an anaerobic animal manure treatment system for the treatment of swine manure in Jinshan Modern Agricultural Park Songlin Market  Swine Farm. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. At this stage, part of the recovered biogas will be used to generate electricity at the biogas power plant for the daily use of the swine farm. According to the feasibility study report, the designed installed capacity of the biogas power plant is 0.52MW. Waste heat recovery boiler will also be installed at the biogas power plant to recover and supply waste heat to the auxiliary equipment of the project. The residual waste from the CSTR digesters will be used as organic fertilizer directly on agricultural land in the project vicinity.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system (lagoon) and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas.
vcs-4679: The agricultural sector in India faces challenges due to traditional waste disposal methods of open field burning and decay of biomass, leading to greenhouse gas emissions and environmental degradation. Together for Restoration presents Project Reignite, aimed at transforming agricultural waste into biochar for soil enrichment in India, with an initial cohort of 5,000 farmers in the state of Odisha. The project employs flame curtain pyrolysis in steel-shield soil pits, producing biochar that is mixed with manure and applied to soil. Estimated to remove 110,760 tCO2e annually and 775,320 tCO2e over a seven-year crediting period, the project offers a triple win: removing carbon, enhancing soil fertility, and uplifting marginalised local communities.
vcs-4680: The purpose of this project activity is the introduction and distribution of electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers which will displace the use of fossil fuel-based mainly motor gasoline-fueled vehicles in the transportation sector. The project is owned and implemented by Wardwizard Innovations & Mobility Limited. In the absence of the proposed project activity, the beneficiaries/users would have been used the motor gasoline-powered vehicles for the transportation purpose which will lead to greenhouse emissions into the atmosphere
vcs-4681:
The YBYRÁ REDD+ Project is a unique REDD+ Project, composed by 74 rural private properties with a project area of 76,481.34 hectare of Amazon rainforest. The project is located in four municipalities: Paragominas, Ipixuna do Pará, Tomé-Açu and Ulianópolis, in the state of Pará, Brazil. The main goals are forest conservation and reduction of GHG emissions of 12,065,803.14 tCO2 in 30 years by avoiding deforestation of 38,317.74 ha in the Project area. 
Pará explores unsustainably the Amazon Forest since its historical occupation. In 2021, almost 25% deforested areas in Brazil were in Pará.  The document known as “Deforestation Arc” presented a list with 52 cities considered priority for prevention, monitoring, and control actions against deforestation  in the Amazonian region (decree nº 6.321/2007 and Ordinance n° 428 (2018) by the Ministry of Environment). The list includes Paragominas and Ulianópolis. 
The deforestation of the amazon forest in the region of the project is due to anthropic activities: timber exploration, pasture for cattle raising and agriculture. The pressure on turning forest into non-forested areas is consequence of the expansion of these economic activities, leading to invasions of private properties. For the project region, the main land use activity is the implementation of pasture for cattle raising. In relation to the social aspects, most of the communities are formed by rural farmers with social vulnerabilities, with presence of food insecurity, low income and lack of job opportunity.
Considering the aspects presented, the Project’s main goals, through conservation of forest areas and combating deforestation of the Amazon Forest, are: 1) To promote adaptations to climate change in the region; 2) To improve the quality of life of the population that lives close to the forest and 3) To conserve biodiversity and ecosystem services, through environmental education actions and foment initiatives to connect forest fragments of the PA.
vcs-4684: The project is installation of 8 MW hydro project in Lao PDR. The project is being developed by EDL-Generation Public Company in Champasak province of Lao PDR.  The primary purpose of the project is to generate electricity to the Lao Power Grid. Total installed capacity of the project is 8MW, provided by two (2) Kaplan turbine and the unit capacity is 4MW. Project is commissioned on 14/12/2022 with an expected average annual electricity output of 22,640 MWh. The baseline scenario of the project is continuation of the present situation, i.e., electricity supplied from the power grid. By displacing part of the power generated by thermal power plants, the project is therefore expected to reduce equivalent CO2 emissions from grid-connected power plants.
vcs-4686:
“PUR - Agroforestry Project in coffee landscapes of Costa Rica” began in 2020 in the west of the country in a coffee production cluster known as La Giorgia. The objective of the project is to plant trees under agroforestry models with small and medium-sized coffee producers certified as AAA producers of the Nespresso program, who want to engage in more sustainable agricultural practices to improve resilience to climate change. 
PUR is implementing this agroforestry project, with the support of 3 local implementing partners (ECOM, VOLCAFE and ASANA) and coffee farmers to plant trees in their coffee lands and at the landscape level. The implementing partners oversee operations of the project providing technical support, training, and free access to seedlings to farmers. 
The project is being implemented in coffee plantations established in the 1920s. Historically the coffee landscape has had little or no shade within the crop. Without the project, Farmers engaged in the project are small scale farmers with very little financial resources: without the project, they wouldn’t have the capacity to invest in tree planting since it can be an expensive activity, especially under agroforestry complex and diversified models.
Main objectives of the project are:
●	Climate change mitigation through carbon removals generated by tree-planting activities.
●	Increase climate change resilience of agricultural lands.
●	Rehabilitation and restoration of degraded lands.
vcs-4687:
The Tueré REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Brascomp  Compensados do Brasil S.A. and aims to promote forest conservation, maintain carbon stocks and mitigate climate change by reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from land use changes. In addition to  climate benefits, the Project also aims to generate social benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and improving the well-being of surrounding communities, in addition to environmental benefits through actions aimed at the conservation of local fauna and flora.
The Project Area has 135,342 ha of Amazon forest, located in the mesoregion of Marajó, in the municipality of Portel, state of Pará, and is located on the banks of the Anapu and Tueré Rivers. Communities have been identified that are directly or indirectly influenced by the Project, and that are geographically close to the Project Area and depend on its ecosystem services.
vcs-4689: The Ateles REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and AgroSB Agropecuária and aims to promote forest conservation and mitigate climate change by reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from changes in land use. It is made up of a significant part of the Amazon rainforest, located in the municipality of São Félix do Xingú, in the southeast of the state of Pará. The entire project is part of the APA Triunfo do Xingu, a conservation unit with the greatest pressure from deforestation in Brazil, which over the last few decades has suffered major threats to the maintenance of its forest remnants due to large-scale illegal deforestation. Furthermore, the region is of great importance in terms of its biodiversity, as it is located in the Tapajós Endemism Center, a place with a high concentration of rare and endemic species. In addition to climate benefits, the project aims to ensure the conservation and protection of biodiversity and natural resources through mitigating and preventative measures such as strengthening asset surveillance, social inclusion and regional socio-economic development through alternative practices to deforestation and the development and strengthening of value chains, the establishment of a biodiversity conservation program, promoting in situ monitoring of fauna and flora in the Project Area, the development of strategies that seek to bring land security and territorial belonging, as well as the strengthening of local governance, stimulated mainly by the engagement and involvement of stakeholders.
vcs-469: The project activity operates low GHG emitting rolling stocks having regenerative braking system in Delhi Metro Rail. The project activity replaces the conventional electro-dynamic rheostatic braking technology, with regenerative braking technology fitted rolling stocks. The regenerated electrical energy reduces the consumption of equivalent grid electrical energy required by the powering trains, thereby conserving electrical energy and subsequently leading to GHG emission reduction. The DMRC System is designed for rolling stock where coaches are equipped with 3 phase AC traction motors with regenerative braking system A typical rolling stock used by DMRC consists of two units, each comprising of two cars, a Driving Trailer car (DT) and a Motor Car (M). The electro-dynamic rheostatic braking system converts the kinetic energy of decelerating Rolling stock into the thermal energy of rheostats which is dissipated as heat without regenerating electrical energy while decelerating.
vcs-4690:
The Ningxia 2021-2023 Pengyang Afforestation Project, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region (hereafter as ‘the project’) is located in Pengyang County, Guyuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region of China. The aim of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and to contribute to the local sustainable development by planting the trees and shrubs on the barren mountains and barren land. The project was implemented by Bureau of Natural Resources in Pengyang, who is the proponent of this project (hereafter ‘the project proponent’). The forest is to be established in the project in 10,150 hectares by direct planting various tree and shrub species on barren hills in the selected states. These tree species include Robinia pseudoacacia, Populus hopeiensis, Pinus tabuliformis, Picea, Pinus sylvestris, Red Armeniaca sibirica, Dahurian larch, Salix matsudacernegundo, Acer truncatum, Platycladus orientalis, Pinus bungeana Zucc, Salix matsudana, Chinese Robinia, Robinia, Acer negundoaurea, Ulmus pumila, Armeniaca sibirica, Prunus davidiana, and shrub species involves Shinyleaf Yellowhorn, Hippophae Fructus, Korshinsk Peashrub, Cerasus humilis, Rosa xanthina Lindl and Clove. 
The project is located in the Pengyang County, which covers 12 towns and 3 tree farms, Baiyang Town, Caomiao Town, Chengyang Town, Fengzhuang Town, Gucheng Town, Honghe Town, Jiaocha Town, Luowa Town, Mengyuan Town, Wangwa Town, Xiaocha Town, Xinji Town, Caiyang Town, and Ruhe Tree farm, Caomiao Tree farm, Xiaoyuanzi Tree farm.
The land in the project area was barren mountains and barren land, according to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, there was no natural or secondary forest in the project area. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forest.
The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 3,197,649 tCO2e in 60 years, the average annual emission reduction is 53,294 tCO2e.
vcs-4691:
The implementation of the Shaanxi Ningshan project is according to Methodology Improved Forest Management: Conversion of Logged to Protected Forest. The methodology quantifies the GHG removals generated from preventing logging of forests that would have been logged in the absence of carbon finance.
The Shaanxi Ningshan IFM(conversion of logged to protected forest) Project(hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Tongchewan Town and Longwang Town. All forest tenure is legally owned by each township collective above.The geographic coordinate of the project is 108°02’E~108°56’E and 33°07’N~33°50’N, area about 37,073 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IMF) of the conversion of logged to protected forest.
Prior to the implementation of the project,the forests are logged annually according to the valid and verifiable government’s timber management plan for timber in the project area.The implementation of the project activity ceases to log to protect forests to generate the GHG emission reductions and removals.The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation and soil erosion control), thus contributing to sustainable development.
During the activity cycle, the total emission reduction of the project activity is 12,781,271 tCO2e, and the average annual emission reduction is 639,064 tCO2e in 20 years. And the Verified Carbon Units (hereafter “VCUs”) with buffer deductions is about 9,969,389 tCO2e in 20 years, and the average annual VCUs with buffer deductions is 498,469 tCO2e.
vcs-4692: The purpose of this project is to utilize anaerobic digesters to treat the city's food waste and utilize the recovered biogas for external power generation. The project activities include waste collection, waste pretreatment system, biodiesel production system, anaerobic digesters, and biogas purification. The project utilizes anaerobic digestion tanks to process urban catering food waste and collects and destroys/utilizes the biogas generated by the anaerobic system, thereby preventing the methane emissions produced during the anaerobic fermentation of fresh waste in local landfills from being released into the atmosphere.
vcs-4694:
The composting of organic waste project in Hubei province(hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Hubei province, China. The project is invested and owned by Hubei Jiubao Ecological
agriculture Co.,Ltd. The proposed project is a new building composting plant which designed to treat organic wastes to produce organic fertilizer. The proposed project comprises of fermentation system and organic fertilizer production system, etc. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue.. The project is
designed to treat 280,000 tonnes wet organic waste per year and produce 100,000 tonnes organic fertilizer per year.
In absence of the project, the organic wastes would have been dumped in the landfill sites. This new project will avoid CH4 emissions from the disposal of the waste in a landfill site in absence of the
Project. The proposed project is estimated to deliver totally 3,110,009 tCO2e emission reduction during the 10 years’ crediting period, at an average amount of 311,000 tCO2e per year. This project started operation on 05/05/2021. 
The contributions of the proposed project to local, host country and global environment and economy sustainable developments are shown as follows:
- The proposed project will avoid GHG emissions by treatment organic waste that would have been dumped in landfill site. Thus will effectively improve the living circumstances for local people.
- This project will also improve soil condition by providing organic fertilizer for local people, boosting farm crop production and promote the incomes of local farmers.
- This project could provide job opportunities for local people, which is beneficial for local livelihood.
vcs-4695:
Xinxiang Yanmai Biogas Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is located at Yanjin County Industrial Agglomeration Zone, Yanjin County, Xinxiang City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is owned and implemented by Xinxiang Yanmai Food Co., Ltd

The project will introduce new anaerobic waste water treatment system (Two anaerobic
Digesters with effective volume of 8000m3 and 5000m3 separately) to treat waste water from starch production of Xinxiang Yanmai Food Co., Ltd.. The project uses digesters to treat waste water, collect and utilized the generated biogas to avoid methane emissions. The generated biogas will be captured and used for heat generation which will be used for starch production
with 8t/h biogas boiler within the project site. The residual waste from the digester will be used for soil application. Wastewater from the waste water treatment system will be discharged to Yanjin Municipal Sewage Treatment Plant for advanced treatment. 

Prior to the implementation of the project, the waste water was treated in open anaerobic lagoon at the project site and generated methane was emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility. The project is expected to avoid GHG emissions of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas.
vcs-4696:
Biaofa Juancheng Animal Manure Management Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Wanhua Industrial Zone, Hongchuan Town, Juancheng County, Heze City, Shandong Province, P.R.China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Biaofa Ecological (Juancheng) Co., Ltd. 

The purpose of the project is to treat the manure to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. The project will introduce a new waste management system (enclosed anaerobic digesters) to treat animal manure from 19 livestock farms in Juancheng County to replace the existing open anaerobic lagoons at the livestock farms. The treated manure is collected by tank trucks from the livestock farms to the project site and the collected manure is subsequently treated at
project site. 

By treating the manure with enclosed anaerobic digester with total effective volume of 75.360 cubic meters. The project will avoid the emissions of methane that would be generated from animal manure treatment in the existing open anaerobic lagoons at the 19 livestock farms. The biogas generated during the treatment process will be partly used for electricity generation used for operation of the project, partly used for heat generation used within the project and the rest will be supplied to users nearby for heat generation (the generated GHG emission reductions from electricity generation and heat utilization will not be claimed for conservativeness). The fermented sludge from the enclosed anaerobic digesters will be treated aerobically and used in nearby farmland as organic fertilizer. Wastewater from the treatment system will be used for agriculture irrigation.
vcs-4698: The Hive Ecosystems Project is a revegetation and restoration project aimed at addressing the impact of long-term degradation caused through unsustainable livestock production over the past century within the Albany Thicket Biome of South Africa.The initial project instances are located on a 7,300 hectare private landholding. The project aims to rehabilitate degraded farmlands through extensive planting and management of P. afra. Active restoration has been shown to successfully rehabilitate the vegetation type and lead to gradually recovery of carbon stocks that were released following early degradation.  The outcomes of the project extend far beyond the sequestration of carbon. A primary outcome is the rehabilitation of an indigenous, diverse vegetation type that in a functional state, provides resilient ecosystem services to both local residents and downstream urban hubs. In an area that is predicted to become warmer and drier over time and has recently experienced a protracted drought (Mahlalela et al. 2020), the climate change adaptation benefit of raising livestock and securing water in a resilient manner is perhaps of greater importance than the climate change mitigation outcome of the initiative.
vcs-4699: The Baviaanskloof Carbon Project will seek to sequestrate carbon through rehabilitation and restoration of the subtropical Albany Thicket biome The project includes a broad set of additional activities, including initial land rehabilitation (e.g., erosion control measures), the establishment of nurseries and replanting of specific indigenous species, as well as the long-term management of grazing pressure at a level that allows thicket recovery. This process leads to an increase in both biomass- and soil organic- carbon stocks, thereby gradually sequestering atmospheric carbon over time.
vcs-47: The Jinan Landfill Gas to Energy Project (hereafter, the “Project”) developed by Shandong Shifang New Energy Ltd (hereafter referred to as the “Project Developer”) is a landfill gas collection and utilization project located in the city of Jinan, Shandong Province, China (hereafter referred to as the “Host Country”). The project will have an electricity component with maximum installed capacity reaching 3.5 MW.    The Jinan landfill began operation in 1997 and currently holds approximately 3.84 million tonnes of waste. The 147,600 m2 landfill has an average depth of 20 metres and can currently expect an approximate daily input of 2,000 tonnes of domestic waste. The objective of the project is to collect and utilize the landfill gas (LFG) generated by the Jinan landfill.
vcs-470: Xinjiang Dabancheng Sanchang Phase III Wind Power Project (hereafter referred as the proposed project) is located in Tuoli Village, Urumchi County, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Northwest China. Totally 33 sets of 1500kW wind turbines (Goldwind 77/1500kW) will be installed, providing a total capacity of 49.5MW. With average annual electricity supplied of 136,610 MWh, the proposed project will achieve CO2 emission reduction by replacing electricity generated by fossil fuel fired power plant connected into Northwest China Power Grid. The proposed project is estimated to deliver 134,943 tonnes CO2 emission reduction annually.
vcs-4702: The Chahar Right Rear Banner Improved Grassland Management Project aims to restore degraded grassland ecosystems through grazing management in the project zone. By introducing sustainable grazing practices such as grazing prohibition and grassland-livestock balance, manual restoration measures such as fence building, rodent control, and other sustainable grassland management measures, this project is expected to enhance local carbon sequestration and contribute to the development of local ecosystems. The existing degradation and salinization area accounts for 99.67% of the local grassland. To combat and reverse this degradation, the project proposes to implement improved grassland management across 225,382.93 ha of degraded grassland.
vcs-4703: The Project activity, under the premise of ensuring the quality of the product, will recycle andprocess the waste plastic PET instead of using the raw material (crude oil and natural gas) to produce the PET flakes. Therefore, the GHG emission reductions will be generated through the implementation of the project by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials andreducing related energy consumption as well. The project is owned by Xingning Tokzin Yinghui Resources Co., Ltd. Its annual productivity is55,000 tons PET flakes, and the Project will recycle 65,000 tons waste plastic PET. The estimated annual emission reductions are 59,201 tons CO2e.
vcs-4704: The Yecheng Grassland Sustainable Management Project (Phase 2) is located in the Kashgar region of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in northwest China, on the edge of the Taklamakan Desert. The project site includes four townships, Qipan Township, Wuxiabashi Township, Kekeya Township and Xihexiu Township.This project is jointly implemented by Yecheng Natural Resources Bureau and Yecheng Jincheng Urban and Rural Construction Investment and Development Co., Ltd. This project has implemented sustainable management of 234,033.22 hectares of degraded grasslands, with an estimated 40 year greenhouse gas removal of 12,673,960 tCO2e and an average annual greenhouse gas removal of 316,849 tCO2e.  The project aims to restore the degraded grassland ecosystems and enhance the grassland carbon sequestration function through sustainable grassland management measures. It also aims to improve the skills of herders, provide employment opportunities, increase their income, and improve the habitat environment for wildlife, thereby enhancing local biodiversity.
vcs-4705:
This project description (PD) contains information about the KIS BIOFUELS- UKINDO Methane Avoidance from Industrial Wastewater in Indonesia.
The proposed project will implement biogas recovery, flaring and/or utilization systems for industrial wastewater treatment in Indonesia. The project involves installation of ZPHB® biogas tank & lagoon system plant for the treatment of wastewater from PT. UKINDO mill along with capturing the methane emissions from the plant and thereby reducing greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions into environment.
The project is located PT United Kingdom Indonesia Plantations (PT. UKINDO), a member of Anglo Eastern Plantations (AEP) Group, Blankahan POM, Desa Blankahan, Kec. Kuala, Kab. Langkat, Sumatera Utara Province, Indonesia.
vcs-4706:
The proposed project activity will utilize the wood waste as feed stock for production of particle board. The project activity is first of its kind in host country to use a wood waste as a resource for industrial production of particle board, which will replace wood log-based plywood produced from virgin wood sourced from forest.
The project activity has installed 350 m3/day particle board production capacity, which requires around 550 Tonnes of dry wood waste per day. The manufacturing of particle board involves use adhesive and paraffin wax.
Prior to project activity, majority of wood waste is generally managed as a waste product. In the Nkok SEZ region, most of the wood waste are deposited in landfills. A small percentage of the wood waste is used for energy generation for captive usage.
The project activity will reduce greenhouse gas emissions by reducing methane emissions from biomass waste that is otherwise left to decay in a dedicated landfill in the area.
vcs-4707:
Methane Destruction Grouped Project  initiated by 
Danish Crown A/S is a grouped project to mitigate the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions especially methane (CH4) 
gas from its supply chain. The project activity instances will be situated in different regions 
in Denmark. The project is owned by animal farmers affiliated with Danish Crown but 
implemented by Danish Crown A/S. The project activity consists of anaerobic digestion (AD) 
swine slurry treatment and flaring systems. The reduction potential is between 1500 - 3000 tons co2e pr. farm pr. year
vcs-4708:
This Tasar Forest Carbon Project will promote tree-based wild silk production outside traditional forests by utilizing privately owned barren / fallow uplands of tribal farmers. The project will undertake wild silk (locally called Tasar) tree planting and promote sericulture-based livelihoods. Sericulture is a traditional livelihood, however lack of availability of host trees in natural forests constrains its expansion. Traditionally, the tribal communities in the targeted areas depend majorly on forests for their livelihoods and have a long history of wild silk production from natural forests – wild silk is second to agriculture as a source of livelihoods. However, production from the forests declined due to government regulation of forest access rights. Yet there are large areas in these regions that are severely degraded, fallow, etc. that would benefit from restoring their productive capacity and biodiversity through profitable tree planting investments. 
The project is implemented by Cognisphere Solutions Ltd. (CSL) with investment from Climate Partner Impact GmbH starting in 2022. The project will afforest 2,000 hectares of privately-owned wastelands with Tasar silk-host trees in the adjoining states of Jharkhand and West Bengal in India. The project implementation started from May 2022 and plantations were initiated in the season Jun to Oct 2022.
It will involve the participation of ~3,000 households in 125 villages, grouped into two clusters broadly in Jharkhand, and West Bengal. People in the project areas are majorly tribals with limited options to escape poverty and deprivation. Tasar host trees such as Terminalia arjuna and T. tomentosa will form the core species, accompanied with a diversity of other indigenous tree species. The planted trees will be managed as long-term agroforestry systems –integrating crop production (intercropping), Tasar silk production and associated value chain development.
vcs-4709: The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for farmers to provide financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in Uttar Pradesh, India.  Agroforestry in Uttar Pradesh is a dynamic, ecologically based natural resource management system through which the integration of trees/woody perennials in farms and rangelands diversifies, and sustains production for increased social, economic, and environmental benefits.The project shall enhance farmer communities’ income, biodiversity conservation, and soil health improvement.
vcs-471: This proposed project is aimed to build a Bogeda 40.5MW wind power farm located within Bogeda area of Tuoli Town of Urumqi County, under the jurisdiction of the Urumqi Municipal, capital of Xinjiang Uigur Autonomous Region of the P.R.C. As the proposed project activity, 27 wind turbines with 1.5MW capacity per unit will be invested, installed and operated by CECIC Wind Power (Xinjiang) Co. Ltd. It falls within sector scope 1: energy industries (Renewable electricity) from the perspective of proposed CDM activity. The proposed Bogeda wind power project is expected to generate 142,320 MWh annually, and about 120,260MWh of the wind electricity will be newly delivered to the Northwest Power Grid via Xinjiang power grid annually. The wind electricity generated by the project activity will be connected to the 220KV substation through 110KV transmission line
vcs-4710: The Energy Drive Energy Efficiency Grouped Project (the Project) is a grouped project applying Variable Speed Drive (VSD) technology to achieve electrical energy efficiency improvements in industrial facilities within the Republic of South Africa. The Project Proponent offers energy efficiency solutions for medium and low voltage motor systems. The motor system is retrofitted with a VSD and data collection system which is capable of actively optimising the way power is delivered to the motor system and thus reducing electricity consumption. Energy Drive actively maintains the VSD system and analyses significant amounts of data about the VSD system, motor system and other facility parameters.
vcs-4711: Food rescue organizations play a pivotal role in our society, and represent an unexpected yet critical force to mitigate the speed of climate change. This project aims to measure avoided food loss and waste, and in particular, the avoidance of toxic methane gas and other greenhouse gasses into the atmosphere. This occurs as a result of the diversion of edible food from a landfill to feed those experiencing food insecurity, thereby keeping food within the human supply chain in accordance with Verra Methodology VM 00046 v.1.
vcs-4712:
This project aims to implement permaculture activities through community participation in 9,400 ha in the region of Moba, Democratic Republic of Congo. The specific objectives of the grouped project are:
1.	Setting up large-scale tree planting projects on 9,400 ha based on the “direct seeding” technique.
2.	Implement solutions for soil fertility, water conservation, climate change mitigation, and animal habitat.
3.	To raise awareness of climate change and adaptation strategies.
4.	Creation of permaculture schools’ farms through the implementation of a community program that fosters the training of the community on permaculture practices with native species with the aim of creating a community using self-sustaining systems.
The project contributes to the mitigation of greenhouse gases through a combination of sustainable land management practices and principles that promote carbon sequestration and reduced greenhouse gas emissions.
vcs-4713:
Agroforestry can help in the conservation and rehabilitation of ecosystems and provide better livelihood opportunities for rural communities. The proposed Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) GKF agroforestry project, titled 'Enhancing Rural Livelihoods of Small and Marginalised Farmers through Carbon Finance,’ operates in several districts across Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, situated in the southeastern region of India. The project spans five districts in Telangana, namely Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet, Karimnagar, and Mancherial, as well as six districts in Andhra Pradesh, namely West Godavari, East Godavari, Eluru, Kakinada, Konaseema, and Alluri Seetharama Raju.
The agroforestry project seeks to foster sustainable agroforestry practices among small-scale farmers in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, India. The primary objectives are to enable farmers to attain financial benefits while also ensuring greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation within the region.
vcs-4714: This project features implementation of rapid rotational grazing practices by dense aggregations of livestock to restore perennial grasses on degraded rangelands across 1.5 million hectares in southern Kenya. These new grazing practices are additional because they differ from the seasonal shifts in grazing activity from wet to dry season ranges and would not be possible without carbon revenues to support governance and monitoring of grazing activities. Rapid rotational grazing will enhance adaptation to climate change by improving soil water holding capacity, increasing surface water availability and providing grass banks as a hedge against drought. Habitat improvement from new grazing practices will restore wildlife corridors between iconic High Conservation Areas such as Serengeti, Kilimanjaro, Nairobi, and Tsavo National Parks and their associated ecosystems and enhance diversity of endemic taxa of plants, birds and insects. Finally, the project will provide direct benefits to 17 or more pastoralist communities in form of funds for bursaries to support women and the poorest community members as well as to construct water capture structures and infrastructure for delivering livestock to market. The project is expected to remove more than 63 million tons CO2e over the project lifetime of 40 years, or nearly 1.6 million tons CO2e a year on average.
vcs-4715:
Jinghai Leachate Anaerobic Biogas Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Jinghai New Energy Environmental Protection Power Generation Project, in Chenguantun Town, Jinghai District, Tianjin City, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Tianjin BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd.
Before the implementation of this project, Jinghai New Energy Environmental Protection Power Generation Project invested by Tianjin Gaoneng Environmental Protection Energy Co., Ltd. incinerates domestic waste with a daily treatment capacity of 1,000t /d. Leachate will be produced during the storage and fermentation process in the garbage bin. The supporting treatment system of the factory is Anaerobic (UASB) + membrane bioreactor (MBR) + nanofiltration system (NF)+reverse osmosis system (RO) treatment process. A large amount of biogas is produced in the anaerobic treatment section of UASB. Because it was difficult to collect and treat biogas, the biogas generated by the UASB was emitted to the atmosphere directly without any recovery and utilization. The biogas was being vented to the atmosphere in 28/12/2020 when the Jinghai New Energy Environmental Protection Power Generation Project started operation.
This project collects the biogas generated by the anaerobic treatment section of leachate to generate electricity and connect to the grid, which can effectively utilize biogas resources.
The project started to construct on 13/12/2021 and started operation on 12/07/2022. The project has a total designed capacity 1MW (2*500KW) and combusts the leachate biogas, which contains nearly 65% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the North China Power Grid (NCPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period will be 6,630MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid.
vcs-4717: The project involves installation of bundled Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) power plant with a cumulative capacity of 12.37 MW primarily to meet the captive demand of the premises owners and the rooftop, ground mounted and carport solar units are connected to the national grid through net metering mechanism. The premises owners are the customers of the power generated from the solar panels who purchase the power under long term power purchase agreements signed for 25 years. Before installation of the solar units, the Shrinath Rotopack premises and VW2 premises owners used to meet the electricity demand from the national grid of the India. The project thus replaces fossil fuel dominated grid electricity thereby reducing the equivalent amount of GHG emission. The project company for Shrinath Rotopack is AMPSolar Power Generation Private Limited and for VW2, it is AMP Energy Distributed Generation One Pvt. Ltd.
vcs-4718: Hainan Baisha Improved Forest Management (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project”) is located in Baisha County, Hainan Province, China. It is implemented by the representative Project Proponent Baisha Li Autonomous County Rural Revitalization and Development Co., Ltd (hereafter “Project Proponent”). The project has about 2,336.5 ha commercial forest, which is nearly mature or mature. Before the implementation of the project, the forest in the project area shall be planted according to the design of commercial forest, and logged annually according to the timber logging and managing plan issued by the local forest authority. The main object of the project is to improve the forest coverage rate, protect local ecological environment, reduce carbon emissions and carbon sequestration by enhance the management level and converse logged to protected forest in the project area. The implementation of the project will result in significant carbon sequestration and improve the sustainable development of ecological system.
vcs-4719:
The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on ground mounted and
floating base solar power plant in various states of India. The sole purpose of project activity is
to install solar power plant for captive purpose and surplus generated electricity can be supplied
to grid and further equivalent energy will be consumed from grid through net metering
arrangement with state electricity board.
vcs-472: This proposed project is aimed to build a Wulabo 30MW wind power farm to be located within Wulabo area of Tuoli Town of Urumqi County, under the jurisdiction of the Urumqi Municipal, the Capital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region of the P.R.C. As the proposed project activity, 20 wind turbines with 1.5MW per-unit capacity will be invested, installed and operated by CECIC Wind Power (Xinjiang) Co. Ltd. 1, which is the subsidiary company of the CECIC. The proposed Wulabo wind power project is expected to generate 95,430 MWh. And about 89,080MWh of wind electricity will be commercially delivered to the Northwest power grid annually, which is equivalent to the annual operation hour about 2969 hours with full capacity. By replacing the fossil fuel fired power generation in the grid, the wind power project activity would accrue about 83,468tCO2 of the annual CO2 emissions reductions
vcs-4720:
The grouped project “Reforestation of lands for multiple purposes as a sustainable development driver” has as its stated goal the promotion of sustainable reforestation in Southern Brazil, specifically in the states of Paraná and Santa Catarina, aiming to achieve net removals of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere. 
The land use that has historically predominated in these states is non-forested lands, such as agriculture and cattle raising. The project proposes a change in the traditional land use of this region, promoting reforestation practices as a sustainable alternative, either to produce wood for multiple purposes based on rapid-growth species (for example, Pinus.spp or Eucalyptus.spp), and/or to restore areas based on native species of the local phytophysiognomy. The overall purpose of this initiative is to develop economically profitable reforestation system, integrating reforestation activities for the purposes of production and restoration of conservation areas, which simultaneously provides environmental and social benefits to the region. This grouped project also contemplates the possibility of silvopastoral systems implementation, nonetheless, emission removals will only be claimed for the reforestation activities.
vcs-4721:
The proposed VCS project activity has the objective to avoid emission of Greenhouse Gases (GHG) through collection, flaring/combustion and energy use of the LFG. The proposed VCS project activity will also assist Brazil to meet its demand for energy due to the economic growing scenario, improving energy supply and contributing, at the same time, to the environmental, social and economic sustainability through climate change global mitigation and local air pollution. This initiative aims to increase renewable energy participation in relation to the total Brazilian energy consumption.
Prior to the implementation of the project activity the landfill gas is being released to atmosphere and the electricity was generated by other sources in the Brazilian national electricity grid.
Located in the southeast region of Brasil, state of Minas Gerais, city of Santana do Paraíso, the proposed VCS project activity encompasses a voluntary initiative to encourage clean technology investments in the country.
As per its design configuration, combustion of collected LFG occurs in the following methane destruction device(s): 
-	1 high temperature open flare;
-	2 engine-generator sets  of an electricity generation infrastructure (in which collected LFG will be utilized as gaseous fuel for electricity generation).
-	Possibility of future increase of the number of engine-generator sets, maintaining a total combined nameplate capacity up to 10 MW.
vcs-4724:
Xinjiang Altay Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as ‘the project’) is located in Altay City, Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The project aims to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by Improved sustainable grassland management measures, such as rotating grazing and grazing prohibition in the project area by building fences, and improving the degraded grassland ecosystem by reseeding high-quality local grass seeds. After the implementation of the project, the grassland will be scientifically and rationally utilized according to the health status of the local grassland ecosystem. Achieve long-term sustainable management of degraded local grasslands. The implementation of the project has significantly improved the local climate benefits, community benefits and biodiversity benefits. The project sponsor is Xinjiang Altay City Zhujin Investment Co., LTD..
The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 18,687,019 tCO2-e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 467,175.475 tCO2-e.
vcs-4725: The Livestock 2040/Uruguay project is driven and conceived by the consulting firm Profesionales SRL.It involves the participation of farmers in Uruguay who practice rotational grazing and have implemented good management practices on their property. Project is a grouped project.Rotational grazing is the primary activity of the project, which brings benefits to the ecosystem: it prevents and reduces soil erosion, improves the nutrient cycle, increases soil organic carbon (SOC) levels, and boosts pasture production. Participants also implement good practices in grass-fed livestock management with the goal of enhancing the ecosystem's well-being through the management of the plant-soil-animal relationship. Grazing management that enables higher quantity and quality of pasture to support high stocking rates while respecting animal welfare is a key component. Activities that increase biodiversity, such as the inclusion of native species and hunting prohibition, are considered relevant.Additionally, actions are proposed to reduce the use of external inputs, such as fertilizers or livestock feed, which contributes to decreasing greenhouse gas emissions. The result of these practices is an increase in organic matter in the soil, i.e., higher SOC content. Furthermore, the process of grassland degradation is reversed.The baseline consists of soils that were previously used for agriculture or extensive livestock farming. These soils have lost productive plant species, with areas of bare soil, compaction, low fertility, and a high risk of erosion.The project scenario consists of structured soils with a good amount of organic matter, high fertility levels, and enhanced plant growth. Compaction, erosion risk, and the amount of bare soil decrease.Estimations of emission reductions and absorption were made for the first project activity instant located in Sierra de las Animas, Maldonado, Uruguay. Greenhouse gas removals for this phase totaled 12,007 tCO2 over the 20 years.
vcs-4727:
The Trees for Farmers (TFF) Brazil ARR Grouped Project is an initiative located in the Brazilian Amazon biome. The project aims to establish, restore, and enhance vegetative cover through tree planting and assisted natural regeneration on degraded lands, bare soils, low-productivity areas, and areas undergoing regeneration, including Areas of Permanent Protection (APPs) and Legal Reserves (LRs) with limited natural regeneration.
Project activities focus on planting diverse mixes of native species to create biodiverse forests and woodlands, complemented where appropriate by non-invasive, ecosystem-compatible non-native species, and including endangered species.
Originally initiated by Rabobank Carbon Bank, the project is now led by The Green Branch as Project Proponent, in continued collaboration with Rabobank Brazil. Through its extensive farmer network, Rabobank Brazil supports expansion across a potential area exceeding 13 million hectares.
The first project instance covers 92.03 hectares planted within the Botuverá farm condominium (23,551.71 ha total) in Gaúcha do Norte, Mato Grosso. This instance is expected to generate average GHG removals of 756.32 tCO₂e per year.
Over its 40-year crediting period (2022–2062), the Grouped Project is expected to expand progressively, targeting 10,000 hectares of restored and planted land.
In addition to climate mitigation, the project seeks Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) certification, achieving both Climate and Biodiversity Gold Levels. It also promotes local employment, capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and awareness of sustainable land use, biodiversity conservation, and climate change mitigation and adaptation.
vcs-4729: The grouped project proposed by SADA Participações Ltda (hereinafter SADA), “Reforestation activities in Brazil for carbon removals from the atmosphere”, consists of the implementation of new plantations of African mahogany (e.g. Khaya grandifoliola and Khaya senegalensis) and Australian cedar (e.g.  Toona ciliata) in the state of Goiás (GO), in the Midwest region of Brazil. This region is notably marked by the historical tradition in livestock activities and, more recently, by the implementation of agricultural activities.
vcs-473: Henan Nanyang Fangcheng Wind Farm Project is located in Er’langMiao Town, Fangcheng County in the Southwest of Henan Province. The primary objective of the proposed project is to generate renewable electricity for the Central China Grid (CCG). Equivalent electricity service provided by the Central China Grid is chosen as the baseline scenario for the proposed project activity. The proposed project activity is a new wind power project, the scenario existing is the same with the baseline scenario.
vcs-4730:
Xinjiang Habahe Improved Grassland Management Project is located in Habahe County, Altay Region, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The Project aims to reduce the duration and amount of grazing on degraded grasslands by planting pasture grasses and improving grazing practices, in order to restore local degraded grassland systems and ensure grassland sustainability.
The project implemented sustainable grassland management on 91,976.85 hectares of degraded grassland through three measures: artificial grass planting, fencing and grazing ban, and rotational grazing. The implementation of the management measures can effectively increase the carbon stock and reduce non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, and ultimately achieve the purpose of greenhouse gas emission reduction. 
The project is expected to generate GHG emission removals of 6,283,832 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removals of 157,096 tCO2e.
vcs-4731:
The project activity is a biogas-based electricity generation project. The project involves methane recovery through controlled anaerobic digestion of poultry waste and utilization of recovered biogas to produce electricity. The project involves installation of two centralized anaerobic bio-digesters having capacities of 1500m3/day each, at the existing two poultry firms of the project owner with a total capacity of 3000 m3/day and utilization of one number of 100 KVA and one number of 250 kVA capacity biogas based electrical engines for each biogas unit.   On an average each poultry farm produces about 18 MT of poultry manure per day with total of 36 MT from two poultry firms. The electricity generated from the project is utilized for the captive use in the poultry farms.  The project activity is being implemented in phased manner where the first 1500m3 biogas unit is installed in phase I and second 1500 m3 biogas unit is installed in phase II. The project is owned and operated by Sunmax Hatcheries Private Limited company. The project is located in DasarlaPalli Village in Siddipet district of Telangana State, India.

Prior to the implementation of the project activity, the poultry manure waste utilized by the project activity is left to decay in open pits, tanks or anaerobic lagoons at the poultry farms, where the manure undergoes fermentation and release methane, that is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility. 
For electricity component, prior to the implementation of the project activity, the electricity supply for the poultry farm was generated mainly from grid connected power plants.
vcs-4732: The NatureRe project is a grouped project that seeks to sustainably manage 4,500 ha, within which it is estimated there is potential to restore approximately 2,925 ha. This area corresponds to livestock-degraded lands in the Antioquia Department (Colombia), in three subregions: Magdalena Medio, Bajo Cauca, and Nordeste. The project aims to restore native forest species by applying different ANR models.
vcs-4733:
RÊVER Automotive Co., Ltd (RÊVER or PP) is persuading users in Thailand to switch their fossil fuel-based vehicles with traditional internal combustion engines emitting pollutions and greenhouse gases (GHG) to battery electric vehicles (BEVs) for passenger transportation. BEVs are run by electric motors powered by electricity stored in batteries, instead of an Internal Combustion Engine (ICE), that do not emit GHGs per distance driven. 
This project is a grouped project, which allows to include multiple project activity instances throughout the crediting period and intends to generate Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) through the switching of user in Thailand who directly buy the BEVs from RÊVER. All carbon credits issued are owned and managed by RÊVER upon the mutual consent with users. The VCUs will be the promoting factor in term of environment and sustainability awareness rising that persuade users to the switching.
This grouped project applies the CDM methodology AMS-III.C. ver. 16.0, which describes the requirements for displacing the use of fossil fuel vehicles in passenger and freight transportation with new electric and/or hybrid vehicles to issue carbon credits across a range of their applicable vehicles. Based on emission reduction (ER) calculation, estimated ER from this grouped project activity must less than or equal to 60,000 tCO2 equivalent annually.
Before the implementation of this grouped project, the typical mode of transport within the boundary of Thailand is petrol combustion vehicles, with the market penetration of BEVs is lower than 2.5% (0.7% over the last 3 years, 2020-2022). To elaborate, ICE vehicles dominate with approximately 620,961 of its population compared to 9,584 of total BEVs in 2022.
The first and later project activity instance is set to be developed within the boundary of Thailand only. The first instance is the ER from the estimated RÊVER’s BEVs sale value in Thailand during 1 November 2022 to 31 December 2023.
vcs-4734:
The project changes the previous traditional agricultural management practices to multiple Improved agricultural land management practices. The project is in Tanghe County, Nanyang City, Henan province, China. It involves 94,614 ha cropland where corn and wheat are rotated.
Before implementation of the project, long-term and high-intensity deep tillage were conducted every year in the project area and no organic fertilizer was used. Additionally, no crop straw was returned to the field. The soil structure was damaged by these traditional ALM practices, which causes the loss of organic carbon in the soil, and leads to soil degradation. The project activity is expected to improve soil SOC and soil health through multiple ways of IALM practices. The intensity of tillage in the project scenario is decreased by reducing the frequency of tillage. The tillage is conducted every three years instead of each year. Organic fertilizer is used to replace part of the inorganic fertilizers. Moreover, the crop straw in the project area is returned to the field. These IALM practices can improve soil health and the SOC content will also be increased. Besides, N2O emissions are avoided due to reduced application of nitrogen fertilizer.
vcs-4736:
Chengzi Recycled Al Project A aims to produce recycled aluminium from aluminium waste products (e.g., window frames, aluminium cans, etc.) sourced from the MSW and to replace primary aluminium produced from raw materials. The Project located in Group 6, Lotus Village, Chengguan Town, Fang County, Shiyan City, Hubei Province, China and is developed and operated by Hubei Chengzi Aluminum Industry Co., Ltd. and Zhonghe Carbon Sink Science and Technology Research (Wuhan) Co., Ltd..
Prior to the project, pure aluminium was extracted from the aluminium ore obtained from the mining of aluminium mines by means of an electrolytic cell, which was the basic scheme of the project. Therefore, the GHG emission reduction will be generated through the implementation of the project by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and reducing related energy consumption as well. The project has started constructed since May 2021, and the date of production line putting into operation is March 2022.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through an avoiding extraction of raw materials and production of virgin materials. It is estimated that the project will result a total of 410,305 tCO2e emission reductions in the first crediting period of 7 years and with annual average of 58,615 tCO2e emission reduction in the 1st crediting period.
vcs-4739:
The proposed ARR-VCS project is a large-scale grouped project that aims for the long-term restoration of Spain’s forests, achieved through native mixed-species reforestation that reverses the impact of land degradation and the loss of flora and fauna. Land regeneration and biodiversity rejuvenation are central objectives of this reforestation project, which employs the latest technologies and planting techniques. Project activities are implemented by Land Life, a Dutch technology-driven reforestation company that grows forests by planting trees at scale. Land Life uses innovative technology for the planting of native tree species by optimizing tree selection, survival, and resilience. Science-driven nature restoration activities ensure the highest tree survival rate and support the permanent establishment of native forests that complement rural communities.

Project activities are implemented and monitored according to the VCS-approved project methodology AR-ACM0003, with the expectation that additional project instances are to be added over the coming years. The first group of instances of the project covers 285.56 of degraded land in Spain, located at two planting sites: Vega de Doña Olimpa, (116.21 ha), located in the province of Palencia, and Ariza (169.35 ha), located in Zaragoza province. While each project instance is expected to sequester carbon across the entire 100-year crediting period, the ex-ante estimate focuses on the initial 40 years for practical reasons to determine the annual average profile. These project instances (implemented across 2020 and 2021) are expected to sequester approximately 79,613 tCO2e over the initial 42 years of the 100-year crediting period. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals is 1,990 tCO2e. A total of 245,927 native trees are expected to become established in the project areas described in this PD.
vcs-474: Inner Mongolia Bayinhanggai 49.5MW Wind Farm Project is located in Urad ZhongQi, Bayan Nur City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. The primary objective of the proposed project is to generate renewable electricity to meet the ever-increasing demand in the Inner Mongolia Grid and the North China Grid (NCG). According to the conditions of the local wind resource, the proposed project will have the total installed capacity of 49.5 MW. The proposed project is expected to delivery 107 GWh annually to the NCG through the Inner Mongolia Grid. The project operation life is 20 years. Electricity generated by the proposed project will displace part of the electricity generated by the NCG which is dominated by fuelfired power plants. Thus, the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions could be achieved. Theestimated annual GHG emission reductions are 115,079 tCO2e during the first crediting period.
vcs-4741:

The project proponent is Defined B.V., a private limited liability company based in the Netherlands. Defined B.V. is an investment vehicle that holds various climate impact investments all dedicated to reducing worldwide CO2 emissions. Project activities are implemented by Land Life, a Dutch technology-driven reforestation company that grows forests by planting trees at scale.

Project activities are implemented and monitored according to the VCS-approved project methodology AR-ACM0003, with the expectation that additional project instances are to be added over the coming years. While each project instance is expected to sequester carbon across the entire 100-year crediting period, the ex-ante estimate focuses on the initial 40 years for practical reasons to determine the annual average profile.
