vcs-4743: The Yvoty REDD project is an initiative aimed at addressing unplanned deforestation in eastern Paraguay, with its initial focus on the Mbaracayú Reserve. This reserve, spanning 64,400 hectares, houses significant biodiversity and was established in 1992 through an international treaty. However, since 2007, it has faced illegal deforestation due to cannabis cultivation, leading to increased fire incidents. The project, led by the Fundación Moises Bertoni (FMB), aims to reduce these threats by implementing management plans that enhance security, monitoring, environmental education, and community outreach. The project will be funded through carbon certification, specifically the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) and methodology VM0007, with an expected reduction of 19,466,334 tCO2e in emissions over 30 years, equivalent to 645,100 tCO2e per year.
vcs-4744:
Paraguay, renowned for its abundant fauna and vegetation, has emerged as an area of concern regarding deforestation in Latin America. Both legal and illegal practices are slowly depleting these natural resources. Beyond their role as host of a vast biodiversity, the forests are also a crucial carbon sink.
The conversion of forests into cattle ranching, agriculture and timber production is one of the main drivers of legal deforestation in the country. Despite the Oriental Region of Paraguay has a zero-deforestation policy, the Occident, known as the Chaco Region, lost around 4.37 million hectares of forest between 2005 and 2020 to these practices (INFONA, 2022).
Under these circumstances, this project has been designed to preserve the Paraguayan Chaco forests by grouping landowners that have plans and permits to clear land but are willing to reduce this planned deforestation. Our goals include raising awareness about conservation and its positive effects, controlling logging practices and monitoring environmental and social indicators.
According to VCS Standard 4.5, eligible REDD activities are those that reduce net GHG emissions by reducing deforestation and/or forest degradation and, since the land is legally authorized to be converted to a non-forest area, project activities fall under the Avoiding Planned Deforestation category.
In the long term, specific actions related to biodiversity and community will be defined to be developed within the project framework.
Under the selected methodology, the carbon project is expected to generate a total of 45 million tCO2e in emission reductions over the course of a 30-year period. In other words, a yearly emission reduction equivalent to 1,5 million tCO2e.
vcs-4745:
Henan CP Group Swine Farm Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) installs animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 5 swine farms in Henan Province, China. Each swine farm is to build anaerobic animal manure treatment systems to treat manure waste of Breeding Swine Farms separately in Luoyang, Shangqiu, and Pingdingshan owned and implemented by subsidiaries of Charoen Pokphand Group (CP Group). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater on site to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and is flushed and pumped to the aerobic treatment system (HDPE Membrane Enclosed Anaerobic Digester). The biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for heat generation and food processing facility for self-use. An emergency flare is installed in each project activity instance to ensure that biogas would be destroyed when exigencies happened. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is sent out and used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmlands for free. The effluent will be used for agricultural irrigation. 
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. It is estimated that 22,432tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 224,320tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixing crediting period.
vcs-4746:
The Carbono Rural Paraguayan Chaco project aims to promote sustainable grazing practices in degraded pastures in Western Paraguay, targeting farmers practicing continuous or unsustainable grazing. The project aims to enhance grazing system productivity, soil carbon sequestration, and reduce GHG emissions. Paraguayan Chaco's primary economic activity is livestock farming, with farms ranging from 1,000 ha to 60,000 ha. Traditional management includes extensive pastures, resulting in degradation due to mismanagement, pests, weed proliferation, and overgrazing, mainly due to a lack of technical advice and high costs for sustainable practices. The project leverages carbon market incentives to promote sustainable farming.

Current practices lead to severe pasture and soil degradation, reducing land productivity and carbon retention capacity. The project seeks to restore soil properties, prevent degradation, and increase livestock productivity through controlled grazing, pest and water management, and producer capacity building. Desde el Suelo, an agronomic extensionist team, will implement and monitor project activities.

Increased grassland productivity is expected to sequester carbon, improve livestock production, and bring community and biodiversity benefits: i) enhance livestock production efficiency and stability, ii) improve soil quality, iii) raise livestock farming incomes, iv) enhance soil and grassland biodiversity, v) reduce pollution, vi) strengthen community resilience, vii) boost rural employment and skills in grazing management, viii) improve rural worker well-being, and ix) enhance animal welfare. The project aligns with UN Sustainable Development Goals:

SDG Goal 2: Zero Hunger
SDG Goal 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG Goal 13: Climate Action
SDG Goal 15: Life on Land
The project is a grouped initiative in Paraguayan Chaco, aiming to generate 445,697 tCO2e/year reductions and removals using Methodology VM0042 v2.0.
vcs-4747:
The Pantanal biome is located in the center-west of Brazil, covering portions of the states of Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul. Considered the largest continuous freshwater wetland on the planet, this biome oscillates between terrestrial and aquatic phases, forming a mosaic of landscapes that provide great biodiversity of flora and fauna. Analyzing the historical context of the region where the Pantanal is located, there has been a considerable expansion of agricultural activities (the main local economic activity, mainly focused on the breeding of Pantanal cattle) and this factor, together with the high rates of forest fires in this area, results in a scenario of unsustainable exploitation of the natural resources of this biome.
Considering all the applicable legal requirements, landowners who have a surplus of native vegetation on their property and choose to preserve it, would fulfill the first requirement for obtaining economic incentives from the voluntary carbon market, through Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) through Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD). Given all this context, the implementation of the REDD+ Carbon Program on a scale for the Pantanal biome is possible, providing a model of sustainable economic development that can help to redress the balance, reconciling the conservation of environmental services with traditional economic activities. Biofílica Ambipar, in partnership with rural landowners in the Pantanal of Mato Grosso do Sul who are committed to promoting dialogue that benefits both the environment and sustainable economic development, aims to develop economic activities linked to the conservation of environmental services and all their ecological functions through the implementation of the Pantanal REDD+ Program.
vcs-4748:
The main objectives of this project are: First, to recover lands degraded by land uses related to deforestation, such as cattle ranching; through ecological restoration, agroforestry systems and assisted natural regeneration, to ensure the recovery of forests inhabited by many species of flora and fauna, including endangered species such as the brown spider monkey, the blue-billed curassow, capuchin monkey, the white-faced curassow, and the night monkey. Second, by implementing restoration corridors to reconnect wild populations within a grassland matrix to increase the flow of individuals, and therefore the genetic flow, of these populations and thus increase their resilience and probability of survival in the medium and long term. And third, to recover strategic areas that are degraded, such as the banks of rivers and other bodies of water or areas where grassland productivity is low. 
FPP Colombia (project proponent) is a non-profit organization promoting biodiversity research and conservation focusing on endangered primate species. FPP initiated one of Colombia's first studies and conservation programs for the brown spider monkey. FPP operates one of the longest-running research projects in Latin America, focusing on the brown spider monkey, one of the world's most endangered primates. FPP's activities have been concentrated in the Middle Magdalena River Valley, an area relatively little studied affected by human activity and part of a global biodiversity hotspot (Tumbes-Chocó-Magdalena).
The Proyecto de Vida Silvestre, an initiative of Ecopetrol SA, Fondo Acción and WCS, seeks to conserve biodiversity in 3 regions of Colombia of biological and cultural importance, but which face increasing pressures that threaten natural resources. Through the articulation of these conservation initiatives, sustainability is sought through the development of a grouped carbon project which will generate income from carbon credits to achieve the objectives of ecosystem recovery
vcs-4749:
The “Tajimat Pujut, Restoration and Conservation of the Alto Mayo Awajun Forests” is a grouped project jointly developed by the Federacion Regional Indigena Awajun del Alto Mayo (Regional Awajun Indigenous Federation of Alto Mayo - FERIAAM) and Conservation International Foundation (CI). FERIAAM is an indigenous territorial organization that groups and represents 16 indigenous Awajun communities (13 in the department of San Martin, and 3 in the department of Loreto). FERIAAM is the lead project proponent and CI is the co-proponent. The project is located in the provinces of Moyobamba, Rioja and Datem del Marañon, and covers an area of 235,455ha.
The main goal of the “Tajimat Pujut” project is to achieve the restoration and conservation of Awajun forests. In recent decades, deforestation within the Awajun communities has accelerated, with greater impact since 1990 after the opening of the Fernando Belaunde Terry highway. The increase in deforestation is mainly due to a heavy migration of people from the Andes and coastal region of Peru to the Amazon, causing a significant change in forest cover due to the expansion of the agricultural frontier and the illegal logging of high-value timber species. The forests of native communities have been replaced by commercial crops, mainly by farmers (tenants), invaders and illegal loggers. 
The project will focus on implementing strategies and activities to achieve better management of the Awajun territory, strengthen its governance and indigenous identity, restore degraded areas, and diversify sources of income and sustainable productive activities that secure wellbeing for the Awajun people. Tajimat Pujut expects to generate 8,788,206 tCO2eq over the 30 year project lifetime, with an average of 292,940 tCO2eq per year.
vcs-475: renewable energy project developed by Yichun Longyuan Hero Asia Wind Power Co., Ltd. The proposed project is to be located in Jinshantun district Yichun City, Heilongjiang Province, China. The purpose of the proposed project is to generate electricity using wind power resources in the project region and to sell into Northeast Power Grid (NEPG). The proposed project involves the installation of 33 sets of 1,500kW wind turbines, for a total installed capacity of 49.5 MW. It is estimated that the annual generated output will be 112,600 MWh. The project is a new project, and the situation prior to the project is the same as the baseline scenario, which is that the NEPG would provide the same amount of electricity. The electricity generated from the project can displace part of the power from the grid, and the expected annual GHG emission reductions are 128,442 tCO2e.
vcs-4750:
The “WANAMEI” Project is located in Peru, within the province of Manu (department of Madre de Dios), and the province of Paucartambo (department of Cusco). The Executor of the Administration Contract of the Amarakaeri Communal Reserve (ECA – Amarakaeri) is the lead project proponent and will work with Conservational International Foundation (CI) and the National Association of Administration Contract Executors of Communal Reserves from Peru (ANECAP) as co-proponents. The Project area includes the Amarakaeri Communal Reserve, its 10 associated indigenous communities and the Quero Haramba conservation concession, covering nearly 599,286 ha  

The Amarakaeri landscape is under high risk of deforestation as a result of the expansion of illegal gold mining into Madre de Dios. The main agents of deforestation are migrants, who come from neighboring regions in Peru due to the profitability of the mining activity. In addition, increasing migration to the region is driving an increase in deforestation through the conversion of forests to agriculture and cattle pastures.
The Project will reduce GHG emissions by implementing participatory conservation strategies with the indigenous communities’ partners of the ECA, and will be developed based on the RIA (Amazon Indigenous REDD+) guidelines established by indigenous national organizations as safeguards for carbon projects within their territories. These strategies include the strengthening of capacities for landscape monitoring and surveillance, developing sustainable economic activities, strengthening the organizations that lead the indigenous communities and ensuring financial sustainability of the initiative. The project expects to reduce 8.2 million tCO2 over the 30 year project lifetime with an average of 276,419tCO2 per year.
vcs-4751:
The “Bulgarian Sustainable Farming Carbon Project” aims to raise farmers' awareness on the benefits of regenerative agriculture and how changes in agricultural practices can help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. 
Regenerative agriculture land management practices refer to farming and grazing practices that aim to reverse climate change by rebuilding soil organic matter, sequestering carbon, improving degraded soil biodiversity, improving water cycle, and restoring soil fertility. Regenerative agriculture does not imply only one practice, instead, it is generally a combination of techniques.
To achieve this objectives, different regenerative agricultural practices will be implemented. These will include, among others: 
-	Promoting no tillage or minimal tillage: this practice aims to avoid soils tillage which is one of the main causes of soil losses/erosion. This practice helps not only to conserve the soil structure but also to improve it and improve the soil organic carbon levels.
-	Introducing cover crops: this practice aims to avoid having soils without vegetation cover by introducing alternative crops in-between the main productive ones. This promotes soils conservation by avoiding erosion.  For this activity, Agrovar counts with a personalized information platform that processes the soils data which comes from laboratories and satellite information and as a result provides very specialized mixes of cover crops suggested for each land area according to every specific situation.
-	Information system for optimizing farming activities.
The project is developed as a grouped project within the boundaries of Bulgaria. The project activity intends to add more instances over the upcoming years. The project implementation will result in an increase of carbon stocks and a reduction of GHG emissions.
vcs-4752: A project of preserving the natural biome of the Pampa, the unique biome of our land, and its use in the raising of free-roaming cattle, in an environmentally friendly way, while helping local agricultures and it's developers to do the same
vcs-4753:
The project is in Fangcheng County, Nanyang City, Henan province, China. It changes the previous traditional agricultural management practices to multiple Improved agricultural land management practices. 54,901 ha cropland with corn and wheat rotated is involved in the project.
The intensity of tillage in the project scenario is decreased by reducing the frequency of tillage. The tillage is conducted every three years instead of each year. Organic fertilizer is used to replace part of the inorganic fertilizers. Moreover, the crop straw in the project area is returned to the field. These IALM practices can improve soil health and the SOC content will also be increased. Besides, N2O emissions are avoided due to reduced application of nitrogen fertilizer.
vcs-4754:
Puning MSW incineration and power generation project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Yunluo Town, Puning City, Guangdong province, China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Puning Guangye Yueneng Environmental Protection Energy Co., Ltd.. (hereafter referred to as the project owner).
With two 600t/d MSW combustion production lines, the project will treat 1,200 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of two 600t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 25MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 438,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 90 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work over 8,000 hours every year, generating 153,300 MWh electricity, of which 122,640 MWh will be exported to the China Southern Power Grid (hereinafter referred to as CSPG). The remaining electricity will be used by the project itself and there will be no purchased electricity. 
By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the proposed project activity avoids the emission of methane that would be generated under landfill condition. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can produce steam to generate power to replace the electricity that would otherwise be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants which are connected to the CSPG.The baseline scenario of this project is the same as the scenario prior to the implementation of the project, namely the landfill gas is vented directly and the equivalent power is supplied by the CSPG.
The project is expected to provide electricity of 122640 MWh annually into CSPG. The total emission reduction is expected to be 940030 tons of CO2 and the average annual 
emission reduction is 134290 tons of CO2 in a period of 7 years (from 25 April 2022 to 25 April 2029).
vcs-4755:
This project activities involves introduction and operation of new electric and/or hybrid vehicles that displace the use of fossil fuel vehicles in passenger and freight transportation. The vehicles include two-wheelers, electric four wheelers, electric three wheelers, electric light trucks, heavy trucks, haulage trucks, pick-up trucks, tractors, tippers and electric buses in transportation, last-mile logistics and delivery, this will replace the use of fossil fuel-based vehicles. The project vehicles use electric batteries, which displaces the GHG emissions produced by traditional internal combustion engines. As a result, the project results in lower GHG emissions, reduces the cost per delivery, and contribute to a cleaner environment. 
The project activity will be grouped project activity which will include new instances of vehicles in every verification cycle, each vehicle will consider as individual instances and follow the applicability criteria of instances given below. Based on emission reduction calculation of applicable CDM methodology AMS-III.C. “Emission reductions by electric and hybrid vehicles” version 16, overall emission reduction of project activity will not increase from 60,000 tCO2e/year for each instance. In 10 years, crediting period project will generate approx. 69,664 tCO2e and annual average emission reduction will 6,966 tCO2e.
vcs-4757: Jiangsu Suqian AWMS Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the grouped project) is a grouped project which installs 4 new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure for 4 newly built swine farms in Suqian, Jiangsu Province. The grouped project is a greenfield project, it is owned and implemented by Muyuan Foods Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project proponent). Each swine farm installs one set of AWMS to treat the manure on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
vcs-4759:
The “Improved cropland management project in Yunlong” developed by Yunlong County Bureau of Agriculture aims to raise farmer’s awareness on the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change the agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objective of the project is to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage, in order to achieve these, a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried out, the specific activities are one or combination of the following:
•	Reduced inorganic fertilizer application and added organic fertilizer application;
•	Reduced tillage /film mulching
•	improved residue management。
vcs-476: The 28MW Jinkouba Hydropower Project, a run-of-river hydropower project, is located on Baishuijiang River in Gansu Province, China. The project will have an installed capacity of 28MW, provided by two 14MW turbines, with an annual net output of 127,900MWh.Generated electricity will be exported to Northwest Region Power Grid (¡°NWPG¡±) through Gansu Grid.
vcs-4760:
Hebei Wei County Improved Agricultural Land Management Project  is located in Wei County, Handan City, Hebei Province of China. The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by the farms taking part to the project and raise the carbon storage in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. The project was implemented by the Weixian Capital Investment and Operation Co., Ltd and Hainan icarbon Ecological Development Co.,Ltd.
The project is located in Wei County. The project area is 46,666.7 ha. The crop rotation system in this project is winter wheat-summer corn.The proposed project is aimed to prevent the soil degradation through adoption of the improved crop land management practices (collectively referred to conservational tillage) to replace the conventional cultivation mode.
vcs-4761:
The REDD+ Estrela Acapuzinho Project seeks the conservation of forests located in the indigenous territories (Terra Indigena) of Acapuri de Cima, Estrela da Paz and Riozinho. located within the municipalities of Fonte Boa, Jutai and Juruá, in the Amazon state of Brazil. The project area has a total extension of 65,452 ha. The territories of these communities are part of the northern geographic area of the country characterized for its high biodiversity and rain tropical forests and for the presence of deforestation activities and social conflicts. Acapuri de Cima consists of 1 indigenous community (Aldeia), Estrela da Paz of 7 and Riozinho of 4. 

In the last years, it has been a national concern the high deforestation rates and associated social and biodiversity impacts in this region. No natural areas were drained or deforested before project beginning to generate carbon credits. Local understanding of the REDD+ mechanism consist in that the more standing forest that their territory maintains, more benefits will be delivered by the project. Deforestation drivers include mining activities, subsistence agriculture, and activities of illegal use. Social issues include absence of the state and lack of sanitation, energy, education and health infrastructure and lack of technical guidance regarding sustainable production models.

The project aims to mitigate the effects caused by climate change by reducing CO2 emissions derived from deforestation and forest degradation, restore degraded forest lands, promote sustainable management of forests, and develop productive activities to improve community welfare. The project also seeks to protect biodiversity and high conservation values, enhance ecological connectivity and secure natural habitats of vulnerable species (including those within some category of threat and those that represent ecological interest.
vcs-4763:
This project consists of afforesting a net area of 973 hectares: 658 with pine species, 287 with eucalyptus, and 28 with a mixture of 19 native species. In addition, 40 hectares of wetlands and native forests will be protected as areas of high environmental value within the gross area of the project. No logging activities will be carried out in order to maximize CO2 removals. The project activities will be carried out in two locations: the Puerto Valle ranch and the Garruchos ranch, both in the province of Corrientes, Argentina.
The project activity converts a degraded area, where intensive livestock farming was historically carried out, into an afforested area. Since its objective is to maximize carbon removal instead of producing high-quality wood, no pruning activities are carried out. Not cutting down the wood has major environmental advantages: it allows native species to grow spontaneously. Birdlife is not disturbed by forestry operations, as nests remain in place, and terrestrial fauna find continuous refuge within the plantation. Soil disturbance due to harvesting and planting cycles is also avoided.
This ARR project is being implemented in accordance with existing local guidelines on good forestry practices and sustainable forest management (SFM), avoiding negative impacts on biodiversity, local communities, and water bodies.
In addition, a program to enhance native species nursery and growth is being carried out in collaboration with the National University of Misiones, with the aim of further studying the needs and growing conditions of native species.
Greenhouse gas removals will be measured through the growth of above-ground and below-ground biomass, with a start date of September 1, 2022. The project is estimated to remove a total of 1,090,185 tCO2 over a 40-year period, representing an average removal rate of 27,255 tCO2 per year.

vcs-4767: Grow Indigo is implementing a regenerative agriculture-based carbon project in the extensive rice cultivation states of Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Odisha, and Telangana in India. The project area is characterized by traditional and intensive cultivation practices within diverse ecological systems, which emit significant amounts of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The southern region, encompassing Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka, excels in irrigated rice farming and cultivation in deltaic and non-deltaic regions. At the same time, Chhattisgarh and Odisha specialize in rainfed upland and lowland rice cultivation. Intensive agriculture practices in the project area have threatened food security and contributed to increased GHG emissions. The Grow Indigo project aims to incentivise farmers for adopting regenerative agriculture practices, thereby achieving the mitigation of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and fostering positive environmental and economic outcomes. Regenerative agriculture is a holistic farming system that focuses on improving soil health, biodiversity, and water quality. It can help to reduce GHG emissions by sequestering carbon in the soil. These practices include improved fertilizer management, cover cropping, crop rotation, reduced tillage, improved water management, crop residue management, agroforestry, etc. The project will also help to build the capacity of farmers to adopt regenerative agriculture practices through training and technical support. The project aims to scale up to 4 million hectares within the project area over a 5-year period. During the 20-year crediting period, it is estimated that there will be an average annual reduction and removal of 5,326,066 tCO2e. This innovative project has the potential to make a significant contribution to sustainable agriculture and climate change mitigation in India.
vcs-4768: Grow Indigo is implementing a regenerative agriculture-based carbon project that spans across Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. The transition to regenerative agriculture is vital to counteract soil degradation, fertility loss, water pollution, and natural resource depletion. This shift is crucial to maintain the ecosystem services of the Ganga basin. The potential impact of the VCS carbon project is immense. It promises to significantly reduce GHG emissions, improve soil health, and enhance biodiversity. Beyond environmental benefits, the project aims to uplift the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and enhance the resilience of the Ganga basin ecosystem in the face of climate change. Over a five-year period, the project aims to scale up to cover 4 million hectares within the Ganga basin region of the project area. The 20-year crediting period is expected to yield an average annual emission reduction and removal of 5,048,425 tCO2e. Grow Indigo's efforts in this project exemplify a proactive and holistic approach to tackle environmental challenges, offering a ray of hope for the Ganga basin and its residents.

The project “Natural silvopastoral systems in the Colombian Orinoquia Region” is a grouped project comprising a set of activities to improve grassland management. This will be accomplished by enhancing livestock practices through the following project activities:

- Implementation of adaptive multi-paddock grazing with improved deep-rooted grass cultivars, specifically Urochloa humidicola,
- Human-assisted regeneration of arbustive chaparros (Curatella americana) on paddocks to harness the potential of existing natural processes of seed dispersal and resources to restore woody vegetation,
- Cease grassland burns, and 
- Natural regeneration of tropical, highland savannah vegetation in buffer zones around riparian forests, and environmental.

The project activities will take place in approximately 150,000 ha of Vichada and Meta, two of the four departments of the Orinoquia region in Colombia, referred to here as “Colombian Orinoquia”. The crediting period is 2020 to 2040 applying the VCS Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management VM0042 Version 2.0. vcs-4787:
Climate change mitigation in the agricultural sector falls into three approaches. First, by reducing the current carbon emissions, via a better management of the carbon fluxes. Secondly, by avoiding potential emissions (e.g., by reusing the crop residues). Lastly, by enhancing the removals of carbon from the atmosphere (Smith et al., 2008). Regenerative agriculture (RA) is a farming approach which includes several practices (e.g., use of cover crops, reduced tillage) aiming at sequestrating soil carbon and contributing to those three approaches. RA also aims at implementing practices increasing biodiversity (e.g., crop diversity), improving the water cycle (e.g., use of drip irrigation) and increasing resilience to climate change. 
In the present project, the three mentioned approaches are applied in the framework of the Sustainable perennial orchards in Israel (SPOI). The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted and to raise the carbon stored in the soil and in the biomass. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. With perennials, year-round carbon removals will increase; the land will be irrigated with more precision which will increase the micro-organism activity. The leaves and the other biomass residue will remain on the ground from pruning, increasing the organic matter in the project areas. Orchards require less monitoring by tractors, thus reducing the demand of energy and the amount of fuel required, this reduces CO2 emissions in the project area, compared with the baseline scenario. Also, intercrops will be sown to increase the soil organic content. This is a grouped project, located in Israel. The main environmental and sustainable development objectives pursued by the grouped project are: a) reduce carbon emissions from less intensive agricultural practices, b) promote regeneration of soil and the increase of soil organic carbon (SOC), c) increase carbon sequestration.
vcs-4788: The RIZOME KAWAYAN PROJECT 1 is a grouped, Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) project, planting the native Dendrocalamus asper (giant bamboo) located on Mindanao Island, the Philippines. The project involves planting of giant bamboo in relevant planting sites in mostly ancestral domains of Indigenous Peoples of Mindanao. It is implemented in partnership between RIZOME (an engineered bamboo processing company with facilities in Mindanao), Climate Impact Partners (a leader in developing and delivering high-quality, high-impact carbon market solutions) and Indigenous Communities across Mindanao, all of which have legally recognized ‘Certificates of Ancestral Domain Titles’ (CADTs).
vcs-4789: C-Quest Capital’s Regenerative Agriculture and Forestry Technologies project aims to reverse the trends of soil and land degradation by promoting project activities that sequester carbon in agricultural soils and biomass; reduce dependency on nitrogen fertilizers; increase soil organic matter, moisture retention and health; reduce erosion; and diversify crop production and agricultural income streams. Specifically, this project will support conservation agriculture (CA), intercropping of leguminous shrubs, alley cropping, and farmer managed natural regeneration (FMNR) of trees on farmland across Malawi. CA includes adopting minimum or no-till practices, retaining crop residues, and rotating or intercropping multiple crops. Intercropping practices will focus mainly on Tephrosia vogelii, an indigenous fast growing, deep rooted leguminous shrub that can be used as green manure and produces abundant firewood. For alley cropping, multi-use trees or shrubs are planted in rows between crop strips to promote soil fertility and stability as well as diversify farm products. Lastly, FMNR practices vary widely according to the preferences of individual farmers but in general involve the selective protection of trees regenerating naturally from existing rootstock or stumps on croplands. Together, these practices transfer carbon from the atmosphere to above and belowground biomass through photosynthesis, a portion of which is further transferred to the SOC pool through biomass residues and root exudates. Reduced soil disturbance from no-till further protects SOC stocks, increased soil fertility reduces fertilizer use and its associated emissions, and crop residue retention avoids emissions from biomass burning.

vcs-4792:
The proposed small-scale project is methane recovery measures to be implemented in wastewater treatment facility at palm oil mill of PT. Berkat Cipta Abadi Mill, a member of Tunas Sawa Erma Group (TSE Group). The palm oil mill is already in operation and has series of open anaerobic lagoons for palm oil mill effluent (POME) treatment system.
The palm oil mill processes fresh fruit bunch (FFB) with a capacity of 100 tonnes FFB/hour to produce palm oil. During this process, wastewater effluent (around 1000 m3/day) is generated which contains high content of organic compound (around 66,900 mg COD/l). In the absence of the project activity, the POME is treated in open anaerobic lagoons. Decomposition of the organic compound in the POME produces biogas (i.e. methane gas) which under the baseline scenario (i.e. open anaerobic lagoons) is emitted to the atmosphere.
The purpose of proposed project is extraction and capture of methane enriched bio-gas generated from treatment of waste water (POME) and to utilize it for generation of steam/power required for the operating process and any excess methane gas will be flared in controlled manner in an Open flare. This reduces methane emissions a potential greenhouse gas (GHG) into the atmosphere that would have otherwise been emitted from the treatment of wastewater in anaerobic open lagoons without methane recovery. The CME will not account emission reduction from the end use of captured Biogas Plant.

Wuzhong Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) includes two plants, one is Xinwo plant (hereafter referred to as the Plant A) owned by Xinwo Biotechnology Co., Ltd. and the other is Ruiweier plant (hereafter referred to as the Plant B) owned by Ningxia Ruiweier Energy Environment Engineering Co., Ltd.. Both plants, located in Wuzhong City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, People’s Republic of China, have installed two sets of organic fertilizer production lines to treat the cattle manure.  The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions from uncovered anaerobic lagoons through composting techniques.

In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners. 

The project was designed to treat the manure to produce organic fertilizer. The project comprises fermentation system and fertilizer production system. It uses aerobic composting and fermentation technology to treat manure. It is estimated that approximately 210,000 tons of manure can be composted aerobically annually for the project. The final compost product obtained has been sold to local businesses and farmers. 

The project activity reduces GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from uncovered anaerobic lagoons. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 46,602 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 326,214 tCO2e during the first crediting period.
vcs-4794:
Leiyang Hexi Animal Manure Composting Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is a centralized manure treatment plant established in Group 1, Wufeng Village, Xiaoshui Town Leiyang City, Hengyang City, Hunan Province, People's Republic of China. The project recycles animal manure from local swine farms in Leiyang City and removes solids through a solid liquid separation system. 
Prior to the implementation of the project, manure from swine barns was left to decay in uncovered lagoons for uncontrolled anaerobic decay and was used seasonally for irrigation. The lagoons were barely fully drained and cleaned , and the methane produced was not recovered and was emitted directly to the atmosphere.The project activity, which introduces an animal manure composting system associated with solid separation techniques, avoids methane emissions through the separation of manure solids that are prevented from entering uncovered anaerobic lagoons, and further eliminates any potentials for methane emissions from the manure solids, as well as lowers the risk of exceeding nutrient application limits in the irrigation lands.

vcs-4796: The Cachoeira Porteira Conservation Project is located within the Brazilian Amazon, specifically in Oriximiná municipality in the Pará State, Brazil. Therefore, the project shall reduce emissions and combat decreased carbon stocks by conserving the area that would be subject to planned timber harvest in the baseline scenario. The project´s crediting period is 30 years, commencing on November 7th, 2022, and it is expected to be concluded on November 6th, 2052. The estimated average net GHG emission reductions is 567,544.43 tCO2e per year, totaling 17,026,332.88 tCO2e, over the crediting period. It is noteworthy that the Cachoeira Porteira Conservation Project meets the gold level criteria for, climate, community, and biodiversity. In a comprehensive approach, seven activities have been meticulously planned, which are synergistic with the Sustainable Development Goals, including Zero Hunger, Good Health and Well-being, Quality Education, Clean Water and Sanitation, Affordable and Clean Energy, Decent Work and Economic Growth, Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, Reduced Inequalities, and Life on Land.

Located in the center of the Democratic Republic of Congo, in the “Cuvette Centrale”, the Baulu Project is designed to protect 277,131 ha of native Congolese forests legally designated for selective logging. The Project is situated within Forest Concession 009/11 – Baulu, hereinafter referred to as the Baulu Concession. Since January 2018, this concession has been managed by the company Industrie Forestière du Congo (IFCO), which harvests volumes of commercial timber from it, following the terms of the Management Plan that was drawn up at the start of management. In 2023, as part of this project, IFCO has transferred the Baulu Concession to KNCC, with the objective of converting the logging concession into a protected forest.
The main activity of the Baulu Project is to set-aside areas of Logged-to-Protected Forests (LtPF), in the timber production series of 116,181 ha, to maintain and protect ecosystem services in forest production areas legally designated for selective logging. From the cessation of timber harvesting activities, which are present in the baseline scenario, the project aims to avoid emissions generated by logging, transport, processing of raw material as well as collateral damage to vegetation caused by the fall of cut trees on surrounding plants, decomposition of material left in the forest, construction of forest tracks for transport to the storage point and other infrastructure. A further advantage that the project will bring to the area is due to the cessation of the disturbance caused by logging activities to the fauna present in this area, which is very rich and varied, thanks also to the proximity of the Lomako-Yokokala Wildlife Reserve, which includes, among other species, bonobo, forest elephant, or Bongo antelope. Community activities will also be developed in the rural development area, such as awareness raising on illegal logging and poaching activities, awareness raising and training on sustainable agricultural practices, etc.
vcs-4799: This Carbon Disclosure SA Solar PV Grouped Project 1 consists of commissioning new, small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) installations and/or obtaining the rights to pursue carbon reduction from installations in the Republic of South Africa. The PV installations provide a clean, renewable source of electricity. In addition, the PV facilities increase the security of electricity supplies in South Africa. This is primarily because the national utility, Eskom, cannot provide consistent electricity supplies due to aged and failing infrastructure. The quantity and duration of power cuts in 2022 were expected to be the highest since load shedding was initiated in 2007. The Grouped Project is managed by Carbon Disclosure SA (Pty) Ltd. Carbon Disclosure SA outsources the commissioning of the PV facilities to third parties. The grouped project will comprise various project activity instances. Each project activity instance will comprise one or more solar PV facilities, where the total maximum installed capacity of the facilities is below 15 MW, per project activity instance.
vcs-48: The objective of the Shandong Tuoji Island Windfarm Project is to generate renewable electricity utilizing wind power resources and to sell the generated output to the North China Power Grid (NCPG) on the basis of a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). The project activity is located in Yantai City, Shandong Province, and is developed by Changdao Liankai Wind Power Co., Ltd. The project activity is to install and operate 16 wind turbines, each of which has the capacity of 750 kW, therefore, the total installed capacity of the Shandong Tuoji Island Windfarm is 12 MW. vcs-480: The project activity includes “conversion of the existing HSS technology  to Point Fed Prebake (PFPB) technology.  The primary aim of the project is to reduce the PFCs (Perfluorocarbon gases, both Perfluromethane (CF4) and Perfluroethane (C2F6) emissions which occur during anode effect at the smelters.   The emission reduction is expected from: a) Conversion of technology leading to reduction in PFCs (Perfluorocarbon gases, both Perfluromethane (CF4) and Perfluroethane (C2F6)) emission from anode effect mitigation and; b) Improvement in electrical energy efficiency leading to reduction in specific electricity energy consumption and hence equivalent carbon-dioxide emission reduction from the sources of power generation.
vcs-4800:
National Shale Oil Low-Carbon Intelligent Demonstration Base Carbon Sink Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Proposed Project”) is located in Xinbao Village, Yule Town, Huachi County, Qingyang City, Gansu Province, People’s Republic of China.
In the absence of the Proposed Project, the sites of the project are all low-nutrient, low-supply land, and the terrain is steep, with few herbaceous plants growing. Without its implementation, all the sites will keep the same circumstances with no natural renewal and reforestation within the project area. Through the implementation of the proposed project, it enhances ecosystem services through carbon storage, and soil and water conservation. It has a significant potential to mitigate the effects of climate change effects through microclimate moderation and natural resources conservation in the short run and through carbon sequestration in the long run. It also provides employment to rural population, and promote the sustainable development of local economy and society.
The project estimates the GHG removals occurring from afforestation activities in accordance with the methodology AR-AMS0007: “Afforestation and reforestation project activities implemented on lands other than wetlands”, Version 03.1 developed under Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) for small-scale plantations. The project intends to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. The total GHG emission reduction quantified under the project for crediting period of 20 years is 13,184 tCO2e with average CO2 removal of 659.20tCO2e per year.
vcs-4801: The project activity, an agroforestry project, aims to regenerate low-quality agricultural lands and generate livelihood opportunities within the geographical boundary of India through the plantation of trees of native species. The project promotes carbon sequestration, reduces pressure on natural forests, and benefits nearby communities. The project activity intends to increase the tree outside forest (TOF) areas which will help in carbon sequestration by trees and thereby mitigating climate change. The project will engage local communities, including small farmers, self-help groups (SHGs) and farmer produce organizations (FPOs) in the plantation efforts to not only reduce greenhouse gas emissions but also provide a sustainable source of income and livelihood for these marginalized sections.
vcs-4802:
The Rio Muru REDD+ Project is a grouped project developed by Angelim Participações S.A. that aims to mitigate climate change by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from planned and unplanned deforestation along the Muru River in Acre state, Brazil. The first project activity instance with 4,883 ha is part of a property of 30,881 hectares with mostly Open Ombrophilous Forest. It will avoid 2,075,259.83tCO2e of GHG emissions over 6 years by curbing planned deforestation. Additional instances in the Project Zone, covering the prevention of both planned and unplanned deforestation, will be incorporated into the project. 

The Project Proponent works with local families to create opportunities for employment and alternative activities to cattle ranching and slash and burn subsistence agriculture. The region also has high species diversity, including Rare, Threatened and Endangered (RTE) species such as Geoffroy’s Wooly Monkey Lagothrix lagotricha cana, Black Spider Monkey Ateles chamek, Big-leaf Mahogany Swietenia macrophylla and Ipê Amarelo Handroanthus serratifolius, among others. The Project aims to improve their conservation status by protecting and restoring their habitat and curbing harmful activities.
vcs-4803:
The composting process design uses Aerated Static Pile (ASP) composting of municipal curbside food wastes, lawn, and yard waste (L&YW) and other acceptable organic wastes as defined from Alberta’s Code of Practice for Compost Facilities. The ASP operation is chosen for its positive aeration process for its low risk of odours by control of composting temperatures and elimination of pathogen contamination. 
The produced compost will be utilized for agricultural soil regeneration with its quality defined by the CCME Guidelines for Compost Quality: A grade. To conserve the operational footprint at the Westlock Landfill site, storage and final curing will be completed as windrows on regional farms for soil regeneration.
Equipment will include Wheeled Loader, Screener, Mixer, excavators, truck and trailers, aeration blowers for Aerated Stack Piles (ASP) composting, water pumps, sprinklers, and temperature probes.
•Mixing unit (grinder) with conveyor.
•Waste separation unit (depends on quality of Food/Organic Waste).
vcs-4807:
BUFACAP is a national program that contributes to climate mitigation and adaptation efforts set out in the country’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) in the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector. It promotes sustainable agricultural land management on smallholder landholdings and is implemented across all administrative regions in the country, which fall within the Sudanian and Sudano-Sahelian Agro-Ecological Zones (AEZs). The main objectives are to sustainably increase smallholders’ agricultural productivity, food security, income, and welfare, build resilience /adaptation of the agrarian landscapes to climate change, reduce land degradation, and enhance tree/forest cover in line both the National Strategy for Soil Restoration, Conservation and Reclamation in Burkina Faso (SNRCRS) 2020-2024 and the National REDD+ agenda. The improved agricultural land management (IALM) practices promoted include compost/manure application, residue management (mulching), a menu of agroforestry, natural regeneration of trees, a menu of soil and water conservation practices, e.g., erosion control structures, a menu of integrated livestock management, e.g., forage crops, livestock housing, biogas digesters, etc., and a menu of agronomic practices, e.g., mixed cropping, intercropping, crop rotation, etc.  
The BUFACAP is a grouped project as defined in the VCS Standard version 4.5, i.e., “projects structured to allow the expansion of a project activity subsequent to project validation”.  
The project is using a partnership approach with the technical lead being the REDD+ Permanent Secretariat. The activities are expected to result in increased and sustainable agricultural production, tree/forest conservation and land restoration. GHG emission reductions will be generated through increased carbon storage in tree biomass and in soils within the agricultural landscapes. VM0042 will be used to account, monitor, and quantify the project’s GHG emission reductions.
vcs-4808: The Project Proponent, Smart Joules Private Limited, identified various energy saving opportunities and provided EPC services to achieve energy savings across identified Facilities of Apollo Hospitals in India. The Energy Savings are achieved through a combination of various measures including System Design Optimization, Installation of Energy Efficient Equipment and Operational Optimization.
vcs-481: The project activity has been essentially conceived to produce GHG free electricity from the Wind Electric Generators (WEGs). vcs-4810:
This is a voluntary non-AFOLU project promoted by the Plantar Group, hereinafter referred to as Plantar, which aims to reduce greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions from charcoal production in Brazil. The main goal of the project is to reduce methane emissions (CH4) through the installation of a methane abatement unit (afterburners) connected to brick-based carbonization kilns. The Project consists of the installation of the abatement units to reduce methane emissions from wood carbonization process by burning carbonization gases.  
Prior to project implementation, the residual gas of carbonization would be emitted directly into the atmosphere without any methane recovery or destruction. In addition to methane emission reductions, the project activity will provide smoke abatement and air quality improvement at and around the site.
vcs-4811:
The Panna Afforestation and Reforestation Project, is a grouped Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) project, planting a diverse range of native tree species on community and private land in Madhya Pradesh, India in partnership with local implementation partners and local communities. 
The project targets a mix of large-scale afforestation and reforestation on areas of degraded community (Gram Panchayat) land and the plantation of economically beneficial trees in and around smallholder farmers’ fields. Over the next 6 years, the project will plant over 11 million trees, comprising a mix of approximately 19 different native species, selected in consultation with communities and farmers, on an expected 19,000 hectares. 
In addition to ARR activities, the project also involves the construction of water infrastructure facilities such as ponds, dams and community tanks to improve water availability, tree survival and local biodiversity. Water irrigation through borewells and solar pumps help to improve irrigation within the project area. The project also intends to support agricultural productivity gains and minimise amongst participating farmers through an extensive training program, focusing on concepts such as climate smart agriculture practises, zero tillage, and improved mulching. 
A multi-faceted project that goes beyond carbon sequestration, the Panna Project also supports local livelihoods, improves food and water availability, sustainably raises agricultural yields, and positively impacts biodiversity across the project area. Through a community fund approach, the community members will benefit from a share of the carbon revenue as well as a multi-million dollar upfront funding commitment to improve education, healthcare and other aspects of life in the region.
vcs-4812:
India's agricultural sector faces pressing environmental challenges, notably due to conventional waste disposal methods such as open field burning and unmanaged biomass decay. These practices contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions and broader environmental degradation. Addressing this, Together for Restoration (a program by SRCNatura Sure Pvt. Ltd.) introduces Project Terre Boost, an initiative aimed at transforming agricultural residues into biochar for soil enhancement across seven Indian states—Assam, Nagaland, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Jharkhand. 
 
Project Terre Boost employs flame curtain pyrolysis technology in steel-shielded soil pits to convert agricultural waste into biochar. This biochar, mixed with manure and applied deep into the soil, promises a sustainable solution to waste management in agriculture. The project includes an initial cohort of 5,000 farmers (biochar producers). Environmental impacts of Project Terre Boost are substantial, with an estimated annual removal of 116,961 tons of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e), totalling 818,727 tCO2e over a seven-year crediting period. Moreover, the advantages of Project Terre Boost transcend environmental considerations, creating a dual advantage by significantly elevating the welfare of marginalised local farming communities.
vcs-4814:
The Project will cease all future forest land clearing, and implement reforestation, and forest restoration as well as programs for forest monitoring and preservation, biodiversity protection and enhancement, community engagement and sustainable development. 
The Project will implement a series of programs that will allow it to achieve its aims and emissions reduction activities.
vcs-4815:
The Urstamm project is an Improved Forest Management (IFM) project in Switzerland. It is a grouped project. The scope of the project is set to be the entire Swiss forest territory since landowners from the whole country are invited to join the project. The registration period for landowners is organized in cohorts. The pilot project “Kelleramt” is based in the Central Plateau, or “Mittelland” of Switzerland near Zurich.

The project will apply selective logging to the parcels in accordance with the methodology VM0012 Improved Forest Management in temperate and boreal forests. The project will increase the carbon inventory by selective logging. The effectiveness and importance of this method has been confirmed by latest research and it will enable to build a climate anti-fragile or at least resilient forest population that becomes a carbon sink rather than a source.

The management plan is in accordance with the forest goals of the Swiss Confederation in terms of climate change mitigation and increased resilience of the forest to climate change. Indeed, it advises the forest managers to (i) increase biodiversity, (ii) increase structural diversity, (iii) increase genetic diversity, (iv) increase individual tree resistance to stress and (v) decrease the target Diameter at Breast Height (DBH). Selective logging allows the forest manager to actively control the development of the forest and therefore hinder the effect of climate change of the forest carbon sink. For example, this method allows the forest manager to increase light availability on the floor and promote light demanding and climate change resilient species. Also, the project is looking to increase the frequency of logging activities on each parcel in accordance with point (v) of the Swiss government and its forest strategy. 

To monitor the implementation of the sustainable forest management and provide precise information monitoring through remote sensing will be carried out (dMRV).
vcs-4816:
He xi Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Yanshan Village, Hutang Township, Fengcheng City, Yichun City, Jiangxi Province, P.R China. The geographical coordinates for the project site are east longitude 115°36′5.02″ and north latitude 28°18′9.14″. The project is owned and implemented by Fengcheng Xinfengtai Environment Technology Co., Ltd. 
The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects manure waste of swine from the multiple hog farms in the Fengcheng City. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. The recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation at the biogas power plant. The designed installed capacity of the biogas power plant is 1MW. For simplification and be conservative, the emission reductions from electricity generation will not be accounted for. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is used in nearby farmlands by aerobic treatment.
The project started construction on 23-Oct-2020 and started operation on 05-May-2022. Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system (uncovered open lagoon) at the livestock farms and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emissions of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 52,431 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 367,018 tCO2e during the first 7-year renewable crediting period.
vcs-4817: The proposed project seeks to improve the household conditions of rural and semi urban communities living in various districts of Odisha state of India by distributing better and efficient cookstoves called Improved Cookstoves which have higher thermal efficiency and would emit low amount of greenhouse gases (GHG) as compared to traditional cookstoves. The proposed project activity will help in reducing the GHG emissions. The old and traditional cookstoves having low thermal efficiency and emitting high amount of greenhouse gases will be replaced with new and efficient cookstove technologies, viz., Improved Cookstoves (ICS). The project activity, in turn, will contribute to reduction of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere, conservation of forest and also improving the quality of health of the ICS users as the indoor air quality will be also improved along with drudgery reduction in everyday cooking.

This grouped project aims for the long-term rejuvenation of Colorado’s forests, achieved through native mixed-species reforestation that reverses the impact of land degradation and the loss of flora and fauna. Project activities are implemented by Land Life, a Dutch technology-driven reforestation company that grows forests by planting trees at scale. vcs-4821:
The proposed ARR VCS project is a grouped project focusing on the reforestation and restoration of degraded lands in Portugal. 63% of Portugal’s land is classified as vulnerable to desertification, with 32.6% in a degraded state (ICNF, 2020). Land and biodiversity regeneration are central objectives of this project, which employs the latest technologies and planting techniques to ensure the highest rate of survival of mixed-species native trees. Project activities are implemented by Land Life, a Dutch technology-driven reforestation company that grows forests by planting trees at scale and using innovative technology to optimize tree selection, survival, and resilience. Land Life maintains an on-the-ground presence through Land Life Iberia’s office in Burgos and maintains close collaboration with local partners and authorities. The long-term resilience of forest and vegetation composition will be monitored to track the success and permanence of the forests.

Project activities are implemented and monitored according to the VCS-approved project methodology AR-ACM0003, with the expectation that additional project instances are to be added over the coming years. The first group of instances of the project covers 365 ha in Portugal, at five distinct planting sites: Torre de Tavares (70.4 ha), Freguesia de Tavares (90.8 ha), Peges (35.27 ha), Carvalhais (87.8 ha) and Matança (56.27 ha). While each project instance is expected to sequester carbon across the entire 100-year crediting period, the ex-ante estimate focuses on the initial 41 years for practical reasons for each project instance to determine the annual average profile. These project instances (implemented in 2021 and 2022) are expected to sequester approximately 81,802 tCO2e over the initial 41 years of the 100-year crediting period. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals is 1,995 tCO2e. A total of 292,908 native trees are expected to become established in the project areas.
vcs-4822:
The proposed ARR VCS project is a grouped project focusing on the reforestation and restoration of degraded lands in Australia. Land and biodiversity regeneration are central objectives of this project, which employs the latest technologies and planting techniques to ensure the highest rate of survival of mixed-species native trees and support the permanent establishment of native flora and fauna. Project activities are implemented by Land Life, a Dutch technology-driven reforestation company that grows forests by planting trees at scale by using innovative technology to optimize tree selection, survival, and resilience. Local Australian partner Cassinia Environmental brings on-the-ground expertise in forestry and conservation, supporting Land Life’s team of reforestation specialists in managing and implementing quality projects in Australia. The long-term resilience of forest and vegetation composition will be monitored to track the effectiveness and permanence of the forests.

Project activities are implemented and monitored according to the approved project methodology AR-ACM0003. The first group of instances within this PD covers a total of 718 ha of degraded land Australia, with projects located in Victoria, New South Wales, and South Australia. The crediting period of this grouped project is 100 years as each of the initial project instances has 100 years of carbon right assigned from the land owner to the project proponent. While each project instance is expected to sequester carbon across the entire 100-year crediting period, the ex-ante estimate focuses on the initial 41 years for practical reasons to determine the annual average profile. These project instances (implemented across 2022 and 2023) are expected to sequester approximately 213,380 CO2e over the initial 41 years of the crediting period. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals is 5,204 tCO2e. A total of 494,035 native trees are expected to become established at the sites.
vcs-4824:
The Turu EV Charging Network Project (hereinafter Project) is proposed for registration under the Verra Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Standard, Version 4.5, 04 October 2023 (hereinafter Standard) and associated Program Guide, Version 4.4, 29 August 2023 (hereinafter Guide). The Project is a Grouped Project, consisting of multiple Project Activity Instances, and is proposed to be submitted following VCS Methodology VM0038, Methodology for Electric Vehicle Charging Systems, Version 1.0, 18 September 2018 (hereinafter Methodology). The Methodology lays out the requirements for electric vehicle (EV) charging systems to generate emission reductions across a range of potential charging systems and their applicable fleets. The Project follows the additionality requirements set out in VCS Methodology Module VMD0049, Version 1.0, 18 September 2018 (hereinafter Module).

The individual Instances are located across the Republic of Korea, and charging stations implemented by JeJu Electric Vehicle Service Co., Ltd. are also included in the Project. The Project will generate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions through the displacement of fossil fuel powered vehicles across the included fleet categories with grid-connected electricity. The project proponent is also driving the expansion of renewable energy utilization through the introduction and expansion of solar fusion charging stations.
vcs-4825:
The Evergreen II REDD+ project aims at protecting forests located in one of the regions with the highest deforestation rate in the Amazon Biome: the municipality of Apuí. The
South of the municipality has already been reached by the “Arc of Deforestation”. In the last 10 years, Apuí has been one of the most deforested municipalities in the Amazon
Biome. Besides the damage caused to natural ecosystems, the land-use changes have provoked severe social conflicts through processes of land-grabbing and installation of
agriculture and cattle ranching activities, contributing to the expulsion of family-scale forest extractives from that region. The primary objective of the Evergreen II REDD+ project is to avoid unplanned (AUD) deforestation in an area of 36,989.62 hectares of Amazonian forest, equating to 6,191,013.12 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (25-November-2020 to 24-November-2050), with an annual average of 206,367.10 tCO2e. The Project Proponents will adopt additional conservation measures: remote sense monitoring of changes in the land cover using satellite images, deforestation and heat spots monitoring, increasing surveillance hiring private security, and implementing a land, water, and air vigilance plan using quads, boats, drones and a plane, build security bases and provide internet signal to improve communication for illegal deforestation complaints. Other social activities that benefit the local community will be supported, such as improving electricity infrastructure by solar photovoltaic panels, construction of groundwater wells, bioeconomy, and environmental education, improvement of rural roads and bridges, associations support, development the value chain of forest products and agriculture family production (nuts, oils, fish, fruits, legumes, and seeds). The CCB Standards is being considered to assess and monitor the project's contribution to excepcional positive impacts on biodiversity and communities.
vcs-4829: The project focuses on distributing fuel-efficient, improved cookstoves (ICS) in Kenya. The Solaxy improved cookstoves are designed to burn wood more efficiently, enhancing thermal transfer to cooking pots and consequently conserving fuel. Additionally, the use of these stoves will reduce the time women and children spend collecting firewood, thereby contributing to their overall well-being and safety.
