This project will be developed in the Republic of Mozambique. The areas of implementation will be the Central portion of the Country, considering in particular the provinces of Maputo province and Maputo city 
The average annual GHG emission reduction expected with the implementation of the improved cookstove distribution project in the Country is around 89,000 tCO2e per year.
vcs-4879:
The project activity involves the distribution of improved cookstoves (ICSs) among local communities based in rural and peri urban areas of five provinces of Angola, where currently several households still rely on inefficient and pollutant traditional cooking techniques.
The project aims to replace the traditional cooking mechanisms used by local people (three-stone fire or rudimental stoves) with ICSs that require less fuel and decrease the biomass combustion’s emissions, with a consequent reduction of health hazard coming from the indoor smoke pollution. The introduction of more efficient stoves will help to limit the demand for woody biomass, reducing the unsustainable use of forests and halting deforestation that is progressing rapidly in the Country. The improved cookstoves’ deployment will also have a positive impact on women’ life, reducing the time they spend for collecting woody biomass and cooking the meals, giving them the possibility to invest their time in a more effective way.
Through the implementation of engagement and training processes dedicated to the local communities involved in the project, all the households receiving the ICS will be aware of the environmental improvements and the carbon finance benefit generated by their effective use of the stove.
This project will be developed in rural and peri-urban areas of five provinces of Angola. The implementation areas will be the North-Central portion of the Country, specifically in provinces of Luanda, Cuanza Norte, Cuanza Sul, Benguela and Huambo. 
The average annual GHG emission reduction expected with the implementation of the improved cookstove distribution project in the Country is around 164,000 tCO2e per year.
vcs-488: The project activity is a new run-off-river type hydropower plant with a daily regulating pond at the five-hour peak power generation, diverting from the Renun river main stream and eleven (11) tributaries into Lake Toba. The regulating pond has a storage capacity of 500,000 m3 and a power density of 820 W/m2. The total actual installed capacity of the project is 82 MW, consisting of two 41 MW turbines. The project is owned and developed by PT. PLN (Persero), a state-owned electricity company. The project supplies electricity to the connected Sumatra grid. The electricity currently generated by the grid is relatively carbon intensive. The proposed project will increase the utilization of renewable energy sources, in this case hydro energy, by operating a new hydropower plant.
vcs-4880: The Feedworks Agolin Enteric Methane Abatement in Ruminants, Australia & New Zealand project will be implemented by Feedworks Pty Ltd.  and their partners in the dairy sector in Australia and New Zealand through the use of VM0041 Methodology for the Reduction of Enteric Methane Emissions From Ruminants Through the Use of Feed Ingredients. It is a grouped project which aims to reduce methane (CH4) emissions in ruminant dairy cattle through the use of Agolin® Ruminant.
vcs-4881: Since its inception in 1999, over 200,000 participants organized into over 31,000 TIST Small Groups have planted over 25 million trees in Tanzania, India, Kenya, and Uganda - accomplishing GhG sequestration through tree planting, creating a potential long-term income stream, and developing sustainable environments and livelihoods. Tanzania 011 is a subset of the TIST project in Tanzania and applies to 638 Small Groups, 3,740 Participants, 2,611 active Project Areas, and 2,882 hectares.  TIST farmers use a mosaic restoration approach, planting on thousands of individual farms spread across the landscape. The individual farms are found throughout Tanzania and concentrated around Mpwapwa and Kibondo.
vcs-4882: The objective of the Uganda Native Reforestation and Agroforestry Project is to reforest an area of around 10,000 hectares using two approaches: planting agroforestry tree species on agricultural lands,and planting native forest species on degraded forest reserves. Paired together, these two strategies will reforest the landscape while sequestering carbon dioxide and providing ecosystem services. The degraded land will be rehabilitated with tree canopy cover, and over time local hydrology and soil health will be restored. On smallholder farms, the agroforestry trees will also improve crop yields and diversify income streams. The grouped Project will control erosion and increase water infiltration, as well as provide local employment opportunities while contributing to the region’s food security.
vcs-4883: The objective of the Agroforestry Project of Cameroon is to reforest an area of around 10,000 hectares, starting with degraded plots in Cameroon currently managed as unused or under-used agricultural lands or degraded grasslands, and reforest the landscape while sequestering carbon dioxide. The degraded land will be rehabilitated with tree canopy cover, and over time local hydrology and soil health will be restored. The grouped Project will control erosion and increase water infiltration, as well as provide local employment opportunities while contributing to the region’s food security.
vcs-4884: The objective of the Forest Landscape Restoration in Panama project is to reforest an area of around 25,000 hectares, starting with unused or under-used, degraded land in Panama currently managed as abandoned or cattle pasture grazed at very low densities, and restore this ecosystem with tree cover in order to sequester carbon dioxide. The degraded land will thus be rehabilitated with a forest canopy, and over time biodiversity and local hydrology will be restored. The grouped Project will control erosion, regenerate soil health, and increase water infiltration, consequently improving ground water levels in the area, as well as provide local employment opportunities. Most land being considered is in the central region of Panama, but all regions of the country with degraded cattle pasture are eligible.
vcs-4885:
Groundwork BioAg Rootella Carbon Agricultural Program (the ‘Project’) enables the adoption of improved agricultural land management (IALM) practices on continental United States and Canada, where the project instances and baseline scenarios of similar nature. The project developer (Groundwork BioAg) will facilitate this adoption through financial incentives and technical support. Landowners and tenant farmers (‘farmers’) will improve soil carbon sequestration rates by applying one or more of the following practices to increase soil carbon sequestration rates and/or reduce on-farm greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions: 
•	Soil Amendments or seed treatments 
•	Reduced Tillage and Stubble Management: 
•	Cover Crops 
•	Fertilizer Nitrogen Reductions 
•	Energy Consumption Reductions through Practice Changes 
•	Improved Crop Rotation 
•	Methane Emission Reductions 
The focus of the Project is farmers who grow crops such as, but not limited to, corn, soy or wheat using conventional farming practices. These practices vary from farm to farm but may include one or more tillage passes per year, fields are generally left bare over winter, and excessive fertilizer application.
vcs-4887:
Wastewater to Biogas Grouped Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is a grouped project which consists of biogas recovery projects located in Malaysia.
The project is owned by Green Lagoon Technology Sdn Bhd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner), and implementation of the projects are by the individual plant operators of each project activity instance (PAI). The purpose of this Grouped Project is to recover biogas generated from wastewater treatment process which would have otherwise, been emitted into the atmosphere resulting in GHG emissions. The recovered biogas is expected to be utilized for various purposes:
a. To upload to grid, and/or
b. Use in transportation applications, and/or
c. Bottled and distributed to end users, and/or
d. Hydrogen production, and/or
e. Excess biogas will be flared in open/enclosed flare.
vcs-4888: Our project, based in Uganda, focuses on carbon removal by collaborating with private landowners to significantly enhance the country's vegetation cover. Our goal extends beyond carbon removal; we strive to uplift local communities and enrich biodiversity. Through our initiatives, we aim to create a positive impact that transcends environmental benefits, fostering sustainable development and harmony between people and nature.
vcs-4889: The project 'Natural Forest Regeneration for Enhanced Carbon Stocks in the Albertine Rift' (FRECAR) focuses on the Kagombe-Bugoma areas in the Northern part of the Albertine Rift, known for their highly biodiverse tropical moist forests. The project aims to protect and restore the natural value of four Central Forest Reserves through replanting indigenous trees, addressing agricultural encroachment, reducing unauthorized access to forest resources, and promoting sustainable practices. The project is estimated to generate significant greenhouse gas reductions and removals while improving biodiversity and fostering sustainable livelihoods for local communities. These triple benefits for community, biodiversity, and climate will be achieved through establishing climate resilient and adaptative measures for communities, forest conservation through the planting of indigenous trees, and tackling human-wildlife conflicts.
vcs-489: The purpose is development, design, engineering, procurement, finance, construction, operation and maintenance of bundled wind power project of 44 MW in the Indian state of Maharashtra to provide reliable, renewable power to the Maharashtra state electricity grid which is part of the NEWNE grid. The project considered has used the barren land at Satara, Sangli, Nasik, and Ahmednagar District in the state of Maharashtra. The project is helping in bridging the gap between demand and supply by using wind as a source of generating electrical energy
vcs-4890: The Regenerative Development of Anlo Wetlands Project is a grouped project that aims to help adapt to climate change, enhance biodiversity and ecosystem health, and improve livelihoods of communities dependent on the local mangrove ecosystem. With a potential for expansion of planting up to 9,991 hectares of mangrove in the Keta Lagoon in Ghana, the first instance covers approximately 1,536 hectares. The primary objective of the project is to expand the mangrove area through the planting of diverse native mangrove species. This aims to enhance the positive functions and ecosystem services that mangroves provide to communities and biodiversity. The project is situated in the Volta region, within the Keta Lagoon Complex Ramsar site. This site is recognised for its exceptional biodiversity and wetland ecosystems and faces a necessity of preservation. Thus, the project's location contributes to enhancing the health and connectivity of habitats and ecosystems. The project is led by Terraformation as the project proponent, with the Regenerative Development of Anlo Wetlands Foundation as the project implementer of the project activities. The project activities will take place in locations selected based on their ecological suitability, in collaboration with local communities. The project design encourages and promotes active participation from these local communities. The project plans to reverse mangrove decline, restore ecosystem services, and offer sustainable livelihood opportunities while preserving biodiversity. The project will achieve these aims through large-scale mangrove reforestation, regenerative aquaculture, and apiculture. In addition to restoring native vegetation and habitat for fish and wildlife, the project will generate GHG benefits by sequestering carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through the restoration of mangrove ecosystems.
vcs-4891: The project is a grouped afforestation project in the Districts of Mzimba and Nkhotakota, Malawi. The project will establish smallholder woodlots on degraded land. The project will build landholder capacity to manage tree nurseries, plant trees and manage the woodlots and provide an alternative source of income to the people participating in the project. The first activity instance of this grouped project started in Mzimba with 1.8 million trees planted in 2022 and 2023.
vcs-4892: The proposed project aims at increasing the tree cover outside forest (ToF) areas through ARR activities. The planting activities occur on predominantly privately owned agricultural lands and consist of planting farmer-friendly trees on the bunds of and within these plots. In some cases, planting occurs on community lands and other non-forest & non-agricultural private lands, that are used by physical structures such as schools and ashrams. Implemented in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, overall the project addresses livelihoods, the financial security of local farming and other communities through planting of farmer friendly trees in the project area along with associated community-based interventions.
vcs-4893:
The proposed VCS project “Landscape-based approach towards the revitalization of degraded agro-ecology for livelihood generation of marginalized communities”, represents an afforestation project in the states of Odisha and Maharashtra, India. The project promotes and implements the plantation of Eucalyptus species with short rotations in privately owned lands of small and marginal farmers in the project area. 
Maharashtra (63.7% ) and Odisha (20.61% ) are among the largest contributors to the agricultural sector of the country, and are majorly dependent on rain-fed agriculture (around 75% - 80%  ) for sustenance making them vulnerable to the changing climatic conditions. Rise in temperature, unpredictable rainfall, soil erosion and increasing drought are among the major conditions that are affecting the productivity of the land leading to crop failure  . 
Urvara Krsi Private Limited (UKPL) has been promoting agroforestry with small & marginal farmers belonging to various tribal communities across the states of India. UKPL with its landscape approach is implementing plantations under models such as Block plantation, Wadi Model (NABARD), Bund Plantation etc. in agricultural areas, bunds, wasteland, community land, and barren land. They provides expert technical guidance to the farmers on the selection and maintenance of plantations and assists in creating market linkage for the sale of timber/pulp. This model not only helps in increasing the productivity of the land but also creates additional livelihood opportunities for the farmers.
The project area is estimated to carry out plantation on 13,255 ha of land between 2021 to 2024. Over a crediting period of 29 years the project will generate gross removals or net removals of 12,63,577 tCO2e and 43,571 tCO2e/yr.
vcs-4894:
This grouped project is designed to establish in the first stage 810.98 hectares of native species in the municipalities of Aracataca, Fundación, Santa Marta, Ciénaga, Dibuya, and El Copey, Colombia. The specific objectives of this project are:
1.	Setting up large-scale tree planting projects on 810.98 ha based on the “direct seeding” technique.
2.	Implementation of solutions for soil fertility, water conservation, climate change mitigation, and animal habitat.
3.	To raise awareness of climate change and adaptation strategies.
4.	To develop economic instruments to ensure the sustainability of the project over time.
5.	Creation of schools’ farms through the implementation of a community program that fosters the training of the community on sustainability restoration practices with native species to create a community using self-sustaining systems.
The project contributes to the mitigation of greenhouse gases through a combination of sustainable land management practices and principles that promote carbon sequestration and reduced greenhouse gas emissions planting 731,765 trees in the first instance. These plants capture and store carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through photosynthesis, effectively sequestering carbon in the biomass and soil, and will result in an annual average of 46,053 tCO2, during 30 years, thus, a total of 1,381,590 tCO2.
vcs-4895:
Ishinomaki Improved Forest Management Project (IIFMP) intends to switch from less productive forests to high productive and diversified forest through Forest Improved Management practices. IIFMP takes place in forests under the jurisdiction of the Ishinomaki District Forestry Association. 
Ishinomaki District Forestry Association  (Ishinomaki Chiku Shinrinkumiai in Japanese, hereafter  IFC) is a broad-based forestry cooperative that covers Ishinomaki City, Higashimatsushima City, and Onagawa Town in Miyagi Prefecture. Focusing on forest maintenance, timber production and sales, and timber recycling, the cooperative aims to revitalise forests and forestry by promoting environmental considerations, and is working to realise a wood first society that takes the initiative in utilising timber, such as by promoting the use of biomass power generation chips and timber for public housing. 
IIFMP is a grouped project with a scope area of 3919 ha and a first instance of 900 ha of conifers forest.
vcs-4896:
The Brazil Precision Agriculture Carbon Program (BPACP) incentivizes the large-scale adoption of big data-driven precision agriculture in Brazil.

It is a grouped VCS project implemented by a national carbon credit cooperative society (“Carbon Coop”). The project has partnered with multiple stakeholders on a national scale, including soil laboratories, a big data analytics platform, agro-inputs and machinery dealers, local agricultural consultants and soil sampling experts, to connect with farmers and leverage the adoption of precision agriculture.

The carbon project intends to harness data analytics, remote sensing, climate and crop modelling, artificial intelligence, and in-field sensors, to help farmers make data-informed decisions that sustainably increase productivity and crop resilience (adaptation), reduce and remove greenhouse gas emissions (mitigation), and enhance achievement of global food security and national development goals.
vcs-4897:
The Fortaleza Ituxi III ALM project is located in one of the regions with the highest deforestation rate in the Amazon Biome: the municipality of Lábrea. For the last 10 years,
it has been one of the most deforested municipalities in the Amazon Biome and the south of Lábrea has already been reached by the “Arc of Deforestation”. Beside the
damage caused to natural ecosystems, the land-use changes have provoked severe social conflicts through processes of land-grabbing and installation of agriculture and
cattle ranching activities (often irregular or even illegal), contributing to the expulsion of family-scale forest extractives from that region. The main activity of the Fortaleza Ituxi III ALM project consists of growing Açaí (Euterpe oleracea) in an integrated production system intercropped with pasture for a low carbon cattle grazing. The project area is located in the municipality of Lábrea, in the state of Amazonas, in northern Brazil. The project area covers an extension of 371.52 ha, referring to the lease of the first instance and lies to the north of the Ituxi River, situated on the Nossa Senhora das Cachoeiras do Ituxi farm. The Fortaleza Ituxi III ALM is an Agriculture Land Management (ALM) project based on Improved Grassland Management (IGM) and it aims to include practices that demonstrably reduce net GHG emissions of grassland ecosystems by increasing soil carbon stocks, improving aboveground biomass and reducing N2O emissions and/or reducing CH4 emissions. The estimated GHG emission reduction is 58,099.93 tCO2e over the 20-year project lifetime (01-July-2023 to 30-June-2043), with an annual average of 2,905.00 tCO2e.
vcs-4898: This project, situated in Kenya, focuses on carbon dioxide removal within the Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) framework of Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use (AFOLU) initiatives. Its primary objective is to bolster community resilience against the adverse effects of climate change. This is achieved through the enhancement of local capacity and the adaptation of agroforestry systems, promoting both well-being and environmental sustainability. The chosen tree species for plantation are well-received by the local community and have seamlessly integrated into the surrounding ecosystem over time.
vcs-4899: This initiative is a carbon dioxide removal project located in Uganda, classified as a Least Developed Country (LDC) according to the UN List. The primary goal is to increase the green cover in the Jinja district and other regions that have experienced notable deforestation over the past two decades. Beyond carbon removal, the project contributes significantly by generating employment opportunities for various local communities and yielding additional co-benefits.
vcs-49: Liaoning Huanren Niumaodashan Wind Power Project is located in Huanren County, Benxi, Liaoning Province of China. The project is installed of 29 (7 Gamesa-52 and 22 Gamesa-58) wind turbines with a nominal capacity of 850 KW, providing a total installed capacity of 24.65MW. The estimated annual generation of the project is 53.93GWh. As a result, annual 61,739 tones of CO2 emission reduction are achieved by replacing equivalent electricity generated by Northeast China Power Grid, which is dominated by thermal power plants.
vcs-490: The project is located at Kita and Bhu village in Jaisalmer District of Rajasthan state in India. It involves the installation of 75 turbines of Enercon make (E-48), each of which has a rated output of 800kW, providing a total capacity of 60 MW. The purpose of the project activity is to generate electricity using wind power resources in the region and provide reliable, renewable power to the Rajasthan state electricity grid, which is part of the Northern regional electricity grid. The project contributes to sustainability in the region by reducing pollution, creating employment opportunities, improving the livelihoods of the local people. At a larger scale, the project assists Rajasthan and ultimately India in stimulating and accelerating the commercialization of grid-connected renewable energy technologies and markets in India.
vcs-4900: It is a carbon dioxide removal project that facilitates inclusive rural transformation through carbon financing in the oil palm industry. It strives to increase rural incomes sustainably by fostering an efficient and socially responsible oil palm sector. This involves establishing sustainable supply chains, diversifying household livelihoods, creating an enabling environment for scaling-up, and supporting alternative economic opportunities to mitigate social risks. It aims to counteract prior environmental degradation and contribute to sustainable development by converting low-productive grasslands and cropland into perennial Tenera hybrid tree cropland.
vcs-4904: Production and casting of magnesium alloys requires protection against oxidation of the molten metal. While there are various protection systems used in the magnesium industry, the most common is use of Sulphur Hexafluoride (SF6) as a cover gas. SF6 is non-reactive and as such is very effective for protecting molten magnesium during the production process. However, it has a very high Global Warming Potential (GWP) of 23,500. AMACOR has installed an alternate cover gas system at its Facility to switch from SF6 to a perfluoro-2-methyl-3-pentanone product named Bestsolv Zulu. Thus, the baseline scenario as further detailed in the Project Document, is the continued use of SF6 as cover gas, while the project scenario is the use of the Bestsolv Zulu fluid as cover gas at the Facility. Since Perfluoro-2-methyl-3-pentanone has a lower GWP (2,380) compared with SF6, the substitution results in emission reductions.
vcs-4905:
REDD Pantanal is a multi-activity grouped project located in the Pantanal of Brazil. The project is classified under scope 14 - AFOLU and falls into the category of REDD considering planned and unplanned deforestation. Its main goal is to conserve the remaining forest cover of properties under pressure from deforestation and forest degradation, reducing GHG emissions.
Mapbiomas’ Annual Deforestation Report of Brazil indicates that Pantanal deforestation has increased by 8.2% from 2021 to 2022. The 2022 deforestation rate was 31,212 ha. The increase in deforestation in natural forests of Brazil, threatens climate change mitigation and affects provisions of energy, water, and food security in Brazil and worldwide. 
REDD Pantanal seeks landowners who opt to keep conserved areas which could be converted legally. Additionally, it will strengthen the protection of Permanent Preservation Areas (APP) and Legal Reserves (RL), which have also been targeted by illegal deforestation and degradation. ECCON will be responsible for the development, implementation across different instances, and monitoring of the climatic parameters of REDD Pantanal. Landowners are also involved in the project, who, through the signing of a contract contribute effectively to maintaining their areas under native vegetation. This commitment allows them to support the activities to be developed by the project. 
The revenue from carbon credits generated by REDD Pantanal will contribute to conservation, making the activity more appealing for the rural producers. Therefore, maintaining the standing forest will be a competitive alternative to other land uses, which poses a threat to the conversion of native vegetation in the current scenario.
REDD Pantanal activities commenced in 2021, with a 45-year crediting period, from November 18, 2021, to November 17, 2066. PAI 01 is the first instance of the project, which will prevent the emission of 1,837,304 tCO2e over 30 years.
vcs-4908:
The project - SIDBI EV PROGRAM -development objective is to foster a transition from conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) to sustainable electric vehicles (EV) in India. The Project supports Resource-Efficient Growth through accelerating the transition from ICE vehicles to EVs in India and reduce costs, oil imports, energy consumption, air pollutants and GHG emissions while supporting mobility needs of low- and middle-income groups. The Project is aligned with the Government of India (GoI) National Clean Air Program for adoption of cleaner technologies in cities and will contribute towards the achievement of India’s EV 30@30, Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) target on emission intensity reduction and Net Zero targets through the development of an integrated, efficient, inclusive, low-carbon transport system. Despite the positive economic benefits of introducing EVs, and strong government efforts, EV adoption remains low relative to targets. 
The project through a multi-pronged approach will address the key market failure of lack of affordable commercial financing for EVs among other issues. Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), a pan-India financial institution, will launch and implement the grouped project and perform the role of ‘Program Manager’ (Implementing Agency).
The first instance under the grouped project with about 50,000 EVs is expected to lead to annual average emission reduction of about 19491 tCO2 and total 19,49,16 tCO2 over a 10-year crediting period.
vcs-491: The small-scale project activity is to build, operate and maintain a landfill gas collection and flaring system on the Antanas landfill in Pasto, Colombia. It is an anaerobic managed landfill, owned by the municipality of Pasto and managed by Empresa Metropolitana de Aseo de Pasto (EMAS – Pasto S.A.E.S.P.). The landfill started operations in April 2001 and will close in 2034. Since its opening, the landfill has received approximately 600,000 tons of solid waste from the municipality of Pasto and neighbouring municipalities. It currently receives 220 tons of waste per day. The landfill is covered with clay and vegetal soil on areas which do not receive waste anymore. The location details of the landfill are provided in section A4. The equipment includes inter alia a gas collection network, a high temperature enclosed flare, monitoring and control systems and civil works.At a later stage, the landfill gas collected may be used as fuel for electricity generation.
vcs-4911: Bigbloc Building Elements Private Limited has established an aerated autoclaved concrete (AAC) blocks manufacturing unit in Wada, Maharashtra, with an annual capacity of 2,50,000 m3. The project focuses on producing AAC blocks, a lightweight, precast, and thermally insulating building material with lower embodied energy and reduced environmental emissions compared to conventional materials. The initiative emphasizes optimizing manufacturing processes, incorporating renewable energy sources, and adopting sustainable supply chain practices. By replacing traditional building materials like bricks and concrete, AAC blocks are expected to generate a significant annual average reduction of 48,032 tons of CO2 equivalent, based on analyses of AAC block production's reduced energy consumption, raw material use, and transportation emissions compared to traditional materials.
vcs-4912: The Regenerative Agriculture-Driven Afforestation & Restoration (i.e., ARBRE is the French equivalent acronym that is the project title) is a VCS grouped ARR project being launched by a Quebec, Nature-based solutions project developer, Carbon Terre a Terre (CTaT). With the ARBRE grouped project, CTaT is strategically positioning itself and its partners, at the dynamic intersection between climate change mitigation, climate change adaption and efforts to render industrial agriculture more regenerative in the Province of Quebec. The main ARBRE project activity is to convert nonproductive degraded non-forest old fields / abandoned former agricultural fields to sugar maple producing orchards in a shelterwood arrangement that will mimic natural succession ecological processes. Some low value productive agricultural land will be afforested  The baseline scenario is the old fields staying as degraded non forest and unproductive land, with a thick herbaceous layer and/or shrub mat impeding natural tree regeneration and/or continued agricultural production of low value agricultural land.  CTaT has selected old-fields sites where the above mentioned pre-existing conditions will cause a long regeneration delay, with only marginal shrub and/or tree ingress over the crediting period.   CTaT is planning a first annual instance/pilot project of 125 hectares to be established in 2024 as part of an overall buildout of 1000 hectares from 2024 to 2029.  Total net project minus baseline sequestration over for all 5 annual instances is estimated to be approximately 500,000 tCO2e.  The ARBRE project offers multiple non carbon benefits such as enhanced wildlife corridor habitat and slope stability as well as diversified regenerative agriculture values to farmers.  The project will help to rejuvenate and augment sugar maple production in Quebec.  It offers a high level of additionality for its atmospheric decarbonation benefits without any significant risk to food security.
vcs-4913:
The entire project lies within the geographical boundaries of Northern Cameroon that covers three regions i.e. the Adamawa, the North and Far North regions. In the first instance, the project activity is limited to the Adamawa region. Being a grouped project, the sites of the other two regions will be added as ‘future project instances.
The project activity involves planting dozens of indigenous fruit trees in the area. In the first project instance, fruit and forest trees will be planted during a period of ten years on 25,000 hectares of the Nyambaka council forest. The Nyambaka council forest is a mosaic of forest and savannah registered as part of the Country’s permanent forest estate and thus managed by the Council of Nyambaka. All project instances within this grouped project activity will consist of afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR)
The grouped project activities have as objective to contribute to sustainable environmental management, community development and poverty reduction. These activities will significantly improve the livelihoods of communities through job creation. The establishment of such plantations will increase carbon sinks, thus, contributing directly to climate change mitigation and adaptation. The communities will be organized into cooperatives to develop and exploit the value chains of non-timber forest products (cashew, Arabic gum, Shea butter, mango, etc.).
vcs-4914:
Rocio Bioenergy Plant for Manure Management – AMBICOOP is a centralized biogas plant that will be implemented in Toledo, Paraná, Brazil, to treat swine manure and gainfully use it for renewable energy. The project will collect waste from livestock farming activities from cooperative members and, in a smaller proportion, other organic waste types, in the Rocio community of Toledo. Therefore, the project will contribute to climate impact primarily by capturing and destroying methane emissions from livestock manure. It is estimated that the project will reduce 51,062 tCO2e annually and 357,573 tCO2e during the first crediting period.  

The Project Proponents are AMBICCOP, responsible for project implementation, monitoring and operation, and ecosecurities, responsible for carbon project development and management, reporting and quality check. 

Currently, confined animal waste is managed in dedicated pits or lagoons designed to store and stabilize manure commonly referred to as esterqueiras (“manure holders”). The volume of manure combined with this handling method produces several negative impacts on the environment and on human well-being, including limitation to livestock production, emission of greenhouse gases, spread of undesirable odours; potential dissemination of pathogens and potential contamination of soil and water systems. 

The project contributes to the sustainable development of the region by providing an environmentally-sound solution to the destination of animal waste and simultaneously promote access to a clean and renewable energy source. It specifically creates impact relating to the following SDGs (apart from Climate Action): SDG7, by supplying clean and renewable energy to the national grid; SDG8, by creating new permanent employment opportunities; SDG11, by providing adequate destination to livestock waste; and SDG12, by recycling livestock waste into fertilizer, promoting sustainable agricultural production systems.
vcs-4915:
The Mafisa Livestock Grazing Carbon Project (MLGCP) is proposed by ZayoHub, a Zambian non-profit. The project aims to generate carbon credits through enhanced grazing and fire management, utilizing VM0032 methodology, (Adoption of Sustainable Grasslands through Adjustment of Fire & Grazing). It will monitor activities and impacts through on-the-ground livestock tracking by grazing coordinators and via remote impact assessment via satellite imagery. 

The initiative focuses on empowering impoverished local communities residing in mopane and miombo woodlands in southwestern Zambia. In this region, soils are poor; farming is largely subsistence-based and highly marginal, and cattle rearing is the dominant historical land use. Key aspects of long-standing traditional farming practices reflect the principles of rotational grazing and good fire management, but their use has lapsed in recent decades. 

Improving animal husbandry on sustainably managed rangelands is a significant opportunity for sustainable livelihoods in the project area. However, at present animals are usually not herded, contributing to degradation of grassland degradation. High tick-borne disease prevalence and other parasites greatly impede productivity. 

MLGCP promotes cattle grazing rotations to restore traditional grazing practices, simulate wild herbivores' migratory patterns, and foster grassland regeneration. Additionally, it targets the reduction of burning frequency, enhancing carbon storage. MLGCP will provide animal health services for farmers participating in collective planned grazing. 

Anticipating annual net removals of 1 ton of CO2e/ha, the project plans to expand from 220,000 ha initially to 1.26 million ha by 2030. Projected annual carbon credit yields are set to rise from 220,000 tons CO2e in 2024 to around 1.26 million tons CO2e by 2029, sustaining until 2063. Overall, MLGCP aims to remove over 47 million tons CO2e, contributing to long-term atmospheric carbon reduction.
vcs-4916:
Guangxi Laibin Organic Wastewater Biogas Power Generation Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located on the east side of the paper mill area of Guangxi Xinggui Paper Industry Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as Xinggui paper mill), Honghe Farm, Mengcun Town, Xingbin District, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, P. R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Guangxi Gangya Shengda New Energy Co., Ltd. 
The project started to construct on 05/03/2023 and started operation on 29/06/2023.The project has a total designed capacity 2MW (3*1MW, one is for back-up use) and combusts the organic wastewater biogas, which contains nearly 74.93% of methane, to generate electricity for Xinggui paper mill to consume. The project collects and utilizes the biogas generated by the anaerobic treatment section of organic wastewater to generate electricity, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the organic wastewater biogas has been emitted to the atmosphere since the sewage treatment station started operation. Therefore, the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. The project activity is expected to displace 14,400 MWh of electricity per year by reducing the import from the grid to the plant. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reduction of the project is 62,771 tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 627,710 tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.
vcs-4917: The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on ground mounted in the state of Assam, India. The sole purpose of project activity is to install solar power plant for captive purpose and surplus generated electricity can be supplied to grid. M/s. Dalmia Cement Bharat Ltd (to be referred as DCBL from here on) is installed & develop a DC capacity of 20 MW (AC capacity- 16.64 MW) ground mounted on site Solar Photovoltaic Power Project (Project) for Captive Power Consumption at Lanka- Mosoka Rd, Pipal Pukhuri No.2 village, Hojai District in the State of Assam.
vcs-4918:
The Carbon Smart Cropping and Pasture Systems Australia project is a grouped VCS AFOLU project open to regenerative row crop farmers and graziers within Australia. The farms that will enroll in this project are growers and graziers that have mostly been following traditional farming methods such as tilling, removal of crop residue, no or minimal cover crops and with a strong reliance on chemical inputs, but who are now motivated to reduce their impact on the environment. 
For this grouped project, greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions and removals will be achieved by the implementation of a combination of practice changes, including the application of organic amendments and supplements, such as mulch and compost to reduce the reliance on synthetic fertilizers and to improve soil health, cover cropping, pasture improvement, improvement of herd management and grazing practices, improved water use efficiency and others.  
The undertaking of this project will support a number of United Nations Sustainable Development Goals in the project area, local communities, surrounding environments, and in the supply chain. The project will contribute towards SDG 2: Zero Hunger, SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, and SDG 13: Climate Action.
vcs-4919: The Peruvian Amazon Conservation Project is an Improved Forest Management Project (IFM) that will reduce greenhouse gases (GHG) by preventing commercial logging (logged to protected forest - LtPF) in 291,590 hectares of tropical rainforest. The project is implemented by 21 tribal communities in partnership with the Amazon Conservation Group (ACG) and Desarrollo Ambiental y Social Peru (DAS).  The project is located in the Purús Province in the Ucayali Region in the central Amazon rainforest of Peru. The project area is made up of several indigenous territories and represents ancient ecosystems. These ecosystems provide critical habitat to threatened fauna and flora as well as provide ecosystem services for the local communities that have lived there for millennia.
vcs-492: The project activity is a bundled wind power project activity consisting of 3 numbers of WTG of M/s Muthoot Finance Ltd (MFL) .  M/s Muthoot Finance Ltd has installed 3 number of 1250 kW Suzlon make Wind Turbine Generator in the state of Tamil Nadu. The total installed capacity of the project activity is 3.75 MW and it is expected to generate 10200 MWh per annum.  The objective of the wind power project activity is to generate renewable electricity using wind power resources and to sell the generated electricity to the Tamil Nadu State Electricity Board.  In the absence of the project activity equivalent amount of electricity would have been generated by the grid mix. The Project activity will thus reduce the anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in to the atmosphere associated with the equivalent amount of electricity generation from the grid mix.
vcs-4920:
Shanxi Xiadian CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Xiadian coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mine where the project is located. The project is located in the wind shaft yard of Xiadian Coal Mine on the north side of HouWangjiagou Village, Xiadian Town, Xiangyuan County, Changzhi City, Shanxi  Province, China. The central geographical coordinates are east longitude 112.911585° and north latitude 36.530075°. The Project Owner is Xiangyuan Luxin Coal Mine Methane Power Generation Co., Ltd. 
Prior to the implementation of the project, xiadian coal mine was equipped with CMM extraction facilities and all extracted CMM was vented into the atmosphere directly; the electricity consumed at coal mines was imported from NCPG; the heat was provided by waste coal boilers. For CMM treatment and heat supply, baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. For electricity supply, the NCPG provides the equivalent amount of electricity produced by the Project in the baseline. 
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. Fifteen sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 7.5MW (8*0.5 MW+7*0.5 MW), destroying 16.25 million m3 of methane annually. After the full operation of the Project, the expected annual exported electricity will be 31850 MWh, which will be supplied to the coal mine first through the electricity distribution network in Xiadian coal mine area, and then to NCPG if there is any electricity surplus, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the NCPG and displace part of the electricity generated by NCPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
vcs-4921:
Gaotang Municipal Solid Waste Incineration for Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located at Gaotang County, Liaocheng City, Shandong Province, P.R China. The Project is owned and implemented by Gaotang Guohuan Renewable Resources Co., Ltd.
The project is established for the purpose of treatment of municipal solid waste (“MSW”) with energy recovery and electricity generation and no heat recovered for thermal generation is involved. The project is designed to dispose of a daily average 600 tons of MSW through one incineration systems with the treatment capacity of 600 tons/d of MSW, matched with one set of 12 MW condensing turbine and one set of 12 MW turbo generators. The project will dispose of 219,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 108 tons of light diesel as auxiliary fuel every year. The expected average electricity generation will be 73,510 MWh per year, of which 63,220 MWh will be delivered to the North China Grid Company Limited(NCGC).
The project will dispose of the MSW by incineration technology to avoid CH4 emissions from the disposal of the waste at Gaotang municipal landfill site. Furthermore, the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions can also be achieved by the displacement of the electricity from fossil fuel-fired plants connected to the NCGC, by electricity generated from recovered MSW combustion heat.
vcs-4924: This project features implementation of rapid rotational grazing practices by dense aggregations of livestock to restore perennial grasses on degraded rangelands across 970,685 hectares in northern Tanzania. These new grazing practices are additional because they differ from the currently practiced seasonal shifts in grazing activity from wet to dry season ranges, and the new practices would not be possible without carbon revenues to support governance and monitoring of grazing activities. Rapid rotational grazing will enhance adaptation to climate change by improving soil water holding capacity, increasing surface water availability and providing grass banks as a hedge against drought. Habitat improvement from new grazing practices will result in biodiversity benefits in the form of improved habitat inside wildlife corridors between iconic High Conservation Areas such as Serengeti, Kilimanjaro, Nairobi, and Tsavo National Parks and their associated ecosystems and enhance diversity of endemic taxa of plants, birds and insects. Finally, the project will provide direct benefits to dozens of pastoralist communities in form of funds for bursaries to support women and the poorest community members as well as to construct water capture structures and infrastructure for delivering livestock to market. The project is expected to remove more than 62 million tons CO2e over the project lifetime of 40 years, or more than 1.5 million tons CO2e a year on average.
vcs-4925:
The Credit Union, Savings and Investment Cooperative of the States of Paraná, São Paulo and, Rio de Janeiro – Central Sicredi PR/SP/RJ is a cooperative system that gather together 31 credit unions in the State of Paraná, São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. Its 31 credit unions with independent governance. The Board of presidents and directors of Central Sicredi and its 31 Credit Unions decided to implement the Sicredi Methane Avoidance in Animal Effluents Umbrella Program (SMAAEUP). 
The SMAAEUP is a pilot program, involving six credit unions, eight financial centers and nine Sicredi Associated pig and dairy farmers, from Central Sicredi PR/SP/RJ. The Credit Unions “Vanguarda, Vale do Piquiri, Nossa Terra, Norte Sul, Paranapanema, and Integração” are all based in the State of Paraná and accepted the challenge of being part of this pilot program. Each credit union indicated Sicredi associate pig and dairy farmers who had anaerobic lagoon (effluent pond) for the treatment of animal wastewater. 
	Based on the methodologies AMS-III-Y  Small-scale methodology - Methane avoidance through separation of solids from wastewater or manure treatment systems (version 04.0), sectoral scope: 13. and, AMS-III.I - Avoidance of methane production in wastewater treatment through replacement of anaerobic lagoons by aerobic systems (Version 8), and in the due diligence assessment and local socio-environmental diagnosis of each rural property, the program activities began. 
The SMAAEUP Program is designed to assist in managerial and operational efficiency and better socio-environmental running of small farms located in the states of PR and SC. These small-scale pig and dairy farming producers are members and associated with Sicredi and operate in several areas of family farming
It consists in the use of technology to avoid generating methane gas from pigsties organic wastewater and anaerobic lagoons used in pig and dairy farming.
vcs-4928: Shunping MSW Incineration and Power Generation PPP Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located at the west side of Muze copper material factory in Shunping County and the north side of Baofu Expressway, Baoding City, Hebei Province, P.R.China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Shunping County SUS Renewable Energy Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “the project owner”).This project is the first ultra-low emission domestic waste power plant in Hebei Province.   The purpose of the project is to treat fresh MSW with two 500t/d MSW combustion lines and utilize recovered waste heat for electricity generation. The MSW treatment system is composed of two 500t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with two sets of 12MW steam turbine and two sets of 12MW generator. The project will process 365,000 tons [ 365000t/d is the design value of the daily MSW intake in FSR. ] of MSW every year, and consume 500 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion lines will generate 135,700 MWh electricity every year, of which 108,600 MWh will be exported to the North China Power Grid (NCPG). The implementation of the project will meet the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also, the project fits the priority development sector of integrated utilization of resource and energy saving of China, and helps reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil-fuel fired plants and MSW treatment at landfill.    The project started construction on 31 December 2020 and put into trial operation on 13 May 2022. It is estimated that during the 10-year fixed crediting period of the project (from 13 May 2022 to 12 May 2032), the average annual GHG emission reductions will be 59,854 tCO2e. The total amount of emission reductions is expected to be 598,549 tCO2e during the 10-year fixed crediting period.
vcs-4929:
Sorting and Recycling Company for Environmental Services (EADA) (hereinafter called “the Project”) aims at collecting the end-of-life solid waste and all types of electronic waste (including e-waste like laptops, mobile phones, refrigerators, cables, television sets, CPUs, etc.) from industries and recovering recyclable materials (such as metals and plastics) which can be further sold to the customers. This not only reduces the total amount of the solid waste and e-waste sent to landfills, but also reduces the emissions by replacing the need for production of metals and non-metals recovered, recycled, and reused. Before the implementation of the project, all the waste would be dumped in the landfill or incinerated with no recovery of any recyclable components.

The solid and e-waste post manual sorting and segregating, is sent for dismantling, or refurbishment using a WEEE line or the Cable line depending upon the type of waste and the analysis is conducted. The project facility has recovered more than 43,000 tons of metals and non-metals from the waste received in FY 2022. 

With primary operations in Al Jubail, Eastern Province, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), the project is developed and operated by the Sorting and Recycling Company for Environmental Services (EADA) (hereinafter called “the Project Owner”), a subsidiary of Saudi Investment Recycling Company (SIRC). The construction was started in 12-March-2016 and the project was commissioned on 23-March-2021. 

The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions are 60,000 tCO2e and the estimated GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period are 60,000 tCO2e.
vcs-493: The project activity involves implementation and operation of a 5 MW (2 × 2.5 MW) small scale, grid connected, run-of-the-river Hydroelectric project (HEP), located on the Brahm Ganga Nallah (Tributary of River Parbati) in Kullu District of Himachal Pradesh, India. The purpose of the project is to generate clean energy in a sustainable manner, utilizing hydrological resource of the Nallah. The project consists of two 2.5 MW Horizontal axis Francis turbines. The project activity supplies electricity to the respective State Grid of India, which is highly dominated by thermal based power generating units.
vcs-4932:
In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, Dicle Diyarbakır Landfill Project is being implemented by Dicle Yenilenebilir Enerji A.Ş
The project activity is a Methane Gas Power Generating Plant with an installed capacity  of 6.004 MWe. The first commissioning  was carried out on 11/06/2021 with a 2 * (1.501 MWe / 1,544 MWm)  engines. Then on 03/09/2021, 2 more engines with 1.501 MWe were commissioned. Thus in 2022 the project installed power is 6.004 MWe. The project is built within the premises of Diyarbakır Solid Waste Disposal Site in Diyarbakır province. The projects official license power capacity is 14.509 MWe, according to the contracts with the EMRA Generation License. The project has an area of 400,864 square meters. The project is located in Yukarıakdibek, Baglar district city of Diyarbakir, in Turkey
vcs-4934: The proposed project activity is installation of 10.50 MW hydro project in Sanluang Town, Khoun District, Xieng Khouang Province, Lao PDR. The project is developed by Nonghai Group Sole Company Limited. The electricity generated from this project is supplied to Laon National Grid. The baseline scenario of the project is continuation of the present situation, i.e., electricity supplied from the power grid. By displacing part of the power generated by thermal power plants, the project is therefore reduces associated CO2 emission.
vcs-4935:
Located in the province of Figuig, Northeast Morocco, the Desert Timber Africa (DTA) and Desert Timber Tafilalet (DTT) farms span 600 hectares each, forming a contiguous expanse of approximately 1,200 hectares. These farms are leased to Desert Timber Tafilalet and Desert Timber Africa through separate agreements with the Moroccan government, overseen by the Interior Minister. The lease terms extend to 3-year periods with the possibility of renewal for up to 39 years.

The primary objective of the Project is to establish a framework for accurately, transparently, and consistently accounting for greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction achieved through smallARR activities in urban environments, and adapted to the unique circumstances of urban forestry, whilst aligning with the principles and policies set forth in the VM0047 Methodology (Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation, v 1.0). 
Throughout the 20th century, the UK  has consistently lost woodland cover, and with only 10% today, is now among the developed countries with least tree coverage (with an average of 38% for European countries, and 46% for the rest of the world).  
According to the Climate Change Committee (CCC), which advises the UK and devolved governments on meeting their greenhouse gas emissions reductions targets, a significant increase in tree-planting is needed to manage the climate emergency and achieve the government’s net zero target . 
The UK Government has therefore committed to increasing tree planting rates across the UK to 30,000 hectares per year by 2024. As of 2022-2023, the actual planting achieved was around 13k hectares, less than half of the target.  In fact, 30k hectares annually has only been achieved once over the past 50 years. 
Given the small scale of the country, and its level of density among the highest in Europe , the project aims to leverage carbon crediting mechanisms as a way to unlock a potential source of funding for small scale planting projects and make use of any available “white space”, particularly in urban environments. 
Alongside its role in sequestering carbon, urban nature provides valuable ecosystem benefits that are needed to help mitigate the long-term effects of climate change in urban environments , including reductions in stormwater runoff and flood risk alleviation, energy savings through cooling and heating effects, improvements in air quality, and biodiversity restoration.

The Taiping Township waste resource utilization project (hereafter referred to as the proposed project) is located in Zhaodong City, Suihua City, Heilongjiang Province, China (125°58′7.24″, 45°56′4.03″), which is operated by Zhaodong Boan Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd., which is an affiliated company under Heilongjiang Boneng Green Energy Technology Co., Ltd. 
The proposed project is a new plant which designed to treat organic wastes through anaerobic digestion and composting to produce the natural gas and organic fertilizers. The natural gas produced will be used for distributing in a natural gas distribution grid, and organic fertilizers will be transported to the local planting market. The proposed project uses organic wastes such as straw and livestock manure as raw materials. It is expected to treat 34,500 tons of straw and 69,000 tons of livestock manure annually, producing 3,777,800 Nm3 of the natural gas and 15,769.95 tons of solid bio-organic fertilizers.
The project activities include waste pretreatment unit, anaerobic digesters unit, biogas purification unit, and organic fertilizer production workshop etc. Raw materials such as crushed straw and livestock manure are preprocessed and mixed before being sent to an anaerobic fermentation unit, where organic matter is degraded by microorganisms under anaerobic conditions. After anaerobic digestion, methane and digestate are generated. Methane will be processed through dehydration, desulfurization, decarbonization, and other processes to obtain biogas, the digestate after thorough digestion is sent to the solid-liquid separation system. The separated biogas residue is processed into solid organic fertilizer and returned to the field after being added with straw. The biogas slurry is discharged into the biogas slurry temporary storage tank for subsequent production.

The DIT AgTech grouped project for ‘the reduction of enteric methane emissions from livestock production systems via the uDOSE water medication technology’, will supply a methane reducing feed ingredient (ie Agolin Ruminant L®) through the drinking water of ruminant livestock production systems. This will be achieved by using the uDOSE/uHUB technology already developed by DIT AgTech for the feeding of methane reducing feed additives and the subsequent monitoring, recording and accounting for resultant reduction of GHG emissions.

The uDOSE technology system is designed to accurately and automatically administer a predetermined dosage of supplement into the drinking water of livestock. This ensures that each animal receives a targeted dose proportionate to its body weight. Unlike the consumption of dry feed, where herd-level behavioral competition can lead to inconsistent intake of feed additives and waste due to exposure to environmental conditions, every animal drinks water in proportion to its body weight daily. The uDOSE is connected via satellite enabling bidirectional communication with the uHUB system that constantly monitors, records and controls the dosing activities in real time.

Backed up by the research from CQUniversity (Batley, R. (2023)), the uDOSE system has been proven to be an effective way to mitigate methane production in a livestock production system and therefore proposes a variation to the VM0041 methodology which currently only describes the feeding of methane reducing feed additives to livestock through dry feed.

The Tapera Amazonas REDD+ Project in Urucará and Nhamundá, Amazonas, Brazil, combats severe deforestation. Amazonas experienced considerable forest loss, with 4,913 km² deforested in 2021 and 2,741 km² in 2022, leading to high CO2 emissions. Main causes include illegal logging, cattle ranching, and agriculture expansion. Urucará and Nhamundá, however, maintain high forest coverage, emphasizing their ecological importance. The project focuses on conservation, biodiversity protection, and sustainable practices.

Deforestation drivers in these areas are illegal logging and agricultural expansion, with Urucará particularly affected due to timber industries in nearby São Sebastião. The project, under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) for Forestry, aims to reduce emissions from deforestation and degradation. It plans to improve monitoring, employ new staff for farm management, and use carbon credits for environmental and social enhancements.

In line with Brazil's Forest Code, the project supports maintaining 80% of forest cover in the Legal Amazon. Community benefits include water systems, solar panels, satellite internet, and training for sustainable forest product processing. A processing factory in Urucará will offer alternative income sources. Operations are expected to start in January 2025. The project is significant for biodiversity, located within a Key Biodiversity Area, home to unique and endangered species. It prioritizes ecosystem functions like nutrient cycling and carbon sequestration. Monitoring will involve satellite imagery, drone-based techniques, and fire prevention strategies, focusing on conserving forest areas against legal deforestation pressures.

vcs-4967: The PLUM Peat and Mangrove Conservation and Restoration Project (PLUM Project) is a conservation and restoration project of peat and mangrove forests located in Central Kalimantan Province, Indonesia. The project is implemented on a 23,665-hectare forest concession with Forest Utilization Business License (PBPH). Peat ecosystems will be restored by blocking canals to rewet the area and avoid further peat drainage. The project will provide tangible benefits to local communities living in the surrounding area by working to improve local livelihoods, health, education, and well-being. The project area is home to 31 globally threatened species, including the Bornean orangutan, Proboscis monkey, and the Bornean white-bearded gibbon. vcs-4968: The Nkuba REDD+ Project (NRP) is designed to promote climate change mitigation, preserve biodiversity, and establish alternative livelihoods for communities through the UN-REDD+ framework. The NRP consists mainly of primary rainforest including numerous unique species. The NCA landscape is dominated by plains, plateaus, and low mountains above small marshy valleys. It has numerous rivers and tributaries with conditions for a thriving tropical ecosystem.  The NRP consists of three forest blocks that are recognised by the Congolese authorities as community forest conservation concessions (CFCLs). The CFCLs involved in the NRP are Mbungu, Nsuhu, and Seko, with a total of six clans making up the project communities. The benefits of the NRP forest are significant, but the region continues to experience threats due to deforestation, uncontrolled hunting, artisanal mining, and nomadic activities. The lack of employment, business opportunities, limited access to infrastructure and basic services contribute to local populations exploiting the forest for income generation. In response to these threats to the NCA, the 6 clans in partnership with Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund created NRP with the following objectives: 1) Mitigate climate change caused by deforestation and degradation and develop adaptation strategies for climate variability, 2) Improve the quality of life for local communities by introducing sustainable alternatives to forest exploitation, income-generating activities, and initiatives designed to address community needs, such as health, education, and safety, 3) Contribute to preserving biodiversity through community-led forest management, better land strategies, and forest monitoring, regulation, and surveillance.

The purpose of BRASCARBON Methane Recovery Project BCA-BRA-20 project is to utilize the effluent produced on a total of 10 pig farms in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, in Brazil, to capture methane and generate biogas. The projects have the potential to generate energy from waste using the biogas produced and captured. Regardless this potential, energy will not be a part of this project activity.
Before the project activity, local farmers considered waste as an externality in the pig production process. As such, minimal finance was allocated to this issue and wastewater was often treated in open water lagoons – frequently with profound environmental impacts. The projects demonstrate how the construction of a set of new, covered, in-ground anaerobic digesters can utilize the organic material from the animal operations to produce biogas and fertilizer, whilst reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The   basis   of   the   projects   is   the   anaerobic   digestion, whereby microorganisms break down biodegradable material in the absence of oxygen. As part of an integrated waste management system, anaerobic digestion reduces the emission of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and produces a rich biogas, suitable for energy production, which can be used to replace fossil fuels. The nutrient-rich solids left after digestion are used as fertilizer and the better wastewater management allows more water for irrigation.

Here, in the baseline scenario, the tea plucker communities residing in the tea estates are provided fuel wood, as per the company policy. The communities use these fuelwood in a three stone stove for their daily household needs. One of sustainable green initiative by APPL to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to safeguard the health of the communities, is the distribution of 20,000 Improved Cook-stoves (ICS) to different households to abate the fuelwood burning.  The Improved Cook-stove distributed under the project activity will fulfill their household needs more efficiently and will also have other benefits like reducing health risk and negative environment impacts. By using less fuel wood, global greenhouse gas emissions would be reduced. The average annual GHG emission reduction from the project is estimated to be 69,703 tCO2e and a total of 6,97,032 tCO2e over the crediting period of 10 years
vcs-4982:
This project is to be developed by Reliance BP Mobility Limited (RBML). Reliance Industries Limited and British Petroleum Plc. have partnered to form Reliance BP Mobility Limited to combine international expertise & local strengths to spearhead the future of mobility. Electric Mobility Business operates under the brand name Jio-bp Pulse.
This project includes the installation, operation, and maintenance of EV charging stations by RBML across India through strategic partnerships with public and private sector in order to scale the EV market in the country and also act as an enabler for the Government of India’s National Electric Mobility Plan. This is a grouped project and the new instances will be added as and when the EVCS get installed across India in the future.
The use of this charging infrastructure results in the avoidance of fossil fuel powered vehicle usage and therefore a reduction in the greenhouse gas emissions from the alternative energy supply. This project includes EVCS that are installed, operated, and maintained by RBML.
vcs-4983:
The proposed project activity involves the installation of rooftop and ground mounted solar panels for captive consumption. The surplus electricity if generated can be supplied to the grid and if there is deficit of energy, that can be consumed from grid through a net metering arrangement with the respective state electricity board.
The Net Metering concept states that the customers are to be charged only for the net power that they consume from the electricity service provider that has accumulated over a specific period. In other terms if the installed renewable energy produces more electricity than the consumed then the producer would be paid or credited for the excess amount of electricity generation to the grid over the same period. The Net Metering helps the grid to supply in the peak hours to keep up with increase demand in peak hours. It has been observed that in the actual scenario, no surplus power is exported to the grid as the internal demand of the premises is very high and the status quo is expected to be maintained throughout the operation of the projects. Hence, none of the instances export greater than 50% of generated electricity to the grid, so the project eligibility in the VCS program is justified. The geographical location of the project is entire India. 
The project activity will displace electricity from an electricity distribution system that is or would have been supplied by at least one fossil fuel fired generating unit i.e., in the absence of the project activity, the users would have been supplied electricity from one or more sources listed below:
(a) A national or a regional grid (grid hereafter);
(b) Fossil fuel fired captive power plant;
(c) A carbon intensive mini-grid
The baseline scenario would be either continued by use of fossil fuel dominated grid connected electricity generation or fossil fuel used in power plant or carbon intensive electricity.
vcs-4984:
The projects primary objective is to change the pre-project/baseline scenario of the household cooking practices by replacing inefficient wood-fired mud stoves and three- stone stove technologies with clean, sustainable, and efficient biogas digestion unit and stoves. Each beneficiary household actively participates by utilizing cattle dung as the primary feed for the digesters, strategically curbing greenhouse gas emissions. This approach not only displaces conventional non-renewable biomass, such as firewood, with renewable biogas but also averts emissions of Methane (CH4) and Nitrogen Oxide (NO2) associated with the anaerobic decay of animal manure. Beyond emissions reduction, the initiative plays a pivotal role in enhancing rural hygiene practices through the proper
disposal of animal waste. Furthermore, the residue derived from the bio-digesters is repurposed as organic fertilizer, contributing to sustainable land applications. By replacing non-renewable energy sources with biogas generated from the biodigesters, the project aligns with the broader goals of sustainable development outlined by the United Nations.
vcs-4985: OYU Green's Greening India Mission (GIM) is a multifaceted grouped project, targeting large-scale reforestation in 5,000 hectares of dormant lands in Assam, India. With farmers and landowners at the forefront, GIM focuses on long-term carbon dioxide removal by establishing plantation of locally preferred tree species, promotes sustainable land use, creates income and employment opportunities, enhances digital literacy, and strengthens community resilience to climate change. By restoring habitats and creating wildlife corridors, the project also safeguards local biodiversity in this globally recognized biodiversity hotspot.
vcs-4986: The project activity by Shree Cement Limited is the installation of a new captive solar PV power project with installed capacity of 13.4 MWAC at Beawar in Ajmer district in the northern Indian state of Rajasthan to supply electricity to the cement manufacturing facility, owned by Shree Cement Limited located in the vicinity of the site. The project activity was commissioned on 18-August-2022. The project activity solar PV power plant is expected to generate  25,536 MWh electricity annually and thus reducing GHG emissions of 24,705 tCO2 annually with GHG  emission reduction of 177,939 tCO2e during the entire first crediting period. During the current monitoring period of 18-August-2022 to 31-January-2024, this project activity has generated electricity of 30,497.5 MWh that led to achieved GHG emission reductions of 28,521 tCO2e.
vcs-4987:
This project description document covers COMACO operations in part of the Central province (Mumbwa and Shibuyunji districts) and part of Southern province (Itezhi-Tezhi district) of Zambia. The COMACO South Landscape Management Project (CLMP-South) promotes sustainable agriculture land management and improved forest management. The key objectives of the project are to improve agricultural soil management through climate smart agricultural practices and reduce uncontrolled forest loss and degradation through community base conservation and land use planning. Hence, the project comprises two components:
1. Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) component – which aims to promote widespread adoption of agricultural practices including conservation agriculture and agroforest that increases the food production per unit area. The project promotes the adoption by farmers of legume-based alley cropping, residues management (e.g. mulching; cessation of residue burning), use of organic fertilizers such as composite and animal manure, reduced tillage and the intercropping of Gliricidia Sepium as part of Agroforestry to restore soil quality and sequestrate carbon.
2. REDD+ (Avoided Unplanned Deforestation) component – which aims to reduce forest loss, protect and expand areas under natural forest, and conserve biodiversity. This is achieved primarily through land use planning and creation of Community Conservation Areas (CCAs) for protection of natural forest, coupled with sustainable non-extractive forest use, e.g. honey and mushrooms. The creation of CCAs and the enforcement of by-laws to protect them promotes the protection of ecosystems and biodiversity within and around the CCAs.
The annual average GHG emission reductions of the project are estimated at 224,504 tCO2-e, and total GHG emission reductions over 20 years are estimated at 4,490,084tCO2-e. This estimate considers only the first 10 years of GHG emission reductions for the REDD+ component.
vcs-4989: The current Afforestation Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) project aims to address global climate change through trees plantations in the project area. Planting trees and expanding forest cover significantly contributes to carbon sequestration. APPL’s Tree Plantation initiative in their tea estates located in Assam and West Bengal, is a crucial component of their commitment to sustainability and environmental conservation. With a strong focus on tea estates, this project aims to enhance the region's biodiversity and combat climate change while also increasing the area under ‘Tree Outside Forests’ (TOFs).The area under project boundary consists of altogether 6,62,534 trees in the project area since 2021 in a phased manner, including the shade trees for tea cultivation as per the guidelines of Tea Board. The project is located in the 25 tea estates owned by APPL encompassing the Indian states of Assam and West Bengal. In Assam, eight districts of Charaideo, Dibrugarh, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sonitpur, Tinsukia and Udalguri are covered, while for the state of West Bengal, the project location entails only the district of Jalpaiguri. The project plan is to generate carbon credits for voluntary market under the VCS standard. The project aims at sequestering 5,97,515 tCO2e over 20 years from 2021 to 2040, in line with the Indian government’s goal of increasing the forest and tree cover by 2030. The project will significantly improve local biodiversity, air quality, soil conservation, and erosion control, while also contributing to carbon sequestration and the company's carbon footprint reduction. This plantation project embodies APPL's unwavering commitment to environmental sustainability and a greener future for the region.
vcs-499: The project activity is a Wind energy based power generation project of capacity 4.67 MW consists of 7 Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) that includes 3.75 MW (1250 kW X 3 machines) and 0.92 MW (230 kW X 4 machines).
