vcs-4992:
Yangjiang MSW incineration and power generation project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in No.1 Shengangdong, Baisha Street, Jiangcheng District, Yangjiang City, Guangdong province, China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Yangjiang SUS Environmental Protection Co., Ltd.. (hereafter referred to as the project owner).With two 600t/d MSW combustion production lines, the project will treat 1,200 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of two 600t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 35MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 438,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 138.53 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work over 8,000 hours every year, generating 163,663.1 MWh electricity, of which 148,920 MWh will be exported to the China Southern Power Grid (hereinafter referred to as CSPG). The remaining electricity will be used by the project itself and there will be no purchased electricity. 
By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the proposed project activity avoids the emission of methane that would be generated under landfill condition. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can produce steam to generate power to replace the electricity that would otherwise be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants which are connected to the CSPG. The baseline scenario of this project is the same as the scenario prior to the implementation of the project, namely the landfill gas is vented directly and the equivalent power is supplied by the CSPG.
The project is expected to provide electricity of 148,920 MWh annually into CSPG. The total emission reduction is expected to be 1072817 tons of CO2 and the average annual 
emission reduction is 153260 tons of CO2 in a period of 7 years (from December 31, 2022 to December 31, 2029).
vcs-4993:
Águas da Mata Atlântica forest restoration project is revitalizing degraded land in the Atlantic Forest and aiming to create ecological corridors by restoring native forests to connect two of the largest intact forest blocks in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Through forest restoration, the project expects to generate 2,129,589 tCO2e in net carbon removals over 40 years while improving water infiltration and quality within the Guandu River hydrographic region, a basin that generates water and electricity for approximately 9 million citizens in Rio de Janeiro and surrounding municipalities. Together, Pachama and Instituto Terra de Preservação Ambiental (ITPA) plan to work with multiple landowners in the region to establish approximately 8 million trees—representing more than 30 different species—to restore 5,000 ha of native forest.  

The project started in October of 2023 by planting 80 ha in Paty dos Alferes in the Serra do Mar region.  Another 400 ha is scheduled for planting in 2024.  The project will use the dynamic performance benchmark approach under VM0047 to ensure additionality over time and will employ satellite-based project success monitoring to continually assess forest cover change, as well as natural and anthropogenic risks that might threaten the project area.
vcs-4994:
Climate Investment Partners LLC, in partnership with Entooma Sidai Limited, aims to restore over 650,000 hectares of degraded grasslands in Narok County, Kenya via the Entooma Sidai: A Maasai Mara Rangeland Restoration and Conservation Project. The Project is estimated to generate approximately 689,731 net Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) annually over a 40-year project period for a total of over 27 million VCUs. The Project is being developed using the Verified Carbon Standard’s (VCS) VM0032 Methodology for the Adoption of Sustainable Grasslands through Adjustment of Fire and Grazing, v1.0.

Continued overgrazing in the project area has degraded grasslands and rangelands, reduced grass biodiversity, inhibited grassland regeneration, reduced grass seed banks, increased the spread of invasive species, and decreased the availability of viable forage for both livestock and wildlife. The promotion of planned rotational grazing of livestock will restore degraded grasslands and increase grassland carbon stocks by allowing grasses and plants to recover and regenerate between grazes, which in turn will aid with increasing soil carbon through increasing plant productivity and limiting soil organic matter losses. Overall, the expected impacts of widespread implementation of sustainable grazing management practices are: climate change mitigation, adaptation and increased resiliency; reduced soil erosion and run-off; reduced loss of livestock; improved water infiltration and soil health; increased household income and food security; and the expansion of wildlife habitats and increased biodiversity.
vcs-4996: The current project activity is implemented by Amalgamated Plantations Private limited (APPL) in its 25 tea estates, located in the diverse agro-ecological regions of two different states, Assam and West Bengal. Common practices in the project area are tea cultivation which include conventional methods such as synthetic fertilizer application, tillage, insecticide application, pesticide application and high-irrigation water consumption. These conventional practices contribute to soil depletion and accelerate GHG emissions. To address these challenges, the project proponent, APPL has ventured into sustainable green initiatives by the production of vermicompost. The construction of vermicompost units and subsequent generation of vermicompost, avoids the production of methane from the agricultural residues and cow dung manure; which would otherwise have been left to decay anaerobically within the project site, and cow dung pits/anaerobic lagoons. The vermicompost produced is then applied to the tea bushes to improve the soil structure and nutrient pool. This is further reflected by quantifying the reduction in emission of greenhouse gases through the project activity, i.e., the production of vermicompost from the wastes. In addition, the vermicompost generated is a powerful soil property enhancer as it is able to transform decomposable material into nutrient-rich organic manure. Hence the project will provide replicable model for environment friendly and economically viable for vermicompost production. During the 10-year crediting period, it is estimated that there will be an average annual reduction and removal of 2,51,964 tCO2e from 2,49,854.39 Metric Tonnes of waste
vcs-4997: The primary goal of the project activity is to replace inefficient baseline cookstoves with improved cookstoves (project devices), aiming to improve livelihoods of the rural communities in Uganda. This community engagement initiative intends to introduce clean cooking practices, mitigate indoor air pollution (IAP), and consequently decrease health risks associated with in efficient cooking practices in households.

vcs-5001:
Butuo County Grassland Sustainable Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Butuo County,Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture,Sichuan Province,China. The project’s aim is to restore 48,963.17ha of degraded grassland in Butuo County by adopting a variety of measures including grass seeding and reseeding, rotational grazing, rest grazing and grazing prohibition. The project will increase carbon sequestration, reverse grassland degradation, contribute to local development and preserve cultural traditions. The project proponent is Liangshan Modern Agricultural Silicon Valley Investment and Development Group Co.
The project focuses on 48,963.17ha of moderately or severely degraded grasslands and adopts a combination of the following measures:Grass seeding and reseeding、Rotational grazing and rest grazing、Grazing prohibition.
The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 57,030,382 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 1,425,760 tCO2e.
vcs-5003: The Growing Forest Carbon Project operates in the three Maritime Provinces of Canada. The proponent purchases private forests that are at-risk of being over-harvested and manages them to a high ecological standard that stores additional carbon.
vcs-5004: This Taurus energy efficiency (EE) grouped project “Taurus Energy Efficiency Consortium” focuses upon its portfolio of deep energy retrofits for residential multi-family dwellings, beginning with its development in Orlando, Florida, the Canopy Apartment Villas (Canopy).  The principle EE technologies involved in the Canopy retrofit include: on site solar, weatherization, insulation, duct sealing (HVAC), new heat pumps and new heat pump water heaters, LED lights and water saving fixtures.  Applying the VM0008 (with its minor revision, currently pending), this project validation will focus on the following Canopy technologies: heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, solar installations.  Prior to the retrofit, heating services and water heaters will have been provided by the retrofit baseline technologies which VM0008 assumes as valid for its baselining purposes. For Canopy specifically, these services were provided by AC with electric resistance heating systems and standard electric resistance water heaters, all drawing upon local grid electricity.  Other Taurus retrofit sites will bring in their specific existing retrofit technologies, some of which will include gas and other energy inputs.  The project’s GHG reductions arise as a result of the far more efficient provision of heating/water services due to the heat pump technologies and the delivery of zero carbon renewables electricity from the on-site solar systems, relative to the older technologies’ retrofit baseline GHG emissions.
vcs-5005: The purpose of the NGON Texas Beneficial Use of Waste Flare Gas Grouped Project is to beneficially use otherwise flared natural gas for off-grid electricity generation and consumption. The project activity leads to upstream carbon emissions reduction since the beneficial use of the waste flare gas will avoid the use of electricity generated by the fossil fuel dominated United States (U.S.) electricity grid.
vcs-5006: The project aims to restore degraded agricultural and pasture areas in the Amazon and Atlantic Forest biomes, employing agroforestry systems. Initially covering 2,133 hectares, with the potential to expand to 6954 hectares by 2025, it seeks to promote regenerative agriculture, reducing carbon emissions and environmental pressures. It prioritizes sustainable practices, social inclusion, and the generation of economic opportunities, while adopting policies for biodiversity preservation and prohibiting hunting in intervention areas. Located in states such as Pará, Rondônia, Mato Grosso, and Bahia, selected due to the high levels of degradation observed, the project uses strategies that include the cultivation of cocoa interspersed with native and exotic forest species, as well as short-cycle crops such as banana and cassava. This agroforestry approach not only promotes economic benefits, such as generating jobs for the local community, but also contributes to the preservation and increase of biodiversity in the region. Over 25 years, it is estimated that the project will be able to remove approximately 1,409,852 tons of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e), contributing significantly to climate change mitigation efforts. Furthermore, it will benefit around 300 families locally, providing socioeconomic and environmental improvements in their communities.
vcs-501: The project activity involved development and operation of grid connected wind energy based electricity generation facilities. In this bundled project, the aggregate installed capacity of 8.70 MW is contributed by 8 Wind Electricity Generators (WEGs), including 7.5 MW (1250 kW X 6 machines) and 1.2 MW (600 kW X 2 machine). The WEGs are part of Suzlon wind farms in Sangli and Nandurbar districts of Maharashtra. The electricity generated is fed to the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) grid.  The project is promoted by M/s Savita oil Technologies Ltd., M/s Rajesh Construction Company Limited, M/s Winro Commercial (India) Ltd., M/s Indian Products Trading Co. Pvt. Ltd., M/s Quantum Equipment Co. Ltd. & M/s KN Resources Pvt. Ltd.  In the absence of the project activity, equivalent amount of electricity would have been produced by conventional fossil fuels dominated power plants, which would lead to emissions of GHGs into the atmosphere.
vcs-5010:
Tata Coffee Limited's 25 estates in the Western Ghats are strategically situated across the Kodagu, Hassan, Chikamangalore and Coimbatore in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, India. Kodagu, also known as Coorg, serves as the primary location for these estates due to its favorable climate and suitable terrain for coffee cultivation. The 25 estates are organized into four divisions, each managed efficiently to ensure sustainable and responsible coffee production. The vast combined land area of these estates spans approximately 12,000 hectares, reflecting Tata Coffee Limited's significant presence and commitment to the coffee industry in the Western Ghats region.
The area under the project boundary consists of 14,84,523 old plants which are considered under baseline calculation and 13,02,346  new plants have been planted after 2021 to 2025 in a phased manner in addition to the shade tree number required for coffee cultivation as per the guidelines of coffee board to reestablish the biodiversity of the flora and fauna in the area and to fight with climate change.
The project quantifies the GHG removals occurring from agroforestry plantations using VM0047 “Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation” Version 1.0. The project plans to generate carbon credits for the voluntary carbon market under the VCS standard. The project estimates the total emission reduction for the crediting period of 32 years i.e. from 2021-2052 to be 16,78,836 tCO2e. The length of the project was developed as per the VCS Standard-v4.5 guidelines.
vcs-5011: The purpose of the project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. Eleven sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 24MW (12*2MW), destroying 42.14 million m3 of methane annually. The expected annual exported electricity will be 163,987 MWh, which will be supplied to the coal mine first through the electricity distribution network in Fenghui coal mine area, and then to North China Power Grid(NCPG) if there is any electricity surplus, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the NCPG and displace part of the electricity generated by NCPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. The waste heat from the generators will be recovered by waste heat boilers to provide free hot water to the coal mines, which was provided by waste coal fired boilers before the implementation of the Project.
vcs-5012:
Heilongjiang Datong Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Datong District, Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province, China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land.
The project plans to implement improved agricultural land management practices in 81,984 ha corn field in the first crediting period to increase soil organic carbon (SOC).The improved agricultural land management practices of the project focus on no-tillage on fields evenly mulched with crushed straw for two or three years, followed by plowing or subsoiling once and continued no-tillage for another two or three years. No-tillage can effectively reduce the loosening of the surface soil layer and soil disturbance, reduce the loss of water and nutrients in the soil, ensure the retention of organic matter in the soil, reduce the degree of compaction of the tillage equipment on the tillage soil layer, and preserve appropriate space for the growth of crops, which is convenient for ventilation and keeps the soil with good water storage capacity. The application of no-tillage sowing has solved the problem of sand blowing in bare farmland to a certain extent and played a role in windbreak and sand fixation. No-tillage can maximize the protective effect of straw mulching on soil.
vcs-5014: The Methane Recovery Project in Finca Yalcobé (referred to as “The Project”) is the implementation an anaerobic wastewater treatment facility at Finca Yalcobe palm oil factory in Alta Verapaz, Guatemala and would be a non-grouped project.
vcs-5015: Hengyang New Hope Swine Farm AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project ) apply 1 animal waste management systems (AWMSs i.e. Enclosed Anaerobic Digester, the same below) to treat the manure from the swine farm in Hengnan County, Hunan Province, which are owned by Hengyang Xinhao Agricultural and Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd (hereinafter called the project owner). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the organic fertilizers are distributed to local farmers for free, the rest will be sold in the local market. The liquid will be treated throughanaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for heat generation. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around for free for agriculture irrigation.
vcs-5016:
Longhai Swine Farm AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces a set of new animal waste management systems (AWMSs i.e. Enclosed Anaerobic Digester, the same below) to treat the manure from the swine farm in Xiling Village, Dongsi Township, Longhai District, Zhangzhou City, Fujian Province, China, P. R. China, which are owned by Longhai New Hope Liuhe Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Co., LTD. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater on site to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
In this project, the swine farm installed one AWMS to replace the traditional uncovered anaerobic lagoon. All the manure and wastewater are collected into the collection tanks and then be separated into solid and liquid matters firstly. And the separated liquid will be sent into an anaerobic digester called an Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Bed reactor (UASB). The biogas generated during the anaerobic treatment process will be captured and total 1380*104 m3 biogas are expected to be generated annually. Biogas is then sent into biogas boiler for heat production. The biogas boiler has been installed in the swine farm. All of the heat generated are used by AWMS. The sludge produced by anaerobic digestion is processed by aerobic composting along with separated solids to produce organic fertilizer which is sold to fertilizer companies and finally used for land application, while the effluent is used for agricultural irrigation.
vcs-5017:

R. China, which are owned by Liquan New Hope Liuhe Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd (hereinafter called the project owner). The project started construction in November-2020. On 1-August-2023, the project completed of acceptance, placed in service and generates GHG reductions, so the project start date is on 1-August-2023.
In this project, the swine farm installed one AWMS to replace the traditional uncovered anaerobic lagoon. The sludge produced by anaerobic digestion is processed by aerobic composting along with separated solids to produce organic fertilizer which is sold to fertilizer companies and finally used for land application, and the treated effluent is used for agricultural irrigation.
vcs-5018: Zhejiang Hengxin PET Recycling Protect aims to produce PET flakes by recycling and processing post-consumer PET bottles, to replace the same amount of PET products produced from raw materials. It is planned that 100,000 tons of post-consumer PET bottles per year will be recycled into 85,500 tons of PET flakes at maximum production capacity. The Project is located in the Longyou Industrial Park, Longyou County, Quzhou City, Zhejiang Province, China. The Project is developed and operated by Zhejiang Hengxin Power Co.,Ltd..
vcs-5019:
The “Improved cropland management project in Tangehe”developed by Henan Huiyu Industrial Development Co., Ltd. and Chengtong Carbon Sink Operation and Management (Hunan) Co., Ltd. aims to raise farmer’s awareness on the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change the agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. 

The project activity is expected to improve soil SOC and soil health through multiple ways of IALM practices. After the implementation of the project activities, the intensity of tillage on the cropland was  reduced by reducing the frequency of tillage (Implement tillage every three years), project activities now reduce the application of inorganic fertilizers and start applying organic fertilizers on the cropland. Moreover, the crop straw in the project area has now been returned to the field and water management of cropland was improved. These IALM practices can improve soil health and thus increased SOC content, and can also reduce N2O emissions by reducing nitrogen fertilizer application. 

1) Improve fertilizer (organic or inorganic) management (Reduce the application of inorganic fertilizers and start the application of organic fertilizers).
2) Improve residue management (Returning straw to the field).
3) Reduced tillage.
4 ) Improve water management.
The project is located in Tanghe County, Nanyang City, Henan province, China. The project involves 94,614 ha cropland where corn and wheat are rotated. The start date of the project is 25-May-2021, which is the date of the first IALM practice to be implemented in this project. It is estimated that 314,259 tCO2e GHG emission reduction and removal will be generated annually and total GHG emission reduction and removal during the 20 years of the first crediting period can achieve 6,285,196 tCO2e.
vcs-502: ITC (Paper and Speciality Paper Division) PSPD, Coimbatore Unit (herein refer to as ITC), a part of the ITC Limited group, have installed a co-generation plant and is utilizing agro residues (waste biomass) co-fired with fossil fuel for the generation of steam and electricity. The main objective of the project is to meet the parent paper mill’s total energy (both thermal and electrical) requirement in an efficient manner utilizing renewable agro residues abundantly available in the region and avoid the usage of fossil fuel to the extent agro residue becomes available. The installed power generating capacity of the project is 8MWelectrical.   Utilization of waste biomass not only reduces GHG emission by displacing fossil fuel but also helps control indiscriminate open air burning and decomposition in fields under anaerobic condition. Open air burning of biomass leads to N2O emission and decomposition of biomasses on the fields results in methane emission and obnoxious odour problems.
vcs-5022: FrieslandCampina is the largest dairy company in the Netherlands and one of the top five dairy companies in the world. Structured as a cooperative, it is owned by its 15,137 member farms across the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany. In an effort to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector, FC has introduced feed supplements into the daily feed of dairy cows on member farms in the Netherlands. The additives aim to reduce emissions from enteric fermentation in the rumen of dairy cows. The project has a 10-year fixed term and will run to 2032, and over the course of the project lifetime, FrieslandCampina aims to introduce new feed additives across its farms in the Netherlands. The project estimates average annual reductions of approximately 750,000 tCO2e.

vcs-5024:
The Agri Beef Steam-Flaked Corn Project aims to replace Agri Beef’s current cattle feed of primarily dry-rolled corn to primarily steam-flaked corn to reduce enteric fermentation emissions from feedlot cattle. Adjusting the diet of cattle to steam-flaked corn is a widely recognized practice to increase the energy density and digestibility of the feed and therefore reduce the dry matter intake and associated methane emissions. According to conservative IPCC estimates, feeding cattle steam-flaked corn can reduce enteric fermentation emissions up to 14% compared to dry rolled corn feed.  Peer-reviewed studies have found this reduction to be even higher, up to 26% .
During this project, Agri Beef will build their own steam-flaking production facility on their project site to further reduce emissions associated with the transportation of specialty feeds. 
The pilot project location will be at Agri Beef’s Boise Valley feedlot in Idaho. Additional project instances to come online in the future will be in Moses Lake operation in Washington which includes Agri Beef’s Coulee, El Oro, and Par 4 feedlots. Across Agri Beef feedlots associated with the project, there are on average approximately 160,000 head of beef cattle on site at any time. Prior to implementation of this project, Agri Beef cattle have been fed a conventional diet primarily of a dry-rolled corn mixture. 
During the seven years of the project’s first crediting period, the project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by an average of 17,000 metric tonnes of CO2e per year.
vcs-5025:
The GUARANATUBA REDD+ AUDD Grouped Project (GPD) is an innovative initiative located in the municipalities of Urucara, Maues, and Parintins in the state of Amazonia, Brazil. The project encompasses a total area of 3,910 hectares, including 2,928 hectares of lush Amazon rainforest. The primary objectives of the project are to combat unplanned deforestation, conserve the Amazon rainforests, reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, promote sustainable forest management, enhance local livelihoods, and protect biodiversity. To achieve these goals, the project employs a multi-faceted approach that includes legal protection for forests, advanced monitoring using satellite imagery, biodiversity and biomass inventorying with LiDAR technology, wildfire monitoring and prevention, and community engagement initiatives. Based on a 6-year jurisdictional baseline, the project is estimated to achieve an average annual reduction of 5,856 tCO2e.

The GUARANATUBA project addresses the challenges of agricultural expansion, illegal logging, and the lack of conservation incentives in the region. In partnership with Organica Consultoria LTDA, the project introduces a unique financial model that offers economic incentives to landowners for forest conservation, provides access to the carbon voluntary market, and supports sustainable forest management and legal enforcement of conservation efforts. By reducing GHG emissions, preventing deforestation, protecting biodiversity, and enhancing the livelihoods of local communities, the GUARANATUBA project promotes a harmonious coexistence between economic development and environmental stewardship. This holistic approach makes the GUARANATUBA REDD+ AUDD Grouped Project a groundbreaking model for tackling climate change and environmental degradation in the Amazon rainforest through technological advancements, economic incentives, and community engagement.
vcs-5026: Guizhou  Mayixi Yijing CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Mayixi Yijing coal mine for power generation and supply the generated electricity to the coal mine where the Project located first and then to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus. The project is located in Dahe Village, Dashan town, Panzhou City, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, China.
vcs-5027:
In the Eastern and Western Cape Provinces of South Africa, livestock overgrazing has played a significant role in desertification within the Subtropical Thicket Biome (STB), also known as the Albany Thicket Biome. Approximately 90% of the biome has experienced moderate to severe degradation as a result. This degradation has had detrimental impacts on critical ecosystem functions, including reduced availability of forage, increased soil erosion and runoff, decreased soil fertility and productivity, compromised water retention capacity, and loss of habitats. Consequently, farmers and agricultural workers have been experiencing declines in their livelihoods as the land can support progressively fewer animals.
The main objective of the project is to restore the functionality of 100,000 ha of degraded areas within the STB by reintroducing spekboom (Portulacaria afra), a pivotal species recognized for its effectiveness in thicket restoration. across the municipalities of the Eastern and Western Cape Provinces of South Africa, covering regions where the STB naturally occurs. The restoration efforts are expected to have far-reaching benefits, including carbon sequestration, biodiversity recovery, and improved livelihoods for participating landowners and communities.
vcs-5028:
This project is led by Cornerstone Technologies Holdings Limited (“Cornerstone Technologies”), a leading innovator of environmental sustainability solutions headquartered in Hong Kong, dedicated to providing diversified and convenient electric vehicles (“EV”) charging solutions that cater to the needs of car owners.
This project covers EV chargers that are installed, operated and maintained by Cornerstone Technologies across Hong Kong through strategic partnerships with private and public sectors, with an aim to scaling local EV market and acting as an enabler for the HKSAR Government to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
Under the Hong Kong’s climate action plan 2050, green transport is one of the four main decarbonisation strategies. EV, being an effective alternative for traditional fossil-fuel vehicles, plays a vital role. While the demand for decarbonisation of road transport is accelerating, Hong Kong needs to inject greater urgency into efforts in developing EV charging infrastructure to keep up with soaring sales and achieve carbon reductions.
With the provision of EV charging infrastructure with user-friendly technologies that are accessible to all, Cornerstone Technologies is committed to empowering and transforming its users into agents of change to contribute to cultivating a cleaner environment and decarbonised economy.
Greater use of EV charging infrastructure contributed by the transition of fossil-fuel vehicles to EV would result in reduced greenhouse gas emissions from alternative energy supply.

The proposed grouped project is anchored by “Credo Renewable Private Limited” (herein after called as CRPL). CRPL is a company registered in the Pakistan. 
The Project Proponent (PP) plans to distribute the ICS in different provinces across the Pakistan. The implementation of the group project will not only reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions but also decrease average fuelwood consumption, thereby contributing forest conservation. The purpose of this project activity is to restore the degraded farm lands through the afforestration, reforestration and revegetation activity with a parallel objective to encourage tree plantations and tree based farming system to incrase the tree cover outside the forest area (TOF).
The project activity covers 6304 ha of degraded farmlands and agriculture fallow lands through increasing the vegetative cover by planting multipurpose tree species in twelve forest divisions spanning across ten districts of Odisha State, India. By restoring the degraded farm lands with the native tree species, the project activity will remove the atmospheric carbon dioxide through biological carbon sequestration in the form of tree biomass and soil carbon.
vcs-5032: The project aims to restore degraded mangrove sites in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, focusing on creating a healthy ecosystem and enhancing livelihoods. Project activities involve mangrove reforestation, developing a silvofishery model in converted areas and capacity building with local communities. Targeting 66,700 hectares of degraded and converted mangrove ecosystems, the project aligns with VCS standards to sequester an estimated 41,819,835 metric tons of CO2, contributing significantly to global climate change mitigation. Biomonitoring using eDNA assesses biodiversity changes, focusing on endangered species. Community engagement is integral,  with local stakeholders including communities as the key decision makers.
vcs-5034: The project involves installation of a 90 MW floating solar PV plant on the surface of Omkareshwar Dam at Punasa Tehsil, located in the village of Kheda, Bilaya-Ekhand, Khandwa district, Madhya Pradesh, India. vcs-5035: Silk Grass Farms is a vertically integrated agribusiness in Southern Belize, committed to innovating positive environmental and social impact at scale. Silk Grass Farms, Ltd. operates within a 27,500-acre tract of land in Stann Creek, Belize. 90% of the land, about 24,700 acres, is pristine rainforest, protected in perpetuity by the wildlife preserve. The remaining 10% of the property (approximately 3,000 acres) was previously cultivated for commercial agricultural using conventional farming methods that eroded the topsoil and decreased biodiversity. Following purchase by Silk Grass Farms in 2019, the agricultural portion of the property is now under large-scale land rehabilitation and includes three additional farm properties comprising 4,000 additional acres and a 130,000 square-foot food-processing factory. Silk Grass Farms is a Certified B Corporation (B Corp) which is a certification for for-profit, purpose-driven companies that are legally bound and audited to ensure that they meet high standards for positive environmental and social impact. To better manage their agricultural and food-processing waste and support topsoil regeneration on thousands of acres of degraded farmland, Silk Grass Farms is working alongside expert consultants to construct a custom, state-of-the art biochar unit capable of pyrolyzing all of their post-processing biomass. The biochar feedstock will be agricultural wastes associated with Silk Grass Farm’s farming and food-processing operations, including but not limited to citrus fruits, coconuts, cacao, avocados, mango, watermelon and other tropical fruits and vegetables. The ARTi pyrolysis system is designed to process up to 24 tons of biomass feedstock daily and operations are set to begin in April 2024. Silk Grass Farms intends to use the biochar as soil amendments to support regenerative farming operations. The project has a crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable. The first crediting period of this grouped project is expected to remove an estimated 6,500 tons CO2e (tCO2e) annually, leading to the removal of estimated 44,550 tCO2e over the first crediting period of 7 years.
vcs-5036: The Afforestation Project in Nantou, Taiwan, is an initiative aimed at climate change mitigation through afforestation and land management. This project encompasses three distinct areas, all situated within Nantou County, Taiwan. The first site, located in Guoxing Township, spans 11.812 hectares and is situated at an elevation of around 1,000 meters. The second site, also in Guoxing Township, covers 17.3972 hectares and is located at an elevation of approximately 620 meters. Lastly, the third site, located in Zhongliao Township, covers 6 hectares and is positioned at an elevation of approximately 200 meters. These sites present an opportunity for carbon sequestration through the cultivation of Acacia confusa and other broad-leaved trees. These native species are renowned not only for their exceptional carbon sequestration capabilities but also for their significant contributions to soil conservation and biodiversity.
vcs-5037: The main objective of this CPA is the installation of energy efficient Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in the households (HHs) that are using wood as cooking fuel located within the districts of Tan Lac, Luong Son, Lac Son and Kim Boi within Hoa Binh Province, Viet Nam. A total of 30,000 ICSs are distributed under this CPA. The ICS will result in reduced firewood consumption leading to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. vcs-5038:
The Nigeria Community-Based Forestry Project (henceforth, the project will be referred to as NCBF) has adopted the VCS frameworks for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD)  and Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) . The project aims to promote Community-Based Forestry practices on 180,000 hectares, targeting forest-dependent communities in Nigeria. Supported by CO2balance UK Ltd and City Ministries, the project seeks to promote and implement CBF  principles within forest-dependent communities and generate GHG removals through REDD. 

The project area is characterised by high levels of deforestation and poor management of natural resources, which threatens people's livelihoods. Slash-and-burn agricultural activities contribute significantly to the loss of forest cover, resulting in high forest degradation . The revised 2020 Nigerian National Forest Policy outlines strategies to mitigate environmental challenges, such as climate change resulting from population growth and its impact on forests . Therefore, the NCBF seeks to add effective measures to combat deforestation in Nigeria through REDD+ initiatives. 

The project aims to reduce a total of 2,544,975 GHG emissions over 20 years. On average, this results in an annual reduction of 127,249 GHG emissions. Therefore, the NCBF project is dedicated to contributing to both Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Specifically, the project aligns with SDG 13 (climate action) and SDG 15 (life on land) , underscoring its commitment to addressing climate change and deforestation in Nigeria.

East Africa Soil and Biodiversity improvement project in Eastern Africa is a voluntary carbon project that implements Agricultural Land Management (ALM) practices developed and owned by eAgronom. This initiative is currently underway in Rwanda, Kenya, and Tanzania, with the potential for further expansion into neighbouring countries. It follows Verra's VM0042 methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management, version 2.0, referred to as VM0042, the project is dedicated to enhancing soil organic carbon levels within annual cropping systems.
The project aims to spread adoption of regenerative agricultural practices, ultimately leading to increased carbon sequestration. By doing so, it seeks to improve soil health and deliver significant benefits to farmers. Simultaneously, the project is driven to sequester greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
The Regenerative Agriculture Project in Eastern Africa focuses on elevating soil health, benefiting farmers, and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and build agricultural resilience. By initiating positive changes in East Africa and contemplating expansion, the project holds the potential to become a catalyst for transformative practices in the broader region.

In the context of carbon removal, the BRA-3C Project seeks to implement sustainable soil management practices, highlighting crop rotation to guarantee the diversification of commercial crop, cover cropping to maximize land use through the sowing of two crops in a single season, and the maintenance of plant residues and living plants in the soil, promoting carbon retention, and strengthening soil fertility. Regarding emissions, the project promotes the spread of biologicals as soil conditioners, which include fungal and microbial inoculants. Their use is expected to contribute to soil health improvement, besides establishing control over the nitrogen application's timing and dosage.
 
The BRA-3C Project aims to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks and adopt input management mechanisms to reduce emissions from agricultural activities in the Cerrado biome. The project aims to implement sustainable intensification practices for agricultural land use, to increase land and food productivity, while also expanding the conservation of natural resources. In total, the BRA-3C Project is estimated to produce 10,361,853.33 tCO2e, with an annual average of approximately 259,046.33 tCO2e/year.
The grouped project location includes the geographical extension of the Cerrado Biome within the geographic boundaries of Brazil.

vcs-5046:
Yangquan Guzhuang 8MW CMM Power Generation Project is located at the former site of Guzhuang Coal Mine Cement Plant in Yangquan, Shanxi Province. The Project utilizes coal mine methane (CMM) with a methane concentration of 16% to generate electricity, and the electricity generated is fed into the North China Power Grid for the self-consumption of the Guzhuang Coal Mine, while the heat output is recovered by a waste heat hot water boiler, replacing the original coal-fired boiler for heating in the mine area. The Project Owner is Yangquan Zhonglian Energy Technology Co.
The purpose of this project is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions through the combustion of methane in the coal mine gas during the power generation process. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. The total installed capacity of the project is designed as 8MW, with eight 1000kW gas-fired internal combustion generator sets, which utilize coal mine gas with a concentration of less than 30% to generate electricity, and utilize the waste heat hot water boiler to recover the flue gas waste heat at the tail end of the units. After running at full load, the project can consume 1,262.88*104Nm3 of pure gas per year, with an estimated annual power generation of 4800*104kWh, which will be used for the mine's self consumption through integration into the North China Power Grid, and 5.184*104GJ of residual heat per year, which will be supplied to the outside world for the heating of the buildings on the site. However, to be conservative, emission reductions will not be claimed for waste heat recovery.
During the renewable 7-year crediting period(28-Oct-2022 to 27-Oct-2029, both days included), the total GHG emission reduction of the project can reach 1,748,817 tCO2e, with an average annual emission reduction of 249,831tCO2e.
vcs-5047:
The Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) project is an ambitious initiative aimed at combating climate change, restoring biodiversity, and supporting sustainable development through largescale tree planting and ecosystem restoration efforts. The aim of the project is to address global climate change through promoting native forestry trees, specifically, bamboo, cashew nut and mango plantations in the project area. Bamboo, Cashew nut and Mango have a natural capacity to absorb CO2. The Bamboo has growth from 1.0 to1.2 meters per day and gain mature status within 2.5 to 3 years. All three plants; i.e. Bamboo, Cashew nut and Mango help in preventing soil erosion and restoring degraded areas caused by deforestation or natural disasters which serve various environmental benefits and have the potential impact to the fight against climate change.

The project activity has the following objectives: 

1. The activity encourages plantation of bamboo, cashew nut and mango trees as all these three contribute to carbon sequestration by absorbing carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere
during the process of photosynthesis. This not only helps mitigate the effects of climate change but also improves air quality. Mature Bamboo, Mango and Cashew trees are particularly effective
in this regard, storing significant amounts of carbon in their biomass over their lifespan, which can extend up to 50 years or more.

2. By engaging local communities, such as landowners and their families especially tribal women in plantation, this project not only helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions but also provides a
sustainable source of income and livelihood for farmer communities. 

3. The project provides a sustainable source of timber through bamboo, cashew nut and mango. Bamboo a type of grass has the special ability to keep absorbing carbon even after selective
harvesting. This=means that carbon sequestration continues, making it an effective and long lasting solution.

Tiryaki Agro is a global agro commodity company with 25 production sites across 11 countries. Tiryaki Agro is leading agricultural supply chain company in the region by sourcing from more than 35 countries. Tiryaki Agro' is planning to  implement and widen the regenerative and organic carbon practices in the agricultural areas under control. 

Proposed project will be implemented in Alparslan Farm located in Muş Province of Turkiye, which occupies around 6,000 ha land. Tiryaki grows wheat, sunflower, sugarbeet and other agricultural in this land. Tiryaki and GTE are collaborating to calculate and certify the emission reduction from those activities and replicate this practices in new agricultural areas via funding expected from carbon revenues.
vcs-5049:
Heilongjiang Zhaoyuan Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Zhaoyuan County, Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province, China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land.
The improved agricultural land management practices of the project focus on no-tillage on fields evenly mulched with crushed straw for two or three years, followed by plowing or subsoiling once and continued no-tillage for another two or three years. No-tillage can effectively reduce the loosening of the surface soil layer and soil disturbance, reduce the loss of water and nutrients in the soil, ensure the retention of organic matter in the soil, reduce the degree of compaction of the tillage equipment on the tillage soil layer, and preserve appropriate space for the growth of crops, which is convenient for ventilation and keeps the soil with good water storage capacity. The application of no-tillage sowing has solved the problem of sand blowing in bare farmland to a certain extent and played a role in windbreak and sand fixation. No-tillage can maximize the protective effect of straw mulching on soil.  
The project plans to implement improved agricultural land management practices in 87,479 ha corn field in the first crediting period to increase soil organic carbon (SOC). The project proponent not only introduced more efficient and appropriate tillage method with Zhaoyuan Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau (ZARAB) to the farmers, but also provide technical training and support to the farmers.
vcs-505: Shenyang Faku Heping Wind Power Project (hereafter referred as the proposed project) is to generate electricity from wind resources using advanced wind power generation technology on a commercial basis and to deliver the electricity to the Northeast China Power Grid (NECPG). The implementation of the proposed project will achieve CO2 emission reduction by replacing electricity generated by fossil fuel fired power plant.
vcs-5050: The proposed project is located in Bokpyin Township, Kawthong District, Tanintharyi Region in Myanmar. Mangroves in the region are critical to the sustainability of maritime ecosystems and the food security of local inhabitants. Mangroves in the Tanintharyi Region are feeding and breeding ground for marine animals, which are a vital source of socioeconomic development of the coastal dwellers since time immemorial. The project will restore 7,000 ha and it is estimated to sequester approximately 6,803,769 tCO2e over a period of 25 years with an annual average reduction of 272,151 tCO2e.
vcs-5052: Tech-Bank Swine Manure Composting Project in Jiangsu Province (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces 2 sets of aerobic composting systems to treat the swine manure from Huai’an Huanghuatang swine farm and Yangzhou Huangcheng swine farm in Jiangsu Province, China, which are owned by Tech-Bank Food Co., Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one aerobic composting system, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of swine manure.

Household air pollution is a global crisis and India is not unaffected by the problem. There is significant dependence on 3-stone stoves (Chullah) or traditional pot support for cooking in rural households in the country. Household pollution can cause diseases and women are particularly affected due to their direct exposure to cooking fires and involvement in daily cooking. Combustion of the non-renewable fuels and release of greenhouse gas emissions in the environment adds to global warming problem. 

The proposed project will be addressing this problem by providing access to Improved Cooking Solutions (ICS) in the form of energy efficient cookstoves. This is a voluntary initiative by EVI Green Markets Pte. Ltd. (Project Proponent or PP). PP will be collaborating with local implementation partners to provide ICS for marginalized households living in rural areas of the host country.

At present, this project is located within the area served by the Sidama Coffee Farmers’ Cooperative Union (SCFCU) in the Sidama region of Ethiopia and was started with the Bokasso Cooperative. Since then, the project area has expanded to include 11 different cooperatives as of February 2024. The project may continue to expand to other similar coffee-growing regions of Ethiopia as it grows. The project objectives include:

•	Implementing Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) interventions, including reforestation of degraded land and agroforestry on smallholder producer coffee farms to mitigate the impacts of climate change and develop new, diverse income streams for producers; and
•	Improving yield and quality of coffee, stabilizing the productivity on enrolled farms and ensuring high taste and aroma quality.

This project will implement reforestation interventions on degraded land and agroforestry interventions on the coffee plantations of smallholder producers to generate climate, nature, and socioeconomic benefits. The majority of the greenhouse gas benefits associated with the project will come from the carbon dioxide removed by the trees planted and by the carbon sequestered within the soil as a result of improved agricultural practices by coffee farmers.
vcs-5055:
The Açaí REDD+ project aims to promote forest conservation and reduce potential greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from unplanned deforestation and forest degradation.The property where the project is located covers a continuous area of 16,229.09 ha of Amazon Forest, of which 15,715.82 ha are destined for Avoiding Unplanned Deforestation (AUD).
The Açaí REDD+ project is located in the municipality of Envira, in the state of Amazonas (39,90% of the project area), and in the municipality of Feijó, in the state of Acre (60,10% of the project area). 
The project will conserves 15,715.82 hectares of Amazon rainforest and its biodiversity through the surveillance of the project area by land and river performed by outsourced people and companies, monitoring of forest fires, annual monitoring of forest cover through forest inventories and satellite images, and periodic monitoring of endangered species.

Xinghua City Improved Agriculture Land Management Project is developed by Meicun  Atmosphere Environmental Technology (Chongqing) Co, Ltd. It aims to- raise farmers' awareness of the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent the adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objectives of the project are to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage. In order to achieve these objectives, a package of practices including improved residue management that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried-out.

The project activity is located in Xinghua City, which is a county-level city under the administration of Taizhou City in Jiangsu Province, China. The area of the project activity is 26673 ha, including farmland spreading over 17 towns. Prior to the start of the implementation of the project, there was no similar activities of carbon sequestration, GHG removals or net reduction. The baseline scenario is the continuation of pre-project agricultural land management practices including conventional tillage and straw not returned to fields, which are common agricultural practices in the project area. Over the 20 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated annual average removal and reduction of 96,236 tCO2e. and 1,924,720 tCO2e in total 20 years.

Besides climate change mitigation, the project will also result in a lot of benefits in various social and environmental aspects, such as Enhance soil quality, Reduce pollution and protect the local ecological environment, Develop sustainable local agriculture, Provide training and on-site demonstration activities on convention tillage.
vcs-5058:
Project Sakahk Papakititamo (Forest Breathes) is an Indigenous-owned forest carbon project that creates net climate benefits through improved forest management of lands located in northeastern Saskatchewan, Canada. Project Sakahk Papakititamo (Forest Breathes) is a grouped project which will be comprised of individual project instances brought forward by Peter Ballantyne Cree Nation (PBCN) communities. The collection of PBCN project instances will make up the grouped project as a whole. This project uses the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VM0034 Canadian Forest Carbon Offset Methodology, V 2.0 and will apply the Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) Standard. 

Under CCB this project will also emphasize the biodiversity and the community benefits of protecting native forests. This project will support and strengthen traditional, cultural, and heritage values for the PBCN members within and external to the project area. This project ensures that future generations will thrive thanks to the sustainable practices, and that Indigenous ways of knowing are being understood and valued. As a whole, this project strives to advance Reconciliation.

Under Improved Forest Management (IFM) – Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF), projects utilize practices that reduce net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by permanently converting logged forests to protected forests. It includes forest health monitoring, and low levels of timber harvest may be required for forest health maintenance or improved forest productivity. This project’s activity will switch from a baseline of commercial clearcut harvesting to protected forest, with permissible harvesting of trees to advance conservation purposes (e.g., the removal of diseased trees) and improve forest growth and stocking density to accelerate the sequestration of additional carbon over time. As such, the PBCN project will result in significant GHG emission reductions and additional carbon sequestration.
vcs-5059: Azuero Reforestación Colectiva (ARC) is implementing a grouped restoration project in the Azuero Peninsula of Panama. Together with cattle ranchers and the local communities, the project is expected to plant native and native-adapted species on approximately 10,000 hectares that will contribute to the removal of greenhouse gasses (GHG) while restoring the land, enhancing the well-being of local communities, fostering sustainable job prospects, and promoting biodiversity.
vcs-506: Darıca-1 Hydroelectric Power Plant (HPP) is designed and built by Bilgin Güç Santralleri A.Ş. The objective of the Project activity is to supply 110 MW of renewable electricity. Darica HPP is a run-of-river HPP, the electricity amount supplied to the national grid depends on external physical conditions, i.e. the flow rate.Darıca is located in the Blacksea region of Turkey. The Darıca-1 HPP project helps in reducing the poverty in the area and contribute to the sustainable development goals.
vcs-5061:
This project aims to restore 30,000 hectares of degraded pasture that has been historically cleared for cattle grazing in the Provinces of Guanacaste, San Jose & Puntarenas in Costa Rica. A total of 7,500+ hectares will be reforested, focusing on riparian areas, which will create wildlife corridors to improve biodiversity, and the remaining 22,500 hectares will be transitioned to rotational grazing systems, which will restore ecosystem services and income streams for the participating ganaderos. The 30,000ha project area will comprise a mosaic of privately owned farmland.
The project is comprised of three core interventions:
1.	Reforestation (VM0047) – An accelerator approach to reforestation using pioneer species to provide shade for mid- and late-stage succession species will be implemented on 7,500+ hectares of pasture that has previously been converted from forest. Reforestation will primarily focus on restoring riparian areas and water ecosystem services, which will encourage project permanence, as water is a precious resource in these drought prone areas. 
2.	Rotational Grazing Programme (VM0042) – Ganaderos will be provided with training, equipment and ongoing guidance to transition remaining pasture into more sustainable and productive rotational grazing systems. 
3.	Community Development Strategy and Sustainable Business and Livelihood Fund (SBLF) - Funds generated from carbon credit revenues will be accumulated in the SBLF and be disbursed as a combination of direct payments and sustainable investment finance to further improve profitability and sustainability. Investments may be made at the discretion of the ganaderos into community programmes and local services. 


This project represents a climate adaptation for participating ganaderos by building environmental and financial resilience and is estimated to sequester 5,277,251.77CO2e over the 40-year project period.
vcs-5063: The Delta Blue Carbon Project – Phase 2 (DBC-2) is a public-private partnership initiative of Government of Sindh, Caelum Environmental Solutions and Pollination to promote climate change mitigation and adaptation, conserve and sustainable manage marine and coastal biodiversity, contribute to the achievement of various sustainable development goals and achieve women’s empowerment in the Project Zone12.The Project Zone is an area of 250,000 ha of the Sindh Indus Delta Region in Sujawal and Badin districts of Sindh Province in south-eastern Pakistan. The delta is a vast complex of tidal river channels and creeks, low-lying islands, mangrove forests and inter-tidal areas. The delta’s mangrove forests are unique in being the largest area of arid-climate mangroves in the world.
vcs-5066: The ‘Water Purification System for Safe Drinking Water (SDW) in Cambodia’ (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Project’) aims to expand pipelines connected to low greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting water treatment facilities. The goal is to provide clean drinking water to communities that previously lacked access to a public distribution network for SDW within the host country, the Kingdom of Cambodia. This is achieved through a network of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipelines that connect to water purification facilities equipped with coagulant chemicals, sand filters, disinfectant chemicals, and other substances. The Project serves as an open platform for various water treatment technologies, which are eligible under the methodology AMS-III.AV (Version 08.0).
vcs-5067: The project restores a 438 hectares drained grassland fen peatland in Eastern Latvia.
vcs-5068:
The ARR Rewilding Hub spearheaded and fully owned by Forest Defense AG in northeastern Las Lajitas, Salta Province, Argentina, is set to transform 18,450 hectares into a vibrant conservation area. Using the latest methodology VM0047, this initiative is the largest and most comprehensive ecological restoration project in the region. Previously utilized for agriculture and livestock, the land will be reforested with native species to reestablish typical native forest ecosystems of the semi-arid Chaco region. This project is dedicated to long-term conservation, with plans to maintain its sanctuary status beyond the initial 40-year accreditation period.

This pioneering effort is uniquely positioned at the agricultural and cattle production frontier, set to be a game changer for the region. It promises significant ecological balance and serves as a sustainable model for similar transitions towards environmentally friendly practices across the region. The strategic location enables a substantial multiplier effect, inspiring broader shifts towards sustainability and biodiversity preservation.

Collaborations with The Nature Conservancy (TNC), the National Institute of Agricultural Technology (INTA), and universities ensure a multi-faceted approach, combining traditional practices with scientific research. As a quality-driven project, it aims to create a sustainable ecosystem that supports biodiversity and local communities, setting a new standard for conservation efforts in Argentina.

As the most extensive and quality-driven project in the region, the ARR Rewilding Hub sets a new standard for ecological restoration in Argentina, aiming to create a sustainable and resilient ecosystem that supports both biodiversity and the local community.
vcs-5069:
Pepirí is a grouped certification project of carbon dioxide removal through afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR) of areas with and without vegetation cover in the Selva Paranaense ecoregion of Argentina. The goal of the project is to restore the vegetation cover of areas that have historically suffered land use changes caused by shifting agriculture (burning, cultivation, extensive cattle ranching, abandonment, fallow land), and other areas that have suffered intensive timber logging. The project proposes to implement measures to re-establish vegetation cover through the dynamics of natural regeneration, forestation of native and exotic species in areas without cover, and measures to enrich fallow areas with species of high conservation value. In areas altered by over-exploitation, bamboo control is implemented. Livestock control and management through fencing. A forest fire prevention system will be implemented, including firebreak roads, brigades, and control carriage.
The Project is located in the departments of Gral Manuel Belgrano and San Pedro, in the northeast of the province of Misiones, Argentina. The project area is 12,415.4 ha.  The methodology used is VM0047. The duration of the project is 20 years. Carbon sequestration is expected to average 75,000 tCO2e per year.
The project proponent is Zebra Invest GmbH, and the developer is Manejo de Inversiones Forestales Limitada (Fotosíntesis Chile), a company with long experience and expertise in carbon sequestration projects, carbon monitoring in native forests in the region, state-of-the-art remote sensing, and participatory processes with stakeholders.
vcs-507: Shenyang Faku Baijiagou Wind Power Project (hereafter referred as the proposed project) is to generate electricity from wind resources using advanced wind power generation technology on a commercial basis and to deliver the electricity to the Northeast China Power Grid (NECPG). The implementation of the proposed project will achieve CO2 emission reduction by replacing electricity generated by fossil fuel fired power plant. The proposed project is located in Faku County, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province, and  ortheast China. The proposed project proposes to install 33 sets of 1500KW wind turbines, for a total installed capacity of 49.5 MW. Faku county area where the proposed project is located has relative rich wind resources, it is estimated that the annual generation of the proposed project will be 108,520MW¡¤h. As a result, 124,125 tonnes of CO2 emission reduction will be generated.
vcs-5070: The project uses Biofiltro's BIDA system to separate solids from animal waste and process via vermicomposting.
vcs-5071: The 'Mangrove Afforestation and Reforestation Project in Cambodia' (hereinafter referred to as 'the Project') aims to combat the climate crisis by expanding mangrove forest areas in Cambodia. The project begins with the establishment of 100 hectares of new mangrove forests in Kampot and Kep, Cambodia, with plans to ultimately expand to a total of 500 hectares. Additionally, the project aims to restore over 2,500 hectares of degraded mangrove forests through reforestation efforts. VM0033, a methodology certified by VERRA, is employed to quantify greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions resulting from afforestation and reforestation activities. The total GHG reduction for the initial 100 hectare afforestation phase, spanning 20 years, is estimated at 573,067 tCO2e. GHG reduction estimates for subsequent afforestation and reforestation activities will be updated as the project progresses.
vcs-5077:
The SEIKOPAI REDD+ project aims to reduce and prevent GHG emissions from deforestation activities in the territory of the Native Community located in the basin and right bank of the Napo River, at Santa Maria stream, through the development and implementation of a REDD+ strategy built collectively and in a participatory manner with the members of the community and also aligned with the objectives of the life plan, which is conceived as a communal planning instrument that contains the worldview, history and vision of the community. It also takes into account the territorial planning and environmental protection instruments of the region to articulate the REDD+ strategy. 

This project corresponds to the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector, in the category of Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+). The project area is within the community territory and covers 134.228 ha of amazon humid forest. It is expected to avoid the emission of 8.780.025 tCO2 for 40 years, which corresponds to 219.500 tCO2/year. Aboveground Biomass (BA of trees and non-trees), Belowground Biomass (BS) and Soil Organic Carbon (COS) pools are taken into account in the project's carbon accounting, considering them to estimate the baseline scenario and monitor performance during project implementation.

During the last years, this amazon area has been under threat due to logging, agricultural expansion and fauna exploitation. Mining is also increasing in surrounding areas, thus representing a huge threat to the ecosystem’s conservation. The project aims to tackle forest pressures and contribute to mitigate climate change by reducing CO2 emissions derived from deforestation, restore degraded lands, promote sustainable management of forests and develop productive activities to improve community welfare. The project seeks to protect biodiversity and high conservation values, maintain ecological connectivity and secure natural habitats for vulnerable and threatened species along with other biodiversity of cultural and spiritual importance for the communities.  

The climate, community and biodiversity objectives are detailed next:

The climate objective is to mitigate climate change through measures that reduce and prevent deforestation and forest degradation activities. The expected results include decrease in illegal logging, recovery of degraded forests, reduction of forest conversion to other land uses and maintained forest carbon stocks over time.

The community objectives were defined with the members of the Vencedor community and aim to improve their living conditions in the territory and include: i) strengthening governance; ii) development of sustainable productive activities compatible with biodiversity conservation; iii) increase social investment; iv) improve monitoring and biodiversity protection initiatives.

Regarding biodiversity conservation, the project seeks to protect amazon tropical forest and its diversity, contribute to maintain the functional connectivity of this forest areas, improve knowledge and management capacities of productive systems that favour biodiversity, as compared to baseline scenario conditions.

In this way the REDD+ project generates a positive impact since it contributes to improve living conditions of the native communities and protects biodiversity to secure the provision of ecosystem services and ecological structure in the long term.
vcs-5078:
The proposed project activity has the objective to capture, flare and generate electricity through the use of landfill gas (LFG)  produced in anaerobic conditions into the landfill called “CTR Metropolitana Landfill” (hereinafter referred to as “CTR Metropolitana Landfill”) located in the city of Pilar in the state of Alagoas, Brazil. The landfill started the operation on May 2015, receiving solid waste (type Class II-A Inert and Class II-B Non-inert) .
The project activity results in greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction from the CTR Metropolitana landfill through two ways:

i.	Burning CH4 in flares and/or group generators;
ii.     The amount of electricity generated in the project activity is dispatched to the Brazilian Interconnected Electrical System (SIN), avoiding the dispatch of an equal amount of energy produced by fossil-fuelled thermal plants to that grid. The initiative avoids CO2 emissions and contributes to the regional and national sustainable development.

The project activity aims to capture and to flare the LFG and to generate electricity through the implementation of a power generation plant using LFG. The generation installed capacity during the first crediting period will be equal to 3.71 MW.

The project constructed an efficient capture, collection and flaring system to burn CH4 (a greenhouse gas), and this reduced odours and adverse environmental impacts. Moreover, it installs generators that combusts the LFG to produce electricity, using part of the electricity for self-consumption and the other part is exported to the grid. The flares are kept in operation due to LFG excess, periods when electricity is not be produced or other operational considerations. The LFG power plant has 3.71 MW installed capacity.
vcs-508: Penna Electricity Limited (PEL) (formerly known as Arkay Energy Limited) has established a Natural Gas based Combined Power Project at Valantharavai Village, Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu state, India. The purpose of the project activity is to generate the electrical energy for the state grid by using the natural gas as a fuel. The natural gas is transported to the project site by GAIL from the Cauvery Asset Ramanathapuram Zone of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC). The Natural Gas will be piped by GAIL from the Gas Collecting Station of ONGC, which is located at about 500 meters away from the plant site. The Project Activity is designed exclusively for firing of Natural Gas and No secondary fuel & startup fuels are envisaged in the Project Activity. The Power generated from the Project activity is being stepped up to 110 kV by generator transformers and being supplied to TNEB feeders. The Project has commenced its commercial operation since from 01 Jul 2006.
vcs-5080: The main purpose of the project is the distribution of fuel-efficient, improved cook stoves (ICS) in Philippines. The improved cook stoves distributed through this project will replace the low-efficient baseline cookstoves. In rural Philippines, a large portion of households rely on 3-stone firewood and/or traditional charcoal clay pots for daily cooking. In addition to having a relatively low thermal efficiency, these mud or three-stone stoves also contribute to health risks from indoor air (smoke) pollution.
vcs-5082: The project tackles the critical water crisis by strategically deploying deep-well drilling to tap into natural underground aquifers. This ensures a long-term, sustainable solution for clean water access. Our robust disinfection and distribution system guarantees safe drinking water at the tap. The benefits extend further: eliminating the need to use non-renewable biomass (or fossil fuels) for boiling water fosters environmental sustainability by curbing deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions. Additionally, the project aims to contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by fostering well-being, increasing local employment, promoting gender equality, reducing water collection time, and increasing opportunities for education, income generation, and healthier lifestyles.
vcs-5084:
Gannan Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu Province of China. Gannan Tibetan autonomous prefecture is located in the south of Gansu Province, the junction of Gansu, Qingdao and Sichuan Provinces. The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by seeding grass and building fence on the degraded grassland, increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local development by introducing sustainable grazing and management of grassland.
Totally, 157,153.35 ha of degraded grassland have been managed scientifically by fence building and reseeding of local high-quality forage.
Besides these main restoration measures, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area.
vcs-5085:
Tree Aid (TA) is an international development non-governmental organisation (INGO) that focuses on working with people in the Sahel region of Africa to tackle poverty and the effects of climate change by growing trees, improving people's incomes, and restoring and protecting land. It is a registered charity in the UK. TA is partnering with Earthshot Labs PBC (Earthshot) and Capricorn Investment Group LLC (Capricorn) to restore degraded landscapes in Burkina Faso through enrichment planting and agroforestry activities.
TA has partnered with local communities to identify 37 sites of degraded woodland and shrublands located in 18 communes and 4 regions with the potential to become new forest sites through enrichment planting. These sites have been affected by deforestation and decades of unsustainable agricultural activity, leading to soil degradation that has prevented further agricultural activity. This has resulted in desertification and the loss of access to culturally relevant non-timber forest products (NTFPs) that are extremely significant in socio-economic terms. Thus, the project identified activities in enrichment planting and agroforestry to restore native forests and increase access to NFTPs. 
Through enrichment planting, the project will restore native tree species with high importance to the biodiversity of the area, high restoration potential and some NTFP uses. In total 12,000 ha will be targeted across these 37 forest sites. In total just over 142,500 trees will be targeted on farmland in and around the 37 forest sites.
The project is estimated to remove 3.7 million tCO2e during the project lifetime, with estimated annual GHG emission removals of 92,576.9 tCO2e.
vcs-5087:
The KA’A PYAHU Project is located in Maranhão, Brazil, within the Indigenous Territory of the Guajajara ethnicity, one of the country's most populous. It aims to benefit approximately 13,000 indigenous individuals. Named after the Tupi-Guarani words meaning 'New Forest,' the Ka’a Pyahu project represents 'a new care for nature' for the community. The project area is managed by local communities in the territories of Cana Brava, Rodeador, Lagoa Comprida, and Urucu Juruá, organized around the CONSELHO SUPREMO association since 2019.

Through the establishment of the association and organizational efforts, the community has achieved significant milestones in protecting their territories. Legal actions against damages caused by projects from companies have resulted in decisions favoring the community, leading to reduced deforestation and compensation for previous degradation.

The community's history of organization and strengthened internal governance has empowered them to safeguard the forests in their territories. Additionally, they have gained familiarity with the REDD+ initiative and the carbon market through this process.
The KA’A PYAHU PROJECT aims to ensure better conditions for environmental conservation and sustainable use of forests, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for local communities, particularly in terms of clean water, sanitation, and education.
vcs-5089: The project sources used ODS from facilities in South Africa which is then transported for destruction in a TEAP approved destruction facility located in South Africa.
vcs-509: Project - 6.65 MW Wind energy generation by GTN Enterprises Ltd.  The project activity is a renewable energy project, that involves establishment of a wind power project with a total installed capacity of 6650 KW, in the state of Tamilnadu, INDIA. The Project activity replaces antropognic emissions of GHG into the atmosphere by displacing tthe equivalent amount of electricty generation through the operation of existing/proposed fossil fuel based power plant connected to grid. The project activity thus uses renwable natural resources, namely wind, for electricity generation, thus reducing the consumptions of the depleting non renewable resources and associated GHG emissions which would ultimately lead to sustainable development.
vcs-5090:
The Mount Kei Reforestation Project plans to reforest and rehabilitate a total area of 9050 hectares in Mount Kei Central Forest Reserve (CFR) in the far northwestern part of Uganda. The project is implemented by Equatoria Forest Company Ltd. in cooperation with Form International B.V. and Hummingbirds. 

Due to a complex set of socio-economic factors, including the presence of South Sudanese immigrants in the eastern portion of the reserve, limited law enforcement efforts by the National Forest Authority (NFA), resulting in encroachment by farmers and continued logging and charcoal production, the area has been subjected to severe degradation over time. Likewise, local communities in the region rely heavily on natural resource-based activities such as agriculture, forest products (mostly charcoal) and cattle holding, which leads to grazing, hunting and farming, exacerbating degradation.
