Equatoria Forestry Company Ltd. (EFC), is a Uganda-based company established in 2012. EFC has secured a land lease agreement with the National Forestry Authority (NFA) of Uganda, granting the right to utilize a 9050-hectare area within the Central Forest Reserve (CFR) – approximately a quarter of the total area of Mount Kei CFR – for the establishment and management of a commercial forest plantation. EFC applied for this license in 2018, and the license was granted in 2021. EFC is in the process of acquiring an additional license for natural forest restoration and for additional forest plantation, covering the remaining area of the CFR. 

The project promotes the establishment of sustainably managed plantations, using mainly Tectona grandis and testing native species, as well as assisted natural regeneration and enrichment planting with native species in degraded forest patches, therewith aiming to restore forest cover and generate GHG emission reductions. In addition to these carbon benefits, the project aims to realize multiple socioeconomic and environmental benefits.
vcs-5091: The project seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by keeping food in the human food chain. This is a group project that spans over locations in AL, FL, GA, NC, SC, TN, and VA. This project utilizes food donation programs to achieve emission reductions from diverting food from a food loss and waste (FLW) destination in conformance to the VM0046 Methodology for Reducing Food Loss and Waste, v1.0.
vcs-5092: Zhiduo Grassland Sustainable Management Project  is located in Zhiduo County, Yushu Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China, The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland by adopting a variety of measures including grass planting, fertilization, fence installation, and etc., and protect the grassland ecosystem from further degradation by sustainable grazing management. Finally the project will increase carbon sequestration by reversing grassland degradation, and will also contribute to local development ,preserve cultural traditions, and increase ecosystem biodiversity.
vcs-5093:
Pingnan municipal solid waste (hereafter referred to as “MSW”) incineration and power generation project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Shangdu Town, Pingnan County, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China, with geographic location of 110.356977°E and 23.483333°N. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by BEWG Environmental Protection Guangxi Pingnan Co., Ltd.
The combustion system is composed of one 600t/d mechanical grate incinerator, matched with one set of 12MW steam turbine generator. The project will treat 219,000 tons of MSW every year. The MSW combustion line will work over 8,000 hours every year. The project is expected to generate 88,010 MWh electricity, of which 74,810 MWh will be exported to the China Southern Power Grid (hereinafter referred to as CSPG). When turbine generator is repaired, it may involve in purchased electricity from CSPG. The implementation of the project meets the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also, the project could reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil fuel fired plants and MSW treatment.
Before the implementation of the project, the local MSW was usually disposed of at nearby landfill, where no landfill gas capturing system erected and the landfill gases are released to atmosphere directly. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can transfer steam to generate electricity power to replace the electricity that would be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants. 
The total GHG emission reduction is expected to be 780,570 tCO2e and the average annual emission reduction is   111,570 tCO2e in a period of 7 years (from 7/7/2022 to 6/7/2029 both included).
vcs-5094: Maniurja Climate Conserva Private Limited aims to promote clean cooking practices in rural and semi-urban areas of India by introducing a more efficient cookstove technology. This initiative seeks to enhance living standards by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, environmental degradation, and health risks associated with indoor air pollution. The distribution of Improved Cookstoves (ICS) across various states in the state of Odisha aims to cut fuel usage, cooking time, and health hazards caused by smoke emissions. The project also targets benefits such as increased thermal efficiency, fuel savings, reduced deforestation, minimized indoor smoke exposure, and less time spent collecting firewood, ultimately leading to greenhouse gas reduction, forest conservation, and improved health for ICS users.
vcs-5095:
The project involves establishing and operating an advanced biogas plant in General Paz, situated 30 kilometers away from Cordoba city. This plant is designed to process various industrial substrates, including solid waste, liquids, and animal manure, with the aim of mitigating the negative environmental impacts associated with landfill disposal of industrial waste and promoting renewable energy generation.

Central to the project is its capacity to convert industrial wastes into clean and sustainable energy sources. By diverting these wastes from landfills, the project helps prevent greenhouse gas emissions and minimizes the risk of soil and water contamination, thereby making a significant contribution to reducing local and regional greenhouse gas emissions.

Notably, this biogas plant stands out as a significant milestone in the region, being the only operational facility exclusively fed by organic waste of industrial origin. This uniqueness highlights the commitment of Helios Energia Limpia to innovation and sustainability and positions it as a leader in adopting environmentally responsible practices in the industrial sector.

Additionally, the project has secured an agreement with Cammesa under the Renovar 2 program, ensuring the injection of up to 2.4 MW of renewable energy into the national electricity grid. This strategic partnership reflects institutional recognition and support for the project's importance and viability in transitioning towards a more sustainable energy matrix.
vcs-5096: Agroforestry can help in conservation and rehabilitation of the ecosystem along with providing better livelihood opportunities to the rural community. The proposed VCS agroforestry project, titled Livelihood improvement by Shashwat agroforestry plantation through carbon Finance in Maharashtra (also referred to as Palghar Agroforestry project) operates in Palghar district, situated in the western line of Maharashtra, India. Currently, the project spans eight blocks of Palghar District namely Dahanu, Jawahar, Mokhada, Palghar, Talasari, Vasai, Vikramgad and Wada, and have potential to expand in other districts of Maharashtra
vcs-5097:
The project is located in Banqiao Village, Chishuiyuan Town, Zhenxiong County, Shaotong City, Yunnan Province, P.R.China. The project owner is Zhenxiong Yonder New Energy Development Co., Ltd.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. It is expected that 13.0392 million Nm3 of methane annually will be destroyed to generate electricity. According to Feasibility Study Report (FSR) of the project, 14 sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 9.8 MW (14*700 kW).
After the full operation of the project, the expected annual exported electricity is 49,476 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Zhujiawan coal mine and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, thus displace equivalent amount of electricity that would be supplied by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. 
 It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 13-May-2023 to 12-May-2033), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 243,241 tCO2e, with the total emission reduction of 2,432,410 tCO2e.
vcs-5098:
Bestway Cement Limited (hereafter referred as Bestway Cement Ltd.) has installed Renewable Energy Power Plants based on Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Technology (hereafter referred as “project activity”) at various locations across Pakistan as a grouped project activity. Bestway Cement Ltd. is looking forward to earning carbon credits under VCS mechanism for these Solar PV based power plants.
The proposed grouped project activity supports development of renewable energy generation plants based on Solar PV technology in Pakistan with the objective of supplying electricity to power Bestway Cement Ltd.’s factories. The proposed grouped project is a voluntary action being undertaken by Bestway Cement Ltd. The renewable energy generation plants under the grouped project activity would generate Solar PV based electricity, which otherwise in absence of project activity would have been generated from fossil fuel fired grid connected power plants. The grouped project activity thus leads to reduction in Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions.
There are in total of six project activity instances in this group project, and all the project activity instances are owned by Bestway Cement Ltd., who is also acting as coordinating and managing entity for the grouped project activity. Since the project activity is grouped project activity, more project activity instances can be included in grouped project activity in future. Each instance of project activity under this grouped project consists of one renewable power generation plant using Solar PV technology. All the project instances i.e. renewable energy generation plants to be included in this grouped project will be from within Islamic Republic of Pakistan (hereafter referred as “Pakistan”) only. The estimated annual emission reductions over a 10 year period from initial six project activity instances are 422,719 tCO2e.
vcs-5099:
The project activity aims to manufacture Aerated Autoclaved Concrete blocks (AAC). AAC blocks are a lightweight, precast, and thermally insulating building material manufactured through a process that involves autoclaving aerated concrete, resulting in a product with reduced environmental emissions compared to traditional clay bricks.

The project is implemented by Magicrete Building solutions Private Limited at Wada in district Palghar, state of Maharashtra, India. 

In the absence of the AAC block project, use of traditional clay bricks is widespread in the host country. Clay bricks have high associated GHG emissions.
vcs-51: Acciona Wind Energy Pvt. Ltd. (AWEPL) is an Indian Company and a 100% subsidiary of the Spanish Acciona group of companies, i.e. Acciona Energia Internacional, S.A. and Acciona, S.A. AWEPL has implemented a wind energy project as project owner with 18 wind turbines of 1.65MW each supplied by Vestas Wind Technology India Pvt. Ltd. totaling 29.70MW spread over two locations in close proximity in Jagalur taluk, Davangere district in the State of Karnataka. The project activity involves the development, construction, operation and maintenance of wind based electricity generation facilities connected to the grid.  The project supplies renewable electricity to the Karnataka State electricity grid and reduces greenhouse gas emissions caused by reliance on fossil fuels to that extent. The generated electricity is supplied to BESCOM (Distribution Company) under long-term Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) for a period of 20 years with a standard tariff of Rs.3.40 per kWh for the initial 10 years.
vcs-510: The project activity is set up to produce clean power from the wind electric converters. The objective is development, design, engineering, procurement, construction, operation and maintenance of Kirloskar Wind Farms of 4 MW wind power project in the Indian state of Maharashtra. The generated electricity will be wheeled using the state transmission system for captive consumption.  The Project will lead to reduced greenhouse gas emissions because it displaces electricity from fossil fuel based electricity generation plants. The project activity puts to use barren land at Aloke and Patan Taluka in Ahmednagar and Satara districts respectively in the state of Maharashtra.
vcs-5100:
Guigang biomass wastes through use as feed stock in paper pulp production project is located at  No. 1 Xingfu Road, YueGui Thermoelectric circular economy Industrial Park, Guigang City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Guangxi Guangye Guitang Sugar Group Co., Ltd.

Before the project activities, bagasse was mainly dumped in landfills as solid waste. However, bagasse is one of the better raw materials for non-wood fiber paper making, and the project makes full use of the rich local resources of agricultural waste bagasse to develop pulp and paper making. After the implementation of the project, 65,300 tons of bagasse pulp will be supplied to the market annually. With the project's successful full operation on June 19, 2023, bagasse will be used as a feedstock for pulp and paper production, thus avoiding methane emissions. This project is expected to reduce emissions by 917,205 tCO2e over seven years, or an average of 131,029 tCO2e per year.
vcs-5102: The proposed project activity concerns a greenfield biomass to energy power plant at the FX Group Lothair facility, which is situated in the Mpumalanga province of South Africa. The Project will source biomass from local sawmills and biomass wastes for the generation of electricity in a power-only plant. The woody biomass will be fed into a biomass boiler to create super-heated high-pressure steam. The steam is used to spin a 4.5MW power output steam turbine and electrical generator. The renewable energy produced by the plant will displace the grid electricity, which would have been used to power the industrial facility in the absence of the biomass power plant. Electricity on the South African National grid is largely generated by the state-owned entity Eskom and is highly carbon-intensive due to the reliance on fossil-fuels such as coal and diesel.
vcs-5104: The consumption of non-renewable biomass firewood for household purposes in the rural areas is one of the main causes of deforestation in the surrounding areas of the state of Gujarat and has several implications in the environmental and health aspects of such communities. The Project activity aims to replace the commonly used inefficient wood fired mud stove technology with efficient bio-gas based cook stoves, which is clean and sustainable. In view of the same Amul Dairy has planned to implement a project which is clean, convenient and efficient energy can be accessed by the rural households.
vcs-5106:
The Project is an afforestation and reforestation project initiated by PUR Projet, a French organization specialized in the development of ecosystems restoration and preservation projects, through agroforestry, community reforestation, and forest conservation. PUR Projet also assists companies in insetting their supply chains, and in the management and communication of their socio-environmental commitments.
The project is located in Guatemala where coffee production is recognized for its high quality beans. It is grown by small-scale farmers with an average size of coffee farm close to 1.0 ha. Coffee trees are growing on highly steep terrain, where soil erosion (due to important water runoff and heavy rains) threatens both the quantity and quality of coffee yields. 
Reducing soil erosion becomes critical in order to maintain productivity and quality. Additionally, the
majority of small-scale farmers has been badly hit by rust in the past and is constraint to renew its coffee
fields. Enhancing the coffee production resilience in terms of yields and quality, through an agroforestry
project, constitute the best strategy to support economically local communities.
vcs-5107:
The TERAKA program is a smallholder reforestation and sustainable development initiative in Madagascar. Inspired by the successful TIST model in East Africa, the program empowers farmers to plant and own trees on their land while receiving training from TERAKA and 70% of carbon benefits. Organized into Small Groups, farmers actively combat deforestation, poverty, and drought through sustainable practices that integrate carbon sequestration. By turning carbon credits into a 'virtual' cash crop, the initiative enhances both environmental and economic resilience.
Currently operating in central and eastern Madagascar, TERAKA aims to scale up across the country, starting with 6,000 hectares in its first phase. This phase is projected to sequester more than two million tonnes of greenhouse gases over 40 years while restoring degraded land, improving local livelihoods, fostering sustainable employment, and promoting biodiversity.
vcs-5108:
The Bamboo King Vina Biochar Project aims to address the substantial waste generated from bamboo and wood processing at the Bamboo King Vina (BKV) factory in Lang Chanh district, Thanh Hoa province, Vietnam. The factory, with a daily processing capacity of 1,500 tons, generates approximately 800-900 tons of waste per day. To mitigate this environmental impact, the project will install and operate six biochar production facilities using pyrolysis technology. This process converts bamboo and wood waste into biochar, a carbon-rich material.
The produced biochar will be applied directly to soil or used indirectly in agricultural land through animal feed, livestock bedding, sludge management, composting, or anaerobic digestion. The project's objectives include reducing bamboo waste sent to landfills or left to decay, which contributes to greenhouse gas emissions. Utilizing biochar in soil management aims to enhance agricultural land, promote carbon-rich ecosystems, improve crop yields, and boost food security. Additionally, it seeks to foster healthier communities and economic prosperity for local at-risk populations.
vcs-5109: The Improved cropland management project in Aktaw and Shufu is aimed to raise farmer's awareness on the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change the agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objectives of the project is to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage, in order to achieve these, a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried out, the specific activities are the following: 1) improved fertilizer(organic or inorganic) application; 2) Improved residue management; 3) Improve crop planting and harvesting.
vcs-511: The project activity is located in the Jiangsu Yangtze River International Chemistry Park, which is 20km distance from downtown Zhang Jiagang, Suzhou city in Jiangsu Province. The geographical coordinate of the centre of project site is: East Longitude 120¡ã27¡ä52¡å, North Latitude 32¡ã00¡ä10¡å. The purpose of the project activity is to recover waste heat from sulphuric acid production process to produce electricity, displacing part of electricity supplied by the East China Grid which predominantly relies on fossil fuel-fired power plants for power generation. The project activity involves installation of Monsanto Heat Recovery System (HRS), which is created by MECS in USA, and Siemens condensing turbine and power generation units with the rated output of 50MW.
vcs-5110: The Improved cropland management project in Yanshou and Mulan is aimed to raise farmer's awareness on the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change the agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objectives of the project are to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage, in order to achieve these, a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried out, the specific activities are the following:improved fertilizer(organic or inorganic) application;improved residue management;Improve crop planting and harvesting.
vcs-5112:
The Wuhu Improved Agricultural Land Management Project in Wuhu City, Anhui Province, China, aims for sustainable development by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, increasing soil organic carbon, enhancing biodiversity, and supporting community development.
In the first crediting period, the project area include 2785 ha of agricultural land in Wuhu city, with an anticipation to expread to 19,720 ha in the future. The project addresses soil degradation from excessive fertilizer use and poor management.
Led by Zoomlion Smart Agriculture Co., Ltd.,  the project offers smart agriculture solutions and technical guidance to local large-scale farmers. Farmers voluntarily participate, supported by both government funds and the technology and equipment provided by Zoomlion. The project activities include measures like fertilizer optimization, green manure rotation, water-efficient irrigation, and pest management , a digital platform is built to send out notifications and provide farming guidance.
This project anticipates the removal or reduction of an estimated 14,579,599 tCO2e over its lifetime of 30 years at an estimated average of 129,264 tCO2e annually. The objectives of this project include bringing benefits to three main aspects including climate, community, and biodiversity.
vcs-5113: The grouped project activity comprises solar power plants on both rooftops and ground-mounted systems, empowering small and medium enterprises across Kenya to generate clean energy for captive use. This will significantly reduce reliance on Kenyan national grid and contribute to reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. The project activity provides clean electricity through solar power plants displacing consumption of electricity that would have been supplied by National grid of Kenya in the absence of the project activity.
vcs-5114: The intention of the grouped project involves the installation of low greenhouse gas emitting water purification systems i.e., chlorine dispensers, to provide clean drinking water to low income households/communities in Uganda. For this reason, this proposed grouped project aims at reducing the non-renewable woody biomass consumption from traditional stove users by installing chlorine dispensers at communal water points.
vcs-5115: The intention of the grouped project involves the installation of low greenhouse gas emitting water purification systems i.e., chlorine dispensers, to provide clean drinking water to low income households/communities in Malawi. For this reason, this proposed grouped project aims at reducing the non-renewable woody biomass consumption from traditional stove users by installing chlorine dispensers at communal water points.
vcs-5117:
The project aims to rehabilitate the local forest ecosystem and introduce agroforestry methods to communities within watersheds and along riverbanks across a 1.7 million hectare expanse spanning São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Maranhão. It plans to rejuvenate over 6,000 hectares through reforestation and will incorporate agroforestry near local farms, targeting pasturelands, deteriorated areas, and mono-crop fields. The project's core goal is to restore deforested and degraded lands, enhancing farmers' ability to sustainably produce food and generate income. 

Through agroforestry, the project offers alternative livelihoods, encouraging farmers to shift from traditional to sustainable land management practices. Agroforestry systems of coffee and cocoa will be implemented in partnership with local farmers in pastureland, degraded land, and monocultures, with capacity-building initiatives and training programs planned as part of the project.
vcs-5118: The project Farm Resilience and Regeneration in France and Belgium aims to transform agriculture by empowering and supporting farmers to transition to regenerative practices. It offers robust instruments to enable corporations to contribute to nature regeneration, with a focus on carbon sequestration, biodiversity, and water resources. Spanning arable farming, livestock, mixed crop-livestock systems, and vineyards across mainland France and Belgium, the initiative focuses on creating resilient farms through ecosystem and soil revival. Utilizing the VM0042 methodology for Improved Agriculture and Land Management (ALM) and Quantification Approach 1: Measure and Model, the project targets 3,100 farms over the 20-year crediting period, transforming 460,000 hectares. It conservatively anticipates average annual carbon removals of 428,000 tCO2e, totaling 8,600,000 tCO2e over the crediting period. With tailored agronomic and financial support, rigorous monitoring, and a results and measure-based model, the project targets net carbon removals for VCUs while contributing to multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including improved access to knowledge for small-scale farmers (SDG 2), enhanced gender inclusion (SDG 5), increased water-use efficiency (SDG 6), improved resource efficiency (SDG 8), reduced chemical releases (SDG 12), climate change mitigation (SDG 13), land restoration (SDG 15), and fostering partnerships between industry and farmers (SDG 17). By investing in this project, you are contributing to the future of agriculture, benefiting both farmers and ecosystems, and making your business regenerative.
vcs-512: The project activity leads to annual aggregate energy consumption reduction of 21.84 GWhthermal/year due to energy efficiency improvement initiatives and switching to a comparatively lesser carbon intensive energy source in the glass melting process at the greenfield opal glass manufacturing unit of La Opala RG Limited (LORL). Owing to the comparatively more efficient melting process set-up, the project activity results in lesser wastage of thermal energy input to glass melting process. Since the project activity utilizes a lower quantum of energy generated from a comparatively lower carbon intensive source to produce a given quantity of molten glass, it results in GHG emission reductions to the tune of 4,081 tCO2e per annum on an average as per ex-ante GHG emission reduction calculation provided in Annex-II of the VCS PD.
vcs-5120:
The proposed grouped projects aim at improving the quality of drinking water through dissemination of zero greenhouse gas emitting water purification systems to provide safe drinking water for schools and institutions throughout Cambodia that previously do not have access to public distribution network supply safe drinking water. In this grouped projects, schools include Kindergartens, nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, high schools. Institutions would cover pagodas, community home, home for disabled, orphanage, nursing home, mental home. For this reason, this proposed project activity will avoid the use of thermal energy and/or low energy and associated emissions.
The grouped project activity will minimize the use of fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass utilized for boiling water as a means purification to achieve safe drinking water quality in the absence of this project activity. This directly leads to reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it can be helpful to user’s health.
vcs-5121:
The purpose of the group project activity is to provide safe drinking water to schools/institutions in rural communities of Laos. The proposed project activity aims to reduce the use and demand of wood fuel and fossil fuel that would have been used to boil the water to purify water in the absence of the proposed project activity by installation of safe drinking water treatment stations and distribution of safe drinking water purifier.
The project activity targets schools/institutions with no previous safe drinking water access. The geographical boundary is in Laos. In this grouped projects, schools include Kindergartens, nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, high schools. Institutions would cover community home, home for disabled, orphanage, nursing home, mental home, pagodas… The stations and water purifiers are distributed free of cost to schools/institutions. Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company (SIPCO) shall finance the implementation of the project in full.
vcs-5122:
The proposed group projects aim to improve the quality of drinking water by promoting water filtration systems that do not emit greenhouse gases (GHG). The projects will provide safe drinking water by water purifiers and stations to schools and institutions throughout Viet Nam. In this grouped project, schools include Kindergartens, nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, high schools. Institutions include community home, home for disabled, orphanage, nursing home, mental home. Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company (SIPCO) shall finance the implementation of the project in full.
The project group includes two main technologies: ceramic water purifier and the safe drinking water treatment station. Both technologies offer odor removal and 99.999% sterilization efficiency, significantly reducing the accumulation and growth of harmful bacteria. The distribution of purifiers and stations will be tailored to the number of users at each school or institution. The use of these purifiers and stations also minimizes the need for wood fuel and fossil fuel for boiling water, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The grouped project activity will minimize the use of non-renewable biomass and fossil fuel utilized for boiling water as a means purification to achieve safe drinking water quality in the absence of this project activity. This directly leads to reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it can be helpful to user’s health.
vcs-5123:
This is an agroforestry project on minor agriculture crop land and barren land aims to promote sustainable agroforestry practices across Telangana state of India. By planting diverse range of trees the project seeks to empower smallholders and tribal communities, increase tree cover, enhance income, conserve biodiversity, improve soil health, and generate emission reductions. The targeted farmers are small landholders and the land earmarked for plantation activities is privately owned.

Encompassing a total plantation of 6,000,000 trees in 10,000 ha of land, the farmers have undertaken tree plantations, primarily featuring Mangifera indica (mango), Santalum album (sandalwood), Psidium guajava (guava), Tectona grandis (teak), Azadirachta indica (neem), Swietenia macrophylla (mahogany), Casuarina equisetifolia (horsetail she-oak), Dalbergia sissoo (Indian rosewood), Aquilaria malaccensis (agarwood), Phyllanthus emblica (amla), Punica granatum (pomegranate), and Manilkara zapota (sapota) during the years 2021, 2022, and 2023. The districts included in the project area are :  Vikarabad, Ranga Reddy, Mahabub Nager, Narayanapeta, Sanga Reddy, Jogulambha Gadwal, Wanaparthy and Medchiel.
vcs-5124:
The Project Team ATR Inc. (ATR, hereafter referred as “project proponent”) has the legal right to register the project and issue carbon credits. ATR will manage and monitor the project to ensure it remains eligible under the VCS standard throughout the crediting period. The Waste Heat Recovery based Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred as “Project Activity”) at Bestway Cement Limited (hereafter referred as Bestway Cement Ltd.) in Pakistan is proposed for registration under the Verra Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Standard, Version 4.7, 16 April 2024 (hereinafter Standard) and associated Program Guide, Version 4.4, 29 August 2023 (hereinafter Guide).
There are in total of two project activity instances in this group project. Project Team ATR Inc. acts as both the Project Proponent and the coordinating and managing entity (CME) for this grouped project activity. Since the project activity is grouped project activity, more project activity instances can be included in grouped project activity in future. Each instance of project activity under this grouped project consists of one Waste Heat Recovery Plants (WHRPs) using steam turbine.
Both project activity instances incorporate multiple sources of electricity, derived from both the grid and Bestway Cement Ltd.’s WHRPs. The decision to maintain reliance on the grid alongside WHRP stems from the substantial energy demand required for the operation of the clinker production lines, which surpasses the energy output from waste energy sources. However, there has been a decrease in the consumption of grid-generated electricity after the Project Activity, and this reduction in grid dependency will result in a decrease in carbon emissions. 
The estimated annual emission reductions over a 10-year period from initial two project activity instances are 594,469 tCO2e.
vcs-5125:
The proposed project ‘MZURI methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management’ aims to reduce and sequester GHG emissions by implementing more sustainable agricultural practices on fields in northern Poland. The planned schedule of activities fits within Verra’s VM0042 standard, which comprises a range of regenerative agricultural land management practice changes targeted at reducing net emissions of CO2, CH4, and N2O by grower operations and increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage. This is being achieved in this project by supporting farmers to implement climate-smart agricultural land management practices through the use of innovative land machines and integrated improved agricultural practices, supported by digital data collection tools and modelling. These practices include reductions in fertilizer use, strip tillage, adapted crop rotations, and cover cropping. Overall, these practice changes seem well appropriate to reduce emissions from agricultural production, to increase farm resilience to extreme weather events and the effects of climate change, and to promote increased soil (micro-) biological diversity. Expected co-benefits of the project (other than carbon reduction and sequestration) are expressed along the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Considering the context and location of the project, its scope of activities will contribute to the achievement of:
•	SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), 
•	SDG 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing), 
•	SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), 
•	SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), 
•	SDG 13 (Climate Action), 
•	SDG 15 (Life on Land).
The project’s scope of activities significantly lowers the GHG emissions of agricultural activities vs. baseline scenario, and enhances or restores the carbon storage capacity of the area, thereby sequestering CO2 from the atmosphere. The project meets the criteria for climate additionality as well as community and biodiversity additionality, and shows a regulatory surplus.
vcs-5126:
The Masaka project developed by Madaprojects Srl SB referred to as “MDP”, is a voluntary Grouped Project involving the dissemination of improved cookstoves non-renewable wood fuel among local communities in the region Atsimo-Andrefana, Tulear district in Madagascar, which will result in reduces firewood consumption leading to climate change, mitigation in a sustainable manner.
The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity is the actual baseline scenario which is equal to the existing common practice in the region, i.e. absence of the project activity the equivalent amount of thermal energy generated using non-renewable wood fuel is three stone open fires and/or traditional cooking system to meet the cooking energy demand.
The ex-ante estimation of average annual GHG emission reduction generated by the first Project Activity (PA1) of this grouped project for the chosen renewable seven years crediting period are 59,698 tCO2e/year (average), and 417,883 tCO2e respectively.
vcs-5127:
The Project seeks to develop an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (hereinafter referred to as ARR) VCS project in Russian Federation, the Voronezh Oblast, the Levoberezhnoye Prigorodnoye Forestry district.

The project aims to create carbon-sequestration plantations (hereinafter referred to as CSPs)  on deforested areas to increase carbon stocks of woody biomass. Project activities are implemented in areas previously exposed by fires, which led to the formation of burned-out forests with low rates of natural regeneration.

The project allows to increase the carbon dioxide removal (hereinafter referred to as CO2 removal) by carrying out revegetation activities, including the cultivation of planting material in the form of various tree crops and the carrying of agrotechnical measures for their planting in deforested areas. The activity of creating CSPs in the burned-out forests contributes to an increase in the absorption of CO2 from the atmosphere during photosynthesis and carbon sequestration in carbon pools.
vcs-5128: This grouped project in the Kunene Highlands Elephant Landscape in Namibia aims to work in partnership with 12 Community Conservancies to expand regeneration and conservation efforts, promoting sustainable land management practices and livelihoods. The landscape, representing almost 1 million hectares, is an area of considerable ecological importance, providing biodiversity connectivity between adjacent national parks. It also holds a significant elephant population, and overlaps with ranges of at least 3 species listed as critically endangered, 10 listed as endangered, 12 listed as vulnerable, and 10 listed as near threatened by the IUCN, including large megafauna and birds that are at high risk of habitat loss, poaching and climate change threats. Through regenerative rangeland management, the project will support grassland restoration, carbon sequestration, soil moisture retention and climate resilience.
vcs-5129: This grouped project implements sustainable grazing practices on ranching lands in the state of Montana, USA. The rangeland landscape includes grasslands, steppe, prairies and forests. Wildlife characteristic of the area includes grizzly bears, pronghorn antelope, bison, white-tailed deer, elk and bighorn sheep. The land management practice changes will restore grasslands, increase vegetation cover, foster native plant diversity, sequester carbon, improve water infiltration, and reduce runoff. These impacts will increase the climate resilience of the ranches and support rancher livelihoods.
vcs-513: Salto Pilão project activity consists of the construction of a hydropower plant with a reservoir of 0.15 km2 and an installed capacity of 191,8 MW. The plant is located between the cities of Lontras, Ibirama and Apiúna, state of Santa Catarina, Southern region of Brazil.According to the project license, the geographic coordinates of the project activity are 27º06’and 27º08’S and 49º28’and 49º31’W.
vcs-5130: This project takes place in the state of Coahuila, Mexico, with the goal of restoring lands which have been extensively degraded by overgrazing. These lands are being overrun by invasive species such as desert shrubs, cacti, annual grasses and forbs. The project implements sustainable grazing practices aimed at restoring grasslands, increasing vegetation cover, sequestering carbon, improving water infiltration, and reducing runoff. These impacts will increase the climate resilience of the ranches and support rancher livelihoods. These are biodiversity-rich areas, featuring black bears, bobcats, coyotes, cougars, and golden eagles, among other species.
vcs-5131: This Improved Forest Management project is a Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF) project type, located on approximately 33,000 acres of privately-owned land in Southwestern Virginia. The project activity consists of the buy-out of a long-term timber lease and surveillance of the project area.
vcs-5132: The Omnia Solar PV Group Project involves the commissioning of new, solar photovoltaic (PV) installations in the Republic of South Africa. These installations serve as a clean, renewable source of electricity, contributing to the enhancement of the country’s energy security by reducing reliance on emission-intensive grid-electricity, primarily supplied by Eskom, the national utility facing challenges due to its aged and failing infrastructure.
vcs-5134:
The proposed VCS (Verified Carbon Standard) grouped ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation) project aims to enhance carbon sequestration through the implementation of directly planting native and locally adapted tree species on smallholder and marginalised farmers' land across various locations Central and Eastern India. The first instance of the project area focuses on promoting carbon economy in the states of Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh which encompasses large contiguous and scattered small land parcels planted with timber, horticultural tree species as well as bamboo species. Timber tree species including teak (Tectona grandis), Khamer (Gmelina arborea) etc. and horticultural tree species including Guava (Psidium guajava), Drumstick (Moringa oleifera), Jamun (Syzygium cumini) etc. for the first instance of the project activity. The plantation is being carried out on  degraded, partially cultivated, fallow and current fallow land parcels.

The absence of significant tree cover led to higher vulnerability to soil erosion and reduced agricultural productivity. By transforming these areas through afforestation, the project aims to restore ecological balance, improve soil fertility, and contribute to the mitigation of climate change through increased carbon storage.

The project follows both census and area based approaches as per the methodology VM0047.
vcs-5135:
Guizhou Bijie Yuxing CMM Power Generation Project will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Yuxing coal mine which is a working coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mine where the project is located and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus. The waste heat generated by the generator replace the heat originally generated by waste coal. The project is located in Dongfeng Village, Pudi Town, Hundred—mile Azalea Management Area, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, P.R.China. The project owner is Bijie Yicheng New Energy Technology Co., Ltd.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. It is expected that 60.46 million Nm3 of methane annually will be destroyed to generate electricity. According to Feasibility Study Report (FSR) of the project, 22 sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 26 MW (14*1,000 Kw + 8*1,500 Kw). After the full operation of the project, the expected annual exported electricity is 177,840 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Yuxing coal mine and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, thus displace equivalent amount of electricity that would be supplied by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
The capacity of phase 1 of the project is 14 MW and the capacity of phase 2 is 12 MW. Phase 1 started construction on 01-February-2023 and started operation on 08-May-2023. Eight sets of generators with capacity of 1.5 MW for each (12 MW in total) of phase 2 started construction on 15-October-2023 and operated in 17-March-2024.  It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 08-May-2023 to 07-May-2033), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 1,103,098 tCO2e, with the total emission reduction of 11,030,980 tCO2e.
vcs-5136:
Fujian Nan'an Shengda Aluminium Recycling Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) aims to produce aluminum products by reprocessing waste aluminum products (i. e., clean scraps produced by aluminum products enterprises). And replace the same aluminum products produced from the raw materials. The total production capacity is about 13,747 tons of aluminum product per year, among them, 14500 tons of aluminium scrap is utilised annually. The Project is located in Nan'an City, Fujian Province, China and is developed and operated by Fujian Nan'an City Shengda Aluminium Alloy Co., Ltd. 
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of aluminum was produced from raw materials; the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well.
The first crediting period of the project is from 30-Jan-2023 to 29-Jan-2030. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions are 59,410 tCO2e and the total estimated GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period are 415,870 tCO2e.
vcs-5137:
The Grand Katanga Reforestation Project is an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) grouped project that aims to restore large areas of degraded land through reforestation of native tree species, including enrichment planting and assisted natural regeneration in the Grand Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo). 
The project proponent, Carbon Ventures Africa (CVA), partners with rural communities that have long-term rights to substantial areas of degraded and deforested land that could benefit from reforestation. The project finances the re-establishment of long-term maintenance and protection of native Miombo woodlands by local communities. In parallel, the project finances complementary investments in the local communities including improved agriculture and the planting of fast-growing species for sustainable charcoal production, thereby addressing the two main causes of deforestation in the region.
The project achieves durable, high-integrity GHG removals through nature-based sequestering of carbon dioxide (CO2), resulting from the net biomass growth in successfully implemented reforestation areas, and establishment of vegetation on degraded forestlands, bare soils, and degraded agricultural lands. The project is also seeking the certification to Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) standards as a result of its positive impacts on climate change, local communities and biodiversity.
vcs-5138:
Wuhan Jiangxia Changshankou LFG Power Project Phase II (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project ocated at Changshankou Landfill, Jinkou Street, Jiangxia District, Wuhan City, Hubei province, People’s Republic of China.
The purpose of the Project is to collect LFG from Changshankou Landfill and utilize it for power generation. It includes LFG collection system, LFG pre-treatment system, flaring and electricity generation system. LFG collected will be used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CCPG.
vcs-5139:
The General Villegas Biogas project led by Maria Elena Group is placed in San Marcos, an establishment located in General Villegas, in Buenos Aires Province, Argentina. It consists of 2 biodigesters of 4,500 m3 each, with a production of 15,000 m³ per day. They are fed with swine manure from a farm managed on the establishment, in addition to waste from various agri-food industries, including the dairy, meat, agricultural and cereal industries. 
Prior to the project implementation, the effluents were treated in anaerobic lagoons, while the solid wastes were sent to different MSWDS around the project location. The MSWDS in Buenos Aires Province are considered unmanaged since they only left to decay the waste in deep piles at open air. 
In addition to the reduction of methane emissions is the generation of renewable energy. The plant has achieved a generation of 868 MWh, where approximately 12-13% is consumed internally. This energy consumed is enough to cover 100% of the plant's energy demand. In the future, it is planned to transfer 100% of the energy generated to the national grid and the plant's demand will be covered with energy from it.
Therefore, emission reductions are achieved by i) recovering the methane from the biogenic organic mixture co-digested in the anaerobic digesters and ii) renewable electricity generation. 
The estimated annual average of GHG emission reductions is 10,683 tCO2e/year, reaching a total of 74,782 tCO2e in the first seven years
vcs-514: Validation achieved to the CCB Standards Second Edition, Biodiversity Gold Level, on 27 February 2014. Gap validation to remove two farms from the project area and verification achieved to the CCB Standards Second Edition, Biodiversity Gold Level on 03 March 2017.  The project will establish rubber tree plantations in a project boundary of 2,366.16 hectares of degraded and degrading lands where the traditional use has been cattle grazing, which corresponds to eligible area. The species planted will be Hevea brasiliensis. Direct planting of H. brasiliensis in the project area began in 2007 and will continue through 2013. The real or effective planted area corresponds to 2,252.23 hectares which is given by planting density of natural rubber plantations.  This area excludes other vegetated areas within project boundary such as creeks, borders’ vegetation, and small spots of vegetation.
vcs-5140:
Bundelkhand, straddling between Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh in India, faces severe challenges  such as drought, land degradation, water scarcity, erratic rainfall, soil erosion, and unsustainable  practices, making it one of the most formidable regions in the country. The project area comprises a total 
of 8 districts; Chhatarpur, Hamirpur and Niwari districts in Madhya Pradesh and Chitrakoot, Jhansi, Lalitpur, Mahoba, and Tikamgarh in the state of Uttar Pradesh. The challenges in these districts and the Bundelkhand region are compounded by water stress, primarily caused by insufficient and erratic rainfall, 
high runoff rates, and poor soil water retention capacity, leading to declining soil fertility and productivity.

To tackle these challenges, the project proponent is dedicated to promoting enhanced Agriculture Land  Management (ALM) and improved agroforestry practices. These practices encompass a range of  interventions, including improved fertilizer management, cover cropping, crop rotation, enhanced water management, effective crop residue management, and incorporation of agroforestry plantations, among others.
vcs-5141:
Safe Drinking Water Programme in Punjab, Pakistan is a Grouped Project comprising multiple Project Activity Instances aimed at enhancing access to Safe Drinking Water (SDW) while minimizing greenhouse gas emissions. The Project seeks approval under the AMS-III.AV methodology, which specifically targets development of low greenhouse gas-emitting safe drinking water production systems.
Targeted locations are the place where community lacks enough access to safe drinking water due to the poor water and sewage system. Therefore, people widely choose to boil water with fossil fuel or non-renewable biomass as energy source for getting clean water, and the actions leads to emissions of GHG. Through the project activity, customary water boiling can be replaced with visiting to SDW distribution system included as this project’s instances. This will reduce the need for boiling water using fossil fuels or non-renewable biomass, thereby reducing GHG emissions.
The initial implementation of 802 facilities marks the starting action of the project, and additional instances can be introduced during the crediting period to expand the project's impact. This comprehensive approach ensure that a wide range of communities benefit from the Project’s implementation. With the capacity to meet the water demand of over 4,250,000 residents across Punjab, the Project stands as a significant step toward addressing the water crisis in the region. 
The operation of these water treatment facilities is projected to significantly reduce GHG emissions by average 438,893t/CO2e per year for total 10 years. Moreover, the Project brings about various other environmental, social and economic benefits which contributes the long-term improvement of living conditions for people in Pakistan.
vcs-5142:
Kuza Miti is an agroforestry project that aims to promote planting and growing trees in Kenya. ‘Kuza Miti’ is Swahili for 'growing trees'. This project aims to bring together into a single framework the Kenyan horticulture and agriculture communities, farmers and forestry organizations, in order to drive sustainable development. 
This initiative will improve and inspire sustainability in (and related to) agriculture and forestry, the planet, people, and society; in particular, to promote carbon sequestration and storage through agroforestry in an economically sustainable way.
Kuza Miti is a project also designed to support companies achieve carbon removal through nature-based solutions such as growing trees. This project is designed to sequester carbon in five different pools, by implementing afforestation and reforestation activities with native species and fruit trees, thereby contributing to the mitigation of climate change. This initiative holds the dual purpose of promoting local development and education in climate change mitigation actions. The project will start with two project instances but the scale of the project is national, with an ambitious target to plant more than tens of thousands of hectares to engage local communities to ensure sustainable development and financial inclusion. The selection of tree species includes native varieties, but some species being specifically chosen for fruit and nut production but never in monoculture.
The forest management will be of two types: 1) forest without timber harvesting but fruit harvesting will be considered as part of the management plan and 2) forest with harvesting practices to generate a new source of income from biofuel or timber.
vcs-5143: In order to reduce the climate change impact of the landfilling operation and develop a municipal solid waste management system that is environment friendly and sustainable, Karaganda Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is being implemented by LLP GorKomTrans of the Karaganda city. The project activity includes capture and utilization of landfill gas.
vcs-5144:
Shandong Dezhou ALM Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located in Pingyuan County, Dezhou City, Shandong Province, China. The goal of the project is to enhance the photosynthesis of plants through the use of Dunfenggui products, thereby increasing mesophyll conductance and root secretions. These measures will contribute to increased crop yield and improved soil organic matter content.
The project is implemented by Fujian Dunfeng Carbon Sink Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Project Proponent) and covers an area of 22,333 hectares. The crop rotation system consists of winter wheat and summer corn.
Pingyuan County is situated between 36°–36.5° N latitude and 116°–117° E longitude, with a total area of 1,047 square kilometers. The Project aims to prevent soil degradation by promoting conservation farming practices, such as increasing the use of Dunfenggui, reducing chemical fertilizers, and substituting with organic fertilizers across the project area.
The Project is expected to achieve an average annual reduction/removal of 866,430 tCO₂e, amounting to a total of 17,328,600 tCO₂e over the initial 20-year crediting period. During the current monitoring period, annual average GHG reductions/removals reached 774,369 tCO₂e, with soil carbon sequestration contributing up to 35.68 tCO₂e per hectare.
vcs-5146: A 100MW Redstone concentrated solar thermal power (CSP) plant, which forms part of the South African Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer (REIPP) Procurement Program, is the first project financed CSP with molten salt central receiver project in the world and one of the largest investments in South Africa under the REIPP. It is located near Postmasburg in the Northern Cape Province of South Africa.
vcs-5147: The proposed grouped project is an afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation (ARR) initiative aimed at increasing vegetation cover by planting native tree species on agricultural fallow lands and/or degraded farmlands. The proposed project activity is a voluntary project activity being implemented by LTIMindtree. The project is grouped project activity with the geographic boundary of India. The first instance of the grouped project activity is implemented in 2128 ha distributed across 9 states, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Odisha, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka) of India. The second instance is expected to cover around 2000 ha in the above-mentioned states or in any other states of India.
vcs-5148: -	Project Tamba 20000, implemented by Hommes et Terre in close partnership with local villages, aims to restore 20,000 hectares of degraded land in the Sahelian region of Senegal. This initiative addresses soil degradation caused by drought and overexploitation between the 1960s and 1990s. Utilizing the innovative Vallerani system with the Delfino plough, the project creates microbasins to enhance soil fertility and water retention. Local communities, including women, actively participate in sowing native tree and herbaceous species, collecting seeds, and being involved towards sustainable land management program, supporting the permanence of the restored areas in the long term. Over 40 years, the Project activities are expected to generate 2,179,919 tCO2e of high-quality carbon removals, representing an average of 54,497 tCO2e per year, while delivering employment opportunities for local communities, especially women, as well as ecological benefits.
vcs-5149: Huangtupo CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Huangtupo coal mine which is a working coal mine for power generation, part of the power will be used for self-consumption of the Project and the rest will be supplied electricity to the coal mine where the Project is located for internal consumption. The Project is located in Huangtupo coal mine, Xiaolingdi village, Congziyu Town, Qinyuan County, Changzhi City, Shanxi Province, P.R.China. The Project Owner is Qinyuan County Hetong Comprehensive Energy Service Co., Ltd. Prior to the implementation of the project, Huangtupo coal mine was equipped with CMM extraction facilities and all extracted CMM was vented into the atmosphere directly. The electricity consumed at coal mines was imported from North China Power Grid (NCPG). The heat was provided by waste coal boilers. Baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. The Project aims to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved.
vcs-515: The project has been undertaken to harness the available wind power potential. The project has established 5 number of WTG aggregating to a total installed capacity of 5.6 MW. The project will generate approximately 13.47 million units of electricity per annum, which will be sold to the State Electricity Boards or wheeled for captive consumption. The project will help in greenhouse gas emission reduction by using renewable energy resource for generating power which otherwise would have been generated using non- renewable, carbon intensive fuel common in the grid. The project is a green field project aimed at utilising wind energy to produce power.  The implementation of project will achieve approximately 12,729 tCO2e emission reduction per annum by replacing grid based electricity which is predominately generated by fossil fuel based thermal power plant in Southern Grid.
vcs-5150:
The PGM and Battery Metals Project will implement Elemental technology for safe, environmentally friendly and cost efficient transportation, storage and recycling of spent Li-ion batteries and spent autocatalysts. The project is the result of Elemental R&D works within its newly established and equipped Research and Development Department to develop an efficient process to extract secondary metals and contribute to further enhance benefits from electro-mobility. Secondary metals are intended for re-use in the production of Li-Ion batteries, autocatalysts, tools but also treated as a commodity for investment purposes.  
The PGM facility is about to be completed (the smelting unit is expected to be in operation by end of January 2024) and will ensure the recovery of metals of strategic importance for the European economy (e.g. cobalt, lithium, nickel, platinum group metals) from waste Li-Ion batteries and spent autocatalysts. Elemental will deploy various patented technologies for transporting, sorting of batteries, their discharge (with and without recovery of residual energy), mechanical processing with separation of black mass, electrolyte, metals and light fraction (plastics and paper). Elemental technology also allows recovering alloys containing platinum group metals in pyrometallurgical processes. Finally, processes for refining secondary metals or their compounds from intermediates obtained from the processing of Li-Ion batteries (black mass) and catalysts (i.e. from alloy of collector metal and PGM).
vcs-5151:
This project involves reforestation efforts on the land surrounding Mount Pinatubo,
aiming to regenerate the forest. Mount Pinatubo is a mountain where the largest
eruption of the 20th century occurred, resulting in the destruction of forests. The goal
is to restore the forests lost during the eruption through reforestation activities.
According to historical mapping, these lands were devastated by past eruptions of
Mount Pinatubo, resulting in the loss of forests. Although there have been no human
activities (such as agriculture or reforestation) in the area over the past decade,
natural vegetation regeneration has also not occurred.
Located on the western side of Luzon Island in the Philippines, Mount Pinatubo sits on
the boundaries of the provinces of Zambales, Bataan, and Pampanga.
During the eruption, CO2 absorbed by the forests was released into the atmosphere
as the forests burned. Through current soil analysis and ecosystem research, the
project aims to identify the optimal species for reforestation activities to sequester
CO2 from the atmosphere into the forests and soil.
The land is inhabited by indigenous people called the Aeta, for whom the forest is
vital. However, due to funding constraints, large-scale reforestation activities have
not been feasible. This project is conducted with the expectation of generating
revenue through carbon credits.
The reforestation activities are scheduled to commence in 2024, and will continue for
ten years depending on weather conditions. The project is anticipated to generate
greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions equivalent to 13,588,168tons of CO2e
over a period of 20 years, representing an average annual GHG emission reduction
of 679,408 tons of CO2e.
vcs-5152: VCS project of Leifeng water purification plant sewage treatment system is located in Changsha City, Hunan Province, China. The project owner is Hunan Xiangxin Bishuiyuan Environmental Technology Co.,Ltd. The whole aerobic process includes pre-treatment process,secondary biological treatment process, tertiary deep treatment process and sludge treatment process, with an maximum design influent flow of 125,000 m3/d,the influent and effluent COD concentration are 300 mg/L and 30 mg/L, separately.
vcs-5153: The Kafue-Zambezi Community Forest Project (KZCFP) is a potentially large-scale grouped REDD+ initiative set to be implemented in the watersheds of two of Zambia’s most important rivers: The Zambezi River and the Kafue River in Central-West Zambia. First project activity instances are located in the Western Province, with the project area forming a significant part of the Kavango-Zambezi (KAZA) Trans-Frontier Conservation Area (KAZA TFCA) on the Zambian side. The targeted area for phase one is projected to cover 1.95 million hectares, dependent on community willingness to participate and Government approvals. Implementation will be carried out in collaboration with traditional authorities and the Government of the Republic of Zambia. The project aims to reduce emissions through the implementation of the following mitigation activities: engagement and capacity building with key government and community stakeholders, promotion of alternative and sustainable livelihood activities, direct conservation support as well as performance-based payments to community stakeholders delivered through local institutions.
vcs-5155:
The proposed VCS IALM (Improved Agricultural Land Management) project activity aims at developing a carbon sequestration project in the context of Organic farming adoption and certification by Qmark Foundation for Sustainable Livelihood Development (herein referred as Qmark Foundation) and it is also eliminating the dependency on chemical fertilizers and pesticides by replacing those with environment-friendly organic-based soil amendments. 
The Qmark Foundation is promoting the adoption and organic certification of Organic farming practices on approximately 1,00,000 ha in first project instance in Uttar Pradesh and other states in India. Further future instances will be added.
vcs-5158:
Diebu Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in
Diebu County, Gansu Province of China. The project is aimed to restore the local
degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management
practices, such as reseeding grass, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on
degraded pastures, and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term.
vcs-516: Chamoli Hydroelectric Power Pvt. Ltd has established a 5 MW (2 x 2.5MW) Debal small hydropower project Scheme at Debal Village, Narain Bagar Taluk in Chamoli District of Uttarakhand, India. The project activity utilizes the water flows of right bank of Kailaganga river just before its confluence with Pinder river at Debal. The Project activity supplies generated electricity to Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited (UPCL) grid. The Units of the project activity have been commissioned & started commercial operations from 21 July 2007
vcs-5160:
Fagnako's initiative in Madagascar aims to restore heavily degraded lands. The program begins with a 10,563-hectare plot in the Brickaville district, owned by local municipalities. The restoration effort is based on four technical components, developed in collaboration with herders, farmers, villages, and municipalities to achieve a holistic landscape approach.
The first component is a silvopastoral system centered around the Millettia Pinnata tree and various forage species. This will enhance the pasture for zebu herders, improving the sustainability and productivity of their grazing lands. The agroforestry component, which integrates trees and agricultural crops, ensures sustainable valorization of local farmers' lands. The third component focuses on wood energy by planting fast-growing tree species to meet local energy needs and reduce pressure on natural forests. The final component is the assistance in the natural regeneration of wooded areas, promoting the recovery of native vegetation.
Millettia Pinnata, naturally found in Madagascar, plays a crucial role in soil restoration due to its nitrogen-fixing properties. Additionally, its fruits can be used for biofuel production and animal feed, contributing to both environmental and economic benefits. 
The project's objectives include improving social infrastructure, such as schools and dispensaries, to enhance the well-being of local communities. It also aims to foster economic development in the region by creating sustainable livelihoods, combating soil degradation and biodiversity loss, and promoting renewable energy sources.
Overall, Fagnako's initiative addresses immediate environmental concerns but also lays the groundwork for long-term sustainable development in Madagascar. The project's success could serve as a model for similar restoration efforts in other eligible parts of the country, demonstrating the viability of integrated, community-focused approaches to land restoration and sustainable development.
vcs-5162: The Grouped Project ARR Serra Viva is a holistic model of climate, community, and biodiversity benefits aligned with national and global goals for reforestation and sustainable development. In addition to combating the climate crisis through the removal of atmospheric CO2, the project's activities promote the resilience of ecosystems and communities in the face of extreme weather events. Ecological restoration promotes the generation of employment and income, especially in rural communities, with the expectation of creating sustainable jobs throughout its implementation. The focus on the social and economic inclusion of vulnerable groups, such as smallholders and women, highlights the project's commitment to social equity and the continuous improvement of the living conditions of these populations. In the field of biodiversity, the project aims to create and restore essential habitats for the survival of animal and plant species, connecting habitat fragments in ecological corridors and increasing genetic diversity, which is crucial for the conservation of biodiversity in the Atlantic Forest. The project achieves 10 Sustainable Development Goals, reflecting its commitment to an integration of environmental, social, and governance objectives. With the objective of reforesting 48,000 hectares, the Grouped Project ARR Serra Viva offers a practical and scalable approach to addressing the challenges of climate change while promoting a beneficial socio-economic impact for local communities.
vcs-5164: The Project seeks to develop an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) VCS grouped project across Latvia and Lithuania.
vcs-5165:
The project aims to reduce carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gas emissions by using pure electric vehicles to reduce fuel vehicles. The project activity is carried out by Suzhou Haiweidun Car Rental Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “Haiweidun”), an enterprise committed to providing new energy online ride-hailing services for Chinese drivers, promoting vehicle renters (drivers) to carry out online car hailing activities at a lower cost, increasing employment opportunities, and creating low-carbon travel experience for travelers.
The project promotes the electrification of online ride-hailing services through cooperation with Chinese mobile technology platform (such as DiDi Global Inc., Amap Software Co., Ltd.), thereby reducing carbon emissions and improving the sustainability of passenger transport. The project includes electric vehicles already leased by Haiweidun, which are charged by electricity supplied by regional power grids.
This project has not been applied in GS/CDM/CCER and other emission reduction mechanisms, and there is no problem of double calculation. The project vehicles are all owned by Haiweidun, Haiweidun provides rental services, including vehicle maintenance, repair, driver operations management services and more. The vehicle lessee (driver) all agree to the emission reduction agreement, so as to show that the vehicle lessee (driver) participating in the project activities gives up the right to distribute the carbon emission reduction benefits and avoid double calculation of emission reduction.
Between November 2022 and October 2032, a total of 4547 electric vehicles were used in Jiangsu and Zhejiang. Based on emission reduction calculation of applicable CDM methodology AMS III C “Emission reductions by electric and hybrid vehicles” Version 16.0, overall emission reduction of project activity will not increase from 60,000 tCO2e/year.
In 10 year crediting period project will generate approx 432383 tCO2e.
vcs-5166:
Bac Ninh Province Domestic Waste Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located at Bac Ninh Province , Vietnam. The Project is owned and implemented by Bac Ninh EU - Conch Venture new energy Co., Ltd. which is owned by China Conch Venture Holdings (HK) Limited .
The project is established for the purpose of treatment of municipal solid waste (“MSW”) with energy recovery and electricity generation and no heat recovered for thermal generation is involved. The project is designed to dispose of a daily average 300 tons of MSW through one incineration systems with the treatment capacity of 300 tons/d of MSW, matched with one set of 6 MW condensing turbine and one set of 6 MW turbo generators. The project will dispose of 109,500  tons of MSW every year.
vcs-5167: The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on rooftops in various districts of Tamil Nadu, India. The sole purpose of project activity is to install solar power plant for captive purpose and surplus generated electricity can be supplied to grid and further equivalent energy will be consumed from grid through net metering arrangement with state electricity board.
vcs-5169:
The Sembrando Futuro 2.0 project aims to restore native forests across the Central and Western Andes of Colombia. Designed as a grouped ARR project, its first instance focuses on restoring 555 hectares of degraded lands in the departments of Antioquia, Caldas, and Chocó, with a long-term goal of expanding within the region. Restoration areas span diverse Andean ecosystems—including tropical humid, premontane, low montane, and montane forests—located between 80 and more than 3,100 meters in altitude. These forests have undergone extensive degradation due to agricultural expansion, cattle ranching, and land-use pressures.
The project centers on the recovery of native forests, planting over 70 native species to accelerate ecological succession, improve forest structure, and strengthen connectivity between fragmented habitats. Restoration activities contribute to climate mitigation through increased carbon sequestration and enhanced ecosystem resilience.
Sembrando Futuro 2.0 creates substantial community benefits by generating jobs, strengthening local technical capacity, and improving livelihoods through training and equitable carbon revenue sharing. Participating landowners formalize their commitments through 40-year Conservation Agreements, ensuring long-term forest protection, maintenance responsibilities, and sustained community engagement.
The project promotes biodiversity conservation by restoring habitat within and around areas of high ecological importance and key wildlife corridors. At least eight IUCN-listed plant species are expected to benefit from reduced threats and habitat expansion.
Planting began in September 2023, with the first instance planned for completion in 2025. This initial instance is expected to remove 159,280 tCO₂e over 40 years. Sembrando Futuro 2.0 represents a long-term, scalable effort to restore Andean forest ecosystems, enhance biodiversity, support rural livelihoods, and contribute to national and global climate goals.
vcs-517: The project involves the construction and operation of first phase extension project, first phase technology improvement project and second phase technology improvement project in Changdao County, Yantai City, Shandong Province in China by Shandong Changdao Wind Power Co., Ltd. The total wind turbines of the project are 23 and the installed capacity of the project is 17.55MW.
vcs-5170:
The Supporting Ancestral Domains: Carbon Finance for Climate Action and Sustainable Development in the Mount Mantalingahan Protected Landscape project, led by Conservation International Philippines Foundation Inc. (CIP), is an initiative designed to leverage carbon finance for the dual purpose of climate mitigation and sustainable development. In particular, the project aims to generate and sell carbon credits to fund conservation and restoration activities in Southern Palawan, particularly benefiting Indigenous peoples and local communities (IPLCs).
The project employs a combination of forest conservation, restoration, and sustainable land-use practices. Key measures include:
•	Protecting existing forests to prevent deforestation and forest degradation.
•	Restoring degraded forest areas through reforestation and assisted natural regeneration.
•	Implementing community-based forest management and agroforestry systems.
•	Enhancing carbon stock through sustainable land use and management practices.
•	Using remote sensing and ground-based monitoring for accurate carbon stock assessment and biodiversity monitoring.
The project is located in Southern Palawan, encompassing five municipalities: Quezon, Jose Rizal, Bataraza, Brooke's Point, and Sofronio Española. The project area covers a total of 149,109 hectares, including the Mount Mantalingahan Protected Landscape (MMPL) and surrounding ancestral domains of the Indigenous Palaw’an communities.
Prior to the project, the area faced significant threats from deforestation and forest degradation due to unsustainable agricultural expansion, illegal logging, mining, and encroachment on ancestral lands. These activities led to substantial loss of forest cover, biodiversity, and carbon stocks, contributing to increased GHG emissions and reduced ecosystem services essential for the livelihoods of local communities.
vcs-5172:
Rainforest Builder Ltd is an integrated tropical forest restoration company founded in 2022 to pioneer tropical forest ecosystem restoration as a commercial undertaking, by combining the best restoration science with professional forestry industry practice to deliver ecosystem restoration at unprecedented quality and scale. Rainforest Builder’s projects aim to return degraded formerly forested lands to primary levels of biomass, biodiversity and structural complexity rapidly and resiliently, in partnership with a range of stakeholders.

The ARR VCS-CCB project is a grouped project that aims to restore approximately 100,000 ha in degraded Forest Reserves in Ghana.
