The project aims to achieve the sustainable restoration of highly degraded reserve areas through diversified mixed-species plantings that re-establish native flora and fauna, enhance ecological connectivity, and mitigate the adverse effects of deforestation. Central to this endeavour is the goal of ecosystem restoration, achieved with best-practice planting methods to maximise the survival and growth of indigenous species mixes, using species that are carefully selected to re-create natural forest structure. 

The Climate, Community, and Biodiversity goals of the project are to re-establish and protect natural forest landscapes, recovering threatened biodiversity in a globally important conservation hotspot, sequestering CO2 and improving the provision of ecosystem services including water regulation, nutrient cycling, and climate regulation. The project will provide long-term sustainable employment through reforestation and maintenance activities, promoting economic development and enhancing wellbeing in communities adjacent to project areas.
vcs-5173:
The primary objective of this project is to implement fuel-efficient Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) replacing inefficient traditional cookstoves at the household level. Through this initiative, we aim to promote the adoption of ICS among socially and geographically disadvantaged communities in Nepal, providing households with cleaner cooking solutions. By replacing traditional stoves with ICS, we seek to mitigate indoor air pollution, particularly benefiting women and children who often spend extended periods in kitchens.

The location of the project implementation are six remote municipalities in the Karnali (29.27°N 82.18°E) and Sudurpaschim (28°42′12″N 80°34′01″E) Provinces of Nepal. Prior to this project, the prevailing scenario involved the use of biomass in traditional inefficient cook stoves, contributing to high levels of indoor air pollution and posing significant health risks, particularly to women and children who spend considerable time in the kitchen. These traditional inefficient cook stoves produce a higher level of carbon dioxide which is responsible for climate change. ICS consume less firewood and substantially reduce the emission of carbon dioxide than in the traditional inefficient cookstoves.
vcs-5175: The Veracruz Mangroves for Life Project aims to restore the mangrove and floodplain forest ecosystems within the Alvarado Lagoon System (ALS) wetland in Veracruz State. Its objectives include enhancing the region's resilience to climate change, safeguarding biodiversity, and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions. The project seeks to reconcile people and its environment in the ALS through the restoration of environmental services in 2,037 ha of mangroves and flooded forest, that have been degraded in the past 20 years. This is a grouped project and through this restoration work, it will sequester aproximately 1,2 million tons CO2eq in 20 years, directly support the livelihoods of 400 families in the short term and indirectly support 7,000 people living in the area whose livelihoods depend on the quality of this ecosystem. The project proponent (Livelihoods) will implement the project together with the local communities and the Mexican ONG Pronatura Veracruz (PNV). Livelihoods and Pronatura Veracruz implement the 'Veracruz Mangroves for Life' which is a community initiative that aims to provide a new financing mechanism to contribute to the restoration of wetlands through the afforestation of mangroves, allowing communities benefit from the voluntary carbon market and thus have a better quality of life. Specifically, the project will work with landowners, smallholders, local village families and communities in the municipalities of Alvarado, Acula and Tlacotalpan to achieve the following outcomes after 20 years: 2,037 hectares of mangroves and flood forest restored. Degraded sites with previous mangroves and flood forest cover are restored through the establishment of “chinampas” technique using three main local mangrove species and up to 8 flood forest species, and, to rehabilitate the hydrologic function, blocked water channels are rehabilitated, and fire breaks will be established to protect the plantations.
vcs-5176:
The Sustainable Silvopastoral Producers of the Argentine Pampas aims to remove GHG through the implementation of an agroforestry project, contributing to climate change mitigation while promoting positive ecosystem impacts. 
The grouped project area covers 27,660,209 hectares in the southern provinces of Entre Ríos, Santa Fe, and Córdoba, and in the northern of Buenos Aires (the Argentine Pampa Ecoregion). This area includes grazing and agricultural lands with varying levels of degradation due to a long history of unsustainable use, which has caused a gradual disappearance of natural grasslands and the original vegetation cover. The project proposes integrating a low density of trees in farmland and rangeland to increase GHG removal, foster the creation of a new forest-industrial cluster, generate new employment opportunities, and enhance the provision of ecosystem services.
The project will primarily use eucalyptus species and intergeneric hybrids, including Eucalyptus grandis, camaldulensis, dunnii, viminalis, benthamii, and globulus. The main silvopastoral designs used will be paired row planting and alley cropping.
The first PAI is being developed in the departments of Suipacha and Carmen de Areco (Buenos Aires). A total of 1,555 hectares is expected to be planted, with an LTA of 156,083 tnCO2eq, implying a total GHG benefit of approximately 5203 tCO2e per year during 30 years.
The project proponent is Comercio y Desarrollo S.A., who is working in coordination with “Establecimientos La Negra S.A.,” creating synergy between a typically forestry company and a typically agricultural one. Additionally, this project is part of a Research and Development Agreement involving INTA, regional universities, and private companies. This agreement contributes to the successful development and implementation of project activities, ensuring that the SPS implemented have an innovative and sustainable approach at all stages of the project.
vcs-5177: The Lavushimanda Community Conservation Project aims to deliver transformative and sustainable positive impacts for communities and for conservation in an area of environmental importance linking two protected area clusters. The project will empower community-based forest governance institutions to reduce the drivers of deforestation and degradation and improve forest management practices; stimulate sustainable alternative livelihoods; and enhance the biodiversity index of the project area. It will also create a platform to bring together diverse stakeholders behind one vision of conservation-based green economic development, including communities, private landowners, the government, and the private sector.
vcs-518: Fujian Nanridao 16.15MW Wind Power Project is a grid connected renewable energy project. The objective of the project is to generate electricity from wind resources using advanced wind power generation technology and deliver to the East China Power Grid.
vcs-5180:
The Ganaderos y Bosques (GANBOS) Azuero project, Panama, is located within the province of Los Santos, which was hisorically covered by neotropical seasonally dry forest (NSDFs), however, the majority of these forests have been converted to pastures for livestock grazing, with very little primary dry forest remaining in the fragmented forest landscape. Due to this, diverse and endemic NSDF flora and fauna unique to the country’s Arco Seco (Dry Arc) now suffer from increasingly restricted natural ranges, causing reduced climate change resilience and greater risk of biodiversity loss (Garen et al., 2011). 

To recover these lost ecosystem services, improve agricultural productivity, increase carbon sequestration and protect NSDF biodiversity, project activities will encompass both native forest restoration and widespread adoption of rotational grazing on areas of pasture, with reforestation taking place on areas historically deforested for grazing. The project zone comprises a total zone of 397,556ha and within this the project will identify 20,000 ha of project area where interventions will occur. Reforestation will take place on 30% of the project area (6,000 ha), prioritising restoration of riparian corridors, and rotational grazing will be introduced on the remaining 70% of pasture (14,000 ha).

The three core project interventions are: (1) Native Ecosystem Restoration, (2) Rotational Grazing, and (3) The Community Development Strategy (CDS) and Sustainable Business and Livelihood Fund (SBLF). Together they aim to achieve holistic enhancement of Los Santos carbon sequestration, ecosystem health and biodiversity alongside agricultural productivity and sustainability. Intervention (3) will ensure the project’s environmental benefits have permanence by investing in solutions to existing drivers of degradation and that local stakeholders are the primary project beneficiaries, experiencing socio-economic gains as a result of the project activities.
vcs-5181: Silk Grass Farms is a vertically integrated B-certified agribusiness in Southern Belize, committed to innovating positive environmental and social impact at scale. The farm operates within a 27,500-acre tract of land in Stann Creek, Belize.  Approximately 90% of the land (24,700 acres) is pristine first-growth rainforest, protected in perpetuity by the Silk Grass Wildlife Preserve (SGWP). The remaining 10% of the property (approximately 3,000 acres) was previously cultivated for commercial agriculture using conventional farming methods that eroded the topsoil and decreased biodiversity. Maintaining SGWP is critical to the survival of many species and to protecting the natural ecological processes that keep the landscape healthy. The preserve sits at the northeastern edge of the Chiquibul Maya Mountain Massif, which is among the most intact tropical forests north of the Amazon and accounts for 22.2% of the land mass of Belize. Silk Grass Farms is working alongside expert consultants to develop an Avoided Planned Deforestation project to protect 13,000 acres of forest that would have been converted to agricultural lands in the absence of funding from a carbon project. Financial benefits generated through the project activities will be used to support the goals and operations of Silk Grass Wildlife Preserve.
vcs-5183:
Zhangye Improved Grassland Management Project Phase II (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Zhangye City, Gansu Province of China. The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by seeding grass and building fence on the degraded grassland, increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local development by introducing sustainable grazing and management of grassland.
Totally, 138,293.34 ha of degraded grassland have been managed scientifically by fence building and seeding of local high-quality forage. Besides, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area.
vcs-5184:
Working Trees is mobilizing the next generation of cattle ranching - where productive forests are integrated into pastures, rural communities prosper, and nature and agriculture thrive together. Our vision is to drive gigaton-scale carbon removal in partnership with farmers through the deployment of silvopasture - a regenerative agricultural practice that integrates trees with grazing livestock on the same land.
 
The Working Trees - Scaling Brazilian Silvopasture (WT-SBS) project advances this vision by enabling cattle producers to adopt silvopasture across degraded pasturelands in eight Brazilian states. Within our defined Grouped Project Area, there are almost 100 million hectares of pastureland potentially suitable for silvopasture adoption.
 
At the core of our model are the farmers. We support them through tailored technical assistance and financial incentives, helping them implement silvopasture systems customized to each farm, balancing economic returns from tropical hardwoods and non-timber forest product (NTFP)-generating species with the restoration of native biodiversity.
 
By 2030, we aim to plant over 1 million hectares of silvopasture, generating more than 100 million tons of CO₂e in lifetime removals (2.5 million Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) annually). WT-SBS is already underway, with over 700 hectares planted across eight farms.
 
A project of this scale mandates the use of multiple technologies across the value chain - from farmer engagement to carbon accounting. We leverage digital tools to optimize farmer origination, streamline enrollment, support long-term success in the field, and ensure highly accurate and auditable monitoring and reporting.
 
Our near-term goal is to reach 1 million hectares by 2030. Long-term, we aim to scale across millions of hectares - positioning Working Trees to catalyze the one of the largest deployments of natural climate solutions in the world - led by farmers, grounded in science, and built to scale.
vcs-5186:
The Quanzhou Canhua PET Recycling Project (hereafter referred to as the project) aims to produce PET flakes by recycling and processing post-consumer PET bottles, thereby replacing the equivalent PET products produced from raw materials. The project has a processing capacity of 102,000 tons of waste PET per year, resulting in an annual production capacity of approximately 90,000 tons of recycled polyester (PET) flakes. The project is located in the Pu’an Industrial Area, Quangang District, Quanzhou City, Fujian Province, P.R.C.
Prior to the project's implementation, the equivalent amount of PET flakes was produced using raw materials such as crude oil and natural gas. The project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of these raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption.
vcs-5187: Batéké Carbon Sink (BaCaSi) is an integrated landscape management project taking place in the Plateaux Province of the Republic of Congo, close to the city of Ngo, including planting and Assisted Natural Regeneration (ANR) activities. The Project proposes solutions to the local problem of ecosystem degradation by meeting the needs of local populations. The establishment of agroforestry plantation and plantation for timber purpose will (i) improve livelihoods of local populations in the long term, (ii) decrease pressure on ecosystems, and (iii) permanently increase the amount of carbon stored in the area.
vcs-5188:
The Methane Avoidance in Anaerobic Lagoons Grouped Project is designed by GHG Biotecnologia Ltda. The Grouped Project (GP) converts anaerobic treatment in deep lagoons into aerobic lagoons in Brazil by installing aerators and using biotechnology.
The projects to be included in this Grouped Project are methane avoidance projects where the anaerobic systems are replaced with biological aerobic systems, where the applied aeration rate, both from the aerator system and microorganisms, does not allow the methanogen process to occur within the lagoons, thus preventing methane from being released into the atmosphere.
vcs-519: Yichun Daqingshan Wind Power Project is a grid connected renewable energy project located in Heilongjiang Province, Northeast of China. The objective of the proposed project is to generate electricity using state-of-the-art wind power generation technology and to sell into China Northeast Power Grid. The proposed project will achieve CO2 emission reduction by replacing electricity generated by fossil fuel fired power plant connected to China Northeast Power Grid.
vcs-5191:
The project aims to adopt Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation activities in Oromia and Sidama regions that cover tropical mountain ecosystems of Ethiopia. The project activity includes plantation of native tree species that includes: Podocarpus Falcatus, Erythrina Brucei5 (endemic to Ethiopia), Acacia 
Albida, Hagenia Abyssinica, Morus Alba and Millettia Ferruginea. and highland bamboo Yushania Alpina.
The project will implement sustainable management practices in the project area to ensure the proper growth and maintenance of tree species. Initially, the project activities will cover 20 hectares and later expand to 12,120 hectares. Various native species will be planted to improve soil fertility and productivity 
and sequester carbon from the environment, ultimately reducing GHG emissions.
vcs-5192: The Mangrove Restoration and Conservation Project takes place in the national carbon and environmental transition strategy of the Republic of Djibouti. The Project aims to enhance carbon sequestration in Djibouti by conducting a country-wide restoration and conservation programme at seven degraded mangrove sites. Alongside the reforestation of 1,675 hectares (ha) of mangroves (Avicennia marina and Rhizophora spp.), the Project intends to carry out terrestrial afforestation, using nine native tree species, in 465 ha directly adjacent to the mangrove sites. In addition, the Project aims to protect existing mangroves from continuing deforestation and degradation, thus quantifying the avoided emissions from the conservation of yet undisturbed mangroves in Djibouti, currently covering approximately 670.6 ha.
vcs-5193:
The Mongolia Afforestation Project (phase I) (hereinafter referred to as the 'project activity')
is implemented in 21 provinces and the capital Ulaanbaatar of Mongolia, and the project
activity aims to increase vegetation coverage in the project area through afforestation.
The project activity covers an area of 15,203 ha, including the capital city of Ulaanbaatar
and 21 provinces, namely Arkhangai, Bayankhongor, Bayan-Ölgii, Bulgan, Darkhan-Uul,
Dornod, Dornogovi, Dundgobi, Govi-Altai, Govisümber, Khentii, Khovd, Khövsgöl, Orkhon,
Ömnögovi, Övörkhangai, Selenge, Sükhbaatar, Töv, Uvs, and Zavkhan provinces.
vcs-5194:
150 TPD Biodiesel Project by Chemenergy Biofuels(P) Limited (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located at Village Ban, Pahasu Chhtari Road, Tehsil Shikarpur, Distt. bulandshahr, State UP of India, within the Economic and Technological Development Zone in India. The project is constructed and operated by Chemenergy Biofuels(P) Limited and is designated to produce biodiesel with capacity of 150 TPD. 
The technology employed for biodiesel production is transesterification of oils (triglycerides) with alcohol which gives biodiesel. The boiler for producing biodiesel is rice husk fired having capacity of 1 TON and feedstock is waste oil.
vcs-5195: The Project establishes EV charging stations that allow for battery swapping i.e. exchanging discharged batteries for charged batteries. The users of EVs are able to change their batteries quickly, making it a fast and seamless process that separates charging from battery usage. The Project includes electric motorcycles and electric rickshaws which receive batteries through the swapping technology as a service from Battery Smart.
vcs-5196:
The clean cooking project involves the distribution of improved cookstoves (ICSs) among local communities based in some areas of Rwanda, where currently several households still rely on inefficient and pollutant traditional cooking techniques. The project aims to replace the traditional cooking mechanisms used by local people (i.e. three-stone fire or rudimental stoves) with ICSs that require less fuel and decrease the biomass combustion’s emissions, with a consequent reduction of health hazard coming from the indoor smoke pollution. The introduction of more efficient stoves will help to limit the demand for woody biomass, reducing the unsustainable use of forests and halting deforestation. The improved cookstoves’ deployment will also have a positive impact on women’ life, reducing the time they spend for collecting woody biomass and cooking the meals, giving them the possibility to invest their time in a more effective way.
Through the implementation of engagement and training processes dedicated to the local communities involved in the project, all the households receiving the ICS will be aware of the environmental improvements and the carbon finance benefit generated by their effective use of the stove.
This project will be developed in Rwanda and the area of implementation will be the eastern region of the country.
The first project instances will be around 40.000 cookstoves delivered to the local communities, with an annual average emission reductions close to 37.500 tCO2e.
vcs-5197:
The Reforestation through Biodiverse Agroforestry Systems in the Amazon (Roraima State) project proposed by Courageous Land (CL) is a grouped ARR project that will start with the establishment of 2,000 hectares of biodiverse agroforestry systems, in the first stage, with the final goal of 10,000 hectares, in private lands belonging to Courageous Land and their partners. This represents approximately 27.48 million trees and shrubs planted over the project's lifetime. The plantings will consist of a mix of native and locally adapted agroforestry-apt trees and shrub species. These agroforestry systems are designed based on “restoration” concepts, which means climate-resilient and sustainable, enhancing biodiversity and soil health while sequestering carbon.

The project has been designed following the rules and modalities of the VCS Standard and is using Methodology VM0047 for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation Projects version 1.0. In addition to the carbon benefits, the project will also provide significant benefits to the local environment and community, including providing habitat for threatened species, improving water quality, and increasing regional employment and landholder incomes. The land in the southern region of Roraima state is commonly degraded pastures used for low-intensity agricultural activities such as grazing. The absence of trees and poor soil health characterize these lands, resulting in minimal carbon sequestration and high vulnerability to degradation and deforestation.

At the moment of project registration, a total of 116 hectares has been acquired by CL, with 63.2 hectares of land eligible for the project, which make up the first instance of the grouped project, with the remaining land to be acquired or partnered with as the project evolves.
It is estimated to sequester 5,745,156.7 tonnes of carbon removals over the first 40 years with a mean of 143,628.9 tons of CO2 eq. annually without accounting for the buffer pool discount.
vcs-5199:
The Marmota EV Charging Offset Project (MEVCCOP), or the grouped project, is an initiative aimed at establishing electric vehicle (EV) charging networks across Canada and the USA. Developed by Marmota Solutions Inc., the “project proponent”, the grouped project partners with companies owning and/or operating EV charging systems for both light-duty and heavy-duty vehicles. The initiative establishes pre-approved standardized criteria for any project partner to join the grouped project and report project activity data.

Each project instance within the grouped project is associated with a distinct partner company. The project seeks to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by displacing emissions from both light-duty internal combustion engine vehicles (ICVs) and heavy-duty vehicles (trucks and buses) with electrically-powered versions of the same.  This includes both Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs) and Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) but excludes conventional hybrids.

The project boundary is Canada (excluding the province of British Columbia (BC)) and the USA (excluding the states of California (CA), Oregon (OR) and Washington (WA)).
 
GHG emission reductions are created by facilitating the transportation of people and/or freight via electrically-powered vehicles, charged from the electricity grid, in place of equivalent fossil fueled vehicles.
vcs-52: The purpose of this project activity is to utilize renewable biomass available in the region for thermal energy generation. The project activity will indirectly help reduce Brazilian deforestation rates, Brazil's main source of greenhouse gas emissions. The project activity consists of a fuel-switch at Nascente Ceramic, which produces structural ceramic devices like bricks, for the local market of Panorama and its surroundings in the state of São Paulo. The firewood used in the ceramic was supplied by the state of Mato Grosso do Sul which is located in the mid-eastern region of Brazil. The project activity consists of using sawdust and sugar cane bagasse to feed the kilns of the ceramic rather than wood from areas with non-sustainable forest management, which does not at all enrich biodiversity. If the ceramic company has harvest issues with these renewable biomasses or is lacking them, the company can also use elephant grass and peanut shells.
vcs-520: The purpose of the project, Enercon Wind Farm (Hindustan) Ltd 68.8MW wind power project in the Indian state of Karnataka, is to provide reliable renewable power to the Karnataka state electricity grid which is part of the Southern regional electricity grid. The project will lead to reduced greenhouse gas emissions because it displaces electricity from fossil fuel based electricity generation plants.
vcs-5200:
The goal of Together the Forest Awaeté REDD+ Project is to Avoid Unplanned Deforestation (AUD) of the Parakanã Indigenous Land in Pará, Brazil. Home of 1,500 indigenous people, the Parakanã Land encompasses 351,697.41 hectares of the Amazon Forest situated in the heart of the deforestation arc, with unparalleled biodiversity of flora and fauna.

Parakanã Land is located within the municipalities of Novo Repartimento and Itupiranga, both identified as high-priority areas for the deforestation prevention, monitoring, and control. Between 2009 and 2019, a total of 291,280 hectares were deforested. The Parakanã Land represents the largest contiguous forested area in the region, largely due to the proactive protection efforts of indigenous communities.

Indigenous People play a pivotal role in the conservation of the Amazon Forest. Their land use practices are often more holistic, combining traditional ways of life with modern perspectives on sustainable use. Within the Parakanã community, despite the vast richness of the forest, families grapple with a heightened degree of social vulnerability due to intense pressures from surrounding activities, such as livestock farming and illegal logging.

The Together for the Forest Program aims to rethink the socioeconomic development model of the Amazon region based on fostering bioeconomy value chains. It proposes a blended finance architecture, that finances several activities to prevent deforestation in the short term, while ensures long term permanence through social, infrastructure and local value chains development. The community played a significant role in prioritizing the value chains of bioeconomy products to be promoted and identifying key social priorities.

It is expected to avoid 69,134 hectares of deforestation, reducing an average of annual emission of 1,294,534 tCO2e, and a total of 51,781,360 tCO2e, over the project’s 40-year lifetime.
vcs-5202:
This ARR Project is located in Argentina, in the North-East of the province of Corrientes, in the department of Santo Tomé. It will be implemented on the Loma Verde establishment, a 2,516 ha property of which 1789 ha are the net planted plots, and around 587 ha are high environmental value protected areas.
Project activities will achieve the afforestation of that surface with non-native and native species in degraded land historically used for extensive cattle grazing. Trees will not be harvested, letting this plantation transition to a secondary forest in the long term.
Besides, we are addressing 9 SDG: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 13 and 15
vcs-5203:
Luoding BCCY New Power CO., Ltd. MSW biogas to electricity generation project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Luoding MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as the Luoding landfill site), in Kangren Village, Luoding City, Yunfu City, Guangdong Province, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Luoding BCCY New Energy CO., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the project owner)
The project has a total designed capacity 2MW (2*1MW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the China Southern Power Grid (CSPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period will be 86,250MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reductions of the project is 44,555tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 445,554tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period（from 28-Dec-2022 to 27-Dec-2032）
vcs-5205: The proposed agroforestry project is an afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation (ARR) initiative aimed to promote sustainable agriculture by planting native agroforestry species in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka states in India and it is being implemented by GKF Agroforestry Pvt. Ltd. The project includes planting of native and locally adapted agroforestry species in 11,000 hectares of land
vcs-5207: Mangrove Restoration Initiative by LTI Mindtree (LTIM) project is a collective effort aimed at restoring degraded mangrove habitat through afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation activities in the Indian states of West Bengal and Odisha. The project's objective is to restore degraded tidal wetlands by planting native mangrove species. The first instance of this grouped project is being implemented in the Sundarbans, West Bengal and Kendrapara district of Odisha State in India covering a total area of 156.45 hectares.
vcs-5208: This project involves the installation of energy efficient LED lighting replacing old inefficient lighting in industrial and commercial facilities.
vcs-5209:
BluSmart Mobility Holding Limited (here-in after BluSmart) is implementing electric taxi cars instead of fossil fuel powered cars. BluSmart Mobility Holding Ltd., is a UAE ride-sharing company, headquartered in Dubai, UAE. It was founded in 2024. As of 2024, the company's fleet of vehicles includes the Tesla model-3, Audi e-tron,etc. Main objective of company is to provide users an electric vehicle ride through app booking. Project activity is replacing fossil fuel (Petrol and Diesel) powered cars from baseline. The usage of electricity powered cars instead of fossil fuel powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven. This is proven in the respective ER calculations. Included Project vehicles are implemented by BluSmart those were taken  on lease. Based on the lease agreement carbon credit rights are owned by BluSmart, thus avoiding issues of double counting. Only those vehicles are counted where such an agreement has been signed.
The project includes electric cars produced by multiple brands. Currently Audi and Tesla cars are implemented in project activity but in future based on requirements other EV brands and models will be incorporated in project activity.
vcs-521: The purpose of the project activity is to generate electricity using hydro potential available in Gaganchukki branch of Cauvery River. The project is a run of the river scheme, utilizing a gradient of about 20 meters downstream of the existing 42 MW Shivasamudram hydroelectric project. The generated electricity will be exported to a grid system of Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited (KPTCL), a state government owned power Transmission Company.  The project involves construction of a diversion wall, canal intake, power canal, penstock, powerhouse, and power evacuation system and tailrace canal. The powerhouse consists of three turbine generator sets of capacity 8.25 MW each.
vcs-5210:
Panzhou County Chicken Farm Manure Composting Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) introduces the aerobic composting system to treat chicken manure from Good Luck Farm of the Panzhou County Layer Chicken Farming Project in Xuzhai village, Yangchang township, Panzhou county, Liupanshui city, Guizhou province, China, which is invested and owned by Guizhou Hanwei Egg Industry Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “the project proponent” or “the PP”).  The Good Luck Farm farms 900,000 laying chickens when fully operates. The project is designed to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting chicken manure.
Leaving all chicken manure to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons within the project boundary is the most likely baseline scenario in the absence of the project activity, in which case methane will be directly emitted to the atmosphere.
The project was put into operation on 05-January-2023. To collect and aerobically treat the chicken manure from the farm and produce organic fertilizer, the project introduces a mechanical manure collection and conveying system, a composting system, and a fertilizer packaging system. It is estimated that 34,492.5 tonnes of chicken manure will be treated every year, and the annual organic fertilizer production is 10,950 tonnes. The produced organic fertilizers will be sold to nearby farmer for soil application.
The project activity will reduce GHG emissions by introducing controllable microbial technology to aerobically treat chicken manure, replacing the direct methane emissions to the atmosphere from uncovered anaerobic lagoons in the baseline scenario. It is estimated that 35,865 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total emission reductions are 358,650 tCO2e during the 10-year fixed crediting period. During the first monitoring period from 05-Jan-2023 to 31-May-2024, the achieved emission reductions are 38,263 tCO2e.
vcs-5211: The project activity is a 12MW Waste to Energy Power Plant located at Village 2, Phu Son commune, Huong Thuy town, Thua Thien Hue province in Viet Nam. The plant utilizes the Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) as feedstock derived from the separation and sorting of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) excluding the recyclable or potentially hazardous materials from the waste stream. Generated electricity is supplied to the national grid through contractual agreement with the Viet Nam electricity corporation.
vcs-5212: The main purpose of the NL+ certification of Kalundborg CO2 Hub (NL+) project activity is to capture and store carbon dioxide (CO2) generated from the production of bioenergy at the Asnæs and Avedøre Bioenergy combined Heat and Power (CHP) plants in Denmark. The project aims to connect all parts of a carbon capture and storage (CCS) value chain to achieve durable carbon dioxide removals (>thousands of years permanence) and will be the first biomass energy carbon capture and storage (BECCS) project implemented under the CCS methodology developed by the CCS+ initiative and Verra.
vcs-5214: Pingjiang County Domestic Waste Harmless Landfill Site LFG Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Taxing Village, Wengjiang Town, Pingjiang County, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, P. R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Pingjiang Baichang New Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Pingjiang County Domestic Waste Harmless landfill site (hereafter referred to as Pingjiang landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
vcs-5218: VCS Development Project of Methane Emission Reduction in Dairy Farming in Yongchang Pasture (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in He Xibao Town, Yongchang County, Jinchang City, Gansu Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Yongchang New Hope Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd (hereinafter called the project owner).
vcs-522: The Chile:Lircay Run-Of-River Project consists of a run-of-river power plant of 19 MW installed capacity that utilizes the waters of the first section of the Maule Norte Bajo canal, in the San Clemente commune, Province of Talca, VII Region del Maule, Chile. It produces an average annual generation of 130 GWh. The project connects to the Central Interconnected System (SIC) and the energy is delivered to industrial and residential consumers in the area.
vcs-5220: This is a proposed project activity by WeAct Pty Ltd. that involves Biochar production using invasive biomass feedstock in the proposed location of South-Eastern part of Madagascar, mainly in Manakara & Mananjary regions. The project intends to address the issue of invasive biomass species in the region by converting such biomass into “Biochar” which will be utilized for soil applications in the local farming communities into their agricultural fields. The biochar being a carbon-rich charcoal-like substance will help improving the soil carbon, thereby help removing GHG emissions through biochar as a long-lived and persistent carbon sink. The project design is proposed with low-technology facility for biochar production and also to ensure sustainable production and application of biochar in the region. The project is currently at pre-implementation stage, yet to be started; and being designed to address sustainable development in the region while addressing the concern of climate change.
vcs-5221: India's agricultural landscape, shaped by smallholder farming and diverse crop cultivation using traditional methods, contributes approximately 14% of the country's gross greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Afforestation emerges as a pivotal strategy to address environmental challenges and foster resilient ecosystems amid issues such as deforestation, habitat loss, and climate change. It plays a crucial role in restoring degraded land, enhancing biodiversity, and mitigating the impacts of climate change. Cropcity Agro Carbons Private Limited (CAPL) leads an Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) project in Karnataka and Maharashtra states, partnering with KMS Private Limited for carbon credit advisory services. The initiative mobilizes farmers to cultivate fruit-bearing trees like Indian blackberry and Jackfruit on fallow agricultural land. Afforestation projects mitigate climate change by sequestering carbon dioxide through tree planting, contributing to greenhouse gas emission reductions.
vcs-5224:
Delta State, Nigeria, is undergoing a comprehensive pre-feasibility study for the restoration and conservation of its mangrove forest ecosystems, spearheaded by Eight Versa. The project employs a 'Carbon Mosaic' approach, integrating mangrove and seagrass restoration, sustainable farming, and biochar production. This multifaceted strategy aims to create a sustainable, community-centric environmental framework addressing both ecological and socio-economic challenges.
The project will implement the following measures:
•	Mangrove Restoration: Conservation of 270,000 hectares of existing mangroves and reforestation of an additional 20,000 hectares.
•	Seagrass Restoration: Conservation of 130,000 hectares of existing mangroves and reforestation of an additional 39,000 hectares.
•	Sustainable Farming: Introduction of sustainable agricultural practices to reduce environmental impact.
•	Biochar Production: Utilisation of agricultural waste and invasive Nipa palms to produce biochar, enhancing soil fertility and promoting environmental health.
The project is located in Delta State, Nigeria, covering extensive mangrove forest areas.
vcs-5225:
Traditional rice farming practices involve the continuous flooding of fields through the crop’s growing period. But when rice paddies are flooded, the soil environment favors methanogenesis. By changing the water management of rice paddies from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded, there is reduced anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the soil, leading to a decrease in methane emissions. This technique is called 'alternate wetting and drying' (AWD); it is a periodic drying and re-flooding irrigation scheduling approach in which the fields are allowed to dry for a few days before re-irrigation. This method reduces greenhouse gas emissions and irrigation water demand, without reducing crop yields.

The Upper Pampanga River Climate-Smart Rice Project is an initiative to transform conventionally flooded irrigated rice production to AWD to achieve emissions reductions, as well as community and biodiversity benefits. The Project will be implemented in Central Luzon in the Upper Pampanga River Integrated Irrigation Systems (UPRIIS) service area of the National Irrigation Administration (NIA), located approximately 150 km north of Manila, and spanning approximately 143,500 hectares over the provinces of Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, Pampanga, and Bulacan. The Project is expected to result in 1,952,264  tons of GHG emissions reductions (CO2-equivalent) over the initial 7-year crediting period.

Specific project interventions include:
1.	Training farmers on implementation of AWD which delivers appropriate knowledge in field preparation, irrigation, drainage, and use of fertilizer.
2.	Provision of incentives to farmers for participating in the AWD program through a benefit-sharing agreement.
3.	GHG monitoring, and monitoring for community and biodiversity benefits.
4.	Capacity-building with local stakeholders including the National Irrigation Administration (NIA), UPRIIS staff, Local Government staff, and local Irrigators Associations (IAs).
vcs-5227: The project activity aims to reduce reliance on chemical fertilizers by substituting them with organic soil amendments. Through practices such as mulching, compost integration, and vermicompost manure, the project seeks to enhance soil carbon sequestration and nutrient levels. This Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) initiative anticipates reducing greenhouse gas emissions by minimizing nitrous oxide release from synthetic chemical fertilizers by replacing them with environmentally friendly organic fertilizers.  The project aims to improve soil organic carbon levels and minimize methane emissions by managing post-harvest crop residue. The project supports smallholder farmers in transitioning to organic farming methods, improving their resilience to climate change while enhancing agricultural productivity.
vcs-5229: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Multilixo Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) at the Unidade de Tratamento e Gestão de Resíduos Sólidos (UTGR)  Jambeiro landfill (hereby termed “Jambeiro landfill”) through collection LFG and its destruction in 2 high temperature enclosed flares (with a maximum flow capacity of 1,500 Nm3/h each), utilization as gaseous fuel in set of 1 engine-generator set of an electricity generation infrastructure (with a total nameplate installed capacity of about 1.4 MW), and a LFG upgrading plant that produces biomethane with a flow of 2,500 Nm3/h.
vcs-523: The Projct activity is 25 MW Power Plant which is generating electricity by recovering waste heat from two 500 TPD Sponge Iron Kilns at the existing facility of Godawari Power and Ispat Limited. Two WHRB were set to capture the waste flue gases from Sponge Iron Kilns and produce power of 25 MW in the project activity. The power generated is used to meet the captive power requirement at the plant and excess power generated is exported to the State Grid. Thus the project helps in mitigating the Green House Gases which otherwise would have been generated from fossil fuel.
vcs-5230: The project tackles the critical water crisis by strategically deploying deep-well drilling to tap into natural underground aquifers. V Carbon Nuku Maimai REDD+ Project (the Nuku Maimai Project) locates in West Sepik (Sandaun) Province, the north-westernmost province of Papua New Guinea. Sandaun Province is comparatively poor. Income-earning opportunities are low across the province. A lack of road infrastructure hinders market access and commercial development in the province. The Nuku Maimai Project covers an area of about 102,779 ha of massive natural forests in a critical region of the threatened biodiversity hotspot of Papua New Guinea.
Some mitigation measures implemented by the Nuku Maimai Project to prevent planned deforestation will be implemented by stepping up local surveillance, mapping local deforestation patterns, forming collaborations with educational and research institutions, and offering advantages to neighbouring communities with the aim of minimizing deforestation by providing alternative income, education, and professional training.
The goal of the Nuku Maimai Project is to help conserving and protecting the natural rainforest within the Maimai Project Area from being cleared and converted as part of the Maimai Integrated Agro Forestry Development Plan. The Nuku Maimai Project’s operations at the Maimai Forest help to safeguard the forest from planned deforestation based on the mechanisms to finance and achieve the Social and Governance (SDG) goals established by the United Nations. 
The forests under the V Carbon Nuku Maimai REDD+ Project will be protected from clearance, and net GHG emission reductions or removals will be achieved.
vcs-5233:
The Gut&Bösel – Living Soils Initiative is an innovative venture aimed at transforming conventional agricultural practices into sustainable and resilient farming ecosystems in Germany. Gut&Bösel is an agricultural operation dedicated to addressing global challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and food security. Through a comprehensive suite of sustainable farming practices—including reduced-till farming, year-round soil cover, diverse crop rotations, on-farm compost production, intercropping, holistic grazing, and agroforestry — the project aims to enhance soil fertility, boost biodiversity, and regenerate entire ecosystems.
 
The Project targets the shortcomings of traditional agriculture in Germany, where extensive monoculture farming dominates the landscape. The heavy reliance on synthetic fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides, have led to significant soil degradation, biodiversity loss, and increased erosion. These methods prioritize short-term yields at the expense of long-term soil health, making farms increasingly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change and threatening their economic viability.
 
Through its implementation, the project aims to achieve significant greenhouse gas emission (GHG) reductions and carbon dioxide removals. These methods reduce soil disturbance, increase soil organic matter, and capture carbon through enhanced biomass growth. Over its lifetime, the project is expected to generate approximately 9,192,300 tCO2e in GHG reductions, equivalent to an annual average of 230,000 tCO2e.
 
The Gut&Bösel – Living Soils Initiative sets a new benchmark for sustainable agriculture in Germany, demonstrating the potential for a healthy, self-sustaining agroecosystem that balances soil health, nutrient cycles, and biodiversity with productivity. This model serves as a crucial example of climate change mitigation and adaptation solutions, offering insights that are vital for farmers across Germany and Europe in the coming decades.
vcs-5234: The primary objective of the project is to increase the mangrove cover through plantation activities on State owned mangrove habitats and create awareness on the importance of mangroves among the project stakeholders. vcs-5236: The agricultural land management (ALM) projects aim to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (CO2, CH4 and N2O) by avoiding the burning of residue and also offset the CO2 emissions by adopting improved ALM practices like residue incorporation & retention. vcs-5239:
Paddy fields are the most dominant anthropogenic sources of methane in the atmosphere (5-20% of the total emission from all anthropogenic sources). Anaerobic decomposition of organic material in flooded rice fields produces methane, which escapes the atmosphere primarily by transport through the rice plants. The annual CH4 emitted from a given rice area is a function of the number and duration of crops grown, water regimes before and during the cultivation period, and organic and inorganic soil amendments. Soil type, temperature, and rice cultivar also affect CH4 emissions. This CH4 emission-intensive cultivation method will be targeted by the proposed programme, which will involve implementing the technology/measures that result in reduced anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in rice cropping soils and, thus, reduced methane generation.
The project activity comprises of grouped projects of rice fields implementing the following methods:
a)	Drum Seeded Rice (DSR) with minimal tillage against transplanted rice cultivation 
b)	Alternate wetting and Drying Irrigation (AWDI) against conventional flood irrigation in rice

vcs-5240:
This complex nexus necessitates the estimation of carbon emissions from groundwater irrigation. Rajan et al. (2020) showed that groundwater irrigation emits 45.3–62.3 MMT of carbon annually (the data seems doubtful; we need to check), contributing 8–11% of India's total carbon emission. This analysis showed that deep tube wells have a huge carbon footprint, and their growing number is a serious environmental concern. Currently, our country accounts for one-fourth of the global groundwater extraction (i.e. 251 km3/year) and uses 90% of the abstracted groundwater for irrigation. Groundwater provides irrigation to around 40–45 million hectares of cultivated land, which is about 60% of the total irrigated area in the Country. Besides stressing the groundwater reserves, intensive groundwater pumping has resulted in higher energy consumption sourced from electricity or fossil fuels, resulting in higher carbon emissions. Judicious and efficient use of water through micro-irrigation can solve the twin problem of accelerated loss of groundwater and reduction of CO2 emissions. Therefore, there is a need to identify practices for efficient water management strategies for different crops and cropping systems and associated GHG emissions. With this background, a project is being proposed with the following specific objectives:
i.	To evaluate water and fertilizer savings under micro-irrigation in different agroecological regions of India.
ii.	To estimate GHG reduction associated with fertilizer and water saving through micro-irrigation.
vcs-5241:
Several horticultural crops are grown in India due to its wide variety of soil and climatic conditions. However, perennial horticultural crops have advantage over annuals as they generally need low inputs such as water, energy, etc., and have high productivity values. Fruit tree-based systems can contribute to carbon sequestration and play an important part in the carbon cycle of terrestrial ecosystems. Because of their propensity to function as carbon sinks and better adaptation to frequent weather aberrations compared with annual crops, fruit tree systems are receiving more attention in recent years and farmers are willing to adopt such systems. Fruit trees such as cashew, mango, guava etc. are reported to have similar carbon sink capacity as forest trees. This capability arises from a variety of factors, including tree lifespan, year-round activity in maintaining living roots, deeper and more widespread root systems; high leaf area index and delayed leaf turnover. Studies from ICCAR-IIHR have indicated that the country as a whole has sequestered 285.005 mt of carbon in its mango orchards.
The carbon sequestration potential of different horticultural cropping systems ranked in the order of mango > cashew > rose > vegetable > medicinal and aromatic plants, and addition of more residues in perennial systems to soil records less emission of CO2 than annual crops. As a consequence, perennial horticulture-based systems provide economic gain through carbon credits. Further, enhancement of carbon sequestration in perennial systems can be attained by improving soil health and through better carbon management strategies.
vcs-5242:
This agricultural land management (ALM) projects aims to reduce the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission and removals CO2 resulting from the adoption of improved ALM practices. The project involves adoption of natural farming that is compatible with regenerative agriculture and has a particular focus on increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage. This will involve management practices that maintain or enhance SOC affect soil quality and may favour the capacity of soils to sequester further organic carbon. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of these measures depends upon both the soil characteristics and the current SOC content. The Projects introduce or implement one or more new changes to pre-existing ALM practices which:
a) Improve organic fertilizer management;
b) Improve water/irrigation management;
c) Reduce tillage/improve residue management; 
d) Improve crop planting and harvesting (e.g., improved agroforestry, mix cropping, crop rotations, cover crops); and/or
The project is initiated in Gujarat and it is today defined as having seven universal principles that can work in different contexts:
•	Soil to be covered with crops for all 365 days in a year
•	Minimal disturbance of soil (zero or minimum tillage)
•	Use of indigenous seed
•	Diverse crops and trees 
•	Integrate animals into farming
•	Increase organic residues on the soil (Mulching)
•	Pest and disease management through botanical extracts
vcs-5243:
The study proposes to prepare biochar from waste material generated in Kulagar (coconut fronds, leaves, coconut and areca nut peelings and husk) using low-cost pyrolysis kilns placed at various locations in these systems. Contributions towards biochar preparation by individual stakeholders (in the biological waste material mode) will be quantified for carbon credits. Biochar (syn. black carbon) acts as a soil conditioner by improving the physical (e.g., bulk density, aggregation, water retention), chemical (e.g., cation exchange capacity), and biochemical (e.g., microbial activity, nutrient recycling) properties of soils, thereby enhancing plant growth. Using biochar as an additional co-benefit in agricultural systems improves soil quality and crop yields and promotes soil carbon sequestration due to its long residence time. Biochar is a recalcitrant material with the inherent capacity to enhance the quality of soil and sequester carbon in the soil.
For the pilot study, a number of kulagars covering approximately 25 ha and 20 low-technology biochar conversion units will be taken up in the first phase, potentially converting approximately 17 t/ha/year of plant biomass and subsequently applied back into the soil. The total amount of carbon generated from the biomass and the quantity sequestered in the soil will be determined. Efforts will also be made to use the biochar in non-soil applications, like making briquettes for stoves.

The project has a crediting period of 7 years, renewable twice. The first instance of this grouped project is expected to remove an estimated 1061 tCO2e annually and 7427 tCO2e over 7 years.

This Agricultural Land Management (ALM) project aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (CO2, CH4, and N2O) resulting from conventional/pre-existing agricultural land management practices. The project involves the adoption of improved agricultural practices that are compatible with regenerative agriculture and has a particular focus on increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and GHG emission reduction. This will involve management practices that maintain or enhance SOC, affect soil quality, and may favour the capacity of soils to sequester further organic carbon. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of these measures depends upon both the soil characteristics and the current SOC content. The Projects introduce or implement one or more new changes to pre-existing ALM practices, which:
a) Improved fertilizer (organic or inorganic) management;
b) Reduce tillage/improve residue management; 
d) Improve crop planting and harvesting (e.g., improved crop rotations, cover crops)

The project was initiated in Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) and Ranjnandgaon (Chhattisgarh). It is today defined as having seven principles that can work in different contexts:
•	Reduced tillage 
•	Avoidance of crop residue burning 
•	Recycling crop residue through composting (vermicompost/windrow composting)

Kerry Group is launching the Improved Agriculture and Land Management Project as part of its wider Group sustainability strategy in agriculture in Ireland. Kerry Group is the world's leading taste and nutrition company, bringing technology leadership and sustainable growth to the food and beverage industries. The Project will deliver verified GHG reductions within Kerry’s supply chain network, containing 3000 farmers via the reduction and implementation of sustainable fertiliser practices.
The project implements Agricultural Land Management (ALM) project activities that reduce net nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from agricultural cropping systems by reducing and sustainable application of the nitrogen (N) fertiliser application rate compared to the business as usual (BAU) scenario. During the project crediting period, the Project will adhere to ‘Best Management Practices’ (BMPs) as they relate to applying synthetic and organic N fertiliser at the project sites as required. These BMPs relate to N fertiliser formulation (or N content of organic additions), dates, and application methods.
The project will target the reduction of GHG emissions from nitrogen fertiliser applications (urea and calcium ammonium nitrate). The project activity owners (or project instance sites) are 3000 Kerry farmers that are currently supplying KERRY with dairy products for milk production in 7 counties located south-west of Ireland, operating on a total of 177,000 ha of land.

The PV installations provide a clean, renewable source of electricity and enhance the country’s energy security by reducing its reliance on emission-intensive grid-electricity, primarily supplied by Eskom, the national utility. vcs-5271:
The Zambruss REDD+ project is designed to tackle the root causes of deforestation, primarily driven by subsistence swidden agriculture and small-scale commercial charcoal production, through a multifaceted approach. It involves the implementation of a mix of disincentives as well as conditional and unconditional incentives. The project encompasses an area spanning 113,260 hectares, within the Kazungula district, located in Zambia's Southern Province, specifically falling within the territorial jurisdiction of the Musokotwane Chiefdom. 

The project aims to reduce GHG emissions related to deforestation, over approximately 113,260 ha. Over the life of the project, we aim to diversify the income of local communities. Currently, small and medium-scale conservation areas have little investment capacity and low or no income, a situation that can influence deforestation and forest degradation, thus generating loss or reduction of carbon stocks. Zambruss will make use of technical and financial tools available for conservation to generate greater benefits and create a diversified portfolio of activities, with the objective of creating a sustainable model for conservation. Specifically, the project's primary objective is to empower rural community members by providing them with opportunities to cultivate alternative livelihoods. This is achieved through the establishment of both an apiary and a commercial tree nursery. It is worth noting that the Mopane and Miombo forest types prevalent in this region, while exhibiting notable endemic species diversity for a sub-tropical semi-arid zone, do not possess high carbon density due to prevailing arid conditions and frequent occurrences of wildfires. The project is expected to yield an estimated average of 96,459 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions reduction per year, as assessed ex ante. The project is scheduled to run 40 years from 2023 - 2062.
vcs-5272: The project combines solar, wind and battery storage technologies to offer dispatchable and reliable power to the national electrical grid. vcs-5273:
Bosques Cautin is a medium sized forestry company in Chile, operating managed planted forests with the aim of supplying primary forest products in the domestic and international markets. Now the company is expanding the scope of its operations to include social, environmental and particularly climate change variables by transforming part of its commercial stands in protected forest to enhance carbon sinks.
This is a grouped project whose development encompasses simultaneously the application of the CCB Version 3.0 Standard and the VCS Version 4.6 Standard, VM0010 Methodology; Sectoral scope 14: AFOLU; Project category: IFM; Project activity type: Conversion of Logged to Protected Forest Project. The project is developed in 8,078 acres of planted forests made up by Eucalyptus globulus, Eucalyptus nitens and Radiata pine stands. The project will be developed in two stages, in Stage 1; 3,647 acres will be incorporated to the project and in Stage 2; 4,431 acres where IFM practices are expected to occur as a result of project activities.
The project is expected to capture over 6.5 million tCO2e when fully implemented. A preliminary estimate of the annual average and total reductions and removals are for Stage 1 of 3,158,040 tCO2e in a 40 years period with an average annual reduction of 78,951 tCO2e.
From the social point of view, it will impact nearly 200 community members for whom their livelihood will be improved with better education, improved connectivity and small business opportunities. From the environmental perspective, positive change in biodiversity is expected as improved conservation of high value conservation areas and in a buffer, area made up by native forests of 3,867 acres.
The company business as usual activities in the remainder of the forest estate will continue and will assure its permanence. The provisional additionality analysis demonstrates that the proposed project activity is economically (or financially) less attractive than the current land use.

vcs-5275: The project, led by SKS Coachbuilders Sdn. Bhd., focuses on advancing sustainable urban mobility in Kuala Lumpur by replacing traditional diesel-powered buses with locally assembled electric buses (e-buses). This initiative supports Malaysia's goals to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and improve air quality. As of 2022, e-buses accounted for only 0.24% of the total 42,081 buses in Malaysia, highlighting the dominance of fossil fuel-powered vehicles due to infrastructure challenges. Through the SKS Go Green initiative, launched in collaboration with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), e-buses will be leased to replace fossil fuel-driven buses for the GoKL City Bus service, which provides free transportation to the public. By deploying e-buses that emit zero tailpipe emissions, the project significantly reduces GHG emissions and improves air quality in urban areas. It also generates employment opportunities in manufacturing, quality control, maintenance, and project management, while enhancing local technological expertise in electric vehicle maintenance. This project not only contributes to environmental sustainability but also supports economic development and skill advancement, aligning with Malaysia's broader goals for sustainable urban development and a low-carbon future.
vcs-5276: This project will take place on farms primarily in the Kasungu District of Malawi. All the involved farms are managed (and owned or leased) by Press Agriculture Limited (PAL). The purpose of this project will be primarily to increase soil-based carbon sequestration, without decreasing the productivity of the involved farmland. The PAL farms will introduce the following interventions to meet these goals: improving agroforestry (and crop planting) through the planting of Msangu trees (either as boundary trees or on fallow land) and the establishment of a liaison to support all the farms involved in this project.
