The Seram Climate and Conservation (SERCOVA) project is an Improved Forest Management (IFM) project that converts logging activities into protected forest activities. SERCOVA is being implemented on a concession area under a forestry license holds by a company named PT Strata Pacific. 
The total size of PT Strata Pacific concession is 73,365 ha, consisting of a total 5,880 ha for protection area, 2,009 for non-effective area, and 66,076 ha for the effective area (i.e. Primary Forest, Secondary Forest, and Non-Forest). The eligible area for Improved Forest Management (IFM) is 56,189 (i.e. Primary Forest and Secondary Forest). The overall methodology for calculating emissions and removals/reductions is using the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VM0010 methodology for IFM. This methodology is applicable because the project activity includes planned timber harvest, and under the project scenario, forest use is limited to activities that do not result in commercial timber harvest or forest degradation. The selected carbon pools were the above ground biomass, deadwood, and harvested wood products. The above ground biomass estimation was following non-destructive sampling using 30 nested-sampling plots (size 0.25 ha each) along six 2-km transects. The number of plots has fulfilled the VCS requirement of 10% error and 95% confidence interval. 
The baseline scenario GHG emission removal and reduction were 50.4 million tCO2e (37 years) or 1,361,337 tCO2e per annum, while the project scenario GHG emission removal and reduction is estimated at 104,135.93 tCO2e per annum. Furthermore, the estimation of market leakage due to IFM LtPF activity was 272,267 tCO2e per annum. The estimated Non-Permanence Risk (NPR) emissions buffer was 175,856 tCO2e per annum. Hence, the potential Verified Carbon Units (VCU) was 37.6 million tCO2e over 37 years of project period, or 1,017,349 tCO2e per annum.
vcs-5286: The Saytek Plastic Recycling Facility, established by Saytek Medikal ve Plastik San. Tic. A.S., includes a plastic bottle recycling line fed with plastic waste material sourced from licensed material recovery facilities. The Project activity has been implemented in Gumusova Organized Industrial Site of Duzce Province in Turkiye. The Project aims to recycle plastic waste while reducing energy consumption that would otherwise be required to produce plastic products made of virgin inputs, and consequently causing greenhouse gases emissions (GHGs). In other words, compared to traditional plastic production methods, projects reduce energy consumption. This efficiency translates into a direct reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, aiding in the fight against climate change. The facility started its’ operation on 04-April-2023 which is implemented from the first invoice generated on the sales of recycled plastic flakes. The start date of the project is the date on which the project began generating GHG emission reductions, i.e. the date on which the project began producing the recycled plastic flakes. The calculation of GHG emission reductions by the project activity is limited to carbon dioxide (CO2) only and its primary source is reducing energy consumption that would otherwise be required for the production of plastic products made of virgin inputs, and consequently reducing greenhouse gases emissions (GHGs). Total emission reductions estimated in this crediting period 04 April 2023 to 03 April 2030 is 116,011 tCO2e for 7 years and yearly estimation is 16,573 tCO2e/year.
vcs-5287:
The V Carbon Nuku Nopan Project is located across Nuku, Aitape-Lumi, and Telefomin Districts of West Sepik Province. Initially planned for logging, the area is now under conservation agreements between Nopan Resources Limited and V Carbon Nopan (PNG) Limited, to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions by preventing deforestation and forest degradation. With a focus on forest preservation, the project's primary land use remains unchanged, barring grasslands earmarked for agroforestry initiatives. The project aims to maintain the forest's carbon storage capacity by helping the conservation of the project area and protecting the natural rainforest in the Nopan Forest Project Area from being cleared and converted as part of the Integrated Agro Forest Development Plan. This further contributes to biodiversity conservation, and support sustainable livelihoods for the approximately 9,000 individuals living in the project area.
By doing so, the project aligns with the Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use (AFOLU) initiatives, contributing to global climate change mitigation efforts while fostering local development and environmental stewardship. Some mitigation measures implemented by the V Carbon Nuku Nopan Project to prevent planned deforestation will be implemented by stepping up local surveillance, mapping local deforestation patterns, forming collaborations with educational and research institutions, and offering advantages to neighbouring communities with the aim of minimizing deforestation and addressing climate change by providing alternative income, education, and professional training, fostering long-term social and economic development support of the local communities.
vcs-5288: It is estimated that surface mines cover up to 600,000 hectares (~1.48 million acres) in the Greater Appalachia region. These mining sites are first deforested, then excavated to remove coal and mineral resources. Despite reclamation policies designed to ensure the restoration of mining areas, former mine lands often remain unforested. Mine lands remain unforested because of financial barriers and ecosystem degradation from mining activities that make effective reforestation challenging. However, Living Carbon is a carbon project developer uniquely positioned to restore forests to mine lands. Our project will achieve GHG emissions removals of CO2 through active reforestation of degraded mine lands that are incapable of naturally regenerating.
vcs-5289: This project unites 106 farmers, including landowners and tenants, organized under various producer associations across 158,000 hectares in Uruguay. Its primary aim is to promote Holistic Management (HM) and regenerative practices in livestock systems, facilitating soil organic carbon sequestration on properties primarily used for extensive livestock farming.
vcs-529: The project is a green-field rice husk based thermal energy generation system to produce steam. The project is owned and operated by Yihai Kerry (Jilin) Bio-cogeneration Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of Wilmar International Ltd.  The project proponent will purchase rice husks from the ‘Yihai Kerry (Jilin) Oils, Grains and Foodstuffs Industries Co., Ltd’ also the consumer of steam. No other co-firing is provided for.  The project comprises two boilers with installed capacity of 15 MT/hour each.
vcs-5290:
The project area is situated in Madre de Dios, a region in the southeastern Peruvian Amazon that suffers from the highest deforestation rates in the country. This region is under constant threat from unsustainable agricultural practices driven by local religious communities, migration pressures, and the expansion of livestock farming. To combat these challenges, the project adopts a dual approach:
- Strengthening protection measures through a robust control and surveillance system, which includes constructing lookout posts, conducting land, river, and aerial patrols, and collaborating with political authorities to enhance law enforcement.
- Promoting sustainable livelihoods by engaging neighboring communities in productive activities that offer alternative sources of income without the need to clear forested areas.
Through these efforts, the project aims to reduce projected deforestation and protect threatened Amazonian forest. In addition to preventing forest loss, the project seeks to improve the conservation of biodiversity, including medium-to-large mammals that are often targeted by illegal hunting and logging activities, as well as forestry fires and agricultural expansion.
The project also focuses on enhancing community well-being by offering alternative income sources, improving food security, and reducing the pressure on natural resources caused by neighboring communities. The involvement of local communities in project activities is essential, as it will help improve livelihoods while ensuring the sustainable management of the forest ecosystem.
By addressing both the social and environmental aspects, this project aims to create a long-term impact on forest conservation, biodiversity protection, and community development.
vcs-5291:
Sothys has purchased degraded lands in Santiago del Estero Province (Argentina) to conduct a Reforestation and Biodiversity Restoration program on 2,995 hectares eligible for ARR activities.
These lands have been degraded over the last several decades due to the expansion of commercial agriculture and cattle ranching

The sole goal is to restore an ecologically functional and biodiverse primary forest of the Arid Chaco subregion. This will be achieved by stablishing different tree species in mixed tree plantations and promoting natural regeneration, using different and native tree species.
vcs-5292: The proposed Grouped Project consists of biogas recovery projects in Indonesia that recover biogas resulting from anaerobic decay of organic matter in wastewater through introduction of an anaerobic treatment system for wastewater and/or sludge treatment with biogas recovery. Therefore, the proposed Grouped Project will reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from industrial facilities by capturing biogas generated in open wastewater treatment systems instead of allowing biogas to escape to the atmosphere.
vcs-5293:
The composting project for carbon mitigation
is being implemented by M/S ENVRO QUEEN PRIVATE LIMITED. The
project involves the installation of numerous compost pits across several villages in Dhar, Madhya
Pradesh, India. Its primary objective is to produce organic fertilizer from cow dung, which would
otherwise be left to decay at the project site in the absence of such an initiative. This
decomposition, if left unmanaged, would result in the emission of methane, a potent greenhouse
gas.
The project activity includes establishment of aerobic composting pits which entails conversion
of animal manure to organic fertilizer through aerobic composting methods by using decomposer.
The aerobic treatment of cow dung (which will be collected from farmers of nearby villages)
results in avoidance of methane (greenhouse gas) emitted in the pre-project baseline scenario
due to anaerobic decomposition of cow dung. Organic compost produced from the composting
process are used for application in agricultural activity, is likely to reduce the application of
chemical fertilizers and greenhouse gas associated with its productions. Using the manure from
the compost pits and by creating working opportunities in local area.
vcs-5294:
The goal for the Maya Forest Corridor REDD Project (“Project”), located approximately 37 km west of Belize City in the Belize and Cayo districts, is to protect and conserve the tropical lowland forest for long-term carbon storage and sequestration, conservation of biodiversity, and community resilience. 

The Project is a 11,856 ha property privately held on trust for people and Government of Belize by the Maya Forest Corridor Trust and is part of the larger Maya Forest Corridor (MFC) in Belize. The MFC is comprised of approximately 37,858 ha of privately-owned lowland forests and savanna in central Belize. The MFC provides the last critical link to Belize’s two largest intact forest blocks: the privately managed northern forest block and the largely publicly owned Maya Mountain Massif in southern Belize. The MFC is part of the larger Selva Maya connecting forests across Belize, Mexico, and Guatemala

The property was under tangible threat of legal conversion from forest to agriculture. To preserve the forest within the project area, the property was purchased and transferred to the Maya Forest Corridor Trust (MFCT) in 2021. The explicit objectives for the Project are to use carbon financing to: 1) avoid the agricultural conversion of the property to preserve its role in the larger Maya Forest Corridor; 2) preserve and conserve the forests on the property to avoid GHG emissions, maintain carbon stocks, and carbon sequestration; and 3) preserve the property to maintain the native floral and faunal biodiversity.

The primary methods employed to achieve the desired result are purchase of the property and transfer to the MFCT, management of the property by the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS), including implementing robust patrols of the property by trained local rangers to prevent illegal hunting as well as detect, mitigate, and control of wildfires. In addition, trained field ecologists from WCS and partners will monitor, and manage native biodiversity.
vcs-5295:
The Agroforestry Novo Horizonte REDD+ AUD Project is located in the Baixo Amazonas mesoregion, within the municipality of Prainha, Pará, an area vulnerable to degradation known as the Arc of Deforestation. Deforestation in this region has been primarily driven by cattle ranching, agricultural expansion, logging, and land speculation. The project, currently in the continuous monitoring phase, began with the implementation of monitoring systems in October 2021 and community training programs since 2022, aiming to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and enhance carbon sequestration over its duration.
To achieve these objectives, the project adopts a multifaceted approach that includes satellite image monitoring, fire prevention strategies, and low-carbon agricultural techniques for the local community. Sustainable practices implemented include agroforestry systems, rotational grazing, and sustainable logging, all aimed at alleviating pressure on forested areas. Community education and stakeholder engagement are critical components, encouraging the adoption of production methods that minimize environmental impact.
Based on modeling and historical averages, it is estimated that the project will result in an average annual reduction of 79,648.32 tCO2e, covering 23,092.85 hectares of Amazon rainforest, totaling cumulative reductions of 477,889.92 tCO2e in the first crediting period (2021–2026). During the first monitoring period (2021–2024), the project already achieved an average annual reduction of 94,143.18 tCO2e, leading to a cumulative reduction of 376,572.70 tCO2e, with no emissions recorded from the project itself and no leakage, following Verra standards to ensure transparency and accountability.
vcs-5296: The project activity involves aerobic decomposition of the biodegradable organic content of the MSW through composting in Baidyabati city of Hooghly district in West Bengal. The project activity will be undertaken by Eastern Organic Fertilizer Pvt Ltd (EOFPL), to avoid methane emissions from anaerobic decomposition of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) materials. The MSW will be supplied and transported by the local Municipal Authority in Baidyabati namely Baidyabati Municipal Corporation at the receipt point of the composting facility from the MSW Supply Area. The MSW Supply Area refers to the area under the municipal jurisdiction of Baidyabati Municipality.
vcs-5297: The proposed grouped project is developed by Continuum Research and Development Private Limited and PersistentClimate India Private Limited. This grouped project includes installing, operating, and managing EV charging infrastructure through strategic collaboration with the public and private sectors to establish and promote a network of Electric Vehicle charging infrastructure and scale up the EV penetration in the host country. The project includes the deployment of EV charging infrastructure and the promotion of electric vehicles, with particular emphasis on renewable energy for EV charging. The project covers the geographical boundary of the host country of India. The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by encouraging the shift from conventional internal combustion engine vehicles (ICE-V) to electric vehicles, which have a lower carbon footprint, whereby the EV Charging infrastructure results in the avoidance of fossil fuel-powered vehicle usage and resulting in the reduction of the greenhouse gas emissions. The project aims to provide accessible, reliable, and efficient charging solutions, fostering a sustainable future through innovation and expanding the EV-charging network. The project also focuses on promoting renewable energy for the proportion of the total energy (electricity) used by the EV Charging stations.The EV Charging monitoring platform managed by Continuum Research provides real-time visibility into key performance indicators/metrics, empowering charge point operators(CPOs), Charge point manufacturers, and regulatory bodies (but not limited to) make data-driven decisions and drive continuous improvement in sustainability performance, by providing AI (Artificial Intelligence) driven customizable dashboards, actionable insights, and collaborative features, which are transparent, non-fungible and fraud-proof by utilizing blockchain technology specially developed for EV Charging Infrastructure.
vcs-5299: Agoro Carbon Brazil Program is a grouped VCS project implemented by Agoro Carbon Alliance. The program will implement a package of regenerative agricultural land management activities as prescribed in the VM0042 methodology. The implementation of these practices will lead to increases in carbon sequestration rates in the soil as well as a host of other co benefits. The main objective of the program is to provide the financial, agronomic and educational support needed for growers to adopt new farming practices that not only produce agricultural products in a sustainable and profitable way, but also have a positive impact on climate change.
vcs-53: The global warming issue has garnered special attention in the last few years. In Brazil, in contrast to industrialized countries, deforestation activities does more to cause global warming than the burning of fossil fuels.  The project activity consists of the fuel switch in Milenium Ceramic that produces structural ceramic devices like roof tiles. The plant maintains a temperature of 900°C and consumes about 30,000 m³ of native wood from Cerrado per year to feed the kilns, producing around 1,000,000 ceramic devices per month. This firewood used in the ceramic was supplied by the state of Tocantins, which is located in the north region of Brazil.
vcs-530: Zhumadian Zhongyuan Gas-Steam Combined Cycle Power Project in Henan China (hereafter refers to as  the  Project  or  the  proposed  project)  is  located  in  Zhumadian  City,  Henan  Province,  China.  The designed  installed  capacity  of  the  Project  is  2×377.2MW,  which  is  aimed  at  electricity  generation  of 2,640.4000GWh annually with 2,584.4235GWh electricity per year to be delivered to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG) via Henan Provincial grid that the Project is connected to. The Project will consume 522.62×106 Nm3 natural gas per year for power generation, without using other fuels.  The first set of the unit was put into testing operation in November 2006. The Central China Power Grid, under which the proposed project is covered, is dominated by coal-fired power plants.  The  electricity  generated  by  using  natural  gas  which  is  clean  energy  with  less  carbon content, in the  project  site,  can  displace  electricity  generated  by  coal-fired  thermal  power  plants  which would have been built otherwise. Thus the proposed project activity can reduce CO2 emissions accrued from the CCPG. The estimated annual GHG emission reductions are 858,165 tCO2e.
vcs-5300: The purpose of this project is to introduce and distribute electric two-wheelers, replacing fossil fuel-based (motor gasoline) vehicles in the transportation sector. This initiative is owned and implemented by TVS Motor Company Limited. Without this project, beneficiaries/users would continue using motor gasoline-powered two-wheelers, resulting in greenhouse gas emissions into the atmosphere.
vcs-5304:
Project Description:The Rivulis Climate Sustainable Orchards in the Iberian Peninsula (RCSO) grouped project aims to create a new sustainable farming approach for olive groves and tree and nut orchards in the Iberian Peninsula. The first instances of the project are in Portugal, we expect to add more instances in Portugal and Spain.
The three main goals of this project are as follows, first to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from farming by reducing on-farm energy consumption through the adoption of more efficient irrigation methods such as micro-irrigation coupled, when possible, with more efficient energy sources and by decreasing usage of synthetic fertilizers through the use of fertigation solutions and organic fertilizers, secondly, Increase carbon storage in soils through the implementation of soil conservation practices such as Cover crops and/or inter-crops, tillage reduction and incorporation of tree pruning residues in soils and lastly by increasing carbon storage in the woody biomass by the plantation of native olive groves and fruit, nuts and tree orchards.

The baseline conditions of our project are defined as  conventional row crops and intensive farming resulting in high greenhouse gas emissions from inefficient irrigation methods such as central pivots, intensive use of synthetic fertilizers, and limited focus on carbon sequestration in soil and soil health. This is due to extensive tillage; minimal incorporation of crop residues into the soil, limited adoption of cover crops and intercrops, and little to no woody biomass. 
 The project is led by Rivulis Climate, as part of a global initiative developed by Rivulis Pte. Ltd, a leader in irrigation solutions, that supports the agriculture transition to more sustainable farming practices. 
The project is developed according to VCS methodology - VM0042 Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management V2.0 - and falls under VCS Sectoral Scope 14, AFOLU.
vcs-5305:
The project aims to undertake afforestation across 11,452 hectares of degraded grasslands, using a mix of native species and eucalyptus trees, and to preserve the planted areas. The objective of the project is to build biodiversity corridors across the land that is primarily dominated by cattle grazing, provide economical alternative livelihoods to local populations in the sparsely-populated region, and provide a source of material for fencing (from thinning activities, not for commercial harvesting) for local use. At the time of the project’s listing process' start (October 2024), 20.5 hectares have been planted in the Potosí farm and constitute the initial activity instance for the project. 

The initial instance of the grouped project is located in the Primavera municipality, roughly halfway between Puerto Carreño, the capital of the Vichada Department, which is situated on Colombia's eastern border with Venezuela, and Villavicencio, a sizable city in the westernmost part of the Meta Department.

All project areas have historically been used for cattle grazing activities and rudimentary fire management practices, which have led to a continuous state of degradation, which is expected to continue.
The project is expected to remove 15,374 tCO2e from the atmosphere with this initial activity instance and an average annual sequestration of 512 tCO2e. Overall, the project will have a positive community impact, providing economic opportunities to residents (and non-residents ) in the area. It will bring skilled training to seasonal and year-round employees of the project partners.
vcs-5308:
Gashaka Gumti National Park (GGNP) is Nigeria’s largest national park at 6,731 square kilometers (670,000 ha) and is located in Adamawa and Taraba states along the international border with Cameroon. GGNP has been a national park since 1991 and is one of the most biodiverse locations in Africa due to its varied topography and habitats. Despite being a national park, GGNP has not received adequate support and significant portions of the park have been degraded by human activities including cattle crazing, farming, logging, poaching, and artisanal mining. Anthropogenic fires, used by cattle grazers to promote pasture growth and hunters to flush out game, have impacted large areas of the park and prevented forest regeneration. 

In 2017, African Nature Investors Foundation (ANI) signed a 30-year (indefinitely renewable) co-management agreement with the National Park Service allowing ANI to carry out financial, technical and management activities alongside NPS for GGNP, including the ability to employ and supervise additional park rangers. ANI is looking to establish an ARR carbon project (392,000 eligible ha within the 673,100-ha park) that protects the park and provides funding to further support its long-term conservation. Planned project activities are aimed at facilitating protection of the forests, thus promoting their natural regeneration and the restoration of ecosystem functions. The project will develop fire and grazing management plans that will allow forest regrowth in areas that would naturally regenerate if not for anthropogenic pressures, in addition to improving the law enforcement presence in the park to deter illegal activities and protect carbon stocks. ANI will carry out additional activities that support park conservation, improve community livelihoods (including providing alternatives to illegal activities), and minimize leakage.
vcs-5309: The project focuses on transforming coastal mudflats in Gujarat's Bharuch district into thriving mangrove habitats. Mangroves help lessen the effects of natural disasters like cyclones and tsunamis by shielding the shoreline from coastline erosion brought on by wind and ocean currents. They are one of the most important carbon sinks in coastal and intertidal regions and are the major producers of intertidal areas.
vcs-531: Jiwa small hydel project is a 1000 KW run - of - the river small hydro project developed by Chevron Hydel Pvt. Ltd. for electricity generation on Jiwa Khad, a tributary of river Sainj in the Beas Basin. The project uses the potential energy in the available head of water to run the Horizontal Axis Francis turbine (1 * 1000 KW) coupled to an AC synchronous generator for production of electricity.
vcs-5310:
Ankang Hanbin Landfill Gas Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project is located next to Yangpigou Landfill at Hanbin District, Ankang City, Shaanxi Province, People’s Republic of China. 
The purpose of the project is to collect LFG from Yangpigou Landfill and utilize it for power generation; a flare system destroys LFG when the power generators are out of operation or under maintenance . The project started construction in 2021. Three power generators of 1.067 MW each, which add up to 3.201 MW, have been installed, and they were put into operation on 03-April-2023.
The project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by the fossil-fuel-dominated NWCPG.
vcs-5311:
Dalian Wafangdian LFG Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as “the Project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project located at Loufang Village, Sun Street Office, Wafangdian City, Dalian City, Liaoning Province, China.
The purpose of the project is to capture and utilize landfill gas for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is supplied to Northeast Power Grid (NEPG). The new gas extraction and utilization systems have been installed by the project. Before the implementation of the project activity, the landfill gas that was captured and utilized by the project was emitted into the atmosphere directly. Equivalent electricity was provided by Northeast Power Grid (NEPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations. This is the scenario that existed prior to the implementation of the project activity and is also the baseline scenario.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by NEPG.
vcs-5312: The Oya Hybrid Project combines 155 MW of solar PV power, 86 MW of wind power, and a 128 MW battery energy storage, all within a single location. This greenfield development spans the Western and Northern Cape Provinces, between the towns of Ceres and Sutherland in South Africa.
vcs-5313: Lichuan City Domestic Waste Landfill Site Biogas Pollution Treatment and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in No.1 Group, Yangliu Community, Dongcheng Street Office, Lichuan City, Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Hubei Province, P. R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Lichuan City BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Lichuan city domestic waste landfill site (hereafter referred to as Lichuan landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
vcs-5314:
Shangluo Shangzhou District MSW Disposal Site Biogas Pollution Control and Comprehensive Utilization Project is located at Shangluo MSW treatment site, Longshan Village, Dazhaoyu Sub-district Office, Shangluo City, Shaanxi Province, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Shangluo BCCY New Power CO., Ltd.
The project started to construct on 21-Dec-2022.The project has a total designed capacity 1MW (2*0.5MW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Northwest China Power Grid (NCPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period from 23-Mar-2023 to 22-Mar-2033 will be 52,696MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions of the project is 32,121tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 321,210tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period from 23-Mar-2023 to 22-Mar-2033.
vcs-5315: The Ecobase IFM Project utilizes the Verra VM0003 methodology, version 1.3. The proposed project activities include extending the rotation age of even-aged stands and converting rotation stands into continuous cover forestry. The Project will include instances located in Norway, Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Ireland, the UK, Portugal, and Spain.
vcs-5316: The proposed project is a voluntary project activity undertaken by the project proponent. The project proponent is implementing the agroforestry project in cooperation with the implementation partner with the twin goal of enhancing the climate resilience of the agricultural systems & supporting the farmer's livelihood along with removing the atmospheric carbon dioxide. Together all the benefits to contribute toward enhancing the farmer's livelihood and mitigating the impact of climate change in the long term. Additionally, the Project activity will improve soil health, prevent land erosion, and enhance biodiversity, thereby improving the overall health of the ecosystem and ecosystem services of the project area. This initiative also aims to increase the climate resilience of the agriculture landscapes to both current and future climate vulnerabilities in the project area.
vcs-5317: The project activity is a grouped project which includes anaerobic bio digestion systems and biogas units of different capacities. Each project instances will utilize different types of organic waste generated from various source (ex: agriculture field, agro industries, dairy farms & gaushalas, food processing industries, hotels & restaurants etc.). The purpose of this grouped project is to support the development, installation and operation of biogas projects in different locations in India. The technology involved in this project activity is anaerobic digestion technology. The anaerobic decomposition in a continuous stir tank reactor. Anaerobic decomposition is a complex and natural process of degradation of a variety of intermediates into Methane, Carbon-dioxide, and other gases. The project instances will use latest anaerobic Digestion technology to convert biodegradable organic waste into biogas & compressed biogas. The project activities involved in this grouped project manufactures Biogas, Compressed Biogas (CBG) and Biofertilizer using different types of biodegradable wastes. The biowaste digester and Biogas/CBG production system to be installed in each project instances will be of different capacity. The anaerobic digestion is a waste management and renewable energy generation process in which microorganisms break down biodegradable organic waste in the absence of oxygen. Anaerobic digestion technology is considered as the clean & green process to make clean energy and organic content (OC) rich organic manure. to provide clean energy and thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions into the environment.
vcs-5318:
The Credits for Life ARR and IFM project focusses on supporting the livelihoods of and natural ecosystems protected by Cabruca Cacao Farmers in the Atlantic Forest of Bahia.

This new project builds on top of our work developing conservation credits for the existing ecosystem services provided by these farmers, with the ARR component following the VM0047 methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation of dilapidated and degenerating lands adjacent to the protected plots managed by the farmers. 50% of incomes from this project go towards supporting the farmers in transitioning to regenerative, shade-grown, cabruca farming which has significant benefits towards local biodiversity as well as production yields and farmer livelihoods.
vcs-5319: The clean cooking project involves the distribution of improved cookstoves (ICSs) among local communities based in Northern region of Sierra Leone, where currently several households still rely on inefficient and pollutant traditional cooking techniques. The project aims to replace the traditional cooking mechanisms used by local people (i.e. three-stone fire or rudimental stoves) with ICSs that require less fuel and decrease the biomass combustion’s emissions, with a consequent reduction of health hazard coming from the indoor smoke pollution. The introduction of more efficient stoves will help to limit the demand for woody biomass, reducing the unsustainable use of forests and halting deforestation that is progressing rapidly in the Country. The improved cookstoves’ deployment will also have a positive impact on women’ life, reducing the time they spend for collecting woody biomass and cooking the meals, giving them the possibility to invest their time in a more effective way. Through the implementation of engagement and training processes dedicated to the local communities involved in the project, all the households receiving the ICS will be aware of the environmental improvements and the carbon finance benefit generated by their effective use of the stove. The areas of implementation will be in the North region of the Country, specifically in the districts of Tonkolili, Moyamba and Bombalì. The first project instances will be around 120.000 cookstoves delivered to the local communities, with an annual average emission reductions close to 73,000 tCO2e
vcs-532: The project activity consists of installation of different Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) with the cumulative capacity of 4.85 MW, to produce electricity using wind energy generation technology. The electricity generated is export to the grid with the purpose of either selling it to the electricity board or for the use of their own captive consumption. The project activity is using environmentally clean and safe technology i.e. wind energy.
vcs-5320: The clean cooking project involves the distribution of improved cookstoves (ICSs) among local communities based in Southern region of Sierra Leone, where currently several households still rely on inefficient and pollutant traditional cooking techniques. The project aims to replace the traditional cooking mechanisms used by local people (i.e. three-stone fire or rudimental stoves) with ICSs that require less fuel and decrease the biomass combustion’s emissions, with a consequent reduction of health hazard coming from the indoor smoke pollution. The introduction of more efficient stoves will help to limit the demand for woody biomass, reducing the unsustainable use of forests and halting deforestation that is progressing rapidly in the Country. The improved cookstoves’ deployment will also have a positive impact on women’ life, reducing the time they spend for collecting woody biomass and cooking the meals, giving them the possibility to invest their time in a more effective way. Through the implementation of engagement and training processes dedicated to the local communities involved in the project, all the households receiving the ICS will be aware of the environmental improvements and the carbon finance benefit generated by their effective use of the stove. The areas of implementation will be the Southern region of the Country, specifically in the districts of Pujehun, Kenema and Kaliahun. The first project instances will be around 180.000 cookstoves delivered to the local communities, with an annual average emission reductions close to 155,000 tCO2e
vcs-5321:
The proposed project activity has the objective to capture, flare and generate electricity through the use of landfill gas (LFG)  produced in anaerobic conditions into the landfill called “Central de Tratamento e Destinação de Resíduos Três Rios” (hereinafter referred to as “CTDR Três Rios”) located in the municipality of Três Rios in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The landfill started the operation in July 2017, receiving solid waste (type Class II-A Inert and Class II-B Non-inert) .

The project activity results in greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction from the CTDR Três Rios through two ways:
i.	Burning CH4 in flares and/or group generators;
ii.	The amount of electricity generated in the project activity is dispatched to the Brazilian national grid, avoiding the dispatch of an equal amount of energy produced by fossil-fuelled thermal plants to that grid. The initiative avoids CO2 emissions and contributes to the regional and national sustainable development.

The project constructed an efficient capture, collection and flaring system to burn CH4 (a greenhouse gas), and this reduced odours and adverse environmental impacts. The flares are kept in operation due to LFG excess, periods when electricity is not be produced or other operational considerations. The LFG power plant has 2.11 MW installed capacity.

The LFG capture and collection systems and flaring station consists of a LFG pipeline grid and a flaring station, equipped with flares, centrifugal blowers, and all other supporting mechanical and electrical subsystems and appurtenances necessary to run the system. The power generation facility comprises of LFG engine generator sets of high-performance standards. The engine-generator sets are the primary equipment to combust the collected LFG once they are installed. A fraction of the collected LFG is diverted to flares, which is used to combust any gas in excess of the fuel demand for the engines, as well as a contingency backup.
vcs-5322: The proposed project activity is located in the Kachela village in Sanchor Tehsil of the Jalore district in Rajasthan. The biogas plant will use anaerobic digestion technology to convert primarily cow dung and bio-waste into bioCNG. Anaerobic digestion is a waste management and renewable energy generation process in which micro-organisms break down biodegradable organic waste in absence of oxygen. The project activity involves the establishment of biogas plant to generate energy out of primarily cow dung. Project may use other organic waste in small quantity available in nearby areas. Anaerobic digestion is the prominent technology used for degradation of biodegradable organic waste. Anaerobic Digestion (AD) is a biological process that happens naturally when bacteria breaks down organic matter in environments with little or no oxygen. It is effectively a controlled and enclosed version of the anaerobic breakdown of organic waste in disposal site or dumping yard which release methane. The biogas so generated shall be purified further and would be bottled as bio-CNG.
vcs-5323: The project entails the installation of a biogas power plant and an anaerobic wastewater treatment facility at the Rohul Sawit Industri palm oil mill factory in Riau, Indonesia. The factory produces palm oil, which is made from the fruits of oil palm trees. By capturing the biogas generated from the digestion of organic matter in the Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) and combusting it to produce electricity, the project is anticipated to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while preventing the direct release of methane into the atmosphere.
vcs-5324:
The Sembrando Futuro project is an initiative that promotes the ecological restoration and conservation of ecosystems such as tropical dry forests, and Andean forests. By restoring these ecosystems, the project supports biodiversity but also aligns with global climate change mitigation efforts.
Fundación Argos has designed a comprehensive intervention model based on achieving several components. These include contributing to sustainable development goals, driving the company towards carbon neutrality, and preserving the country's ecosystems. Restoration and conservation activities are made possible through conservation agreements with private landowners, which allow for reforestation and ecological rehabilitation.The project is expected to deliver significant climate benefits, with an average annual greenhouse gas removal of 11,673 tCO₂e and a total removal of 478,587 tCO₂e over the crediting period (40 years). These carbon reductions will contribute to Colombia's national efforts to address climate change and improve the sustainability of natural landscapes.
vcs-5325:
The Open Field Carbon Farming Project is a pioneering initiative designed to advance improved agricultural land management (IALM) practices across open-field cropping systems in diverse regions. With a strong focus on sustainable soil health, the project emphasizes Mycorrhizal Inoculation and Reduced Tillage as core strategies to enhance soil carbon sequestration and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Participating farmers—including both landowners and tenant operators—will implement one or more of the following regenerative practices to increase soil carbon levels and reduce emissions:

Soil Amendments or Seed Treatments: Improve nutrient uptake and crop productivity, reduce fertilizer requirements, restore soil vitality, and elevate soil organic carbon.

Reduced Tillage: Limit soil disturbance to minimize organic matter decomposition and carbon loss.

Nitrogen Fertilizer Reductions: Apply less nitrogen overall, optimize timing and placement, and adopt technologies such as slow-release fertilizers or urease and nitrification inhibitors to reduce nitrogen volatilization and leaching.

Energy Use Reduction through Practice Changes: Decrease fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions by limiting machinery use and optimizing field operations.

The project is implemented across a variety of cropping systems—including, but not limited to, corn, wheat, and other open-field crops—and is tailored to suit local agronomic and climatic conditions. As a grouped project, it brings together multiple farms and fields, enabling site-specific adaptation of practices based on crop type and soil characteristics.

By integrating science-based regenerative practices at scale, the Open Field Carbon Farming Project offers a replicable, results-driven model for soil restoration, climate change mitigation, and long-term agricultural sustainability in open-field systems worldwide.
vcs-5327: The ‘Bosques de las Serranías’ project is a grouped forest plantation project designed to establish large-scale plantations of Eucalyptus smithii and Eucalyptus dunnii for pulp production in Uruguay. This project has been developed and initially presented to in the carbon framework, on a total area of 4,926 hectares of degraded grasslands in the Center East region of Uruguay, across a combination of properties owned by the project proponent (five properties) and leased lands (fifteen properties) (see Section 1.13 - Project Location for further details). This initial instance includes 4,793 hectares of Eucalyptus smithii and 133 hectares of Eucalyptus dunnii, planted progressively between 2021 and 2024.
vcs-5328:
The PROCarbono Project, initiated by Bayer Crop Science in Latin America, facilitates the adoption of regenerative agricultural practices and the optimization of inputs through innovative supportive tools that provide essential technical awareness. These tools enable growers to receive tailored management recommendations based on their baseline and edaphoclimatic factors, ultimately aiming for significant reductions and removals of greenhouse gas emissions.
Utilizing remote sensing technology, the project effectively monitors crop planting, harvest cycles, and soil coverage, identifying key opportunities for enhancing carbon sequestration. 
The initiative has already monitored fields across four of Brazil's six biomes and in 15 states, focusing on improvement of Agricultural Land Management (ALM) and carbon stock assessments to deepen understanding of soil organic carbon dynamics in tropical and subtropical climates. Over the project's duration, participating growers are encouraged to expand these sustainable practices to additional areas of their farms.
Given the rapid dynamics and challenges posed by climate change, the project emphasizes the gradual implementation of resilient practices supported by digital agriculture tools. By fostering a year-by-year transition, these combined practices aim to enhance both carbon stocks and overall crop productivity, contributing to a more sustainable agricultural future in Brazil.
vcs-533: Feke I hydroelectric power plant project is located at the south of Turkey, in the Mediterranean Region, on the Goksu Creek, a main branch of Seyhan River, within the province of Adana, about 10 km to Feke district.   The project consists of a 80 meters long concrete weir at 6 meters riverbed elevation, 2405 m long horseshoe shaped tunnel, 5200 m long transmission channel, forebay, desilting pool, spillway, 120 m long penstock pipe and a powerhouse with 2 vertical axis Francis turbines.   Feke I HEPP project has an installed capacity of 29.4 MW and expected to generate annually about 117 GWh of electricity on the average.
vcs-5330: The Western American Rangelands Regeneration project aims to remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere by implementing adaptive multi-paddock grazing on numerous ranches across the American West. It is a grouped projected starting with over 80,000 acres in the first instances. AMP grazing allows for the rest and rotation of pastures that have been historically overgrazed and the restoration of perennial and desirable grass species, thus leading to greater carbon inputs into the soil.
vcs-5331:
Re Up Geri Dönüşüm Sanayi Ve Ticaret A.Ş. Repet Şube (hereinafter “Re&Up”) operates in İnegöl, Bursa, pioneering textile recycling efforts by employing advanced recycling technologies. The project, RE&UP Bottle PET Recycled Chips, Flakes & Next-Gen T2T PET Recycled Chips Production (hereinafter “the Project”), focuses on transforming PET bottle waste and PET textile waste into high-quality, sustainable raw materials, namely PET flakes and PET chips.
Through the up cycling of PET waste, the project ensures that plastic materials are returned to the production cycle, fostering a circular economy and contributing to a more sustainable future.
The project employs both mechanical and thermomechanical recycling technologies to process PET flakes and superior PET chips. The recycling process involves sorting of polyester waste, mechanical shredding, melting, filtration, deep vacuum treatment, crystallization, and precision cutting. This results in high-performance granulates suitable for new textile products, extending the lifecycle of PET materials while meeting stringent quality standards.
Re&Up operates as a high-capacity, scaled-up recycling facility. As the “first of its kind” in the region, the project mechanically transforms both textile and PET bottle waste into high-quality PET flakes and chips . Leveraging innovative and scalable technologies, the recycled materials are made suitable for direct reuse in the textile industry. This facility, aligned with sustainability goals, makes a valuable contribution to recycling efforts.
Re&Up is committed not only to environmental sustainability but also to creating local employment opportunities, particularly for women, to promote social equity in the workforce. The Project’s forward-looking approach aims to expand recycling capacities with revenue from carbon credits , supporting Turkey’s circular economy targets and contributing to regional sustainability efforts.
vcs-5333:
The Forest Restoration in Mantiqueira region, Brazil Grouped Project (GP) aims to increase carbon removals by restoring degraded lands into forests in the Serra da Mantiqueira, Southeast Brazil, which holds the springs that supply water to 22 million people in the two largest metro regions in the country, and feed important hydroelectric hubs. This region has lost much of its forests, and the inappropriate past use of land has left a scenario of degradation: about 900 thousand hectares are degraded pastures. But there are opportunities for restoration: nearly 3 million hectares have potential for natural regeneration.
The GP will contribute to climate change mitigation by removing carbon from the atmosphere through reforestation and enhancement of the natural regeneration in degraded lands; improve the climate resilience by restoring water quality and stabilizing fluvial systems, through the reforestation of springs and riparian zones; improve ecosystem services and landscape maintenance. It’ll bring benefits to landowners and stakeholders, such as improved infrastructure, technology transfer and help to preserve biodiversity using native species and expanding the remaining forest fragments connectivity.
The project zone comprises the Conservador da Mantiqueira Program (CMP), a collective action that promotes the restoration of landscapes over 600 towns in São Paulo, Minas Gerais, and Rio de Janeiro states, to build an implementation network, based on positive experiences carried out in the region since 2006. 
The GP aims to add financial assets from the carbon market, increasing attractiveness for landowners through payment for ecosystem services. It will apply the most suitable restoration methods (full planting, assisted natural regeneration, secondary forest enrichment, agroforestry) and will be implemented on private lands (abandoned cropland or low productive pastures), mainly in sites with potential for natural regeneration.
vcs-5334:
Zhengzhou Lvyuan Food Waste Treatment Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is located at the Houzhai Food Waste Treatment Plant, Erqi District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province, China. The project is owned and implemented by Zhengzhou Lvyuan Food Waste Treatment Co., Ltd. 
The purpose of the project is to treat MSW with anaerobic digesters and utilize recovered biogas for electricity generation. The project activity includes MSW collection, MSW pre-treatment system, anaerobic digestion tank, biogas purification, electricity generation system, heat generation system and waste heat recovery. However, in terms of the heat generation system and the waste heat recovery, the waste heat will be recovered to be the source of heat supply for the operation. To be conservative, emission reductions will not be claimed for heat generation system and for the waste heat recovery. 
The fresh waste of the project is mainly kitchen and catering waste of the Zhengzhou City and the design processing capacity of the project for the fresh waste is 300 tonnes per day. The biogas from anaerobic digestion will be used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators. The total installed capacity will be 2.252 MW included 2 generators with each 1.126 MW. 
The liquid digestate and solid digestate will be produced in anaerobic digester. The solid digestate will be transported directly to a nearby landfill for landfill and will not be stored under anaerobic conditions. And the wastewater will be discharged through the water treatment system up to standard. 
The project is to utilize the biogas produced by anaerobic digestion for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is supplied to Central China Power Grid (CCPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations. Before the implementation of the project activity, the fresh waste would be treated in a landfill site with a partial capture of the landfill gas (LFG) and flaring of the captured LFG.
vcs-5335: This grouped project promotes sustainable grazing across Colombia’s diverse ecosystems, including the Llanos Orientales and inter-Andean valleys. Decades of overgrazing have degraded grasslands, causing soil erosion, compaction, and nutrient depletion, which reduces pasture productivity. This project supports the local ranchers in adopting practices such as rotational grazing, pasture enhancement, and improved livestock genetics suited to local conditions. Additionally, it promotes silvopastoral systems that integrate trees to boost carbon sequestration and discourage overgrazing, burning, and logging. The project will be implemented with the collaboration of field partners, who will help transfer knowledge and incentivize better ranching practices. The carbon finance resulting from this project is also expected to incentivize the implementation of the project activities. We estimate an initial yearly GHG removal of 700,000 tCO2e using the VM0042 methodology, version 2. The number of ranchers participating in the program is also projected to grow over the course of the crediting period. The project aligns with SDGs 2, 6, 8, 13, and 15, aiming for broad impact across Colombia’s grassland regions.
vcs-5336:
The Shaoyang Xinning Landfill Gas Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project located at the Laohutuo Landfill in Hengqiao Village, Wantang Town, Xinning County, Shaoyang City, Hunan Province, P.R. China.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the LFG generated from the Laohutuo Landfill was released into the atmosphere; the equivalent amount of electricity generated by the project activity was supplied by the fossil-fuel-dominated Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The baseline scenario is the same as the conditions existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions will be reduced by avoiding CO2 emissions from those fossil fuel-based power plants connected to the grid and by avoiding GHG emissions from releasing LFG into the atmosphere at the landfill site.
vcs-5337: The Project is a single dispatchable facility comprising of solar photo-voltaic technology linked to a battery energy storage system (BESS). The Project is located 5km South East of De Aar in the Northern Cape and roughly 8km North of the Eskom Main Transmission Substation, Hydra. The Project will have a Contracted Capacity of 75 MW (AC) at the Delivery Point. The solar portion is split over 3 x authorized footprints located adjacent to one another and forming a combined total installed capacity of an approximately 216 MW peak (DC). The BESS is to have a combined energy capacity of 450 MWh, 105 MW charging capacity and 75 MW discharging capacity at the Delivery Point.
vcs-5339: The proposed project involves establishing a biogas facility that efficiently captures methane from biodegradable waste, converting organic material into renewable energy and valuable byproducts. By transforming waste into biogas, the facility not only mitigates methane emissions but also produces sustainable fuel (Bio-CNG) and nutrient-rich bio-manure for agricultural use. This process supports environmental health by reducing landfill waste and providing clean, renewable energy alternatives. Additionally, due to its nature, the project contributes to several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
vcs-534: Feke II Hydroelectric power plant project is located at the south of Turkey, in the Mediterranean Region, on the Goksu Creek, a main branch of Seyhan River, within the province of Adana, about 9 km southwest of Feke I district. Feke I and Feke II projects were first developed by General Directorate of DSI (State Hydraulic Works) as a single project, to generate energy by utilizing the water potential of Goksu Branch in Seyhan Basin. However it was seen during the feasibility studies that the project would cause whole of Feke district to be covered with water, therefore the project was divided into Feke I and Feke II projects which are developed as individual projects. The project consists of compressed concrete dam with a crest length of 256 meters and a height of 60 meters from the riverbed; 317 meters long derivation tunnel, upstream and downstream cofferdams, spillway, 171 meters long penstock, a powerhouse of 44 by 32 meters dimensions and 2 vertical axis Francis turbines.
vcs-5340: Yangmei Xin Da Di 16MW CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the 'Project') is located at Hougou Village, Yixing Town, Heshun County, Jin Zhong City, Shanxi Province, China, the north of Yangmei Xin Da Di Coal Industry. . The central geographic coordinates of the project site are37°21'17N 113°34'53E.The Project utilizes coal mine methane (CMM) with a mix concentration of 10% from Xin Da Di Coal Mine for power generatation to supply electricity to North China Power Grid (NCPG). The Project Owner is Heshun County Yanyan Power Generation Co., Ltd.
vcs-5342:
Yingkou Dashiqiao LFG Power Generation Project  (hereinafter referred to as “the Project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project located at Dashiqiao Huzhuang Landfill, Huzhuang Town, Dashiqiao City, Yingkou City, Liaoning Province, People’s Republic of China.
The purpose of the project is to capture and utilize landfill gas for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is supplied to Northeast Power Grid (NEPG). The new gas extraction and utilization systems have been installed by the project. Before the implementation of the project activity, the landfill gas that was captured and utilized by the project was emitted into the atmosphere directly. Equivalent electricity was provided by Northeast Power Grid (NEPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations. This is the scenario that existed prior to the implementation of the project activity and is also the baseline scenario.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by NEPG.
vcs-5343: The Stock Carbon Mazuay REDD+ project seeks to reduce carbon emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, promoting the conservation and sustainable management of forests in critical preservation areas. The initiative aims to contribute to global greenhouse gas reduction targets, generate environmental and social benefits for local communities and preserve the biodiversity of threatened ecosystems.
vcs-5344:
Ejin Horo Banner MSW Landfill Biogas Pollution Control and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at MSW landfill site, #4 Community, Zhang Gangtu Village, Altenheige Town, Ejin Horo Banner, Ordos City, Iner Mongolia Autonomous Region, PR China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Ordos City BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Ejin Horo Banner MSW Landfill site (hereafter referred to as Ejin Horo Banner landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
Ejin Horo Banner landfill site is harmless treatment landfill site with a total design effective storage capacity of 1,800,000 m³, design daily municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 600 tons. At present, the daily disposal is around 380 tons. Ejin Horo Banner landfill site is expected to close at the end of 2028. The project has a total designed capacity 2MW (2*1000kW) and combusts the LFG, which  contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the North China Grid Company (NCGC).
vcs-5345:
The Soutpansberg Restoration and Conservation Project, led by Few & Far LLC and supported by C4 EcoSolutions, aims to revitalize and protect the Soutpansberg Mountain Bushveld and Makhado Sweet Bushveld in South Africa. 

Spanning approximately 100,983 hectares, the project addresses significant ecological challenges caused by deforestation, overgrazing, illegal harvesting, and land transformation due to agriculture and mining.

The project employs a phased approach to restoration, targeting northern and western sections in its initial phase with interventions that include reforestation, revegetation, game management, and ecotourism promotion. Active restoration efforts, such as tree planting and mechanical bush clearance, are combined with passive methods like rotational grazing, anti-poaching, and herbivory exclosures to encourage natural regeneration. In addition, the project reduces tree density in bush-encroached areas and enhances water and soil conservation through contouring and terracing.

Aiming to improve ecosystem resilience to climate change, the project prioritizes socio-economic benefits for local communities, integrating sustainable land management practices and offering environmental education. Expected outcomes include increased biodiversity, stabilized water resources, and enhanced carbon sequestration, contributing to Sustainable Development Goals related to clean water, climate action, decent work, and life on land.

Designed as a VCS-grouped project, this initiative can expand its conservation footprint with new instances while avoiding repetitive validations.
vcs-5347:
NaturAll Carbon Limited presents the NaturAll Carbon Program – Regenerative Agriculture in Brazil – Project II, a transformative initiative covering 253,128,708 hectares across 13 Brazilian states within the Cerrado and Amazon ecotone. Recognizing that inadequate agricultural management practices are primary drivers of high greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and soil degradation, this project addresses the critical need for effective programs that support farmers in transitioning to regeneration-focused soil management.

Launched on January 1st, 2022, the project implements regenerative agricultural practices that are not common in the region, ensuring additional environmental benefits. These practices aim to reduce and remove GHG emissions from the atmosphere, increase Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), and prevent physical, chemical, and biological soil degradation. By enhancing soil fertility and productivity, the initiative also improves resilience to extreme weather events, ensures food security, and preserves natural resources along with their ecosystem services.

The program plans to expand over time, engaging multiple stakeholders across diverse agricultural and livestock activities. By fostering resilient and sustainable agropastoral systems in the Cerrado and Amazon ecotone region, NaturAll Carbon Limited is committed to driving positive environmental outcomes.
