vcs-5349: Mufin Green Finance Limited is implementing commercial electric 2 wheeler, 3 wheeler and 4 wheeler instead of fossil fuel powered vehicles. Mufin provides solutions to top e-commerce, e-grocery, FMCG, logistics and D2C companies to optimize their logistics costs and meet their goals of reducing carbon emissions. At the same time Mufin works with OEMs and driver cum owners to helps address various constraints that are coming in the way of EV adoption. Project activity is replacing fossil fuel (Petrol, Diesel and CNG) powered vehicle from baseline. The usage of electricity powered vehicles instead of fossil fuel powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven. This is proven in the respective ER calculations.
vcs-535: AKOCAK is a run of river type hydroelectric power plant (HEPP) project located on Karadere River, in Trabzon province, in East Black sea region of Turkey. The purpose of the project is to generate energy from the running waters of Karadere River.   The project includes two weirs. The first weir called Erikli weir shall be built on Alcak Brook, a branch of Karadere, on 1,339 meters riverbed elevation. A sediment pool of 41 meters long and 2.3 meters wide shall be built along the riverbed. The other weir called Akocak weir shall be built on Karadere branch of the river, on 1,328 meter riverbed elevation. The UTM ED coordinates for Erikli weir is 580 500 E, 4 495 600 N; Akocak weir: 577 425 E,  4 496 300 N; powerhouse: 576 375E,  4 502 625 N.
vcs-5350:
The project activity involves the establishment & operation of a biogas plant with purification unit. The biogas plant can treat 220 tons/day (TPD) of organic waste through anaerobic digestion and produce 23,000 m3/day of biogas & 45 TPD of organic fertilizer. The biogas is then purified and upgraded into Compressed Biogas of 10.6 TPD. 

By capturing the methane emissions being released from the organic waste and by reducing the carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel, the project has contributed to Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission reductions (ER). The estimated annual average ER from this project activity is 93,851 tCO2e/year and the total ER over the first crediting period of 7 years is 7,50,808 tCO2e.
vcs-5351:
Rainforest Builder Ltd is an integrated tropical forest restoration company founded in 2022 to pioneer tropical forest ecosystem restoration as a commercial undertaking, by combining the best restoration science with professional forestry industry practice to deliver ecosystem restoration at unprecedented quality and scale. Rainforest Builder’s projects aim to return degraded formerly forested lands to primary levels of biomass, biodiversity and structural complexity rapidly and resiliently, in partnership with a range of stakeholders.

The ARR VCS-CCB project is a grouped project that ultimately aims to restore approximately 100,000 ha of degraded community-owned land across Sierra Leone by 2040. The project will deliver sustainable ecosystem restoration through diversified native mixed-species plantings that re-establish the structure and function of natural rainforests, enhancing ecological connectivity and mitigating degradation effects resulting from existing unsustainable land uses. Central to this endeavour is the implementation of best-practice silviculture and planting methods, using mixes of framework tree species that are carefully selected to provide key structural and functional roles. The Climate, Community, and Biodiversity goals of the project are to re-establish and protect natural forest landscapes, recovering threatened biodiversity in a globally important conservation hotspot, sequestering CO2 and improving the provision of ecosystem services including water regulation, nutrient cycling, and climate regulation. Long-term sustainability is enhanced through the creation of small-scale commercial harvesting areas to provide local communities with secure job opportunities and diversified long-term revenue streams. Monitoring of forest and vegetation composition, biodiversity and community impacts will be conducted over the long term to assess the progress of the initiatives.
vcs-5352:
Chongqing Fengdu LFG Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project is located in the Fengdu County Municipal Solid Waste Landfill in Yanfeng Cave, Dali Village, Mingshan Town, Fengdu County, Chongqing City, People's Republic of China.
The purpose of the project is to capture and utilized the landfill gas for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is supplied to Southwest Power Grid (SWPG). The new gas extraction and utilization systems has been installed by the project. Before the implementation of the project activity, the landfill gas that captured and utilized by the project was emitted into the atmosphere directly. Equivalent electricity was provided by Southwest Power Grid (SWPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations. This is the scenario that existed prior to the implementation of the project activity and is also the baseline scenario.
In absence of the project, equivalent amount of electricity exported to the grid by the project would have otherwise been supplied by Southwest Power Grid (SWPG). Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions will be reduced by avoiding CO2 emissions from those fossil fuel-based power plants connected to the grid and by avoiding GHG emissions from releasing LFG into atmosphere at the landfill site.
vcs-5353:
Life Climate Soil Carbon Project in Turkiye (referred to as the 'Project' hereafter) is developed by Life İklim ve Enerji Ltd. Şti. to implement activities aimed at reducing agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. It utilizes the VM0042, Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management. The project's goal is to increase farmers' understanding of the advantages of sustainable agriculture and raise their awareness to modify their agricultural methods to contribute to mitigating and adapting to climate change.

Life Climate Soil Carbon Project in Turkiye aims to decrease emissions resulting from agricultural practices and enhance the storage of carbon in the soil. The Program will implement a package of regenerative agricultural land management activities. The project activities are the following:

•	Tillage and/or residue management
•	Crop planting and harvesting (e.g. crop rotations)
•	Fertilizer (organic) application management
•	No-plough cultivation

The baseline farming practices, characteristic of conventional agriculture, typically involve intensive tillage methods, including ploughing and cultivation during planting and weed control, often leaving the soil exposed. These practices can lead to the degradation of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), which may result in the increased use of synthetic chemical inputs to maintain crop production and yields. Over time, this reliance on chemical fertilizers and pesticides can further degrade soil health and sustainability.

Life Climate Soil Carbon Project in Turkiye is a grouped project. The project is located in Turkiye (İzmir, Aydın, Manisa, Denizli, Şanlıurfa). The project will cover 4,956.43 ha. The project is expected to expand to an area in the provinces of same locations and Kahramanmaraş in the coming years.
vcs-5357:
TCL Aobo (Tianjin) E-waste recycling and comprehensive utilization project(Phase II) aims to produce recycled metals and plastic by recycling E-waste (like waste televisions, washing machines, refrigerators, air conditioners and computers, etc). The project is located in No.10, No.15 Road, Ziya Circular Economy Industrial Park, Jinghai District, Tianjin City, China, and is invested and owned by TCL Aobo (Tianjin) Environmental Protection Development Co., Ltd. 
The project includes disassembly lines for refrigerators, air conditioners, washing machines, LCD TVs, small household appliances, and a deep processing line for products. The most abundant metals in waste electrical and electronic products are steel, aluminium and copper, which are non-renewable resources. The dismantled plastics are mainly ABS and hybrid plastics.
After the completion of the project, the annual disassembling and processing capacity of E-waste will be 200,000 tons.
vcs-536: Uluabat HEPP and Cinarcik Dam Project is an integrated project located on the lower basin of Orhaneli Creek, one of the major branches of Mustafa Kemalpasa River. It is built within the scope of Emet Orhaneli Project developed by General Directorate of DSI (State Hydraulic Works) for utilizing the water potential in Marmara Region and has two components.  First component, Cinarcik Dam is built by DSI mainly for providing agricultural, industrial and drinking water for Bursa city whereas second component, Uluabat HEPP project has been awarded to Akenerji Elektrik Uretim A.S. for 49 years period after the bidding by the Turkish Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EMRA).  Uluabat HEPP project has installed capacity of 100 MW and expected to generate 422.6 GWh as per the license however due to the use of water for other purposes, it is expected to decrease to 373.03 GWh in 2021 and 323.653 GWh in 2028 in parallel to GWh. For the first crediting period, it has been assumed that average generation will be 422.6GWh and emission reduction has been calculated respectively. Electricity generated by the power plant will be delivered to the grid by an 11.2 km long 154 kV double circuit overhead transmission line.
vcs-5360:
Fronterra, in partnership with rural communities, lead an ambitious initiative to restore 12,000 hectares of degraded land across 40+ communities in the Peruvian Andes. This initiative addresses environmental degradation, climate change, and poverty while fostering sustainable economic development and empowering local populations.

The Andes, known for their biodiversity and cultural heritage, face severe challenges from centuries of deforestation, erosion, and climate change, which threaten ecosystems and livelihoods. Sumaq Allpa provides a solution, blending ecological restoration with economic empowerment and climate action through sustainable forestry.

Key Solutions
Land Restoration: Transform degraded lands into productive forests, improving soil fertility, reducing erosion, and enhancing water retention.
Sustainable Pine Forestry: Certified plantations produce timber, resin, and mushrooms, ensuring perpetual forest health and creating diverse income streams.
Community Empowerment: Green jobs, capacity building, and governance strengthen rural communities, making them true partners in success.
Biodiversity Conservation: Native species like Queñual trees (polylepis spp) restore riparian zones and biodiversity corridors, supporting ecosystem resilience.
Climate Impact: Over 40 years, 6.6 million tCO2eq will be sequestered, making Sumaq Allpa a significant contributor to Peru's climate goals.

Sustainability Model
The project adheres to best practices and guidelines on FPIC and IFC Performance Standards, ensuring communities co-design and co-manage activities. A benefit-sharing model aligns carbon revenues and profits with community development, fostering long-term participation and impact.

Sumaq Allpa isn’t just a project; it’s a movement to empower communities, regenerate landscapes, and deliver high-quality carbon credits. Join us in creating a sustainable future for such a beautiful land and communities in the iconic Peruvian Andes.
vcs-5362: The Shuangjianghu wastewater treatment Plant project is located in Yiwu City, Zhejiang Province, China. The project owner is Yiwu Water Treatment Co., Ltd. The entire process includes pre-treatment process, biological treatment process, deep treatment process, and sludge treatment process. The maximum designed inflow flow rate is 160,000m3/d, the inflow COD concentration is 400mg/L, and the outflow COD concentration is 30mg/L.
vcs-5363: Poultry Manure to Compost grouped project in Bangladesh (hereafter referred to as the grouped project) is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure waste. The project is invested, owned and operated by Kazi Farms Limited  and the carbon business development is responsible by EKI Energy Services Limited. Kazi Farms Limited is implementing a set of organic fertilizer production lines to treat poultry manure from poultry farms owned & operated by Kazi Farms in Bangladesh only, which is a Least Developed Country (LDC) as per UN list of LDCs , Project Activity instances: The details of the first/current project activity instances have been tabulated along with the details viz., Compost Production & Manure Treatment Capacities of the instance, Location & Commissioning Date.
vcs-5364:
DABACO Thanh Hoa Biogas recovery and utilization from Animal Manure Waste Management (hereafter referred to as the grouped project) is to treat the raw manure from DABACO Thanh Hoa Swine Farm by the anaerobic digester and use the biogas generated during the treatment process for power generation for captive consumption purposes. The project is invested, owned and operated by DABACO Thanh Hoa Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as the project owner) and the carbon business development is responsible by EKI Energy Services Limited. 
DABACO Thanh Hoa Company Limited would be implementing a set of Biogas recovery and utilization units to treat manure from Swine Farm farms owned & operated by them in Vietnam.
vcs-5365:
The project aims to mitigate climate change through the restoration and conservation of mangroves. It focuses on planting mangroves in the intertidal zones of the Egyptian Red Sea Coast and Qaroun Lake in Fayoum, Egypt. Key activities include planting, enhancing existing mangrove stands and engaging local communities in conservation efforts.
This initiative is led by the Environment Without Borders Foundation, an Egyptian NGO, in collaboration with various stakeholders. GreenWorks Consulting oversees project management and advisory, while BeFlat Services facilitates climate finance.
The project will rehabilitate 150 hectares of existing mangroves, increasing their density to 2,500–3,000 trees per hectare, and expand to an additional 6,256 hectares with similar tree densities. Over 20 years, the project is expected to sequester 5,267,219 tCO2e, with an average annual reduction of 263,361 tCO2e.
vcs-5366:
Henan Zhumadian Youran Xiping Dairy Farm Biogas Utilization Project  (hereinafter referred to as “the Project”) is locates in Hongcunpu Village, Leizu Town, Xiping County, Zhumadian City, Henan Province, P.R China. 
The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects manure waste from dairy cows from Zhumadian farm in Xiping County. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. The recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation at the project site. The residual waste from the CSTR digesters will be used to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
The baseline scenario is the situation where, in the absence of the project activity, the animal manure waste are left to decay within the project boundary and methane is emitted to the atmosphere. The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas.
vcs-5367: The Accelerating Access to Clean Energy project involves the design, installation, and commissioning of embedded solar photovoltaic (PV) generators and micro-grids across multiple locations in South Africa. Implemented and managed by Fuel Swich SA (Pty) Ltd (hereinafter referred to as Fuel Switch), the project reflects their commitment to supporting environmental sustainability and advancing clean energy solutions. The project operates within the geographical boundaries of South Africa and aims to reduce the country’s reliance on coal-based electricity by providing renewable electricity through embedded generators and micro-grids.
vcs-5368:
The aim of this carbon project is to provide financial incentives to the farmers, sequester more carbon and promote sustainability through the integration of trees or woody plants into agricultural landscapes of the individual farmers in the selected ten districts of the state of Assam namely, Baksa, Barpeta, Bongaigaon, Darrang, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nalbari, Sivasagar, Sonitpur and Udalguri. The plantations were undertaken by the farmers and/or homestead owners from the years 2022, 2023 and 2024 under the supervision of AAU.
The project is a voluntary initiative by the AAU and farmers to implement forestry activities by planting trees on privately owned lands of the farmers. The project intends to generate carbon credits under the voluntary carbon market mechanism as per the VCS standard. The expected GHG annual average removal is 276,890 t CO2e.
vcs-5369:
The Sierra del Divisor Conservation Corridor Grouped Project, led by Fronterra, aims to create a conservation model that unites public, private, and community efforts in the Peruvian Amazon. Starting in Loreto, the project will expand into Ucayali, targeting over 2 million hectares, including native and farming communities, protected areas, and forestry concessions. The project prioritises primary forest conservation and sustainable rural development, engaging local communities in sustainable activities that protect biodiversity and mitigate climate change.
Key components include control & surveillance, biological monitoring & research, sustainable economic activities, and carbon impact certification. The project begins with 6 native and farmers communities along the Ucayali River, organised under Asociación de Pueblos 5 Unidos (APCU), focusing on restoring degraded pasturelands through cocoa-based agroforestry, fostering economic growth and stabilizing land use. The communities are committed to binding agreements preventing deforestation in their territories and adjacent protected areas. A rigorous FPIC process ensures strong community participation and informed consent.
The project envisions scaling from APCU to include more areas, such as a proposed regional protected area, national parks, and other native communities in the Sierra del Divisor landscape. Advanced technology, including GIS & remote sensing, powered by AI, will support monitoring impacts and ensuring transparent reporting.
The expanded project aims to protect the Sierra del Divisor Occidental and Yavari Tapiche Indigenous Communities Reserve, safeguarding one of the Amazon's last uncontacted tribes. At its initial stage, the project is expected to reduce 121,664 tCO2 emissions annually, totalling approximately 3.65 million tCO2e over 30 years. This initiative represents a major contribution to climate action, biodiversity conservation, and community-led sustainable development.
vcs-537: The project activity undertaken by Gujarat Paguthan Energy Corporation Private Limited (GPECL) utilizes the kinetic energy present in wind to generate electrical power in the state of Gujarat in India. GPECL has installed 63 Wind Electric Generators (WEGs) of individual capacity 800 kW that have been supplied by Enercon India Ltd. totaling installed capacity of 50.4 MW.  Purpose of the project activity is to export power generated from WEGs to NEWNE grid of India and help in decreasing power shortage, diversify the grid composition, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions thereby contributing to sustainable development. Out of the 63 WEGs, one WEG is under a wheeling and banking agreement with Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited.  First and last WEGs were commissioned on 12th Apr 2008 and 12th Mar 2009 respectively. This project activity was registered as a CDM project activity on 13th Feb 2010. Details of the same are available on http://cdm.unfccc.int/Projects/DB/RWTUV1250689673.15/view
vcs-5370:
The Forestal Sylvis Silvopastoral Carbon Project aims to reduce GHG emissions through an agroforestry initiative, contributing to climate change mitigation and generating positive ecosystem impacts. 
The grouped project area covers Paraguay's Eastern Region, which represents 39% of the country's total area. This region includes grazing and agricultural lands that have experienced various degrees of degradation due to unsustainable land use, overgrazing, land conversion, and wildfires. The project proposes introducing silvopastoral systems to create sustainable socio-environmental frameworks, sequestering GHGs through tree biomass, improving ecosystem services, and diversifying productive, economic, and cultural practices to increase system resilience.
The project will mainly use eucalyptus species (including hybrids like Eucalyptus grandis x urophylla), but other native species like Paulownia tomentosa (kiri), Cordia trichotoma (peteribí), Anadenanthera colubrina (curupay), and other genera such as Pinus, Gmelina, and Cedrus may also be included.
The first PAI is taking place on a portion of the Loma Linda farm in the south of the Eastern Region, in the Caazapá Department. A total of 1,905 hectares were planted, with an LTA of 694,328 tCO2eq, implying a total GHG benefit of around 30,188 tCO2e per year over 23 years.
It is worth noting that two ARR projects are being developed in collaboration with Forestal Sylvis S.A. and AF Madera as proponents. These projects are the result of a cooperation agreement between the two companies, aiming to enhance their business models. The decision to present two separate projects is based on land ownership considerations and the intention to manage carbon credits independently while leveraging each company's capacities and experience.
vcs-5371: The Kubu Peatland Project is an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) and Avoided Planned Wetland Degradation (APWD) project that seeks to protect 20,155 ha of peatland ecosystem in Indonesia. The project is being developed in the concession of PT. Menggala Rambu Utama (PT. MRU). The project is located in the coastal Kubu Raya Regency, south of the Provincial Capital Pontianak. Under the baseline scenario, 15,266 ha of the concession area would have been deforested and drained to establish a short-rotation Acacia plantation. The project is now seeking to conserve the ecological functions of the peatland, to avoid the emissions that would have been associated with conversion to an industrial tree plantation and to benefit critically endangered biodiversity and provide benefits for local communities.
vcs-5372:
Biowaste Energy Ventures is developing a biogas and biomethane facility in District Gadap, Karachi, near Nagori Cooperative Farming Society. The plant will convert livestock manure into biogas and upgrade it into biomethane for industrial users in Karachi.

Feedstock will be sourced from nearby dairy clusters (Nagori, Diamond, Madina) with backup supply from Karachi Dairy Cattle City, Areesha, Shamsi, Paradise and Dua Dairy Farms. At full capacity, the plant will process about 1,320 tons/day of cow dung, managing manure from an estimated 81,000 dairy and 9,000 non-dairy cattle. Four digesters will operate initially, with eight more added within two years. 

The system comprises twelve anaerobic digesters totaling 60,000 m³. It will generate ~74,000 m³/day of raw biogas (≈59% CH₄). Around 20% will fuel plant auxiliaries via two biogas generators, while the remainder will be upgraded to pipeline-grade biomethane. 

Biomethane production is expected at ~34,831 m³/day (CH₄), transported by high-pressure tube trailers to industrial end-users. Digestate will be dewatered and processed into ~33 t/day of organic fertilizer. 
The project will signiﬁcantly reduce methane emissions from unmanaged manure and organic waste dumping, contributing to SDG 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 13. 

The crediting period is 7 years (renewable). Expected average annual emission reductions are 372,254 tCO₂e, totaling 2,605,775 tCO₂e in the ﬁrst period.
vcs-5373: The project focuses on providing off-grid solar energy solutions to underserved communities, particularly in rural areas, by installing Solar Home Systems (SHS). These systems will enable households to access clean, renewable energy, which will help improve their living conditions and reduce reliance on traditional fossil fuels. In addition, the project will provide reliable lighting for students, thus enhancing their ability to study and access education. The project reduces the time spent on collecting firewood and other fuel sources, particularly for women and girls, and thus the project promotes gender equality. The initiative will also generate jobs in the solar installation and maintenance sector, contributing to economic growth and employment opportunities.
vcs-5376: The Seeds of Recovery: The Ukrainian Regenerative Agriculture & Carbon Removal Program is an Agricultural Land Management project developed and owned by Sentinel Earth aiming to enhance soil organic carbon levels and decrease farm's GHG footprint. In context of severe impacts of Russian military invasion we aim to bring funding incentives and knowledge for affected entities to modernize their technology and practices and build back Ukrainian agriculture better.
vcs-5378:
The Clean Choola Initiative aims to distribute improved cookstoves to households mostly dependent on traditional chulah in Pakistan. The project is being implemented by Core Carbon Canada, this project seeks to improve cooking practices and enhance livelihoods within rural households. (hereafter The Clean Choola Initiative is called as The Project)
This project represents a transformative initiative aimed at changing from traditional cooking stoves to improved cookstoves, promoting hygiene, and empowering rural communities, particularly women, from all over the Globe. At its core is the introduction of the double-stove innovation, offering a cost-effective and environmentally friendly alternative to traditional single-stove setups. Equipped with a chimney for improved ventilation, the project minimizes cooking time and smoke emissions, significantly improving the cooking experience and promoting better respiratory and eye health for women disproportionately affected by indoor air pollution. 
Elevated on raised earthen platforms, these stoves provide clean dining spaces fueled by readily available agricultural waste or cow dung, reducing reliance on biomass and saving time for households. Adding a designated washing area shows the project cares about keeping families healthy by promoting good hygiene habits.
The project's impact extends beyond practical cooking solutions. Through the training of Barefoot Entrepreneurs, known as Chulah or Stove Sisters, rural women/housewives have the skills to construct and maintain these stoves. 
Overall, The Project represents a holistic approach to addressing cooking challenges in rural areas across the Globe, initiated in Pakistan and further expanding to other developing countries and least-developed countries, combining innovation, community empowerment, and sustainability to improve the lives of countless families while fostering a sense of dignity and self-sufficiency within communities.
vcs-538: ITC Ltd, in its packaging and printing facility, has installed 9 numbers of WEGs of total 14.1 MW capacity (4 of 1.65 MW and 5 of 1.5 MW). The main objective of this initiative is to meet the electricity requirement at the packaging and printing facility located at Tiruvottiyur, Chennai, Tamil Nadu in India. The project installs the model V82 Vestas-make WEGs of individual capacity of 1.65 MW and S82 Suzlon-make WEGs of 1.5 MW. This project generates electricity from wind by converting the kinetic energy of wind to mechanical energy and then to electricity by using the generators. The plant and machinery will be owned by ITC Limited, whereas the EPC contractors will be individually responsible for operation and maintenance of the machines supplied by them.
vcs-5380: The project aims to implement an energy efficiency lighting retrofit program across 3,824 schools in the Limpopo Province of South Africa. During the project roll-out 48W linear LED lights and fittings will be installed and replace double 156W fluorescent lights and their fitting. The implementation of LED lights will reduce electricity demand from the carbon-intensive electricity grid and as such reduce the emission of greenhouse gasses the cause climate change.
vcs-5381: The Alien Energy Biomass Waste to Energy Project utilises biomass waste as a fuel in heat generation equipment within the Republic of South Africa. The biomass waste originates from sustainable sources and is converted into pellets at several biomass treatment facilities across the country. The biomass pellets are utilised in a range of boilers, where they displace fossil fuel and a such reduce the emissions of GHGs that cause climate change.
vcs-5382:
This Project seeks to sequester carbon through the implementation and long term management of afforestation activities on lands in the UAE. The primary objectives of this project are to sequester carbon, improve local ecosystems to increase habitat area for native plants and wildlife, and to prevent further soil degradation. Several native species will be planted, all verified as meeting the Environmental Agency Abu Dhabi's guidelines.
The Project is designed to meet the UAE's goals and mandates on the preservation of biodiversity, and to aid the efforts in combating desertification.
The project area selected is currently desert with no significant flora coverage. The Project boundary has been established with specific planting locations and species selection determined to maximize the ecosystem benefits.
vcs-5383:
The agroforestry project “Agroforestry plantations in Karnataka for greener tomorrow” is operated by Shalmala Agro fair & Elite services Pvt. Ltd in Karnataka located in the southern region of India. The project proponent is working as a wholesome distributor of products in Karnataka with the main objective of promoting and marketing a diverse range of agricultural products, including homemade pickles, chips, and honey products, sourced directly from local farmers to enhance the economic well-being and socio-economic status of farmers in the region. The project proponent has also established a meaningful collaboration with the SCODWES NGO (Sahyadri Community Development and Women Empowerment Society). This partnership allows Project Proponent to actively engage with farmers organized under the umbrella of SCODWES NGO. They work together to bring their diverse produce to the market, ensuring a fair and sustainable market place for the farmers.

A total of around 18,000 hectares of area (where major participants are small and marginal farmers for the region) has been taken for agroforestry plantation in which plantation activities have been started since the year 2021-2022. Main tree plantations which have been carried out by the farmers are Areca catechu (Betelnut palm), Mangifera indica (mango), Manilkara zapota (Sapota) and Anacardium occidentale (Cashew), Cocos nucifera (Coconut) and Psidium guajava (Guava). The prior condition to the project activity was lands with majorly paddy cultivation along with some barren/fallow designated agricultural lands owned by the participating farmers/land owners. 

This project will also help in increasing tree outside forest (TOF) that will aid in mitigating climate change. And along with enhancing income of small and marginalized farming communities, the project will promote biodiversity conservation, women empowerment and improvement of soil health.
vcs-5384:
The One Acre Fund Tanzania Intensive Agroforestry Project promotes multifunctional tree planting in agricultural lands, fallow lands, and around home sites by providing subsidized packages of agroforestry trees to participating smallholder farmers. The project is a grouped Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation project located in southwestern Tanzania, spanning the administrative regions of Iringa, Njombe, Mbeya, Songwe, Rukwa, and Ruvuma. 

One Acre Fund curates its agroforestry tree packages to include a mix of Indigenous and non-invasive naturalized species that will provide farmers with a sustainable source of fuelwood and fodder as well as soil fertility and erosion control co-benefits. A portion of tree species are intended to be planted on the boundary of croplands for erosion control and fuel or fodder provisions, while others are intended to be planted within crop fields for improved soil fertility and hydrologic function. One Acre Fund also offers high-value trees, such as fruit and nut trees, along with the agroforestry tree packages as further incentive, food source, and income for farmers. The project will generate emissions removals occurring as a result of enhanced carbon sequestration in biomass of the distributed agroforestry trees. Carbon stored in tree biomass over the crediting period will depend on the tree species, tree growth rate as mediated by site conditions of soil and climate, and tree management activities (e.g. pruning). While tree species provided over time and in different locations may vary depending on local conditions and farmer interest, trees selected for the agroforestry packages are expected to be long-lived trees that will not be coppiced or harvested. Preliminary ex-ante estimates indicate the project will remove approximately 3,411,450 tCO2e over a 26 year crediting period, with estimated annual GHG emission removals of roughly 130,000 tCO2e yr-1.
vcs-5385:
The AF Madera High Quality Timber On Silvopastoral Project aims to reduce GHG emissions through an agroforestry initiative, contributing to climate change mitigation and generating positive ecosystem impacts. 
The grouped project area covers Paraguay's Eastern Region, which represents 39% of the country's total area. This region includes grazing and agricultural lands that have experienced various degrees of degradation due to unsustainable land use, overgrazing, land conversion, and wildfires. The project proposes introducing silvopastoral systems to create sustainable socio-environmental frameworks, sequestering GHGs through tree biomass, improving ecosystem services, and diversifying productive, economic, and cultural practices to increase system resilience.
The project will mainly use eucalyptus species (including hybrids like Eucalyptus grandis x urophylla), but other native species like Paulownia tomentosa (kiri), Cordia trichotoma (peteribí), Anadenanthera colubrina (curupay), and other genera such as Pinus, Gmelina, and Cedrus may also be included.
The first PAI is taking place on a portion of the Loma Linda farm in the south of the Eastern Region, in the Caazapá Department. A total of 114 hectares were planted, with an LTA of 119.172 tCO2eq, implying a total GHG benefit of around 3724 tCO2e per year over 31 years.
It is worth noting that two ARR projects are being developed in collaboration AF Madera and Forestal Sylvis SA as proponents. These projects are the result of a cooperation agreement between the two companies, aiming to enhance their business models. The decision to present two separate projects is based on land ownership considerations and the intention to manage carbon credits independently while leveraging each company's capacities and experience.
vcs-5386:
The ARR REECO Fronteiras Verdes Project, proposed by BWP Trading Company and Ambipar Environment, aims to restore at least 15,000 hectares of Atlantic Forest through large-scale forest restoration. This initiative will create interconnected ecological corridors between Itatiaia National Park, Serra da Bocaina National Park, and Cunhambebe State Park. The project promotes the planting of native species, encourages natural regeneration on private rural properties, and focuses on the recovery of degraded soils through agroforestry systems tailored to local conditions and socio-economic interests. Additionally, another 15,000 hectares will be dedicated to agroforestry systems that support low-carbon bioeconomy activities.
The project is located across 18 municipalities in the states of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, Brazil, with the first module centered in Resende, RJ. This module is situated in the sub-basin of Médio Paraíba do Sul and includes pre-selected properties that share similar agroclimatic characteristics and land-use histories.
Historically, this region was dominated by coffee production from 1830 to 1920 before transitioning to extensive cattle ranching, which resulted in deforestation and the spread of Brachiaria grasslands. Some properties also leased land for eucalyptus forestry, with plantations established between 2003 and 2006.
The project not only focuses on ecological restoration but also aims to promote sustainable land-use practices and serve as a model for conservation and bioeconomy initiatives on a global scale.
vcs-5387:
The Renascer das Serras ARR Project is located in the Atlantic Rainforest, Brazil's third largest biome and the second largest tropical rainforest on the American continent. It will be dedicated to large-scale forest restoration in priority areas for environmental conservation, by planting native forest species and facilitating natural regeneration on private rural properties in the south of the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
The Project Area faces a scenario of environmental degradation, characterized by deforestation and habitat fragmentation, where historically inadequate land exploitation has resulted in biodiversity loss, soil degradation and compromised ecosystem services. 
Given that the restored forests will act as carbon sinks, absorbing CO2 from the atmosphere and contributing to climate change mitigation, the project is expected to generate significant reductions in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by capturing carbon dioxide (CO2) during tree growth. In addition, the increase in forest cover will help improve soil quality and regulate hydrological cycles, reducing erosion and sedimentation in water bodies.
This ARR project not only seeks to mitigate climate change, but also to strengthen the resilience of local communities and restore the region's rich biodiversity. As a result, the project has the potential to reforest 20,000 hectares, creating jobs and contributing to the conservation of endangered species.
vcs-5388:
The proposed project activity involves installing low greenhouse gas emitting Reverse Osmosis (RO) Water Plants powered by Photovoltaic (PVRO) systems. This initiative aims to reduce the wood fuel consumption of traditional stove users by providing clean drinking water to local communities in Pakistan.
The project targets areas with insufficient access to safe drinking water (SDW) due to poor water quality, specifically within the geographical boundary of Sindh, Pakistan. United Energy Group Limited (UEGL) fully financed the implementation of this project.
By implementing the project, the use and demand for fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass, which would have been used to boil water for purification, are decreased. This directly leads to a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions and has positive implications for users' health.
RO Plants are installed in remote and arid areas where residents either fetch water from distant irrigation canals or rely on groundwater sources. So the baseline scenario, prior to project implementation, involved households using firewood in traditional cookstoves to meet their boiling water needs.
The initial phase includes the implementation of 18 plants, with plans to introduce more during the crediting period to further expand the project's impact. With the capacity to meet the water demands of over 45,000 residents across Sindh, the project is a significant step toward addressing the regional water crisis.
The operation of these water treatment plants is projected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by an average of 17,833 tCO2e per year over ten years（22-June-2023 to 21-June-2033）
vcs-5389:
This grouped project will carry out the large-scale reforestation of Brazil. Carbon dioxide removals will be generated by the establishment of forest cover, through both tree planting and assisted natural regeneration (ANR), on previously degraded pasture land. 

A diversity of species will be selected for planting, based on their survival rates, stress tolerance, and GHG removal potential. Endangered species will also be included in the species selected for planting. In areas selected for ANR, the project will implement activities to ensure regeneration success after cattle are removed, such as installation of firebreaks and control of invasive plants and insects.

The project will reforest pastureland previously used for cattle ranching. Mombak will obtain land rights at each project instance via direct purchase of the property or by establishing strategic rural partnership agreements with land owners. 

The first project activity instance (PAI), also referred to as the Turmalina farm, will generate an estimated total of 586,275 tCO2e removals over the 10 year ex-ante period specified in the methodology, with an estimated annual average of 58,627 tCO2e removals over the 10 year period.
vcs-539: Liaoning Kangping Furaoshan Wind Power Project (hereafter referred as the proposed project) is located in Kangping County, Liaoning Province, Northeast China. Totally 66 Goldwind 50/750 wind turbines with a nominal capacity of 750 kW have been installed, providing a total capacity of 49.5 MW. With an average electricity supply of 97,486 MWh, the proposed project will achieve CO2 emission reductions by replacing electricity generated by fossil fuel fired power plants connected into Northeast China Power Grid. The proposed project is estimated to deliver 111,719 tonnes of CO2e emission reduction annually. It is noted the proposed project has an annual theoretical generation of 138,277 MWh, while the annual electricity supply is 97,486 MWh.
vcs-5390:
The Caiarara REDD+, proposed by proponents Dow Brasil and Biofilica Ambipar Environmental Investments , is developed within the scope of REDD+ AUD, with the objective of promoting forest conservation and contributing to sustainable development. Located in the municipality of Breu Branco, in the state of Pará, Brazil, the project is spread across two properties with a project area of approximately 32,620 hectares in two farms.

The project activities include the protection and conservation of the forest in the project area, ensuring the preservation of local biodiversity and contributing to the mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions. In addition, the project generates socioeconomic benefits for the communities in the region, promoting sustainable initiatives that strengthen the quality of life and stimulate local development, while protecting natural resources and ecosystem services essential to the region.
vcs-5391:
The Colorado REDD AUD Project is located in the Baixo Amazonas mesoregion, in Prainha, Pará, Brazil, within the Arc of Deforestation where significant deforestation has occurred due to cattle ranching, agriculture, logging, infrastructure, and land speculation. The project is focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and enhancing carbon sequestration. It is currently in its implementation and continuous monitoring phase, with key milestones such as the establishment of monitoring systems in 2022, community training programs, and ongoing local support.
The project uses satellite image monitoring, fire prevention, and low-carbon agricultural techniques, including agroforestry systems, rotational grazing, and sustainable logging. These efforts aim to alleviate pressure on forests while educating the community and engaging stakeholders in adopting sustainable production methods. The project targets conservation by reducing emissions from deforestation and degradation, driven by economic activities such as cattle ranching, agriculture, and illegal logging, alongside insufficient conservation incentives.

Before the project began, the area faced unplanned deforestation due to the expansion of agriculture, cattle ranching, and illegal logging, exacerbating deforestation rates and leading to significant greenhouse gas emissions and ecosystem degradation. The project, proposed by Colorado, a company with years of sustainable forest management experience, aims to generate both socio-environmental and climate benefits.
Estimates based on historical averages project that the project will reduce 30,271.38 tCO2e annually over 16,889.85 hectares of Amazon rainforest. Over the 2022-2027 crediting period, the total estimated reduction is 275,315.42 tCO2e. These estimates will be verified through ongoing monitoring. In the first monitoring period (2022–2024), the project achieved an average annual reduction of 53,555.76 tCO2e, totaling 160,667.28 tCO2e.
vcs-5392:
“The regenerative and eco-oriented agriculture project in Ukraine” is the first initiative entirely developed and managed by Ukrainian team to support national farmers in adopting eco-friendly and regenerative agricultural practices. Aligned with the Agricultural Land Management (ALM) category and Verra’s VM0042 (v2.1) methodology, this project focuses on improving soil health, increasing carbon sequestration, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

By transitioning from traditional farming methods to regenerative approaches, the project aims to enhance soil quality while contributing to global ecological balance through improved carbon storage and strengthened resilience to the impacts of climate change.

The Carbonex team provides comprehensive support to participating farmers, including consultations, training and technical assistance. Collaboration with the National University of Life and Environmental Sciences of Ukraine ensures the implementation of best practices tailored to local conditions. Beyond its environmental benefits, the project strengthens the economic sustainability of Ukrainian agricultural communities.
vcs-5393:
El proyecto se localiza en el Municipios de Santa Barbara, en el Departamento de Santa Barbara y está formado por 12 Aldeas, tiene una extensión geográfica de 13,517.31 hectáreas.
Protección, restauración, silvicultura y producción forestal, conservación de biodiversidad, evangelización, desarrollo local y ayuda humanitaria.
vcs-5394:
The Kowen Antami REDD+ Project aims to protect two of its protected areas: Yanachaga Chemillén National Park and San Matías–San Carlos Protection Forest.
The Consortium, comprising two indigenous community organizations and DRIS (DESARROLLO RURAL SUSTENTABLE), has been granted a 20-year administration contract to manage these areas. The project aims to reduce deforestation and forest degradation, mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, and improve the capacity of local communities to adapt to climate change.
The project prioritizes reducing deforestation and forest degradation, with a focus on addressing threats from agriculture, road construction, and forest fires. To achieve this, the project will strengthen governance, implement conservation agreements, and establish a financially sustainable strategy. The project is guided by the REDD+ Indigena Amazonica (Perú) guidelines to ensure the protection of indigenous communities and the environment.
vcs-5395:
The proposed VCS-WRC project is a grouped project centered on the rewetting and restoration of drained peatlands in the Republic of Ireland. 

Historically, these peatlands have been used for livestock grazing, crop production and peat extraction. To achieve these purposes, the water tables were lowered by creating drainage channels. This drainage caused a degradation in peatland vegetation and the overall ecological functionality of these habitats, reducing in biodiversity. Next to this, increased oxidation of peatlands results in higher GHG emissions.

This grouped project aims to restore these habitats by blocking the drainage channels and parallel field drains with the use of different types of dams. This will prevent water outflow and with existing precipitation and groundwater inflow the water table will rise again to reflect natural peatland levels, allowing spontaneous recovery of peatland vegetation.

Through these activities, the grouped project expects to generate a reduction in GHG emissions during the project crediting period, as the rewetting of peatlands reduces both the oxidation of the soil as well as the outflow of dissolved and particulate soil organic matter (DOC and POC). Next to this, the return of the peatland vegetation cover, enhanced by the recovered wet conditions of the site, will sequester additional atmospheric carbon and store it in the soil.

Grouped project activities are implemented and monitored according to the VCS methodology VM0036, Methodology for Rewetting Drained Temperate Peatlands.

The initial Project Activity Instance included in this grouped project covers 708 ha of drained peatland near Bangor Erris, in County Mayo. The net GHG reduction due to project activities is expected to be 84633 tCO2eq over the 40 years duration of the PAI, equating to 1296 tCO2e per year.
vcs-5396:
The Government of Liberia and Fauna & Flora have initiated the development of a REDD+ Project in partnership with local communities in the Wonegizi Proposed Protected Area in North-west Liberia to respond collaboratively to the drivers of deforestation and to protect and conserve the forests and their biodiversity and ecosystem services for the benefice of forest communities.
The core technologies/measures being implemented by the project for generating the GHG emission reductions are:
The clarification of land rights in the project area following the Liberia Land Rights Act of 2018
The long-term conservation of the area in agreement with stakeholders and associated participatory land use and co-management planning.
The patrolling and biomonitoring of the project area.
The development and implementation of a sustainable livelihoods programme for local communities to address the primary deforestation drivers and create tangible benefits from their effort to protect and sustainably manage their natural resources.
Nationally, the project supports Liberia in developing the policy frameworks necessary to access carbon finance, to help replicate and scale up forest protection that drives more effective livelihood improvement and poverty alleviation, and to deliver on its international commitments to reduce the impact of climate change.
The project will conserve the forest against a deforestation baseline, creating emission reductions through avoided unplanned deforestation (AUD). The implementation of the core technologies/measures commenced from 1st January 2022 in the Wonegizi Proposed Protected Area. It is estimated that this will result in total emission reductions ranging from 4,591,936 tCO2e (114,798 per year) and 7,556,674 tCO2e (188,917 per year) at 65% and 85% project effectiveness respectively over the 40-year project crediting period.
vcs-5397:
The Impact Forestry Initiative addresses critical challenges in forest management and carbon sequestration across Estonia, Sweden, and Latvia by implementing extended rotation forestry and Improved Forest Management (IFM) practices. These practices increase carbon storage, restore biodiversity, and enhance forest resilience, targeting private lands across a combined forest area of 240,000 hectares.

European forests, covering 39% of the continent, face degradation due to historic reliance on clearcutting and climate change impacts, leading to a 97% loss of old-growth forests and significant carbon sink declines. Estonia’s LULUCF sector, for instance, has shifted from a carbon sink to a net emitter, releasing 2.9 Mt CO₂e in 2021. Latvia’s clearcutting rates and Sweden’s 21% tree cover loss further illustrate the urgency for action.

The initiative transitions from standard rotation clearcutting to selective harvesting and extended cycles, reducing soil carbon emissions by 25–30% while fostering natural regeneration. Improved practices aim to sequester 4–7 tonnes CO₂e per hectare annually, contributing an average annual reduction of 2,374,939 tonnes CO₂e during the crediting period.

Technologies/Measures
Extended rotation and selective harvesting enhance forest health, biodiversity, and carbon storage. Natural regeneration promotes ecosystem resilience without replanting, reducing reliance on clearcutting, which contributes 100–200 tonnes CO₂e per hectare emissions in current scenarios.

Social & Environmental Co-Benefits
The initiative aligns with UN SDGs by supporting biodiversity, improving soil health by 10–15%, and fostering sustainable livelihoods for landowners. Grouped project approaches ensure scalability and empower landowners with access to carbon markets, creating a replicable model for sustainable forestry in Europe.
vcs-5398:
The La Florida Afforestation Project with Exotic and Native Species in Northeast Argentina is an Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) initiative targeting degraded grasslands with both native and exotic species. The project is located on a rural property named La Florida, currently used for extensive livestock grazing in the Province of Corrientes, northeast Argentina, in the ecotone between the Campos y Malezales and Atlantic Forest ecoregions.
The overarching goal of the project is to promote innovative afforestation management by integrating exotic and native species. The project aims to produce high-quality wood and other non-wood products.
The project covers a total area of 2,390 hectares, with the effective plantation area consisting of 1,559 hectares of converted and/or degraded grassland. Of the planted area, 63% (978 hectares) will be cultivated with a mix of exotic and native species from the Atlantic Forest ecoregion (known as Selva Paranaense in Argentina), while the remaining 37% (581 hectares) will be planted with non-invasive pine species. The remainder of the area will be preserved and designated as a high conservation value zone.
The pure-pine plantation designs will be replanted following the first harvesting cycle (year 35). In the mixed pine-native plantation designs, after the pine harvesting, no further pine replanting will occur, and only native trees will remain in perpetuity, allowing for assisted colonization by native species.
The project seeks to generate an average greenhouse gas (GHG) benefit for the environment of approximately 15,151 tCO2e per year over the 40-year project duration, with an estimated Long-Term Average (LTA) of 606,036 tCO2e. The project is developed by GMF Latinoamericana, a well-experienced Nature-Based Solutions (NBS) project developer in Argentina.
vcs-5399:
Regenerating Rajasthan - Climate Aligned Economic Development is an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation project under VM0047 located initially in the districts of Jaipur, Udaipur and Rajsamand in the state of Rajasthan, North-West India.  The project is implemented and monitored by Mewar Climate Regenerative Pvt. Ltd. in partnership with NGO, Arpan Seva Sansthan. Working with Gram Panchayats, democratically elected local village committees, and smallholder farmers the initial Project Activity Instance (PAI) will regenerate 236 hectares of degraded land. This first PAI is forecast to sequester 84,561 tCO2e over 30 years, equating to 2,819 tCO2e per year.
 
The overall Project objective is to regenerate over 29,700 hectares on community and private lands through planting c. 24.4 million trees (predominantly native and fruit species) to generate 6,691,984 million tCO2e in total GHG emissions removals over 30 years from 2023 to 2053, equating to 223,061 tCO2e per year.
vcs-540: The CGN Inner Mongolia Huitengliang Phase¢ñWind Farm Project, developed by CGN Wind Power Co., Ltd, is a grid connected renewable energy project in the Huitengliang area of Xilinguole League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, in the People¡¯s Republic of China. vcs-5400:
The project aimed to restore tidal wetlands through native mangrove communities by Restoring Wetland Ecosystems (RWE) and Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) activities. The proposed project activity titled “Mangrove Restoration and Biodiversity Conservation for Coastal communities of India” involves sequestration and storage of carbon (Blue Carbon) through mangrove restoration in degraded coastal land with a focus on coastal community of India. The first instance of the program’s objective is to restore 4,500 ha of degraded coastal area in two years (1st year 2,000 ha; 2nd year 2,500 ha) with native mixed mangrove species plantation in human dominated low-lying landscape of the districts of North & South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur (East Midnapore) situated in coastal belt of the state of West Bengal, India. 
This mangrove restoration project will provide a range of ecosystem services:
•	Reduction in GHGs emissions by planting native mixed mangrove species (SDG 13)
•	Coastal protection from storm surges, cyclone, sea-level rise and coastal erosions (SDG 14)
•	Increased vegetation cover, habitat for wildlife & biodiversity enhancement (SDG 15)
•	Water quality regulation through nutrient recycling (SDG 6)
•	Supporting fisheries and underwater life (SDG 14)
•	Ecotourism and sustainable livelihood (SDG 1, 2 & 8)
The project area hosts a population of 44,26,259 spreading over 19 community blocks as per 2011 census out of which ~ 40% falls under Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe category. Population density in this region is 996 per sq km. 38% of its total population are main workers whereas the rest are non-working and marginal working class. Around 15 % of the population of Sundarbans is multidimensionally poor as per Niti Aayog’s latest Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI, 2023). Large-scale community-based mangrove restoration projects can provide long term climate benefit and sustainable livelihood opportunities for these communities.
vcs-5401:
The project aims to restore and revitalize 20,000 hectares of degraded agricultural land privately owned by marginal and smallholder farmers, empowering them to adopt diverse, native agroforestry systems. These systems are designed to address both ecological and economic challenges in the region, fostering long-term resilience and sustainability.
Key interventions include training farmers in regenerative, climate-resilient agroforestry and agriculture practices tailored to the tropical dryland ecosystem. This involves providing access to high-value saplings of commercial fruit trees, timber species, and non-timber forest products, carefully selected to optimize carbon sequestration and enhance vital ecosystem services such as biodiversity restoration, soil health improvement, and water retention.
To combat decades of soil degradation caused by unsustainable monoculture farming, the project will implement advanced soil revitalization techniques. These include the integration of biochar to improve soil fertility, increase organic carbon content, and enhance long-term productivity. Regenerative agricultural practices, such as cover cropping and composting, will also be promoted to restore soil health, increase organic matter, and prevent erosion. Biochar application will complement these efforts by enhancing water retention and nutrient efficiency, critical for this drought-prone region.

Beyond ecological restoration, the project aims to uplift the socio-economic well-being of farmers. By diversifying income streams through the production of high-value horticulture crops, and other NTFP products, the project seeks to significantly increase farmers' annual incomes. Additionally, training programs and capacity-building initiatives will equip farmers with the skills and knowledge necessary to adopt and sustain regenerative agroforestry and agriculture practices, creating a replicable model for large-scale landscape restoration.
vcs-5402:
The Improved Forest Management Project uses the Extended Rotation Age (ERA) strategy to enhance carbon sequestration, reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and generate social and biodiversity benefits. ERA promotes denser wood production, increasing medium- and long-lived wood products while reducing short-lived ones. This approach reduces GHG emissions and ensures long-term carbon stock maintenance, contributing to lasting climate benefits.  
The grouped project area encompasses the Mesopotamia region of Argentina, covering the forest basins of the provinces of Misiones, Corrientes and Entre Ríos, and the Delta and Islands of the Paraná region. The first Project Activity Instance (PAI) covers 537.7 hectares of the Villa Zenaida farm, Gobernador Virasoro, Corrientes. The strategy is to extend the cutting cycle from 18 to 40 years, therefore, it is estimated that the first PAI will reduce or remove 209,130 tCO2eq over for the 43-years crediting period, averaging 4,863 tCO2eq annually.  
Moreover, the first PAI protects 2,060.5 hectares of High Conservation Value areas to safeguard endangered species and promote biodiversity, including 32 threatened flora species, 18 threatened bird species, and 5 threatened mammal species. Additionally, biological corridors will facilitate species movement, enhance ecological connectivity, and preserve ecosystem services.  
For local communities, the project provides training, scholarships, and internships to foster academic and professional growth, benefitting 129 scholarship recipients, 86 interns, and 53 trained workers over the 43-years crediting period of the first PAI. It also generates over 30 permanent jobs annually, improves healthcare access for 120 workers and their families, and collaborates with organizations to combat child malnutrition.
vcs-5403:
The Project Reforestation in Northern Argentina focuses on reforestation in the northern region of Argentina. It promotes innovative reforestation management on deforested lands, combining native and non-native species to establish productive forests with integrated biodiversity conservation areas.
The grouped project includes Dry and Humid Chaco, Yungas, and Selva Paranaense ecorregions, which together cover 78 million hectares. These regions have experienced severe deforestation since 1970, losing over 12 million hectares of native forest, leading to degraded landscapes and compromising ecosystem services.
The Project aims to reforest areas that have been continuously cleared for extensive cattle grazing. Activities include Eucalyptus species and clones, and native species like Algarrobo that make up 15% of the plantations and are strategically located in areas of high conservation value. These efforts aim to produce high-quality timber while restoring degraded ecosystems.
The first Project Activity Instance (PAI) will be carried out on 6,954 hectares in part of Altos del Guayacan farm in Patiño Department, Formosa Province. In this PAI 2,339 hectares will be destinated for conservation activities, while 4,615 hectares will be reforested and expected to achieve ≈1,196,590 tCO2e in net GHG reductions over 35 years, providing a yearly GHG benefit of ≈ 34,188.3 tCO2e.
vcs-5404: The Atebubu and Wiase Forest Landscape Restoration Project in Ghana's Bono East Region restores degraded landscapes and builds community resilience. Partnering with local communities, iNovaLand, NGPTA, AstraZeneca, APSD, and NDF, the project implements natural forest restoration and agroforestry on smallholder farms. This initiative aims to plant more than 6 million trees, restore 15,580 hectares, and remove over 4 million tonnes of CO2e over 30 years. It also seeks to create sustainable livelihoods, promote biodiversity, and enhance ecosystem health through improved soil, water quality, and watershed replenishment. A robust governance structure ensures stakeholder engagement and effective project management.

Tongyi CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize
the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Tongyi coal mine which is a
working coal mine for power generation and supply electricity to the coal mine where the
Project is located for internal consumption. And the waste heat from the generators will
be recovered by waste heat boilers to provide free hot water to the coal mine.The
Project is located in Tongyi coal mine, Songjiazhuang Village, Guanshan Town, Pingding
County, Yangquan City, Shanxi Province, P.R.China. The Project Owner is Pingding
County Yonder Coal Mine Methane Utilization Co., Ltd. Prior to the implementation of
the project, Tongyi coal mine was equipped with CMM extraction facilities and all
extracted CMM was vented into the atmosphere directly. The electricity consumed at
coal mines was imported from North China Power Grid (NCPG). The heat was provided
by waste coal boilers. Baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the
implementation of the project activity. The Project aims to utilize the extracted CMM with
low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane
(CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4)
emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in
the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of
electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the
NCPG. It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 14- September-2024 to13-September-2034), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 172,394 tCO2e and the total emission reductions will be 1,723,940
tCO2e in the 10-year of crediting period.

Fuyang Dafengye E-waste Disassembly and Resource Recycling Project aims to produce recycled metals and plastics by recycling E-waste (refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, TV sets, computers and other small household appliances, etc). The project is located in No. 819, north side of Wanfo Lake Road, east side of Yu'an Road, Jingjiu Street, Fuyang Economic Development Zone, Anhui Province, China, and is invested and owned by Fuyang Dafengye Renewable Resources Co., Ltd.
The project includes eight disassembly lines for refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, computers, LCD TV sets, CRT TV sets and computer monitors, and small household appliances respectively, as well as a Plastic Pelletizing Line. vcs-5412: In the proposed project, about 30,000 ha of cropland in Xiangzhou District, Xiangyang City, Hubei Province, China, will be managed by a package of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) practices, including tillage reduction, straw returning, etc., which minimize disturbance to the soil, therefore improve resilience of the soil, sequester carbon and increase soil organic carbon.

The CoolPath Veles California Rangeland Ecological Restoration Project aims to restore degraded rangeland ecosystems across California, addressing the widespread ecological damage caused by invasive annual grasses, altered fire regimes, and overgrazing. Using the Verra VM0042 methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management, the project implements sustainable land management practices, including the application of Title 14-compliant compost, improved grazing management, and re-seeding of native plants. These measures are designed to enhance soil organic carbon levels, improve soil quality, and restore the biodiversity and functionality of California’s rangelands.

The primary intervention involves applying Title 14-compliant compost to degraded soils to increase soil organic carbon, stabilize soil structure, and improve water retention and nutrient availability. The compost application also provides a sustainable use for organic waste, aligning with California's Senate Bill 1383, which mandates the diversion of organic waste from landfills. Compost application not only prevents methane emissions from organic waste disposal but also enhances soil health, promoting the growth of native perennial grasses that have been displaced by invasive annual species over the past 300 years. This approach is supported by extensive scientific research, which demonstrates the long-term stability of carbon sequestered in rangeland soils through compost application.

The degradation of California’s rangelands has been driven by historical factors, including overstocking of livestock during the California Gold Rush and the introduction of non-native grasses. These invasive grasses, characterized by shallow root systems, outcompete native perennial grasses, reducing soil stability and productivity. The Vale do Rio Branco REDD+ Grouped Project is an AFOLU project located in Roraima State, in the Brazilian Amazon Biome. Developed by ZEG Florestal, it is a grouped project under Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) category, within Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project type and, so far, is not covered by a jurisdictional REDD+ program. Its first instance covers an area of approximately 5,926 hectares in Caracaraí municipality, southern Roraima State. Initially, the first instance belongs to the Vale Verde property, a 14,029 hectares property located along the Branco Riverbank, approximately 35 km from the BR-174 highway, that connects Manaus, Amazonas state capital, to Boa Vista, Roraima State capital, which provides the main land access to the city. The farm was previously managed by Madeireira Vale Verde (timber company) from 2006 to 2018, during which time Sustainable Forest Management was performed in the area. Operations ceased and the property was acquired
by a rural producer, who is the current owner. Promoting the conservation of forest land and reducing net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by preventing associated risks of degradation, deforestation, and forest fires are the project's main objectives. To achieve this, the project seeks to implement forest monitoring through remote sensing, local surveillance and firefighting efforts. In terms of biodiversity, the project will introduce technologies for monitoring flora and fauna, establishing a comprehensive biodiversity inventory and database. Additionally, the project will develop opportunities concerning bioeconomic development in the region, aiming to contribute to socioeconomic improvements and general well-being in local communities.

Thus, the project activities deliver electricity as a substitute to displace fossil fuels, reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions.

vcs-5424:
Ecofy is dedicated to advancing the global shift towards a net-zero carbon future by providing targeted financial solutions for electric vehicle (EV) projects. This project activity focuses on financing the purchase of EVs to promote the adoption of green technologies.
The project implements several key measures like financing EVs by providing competitive financial products to individuals and businesses for purchasing EVs to support widespread adoption and offering expert guidance to organizations on transitioning to sustainable practices and technologies.
The Ecofy project commenced on 26 July 2023, with financing of the Electric Vehicles. The project is expected to maintain continuous operation throughout its crediting period, which extends from 2023 to 2033. Operating on a pan-India scale, the project targets urban and suburban areas with high potential for electric vehicle (EV) adoption. It aims to achieve substantial GHG emission reductions by financing EVs to replace fossil fuel-powered vehicles. The baseline scenario before the project involved high CO2 emissions due to reliance on conventional vehicles and insufficient EV infrastructure. The project is estimated to reduce 18,618 tCO2e annually, with a total of approximately 186,182 metric tons over the 10-year period. During the monitoring period, the project has already achieved verified reductions of 4,101 tCO2e, demonstrating its effective contribution to lowering emissions.
vcs-5427: The Community-Based Mangrove Conservation and Restoration project in Guinea, the second initiative under development by West Africa Blue, focuses on restoring and conserving mangrove ecosystems in the southern Guinean prefecture of Forécariah. With an emphasis on sustainable community development, biodiversity conservation, and climate change adaptation, the project aims to generate greenhouse gas reductions and removals by reducing mangrove deforestation and restoring degraded areas, respectively. Forécariah, once dominated by mangrove forests, is largely covered in converted rice farming areas that are now facing severe coastal erosion, saltwater intrusion, and flooding, which threaten local rice and vegetable farming livelihoods. As wood becomes scarce and expensive to buy from other areas, additional livelihoods such as bread baking and salt production are similarly abandoned. To address these challenges, the project will implement a range of activities including efficient cookstoves, improved fish smoking ovens, solar salt, and the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), alongside education and awareness campaigns rooted in the principles of Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC). Spanning 22,600 ha of mangrove forest for conservation and 4,732 ha of degraded area identified for restoration, the project will contribute to preserving critical mangrove habitats, protecting endemic species, and improving local livelihoods, while reducing the impacts of deforestation and climate change.
