NOVAAGRI, founded in 2008, is a visionary player in the Agribusiness sector, specializing in independent storage and logistical services for agricultural commodities in domestic and international markets. The company’s strong commitment to the environment is evidenced by its aim for a 50% reduction in
greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2050, which is supported by its carbon projects, all of which allocate a portion of its financial returns to social actions in nearby communities.

A key example of NovaAgri's strategy is its collaboration with the Grupo Progresso farms for the CULTIVAR PROGRESSO REDD+ PROJECT, located in the Piauí State across the municipalities of Uruçuí, Sebastião Leal, Landri Sales and Antônio Almeida, covering a biodiversity hotspot rich in carbon reservoirs.

The project centers on AUD (Avoiding Unplanned Deforestation) mechanisms, adhering to REDD+ principles and VERRA's VM0015 methodology. The baseline acknowledges the intense deforestation pressure in Piauí's ecosystems, induced by agents such as illegal land grabbers and small-scale farmers who rely heavily on deforestation as an agricultural practice. Additional contributing factors include drivers such as the high market value of deforested lands in the state and the elevated prices of agricultural commodities, all factors compounded by widespread non-compliance with Brazilian environmental legislation.

The project expects to avoid net emissions of 2,629,994 tCO2e, which means an average of 43,833 tCO2e per year and 25,339 hectares preserved during a horizon of 60 years. The total GHG emission reductions generated in the monitoring period is 31,376.
vcs-5431:
Baoshan East Hope Swine Farm AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) applies one animal waste management system (AWMS i.e. Enclosed Anaerobic Digester, the same below) to treat the manure from the swine farm in Baoshan City, Yunnan Province, which is owned by Baoshan East Hope Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd (hereinafter called the project owner). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
This project is expected to generate approximately 6.04*104 m3 of biogas per year. This biogas will be collected and utilized for power generation. The electricity generated will only be used for the daily operation of AWMS and will not be provided to other users. For the sake of conservatism, the baseline emissions from electricity generation have been ignored.
The project activity will reduce GHG emissions in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 75,479 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 754,790 tCO2e during the fixed 10-year crediting period.
vcs-5432: The Kwahu Landscape Restoration Project is a grouped project that will restore deforested lands across the indigenous territories of the Kwahu Traditional Council in the Eastern Region of Ghana. The approximately 50,000-ha grouped project will remove, on average, an estimated net 750,000 tCO2e per year. At the local level, the project is improving farmers’ livelihoods through our unique plantain-led agroforestry system resulting in significant increases in family incomes and diversification of incomes. The project is generating significant new employment opportunities and increasing communities' capacity to adapt to the effects of climate change. The project will support a wide selection of community-led development projects which may include such solutions as boreholes for safe water, rehabilitation of health clinics, and schools, noting that communities will ultimately select their own priorities for such projects. Furthermore, the project will enhance biodiversity by increasing forest cover, managing bushfire events and expanding healthy natural habitats.
vcs-5433: Rainforest Builder Ltd. is an integrated tropical forest restoration company founded in 2022, incorporated in the UK with operations in Ghana and Sierra Leone. The company was founded to pioneer tropical forest ecosystem restoration as a commercial undertaking, by combining the best restoration science with professional forestry industry practice to deliver ecosystem restoration at with unprecedented quality and scale. Rainforest Builder’s projects, in Ghana and  other countries, aim to return degraded, formerly- forested lands to primary levels of biomass, biodiversity, and structural complexity rapidly and resiliently, in partnership with a range of stakeholders.
vcs-5434:
The Grouped Project, developed by Duferco Mobility S.r.l. with the support of Carbonsink (a South Pole Ltd. company), aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by replacing internal combustion vehicles with BEVs and PHEVs thanks to the deployment of new public access charging stations in Italy.
The project, that follows the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) v.4.7, is developed in Italy with the VM0038 v.1.0 methodology, which enables the reduction of GHG emissions through the installation of charging stations and the consequent provision of electricity for charging electric vehicles as passenger cars and other LDVs (Light Duty Vehicles).
Over time, the Grouped Project has the potential to expand, involving not only Duferco Mobility (the proponent) but also any other Charging Point Operators (CPOs) that are already operating in the e-mobility sector or that will want to foster the E-Mobility in Italy thanks to the growth of the national charging network and at the same time impacting also in the relevant sustainability goals. 
In its initial phase, the project aims to achieve at least a reduction of 7,966 tCO₂eq per year.
vcs-5436: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Catanduva Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane (CH4 at the Centro de Gerenciamento de Resíduos (CGR) Catanduva landfill landfill (hereby termed “Catanduva landfill”) through destruction of collected LFG in a high temperature open flare and utilization of collected LFG as gaseous fuel in a set of 2 engine-generator sets (to be gradually implemented) which represent the major components of an electricity generation infrastructure with a total combined nameplate installed capacity of about 2.8 MW.
vcs-5437:
The Rewetting of the Paltinskoye Peatland project is a large-scale ecological restoration initiative aimed at mitigating climate change by restoring degraded peatlands in Perm Krai, Russia. Peatlands are among the most efficient carbon sinks on Earth, yet when drained, they become significant sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, releasing CO₂, methane (CH₄), and nitrous oxide (N₂O). This project addresses these challenges by rewetting 212 hectares of the Paltinskoye peatland in Phase I, preventing further peat degradation, reducing fire risks, and restoring natural carbon sequestration processes. 
By restoring the peatland’s natural hydrology, this project is estimated to sequester 112,522 tCO₂e over a 40-year period (2026–2065) in Phase I. Beyond carbon benefits, the project contributes to biodiversity conservation, enhances ecosystem services such as water filtration and flood control, and supports local communities through job creation and education on sustainable land management.
vcs-5438:
The objective of ART Line T4 in Yibin, Sichuan (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is to establish an efficient, reliable, rapid and convenient mass rapid transit system based on ART in the urban area of Yibin, located in Sichuan Province, People’s Republic of China. With a total length of 46.69 km and 22 stations, it serves as a vital artery connecting various urban functional areas. By providing convenient transportation options for commuters and residents throughout the day and replacing part of the conventional modes of transportation, the ART Line T4 helps alleviate traffic congestion, reduce air pollution, and enhance overall mobility within the city. 
The project is managed and operated by Yibin Autonomous-rail Transit Co.,LTD. The geographical boundary of the project is the urban area of Yibin. Gases included are CO2, CH4 and N2O.
The project boundary includes Yibin ART Line T4 and the entire urban area of Yibin as well as the power plants connected to Southwest China Power Grid.
The pre-project scenario is the usage of buses, passenger cars, taxis and motorcycles as well as non-motorized transport for transit purposes. No rail-based urban mass transit was available in this route prior to the project, and public transport relied exclusively on conventional bus systems. The baseline scenario is the continuation of the use of pre-project modes of transport
vcs-5439:
The project is located in the department of Ucayali, province of Atalaya, and district of Sepahua. To the north, it borders Villa Esperanza Association, Hormiga Association, Remoque Native Community, and Jerusalén Hamlet; to the east, it borders a forest area (District of Sepahua); to the west, it borders Santa Isabel Native Community and Unión Miraflores Capirona Native Community; and to the south, it borders Sepahua Native Community, Fundo Llanero, Sheboja Native Community, and Triunfo Population Center.
The main objectives of the project are to prevent forest degradation in an area of 54,924 ha by replacing activities related to timber-oriented forestry operations with forest protection, estimating a net average reduction of GHG emissions of 121,323 tCO₂e/year, with a total of 4,852,908 tCO₂e over 40 years.
The total cessation of extractive activities for timber purposes is established in the areas designated for the project (project area), including related production and commercialization activities. The project is based on strategic pillars designed to increase the economic benefits for communities by improving routine, cultural, and ancestral practices, as well as contributing to a better quality of life by facilitating access to essential basic services such as health, education, potable water, electricity, and other vital needs. As part of the project's activities, technical training in leadership will be provided to strengthen the capacities of community representatives, enabling them to make well-informed decisions that benefit their communities.
vcs-544: The Gansu Guazhou Daliangxi Wind Power Project, developed by Gansu CGN Wind Power Co., Ltd, is a grid connected renewable energy project in Guazhou County,  Gansu Province, in the People¡¯s Republic of China. It involves the installation of 33 turbines, each of which has a rated output of 1500 kW, providing a total installed capacity of 49.5 MW, with a predicted power supplied to the grid of 115,144 MWh per annum.
vcs-5440: This project seeks to enhance key climate indicators, such as soil carbon sequestration and emission reduction, in woody crop farms located within the Mediterranean basin. These farms currently employ conventional management practices characterized by the export of plant residues, bare soils, minimal organic matter application, and frequent tillage. Such practices contribute to soil degradation, increased greenhouse gas emissions, and a decline in biodiversity. However, this scenario also presents a unique opportunity to improve agroecosystems by implementing sustainable management practices. Through the systematic adoption, monitoring, and reporting of these practices, the project will gather valuable data that supports both the scalability of these interventions and their positive environmental impact. Continuous monitoring and adaptive management will ensure ongoing improvement, while financial support will be provided to farms via the generation of carbon credits. These credits can be used to offset residual emissions from corporate activities, helping to meet ambitious net-zero targets. In addition to mitigating environmental impacts, the project will foster biodiversity restoration and promote social benefits by strengthening local agricultural systems, improving farm resilience, promoting effective knowledge transfer and creating new economic opportunities for rural communities.
vcs-5441:
To address South Africa's persistent electricity crisis, the VCS grouped project is designed to harness the country’s abundant sunlight and deliver a sustainable, reliable energy solution. Strategically located in the geographical boundary of South Africa i.e. the Host country, the grouped project aims to reshape the nation’s energy landscape by generating clean and reliable renewable energy. At its core, the grouped project seeks to tackle critical challenges such as electricity distribution inefficiencies and load-sharing imbalances, providing a much-needed boost to the national grid while reducing reliance on carbon-intensive fossil fuels.

The project is committed to environmental protection and building a climate resilient energy system. By harnessing advanced solar technology, clean energy will be generated relieving the strain on South Africa's national power grid. This initiative will reduce reliance on coal, lower carbon emissions, and contribute to a cleaner, more sustainable future
vcs-5442:
Starting in 2022, the Cooperativa Agraria Forestal y de Servicios Ambientales Madre de Dios (COOPAFSAMAD) together with forest concession holders and rural landowners, have joined together to implement the PROYECTO REDD+ JUNTOS POR LOS BOSQUES, whose objective is to reduce deforestation in the forests of the project participants, who are forest concession holders and rural forest property owners. This project aims to generate and sell carbon credits to generate income and finance activities for sustainable forest management and conservation, and improve the livelihoods of the participants and their families, and communities that live and depend on these forests.
Climate Objective: Reduce CO2 emissions caused by deforestation in the project area, which would have occurred in the absence of the project, by strengthening the technical capacity of the participants to monitor and protect their forests against deforestation and forest degradation threats (e.g, the conversion of forest into farmland for agriculture, cattle ranching, mining or other land uses). 
Community Objective: Strengthen the organizational capacity of COOPAFSAMAD and the capacity of forest concession holders and rural landowners for sustainable management, forest management, and production and marketing of their products. Biodiversity Objective: Preserve the biodiversity and ecosystem services of the forests within the project area, especially species listed as threatened and high conservation value (HVC). The Project is located in three provinces (Manu, Tambopata and Tahuamanu) of the Department of Madre de Dios, and in the province of Paucartambo in the Department of Cusco, Peru.
vcs-5443: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Santos Landfill Gas Project” (hereinafter termed “project activity”) encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) at the landfill site hereby termed “Terrestre landfill” through combustion in a high temperature enclosed flare and utilization of collected LFG as gaseous fuel in engine-generator sets (engines) of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of about 5.716 MW).
vcs-5444: The Solareff Rooftop PV Project consists of the installation and operation of solar photovoltaic (PV) installations on the rooftops of commercial and semi-industrial facilities. The project reduces GHG emissions by displacing fossil fuel-based electricity from the national grid. The facilities utilise the majority of the electricity generated by the PV installations deployed across the Republic of South Africa.
vcs-5445:
The Noor 2 Street Lighting project marks a pivotal advancement in Abu Dhabi’s commitment to sustainability and energy efficiency, aligning with the UAE’s broader strategy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and achieve Net Zero by 2050. The project focuses on modernizing Abu Dhabi’s road lighting infrastructure with advanced, energy-efficient technology to significantly cut energy consumption and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

Under a long-term concession awarded by the Department of Municipalities & Transport (DMT) to Nojoom, the project involves the supply, installation, financing, operation, and maintenance of 133,473 existing high-pressure sodium (HPS) and metal halide (MH) luminaires. These will be replaced with state-of-the-art, energy-efficient LED luminaires. The new LED lights will be wirelessly connected to a central road lighting control system, enhancing operational efficiency and monitoring capabilities. 

The Noor 2 project spans a vast network of urban roads and highways across Abu Dhabi's mainland. It is structured into five distinct phases, each targeting a different geographical zone within the Emirate. This phased approach ensures efficient implementation and continuous operational functionality throughout the project’s lifecycle. 

The LED luminaires offer significantly higher energy efficiency compared to the traditional HPS and MH lights, leading to a substantial reduction in electricity consumption. Over the crediting period, the project is expected to save approximately 2,650 million kWh of electricity. These savings will translate into an average annual reduction of about 106,095 tons of CO2 emissions, contributing significantly to the UAE’s sustainability goals.
vcs-5446: Project Gamma aims to restore approximately 30 000 ha of deforested land in Selenge province, northern Mongolia, over the next 5-10 years. The project will reforest the land with native boreal species, e.g., scots pine and Siberian larch.  This project will not only contribute to the sequestration of green house gases (GHGs) but also support  biodiversity and the well-being local communities through employment and benefit sharing
vcs-5448: The proposed BlueRizon project, located along the Northern coast of Java across three Indonesian provinces (West Java, Central Java, and East Java), aims to generate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions and removals through increased biomass from tree plantations and enhanced soil organic carbon. The project focuses on restoring and conserving tidal wetlands and mangrove ecosystems, which will contribute to carbon sequestration, water and soil conservation, natural disaster prevention, and sustainable livelihood development for vulnerable communities. The goal is to create a carbon-livelihood landscape by revitalizing degraded tidal wetland ecosystems, improving both ecological and socio-economic resilience. Indonesia, home to the largest mangrove area and biodiversity globally, has seen over 70% of its mangroves degrade due to factors such as land-use changes, deforestation, and climate change impacts. This degradation has led to frequent floods, coastal erosion, loss of natural resources, food insecurity, and marginalization of local populations. Mangroves play a crucial role in carbon storage, with Indonesian mangroves being among the highest in the world for carbon accumulation. The project will restore approximately 3,323 ha of mangrove areas through planting new seedlings in coastal areas (80%), ponds (15%), and riverbanks (5%), with a focus on creating a blue carbon ecosystem that includes seagrass and coral reefs. The project will be implemented under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS - VM0033 Methodology) and the Climate, Community and Biodiversity (CCB) certification, with carbon sequestration estimated at 3,059,210 tCO2e over 30 years. With a focus on community involvement, the project will support over 3,000 households, enhancing local livelihoods through sustainable income-generating activities like silvo-fishery and mangrove-based businesses.
vcs-5449:
The Ecoprial Emission Avoidance Project was implemented by Asesorias Los Olivos S.A., located at Ruta U-400 Km 6, Osorno, Chile. It has been operational since 2023, generating energy and helping to prevent the emission of greenhouse gases (GHGs) into the atmosphere.

The Ecoprial plant receives organic waste from around 70 clients (milk, fishing, slaughterhouses and other industries), totalizing around 55,000 tones/year. 

The project consists of the implementation of anaerobic digesters to process the organic waste received at Ecoprial plant and use of the methane generated. By capturing methane, Ecoprial will use it for heat and power generating purposes (up to 0.360MW of installed capacity); therefore, reducing significantly the amount methane that would otherwise be released into the atmosphere.

Before project implementation, the industrial organic waste received by Ecoprial was directly disposed of into 4.5-meter-deep cells lined with HDPE geomembrane. Once these cells were fully filled, they were covered with soil and an additional layer of HDPE geomembrane.
vcs-545: The project activity is located in the district of Kutch, Gujarat, India. The project activity involves installation of 17 wind mills of varying capacities of 1.5 MW capacity (1 wind mill), 1.25 MW capacity (2 wind mills) and 0.6 MW capacity (14 wind mills) tuned to an aggregated capacity of 12.4 MW. The Seventeen wind mills are located in Suthri, Kadoli, Panchetiya, Chandrodi, Naransari and Khodasar villages of Kutch district. The proposed project would generate energy from wind resources thereby displacing, electricity generated using existing fossil fuel based power plants or future capacity additions in the State of Gujarat. Gujarat is a part of the country’s NEWNE Regional Grid.
vcs-5451:
The project activity aims to promote sustainable and resilient agricultural practices in Kenya’s arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs), which are increasingly affected by land degradation, erratic rainfall, and nutrient depletion. The project encourages the adoption of climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices such as organic farming, conservation tillage, agroforestry, crop rotation, and residue management. These practices are designed to enhance soil health, improve biodiversity, and optimize farming systems, leading to increased productivity and sustainability. 

By transitioning from conventional farming practices that rely heavily on chemical inputs, the project seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, restore soil organic carbon (SOC) levels, and support global climate goals. This initiative not only strengthens food security but also enhances the climate resilience of smallholder farmers, providing a scalable model for sustainable agriculture in resource-constrained regions.
vcs-5452:
The Monsoon Wind Power Project is situated in the Sekong and Attapeu Provinces of Lao PDR and represents the first cross-border onshore wind farm between Laos and Vietnam. Developed under a Memorandum of Understanding between the governments of both countries, the project facilitates the supply of renewable electricity from Lao PDR to Vietnam.

Utilizing advanced onshore wind technology, the project will achieve a total installed capacity of 600 MW, with an estimated annual electricity generation of 1,707 GWh. The generated power will primarily be transmitted to Vietnam’s grid via the Thanh My substation. By harnessing the region’s wind resources, the project will contribute to clean energy production, reducing dependence on fossil fuels and enhancing regional energy security.

Beyond renewable energy generation, through the community development program, the project is expected to support local infrastructure development and improve livelihoods in the Sekong and Attapeu provinces.
vcs-5453:
NativState’s Afforestation in the Mississippi River Alluvial Valley Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) Project (the “Project”) seeks to restore forests on over 20,000 hectares in the lower Mississippi River alluvial valley and portions of adjacent ecoregions by 2030. To accomplish this ambitious goal, NativState engages and contracts with private landowners to restore forests on grazing lands and/or marginal farm ground that is no longer economically viable for traditional row crop farming. The grouped Project will restore high-quality forests to bring value to private landowners and help achieve national and global GHG mitigation targets.

Project instances, or “Sites”, are prepared and planted with a mixture of native tree species, in consideration of landowner preferences, that are designed to store carbon, improve wildlife habitat, enhance biodiversity, and reestablish forest cover. After planting, sample plots are established and monitored using a combination of field and remote sensing measurements for survival, growth, and recruitment. The Project uses an area-based approach to quantify changes in carbon stocks. Changes in carbon stocks are compared against a baseline performance benchmark to conservatively estimate carbon removals. Changes in carbon stocks will be verified no later than every 5 years. 

The objective of the Project is to achieve GHG emission removals of CO2 through active reforestation of grazing lands or marginal farm ground by enhancing carbon sequestration in the form of woody biomass and organic matter in the soil. The Project aims to generate carbon credits under the VCS and the initial Project Sites are expected to remove approximately 590 mt CO2e annually or 35,429 mt CO2e over a 60-year crediting period.  Once fully implemented, the Project aims to remove approximately 148,000 mt CO2e annually or 8,880,000 mt CO2e over a 60-year crediting period.
vcs-5454:
The project aims to reduce carbon dioxide emissions related to the transportation of mining companies workers by replacing their fossil fuel-based fleets of buses by electric ones. The project activity is carried out by Transición Energética I SpA, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) responsible of financing this replacement of buses and making it possible to Chilean bus operators to use this kind of technology, since they don’t have the book value to buy this type of buses.
Different mining companies opened bidding processes for replacing part of the current operating diesel buses. The project, structured with Enel X, a local company with extensive knowledge in energetic solutions, won biddings for 3 mining sites in the north of Chile:
Compañía Minera del Pacífico (CMP): Operation in the Atacama Region
Codelco El Salvador Division: Operation in the Atacama Region
Codelco Radomiro Tomic Division: Operation in the Antofagasta Region
Prior to the implementation of the project, the workforce of the 3 mining companies was transported in diesel fuelled buses. There was not an appropriate infrastructure for using electric buses and, the high price of these, didn’t allow Chilean bus operators to invest in them or even access to financing through bank debt. Considering circulation permits
1, the percentage of electric buses operating in 2023 was 0% and 1.4% in the regions of the projects, which are Atacama Region and Antofagasta Region respectively.
The project achieves emissions reductions of carbon dioxide by replacing fuel buses by electric ones. In the 10-year crediting period, up to 121 buses will be operating which, considering the calculation of the applicable CDM Methodology AMS III C, will generate approximately 49,465 ������2�� reductions and an annual average GHG emission reduction of 4,946 ������2��.
For the monitoring period, between May 2024 and December 2024, 84 electric buses have been put into operation, starting in different months.
vcs-5455:
Taiwan Electric Vehicle Charging System Grouped Project (TEVCS), led by UPASSETS CO., LTD., focuses on integrating electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure and logistics management to reduce emissions from traditional fossil fuel vehicles (diesel and petrol) and provide convenient access to charging stations.

The project's goal is to generate Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) by reducing greenhouse gas emissions through the displacement of fossil fuel vehicles with electric vehicles. The project achieves emission reductions by providing electricity-powered vehicles instead of fossil fuel-powered ones, lowering greenhouse gas emissions per distance driven.

The project will involve multiple instances as more charging point owners join, with all carbon credits accruing under UPASSETS CO., LTD.'s jurisdiction. The project follows Verra Methodologies VM0038, which focuses on improving systems and adding EV infrastructure like charging stations to replace the carbon emissions of traditional vehicles. The estimated annual carbon reduction is 19,801.34 tCO2e, below the 60,000 tCO2e/year limit.

Before starting, the project will evaluate the electric vehicle market penetration, ensuring it is below 5%, in line with Verra's VCS module VMD0049. The first project will be in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, with plans to expand nationwide and eventually to other countries, such as Saint Lucia, Haiti, Paraguay, Guatemala, and the Marshall Islands, to support climate action and climate justice.
vcs-5456: The BissauBlue Project aims to restore around 11,000 ha of degraded mangroves in the southern provinces of Quinara and Tombali in Guinea-Bissau. This region once characterized by its thriving mangrove ecosystems, has experienced significant environmental degradation over the years, primarily due to unsustainable agricultural practices. The project aims to address this degradation by restoring the abandoned rice fields in the region, thereby revitalizing critical ecosystems and supporting sustainable development goals.
vcs-5457: TanzaBlue aims to restore 5,000 ha of degraded mangroves in Kilwa district in the province of Lindi in Tanzania. The project will actively engage with the local communities to restore the degraded mangroves while helping them with alternative livelihood programs that aims to reduce the pressure on existing mangroves.
vcs-5458:
The Sanggala Corridor Project is a community-centered forest conservation and restoration initiative aimed at preventing planned logging across more than 16,000 hectares of Borneo Lowland Rainforest, including 6,900 hectares designated for ARR activities. Adjacent to the Gunung Nyiut Nature Reserve, the project area serves as a vital habitat for 59 globally threatened species, including Hornbill Birds, Langurs, Pangolins, Gibbons, which are crucial for sustainability of ecosystem services in the landscape.
A core aspect of the initiative is its close collaboration with indigenous people and local communities, supporting their transition from unsustainable farming practices, such as slash-and-burn agriculture, to sustainable agroforestry. To promote sustainable livelihoods, the project develops alternative income sources, including agroforestry-based farming, eco-tourism, non-timber forest products, local employment, and village-owned enterprises. Additionally, it improves access to education, healthcare services and clean water, ensuring long-term environmental and community resilience.
vcs-5459: The forest area of Savannakhet has long been a natural forest. In recent years, the government has issued a plan and document for the logging of natural forests in the Savannakhet area to extract wood for construction due to the need to build large-scale infrastructure and improve the quality of life of the Lao people. The project owner proposed that the contracted area be a protected area and continue to be a forest area without logging, and through a series of protection measures, the normal growth of the forest will be protected. In this way, deforestation is reduced, carbon dioxide is absorbed, and the environment is protected. Before the implementation of the project, the project area has always existed as a natural forest, and most of the tree species are broad-leaved trees. After the implementation of the project, further forest protection measures have been taken to prevent the forest in this area from being cut down. The average annual emission reduction is expected to be 280,463 tons, and the total emission reduction is expected to be 5,609,260 tons over a period of 20 years.
vcs-546: The Jilin Da¡¯an Dagangzi Wind Power Project Phase ¢ó, developed by Jilin CGN Wind Power Co., Ltd, is a grid connected renewable energy project in Da¡¯an city, Jilin Province, in the People¡¯s Republic of China. It involves the installation of 33 turbines, each of which has a rated output of 1500 kW, providing a total installed capacity of 49.5 MW, with a predicted power delivered to the grid of 95,390MWh per annum.
vcs-5460: The proposed VCS grouped Savannakhet Town Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as the project), represents one of the first major reforestation projects implemented by the private sector in Lao PDR. The project will seek to utilize financing from carbon credits to conduct reforestation of up to 10,000 hectares (ha) of degraded land. In Government of Lao PDR (GOL) zoned Production Forest Areas (PFA’s) that have recently been made available to Laos Global Carbon Technology Co., Ltd (hereafter referred to as Project Proponent) for forestry plantation development. The Project Proponent has obtained approval from the GOL to identify and develop approximately10,000 ha located in Savannakhet Province.
vcs-5461: The forest area of Louang Namtha has long been a natural forest. The project owner proposed that the contracted area be a protected area and continue to be a forest area without logging, and through a series of protection measures, the normal growth of the forest will be protected. In this way, deforestation is reduced, carbon dioxide is absorbed, and the environment is protected. Before the implementation of the project, the project area has always existed as a natural forest, and most of the tree species are broad-leaved trees.
