The average annual emission reduction is expected to be 276,496 tons, and the total emission reduction is expected to be 5,529,920 tons over a period of 20 years.
vcs-5462: The proposed VCS grouped Louang Namtha Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as the project), represents one of the first major reforestation projects implemented by the private sector in Lao PDR. The project will seek to utilize financing from carbon credits to conduct reforestation of up to 10,000 hectares (ha) of degraded land. In Government of Lao PDR (GOL) zoned Production Forest Areas (PFA’s) that have recently been made available to Laos Global Carbon Technology Co., Ltd (hereafter referred to as Project Proponent) for forestry plantation development. The Project Proponent has obtained approval from the GOL to identify and develop approximately10,000 ha located in Louang Namtha Province.
vcs-5463: The project started in 2022. Project proponent found that due to the low living standards of local residents and lack of ecological protection awareness, there were illegal deforestation and timber sales to obtain funds, illegal deforestation to build houses, etc., which caused great ecological damage. The goal of the project is to use carbon financing to: protect forest plots from illegal logging; protect the normal growth of trees to avoid greenhouse gas emissions, maintain carbon storage and carbon sequestration; protect and maintain local plant and animal diversity; enhance local community-led protection and climate restoration by raising awareness of key environmental and climate issues; and enhance the community's ability to achieve sustainable livelihoods and nature-based climate solutions.
vcs-5464:
The Muyuchi IFLR grouped project is implemented in the Ucayali and Loreto regions in Peru. Eventually, over 30,000 hectares of land will be restored and will recover their productive capacity. IFLR projects are grouped projects that incorporate activities taking place on private small farmers-owned lands as well as large degraded areas owned by institutions and companies. Activities fall under multiple AFOLU project categories including ARR (restoration of degraded lands and establishment of productive forestry and agroforestry systems, assisted
natural regeneration, etc.), REDD (conservation of existing primary and secondary forest) and IFM. In fact, at the landscape level, we expect to implement tens of different land use models, each of which having its own carbon removal and emission reductions profile. This variability complexifies the model, but is core for its ability to be widely adopted and become a standard practice within the given landscape, hence reverting the deforestation cycle.
For this particular proejct, only ARR activities are subject to the issuance of VCUs.
vcs-5465:
“Enteric fermentation emissions’ reduction program of Italy” enters. This project consists in providing a natural additive composed by essential oils, flavonoids, and tannins: Anavrin®. VCS Project Description Template, v4.3 
The project will result in a reduction of methane emissions from enteric fermentation in beef cattle and dairy cows. 
Anavrin® is a product that has been tested in recent years at the universities of Milan, Sassari, Santa Maria in Brazil, Faculty of Veterinary Medicine in Uruguay, National Agriculture Investigation Institute in Uruguay and Wageningen University in Netherlands, among others. In addition, tests have been carried out in other parts of the world, where it was highlighted that the correct use of Anavrin® can improve the animal's daily production, around 70 g/animal/day, or 1.5 l daily milk gain per capita1. 
In the long-term, the project will comprise approximately 1,000,000 veals, steers, bulls, heifers, and cows per year. The project will start with one instance of beef animals in feedlot farms. In this system steer enters with a weight of 250 kg and after 6 to 9 months they weigh around 800 kg. Based on the calculations done in emission reductions and project emissions, the project will generate an emission reduction of 24,239 tCO2 per year. 
This is a grouped project with a project starts date of 21 March 2024. New instances (farmers) will be part of the project, benefiting from the use of the product itself but also from the generation of carbon credits.
vcs-5467:
Shanxi Xiangning Detong CMM Power Generation Project will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Detong coal mine which is a working coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mine where the project is located and to North China Power Grid(NCPG) if there is any electricity surplus. The project is located 1,2km south of Shapo Village, Zao Ling Township, Xiangning County, Linfen City, Shanxi Province, China. 
Prior to the implementation of the project, Dengtong coal mine was equipped with CMM extraction facilities and all extracted CMM was vented into the atmosphere directly; the electricity consumed at coal mines was imported from North China Power Grid (NCPG); the heat was provided by waste coal boilers. Baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. 
It is expected that 8.64 million Nm3 of methane annually will be destroyed to generate electricity. According to Feasibility Study Report (FSR) of the project, 8 sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 4.8 MW (8*600 kW ).
After the full operation of the project, the expected annual exported electricity is 27,360 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Detong coal mine and to North China Power Grid(NCPG) if there is any electricity surplus, thus displace equivalent amount of electricity that would be supplied by NCPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. 
It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 10-August-2024 to 09-August-2034), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 162,770tCO2e, with the total emission reduction of 1,627,700 tCO2e.
vcs-5468:
Shanxi Yangcheng Huanglian CMM Power Generation Project will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Huanglian coal mine which is a working coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mine where the project is located and to North China Power Grid (NCPG) if there is any electricity surplus. The project is located in Huangcheng Village, Beiliu Town, Yangcheng Country, Jincheng City, Shanxi Province, China. The project owner is Yangcheng County Jingde CBM power generation Co., LTD.
Prior to the implementation of the project, Huanglian coal mine was equipped with CMM extraction facilities and all extracted CMM was vented into the atmosphere directly; the electricity consumed at coal mines was imported from North China Power Grid (NCPG); the heat was provided by waste coal boilers. Baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. 
It is expected that 7.56 million Nm3 of methane annually will be destroyed to generate electricity. According to Feasibility Study Report (FSR) of the project, 6 sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 4.2 MW (6*7,000 Kw). After the full operation of the project, the expected annual exported electricity is 25,935 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Huanglian coal mine and to North China Power Grid (NCPG) if there is any electricity surplus, thus displace equivalent amount of electricity that would be supplied by NCPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. 
The project started construction on 19-May -2023 and was put into operation on 14-November-2023. It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 14-November-2023 to 13-November -2033), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 143,835 tCO2e, with the total emission reduction of 1,438,350 tCO2e.
vcs-5469:
This project involves the shifting of irrigation water management in rice cultivation in An Giang Province, Vietnam, implementing the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method instead of continuous flooding (CF).
Vietnam has 7.0 Mha of rice paddy fields with a total production of 42.6 Mt in 2023, making Vietnam the world’s 5th largest rice producer. Rice cultivation, on the other hand, is a substantial source of greenhouse gasses (GHG) through the emission of methane (CH4). Specifically in Vietnam, it is estimated that rice cultivation is responsible for up to 48% of greenhouse gas emissions and 75% of CH4 emissions in agriculture. Additionally, rice cultivation consumes most of the irrigation water in agriculture, as previous studies have shown it consumes 34 to 43% of the total agricultural irrigation water.  
One of the solutions to improve water productivity and decrease methane gas emissions in lowland rice production is the implementation of AWD, a water-saving irrigation measure. In AWD, the time intervals between dry and wet circumstances aid in the shift from aerobic to anaerobic soil conditions, resulting in a considerable reduction in methane output. As a result, the project adopts the AWD approach to minimise CH4 emissions. This will also result in a reduction in water use, lowering the farmer's input costs.
As a scenario prior to the execution of the project, the farmers in the project area are following the traditional continuous flooding method, which results in significant CH4 emissions due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the soil. The project proponent along with local partners held training sessions and meetings with farmers to educate them on the benefits of using AWD, which is followed by the installation of AWD pipes in the fields of registered farmers.
The expected annual average emission reductions of the project area are 590,682 t-CO2eq, with a total GHG emission reduction of 24,134,780t-CO2eq.
vcs-547: The project activity undertakes the implementation of the WTGs in the state of Maharashtra. The project will harness the wind resource for electricity generation and will displace the electricity generated from the grid which comprises mainly the thermal generated resource. The project activity can be categorised as renewable energy generation. The project is a bundled project activity which involves 16 investors and a total of 20 nos. of Wind Electric Generators (WEGs).
vcs-5470:
Guizhou Jinsha Changxing CMM Power Generation Project will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Changxing coal mine which is a working coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mine where the project is located and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus. The waste heat generated by the generator replace the heat originally generated by waste coal. The project is located in Sanlian Village, Changba Town, Jinsha Conty, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, P.R.China. The project owner is Jinsha Yonder Southwest New Energy Development Co., Ltd. 
Prior to the implementation of the project, Changxing coal mine was equipped with CMM extraction facilities and all extracted CMM was vented into the atmosphere directly; the electricity consumed at coal mines was imported from China Southern Power Grid (CSPG); the heat was provided by waste coal boilers. Baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. It is expected that 8.2519 million Nm3 of methane annually will be destroyed to generate electricity. According to Feasibility Study Report (FSR) of the project, 7 sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 5.8 MW (4*700 Kw + 3*1,000 Kw). After the full operation of the project, the expected annual exported electricity is 27,550 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Changxing coal mine and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, thus displace equivalent amount of electricity that would be supplied by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 05-December-2023 to 04-December-2033), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 152,290 tCO2e, with the total emission reduction of 152,290 tCO2e.
vcs-5471:
The proposed VCS project activity “Canhanduba Landfill Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) at the Canhanduba landfill site through destruction of collected LFG in a high temperature enclosed   flare(s) and utilization of LFG as gaseous fuel for electricity generation (in engine-generator sets), with the flare and the engine-generator set being installed at the Canhanduba landfill as part of the project activity. Thus, besides methane destruction, the project activity also promotes generation of  electricity by using a renewable energy source.
The Canhanduba landfill is a well-managed landfill site located to the Southwestern region of the city of Itajaí, Santa Catarina State, Southern Region of Brazil. The Canhanduba landfill started its operations in year 2006. Disposal of about 300 ton of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) per day has occurred in the landfill. The landfill site has been served as permanent disposal site for MSW generated in the cities of Itajaí, Balneário Camboriú both located in North-Eastern region of Santa Catarina State.
vcs-5474:
The Pahang Peatland Restoration Project (PPRP) aims to restore and conserve approximately 96,569 hectares of peatland and alluvial marshland in Pahang state, which is the largest continuous peat and wetland ecosystem in Peninsular Malaysia. The project spans across 11 timber production forest reserves. 77,478 hectares of this is designed as the initial project area. 

The objectives of PPRP include combating climate change, providing sustainable livelihoods, and protecting globally significant ecosystems and species. The project focuses on several key strategies:
1.	Fire monitoring and prevention: Utilizing satellite imagery, drones, and ground sensors to detect fire risks; managing ground water and promoting community awareness to prevent fire; and operating a dedicated fire-fighting team.
2.	Community development and livelihood enhancement: Designing sustainable income-generating activities to reduce reliance on peatland-degrading practices and foster local stewardship.
3.	Forest monitoring and law enforcement: Implementing real-time monitoring systems and collaborating with authorities to prevent illegal logging, land conversion, and peat drainage.
4.	Land and hydrology rehabilitation: Conducting peat rewetting, hydrological management (e.g., damming drainage canals), and forest restoration to reverse ecosystem degradation, improve biodiversity, and enhance carbon storage.

Without PPRP, extensive deforestation and peatland degradation would continue, resulting in significant biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, and GHG emissions. Land conversion pressures are also intensifying, with plans for oil palm plantations, an agroecology park, and a dairy farm.

PPRP is expected to avoid ~132.5 million tons of CO2e over 59 years by halting degradation from logging, agriculture, and canal construction. Reforestation of degraded and drained areas will remove ~11.3 million tons of CO2. Total reduction and removal averages 2.4 million tons annually.
vcs-5475: The project involves implementation of eco-conservation activities in a wetland eco-system that had been operating with a long-term concession license for commercial timber logging. The ‘wetland conservation and restoration (WRC)’ activities are combined with the main project activity involving ‘Improved Forest Management (“IFM”)’ – ‘Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF”)’ activities in legally approved forest areas within a larger forest concession project boundary. The areas that are within this concession boundary but not within the IFM sub-boundary are threatened with illegal logging and encroachment in unmanaged forest areas resulting in forest degradation. The project also involves implementation of replanting activities in those degraded areas as part of the WRC activities, and conservation/patrolling activities in remaining forest areas as per ‘Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (“REDD”)’ procedures. Wherever outside of identified replanting area if any re-planting activities are implemented that had less than 10 years of degradation history, all such areas are not accounted for contributions to net GHG emission removals based on inclusion/exclusion conditions defined in the applied VCS methodologies. The ‘soil organic carbon (“SOC”)’ based GHG emissions in the baseline are accounted for the full project area comprising the areas for three types of project activity components, namely, IFM, ARR and REDD, and any stand-alone areas within the concession boundary. The sections 3.1 and 3.2 of this PD provides information on how a combination of VCS methodologies have been applied to account for the GHG emissions and removals from different carbon pools that describes the project activity components referred earlier.
vcs-5477:
Puer MSW Landfill Biogas Pollution Control and Comprehensive Utilization Project is located at Lianhua Village MSW landfill site, Simao District, Puer City, Yunnan Province, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Puer BCCY New Power CO., Ltd.
The project started to construct on 20-Jul-2023 and put into operation on 01-Oct-2023.The project has a total designed capacity 2MW (2*1MW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the China Southern Power Grid (CSPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period from 01-Oct-2023 to 30-Sep-2033 will be 72,122MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions of the project is 37,257tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 372,573tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period from 01-Oct-2023 to 30-Sep-2033.
vcs-5479:
The project mitigates methane leaks from oil production activities at Karabagli and Kursengi, facilities operated by GL International (GLI). Using advanced Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) technologies, methane leaks are detected, measured, and repaired, reducing upstream emissions (VCSs).
This project targets leaks from components in production units related to oil and associated gas operations. All included facilities are within the upstream oil production fields. Fugitive emissions, defined as unintentional methane leakages from oil and gas operations, occur as oil and associated gas circulate under high pressure, escaping through worn connections, seals, valves, flanges, and other components due to wear, thermal and vibrational stress, and temperature changes.
Currently, these components are not routinely inspected for emissions, and GLI relies on basic leak detection techniques (e.g., LEL sensors, olfactory observations) to prevent direct safety hazards rather than to reduce emissions. Existing maintenance focuses on operational functionality rather than methane mitigation. Without intervention, methane would continue to be emitted unhindered.
The baseline scenario assumes conventional LDAR, whereas this project goes beyond by implementing advanced LDAR, leading to ex-ante estimated emission reductions of 48,323 tons CO2e per year.
Contribution to Sustainable Development
The project supports Azerbaijan’s sustainable development by reducing anthropogenic methane emissions, local air pollution, and environmental impacts. Additionally, it lowers emissions of harmful gases, including carcinogenic non-methane Volatile Organic Compounds (nmVOCs), and improves worker safety and health.
The use of advanced leak detection and quantification technologies in upstream oil production facilities has strong replication potential, enhancing resource efficiency and environmental protection.
vcs-548: The Jilin Da¡¯an Dagangzi Wind Power Project Phase ¢ò, developed by Jilin CGN Wind Power Co., Ltd, is a grid connected renewable energy project in Da¡¯an city, Jilin Province, in the People¡¯s Republic of China. It involves the installation of 33 turbines, each of which has a rated output of 1500 kW, providing a total installed capacity of 49.5 MW, with a predicted power delivered to the grid of 103,130MWh per annum.
vcs-5480: The project activity implements Carbicrete, Inc.’s cement-free concrete technology at one of the largest manufacturers of concrete products in North America. Carbicrete, a Montreal-based carbon removal company, has developed technology to mineralize waste CO2 during the curing stage into permanent removals and eliminate Portland cement (“PC”) from concrete production.
vcs-5482:
The project proposes 5.8 TPD CBG production.The plan is located in Jeetpur Village in Meerut District, Uttar Pradesh. The project activity involves the establishment & operation of a biogas plant with purification unit. The biogas plant can treat 160 tons/day (TPD) of organic waste through anaerobic digestion and produce 13600 m3/day of biogas & 25 TPD of organic fertilizer. The biogas is then purified and upgraded into Compressed Biogas of 5.8 TPD. 
By capturing the methane emissions being released from the organic waste and by reducing the carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel, the project has contributed to Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission reductions (ER). The estimated annual average ER from this project activity is 35432 tCO2e/year and the total ER over the first crediting period of 7 years is 248024 tCO2e.
vcs-5483: Trees for the Future Inc. (TREES) is developing The Lake Victoria Watershed Agroforestry Carbon Project II. This project uses VERRA methodology VM0047 with CCB to develop and monitor VCUs with smallholder farmers on 150,000 hectares of land within the Lake Victoria watershed in Uganda. This project will involve training and implementing sustainable agroforestry practices with farmers to transform conventional agriculture land into nature-based carbon sinks with above and below ground biomass and improved soils. In addition, to creating VCUs, the sustainable agroforestry techniques and extension services provided to farmers will ensure diversification of cropping systems including horticulture crops and fruit and fodder trees. The projects aims to improve nutrition, increase income and resilience, develop the sustainable growing capability of the land, and enhance biodiversity in the region. The restoration effort will generate 35 millions of Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) over the project lifetime and help farmers adapt to the impacts of climate change.
vcs-5484:
Hachijojima IFM project aims to promote healthier forest growth and increase carbon sequestration in a matured natural forest which also suffers from pest damage due to  aging, and generate carbon credits through the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VM0045 Methodology for Improved Forest Management using appropriate forest management practices for natural forests. 

The project aims to store more GHG (e.g. carbon) than currently present in forest carbon stocks by implementing selective logging that promotes natural regeneration of more biomass productive tree species, while reducing overcrowd of less biomass productive shrubs and tree species. In addition, the project focus on the removal of lianas that usually supresses tree growth. Most of the lands in the project area are covered by climax forests and it is less diversified in terms of stand age structure. The projects aims to produce more diversified ecosystems through forest activities that promote healthier natural regeneration and resilience though diverse stand structures.
vcs-5485:
Germany’s forests have suffered severe climate-induced damage, with over 500,000 hectares lost in recent years due to drought and bark beetle infestations. Large-scale spruce forests in unsuitable lowland areas have further increased vulnerability to extreme weather and pests, emphasizing the urgent need for restoration.
This project aims to restore degraded Norway spruce monocultures by transforming them into climate-resilient mixed forests. Introducing a balanced mix of deciduous and coniferous species will enhance biodiversity and strengthen ecosystem stability. Targeted silvicultural interventions will optimize species composition, improving resilience against drought, storms, and pest outbreaks.
Additionally, the project addresses financial barriers to reforestation. The widespread loss of spruce stands has disrupted timber markets, making reforestation financially unfeasible for many forest owners. By providing essential financial support through pre-financed pri-vate funding, this initiative enables landowners to establish sustainable, climate-resilient forests while ensuring long-term carbon storage and ecosystem health.
vcs-5486:
The Green Mpumalanga Project (GMP) is a large-scale ecosystem restoration initiative focused on rehabilitating degraded grassland and savanna ecosystems across 26 nature reserves in Mpumalanga Province, South Africa, spanning over 200,000 hectares. The project tackles degradation from overgrazing, uncontrolled fires, and illegal mining—which have led to biodiversity loss, declining soil organic carbon, and increased erosion—thereby reducing ecosystem resilience to climate change.
GMP implements a structured grazing and fire management programme to improve ecosystem functionality and enhance carbon sequestration. Key interventions include: (1) rotational grazing systems that allow vegetation recovery and enhance soil stability; (2) firebreak establishment and controlled burning regimes to lower wildfire intensity and frequency; and (3) erosion control measures to stabilise soils and promote vegetation regrowth. Complementing these, the Green Beef Initiative (GBI) encourages sustainable, carbon-neutral beef production by incentivising local livestock farmers to adopt regenerative grazing practices that improve pasture conditions and carbon storage, with premium market pricing for compliant products.
Designed as a phased, grouped carbon project under the VCS using the VM0032 methodology, the first project instance will be piloted in Songimvelo Nature Reserve, selected for its diverse ecosystems and established community engagement. Subsequent phases will expand interventions to additional reserves based on adaptive management from pilot outcomes. The GMP is projected to sequester up to 300,000 tCO₂e annually and directly supports Sustainable Development Goals related to climate action (SDG 13), land restoration (SDG 15), and sustainable economic growth (SDG 8). It also incorporates Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) mechanisms to provide financial benefits to local communities.
vcs-5487: This project activity will capture waste CO2 which would have otherwise been emitted into the atmosphere, or atmospheric CO2 which would otherwise be in the atmosphere, and utilize that gas as a feedstock in the production of concrete. These project activities reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sequestering CO2 via the production of concrete. This manufacturing process has the additional benefit of requiring less Portland cement, which further reduces emissions, because the cement production process is highly energy and carbon intensive. The project activity will take place at the location where the concrete is first manufactured (mixed with cement, water, aggregates, etc.).
vcs-5488: The Scatec RMI Hybrid Cluster is a single site, dispatchable power facility, comprising of solar photo-voltaic power feeding a battery energy storage system (BESS) technology. The Project is located approximately 15 km North-East of the town of Kenhardt in the Northern Cape province of South Africa and is located near Eskom’s Nieuwehoop Substation. The Project will have a Contracted Capacity of 150 MW at the Delivery Point. The solar portion is split over three footprints located adjacent to one another and forming a combined total installed capacity of an approximately 540 MW peak.
vcs-5489:
The Los Llanos de Apan: Ecological Restoration Project aims to restore degraded land in the states of Hidalgo and Tlaxcala, Central Mexico, through Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) activities under the VCS Standard v4.7.

The project area is in a semiarid region where the expansion of intensive agriculture (monoculture, heavy machinery, pesticides, and chemical fertilization) for barley production over the past decades, accompanied by overgrazing, logging, human-induced forest fires, and groundwater exploitation have led to deforestation, soil erosion, water scarcity and the degraded landscape we see today.

The Project includes two main restoration strategies to reduce soil erosion, increase vegetation cover, and enhance carbon sequestration through biomass. The first involves direct restoration through reforestation and revegetation using native woody species like Juniperus deppeana and non-woody species like Agave salmiana and Opuntia spp. The indirect restoration includes livestock exclusion through strategic fencing, hydroponic green fodder production, and fire prevention measures.

The Project is implemented on Ejidos land, a unique form of communal land tenure in Mexico. The project intends to increase carbon sequestration on 2,325 hectares of communal land within five Ejidos: Unión Tierra y Libertad in the state of Tlaxcala, and Almoloya, Alcantarillas, Rancho Nuevo, and Matías Rodríguez in the state of Hidalgo. Thirty-year agreements were signed between the Ejidos and the project proponent to ensure the long-term permanence of the Project.

In addition to ARR activities, the Project focuses on strengthening Ejido governance, promoting local employment, and improving access to healthcare, workshops, and training opportunities.

The restored vegetation cover will act as a carbon sink, sequestering 370,553 tCO2e over a crediting period of 30 years (period 2022-2052), with an annual average of 12,352 tCO2e
vcs-549: The “project activity” includes construction, installation and operation of a grid connected 6 MW biomass based power plant. The project proposes to fire rice husk as primary fuel for power generation. During conditions when high moisture laden rice husk would be available, supplementary fuel such as coal would be fired along with rice husk to provide the necessary energy to remove the excess moisture from the rice husk and additionally provide the required thermal energy to generate electricity.  The power plant is expected to generate net electricity of about 44 MU in a year at 100% PLF and 340 days of plant availability for 24 hours. The project power plant will export the generated electricity to the connected local grid. Since the electricity generated from the project activity will replace the grid electricity, thus will help in reducing Greenhouse Gases emissions at sources.
vcs-5490: The project activity involves the establishment of biogas plant to generate energy out of press mud. Press mud is a solid bio-degradable organic waste generated from the sugar manufacturing. Anaerobic digestion is the prominent technology used for degradation of biodegradable organic waste. Anaerobic Digestion (AD) is a biological process that happens naturally when bacteria breaks down organic matter in environments with little or no oxygen. It is effectively a controlled and enclosed version of the anaerobic breakdown of organic waste in disposal site or dumping yard which release methane. The biogas so generated shall be purified further and would be bottled as bio-CNG. The project activity is expected to generate approximately 12 Ton per day of bio-CNG for supply in domestic market of the country and would produce 52 MT of solid bio-manure and 135 MT of liquid manure per day.
vcs-5496: The NZ IFP Project 2 is an Improved Forest Management; Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF) project located in New Zealand that was developed using the VM0012 methodology. The project aim is to convert Pinus radiata plantations that were established with the objective of harvesting the timber for commercial purposes into protected forests, with the long-term goal of transitioning them to permanent native forest.New Zealand Forestry Removals Limited (an entity within New Zealand Carbon Farming Group) has a legal right to control such properties in order to convert the plantations into protected forests, with the long-term goal of transitioning them to permanent native forest.
vcs-5497: The project activity repairs, upgrades and installs new heating systems and insulates properties to improve energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions in UK dwellings. The project involved assessing over 10,000 properties across the UK, resulting in the installation on average of 2.2 energy efficiency measures . In 2023 over 4,500 properties received a whole house retrofit solution, i.e., multiple measures and a ventilation upgrade. Around 5,000 other properties received repairs or single measures. The project activity resulted in emission reductions of over 14,600 tCO2e.
vcs-5498: The project locates in Pengfang Village, Luoshi Township, Fengcheng City, Yichun City, Jiangxi Province, P.R China.  The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects manure waste of swine from the multiple hog farms in the Fengcheng City. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in two Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. The recovered biogas is used for electricity generation, or flared in case biogas generators are not available or under maintenance. Two generators with an installed capacity of 1.2 MW have been installed in the biogas power plant. The residual waste from the CSTR digesters is used in nearby farmlands by aerobic treatment. The project is designed to collect 365,000 tons of manure annually and generate 7,300,000 m3 of biogas annually. The project is estimated to generate 14,600 MWh annually. In addition, all of the electricity generated from the biogas is delivered to CCPG. Waste heat recovery boiler will also be installed at the biogas power plant to recover and supply waste heat to the auxiliary equipment of the project. For conservativeness, the emission reductions from electricity generation and generator waste heat recovery will not be accounted for.
vcs-5499:
The objective of Autonomous rail Rapid Transit (hereafter referred to as “ART”) Line T2 in Yibin  (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is to establish an efficient, reliable, rapid and convenient mass rapid transit system based on ART in the urban area of Yibin, located in Sichuan Province, People’s Republic of China. With a total length of 17.73 km and 15 stations, it serves as a vital artery connecting various urban functional areas. By providing convenient transportation options for commuters and residents throughout the day and replacing the conventional modes of transportation, which produce more carbon emissions than the project, the ART Line T2 helps alleviate traffic congestion, reduce air pollution, and enhance overall mobility within the city.
The project is divided in to early-term (2024-2028) and near-term (2028-2035). The passenger volume is 33,900 passengers per day in the early-term and will increase into 56,200 passengers per day in the near-term. This growth in passenger traffic is attributed to commercial cluster development and urban expansion.
The project is managed and operated by YIBIN AUTONOMOUS-RAIL TRANSIT CO.,LTD. The geographical boundary of the project is the urban area of Yibin. Gases included are CO2 and CH4.
The project boundary includes Yibin ART Line T2 and the entire urban area of Yibin as well as the power plants connected to Southwest China Power Grid.
The pre-project scenario is the usage of buses, passenger cars, taxis and motorcycles as well as non-motorized transport for transit purposes. No rail-based urban mass transit was available in this route prior to the project, and public transport relied exclusively on conventional bus systems. The baseline scenario is the continuation of the use of pre-project modes of transport.
During the seven-year crediting period (02- Jul -2024 to 01-Jul-2031), the project is expected to achieve 17,600 tCO2e emission reductions, with annual average GHG emission reductions of 2,514 tCO2e.
vcs-55: Lucevans Ceramic is a small ceramic industry that produces ceramic devices, bricks, for the local market in Panorama city, in the state of São Paulo. The ceramic is involved in an innovative activity, the switching fuel of its burning process.  The project activity consists of utilizing sugar cane bagasse, sawdust and peanut shells to feed the ceramic’s kilns, replacing the use of wood from areas with non sustainable forest management, which does not have any kind of contribution to the level of biodiversity enrichment. The ceramic company can use those renewable biomasses.  This project pointed out the possibility to switch non-renewable biomass for renewable biomasses, which was unattractive due to high investments on the adaptation of machineries to work with the new biomasses and other barriers. The ceramic owner considered the income from the commercialization of the carbon credits to become the project activity viable.
vcs-550: Rajaram Maize Products (RMP) is operating a Starch, Glucose & Dextrose Monohydrate manufacturing plant at Village Mohad, Dist. Rajnandgaon in Chhattisgarh. In the production process, steam and electricity are required as source of energy. Before the project activity, steam was generated in two solid fuel fired boilers (One 10 TPH for regular operation and one 6 TPH as a standby) and electricity was taken from state electricity grid. Fuel for boiler was mostly coal. In order to improve electricity availability and plant productivity the plant management decided to go for captive power generation.  The plant management had mainly two options for choosing fuel for co-generation plant, viz. coal & rice husk. The management decided to go for rice husk fired co-generation plant. Thus the project activity aims at reducing the GHG emissions that would have been generated by using coal as a fuel for co-generation plant.
vcs-5500: The Drawn Carbon ARR Foundations Project is a trailblazing initiative designed to address critical challenges in the voluntary carbon market (VCM) and accelerate meaningful climate and community impacts. This initiative is designed as a grouped project that brings together participants from around the world under a single, simple project design. The Drawn Carbon ARR Foundations Project achieves GHG emissions removals by increasing vegetative cover through afforestation and reforestation, at both a large and small scale. Participants are vetted and supported through the digital platforms of Drawn Carbon and Impact Inside, which collectively simplify the project design, registration, validation, and monitoring process. The initial project activity instance (PAI) will work with landholders in the Petén Department of Guatemala to introduce agroforestry and assisted natural regeneration to agricultural lands adjacent to the Maya Biosphere Reserve.
vcs-5501: The Drawn Carbon REDD+ Foundations Project seeks to unlock the benefits of climate finance for small-scale forest holders by democratizing access through easier, faster, and more affordable participation in the Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM). Unlike other carbon projects, this initiative is designed as a grouped project that brings together participants from around the world under a single framework. The Drawn Carbon REDD+ Foundations Project will achieve GHG emissions reductions by leveraging legal conservation agreements and developing sustainable alternative livelihood opportunities to prevent subsistence-driven deforestation. Participants are vetted and supported through the digital platforms of Drawn Carbon and Impact Inside, which collectively simplify the project design, registration, validation, and monitoring process. The initial project activity instance (PAI) will work with landholders in the Petén Department of Guatemala to conserve remnant forests in lands adjacent to the Maya Biosphere Reserve.
vcs-5503:
Revfin Services Private Limited is committed to revolutionizing sustainable mobility in India by providing innovative financial solutions for electric vehicle (EV) adoption. Founded in 2018, Revfin has disbursed loans to owners of electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and four-wheelers, enabling inclusive access to clean mobility solutions. Revfin combines inclusive targeting, transformative technology, innovative financing, and ecosystem partnerships to create a thriving EV ecosystem.
The project aims to finance over 3.5 million EVs by 2033, fostering a significant reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while enhancing economic opportunities for individuals and small fleets. By leveraging behavioural data and deep partnerships within the EV ecosystem, Revfin mitigates risks and scales operations efficiently. The project implements several key measures like financing EVs by providing competitive financial products to individuals and businesses for purchasing EVs to support widespread adoption and offering expert guidance to organizations on transitioning to sustainable practices and technologies. Within crediting period from 1st Jan 2024 to 31st Dec 2033 project is able to generate 3,486,176 tCO2e from 2 W, 3W and 3W, and annual average 348,617 tCO2e/year 
In addition to its lending services, Revfin is driving rapid fleet expansion by streamlining loan disbursement processes with minimal paperwork, making EV ownership more accessible to a larger audience under its brand RevfinMobility. 
Revfin also offers comprehensive insurance solutions under the Revfinsure brand.  
Through RevIoT, the company uses smart telematics to monitor and improve EV performance and driver behaviour.
Finally, Revshaala extends the lifespan of EV batteries with dedicated battery life extension centres.
Together, these initiatives position Revfin as a leader in facilitating the transition to sustainable transportation in India.
vcs-5506: The project, catalyzed by Afriwild Carbon Developments in partnership with Zuka Private Game Reserve, the wider Munywana Conservancy, and Wild Impact, aims to enhance nature-based carbon sequestration efforts within the Munywana Conservancy and adjoining communal rangelands through targeted interventions in fire management, grazing management, and the restoration of grassland. The project area is an ecologically significant area situated in the Maputaland-Pondoland-Albany corridor, and bordering the World Heritage Site of iSimangaliso Wetland Park. It is characterized by a complex mix of savanna grassland and moist broadleaf woodland, including sandveld woodlands, palm savannas, mixed acacia woodlands, mixed Lebombo woodlands, floodplain grasslands, and riparian forests. The project area encompasses sections of the iSimangaliso Key Biodiversity Area (KBA), the Pongolapoort KBA and the Thanda – Manyoni KBA. Within the core project area, 22% constitutes threatened ecosystems in urgent need of restoration and protection, thereby contributing to Targets 2 and 3 of the Global Biodiversity Framework. Land-uses in the project area include private and state wildlife areas, extensive livestock faming and croplands. However, these livelihoods are under threat as, over the baseline period, woody and invasive plant encroachment has led to a net loss of grassland ecosystem and degradation of at least 24% of grassy habitats, resulting in a loss of biodiversity, water retention, and grazing potential. This has catalyzed overgrazing as grass forage decreases, reinforcing a poverty trap in communities that rely on grassland ecosystem services . Ecotourism enterprises in the area are also being diminished as woody encroachment reduces game viewing potential and homogenises habitats. Both woody encroachment and overgrazing negatively impact soil carbon stocks.
vcs-5508:
Kenya Smart Cooking Solutions promotes clean and energy-efficient cooking technologies to combat household air pollution and reduce deforestation, while reducing GHG emissions from traditional inefficient cooking methods. By providing accessible improved cookstove technologies, the project empowers rural and underserved communities with efficient, safe, more sustainable, and cost-effective cooking alternatives. The initiative focuses on developing and distributing high-quality, fuel-efficient cookstoves tailored to local needs. These stoves help households reduce fuel consumption, lower cooking costs, and minimize indoor air pollution—leading to significant health and environmental benefits. 

Beyond enhancing energy access, the project supports sustainable livelihoods, promotes environmental conservation, and strengthens climate resilience. By fostering healthier homes and empowering communities, it paves the way for a greener, more sustainable future in Kenya.
vcs-5509: The project promotes to enhance agricultural sustainability by implementing a variety of eco-friendly practices. It focuses on transitioning from inorganic to organic fertilizers, incorporating green manure and compost, and minimizing water usage through efficient management techniques. Reduced tillage and no-till practices will help preserve soil structure, while proper crop residue management will prevent burning and promote soil health. Agroforestry will be incorporated to boost biodiversity and carbon sequestration. Additionally, the project will assist farmers with market linkages and fair pricing. These initiatives aim to mitigate climate change, improve soil fertility, and support long-term agricultural sustainability. Over the next 40 years, the project is expected to reduce and remove 76,656 tons of CO2 annually, totalling 3,066,240 tons over its lifetime.

The generated electricity from WTGs is supplied to Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited which comes under NEWNE grid. The project activity will lead to following benefits: 1.  The project activity contributes to climate change mitigation efforts through generation of electrical energy from renewable wind power resources. 2. vcs-5510:
Project Caraga is a grouped project located in the Republic of the Philippines, northeastern Mindanao, within Region XIII (Caraga Region). It is being designed to generate premium carbon credits through Nature-based Solutions comprising a range of environmental and socio-economic efforts. The Project focuses on REDD+ and Avoiding Unplanned Deforestation (AUDef) by applying the VM0048 methodology and intends to work with up to 17 Indigenous Cultural Communities and Indigenous people (ICC/IP) with Certificates of Ancestral Domain Titles (CADTs), with a potential eligible project area of approximately 200,000 ha. 

Project Caraga will ultimately include a range of forest protection, conservation, restoration, and sustainable land management approaches to enhance biodiversity and ecosystem services. As part of this process, the Project will also help empower ICC/IP to manage and actively protect their ancestral domains, promote community development, and strengthen existing Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Practices (IKSP) to enable effective self-governance. In future years, Project Caraga is also exploring to incorporate additional activities, such as APDef (Avoiding Planned Deforestation) and ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation, and Restoration), and may also pursue certification under the CCB Standard at a later stage.
vcs-5511:
The Brazil Cerrado 1 Project is developed pursuant to a reforestation strategy that seeks to generate risk-adjusted returns and GHG removals primarily through the protection and/or restoration of natural forests across ~50% of biologically productive land area, and the establishment of Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) certified sustainably managed commercial tree farms across the remaining ~50%.

The Brazil Cerrado 1 Project will produce GHG removals by reforesting degraded pastureland in the Brazilian states of Mato Grosso do Sul, Mato Grosso, and Minas Gerais, largely focused on the Cerrado region. Reforestation will occur through restoration of natural forests (via natural regeneration, assisted natural regeneration and native tree planting) and by planting sustainably managed FSC-certified Eucalyptus tree farms (E. Urophylla x E. grandis hybrids) managed on an extended rotation as compared to business-as-usual practices in the region.

Cattle ranching is the dominant land use in the project’s target region. Cattle ranchers often introduce non-native grasses (e.g. Brachiaria sp.), and any native vegetation that naturally regenerates is grazed by cattle. Once every 3-5 years, ranchers typically use tractors to mechanically remove any woody vegetation that has survived grazing, and the cycle begins again. This leads to a landscape that sequesters minimal carbon and is largely devoid of the natural Cerrado biome flora structure.

Through this project, woody vegetation will be re-established by removing grazing cattle, planting Eucalyptus spp., and restoring and permanently protecting native habitat areas. This will increase the native Cerrado cover in the area while also increasing carbon sequestration and wood products production in the area.
vcs-5512: Refrigerant Management Canada operates a nonprofit organization which administers a voluntary refrigerant ODS destruction program. As there are currently no regulations or market incentives in place to collect and destroy ODS at the end of a product’s useful life, they can be stockpiled indefinitely, resulting in their gradual release to the atmosphere. Through RMC's voluntary program, surplus ODS from Canadian refrigeration and air conditioning industries is collected, transported, stored and disposed of at destruction facilities in Canada and the United States. Through contractual agreements, Anew Environmental, LLC has been granted the legal title to, and exclusive right to market all VCUs associated with the project activity.
vcs-5513:
The proposed project activity is a Waste to Energy (Bio-CNG) initiative based on a Circular Economy Model, designed to generate approximately 14,000 cubic meters of biogas per day from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW). Through advanced technology and process control mechanisms, it is now highly feasible to convert biodegradable waste—such as MSW, fruit and vegetable waste, and cow dung—into renewable fuels like biogas, Compressed Biogas (CBG) or Bio-CNG, and green electricity, while simultaneously producing valuable by-products including bio-compost and nutrient-rich slurry.
The project adopts a proven anaerobic digestion process followed by biogas purification and upgrading to produce Bio-Methane (Bio-CNG). The controlled process parameters ensure optimal gas yield and quality of by-products. These by-products serve as organic fertilizers and soil conditioners, enhancing agricultural productivity and contributing to circular waste management. The initiative promotes environmental sustainability, reduces land and air pollution, supports local livelihoods by generating employment, and provides an alternative source of income for farmers and waste collectors.
Prior to the implementation of this project, MSW was openly dumped, leading to unregulated methane emissions—a potent greenhouse gas—thereby contributing significantly to climate change. This project captures methane through controlled anaerobic digestion, purifies and compresses it for sale to Oil Marketing Companies as Bio-CNG, thereby replacing fossil fuels and reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
The project has been awarded through a competitive tender process to our company, which met the necessary technical and financial qualifications. The project is currently being implemented at different locations, positioning it as a significant step toward sustainable urban waste management and clean energy transition.
vcs-5514:
According to baseline surveys, before the implementation of the project, the grasslands in the region were facing severe degradation due to overgrazing, with livestock numbers exceeding the carrying capacity by 1 to 5 times, and the adverse effects of climate variability. These conditions resulted in significant vegetation loss, soil erosion, and depletion of soil organic carbon. 
The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as implementing systematic seasonal pasture rotations, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and providing regular training to herders on sustainable grazing practices. 
Totally, approximately 365,000 ha of degraded pastureland are targeted for restoration through scientifically managed measures. This project quantifies only GHG removals from new project activities using VM0042 methodology, version 2.1. It is estimated to generate an average annual GHG emission removal of 200,000 tCO2e in 40 years. The project contributes to multiple SDGs by creating local jobs (SDG 8), mitigating climate change (SDGs 13), and improving the quality of the grassland and enhancing biodiversity conservation (SDG 15).
vcs-5515: The Project seeks to develop an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) carbon offset project across Latvia.
vcs-5516:
The Project seeks to develop an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) carbon offset project across Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Finland.
The Project will increase carbon sequestration and/or reduce GHG emissions by establishing, increasing or restoring vegetative cover through the planting, sowing or human-assisted natural regeneration of woody vegetation
vcs-5517: AfriScout LLC and Global Communities, in collaboration with local pastoralist communities, are leading the AfriScout Regenerative Grazing Project to address severe rangeland degradation in Southern Ethiopia's Oromia, Somali, and South Ethiopia Regions. This degradation, stemming from overgrazing, climate change, and land use shifts, threatens livelihoods historically reliant on grazing. The project focuses on restoring communal grasslands through community-led adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) rotational grazing, where livestock movements are managed across defined paddocks to allow pasture recovery. This core activity integrates local knowledge with participatory planning, supported by the AfriScout mobile app for monitoring and decision-making. Complementary actions include reseeding, water management structures, and using mobile corrals for soil enrichment. Structured as a grouped project, the project allows expansion to new communities over its 30-year crediting period. The initiative follows the VM0042 methodology for improved agricultural land management, aiming to quantify significant soil organic carbon sequestration and reduce GHG emissions, with initial estimates around 150,000 tCO2e annually. The local pastoralist communities co-design activities and benefit from improved rangelands, enhanced climate resilience, reduced resource conflicts, and shared carbon revenues from the project. The project targets substantial positive impacts on both the environment and local livelihoods, contributing to climate mitigation and adaptation.
vcs-5518:
The San Miguelito Afforestation project in Northeast Argentina is an ARR initiative using exotic and native species on degraded grasslands. Located in Corrientes Province, within the “Campos y Malezales” and Atlantic Forest ecoregions, it promotes innovative afforestation by combining native and exotic species, aiming for a full native forest after harvesting exotic species. Covering 2,430 ha, 1,598 ha of converted and degraded grasslands will be planted — 60% with native Atlantic Forest species and the rest as mixed plantations of native and non-invasive pines. Remaining wetlands and grasslands will be preserved. After 35 years, harvested pine areas will be prepared for native species colonization.
The project aims to provide GHG benefits of approx. 14,964 tCO2/year over 40 years, totaling 598,578 tCO2 in carbon fixation. Developed by GMF Latinoamericana, an experienced NBS developer in Argentina, it adheres to VM0047 methodology and sustainability standards such as FSC certification. It also strives to positively impact priority communities.

vcs-5520: The Pekanbaru Suntara Peatland Project (PSPP) is a peatland and forest conservation and restoration project located in Dumai, a subdistrict in Pekanbaru, Riau Province, Indonesia, implemented on forest concession land where PT. Suntara Gajapati holds a forest utilization management license, with a total area of 35,644.39 hectares. The PSPP is being developed in the scope of PT. Suntara Gajapati ownership by PT. Suntara Gajapati and Indacom, Pte, Ltd., and the PT. Suntara Gajapati (“Suntara”) and Indacom, Pte, Ltd. (“Indacom”) are the project proponent together.  The project is expected to generate a range of climate, community and biodiversity benefits by protecting and restoring the integrity of peatland and forest landscapes and the rich biodiversity of the region, while improving the well-being of local communities. In terms of climate benefits, it is estimated that the PSPP project will achieve a net reduction and removal of 26,623,828 tCO2e over 40 years of crediting period. This will be achieved through activities covered by the VM0007 REDD+ approach framework and VM0047 Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation, including the restoration of wetland ecosystems of peatlands (RWE), Avoid unplanned deforestation (AUPD) and the restoration of vegetation (ARR). In addition, the project will provide climate change adaptation benefits by increasing the resilience of local communities and biodiversity to climate change. The project will bring tangible benefits to local communities living in the surrounding areas by working to improve local livelihoods, health, education and well-being. The project's goals are to protect remaining forests, improve peatland hydrology, restore ecosystem functions, conserve biodiversity, and improve community well-being to withstand climate change. Overall, it is expected that the PSPP project will help protect the integrity and biodiversity of the region's peat forest landscapes while improving the well-being of local communities.
vcs-5521: The proposed project 'Blue Flame for Commercial Kitchens in Ghana' is a voluntary initiative by Envirofit International Inc. to improve access to clean and efficient cooking solutions, for commercial cooking in Ghana. The project involves the dissemination of energy and emission efficient liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) stoves / burners (hereinafter referred to as ‘LPGS’) to commercial kitchens operating in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), across multiple locations in Ghana. The project aims to replace traditional cooking fuel and technology, primarily three-stone fires or inefficient biomass stoves using non-renewable biomass fuel such as firewood and/or charcoal—with LPGS. The project LPG based / burners. The project devices have high thermal efficiency (more than or equal to 40 percent) and significantly reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and indoor air pollution (IAP) attributed to use of traditional biomass cooking practices. The initiative will help mitigate deforestation and health hazards caused by the widespread use of traditional and inefficient non-renewable biomass (NRB) on traditional / inefficient stoves, which is a major driver of land degradation and respiratory illnesses in the region.
vcs-5522:
The Grouped Mangrove Restoration Project to Secure Livelihoods and Combat Climate Change in India project is a collective effort aimed at restoring degrading wetlands through afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation activities initiated from the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. This voluntary grouped project is being carried out by Infinite Environmental Solutions Limited (IESL) in collaboration with the Outreach Project Limited and Mangrove Foundation of India in cooperation with local communities. The project area primarily consists of unvegetated mudflats and patches of scattered vegetation that have suffered from sedimentation and soil erosion. The exposed mudflats are vulnerable to soil erosion and loss of soil mass.

The primary objective of the project activity is to restore degrading tidal wetlands by introducing native mangrove species. The project activity is implemented in the Tamil Nadu and other State of India, and it will cover up to 4000 ha area. The native mangrove tree species used for restoration activity includes Avicennia marina, Rhizophora mucronata, and Rhizophora apiculate etc.
vcs-5523:
The Pama project is located in the Pama Special Reserve which is a vast area of 141,906 ha located west of Bangui, the capital in Central African Republic (CAR). This project includes a mosaic of savannahs and gallery forests. The human activities observed here are traditional in CAR: slash-and-burn subsistence farming, firewood collection, transhumant livestock rearing, etc. For many years now, the main obstacle to forest expansion and biomass accumulation in the Pama reserve is bushfire. Indeed, an average of 71,603 ha (i.e. half the surface area) burns annually during the dry season. These fires are a brake on the expansion of gallery forests and they also prevent the development of tree species in the savannah, thus preventing the savannah from becoming forest. Project Pama is then designed to place local communities at the heart of a vast rural and ecological development program, aimed at revitalizing the socio-economic fabric of the region while protecting forest cover and savannahs against fires.
The Pama Project is an integrated land development project with a climate vocation aimed at local communities. Its objectives are:
-	Restoration of forest landscapes through protection activities and assisted natural regeneration;
-	Conversion of actual hunting practice into more sustainable practices;
-	Support for local development with the setting up of cooperatives to provide farming equipment, train and support for farmers.
The project will have a number of social and environmental benefits, such as (1) Creating jobs and increasing incomes, (2) Improving agricultural skills and yields, (3) creating ecological corridors and reducing habitat fragmentation, (4) improving soil fertility and reducing erosion, (5) mitigating climate change, (6) protecting biodiversity hotspots, (7) reducing deforestation and forest degradation.
The sequestration of GHG through protection activities (under the VM0047 methodology) is estimated at 11,120,708 tCO2 over 50 years.

vcs-5525:
The carbon capture and storage (CCS) project that is described in this document (the “Project”)
is comprised of three distinct project activity modules—capture, transport, and storage—as
defined by VM0049 (Carbon Capture and Storage v1.0), which establishes the criteria and
procedures to quantify the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission removals from proposed carbon
capture and storage (CCS) projects. The Project is comprised of a direct air capture facility (the
“STRATOS DAC facility”) that will capture carbon dioxide (CO2) directly from ambient air (the
“Capture Project Activity”), a pipeline (the “BRP CO2 Pipeline”) that will transport the captured
CO2 from the point of capture to the point of sequestration (the “Transport Project Activity”), and
the Brown Pelican Carbon Dioxide Sequestration facility (the “BRP CO2 Sequestration facility”)
that will store the captured CO2 (the “Storage Project Activity” and collectively with the Capture
Project Activity and the Transport Project Activity, the “Project Activity”).
The Capture Project Activity is designed to capture atmospheric CO2 from ambient air using a
chemical absorption process with liquid solvents and prepare the captured atmospheric CO2 for
durable storage in a saline aquifer. The Capture Project Activity is designed to regenerate the
primary capture fluid or media, such that it is not a one-time use, and a concentrated CO2 stream
is recovered from regeneration and available for subsequent transport and storage. The Capture
Project Activity will take place at a new direct air capture (DAC) facility, STRATOS DAC, which is
located in Ector County, Texas, in the United States. There was previously no existing DAC facility
in place at this location.

vcs-5527: The Mandassaia Farm Carbon REDD+ Project, developed by Pau-Brasil Forest Assessment, aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by preventing unplanned deforestation (AUD) in a privately owned area located in the municipality of Juara, state of Mato Grosso, Brazil. The project encompasses a total area of 39,296 hectares, entirely covered by Amazon biome native forest. In addition to delivering verified emissions reductions, the project is designed to generate positive co-benefits by allocating a portion of the carbon credits to social and environmental initiatives. These include strengthening local deforestation monitoring and control, promoting environmental education, fostering awareness, and supporting alternative livelihood opportunities for surrounding communities. Over the 40-year crediting period (from 03 April 2023 to 02 April 2063), the project is projected to avoid 28,760 hectares of deforestation, corresponding to an estimated reduction of 14,048,280 tCO₂e in GHG emissions, an average of 351,207 tCO₂e annually. The project's contributions to climate, community, and biodiversity are being monitored and validated under the Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standard.
vcs-5528: Biodiesel Project in Uttar Pradesh, India is developed by Nirvaanraj Energy Private Limited and is located at Village Uldeypur, Tehsil Meerut, Distt. Meerut, State UP of India. vcs-5530:
Taishan municipal solid waste (hereafter referred to as “MSW”) incineration and power generation project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Jinkeng village,Taicheng street Taishan City, Guangdong province, China, with geographic location of 112.764870ºE and 22.233560ºN. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Public Energy Investment(Taishan) Co., Ltd.
The combustion system is composed of two 500t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 25MW steam turbine generator. The project will treat 365,000 tons of fresh waste very year. The MSW combustion line will work over 8,000 hours every year. The project is expected to generate 156,392MWh electricity, of which 128,241 MWh will be exported to the China Southern Power Grid (hereinafter referred to as CSPG) when the project generates full load. When steam turbine generator is repaired, it may involve in purchased electricity from CSPG. The implementation of the project meets the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also, the project could reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil fuel fired plants and MSW treatment.
Before the implementation of the project, the local MSW was usually disposed of at nearby landfills, where no landfill gas capturing system erected and the landfill gases are released to atmosphere directly. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can transfer steam to generate electricity power to replace the electricity that would be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants. 
The construction period of the project is from 04/2024 to 10/2024, and the start date of the project is 17/04/2024. The total GHG emission reduction is expected to be124,8646 tCO2e and the average annual emission reduction is 178,378 tCO2e in a period of 7 years (from 17/04/2024 to 16/04/2031 both included).

vcs-5533:
The proposed afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation (ARR) project aims to restore degraded and fallow land by promoting sustainable plantation practices in Purulia district, West Bengal, India. The initiative involves planting timber and fruit-yielding species owned by individual farmers, integrating climate-resilient strategies. The targeted farmers are indigenous landholders that have adhered to traditional agricultural methods for generations. The land earmarked for the project is privately owned by them.
Native and locally adapted trees are planted to enhance carbon sequestration, conserve biodiversity, improving ecosystem services and soil health along with empowering communities and boosting farmers’ income. This effort aligns with multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and national commitments to sustainability and climate change mitigation. 
The project spans Manbazar 1, Manbazar 2, Arsha and Bundwan blocks in Purulia district, West Bengal, India.
vcs-5535:
The project aims to remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere by implementing regenerative grazing practices in the Ralicó farm, located in the shouthwestern region of the Córdoba province, within the General Roca department in Argentina. The eligible farm area includes both wooded areas and open land. A significant portion is covered by Caldén forest, which shows different levels of density and conservation, while the rest consists of cleared areas, all suitable for grazing management activities.

The core strategy of this approach involves subdividing the farm’s large pastures into smaller paddocks and implementing a rotational grazing system. This method ensures that each paddock receives adequate rest and recovery time between grazing periods, promoting healthier soil, improved vegetation cover, and increased carbon sequestration across the landscape
vcs-5536: This project is made up of rooftop Solar PV projects of small and medium size in South Africa. It contains projects from multiple Solar developers and consists of thousands of installations at households in the country. Developers included are GoSlr and Versofy.
vcs-5539:
The project activity entails transformation of agricultural wastes to biomass pellets for sustainable energy purposes. The project activity includes setting up of industrial scale biomass pellets and briquetting plants in the Kishangarh region of Bhikhi village situated in the Mansa district of Punjab. The project is designed to process around 90,000 tonnes of agricultural residues per year to produce biomass pellets (biofuels) by using the Vantage Waste Processing Technology (VWP). This technology processes the entire organic waste without leaving any residues, removes the odour, sanitizes the waste, achieves volume reduction and produces quality biofuel. Output product range includes biomass pellets and biomass briquettes.  The project activity will use 2MW electricity which will operate the Vantage Waste Processor, shredding machines, hammer mills, pellets and briquetting machines and other equipment entirely.
Prior to the project activity, Stubble burning of the agricultural residue left after harvesting was carried out extensively creating massive air pollution releasing numerous harmful greenhouse gas and also have severe consequences on human health. Also, in thermal power plant coal was being combusted for energy purposes and the electricity generated was delivered to the grid connected power stations. The biomass pellets produced will replace coal in the baseline and provide clean energy to the grid connected power plants that will be further supplied to households. The biomass pellets shall also be used in other industries like FMCG, pharma, food etc for meeting their thermal energy requirements which in the baselines scenario is being met through utilization of coal as fuel source. Conversion of agricultural residues to biomass pellets will also reduce the incidences of stubble burning significantly, which is both a local and global issue.
vcs-554: ÖZGÜR Elektrik Üretim A.S. (in the following: Özgür) plans to install a hydro power plant in the southern part of Turkey in the Province of Icel at the Ermenek river. vcs-5542: The Malaysia Grouped Biomass Waste Recovery and Utilization Project is a national-scale initiative aimed at catalyzing the transition from underutilized biomass waste to sustainable energy generation in Malaysia. Cleanroads Infrastructure Innovation Society, (hereafter referred to as “Cleanroads), is a non-profit organization that represents various companies in the BC road building and maintenance industry. The member companies include highway maintenance contractors, construction contractors, underground/utility contractors, paving contractors and the various service and supply companies in the industry. Cleanroads is the project proponent of this grouped project, which aims to reduce the GHG emissions of road building and maintenance activities in British Columbia and beyond. 
Prior to project implementation, the existing scenario consists of the utilization of conventional fossil fuels such as gasoline or diesel in on-road vehicles and mobile machinery (wheel loaders, aggregate crushers, dozers, among others). It also consists of the utilization of mobile machinery without energy efficiency technology. These mobile machineries also use conventional fossil fuels such as diesel. These on-road vehicles and mobile machinery are used in road construction and maintenance activities.
The grouped project aims to reduce GHG emissions through the electrification of on-road vehicles, energy efficiency improvements in mobile machinery, and electrification of mobile machinery. The electrification of on-road vehicles and mobile machinery will reduce GHG emissions by displacing the use of conventional fossil fuels. GHG emissions will also be reduced by improving energy efficiency in mobile machinery by utilizing diesel-electric drive technology. This combination of activities will enable the road building industry to reduce its contribution to regional, national, and global GHG emissions.

vcs-5546:
The “Electric Mobility Program South Africa” is a grouped project comprising multiple Project Activity Instances (PAIs), each managed by individual participants under contract with the project proponent, Zeroca B.V., which holds overall responsibility. The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through the deployment of battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) and battery-electric mobile machinery (BEMM) across South Africa, replacing fossil fuel-powered units.

The Project applies several methodologies: UNFCCC CDM AMS-III.C (Version 16.0) for EVs, including methodology revision M0299 for EMMs; VCS VM0038 (Version 1.0) for charging infrastructure used by light-duty vehicles (LDVs); and optionally AMS-I.F (Version 5.0) for renewable electricity generation (solar or wind) used for charging.

Each PAI includes only one technology type (either EV/EMM or charging infrastructure). Only BEVs and BEMMs are eligible, excluding hybrids and fuel-cell vehicles. All road vehicle and mobile machinery categories are covered, along with both public and private charging stations (Level 1, Level 2, and DC Fast Chargers).

The baseline scenario is the continued use of fossil fuel-powered vehicles and machinery. The project achieves GHG reductions by replacing these with electric alternatives and promoting clean energy charging solutions, with implementation nationwide in South Africa. It also contributes significantly to the Sustainable Development Goals SDG 3 (“good health and well-being”), SDG 7 (“affordable and clean energy”), SDG 11 (“sustainable cities and communities”), and SDG 13 (“climate action”).
vcs-5547: The project seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve public health in rural communities across South Africa by distributing energy-efficient improved cookstoves. By replacing traditional, inefficient cooking methods, the project lowers fuel consumption and indoor air pollution, addressing critical environmental, health, and socio-economic challenges. Through this initiative, Oyu Green aims to promote cleaner cooking, enhance livelihoods, empower women and girls, and support sustainable development across vulnerable communities
vcs-5548: The Clean Waste Collective project is a high-impact sustainable waste management initiative to be implemented across various regions of South Africa. The project aims to transform waste streams into valuable resources while promoting climate resilience, green jobs, and circular economy practices. Prior to the project intervention, the organic fraction of waste including household waste, animal manure, garden waste, and agricultural residues was typically left to decay in municipal solid waste (MSW) systems or dumped in landfills. This uncontrolled decomposition led to significant methane emissions, a potent greenhouse gas. In parallel, recyclable materials such as plastics, cardboard, and metals were routinely discarded into landfills. The continued demand for virgin raw materials to produce plastic and metal contributed further to carbon emissions and environmental degradation. To address these challenges, the Clean Waste Collective introduces a dual-pathway solution in which the organic waste is processed through controlled aerobic composting, which prevents methane formation and produces nutrient-rich compost for use in agriculture, landscaping, and soil restoration. Simultaneously, recyclable waste streams—plastics, metals, and paper—are collected, sorted, and re-integrated into manufacturing processes, reducing the reliance on virgin materials and lowering the overall environmental footprint. This integrated approach diverts significant waste from landfills, conserves natural resources, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthens material recovery systems. It supports Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including the SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13(Climate Action) The project enhances community resilience, promotes responsible waste behaviour, and offers a scalable model for sustainable waste management in developing regions beyond its enviro
