HeShan municipal solid waste (hereafter referred to as “MSW”) incineration and power generation project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Mashan Landfill is located north of Mashan Jizaidi Village, Hecheng Town, Heshan City, Guangdong province, China, with geographic location of 112.803457ºE and 22.629485ºN. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Public Energy Technology (Heshan) Co., Ltd.
The combustion system is composed of two 350t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 18MW steam turbine generator. The project will treat 255,500 tons of fresh waste very year. The MSW combustion line will work over 8,000 hours every year. The project is expected to generate 112,800MWh electricity, of which 90,840 MWh will be exported to the China Southern Power Grid (hereinafter referred to as CSPG) when the project generates full load. When steam turbine generator is repaired, it may involve in purchased electricity from CSPG. The implementation of the project meets the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also, the project could reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil fuel fired plants and MSW treatment.
Before the implementation of the project, the local MSW was usually disposed of at nearby landfills, where no landfill gas capturing system erected and the landfill gases are released to atmosphere directly. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can transfer steam to generate electricity power to replace the electricity that would be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants. 
The construction period of the project is from 09/2022 to 01/2024, and the start date of the project is 28/05/2024. The total GHG emission reduction is expected to be 647,752 tCO2e and the average annual emission reduction is 92,536 tCO2e in a period of 7 years (from 28/05/2024 to 28/05/2031 both i
vcs-5552:
The AYR RIBA project aims to reduce carbon emissions in urban environments through the deployment of electric scooters for mobility services in Brazil, such as delivery services in B2B solutions or as temporary manner of travel in B2C solutions. 
The project involves acquiring and expanding the electrical fleet in urban areas instead of acquiring conventional fossil fuel powered motorcycles, primarily targeting last-mile delivery and transportation services. 
Located in urban centers in Brazil, with operations in São Paulo and Maringá and with plans to expand to other urban centers in Brazil, as evidenced in the Riba Brasil documentation, the project leverages electric mobility technology developed in partnership with CEiiA, a Portuguese engineering and product development center focused on sustainable technologies.
The project is expected to generate only GHG emission avoidance (emission removals are out of scope), by:
Acquiring zero-emission electric scooters instead of high-emission internal combustion engine motorcycles, 
Implementing a battery swap infrastructure,
Utilizing advanced telemetry and AI systems to optimize routes and energy usage
Integrating with AYR platform (developed by CEiiA) to quantify and value CO2 emission avoidance
Prior to implementation, last-mile delivery services in target areas predominantly used conventional motorcycles with internal combustion engines, which contribute significantly to urban noise, air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. These motorcycles typically have catalytic converters that become ineffective after 18,000 km of use, further increasing emissions.
The project is estimated to achieve significant annual greenhouse gas emission avoidance by eliminating tailpipe emissions from delivery vehicles and utilizing clean energy sources for charging infrastructure.
For the 7-year crediting period (excluding renewals), it is estimated a reduction of 43,745 tCO2 with a yearly average of 6,249.28 tCO2.
vcs-5553: The Methane Recovery Project in Palmas de Ixcan Planta San Roman (referred to as “The Project”) is the implementation of an anaerobic wastewater treatment facility at the palm oil factory in Petén, Guatemala and would be a non-grouped project.
vcs-5555:
The proposed Project activity intends to restore degraded mangrove habitats in the Indian Sundarbans region.  The project activity plans to restore up to 2,000 hectares of degraded mangrove ecosystems in phased manner through the plantation of diverse native mangrove tree species. The project activity is being implemented in the Indian part of Sundarbans delta situated in the West Bengal state of India. The project is implemented by the proponent in collaboration with the project implementing partner organization, site specific ground partners, and the local communities. The project activity will ensure the active participation of women in various stages of project implementation and post implementation management of the project interventions

By restoring the degraded mangrove land with the native tree species, the project activity will remove atmospheric carbon dioxide through biological carbon sequestration in the tree biomass and in the soil there by avoiding the equivalent amount of GHG emissions which would have not been occurred in the pre-project scenario as the land remains degraded land with no carbon sequestration.
vcs-5556: The Green Samar project is an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) project located in the island of Samar, Eastern Visayas, Philippines, and eligible under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) program. The project boundaries cover the Samar Island Natural Park, and the initial project instance is located in the Strict Protection Zone of the Park for around 29,000 ha of degraded forest targeted for assisted natural regeneration (ANR) and 1,025 ha of grasslands targeted for reforestation through direct planting. Project activities include establishing nurseries for native tree seedlings, using direct planting on grasslands, and enhancing natural forest recovery in degraded areas through enrichment planting and forest protection. These interventions are designed to sequester carbon by promoting substantial biomass accumulation in both newly established stands and regenerating forests, while stopping deforestation by dramatically improving the park protection capacity and the livelihood condition of the local communities. Prior to implementation, these lands had experienced deforestation, degradation, and low biomass levels due to slash-and-burn farming, illegal extraction, and minimal management. Over a 40-year crediting period, the Green Samar Project is expected to remove an estimated total of approximately 12.5 million tonnes of CO₂, yielding an annual average removal of about 312,464 tonnes of CO₂ per year.
vcs-5557:
Shandong Shouguang Youran Dairy Cattle Manure Management Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) locates in Northeast of Langjiaying Village, Tianliu Town, Shouguang County, Weifang City, Shandong Province, P.R China.
The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects dairy cattle manure waste from Shouguang Youran Dairy Farm. Some of the recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation for self-consumption and supplied to the farm, and some will be used for heat generation for warming up the anaerobic digesters of the project, and the excess part will be flared. A biogas boiler will also be installed to generate the heat supplied to the anaerobic digesters of the project. The biogas residue (dried part) from the CSTR digesters will be used as cattle bedding material, and biogas slurry (liquid part) will be directly returned to the nearby farmland through a lifting pump station and a pipeline network.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system (lagoon) at the livestock farms and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility. The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas.
vcs-5558:
Changyi Youran Dairy Cattle Manure Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the Project”) locates in north of Dongyong’an Village, Duchang Street, Changyi City, Weifang City, Shandong Province, P.R China.
The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system that collects manure waste from dairy from farm in Changyi Weifang City. Some of the recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation for self-consumption and supplied to the farm, and some will be used for heat generation for warming up the anaerobic digesters of the project, and the excess part will be flared. A biogas boiler will also be installed to generate the heat supplied to the anaerobic digesters pf the project. The biogas residue (dried part) from the CSTR digesters will be used as cattle bedding material, and biogas slurry (liquid part) will be directly returned to the nearby farmland through a lifting pump station and a pipeline network.
The baseline scenario is the situation where, in the absence of the project activity, the animal manure waste were left to decay within the project boundary and methane is emitted to the atmosphere. The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas.
vcs-5559:
The project activity has the objective to capture, flare and generate electricity through the use of landfill gas (LFG)  produced in anaerobic conditions into the landfill called CTRCI - Central de Tratamento de Resíduos Cachoeiro de Itapemirim, located in the municipality of Cachoeiro de Itapemirim in the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil. 

The project activity results in greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction through two ways:
i.	Burning CH4 in flares and/or group generators;
ii.	The amount of electricity generated in the project activity is dispatched to the Brazilian national grid, avoiding the dispatch of an equal amount of energy produced by fossil-fuelled thermal plants to that grid. The initiative avoids CO2 emissions and contributes to the regional and national sustainable development.

The project constructed an efficient capture, collection and flaring system to burn CH4 (a greenhouse gas), and this reduced odours and adverse environmental impacts. Moreover, it installs generators that combusts the LFG to produce electricity, using part of the electricity for self-consumption and the other part is exported to the grid. The flares are kept in operation due to LFG excess, periods when electricity is not be produced or other operational considerations. The LFG power plant has 2.8 MW (2 x 1.4 MW) installed.
vcs-556: The Xilinguole Huitengliang Wind Power Project Guotai Phase I is a grid connected renewable energy project in Xilinhot city, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China. It involves the installation of 66 wind turbines, each of which has a rated output of 750kW, providing a total installed capacity of 49.5 MW. The purpose of the project is to utilise renewable wind power to generate zero emissions electricity for the North China Power Grid.
vcs-5562:
The objective of the Galician Atlantic Forest Restoration Grouped Project is to restore the forest cover lost due to forest fires and to establish forests in deforested areas where natural regeneration is scarce and hampered by the abundance of scrubland. The initiative focuses on reforesting ecologically degraded areas to promote biodiversity, prevent soil erosion, improve water regulation and improve ecosystem resilience. Through restoration activities the project aims to restore areas in multiple sites within Galicia by promoting the recovery of the forest ecosystem through the implementation of mixed multi-species plantations, composed of 100% native conifers and hardwood species adapted to local conditions. This combination creates a resilient forest ecosystem capable of withstanding environmental changes while enhancing landscape diversity through deciduous and evergreen trees. In addition to ecological restoration, this mixed composition plays a key role in forest fire prevention by breaking the horizontal continuity of the forest canopy, reducing the risk of fire spread. Apart from environmental benefits, the project brings social value by creating employment opportunities and promoting sustainable land management practices.
The proponents of this grouped project are CO2 Revolution and the Tierra Pura Foundation. Both organizations have extensive experience in reforestation initiatives and are implementing the project activities in partnership.
Project activities for the first instance began in September 2023, focusing on three community-based land managed areas (Comunidades de Montes Vecinales en Mano Común): Borela, Couso, and Carballedo. To date, planting has been completed for the 210.22 hectares comprising the project area for the first instance across two municipalities: Cerdedo-Cotobade in the province of Pontevedra and Avión in the province of Ourense. These areas were occupied by dense gorse and broom thickets, which after a history of forest fires.
vcs-5564:
The Carbon Roots Project is a climate resilience and sustainable agriculture initiative aimed at transforming how agricultural waste is managed in rural India. Traditionally, farmers have disposed of crop residues through open burning or by leaving them to decay, both of which release harmful greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and degrade soil health over time.
This project introduces an environmentally responsible alternative by converting agricultural waste biomass into biochar using low-tech, decentralized pyrolysis systems known as TLUD kilns. Trained representatives of the project collect the waste biomass from farmers in nearby areas, process it into biochar on-site, and return the biochar to the farmers mixed with bio fertilizers such as cow manure and compost and applied to the soil. This enhances soil structure, boosts fertility, increases water retention, and sequesters carbon in a stable form within the soil for centuries.
The project is being implemented across 10 Indian states and is rooted in principles of regenerative agriculture and circular economy. It not only prevents greenhouse gas emissions from biomass burning and decay but also reduces reliance on chemical fertilizers and supports long-term agricultural productivity. By addressing a major environmental challenge with a locally adaptable and scalable solution, the Carbon Roots Project contributes meaningfully to climate change mitigation and rural development.
vcs-5565: The project aims to implement a mechanism for Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD+) in the Xikrin do Cateté Indigenous Land, located in the state of Pará, Brazil. Its primary objective is to prevent deforestation and conserve forest carbon stocks by enhancing territorial value and strengthening Indigenous governance. The initiative is being executed with the active participation of the Xikrin people, respecting their cultural and social practices, and seeks to deliver long-term environmental, social, and climate benefits through forest protection and sustainable land management. In this context, the main objective of the Xikrin do Cateté REDD+ Project is to prevent deforestation of approximately 45,513 ha over the life span of 40 years (average of 1,137.825 ha/year), which corresponds to a reduction in emissions of around 44,475,409.35 tCO2e (average of 1,111,885.23 tCO2e/year).
vcs-5566: The Boomitra Grassland Restoration in Costa Rica project is a grouped initiative supporting ranchers in transitioning from conventional to regenerative, climate-smart grazing practices. Livestock production—covering 35.5% of Costa Rica’s land and employing 12% of the rural workforce—is a key economic sector, but also a major contributor to land degradation and greenhouse gas emissions, accounting for 23.6% of the country’s total. The project addresses financial, cultural, and technical barriers by using carbon finance to enable sustainable practices such as rotational grazing, pasture improvement, silvopastoral systems, and hedgerow integration. These interventions aim to restore soil health, increase productivity, and enhance climate resilience. The project is expected to achieve annual GHG removals of approximately 169,950 tCO₂e, with rancher participation projected to grow throughout. In addition to emissions reductions, the project contributes to multiple Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2, SDG 6, SDG 8, SDG 13, and SDG 15.
vcs-5567:
The project is centered on soil health regeneration through the adoption of improved agricultural land management practices. Its core objective is to support farmers in transitioning to regenerative farming by addressing one of the most critical barriers: access to finance.
By leveraging a climate-focused investor community, the project provides affordable financing solutions that enable farmers to maintain profitability while using fewer resources during the transition phase. This support not only empowers farmers to adopt sustainable practices but also enhances their resilience to climate-related events and contributes to the stability of the global food supply chain.
vcs-5568:
Tourba Improved Agriculture Practices in Nigeria Project is the first of its kind in the country, developed by the Tourba team to support farmers in adopting regenerative agricultural practices. Aligned with the Agricultural Land Management (ALM) category and Verra’s VM0042 (v2.1) methodology, the project aims to improve soil health, increase carbon sequestration, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Beyond its environmental goals, the initiative enhances the economic resilience of smallholder farmers by working closely with them on the ground. It addresses barriers to the adoption of sustainable land management through hands-on training, continuous support, and by building long-term incentives for climate-friendly agriculture — including a fair share of revenues from carbon markets.
The project is designed for long-term impact, with plans to scale across diverse farming systems and regions. By empowering farmers and fostering resilient agricultural landscapes, it contributes to both Nigeria’s development goals and global climate action.
vcs-557: The project is a CDM registered project with UNFCCC ref no 1575The project involves installation of 2 X4.5 MW small hydro power plants.The energy created is exported to the Karnatake grid.
vcs-5570:
The Bago Bamboo for Climate Carbon Forest Project is a Verra VCS-registered initiative in Myanmar’s Bago Region, restoring 244 hectares of degraded land through sustainable bamboo (Dendrocalamus asper) cultivation. Certified under VM0047 methodology, the project combats climate change by sequestering ~80,000 tCO₂e over 20 years (2025–2045), while addressing deforestation-driven baseline emissions (283 tCO₂e/year). Bamboo’s rapid growth (3–5 years) and perennial regeneration create a durable carbon sink, with peak sequestration (19–22 tCO₂e/ha/year) within 7–10 years.
The project integrates biodiversity conservation through native understory planting, riparian buffers, and wildlife corridors, while enhancing soil health and water retention. It aligns with 11 UN SDGs, including Climate Action (SDG 13), Life on Land (SDG 15), and No Poverty (SDG 1), generating 100+ local jobs in bamboo cultivation, processing, and biochar production. Thirty percent of carbon revenue funds community development, fostering gender equity (40% women participation) and food security via nutrient-rich bamboo shoots.
Implementation employs remote sensing, GIS mapping, and ground sampling for rigorous monitoring. Leakage risks (e.g., displaced agriculture) are mitigated via contractual land-use restrictions, GPS-monitored grazing zones, and market controls. A 20% buffer pool safeguards against non-permanence risks, leveraging bamboo’s regenerative capacity.
Developed by Green&Blue VCM Carbon Initiative and SANNANN Co., Ltd., the project adheres to Myanmar’s environmental laws, Free Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) protocols, and global standards. It supports Myanmar’s NDC targets, ASEAN Climate Vision 2025, and Paris Agreement goals, offering a replicable model for nature-based solutions in tropical ecosystems. By transforming degraded landscapes into productive carbon sinks, the project balances ecological restoration, climate resilience, and inclusive economic growth.
vcs-5571:
The Tea Shade Development and Ecological (TSHADE) Restoration Project aims to increase ecosystem productivity in tea plantations in Sri Lanka, by establishing additional shade trees and other restoration activities in selected land areas to access a range of socioeconomic and environmental advantages. The benefits include: a restoration of local biodiversity, improved soil health and ecosystem services, and additional income options for smallholder farmers. 
The establishment of shade trees will increase carbon stocks and produce carbon revenue, which will supplement the Project costs. The quality of the tea produced is expected to improve with shade cover, and access to various non-timber products in buffer zones will increase with the improvement of soil fertility. Additionally, the Project will act to empower women and educate local communities, through programs with a specific focus on sustainable land management and implementing carbon projects. 
Carbon financing is essential for the viability of the Project with the income from the carbon credits needed to secure an attractive return on investment for investors. Registration of the Project under Verra’s Voluntary Carbon Standard (VCS) and Climate Community and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards are key to enabling the sale of verifiable credits and securing a favourable price to enable the project implementation.
The total Project Area is 100,000 hectares (ha) which are selected from existing tea fields, buffer zones, low-productive areas and riparian zones currently managed by tea plantation companies and smallholder tea farmers. The Project will be rolled out over an 8-year period, with a phased approach to planting and establishment.
vcs-5574:
Weifang Youran Dairy Cattle Manure Management Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is located in the north of Zoumaling Village, Binhai Economic and Technological Development Zone, Weifang City, Shandong Province, China. This project is owned and implemented by Weifang Youran Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd.
This project utilizes the waste such as cow manure and urine generated from the newly built 12000 cow pasture of Youran Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd. as raw materials, and adopts the medium temperature CSTR anaerobic fermentation process to construct a comprehensive utilization project for manure. The biogas is used for biogas heating boilers and biogas power generation systems. The electricity generated by the biogas generator unit is used for the project's own use, and the heat energy is used for anaerobic system warming and insulation. After solid-liquid separation, the sludge is air dried and reused as cow mattress material. This project not only develops biomass energy, effectively utilizes resources, but also reduces environmental pollution caused by aquaculture, improves the ecological environment, and achieves sustainable development of modern aquaculture.
The emission reductions from electricity generation and heating will not be accounted for. 
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 44,446 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 311,122 tCO2e during the first 7-year crediting period.
vcs-5576:
The Project involves the ecological transformation of degraded pastoral and farmland into regenerating native forests across the Chatham Islands. Key measures include:

1.	The exclusion of hoofed animals through targeted fencing.
2.	Feral animal control.
3.	Strategic pest and predator management.
4.	The use of gorse as a nurse crop (Plate 1) to facilitate native
forest succession.

In areas where natural regeneration is limited, aerial seeding and drone-assisted dispersal of native species will be employed to enhance revegetation success.  Technologies supporting these measures include the use of GPS- enabled mapping tools for site planning and monitoring, remote sensing and historic aerial photography to track vegetation changes.

Drone-enabled LiDAR technology is utilised to generate high- resolution topographical and vegetation structure data, informing restoration design and providing a robust baseline for long-term monitoring.
Geographic Information System (GIS) platforms facilitate integrated spatial planning and adaptive management, while remote data loggers will eventually be implemented to track environmental variables such as soil moisture and microclimate to support ongoing ecosystem health assessments.
vcs-5577:
The project involves installation of 9.95 MW Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on rooftops at different location in Namakkal, Dindigul and Trichy districts of Tamil Nadu, India. The sole purpose of the project is to generate electricity using renewable energy sources by harnessing solar energy by using rooftop solar photovoltaic technology for meeting the captive requirement. 

The project activity is expected to reduce 13,688 tC02 annually.
vcs-5578:
The Re.green Atlantic Forest Reforestation/Restoration Project is a grouped ARR initiative designed to restore native forest cover across degraded lands within the Atlantic Forest biome in Brazil—one of the world’s most threatened biodiversity hotspots. Spanning 17 Brazilian states, the project targets former pasturelands and degraded or secondary forests, aiming to restore approximately 88,400 hectares and remove an estimated 48.7 million tCO₂ over a 100-year crediting period.
Restoration strategies range from assisted natural regeneration to full planting of native species, including the use of native timber species in silvicultural systems that align ecological and economic outcomes. The selection of models is guided by site-specific diagnostics and considers slope, forest cover, and regeneration potential. The project implements measures to minimize carbon losses, such as firebreaks, satellite monitoring, and local fire brigade training.
The first Project Activity Instance (PAI-001), covering 416 ha in Taperoá, Bahia, is expected to remove 139,794 tCO₂ over 50 years. Future PAIs will be added over time. By converting low-biomass, degraded pasturelands into functional forests, the project enhances biodiversity, improves water regulation, and supports local livelihoods via seed collection, seedling production, and restoration work. The project directly contributes to SDGs 6, 13, and 15, delivering measurable benefits for climate, nature, and communities.
vcs-558: The project of Ituiutaba Ceramic is a red ceramic company located in the Minas Gerais state, which is a region known as Triangulo Mineiro in the southeastern region of Brazil. The ceramic company produces bricks and roof tiles mainly for the regional market in Minas Gerais, but also for Mato Grosso and Goiás, which are boundary states. The fuel that was used in the baseline scenario to fire the ceramic units was native wood from the Cerrado biome, which is a pioneering practice in the region. This type of wood is considered a non-renewable biomass, once it does not originate from areas with reforestation activities or sustainable management activities.
vcs-5580: On June 7, 2022, the Bois Forte Band of Chippewa, one of eleven federally recognized Tribal Nations in the state of Minnesota, reclaimed 28,000 acres of land within its traditional reservation boundaries through a purchase that marks the largest Tribal Nation land return in the United States. Until the land transfer, the Band held 5% of its original territory, and this acquisition nearly doubled its land base. The Band is implementing Improved Forest Management (IFM) on approximately 22,000 acres of eligible forest lands within the acquisition area, allowing for the recovery of forest carbon stocks following intensive harvests under previous Timber Investment Management Organization (TIMO) ownership. Carbon revenue serves to finance the mortgage from the 2022 land purchase, as well as the development and implementation of a forest management plan. The project creates opportunities for the Band to increase access to culturally significant natural resources and preserve healthy woodlands.
vcs-5581:
This project is a mangrove afforestation and restoration initiative located in newly formed coastal char lands near Barisal City in southern Bangladesh. The project is developed and managed by BeFLAT Services, with on-the-ground implementation carried out by Bondhu Foundation, a local partner. It will be executed in collaboration with the Bangladesh Forest Department (BFD) under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change of Bangladesh.
The initiative involves both Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) and Wetland Restoration and Conservation (WRC) activities, qualifying it as a Restoring Wetland Ecosystems (RWE) project. The targeted areas are ecologically degraded, sparsely vegetated, and subject to frequent tidal inundation. Restoration measures include the planting of native mangrove species—Sonneratia apetala, Avicennia officinalis, and Exoecaria agallocha—at a spacing of 1.5 m × 1.5 m (approximately 3,000 seedlings per hectare). To ensure long-term success, gap filling and adaptive species selection based on tidal and salinity conditions will be carried out, supported by GIS monitoring, site growth assessments, and hydrological analysis.
The project covers 2,850 hectares across 28 plots, with boundaries precisely defined using GIS coordinates. Future expansion is planned through the afforestation of additional hectares. The project conforms to VCS AFOLU eligibility requirements for RWE and meets the applicability criteria of VM0033 v4.0: Methodology for Tidal Wetland and Seagrass Restoration.
By enhancing biomass and soil organic carbon (SOC), the project will sequester atmospheric CO₂, while the dense root systems of mangroves will help stabilize sediment, restore hydrological functions, and improve ecosystem resilience.
The project is expected to achieve annual GHG removals of approximately 37,724 tCO₂eq, amounting to a total of 754,448 tCO₂eq over a 20-year crediting period.
vcs-5582:
The Togg Electric Vehicle Project is Türkiye’s first domestic EV initiative developed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by replacing internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles with electric alternatives. Led by Türkiye’s Automobile Joint Venture Group (Togg), the project is implemented at an integrated EV production facility in Gemlik, Bursa.
The project follows a Grouped Project approach under the CDM AMS-III.C small-scale methodology and comprises 32 Project Activity Instances (PAIs), each capped at 60,000 tCO₂/year, across a 10-year crediting period from 2023 to 2033. Each PAI represents a batch of Togg EVs sold during a specific period and includes the following models: T10X, T10F, T8X, and T8V. Emission reductions are calculated based on model-specific electricity consumption under urban driving conditions to reflect real-world use.
The project contributes to zero-emission mobility, supports Türkiye’s climate goals, and positions Togg as a globally competitive player in the sustainable transport sector.
vcs-5585:
The Lestari Project, located within Malinau Regency, North Kalimantan Province, Indonesia, is focused on the conservation of forest resources. The project involves the conservation of three plots of forest area originally designated for logging and conversion into oil palm plantations. The Project Proponent is PT. Agra Inti Investama, which is the landowner of the three plots of land under three of its subsidiaries: PT. Agra Beverindo, PT. Agra Cahaya Keumala, and PT. Agra Water Front Indonesia. The project aims to maintain the primary land use as forest, with a small portion reserved for village expansion and improved social services.
 
Project Proponent is committed to preventing deforestation in the project area with 60,000 hectares of land in the Malinau Regency, North Kalimantan.
 
The project’s mitigation measures include enhancing local surveillance, mapping deforestation patterns, collaborating with educational institutions, and providing alternative income and social benefits to neighboring communities to minimize deforestation. The ultimate goal is to protect the natural forest from being cleared for forestry development.
 
The project operates to safeguard the forest from planned deforestation, with the primary climate objective being to reduce emissions from deforestation and forest degradation. It also aims to promote health and well-being among local populations and protect biodiversity. Monitoring efforts are crucial to ensure the integrity of the forest, with a portion of carbon credits allocated to improving social and environmental conditions in the project region.
vcs-5587:
The Conkouati-Douli National Park (CDNP) Project is led by Noé, which has managed the park since 2021. Noé’s 20-year vision is to preserve CDNP as a sanctuary for iconic Central African wildlife, while supporting local communities and contributing to global climate change mitigation. The project focuses on wildlife conservation, community development, and infrastructure rehabilitation.

Located in southwestern Congo along the Gabon border, CDNP spans 795,500 hectares—including 412,195 hectares of marine area, with an additional 2,900 km² approved in 2023. The park contains primary, lowland, and mangrove forests, hosting rich biodiversity. However, threats such as poaching, illegal agriculture, mining, and logging are degrading its ecosystems. Budget limitations constrain Noé’s ability to address these challenges.

To enhance forest protection and reduce emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD+), the project will combat illegal activities and support 31 surrounding communities with alternative livelihoods. Carbon financing through the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) will support these efforts.

The project also aims for Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) certification by delivering co-benefits in three areas:

Climate: Prevent 14.9 million tCO₂ emissions over 40 years by halting deforestation, aligning with Congo’s NDCs and REDD+ strategy.
Community: Provide improved infrastructure, alternative income opportunities, and training for the 31 local communities.
Biodiversity: Restore degraded areas and enhance habitats for key species, including gorillas, chimpanzees, and forest elephants. The project will support 8 Critically Endangered, 13 Endangered, and 27 Vulnerable species.
vcs-5589:
The proposed project is planned in a phase-wise manner, and the first instance of the project is located in the district of Agar Malwa, Madhya Pradesh state, in India. The project focuses on enhancing biodiversity in the state of Madhya Pradesh, which is the planned project zone, and improving the sustainable use of land through a biodiversity-centric approach across the state of Madhya Pradesh: For the first instance, by instituting the plantation of 16 species of fruit and forest trees on degraded and barren lands, the project aims to restore and enrich local biodiversity while also strengthening the economic resilience of the local communities.
The project is designed with a keen consideration of the local environmental and climatic conditions. Along with the ecological consideration, the species selected was an outcome of consultation with the local communities and stakeholders with an aim to enhance the ecological balance and maximise sustainable livelihoods. The species selection emphasizes biodiversity conservation, incorporating endangered and endemic species into the project. This strategic choice promotes higher tree survival rates and growth, directly contributing to the region's biodiversity and ecological health. Taking cues from a natural forest,  this project includes a multilayer afforestation model that not only optimises land use but also contributes to biodiversity enhancement, thus increasing plantation density to 650 trees per hectare. This project design aids in combating soil erosion, enhances soil fertility, and supports groundwater replenishment in these historically degraded,  barren, and under-utilized lands.

Along with enhancing the ecosystem quality of the project area, the project intends to make a significant environmental impact by sequestering an estimated total of 6,377,357 tCO2e during the entire project lifetime.
vcs-559: The project activity is to install facility to collect and use methane from abandoned coal mines (AMM), which will otherwise be emitted into the atmosphere. The AMM is withdrawn with vacuum pumps from bore holes (Pileski #2 and #3) and then cleaned, compressed, odorized and injected to a nearby pipe line owned by the local natural gas company. For injection to pipeline, the methane is delivered to a pressure swing adsorption unit for purification; the resulting methane gas is then compressed into a pipeline connect
vcs-5590:
NaturAll Carbon Limited presents the NaturAll Carbon Program – Regenerative Agriculture in Brazil – Project IV, a transformative grouped initiative across multiple Brazilian biomes, including the Cerrado, Amazon, Pantanal, and the transition zone between the Cerrado and Amazon.

This extensive program reflects a critical response to the urgent need for effective solutions addressing the environmental impacts of unsustainable agricultural practices. Recognizing that poor soil and land management contribute significantly to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and ecosystem degradation, the project implements regenerative agriculture practices that are not yet common in the region.

These practices focus on increasing Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), improving soil structure and fertility, and reducing both physical and chemical degradation. As a result, they enhance resilience to climate extremes, promote food security, and preserve essential ecosystem services.

The Cerrado, a global biodiversity hotspot, contains 44% endemic plant species among its 10,000 cataloged, while the Amazon harbors half of the world’s terrestrial species and one-third of its tropical rainforests. The Pantanal supports over 4,700 plant and animal species and plays a vital role in the region’s hydrology.

The project start date is June 1st, 2022. It uses the VM0042 v2.1 methodology to quantify climate benefits and estimates an average annual removal of 1,562,585 tCO₂e. Over a five-year validation period, the number of participating rural properties is expected to increase, expanding its reach across agricultural and livestock systems.

Beyond climate impact, the project delivers key social and environmental co-benefits, including biodiversity protection, rural livelihood support, and the long-term regeneration of Brazil’s most vital biomes.

vcs-5592:
The project falls under the AFOLU sectoral scope of the VCS standard, specifically within the Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) category. It is a grouped agroforestry project implemented across several Indian states with initial activity starting from Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and others. The primary objective is to establish agroforestry plantations on degraded, non-forest lands, fallow lands or low productive areas to enhance carbon sequestration and restore ecosystems.
Plantations will be carried out on private land parcels, targeting small and marginal farmers using sustainable practices. The project aims to cover 5,000 hectares, including only those plantations initiated on or after 01-June-2022. A participatory approach ensures voluntary farmer involvement through stakeholder consultations and community meetings.
The initiative promotes planting of native and non-native, farmer and environment friendly species to improve biodiversity, soil quality, and water conservation. It supports rural livelihoods by offering long-term income through carbon credits and secondary produce. The project will be implemented through local partners who work directly with farmers, providing training and capacity-building.
Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals, this project contributes to land restoration and climate change mitigation by increasing tree cover and reducing greenhouse gas emissions, while fostering economic development in rural communities.
vcs-5593: The Grouped Agroforestry Project, “Growing Carbon Sinks Through Agroforestry in India” spearheaded by Infinite Environmental Solutions Limited (IESL) in collaboration with local farming communities, is a visionary effort to restore degrading low productive agricultural lands, fallow lands and non-forest land while securing livelihoods and combating climate change. Spanning across multiple locations in the states of India, this project breathes new life into vulnerable soils threatened by erosion and deterioration. Through afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation, the project introduces sustainable agroforestry systems by planting a diverse mix of horticultural and timber species, including Mango (Mangifera indica), Guava (Psidium guajava), Mulberry (Morus alba), Sheesham (Dalbergia sissoo), Mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla), Gamhar (Gmelina arborea), and Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) and other tree species. By integrating these trees into farmlands, the initiative enhances soil fertility, boosts biodiversity, and sequesters carbon, creating a resilient ecosystem that benefits both people and the planet. With a mission to cover 5,000 hectares, this voluntary grouped project not only revitalizes degraded lands but also empowers farmers with long-term economic stability through sustainable agroforestry practices. By ensure GHG mitigation in the various state of India, fostering environmental resilience and livelihood security.
vcs-5594:
The project falls under AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use) category, focusing on Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR). The project is implemented as a grouped project, with large-scale planting of bamboo—a fast-growing plant known for its adaptability to diverse climatic and soil conditions.
Bamboo plays a vital role in carbon sequestration and bio-diversity conservation. It is an important non-wood forest product used in furniture, construction, shoots as food, pulp and paper industry and even handicrafts. Bamboo is therefore known as green gold, poor man’s timber etc. The key objective of the project is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by enhancing carbon stocks and preventing land use practices such as soil degradation and tillage. Its cultivation not only supports climate change mitigation but also contributes to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by restoring degraded or non-forested lands. Bamboo cultivation is envisioned as a long-term, sustainable livelihood option for farmers, especially in regions affected by deforestation. This has been reported to greatly influence people’s sociocultural lifestyle from plantation of various types of bamboo species. The production of Bamboo for both traditional and modern applications is becoming increasingly significant. As the country progresses, new economic activities focus on the utilization of bamboo resources.  By implementing this strategic design, the initiative is expected to generate quantifiable ecological, social, and economic co-benefits. In addition to increasing carbon stocks, the Project will reduce GHG emissions by preventing land use practices that contribute to emissions - such as soil disturbance from tillage, unmanaged degradation - thereby delivering net climate benefits beyond sequestration alone.
vcs-5595: The proposed Improved Agricultural Land Management (ALM) project aims to to introduce improved agricultural land management practices that reverse land degradation and replenish soil carbon, effectively creating carbon removals and promoting soil health in Nagpur, Maharashtra. The initiative involves improve fertilizer (organic or inorganic) management, Reduce tillage- Minimizing soil disturbance, Improve residue management- Conversion to vermicompost, FYM, compost and improve crop planting and harvesting- Rotational and cover crops introduced in project scenario. The project is developed as a grouped project with a total potential implementation area of 20,000 hectares. In first instance it has enrolled 1,499 smallholder farmers managing a cumulative area of 2,222 hectares for implementation of improved Agricultural Land Management (ALM) practices in Nagpur, Maharashtra .

This grouped project consists out of renewable electricity production and storage devices for own consumption while reducing the reliance on grid electricity and fossil fuel power plants.

The project consists of an inhaul hinge, an intake power tunnel of 11.8km, a 50MW (9MW ¡Á 2 + 16MW ¡Á 2) powerhouse, an 110kV switchyard and 110kV transmission lines for power evacuation.
vcs-560: The project activity is to recover sensible heat from the flue gas to generate low pressure steam using heat re-claimer coils at Emirates CMS Power Company in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, thus achieves GHG emission reduction.
vcs-5605: The “Electric Mobility Program Bangladesh” is a grouped project comprising multiple Project Activity Instances (PAIs), each managed by individual participants under contract with the project proponent, Zeroca B.V., which holds overall responsibility. The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through the deployment of battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) and battery-electric mobile machinery (BEMM) across Bangladesh, replacing fossil fuel-powered units.
vcs-5606: The Grouped project aims to install solar-powered stations, to provide reliable energy for water pumping and other agricultural purposes across Egypt. Project will involve integrating solar photovoltaic (PV) installations with existing diesel generators powering a mini grid system, the initiative seeks to reduce diesel fuel consumption.
vcs-5607:
The group project “Humus Program” supports farms in adopting and implementing organic regenerative agriculture, measuring and certifying carbon sequestration, and restoring soil health and biodiversity—while monetizing these environmental benefits for corporate partners.
The project is carried out on existing arable land previously managed using conventional or organic agricultural methods. From the first year, with no transition period, regenerative organic farming practices are implemented.
Milpa, the project proponent, is a company founded by a group of French farmers who have spent the past decade developing and refining regenerative organic practices.
As of 2025, Milpa deploys these practices across 25 farms spanning 3,255 hectares in northern and western France with a group of technical advisors, deploying these agricultural practices in the field, with the farmers on a day to day basis. More land is expected to join in the coming years, with the goal of reaching 213 000 hectares by the end of the program.
Milpa’s system prohibits the use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides and prioritizes soil health and biodiversity. The system tends toward no  tillage and is designed to boost bacterial and mycorrhizal activity, enhancing organic matter decomposition and its transformation into stable humus. This improves soil structure and fertility, enhances water infiltration, and fosters biodiversity—both in the soil and above ground.
Carbon stock increases will be measured through soil sampling every three years, both on project plots and on baseline control sites, at depths of up to 1 meter. This follows the “Measure and Remeasure” approach, aligned with the VM0042 methodology.
The project aims to remove approximately 100 tCO₂ per hectare over its course. Over time, the project is expected to remove a cumulative total of 14 million tCO₂ from the atmosphere.
vcs-5608:
The project’s climate, community and biodiversity objectives are summarized as follows:
To generate 3,915 tCO2e in emissions reductions and removals over the 40-year project lifetime (2025 - 2064), with an annual average of 91.00 tCO2e. Additionally, the project aims to design and implement Climate Adaptation and Mitigation Plans in collaboration with local communities, increasing their resilience to the impacts of climate change.
To improve the quality of life and well-being of local communities through initiatives in health, water access, basic sanitation, culture, sports, leisure and education. The project seeks to promote productive activities based on agroecology, the bioeconomy, and sustainable resource management. These activities that not only contribute to the conservation of the biome but also generate income and strengthen community livelihoods.
To conserve and monitor local biodiversity, with a particular focus on endemic, protected, and/or endangered species, engaging both communities and local institutions. These efforts will contribute to knowledge generation through education and research. The project seeks to achieve broader impact by fostering the engagement of local stakeholders and building multisectoral institutional partnerships.

Presently the project activity has installed rooftop solar PV of capacities 200 kw, 300 kw, 400 kw and 980 kw at different locations in Dindigul district. Over time, same technology would be implemented in different other sites.
