The AgriCarbon Regenerative Orchards Project is a grouped carbon initiative developed by We-Agri, designed to transition conventional orchards into regenerative systems across multiple farming communities in Israel. The project introduces a diverse mix of perennial tree species alongside regenerative practices to enhance carbon sequestration, restore soil health, and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

Implemented in semi-arid regions facing challenges such as water scarcity, soil degradation, and climate variability, the project promotes techniques like cover cropping, reduced tillage, precision fertigation, and residue management. These climate-smart practices aim to boost soil organic carbon (SOC) levels while supporting ecological and economic resilience.

Registered under the VCS VM0042 Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management, the project brings together growers in a collaborative framework that advances biodiversity, sustainable land use, and rural development.
vcs-5611:
AgCoTech Pty Ltd, an Australian company that has engaged in livestock nutrition and emissions reduction initiatives, has developed methane-reducing feed supplement technology known as Emission Control Block (ECB) for ruminants, particularly cattle and buffalo. In this project, the application of ECB technology in ruminants such as cattle and buffalo aims to reduce methane emissions from the enteric fermentation. Additionally, integration of ECB technology with farmer education programs presents an opportunity to enhance productivity and socioeconomic conditions, improve smallholder farmers’ livelihoods, increase household incomes, and reduce labor demands, enabling diversification of income-generating activities and improved access to education while contributing to global methane reduction targets, substantially supporting Lao PDR’s commitments under the Paris Agreement. 
The project will be implemented in Lao PDR as AgCoTech has a manufacturing facility in Luang Prabang Province, Lao PDR, which has been operational since late 2023. This facility is referred to as Factory 1, and Factory 2 is currently in the planning stage and it is expected to be established either in Vientiane or Savannakhet, Lao PDR. Each factory will have an annual production capacity of 250,000 blocks. The project aims to annually supply the total number of ECB units from Factory 1 and Factory 2 to smallholder farmers and/or farms. As a result, the project activity is expected to generate the total emissions reduction of 1,457,000 tCO2e from 2026-2032 or 208,143 tCO2e per annum.
vcs-5612:
The Biospark CBG Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is a newly built methane recovery and utilization project is located at Village Khedi Veeran, Muzaffarnagar district In Uttar Pradesh State of India. The Project is owned by Biospark Energy Pvt.Ltd.
The Biospark CBG Project converting the waste material, like Cow dung/Poultry Waste/Press-Mud, Fruit-Vegetable Waste into bio-fertilizer and BioCNG (purified biogas) from the organic substrates. The proposed Biospark CBG Project plant shall convert 110 MT of Mix organic waste per day into 4000KG per day BioCNG, which shall then be supplied to retailers  and 21000 KG Bio-fertilizer per day to nearby location to be used as organic fertilizer.
The Plant shall run 336 days per year, using sophisticated and proven Anaerobic Digestion CSTR technology for generation of Raw Biogas and Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) technology for Biogas Purification. Anaerobic digestion is a renewable energy generation process in which microorganisms break down biodegradable material in the absence of oxygen.
The proposed project is claiming emission reduction credits for methane avoidance via treatment of animal manure (cow dung), Fruit-Vegetable Waste and Press mud. Hence, the purpose of the project is to avoid the emissions of methane to the atmosphere from animal manure that would have otherwise been left to decay anaerobically. The baseline scenario is the same as the scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity. The project activity generates GHG emission reductions through recovery of biogas, that otherwise would be vented into the atmosphere directly.
The expected total emission reduction of the Project in the first 7-year renewable crediting period (15-September-2023 to 14-September-2030) is 247,242 tCO2e and the annual average emission reduction for the first crediting period is 35,320 tCO2e.
vcs-5614:
This project supports Pakistan’s transition to cleaner, low-emission transport by replacing internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles with electric and plug-in hybrid alternatives, including passenger cars, SUVs, light commercial vehicles (LCVs), and two- and three-wheelers. It directly addresses one of the leading contributors to urban air pollution in South Asia—transport emissions—by reducing tailpipe pollutants such as CO₂, NOₓ, and particulate matter. The resulting benefits include improved lung health, reduced smog in major cities, and a cleaner, safer environment for millions.

Beyond environmental and public health gains, the project contributes to national economic resilience by lowering Pakistan’s dependence on imported fossil fuels—a major burden on the country’s trade balance. The increased availability of electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles will also foster industrial innovation, green job creation, and long-term energy security.

The project is structured as a grouped activity, facilitating the phased deployment of electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles across Pakistan. Each instance is structured to ensure that annual emission reductions do not exceed 60,000 tCO₂e, in compliance with the applicable methodology.

The first instance is a collaboration between BYD, a global EV leader, and Mega Motor Company (MMC), its exclusive partner in Pakistan. The initiative includes nationwide sales of BYD vehicles through a growing dealership network, alongside the development of Pakistan’s first dedicated electric vehicle manufacturing and assembly facility in Gharo, Sindh. This facility will reduce vehicle costs, stimulate local industry, and create employment.

All vehicles deployed under the project will be equipped with telematics systems to track mileage and electricity consumption, enabling transparent, data-driven monitoring and verifiable emissions reductions.
vcs-5615:
The Regenerative Agriculture and Forestry Technologies (RAFT) project aims to reverse deforestation and restore degraded Miombo woodlands across Malawi’s Northern, Central, and Southern Regions. Implemented by Bridge Carbon in partnership with Total Landcare and local communities, the project uses nature-based solutions such as Assisted Natural Regeneration and enrichment planting to accelerate forest recovery while enhancing biodiversity and ecosystem services.

Through inclusive and participatory sustainable land-use management, RAFT empowers smallholder farmers and local communities to take a leading role in the management and protection of forest areas. By strengthening community governance structures and delivering long-term benefit-sharing mechanisms, the project ensures that rural livelihoods are enhanced through climate finance and co-benefits such as improved market linkages and alternative incomes, as well as sustainable woodfuel harvesting and habitat restoration.

The project is implemented under Verra’s VM0047 (v1.1) methodology and adheres to the CCB Standards (v3.1), targeting both Verified Carbon Units and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Gold distinctions. With a crediting period starting in September 2023, RAFT supports climate mitigation by sequestering carbon in biomass, contributing to Malawi’s national restoration and aligning with NDC targets, while strengthening climate resilience in vulnerable landscapes. The project reflects a commitment to high-integrity carbon credits and sustainable land restoration, positioning Malawi as a leader in community-driven climate action.
vcs-5616: The purpose of this project activity is the introduction and distribution of electric three-wheelers, which will displace the use of fossil fuel based vehicles in the transportation sector. The project is owned and implemented by TI Clean Mobility Private Limited. In the absence of the proposed project activity, the beneficiaries/users would have used the motor gasoline powered three-wheelers for transportation purposes, which would have led to greenhouse gas emissions into the atmosphere.
vcs-5617:
The project activity aims to mitigate natural gas leaks that occur as a result of oil and gas production activities within selected facilities operated by Uzbekneftegaz (UNG) and its subsidiary. Using advanced Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) technologies, gas leaks occurring within selected oil and gas production fields will be detected, measured, and repaired. Associated gas from oil fields and natural gas from gas fields contain a significant share of methane, which is a powerful greenhouse gas. Thus, the reduction of gas leaks constitutes a reduction of anthropogenic methane emissions to the atmosphere. 

The project activity targets mitigation of leaks from selected components from production units related to ongoing oil, gas and associated production operations at wells, gas and oil treatment plants, gas compressor stations and metering stations. 

Currently, these components are not routinely inspected for emissions, and GLI relies on basic leak detection techniques (e.g., LEL sensors, olfactory observations) to prevent direct safety hazards rather than to reduce emissions. Existing maintenance focuses on operational functionality rather than methane mitigation. Without intervention, methane would continue to be emitted unhindered. 

The baseline scenario assumes conventional LDAR, whereas this project goes beyond by implementing advanced LDAR, leading to ex-ante estimated emission reductions of 2,000,000 tons CO2e per year. 

Contribution to Sustainable Development 

The project supports Uzbekistan’s sustainable development goals by reducing anthropogenic methane emissions and local air pollution as well as lowering emissions of harmful gases, including carcinogenic non-methane Volatile Organic Compounds (nmVOCs), and improving worker safety and health. 

The use of advanced leak detection and quantification technologies in upstream oil production facilities has strong replication potential, enhancing resource efficiency and environmental protection.
vcs-5618: The Tourba Improved Agricultural Practices in Brazil is a large-scale carbon initiative promoting regenerative agriculture across 13 Brazilian states with the main focus on the Cerrado biome. Implemented under Verra’s VM0042 (v2.1) methodology and the Agricultural Land Management (ALM) category, the project aims to restore degraded soils, enhance carbon sequestration, and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions linked to agricultural practices.The project addresses the impact of unsustainable land use by promoting diversified cropping systems and improved pasture management tailored to the specific conditions of each biome. Through site-specific ALM interventions, it delivers both climate mitigation and increased landscape resilience. Its primary objective is to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) and reduce net emissions of CO₂, CH₄, and N₂O from croplands and degraded pasturelands.Beyond its environmental impact, the project strengthens local farming communities. It offers continuous field support and capacity-building to ensure long-term adoption of climate-smart practices. Participating farmers and ranchers receive a significant share of revenues from the sale of high-integrity carbon credits, creating meaningful financial incentives for sustainable land management.By enabling farmers and ranchers and restoring ecosystem function, the project contributes to Brazil’s climate goals and supports global efforts toward a more sustainable and resilient agricultural.
vcs-5619:
The Broadreach Yield Solar PV Grouped Project focuses on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by generating clean, renewable electricity through small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) installations. These installations are deployed across commercial, industrial, and agricultural sites in South Africa, replacing a portion of the electricity that would have otherwise been drawn from the country’s coal-intensive national grid. The project supports lower carbon emissions, reduced energy costs, and a more sustainable energy solution for businesses and communities.
The project consists of small-scale rooftop and ground-mounted solar PV systems, each equipped with solar panels, inverters, and supporting infrastructure to ensure stable energy delivery. Additionally, some sites include the integration of battery energy storage systems (BESS) to store surplus electricity and enhance energy reliability. These systems are designed to operate seamlessly alongside existing power networks, reducing reliance on grid electricity and fossil fuel-based backup power. While the primary goal is self-consumption, some surplus energy generated may be exported to the grid on condition that this is less than 50% of total generation, as per the requirements of the VCS Standard, version 4.7.
By harnessing solar power, the project helps to reduce emissions, improve energy security, and mitigate exposure to rising electricity prices and load shedding.
The first project activity instance in this grouped project is expected to achieve annual emission reductions of approximately 10,304 metric tonnes of CO2e, with an initial installed capacity of 6.3 MW in the first phase.
vcs-562: WWC's first project at Rukinga, Kenya, has been operating since 2005 protecting local wildlife and forests. The aim of this project is to bring the benefits of direct carbon financing to surrounding communities, while simultaneously addressing alternative livelihoods. Human-wildlife conflict has been a problem in the past, as local agents are reliant on flora and fauna as a means for subsistence. The Rukinga project directly addresses such sources of conflict in a holistic, sustainable approach. An additional goal is to secure a contiguous wildlife migration corridor between Tsavo East and West National Parks.
vcs-5620:
The project is an agroforestry-based tree planting activity in Indonesia, covering West Java, Central Java, and East Java. The project area includes watershed zones at different elevations. The lands used for the project are private and community lands . Prior to project implementation, these areas were either degraded or used for seasonal vegetable farming on open slopes with less than 10% tree cover.
The project plants different tree species, using four agroforestry planting patterns, with an average density of 1,200 trees per hectare. These patterns are adapted to different land conditions and farmer needs.

The project is designed as a grouped project, aiming to expand up to 10,000 hectares over 10 years. The first project activity instance (PAI) covers 21 tree species across 78.2 hectares.
vcs-5621:
Location and project description of the technologies and measures to be implemented: The FirstSolar Programme consists of the generation of renewable electricity from small scale, embedded rooftop and/or ground mounted solar photovoltaic (PV) installations on residential, commercial and industrial facilities in South–Africa.
The project activity is Solar PV installations tailored for commercial, industrial or residential agreements applications. These installations efficiently capture solar energy and transform it into sustainable electricity. Each solar PV panel is composed of layers of semi-conducting material, typically silicon, which generates electricity when exposed to sunlight. While optimal electricity production occurs in direct sunlight, the panels are designed to function effectively even on cloudy days, making them well-suited for South Africa's predominantly sunny climate. These installations not only offer a clean and renewable energy source but also enhance the reliability and security of electricity supply in South Africa.
The FirstSolar Programme group project, that is managed by FirstRand Limited, will comprise of various project activity instances. Each project activity instance may comprise multiple PV installations, up to 15 MW total installed capacity, per project activity instance in terms of the CDM methodology AMS-I.F version 05.0.
Generation of greenhouse gas emission reductions: The project activities entail the generation of renewable electricity by the conversion of solar energy. The solar PV facilities will lead to a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions due to the displacement of carbon-intensive, coal-based electricity with zero-emission solar PV based electricity.
Baseline scenario: Grid-based electricity is derived from Eskom, the state-owned enterprise that dominates electricity generation in South Africa. The use of grid electricity is the baseline scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activities.
vcs-5622:
he purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane to generate electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. Six sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 4.2MW (6*0.7MW), destroying 9.5 million m3 of methane annually. With the full capacity operation of the Project, the expected annually exported electricity will be 27,100 MWh, which will be supplied to NWPG, displacing part of the electricity generated by NWPG which is
dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. The waste heat from the generators will be recovered by waste heat boilers for hot water heating.
vcs-5623:
Metha.ai grouped project for the reduction of methane emissions in the United States (US) dairy sector ('project') aims to provide farm level tailored feed additive deployment data to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions produced by the dairy sector. 
This is grouped project following VM00041 methodology to be registered under VERRA
vcs-5624: The project refers to Reduced Impact Logging (RIL-C) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in one or more source categories (i.e. logging, skidding and transport) in the Project Area. The forest production areas within the 3 FMUs are legally designated for selective logging and the project will apply VCS methodology : VM0035 v1.0 (IFM through RIL-C) and its corresponding geographic-specific RIL-C performance module. The baseline scenario of this project is sustainable timber harvesting of the production series of the three FMUs, in line with the authorized extraction volumes and at a rate that optimizes both economic return, carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Gabonese logging regulations do not determine specific logging practices, however CBG implements voluntarily RIL-C practices aligned with its FSC Forest Management certification. These best-in-class practices are additional to business-as-usual scenario, as demonstrated through the additionality benchmark established in the applicable VCS RIL-C module.
vcs-5625: The project aims to reduce GHG emissions and generate removals by improving existing forest management through Logged to Protect Forest (LtPF) practices in productive areas within the FMUs which are legally designated for selective logging. The baseline scenario is the sustainable timber harvesting of the three FMUs, in line with the authorized extraction volumes and at a rate that maximizes economic return. The IFM project activity, which covers certain areas of the timber production series, is the implementation of LtPF areas to maintain and protect ecosystem services. In addition to the voluntary exclusion of production areas for timber production, these areas are also protected from natural disturbances (fires, pests, etc.), illegal logging, etc.; while leakage management activities prevent the displacement of emissions. The project will apply VCS methodology VM0010 v1.4 (IMF: Conversion from LtPF).
vcs-5626:
The proposed VCS project activity titled “Minas do Leão Biomethane Project” encompasses the gradual/phased implementation and operation of a complete and appropriate infrastructure for promoting efficient collection of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane (CH4)) and its destruction and/or supply/export to consumer(s) (by trucks) at the UVS Minas do Leão landfill site. 
The UVS Minas do Leão landfill is a very well-managed landfill site located in the municipality of Minas do Leão in Rio Grande do Sul State (Southern region of Brazil). The UVS Minas do Leão landfill started its operations in year 2001. This landfill has been operated by the host country project participant Solví Participações S.A. since its commissioning date in 2001.
vcs-5628:
The Greening of the Dried Aral Sea project rehabilitates a total area of 10,000 hectares in the Aral Sea region in southwestern Kazakhstan. The project is implemented by DutchGreen Project Management BV, a subsidiary of the Dutch Green Business Group (“DGB”). The Aral Sea, once the fourth-largest lake in the world, has undergone dramatic shrinkage since the 1960s. In response to this escalating challenge, the afforestation project shall rehabilitate these degraded lands by planting Saxaul trees (Haloxylon ammodendron), a native species well-adapted to arid and saline conditions, with the objective of countering the ongoing desertification of the region. 

The project establishes Saxaul as the planted pioneer species and stimulate the regeneration of additional vegetation to control the degraded ecosystem of the Aral Seabed, thereby enhancing biodiversity conservation and control of soil erosion. The project also provides employment and livelihood opportunities to the local communities adjacent to the area. This is achieved by providing jobs at the planting sites and nurseries. This will provide a stable source of income and improve the livelihoods of residents. Employment opportunities will range from skilled to unskilled labor, ensuring broad participation across the community. By creating a Saxaul covered area, the project seeks to restore vegetation cover and generate GHG emission reductions.
vcs-5629: The Maharashtra Methane Mission (M3) aims to reduce enteric methane emissions from 2 crore dairy animals across Maharashtra by deploying AI-enabled monitoring systems,portable methane sensor, smart feed interventions like the Ration Balancing Program (RBP), and innovative feed additives such as Harith Dhara. The project is a joint initiative between eVerse.AI and the Maharashtra Livestock Development Board (MLDB), the state’s apex body for livestock development. MLDB plays a central role in the program as the Project Owner, overseeing field implementation, farmer training, animal health management, and grassroots monitoring across all regions. Through the integration of eVerse.AI’s ConnectedCow and GreenCow platforms, the program targets a 30% reduction in methane emissions while improving milk productivity. The project is designed to generate high-quality carbon credits under the Verra VM0041 methodology.
vcs-563: Sterling Agro Industries Ltd. (Sterling) has undertaken a project activity, which entails thermal energy generation using renewable fuels. The project activity is being implemented at Dairy products manufacturing unit at Bhitouna, Kasganj-Soron Road, Dist-Kanshiram Nagar, Uttar Pradesh. The project activity involves the installation of biomass based boiler with an installed capacity of 15 TPH avoiding use of coal in steam generation. The main fuel (biomass) used is rice husk along with other agriculture residues as available in the region.   In the absence of this project activity, equivalent amount of energy would have been generated from coal based boiler which would spew the comparable amount of GHG into the atmosphere. Hence, the implementation of this project activity leads to reduction in GHG emissions associated with the coal based steam generation.
vcs-5630: The iKapa Solar PV + BESS 240 MWp Project is a Renewable electricity 240MWp power plant located at the West coast of South Africa in Saldanha Bay and comprises of both solar photo-voltaic power and battery energy storage system technology BESS displacing fossil-fuel intensive grid electricity.
vcs-5631: Enviro Rise is an initiative developed in the PT Rimbun Seruyan concession, which spans 34,250 hectares across the Seruyan and Kotawaringin Timur Regencies. With 62% of the area consisting of degraded peatlands, our mission is to transition from an industrial forest plantation business model which involves forest clearing and peatland drainage to one focused on actively restoring and conserving these vital ecosystems. The project also prioritizes the protection of critically endangered species, such as the Bornean orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus). In parallel, we work to empower local communities by promoting sustainable livelihood opportunities and supporting access to higher education.
vcs-5632:
The Green and Carbon Capture Project, is a reforestation project led by Scellec Teca Colombia SAS, located in the Colombian Caribbean, the first project activity instance (PAI) is located specifically within Montería (Córdoba department) and Pivijay (Magdalena department). The primary goal of the project is the establishment of commercial teak (Tectona grandis) and roble (Tabebuia rosea) plantations, while also supporting biodiversity and providing socioeconomic benefits to surrounding communities — contributing to broader climate change mitigation efforts.
The first PAI spans a total of 2,344.6 hectares in areas that have been mainly used for cattle raising since at least 10 years before project start. Project area are owned by Scellec Teca Colombia SAS. Project started in 30 June 2022, with the plantation of first project trees.
Beyond its environmental focus, the project integrates community-focused initiatives, including environmental education, training, and support for planting, maintenance, and monitoring activities. These efforts not only contribute to climate action but also help strengthen the social and economic well-being of local populations, promoting greater environmental awareness and improved living conditions.
Strengthen local employment opportunities by creating sustainable jobs and training the community in responsible forest management practices.
vcs-5633:
Ju'an (Ningbo) New Materials Technology Co., Ltd. as constructed a waste plastic recycling project with an annual output of 20,000 tons of PP flakes in Ningbo. The purpose of the Ningbo Ju'an waste plastic recycling for PP Lunch Box flake Project  (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is to build a waste plastic recycling production line integrating automation, scale, standardization and high cleanliness. According to the plan, 26,000 tons of waste plastic lunch boxes will be processed annually. The project was officially put into production on 01-Apri, 2024 (the date of project start). The project is located at No.3 to No.4 Shizi Zikeng, under Dafengshu, Liai, Qijiashan Street, Beilun District, Ningbo City. The geographic coordinates of the project site are 29.95212,121.74103. The project is developed and operated by Ju'an (Ningbo) New Materials Technology Co., Ltd.  (hereafter referred to as “the project proponent”).
Prior to the project, the same amount of PP Lunch Box flakes were produced using the same raw materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as before the project was initiated. The project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of equivalent raw materials and reducing the associated energy consumption.
vcs-5634:
Lower Sepik REDD+ Project (the Project) is located in Angoram District, Marienberg (LLG) in East Sepik Province of Papua New Guinea, with an area of 39,978 ha. The Project aims to avoid planned deforestation by halting the authorized planned harvesting activities within the scope of the timber permit issued, reducing emissions from deforestation and degradation. 
There is a permit for logging in the project area. Without the Project, the forest in the area would be harvested. Mapac Marki Limited began with the promotion of REDD+ in PNG in 2022, following with obtain the consents from landowners, terminate the logging activities from logging contractors, sign the agreements with landowners and registration the Project, in the aims of ending deforestation and environmental degradation caused by logging, promoting ecotourism, preserving forest resources, and supporting sustainable agricultural practices. It also aims to identify and deliver benefits to the stakeholders, and provide socio-economic benefits to the local communities.
vcs-5637:
The main goal of the REDD+ Arara People Project is to avoid unplanned deforestation (AUD) within the Indigenous Territory (IT) of Cachoeira Seca, located in the state of Pará, Brazil. The area covers 733,688 hectares of Amazon Rainforest, rich in biodiversity and ecosystem services, and is under increasing pressure from land grabbing, selective logging, deforestation, and mining activities (mainly for gold and iron ore), all of which threaten natural resources and wildlife.

The IT Cachoeira Seca lies across the municipalities of Altamira (76%), Placas (17%), and Uruará (7%), all classified by the Brazilian Ministry of Environment and Climate Change as priority areas for deforestation prevention and control. Over 70,000 hectares of natural forest have already been lost up to 2024. As most of the territory remains covered by native forest and is inhabited by the Arara people, the area is crucial for preserving the rainforest, reducing GHG emissions, maintaining biodiversity, and strengthening Indigenous governance over ancestral lands.

In recent years, the territory has faced growing conflicts between Indigenous communities and encroachers seeking land for timber extraction, agricultural expansion, and speculative purposes. These threats endanger the traditional lifestyle, cultural heritage, and environmental stewardship of the Arara people. Supporting the continued presence of Indigenous communities in their land protects biodiversity, as their traditional knowledge and sustainable practices contribute to ecological balance.

The project will carry out a socioeconomic census within the Arara community to support planning and implementation of initiatives that improve access to basic education, healthcare, and social well-being. It will also promote sustainable income-generating activities aimed at financial independence.
vcs-5638:
The Henan Wancheng Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Wancheng District, Nanyang City, Henan Province, China. The project aims to mitigate severe soil degradation caused by conventional agricultural land management (ALM) in local croplands by implementing improved ALM techniques.
Prior to project implementation, the predominant agricultural practices in the region included long-term monocropping, with no application of organic fertilizers and no return of crop straw to the fields, and poor irrigation management. These conventional ALM methods degraded soil structure, led to the loss of soil organic carbon (SOC), and contributed to overall soil degradation.
The project introduces multiple Improved Agricultural Land Management (IALM) practices designed to enhance SOC levels, improve soil health, and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through the following key interventions:
•	Improved Fertilizer Management: Reducing the use of synthetic fertilizers and introducing organic fertilizers into croplands.
•	Improved Crop Planting and Harvesting: Implementing crop rotation and strip intercropping of soybeans and corn.
•	Improved Residue Management: Returning and incorporating straw into cropland at a depth of 25–30 cm.
•	Improve water management/irrigation: Upgrading irrigation facilities to enhance irrigation efficiency.
These IALM practices collectively contribute to GHG emission reductions and removal by rebuilding soil organic matter, sequestering carbon, preventing degraded soil, protecting biodiversity, and improving water cycle.
During the first crediting period from 01-Aug-2022 to 31-Jul-2032, the project will implement these improved agricultural practices on 45,230 hectares of cornfields, aiming to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) levels. It is estimated that 155,063 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total emission reductions are 1,550,630 tCO2e during the first crediti
vcs-5639:
The project is located in Asgat, Dariganga, Ongon, and Naran sums, Sukhbaatar Province of Mongolia. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as implementing systematic seasonal pasture rotations, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and providing regular training to herders on sustainable grazing practices. 
Totally, approximately 300,000 ha of degraded pastureland are targeted for restoration through scientifically managed measures. It is estimated to generate an average annual GHG emission removal of 162,000 tCO2e in 20 years. The project contributes to multiple SDGs by creating local jobs (SDG 8), mitigating climate change (SDGs 13), and improving the quality of the grassland and enhancing biodiversity conservation (SDG 15).

This project is promoted by Ansal Properties and Infrastructure Limited (Ansal API) who has over 40 years experience in the real estate industry and infrastructure development.
vcs-5640: The project is located in Tov Province of Mongolia. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as implementing systematic seasonal pasture rotations, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and providing regular training to herders on sustainable grazing practices. Approximately 270,000 ha of degraded pastureland are targeted for restoration through scientifically managed measures. It is estimated to generate an average annual GHG emission removal of 200,000 tCO2e in 20 years.
vcs-5641:
The proposed grouped project activity will support the introduction and setting up of Bio-CNG production facilities in India to ensure energy security, fuel mix diversification and sustainable growth of India's fuel retail sector. The main objective of the grouped project is to support the country in establishing field-scale biogas plants by integrating competent biogas technologies and implementation. It is based on the availability of locally resourced feedstock such as agricultural residues, animal manure and other organic wastes.
All the Project Activity instances (PAIs) involved in the grouped project includes production of Bio-CNG or Compressed biogas (CBG) as primary product through anaerobic digestion (AD) process. Anaerobic digestion is a key technology for breaking down biodegradable organic waste. This biological process occurs when bacteria decompose organic matter in very low oxygen or in absence of oxygen. Essentially, it’s a controlled version of natural anaerobic breakdown. In this system, organic waste is converted into biogas, a mix of methane and carbon dioxide. Compressed Biogas (CBG) is produced after refining and removing impurities like CO2 and hydrogen sulphide. With methane content exceeding 96%, CBG exceeds industry standards and has properties and calorific value similar to fossil fuel based Compressed Natural Gas (CNG). 
Economically, project activity provides farmers with an additional revenue stream by allowing them to sell paddy straw/cotton stalk instead of stubble burning. It also generates employment opportunities in paddy straw collection, transportation, and plant operation. Through anaerobic digestion, methane is captured for Bio-CNG production, reducing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG), promoting cleaner air, and helping combat climate change.
vcs-5643: The project activity is a grouped ARR project under the AFOLU category, aiming to establish plantations over 10,000 hectares across Uganda over its 40-year lifetime. It involves the planting of Eucalyptus grandis and Pinus caribaea, species well-suited to local conditions, with the objective of increasing Uganda’s forest cover by enabling local landowners to adopt sustainable forestry practices through access to carbon finance. Prior to project implementation, the land consisted of scrublands and croplands used for subsistence agriculture, with low or declining vegetation cover and minimal carbon sequestration potential.
vcs-5644:
The carbon footprint of two scenarios for sewage sludge management was compared:
- The common practice in Croatia is to temporarily store the sewage sludge and then deliver it
to an incineration plant (Scenario 1). A one-year accumulation of sewage sludge in the storage
facility was assumed. For instance, considering legislation in some EU countries like Slovenia,
the waste collector may store the waste for a maximum of 12 months. The prerequisite is that
the storage capacity of the collection facility is not exceeded in this period (Waste Directive -
Uredba o odpadkih, Uradni list RS, št. 77/22 in 113/23).
- PRAIMGEST S.A. has introduced an alternative process whereby sewage sludge is used as
a raw material for the production of geotechnical composite (Scenario 2).
The information on the carbon footprint related to the temporary storage and incineration of
sewage sludge (Scenario 1) was obtained from the scientific literature. For the alternative
Scenario 2, e.g. processing into a geotechnical composite, the carbon footprint was calculated
using data obtained by PRAIMGEST S.A. The Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) method was used
to evaluate the total Global Warming Potential (GWP), which corresponds to the carbon
footprint (both are expressed in units of kg CO2 equivalents).
vcs-5645:
The project involves implementation of an anaerobic wastewater treatment facility and a compressed biogas generation plant at the Silvertoan Papers Limited, located at Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, India. The factory is a producer of Kraft Paper, Kraft Board and Packing Paper. The project was commissioned on 20-12-2023. Project is planned to manufacture CBG and the same will be used in vehicle. As the CBG production facility is not installed the project is using biogas recovered from waste water in power generation in existing power plant of 4 MW capacity. Prior to project activity waste was treated in open lagoon and methane was released into atmosphere. Power was produced in power plant using coal in major portion while vehicles were using fossil fuel. 
•	Power Plant produces around 27 TPH of super-heated steam for power generation at the tune of 4 MW to ensure uninterrupted round the clock electric supply to maintain optimum production
•	Project Activity was commissioned on 20th December 2023
•	The project is located at 9th Km, Bhopa Road Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh-251001, India.
•	The project collects and utilizes the biogas generated by the anaerobic treatment section of organic wastewater to generate electricity, which would otherwise be released into the lagoons.
•	The waste water generated from production of Kraft Paper, Kraft Board and Packing Paper was discharged to the lagoons directly.
•	An estimate of annual average and total reductions and removals-55,000 tCO2.
•	The total GHG emission reductions or removals generated in the monitoring period-65,000 tCO2.
vcs-5646: The Mkomazi Alienfuel Avoided Landfilling Project utilises biomass waste from the Sappi Saiccor pulp mill located in Umkomaas, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Instead of being landfilled the biomass waste is diverted to the adjacent biomass pellet production facility. The biomass pellets are utilised as a substitute to fossil fuel. The project reduces GHG emissions by avoiding methane generation from landfilling.
vcs-5648: The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane to generate electricity. The designed capacity is 4MW. Four sets of CMM power generators is installed with a total installed capacity of 4MW, destroying 8.16 million Nm3 of methane annually. With the full capacity operation of the Project, the expected annually exported electricity will be 26,000 MWh, which will meet the internal needs of the coal mine, and the surplus will be fed into China Southern Power Grid (CSPG), displacing part of the electricity generated by CSPG which is dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
vcs-5649:
The Cquestra project is led by Mari Energies Limited (MariEnergies), a leading oil and gas exploration and production company in Pakistan. Either directly or through its subsidiary, MariEnergies is executing this strategic effort to significantly mitigate its environmental footprint. The Cquestra project underscores MariEnergies’ commitment to climate action and sustainable resource development, aligning with national and global carbon reduction goals. The main purpose of the project is to capture and permanently store fossil-origin carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions generated from natural gas processing at the Sachal Gas Processing Complex (SGPC), located in District Ghotki, Sindh, Pakistan. The CO₂ being captured is of 98% purity (after water removal), making it highly suitable for compression, transport, and long-term geological storage. The captured dehydrated CO₂ will be compressed in gaseous state and injected into a deep saline aquifer, ensuring its safe and permanent sequestration.
This initiative represents Pakistan’s first large-scale CCS project and marks a pioneering step in the region’s decarbonization journey. It aims to establish an end-to-end CCS value chain, encompassing capture, transport, and permanent storage—to achieve durable emissions reductions with storage permanence exceeding thousands of years. The project will also be the first to register in Pakistan under the CCS methodology developed by the CCS+ Initiative and Verra setting a benchmark for future carbon management projects in region.
The project is anticipated to deliver an annual average reduction of 250,000-300,00 tons of CO₂, with cumulative total reductions contingent on the operational lifespan of the sequestration infrastructure. The second phase will incorporate advancements in capture technology, infrastructure optimization, and geological storage design, informed by real-world performance metrics from Phase I.
vcs-565: The Kargacaiyiri Weir and Degirmenustu Power Plant is a run-off-river type project located on Korsulu Creek within the boundaries of Sisne and Degirmenustu Villages of Kahramanmaras. Province. Proposed project consists of a hard-fill weir located at 1235m altitude (thalweg level) and 4m height from the thalweg level. The flow at the weir will be diverted to the conveyance line which has a length of about 3,736.17 m (195.2m canal + 3,545m tunnel). The flow from conveyance line will be fed to powerhouse located at about 940m , through a the penstock of 1173.5m length. The powerhouse will contain three vertical type pelton turbines each having 13.6MW installed capacity and 40.8MWm/40.0 MWe total capacity. The energy generated at Degirmenustu HEPP will be fed to the national grid through a 8km long, 2(3x477) MCM tranmission line.  The installed capacity of the plant is designed as 40.0 MW which will generate a total of annual output of 114.26 GWh. As a result of the project optimization studies, the maximum amount of 15.34 m3/s water usage in the turbines has been calculated to be economical. In return for annual energy generation, about 62,386 tCO2 is expected according to the 2006-2008 Turkish Statistics of Electricity.
vcs-5650: Akdeniz Landfill Gas Power Plant is being developed by Eko En Enerji Elektrik Imalat Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Sirketi (Inc.) within the boundaries of Akdeniz province in Türkiye. This project is being carried out on a landfill site located in the district of Akdeniz, belonging to the province of Mersin. The project activity has a total installed capacity of 10.836 MWe. In terms of operational license capacity, the site has total installed capacity of 10.836 MWe even though the landfill site has licensed capacity of 13.244 MWe. Hence, project’s licensed capacity is total of 13.244 MWe. The project activity is the capture and combustion of landfill gas via combustion engines. The generated electricity is sold to the Turkish national grid.
vcs-5651: The project activity supports the adoption of climate-smart agriculture practices among farmers in South Africa by facilitating access to carbon finance. It incentivizes sustainable land management by linking farmers to carbon markets, enabling them to earn revenue for climate-positive actions on their farms. The initiative contributes to emission reductions, improves soil health, and enhances the long-term resilience of farming systems, while aligning with broader global climate goals and strengthening rural livelihoods.
vcs-5652: Boreal Mix is a grouped IFM project (LtPF) adhering to VCS v4.7 and the VM0012 methodology. The project targets the last remaining healthy forest ecosystems in the boreal forest belt in Sweden, with a focus on protecting and enhancing biodiversity. As a result, the project also generates carbon dioxide reductions and removals, as well as safeguards and improves social values.
vcs-5653:
The project transforms 5,111 hectares of privately owned industrial forests in Quebec’s Mauricie region into sustainably managed protected areas. It adopts Logged to Protected Forests (LtPF), Reforestation (ARR) and Reduced Impact Logging (RIL) practices, replacing clear-cutting with selective harvesting of diseased or damaged trees, to preserve carbon and enhance forest health. We are reforesting historically clear cut areas in line with ARR practices. Advanced technologies like LiDAR and AI ensure precision management, while forest plans prioritize natural regeneration and reforestation.  

The initiative aligns with SDGs 8, 12, 13, and 15; decent work and economic growth, responsible production, climate action, and biodiversity conservation. The region’s diverse wildlife, including the vulnerable Rusty Blackbird, highlights its ecological importance. GHG reductions are quantified using the VCS VM0034 methodology, aiming to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market over a 40-year project duration. By integrating technology, conservation, and sustainable practices, the project advances ecological restoration and carbon offset goals, promoting responsible forestry in Quebec.
vcs-5654:
The project aims to reduce carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gas emissions from employees' use of conventional transportation for commuting and official travel by implementation of new bicycle sharing programs and introduction of e-bikes. The project activity is carried out by Pacific Cycles Inc. (hereafter referred to as “Pacific”), an enterprise committed to providing bicycle and e-bikes services to users. The project contributes to the reduction of traffic, fossil fuel-base vehicles displacement, and reduction of GHG emissions and polluting gases in the cities where the program will be implemented.
The project used the system platform to record usage data, thereby quantifying carbon emission reduction data and improving project feasibility. As a grouped project within the areas and countries of Taiwan, China, Canada, The United States, Belgium, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland, Lithuania, United Kingdom.
The continuation of the current transportation modes in the cities where the project is to be implemented is the baseline scenario. The common scenario in these urban centres comprehends the majority of fossil fuel-based transportation. The introduction of bicycles and e-bikes decrease the use of fossil fuels that would otherwise occur, reducing the amount of GHG emissions. Although the project has electricity consumption’s emissions related to e-bikes implementation, it is still lower than the average emissions of GHG by the usual transport models.
Between October 2025 and September 2032, a total of 22,125 bicycles and 88,576 e-bikes will be used in. Based on emission reduction calculation of applicable CDM methodology AMS-III.BM. “Lightweight two and three wheeled personal transportation” Version 02.0, overall emission reduction of project activity will not increase from 60,000 tCO2e/year.
vcs-5655:
The Lumwana REDD+ Project, spearheaded by Lumwana Mining Company (“LMC”), is a large-scale conservation initiative implemented in Zambia’s North-Western Province, focusing on reducing deforestation and mitigating greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, while enhancing biodiversity and improving local livelihoods. Though not formally part of a jurisdictional REDD+ program, the Lumwana REDD+ Project aligns with Zambia’s National REDD+ Framework, contributing to sustainable forest management and the diversification of the country’s economy.
The Lumwana REDD+ Project targets approximately 548,720 hectares of communal land, covering 21 communities across the chiefdoms of Mumena, Mukumbi, and Matebo within the Kalumbila District. Before the project’s implementation, the region was characterised by extensive deforestation and land degradation driven by slash-and-burn farming and other unsustainable land-use practices. Local communities depended heavily on forest resources for their livelihoods, contributing to significant biodiversity loss and GHG emissions. A partnership between LMC, traditional authorities and the Zambian government has enabled the implementation of the Lumwana REDD+ project, which aims to address these drivers of deforestation and transform unsustainable practices into sustainable development opportunities. The Lumwana REDD+ Project incorporates a range of mitigation measures and sustainable practices to achieve its objectives. By introducing alternatives like beekeeping, poultry production, goat rearing, fish farming, and gardening, the project promotes income diversification and economic resilience. These activities are supported through capacity-building programs, market access initiatives, and infrastructure development. By working with Community Forest Management Groups (CFMGs) and establishing Community Forest Management  Areas (CFMAs), the project secures community involvement and aligns with Zambia's Forest Act of 2015.

vcs-5657: The Aerovolt Electric Aviation Charging Project is the world’s first large‑scale initiative to decarbonize general aviation through the deployment of certified electric aircraft charging infrastructure across the United Kingdom. Beginning with existing installations at major general aviation airfields in the UK and expanding to multiple sites, the project supports the transition from conventional piston‑engine aircraft burning leaded aviation gasoline (AVGAS) to fully electric aircraft such as the Bristell B23 Energic. By replacing fossil fuel flights with electric operations, the project is expected to significant reduce CO₂ emissions during its initial two‑year crediting period, while also eliminating harmful airborne lead pollution. Aerovolt’s proprietary Squadron platform ensures accurate monitoring, reporting, and verification of aircraft usage and charging data. In addition to cutting greenhouse gas emissions, the project delivers co‑benefits of improved air quality, reduced operating costs for flight schools, and alignment with the United Kingdom’s Jet Zero and Net Zero 2050 strategies.

vcs-5660:
The ”Tukuze” Agroforestry Project focuses on the planting of Cashew and Moringa trees on land owned by smallholder farmers in the Coastal region of Kenya (Kilifi County as the first project activity instance), with potential future expansion to additional counties within the Coast belt such as: Kwale County, Lamu County, Tana River County, and Taita-Taveta County, who currently use their plots for subsistence agriculture and commercialize some of their produce. The benefits of the project activity include sustained economic gains for the farmers from the commercialization of cashew nuts, moringa leaves and seeds, the removal of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere for storage as biomass, and annual payments to farmers and ongoing support for the agroforestry activities.  

The area of the first Project Activity Instance (PAI) is 11,089.84 hectares, which are divided into individually owned plots of lands of approximately 30,862 farmers in Kilifi County, Kenya. It is designed as a grouped project and will be expanded into additional instances in the future reaching approximately 53,000 hectares. The project design allows for the potential inclusion of additional species in future Project Activity Instance (PAI), including Faidherbia albida, Gliricidia sepium, Melia volkensii, Mangifera indica, Leucaena leucocephala, or other suitable agroforestry tree species.
vcs-5661: The VCS project activity titled “Costa Rica Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane (CH4)) at the Parque de Tecnología Ambiental (PTA)  Uruka landfill through destruction of collected LFG in a high temperature enclosed flare and utilization of collected LFG as gaseous fuel in an engine-generator set which represent the major components of an electricity generation infrastructure with a total combined nameplate installed capacity of about 170 kW.  By promoting effective and efficient collection and destruction/utilization of LFG at the landfill, the proposed VCS project activity thus aims to promote real, permanent and measurable greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions.
vcs-5662:
The Brazilian Citrus Program for Climate Adaptation aims to convert lower-productivity and degraded pasture areas into productive citrus orchards by promoting sustainable agricultural practices, such as cover cropping and efficient water irrigation systems. These practices are designed to enhance carbon removal from soil and biomass, while improving the resilience of citrus farming to climate change. 
Over the next 25 years, the program intends to remove 2,331,500 tCO2e, managing approximately an area of 30,000 hectares.
The combined effects of record-high temperatures and spread of greening disease caused by bacteria Huanglongbinh (HLB), have required farmers to relocate to areas with different challenges, mainly within the Brazilian Cerrado. Although the incidence of greening remains low in these new areas, farmers might face additional risks due to acidic soils and less favorable rainfall patterns. 
Brazil accounts for approximately 35% of worldwide orange production and 75% of international orange juice trade, therefore the development of an even more resilient and sustainable Brazilian citriculture represents a safeguard to food security worldwide. 
The program seeks to coordinate efforts and promote sustainable agricultural practices to ensure an even more resilient citrus industry. This initiative aims to promote the adaptation to the new climate context while addressing current agricultural challenges.
vcs-5663:
The Lam Son Regenerative Sugarcane Project is an Agricultural Land Management (ALM) initiative under Verra Methodology VM0042. The project operates as a grouped project covering 508.5 hectares in Thanh Hóa Province, Vietnam.

It aims to transition conventional sugarcane cultivation—characterized by high synthetic nitrogen use (up to 350 kg N/ha) and residue burning—to a regenerative, soil-restoring model. Key project activities include: (1) reducing synthetic nitrogen fertilizer to a target of 205 kg N/ha; (2) applying organic amendments such as manure and compost; (3) ceasing post-harvest residue burning in favor of mulching; (4) extending the ratoon-cycle to reduce tillage frequency; and (5) applying lime for soil acidity adjustment.

These measures are designed to sequester soil organic carbon (SOC) and reduce N₂O emissions, thereby generating significant annual emission reductions and removals while improving soil health and farmer livelihoods.
vcs-5666:
The EnviroServ LFG Group Project involves capturing, destroying and utilising landfill gas (LFG) from landfill sites in the Republic of South Africa. LFG destruction will occur through flaring and utilisation through electricity generation.

The first Project Activity Instance under the Group Project will be the Vissershok Waste Management Facility, a solid waste disposal site (SWDS), located near Table View, Western Cape, South Africa. The landfill has been in operation since 1974  and currently receives approximately 600,000 tonnes of waste per year.

The Vissershok Waste Management Facility is owned and operated by EnviroServ Waste Management (Pty) Ltd. The site occupies a 51 hectare area and is permitted to receive Type 1, 2,3 and 4 waste.  The site is a Class A Landfill and currently operates under the following Waste Management Licences: 12/9/11/l19031514536 (Issued June 2019) and 12/9/11/L19111415044/9N 	(Issued 26 March 2020).   

The first Project Activity Instance will be developed in a phased approach, initiated with LFG destruction through flaring. Thereafter, LFG will be used for electricity generation that will be wheeled through the national grid where viable. 

Phase 1 is expected to be initiated by the commissioning of a flare on the 14th of April 2026. This may be followed by the commissioning of the electricity generator at a later stage, dependent on the technical and economic feasibility of the latter technology. 

Furthermore, the installation of a WAGABOX® system to upgrade LFG into biogas may be considered at a later stage, subject to economic feasibility of this technology. Should this materialise, this deviation will be described and justified in the first monitoring report, as it will not impact the applicability of the methodology, additionality, or the appropriateness of the baseline scenario (in line with Section 3.21.1 of the VCS standard V4.7).

The primary goal of the project is to implement a forest conservation initiative in Mexico by promoting sustainable forest conservation practices that enhance carbon sequestration while creating alternative revenue streams for farmers. This will be achieved by preserving existing ecosystems and ensuring responsible land stewardship. Dimitra, in partnership with the Alica Biosphere Foundation, is spearheading an innovative carbon credit conservation project in Mexico's Sierra de Alica region. By combining AI, remote sensing, and blockchain, this initiative empowers indigenous communities and preserves natural ecosystems. Dimitra's technology, combined with the Alica Biosphere Foundation's local expertise, drives this initiative's expansion into new regions, propelling sustainable land management practices and amplifying environmental impact.
● Carbon Sequestration & Forest Conservation: Digitally monitoring land use to prevent deforestation while enhancing biodiversity.
● Indigenous Community Empowerment: Providing technology and economic opportunities through carbon credit revenue sharing.

The Puerto Valle Nuevo mixed afforestation project proposes the establishment of both native and non-native tree species on land that has historically been used for extensive cattle grazing. 

Located within the Ituzaingó department of Corrientes province, Argentina, this grouped-project first instance will be implemented on approximately 2,088.9 hectares of a private property totaling 5,394.45 hectares.

Historically, the dominant land use in the area has been long-term, extensive cattle grazing, which has contributed to land degradation due to the lack of sustainable management practices. To restore ecological balance and enhance carbon removals, the project will plant a rich mix of native species alongside eucalyptus and pine. Plantation design will be guided by site-specific ecological conditions, with native species prioritized near areas of high conservation value.

All forest plantations created under the project will remain unharvested to promote ecosystem recovery and maximize carbon sequestration. This approach supports the generation of measurable, reportable, and verifiable (MRV) carbon removals in line with established methodologies.

Greenhouse gas (GHG) removal will occur through aboveground biomass, cultivated by both planted trees and native regrowth, the belowground biomass, including root system development and enhanced natural regeneration of native species—made possible through project activities.

The project aims to restore degraded grazing land through mixed species planting, improve biodiversity, and provide solid and verifiable benefits.
vcs-5672:
The Lukolela REDD+ Project is a REDD+ investment financed by Taranis Operations Limited and developed by The Shared Wood Company, that aims at implementing an integrated and comprehensive approach designed to reduce (i) carbon emissions by addressing the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation, including small-scale shifting cultivation (slash-and-burn) and population growth among other drivers, and (ii) alleviate poverty with the creation of tangible economic opportunities for local communities.
The activities of the Lukolela REDD+ Project will be implemented within the conservation concession No. 03/24, located in the Lukolela territory of the province of Equateur, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Project zone encompasses the entire surface of the concession, covering an area of 217’929 hectares, primarily covered by forests (210’634 hectares) and rural development areas (7’295 hectares). The forests in the concession that were previously intended for logging have been converted to conservation areas. 
Among the various environmental strategies envisioned, the project will develop agroforestry in the rural complex and perennial crops in forested landscapes, while protecting savannahs and forest mosaics with high conservation value from bushfires. All activities will be implemented through an inclusive and participatory approach based on the creation of Local Development Committees at the territory level. In addition, Local Development Funds will support the construction and rehabilitation of public infrastructure (schools, health centers, roads, and water points), helping to reduce poverty and village isolation.
vcs-5673:
This project seeks to sequester carbon through the large-scale implementation and long-term management of afforestation and reforestation (ARR) activities across federal lands in Northern California. Its primary objectives are to remove atmospheric CO₂, restore forest ecosystems degraded by wildfires, insect infestations, and historical land misuse, enhance biodiversity by expanding habitats for native plants and wildlife, and reduce soil erosion in high-risk zones.

A diverse mix of native tree species, including Douglas-fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii), Coast Redwood (Sequoia sempervirens), and California Black Oak (Quercus kelloggii), will be planted across montane, coastal, and subalpine zones. Species selection follows USDA and CAL FIRE guidelines to ensure ecological integrity and resilience to drought and wildfires.

The project utilizes a hybrid deployment strategy combining advanced aerial drones, autonomous vehicles, and trained planting crews. ISB’s proprietary planting technology enhances early-stage growth by up to 400%, with survival rates exceeding 95%, even under post-fire conditions. Biochar-amended seed pods further improve soil structure, water retention, and soil carbon stocks. Planting capacity can reach up to 2 million trees daily, enabling rapid landscape-scale restoration.

Although carbon credit projects are typically restricted on federally owned lands, this initiative has secured all necessary authorizations and contractual agreements. It aligns with federal and state priorities under USDA’s Climate-Smart Forestry framework and California’s Forest Carbon Plan. The project will generate high-quality Verra carbon credits (VM0047) over a 40-year crediting period, monitored under approved verification standards.

The Misitu ARR Project is an afforestation, reforestation, and riparian revegetation initiative aimed at increasing tree cover across Meru, Murang’a, Embu, Kirinyaga, and Tharaka Nithi counties. Covering 101,606 hectares, the project seeks to restore degraded ecosystems, enhance water infiltration, prevent erosion, and improve carbon sequestration. Additionally, it supports local livelihoods through sustainable agriculture, conservation, and economic activities. 
The project will generate greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions and carbon dioxide removals by implementing agroforestry, reforestation, riparian revegetation, and soil carbon enhancement strategies. Using VM0047 methodology, the project will sequester carbon in three key ways:

1. Above-ground biomass – Trees will capture and store carbon as they grow, increasing forest cover.
2. Below-ground biomass – Root systems will contribute to long-term carbon storage in the soil.
3. Soil carbon sequestration – Improved land management practices, including agroforestry and biochar application, will enhance soil carbon storage.

The integration of biochar will further improve soil fertility and act as a stable carbon sink, enhancing the overall carbon sequestration potential of the project. These efforts will lead to significant GHG reductions, generating carbon credits.
The revenue from carbon credits will be distributed among the project implementor, investors, and local communities. In compliance with legal frameworks, 40% of the earned carbon credits will directly benefit the community through initiatives such as:

1. Improved healthcare access.
2. Agronomy training for better farming practices.
3. Water infrastructure development to enhance resilience against climate change.

vcs-5678:
The proposed VCS-IFM Logged to Protected Forest project is a grouped project centered on the protection of currently logged secondary forests with relevant maturity features and the potential to become old-growth forests in Spain.

Historically, Spanish forests have been modified by humans since antiquity. The main alterations experienced by forests are the selection of a handful of dominant species of economic interest, the rejuvenation of forest communities and the opening of woodlands. ​

As a result of this intensive use most Spanish forests are young, homogeneous in terms of species composition and with simple structures. Like in the rest of the mediterranean region where only 2% of woodlands are considered relatively unaltered, primary forests are extremely rare in Spain. Consequently, forests in a senescent stage are very scarce and the numerous services they render are lost. Among these services are the provision of habitat for highly specialized species which rely on mature forests for their survival due to their structural diversity; the regulation of the hydrological cycle and the carbon removal and long-term storage in living and dead biomass and the forest soil. 

However, it is still possible to find in Spain forests with forest maturity attributes due to decades of low-intensity management​. These forests are the target of this project. By ceasing logging in these sites the project aims to protect forests so they can evolve in the absence of human intervention, develop the natural processes corresponding to the last stages of the sylvogenetic cycle and transform, over time, into old growth forests with their associated ecosystemic services.

Through this activity, the project expects to generate a reduction in GHG emissions during the Project Crediting Period, by avoiding the release of carbon associated with timber harvesting and other forestry operations that would take place in the baseline scenario.
vcs-5679: The Igombe REDD+ Project, located in the Tabora Region, Tanzania, is designed to implement a REDD+ mechanism. Its core goal is to prevent deforestation and preserve forest carbon stocks by promoting sustainable land management, reinforcing Indigenous governance, and enhancing the value of Indigenous territories. The project prevents the loss of forest ecosystems and preserves biodiversity within the project boundaries, while also safeguarding the ecological services relied upon by local communities. To promote economic sustainability and reduce pressure on forest resources, the project establishes a diverse set of livelihood options for participating communities. Project will implement for conservation and community development initiatives such as beekeeping, sustainable agriculture, eco-tourism, and non-timber forest product enterprises. This approach not only strengthens the local economy but also ensures that communities see tangible benefits from forest conservation, reinforcing their commitment over time. Through forest conservation efforts, the initiative aims to generate lasting environmental, social, and climate benefits. Over a 30-year period, the project seeks to prevent deforestation across approximately 106006 hectares— resulting in an annual estimated emissions reduction of 197,030 tCO₂e and total emission reduction achieved through project will be 5,910,900 tCO₂e.
vcs-568: The project activity involves implementation of WEGs as a voluntary measure to strengthen the regional grid of India through environmentally benign energy generation source available to India. The project activity is implemented in over four villages (namely Vanku, Rapharghad, Moti Sindholi and Suthri) in the Kutchh district of Gujarat. The generated electricity shall be fed into the regional grid through the locally available evacuation facility provided by the state utility (GETCO – Gujarat Energy Transmission Company Ltd.).  This project generates electricity using wind energy, which does not result in any greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Thus, this project will lead to a reduction in GHG emissions that would otherwise have occurred when using electricity generated from conventional fossil fuel based sources in the NEWNE regional grid.

CO2rozo is a large-scale grouped project within the AFOLU sector that aims to mitigate climate change through the conservation of strategic ecosystems and the sustainable transformation of livestock systems in the Caribbean region of Colombia. Its approach integrates forest and wetland protection with the implementation of regenerative agricultural practices, combining two methodologies: VM0007 – REDD+ for the conservation of natural ecosystems, and VM0042 – Improved Agricultural Land Management, for the transition to sustainable livestock systems.
The project has a 40-year crediting period, during which it plans to intervene in over 200,000 hectares distributed across private lands in the Colombian Caribbean. The project area encompasses the departments of Atlántico, Antioquia, Bolívar, Cesar, Córdoba, La Guajira, Magdalena, Norte de Santander, Santander, and Sucre, all located within the Colombian Caribbean biome—a region of high ecological value that has experienced significant degradation due to agricultural frontier expansion. This region includes critical ecosystems such as tropical dry forests, seasonal wetlands, and natural savannas.
REDD+ activities (VM0007) are designed to avoid unplanned deforestation and conserve remaining patches of tropical dry forests and inland wetlands through interventions such as knowledge management, land cover monitoring, hydrological restoration, and the formalization of voluntary conservation agreements with rural landowners to protect areas of high ecological value.
IALM activities (VM0042) promote a regenerative livestock model through actions such as the implementation of silvopastoral systems, elimination of fire use, and improved pasture and water management. These measures aim to restore soils, increase soil organic carbon (SOC) content, and reduce emissions associated with enteric methane (CH₄) and nitrous oxide (N₂O) from conventional pasture and manure management practices.
vcs-5681:
Australia’s cattle population is approximately 29 million — and in 2022 it was estimated that they produced 1.4 million tonnes of methane emissions from enteric fermentation, translating to approximately 39.2Mt of CO2e using a GWP 100. (UNSW, Sydney, 2024). Methane emissions from cattle account for approximately 33% of Australia’s reportable methane emissions, or approximately 10% of Australia’s reportable carbon dioxide equivalent emissions (A/Prof. Kelly, 2024).  

To address these GHG emissions, Ruminant Biotech “RBT” proposes a grouped enteric methane reduction project across beef farms in Southern Australia, hereafter referred to as “the project”. “Southern Australia” is, for the purposes of this project, defined as encompassing the states of New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and Tasmania. The project aims to involve a range of beef industry and industry adjacent stakeholders in Southern Australia with the purpose to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the beef and dairy cattle sector.
vcs-5685: EverEnviro Resource Management Private Limited  (hereafter referred to as EERMPL) is developing a Grouped Project aimed at producing renewable Bio-CNG from organic waste, with multiple plant locations across India. The goal of this initiative is to reduce methane emissions from unmanaged waste like biomass residue and animal manure by processing it through anaerobic digestion, and to supply purified Bio-CNG for use in the transport sector. This grouped project allows the inclusion of multiple project proponents operating individual Bio-CNG plants at various locations across India, all following a common technology and methodology framework. Before these plants were operational, the organic waste — especially biomass residue and animal manure — was largely unmanaged. It was typically dumped by farmers in pits to make digestate until it becomes suitable to be used as fertiliser,  and left to decay/ burned in cases of paddy straw. Similarly, cow dung was either disposed of informally or left to decompose in open fields. Both these practices contributed to uncontrolled methane emissions. There was no system in place to capture and use the methane generated from this decay. With the project now operational, methane that would have been released into the atmosphere is captured through sealed anaerobic digesters and directed to an upgrading system that produces high-purity methane. This methane is compressed into Bio-CNG and supplied to customers in the transport sector. For the initial four project activity instances, the projected average annual  GHG emission reductions are estimated at 189,582 tCO₂e, with a cumulative reduction of approximately 1,327,078 tCO₂e over the first seven-year crediting period.
vcs-5686:
Shanxi Lvliang Junliu CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Zhaiyadi coal mine which is a working coal mine for power generation and supply electricity to the coal mine where the Project is located for internal consumption. The project is located Shipanshang Village, Chenjiawan Township, Liulin County, Luliang City, Shanxi Province, China. The project owner is Shanxi Junliu New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. 
The direct combustion technology of the thermal energy island introduced in the Project can safely and stably burn coal mine gas with a concentration of 3% to 9%, effectively reducing methane emissions and environmental pollution. The project generates electricity by producing steam through the thermal energy island and waste heat boiler. According to the Project Feasibility Study Report (FSR), the project is equipped with a 16t/h waste heat boiler and a 3MW Steam turbine generator set. After the project is put into operation, it is expected to destructe 12.0 million Nm3 of methane annually through combustion, and export electricity 21,129 MWh per year. The electricity will be supplied to the coal mine for its own use through the distribution network of the Zhaiyadi coal mine. The waste heat generated by the boiler can provide free heating for the coal mine. 
The emissions reduction of the project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the project that would otherwise have been purchased from the power grid. It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 27-March-2024 to 26-March-2034), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 215,061 tCO2e, with the total emission reduction of   2,150,610 tCO2e.
vcs-5689:
The Karoo Sustainable Landscapes Program (KSLP) is a large-scale soil restoration project in South Africa's Western Cape Province. The project targets livestock and biodiversity conservation across three distinct habitat areas: the wet coastal Garden Route belt, the semi-arid Klein Karoo ecosystem, and the arid Groot Karoo ecosystem. The project aims to remove approximately 938,333 tons of CO2e annually through enhanced soil carbon sequestration. This will be achieved through improved grazing and fire management practices, and rangeland restoration across a planned area of 1 million hectares. The project will scale up progressively, starting with 50,000 hectares in 2025 and reaching full implementation by 2028.
KSLP operates in the Cape Floristic Region, the world's smallest but second most biodiverse vegetation kingdom after the Amazon. This region hosts over 9,000 plant species, with 70% being endemic. The project's activities include implementing controlled burning protocols, systematic grazing rotation, strategic wildlife population management, and vegetation restoration. Beyond environmental benefits, KSLP aims to improve community livelihoods for 50,000 people, primarily from historically disadvantaged communities. The project works across different land tenure regimes, including private landowners, communities, and government agencies.
