vcs-5690:
The proposed project activity is being implemented by Rama Greens, a partnership firm located in Haryana, India. The project aims to establish a Bio-CNG production facility based on anaerobic digestion of organic waste materials such as press mud, poultry litter, and cattle dung. The facility is designed to process approximately 165 metric tons per day (TPD) of these organic waste streams to generate about 15,000 m3 per day of raw biogas. The biogas will then be upgraded to produce 6,000 kg/day of high-quality Bio-CNG using Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) technology. Additionally, the project will generate approximately 40 TPD of solid manure and 160 kiloliters/day of liquid digestate as by-products, which will be utilized as bio-fertilizers.
A key feature of this project is that the produced Bio-CNG will be injected into the existing natural gas pipeline infrastructure operated by entities such as GAIL or IGL, for subsequent distribution and use in domestic households. This approach enables the substitution of LPG (Liquified  Petroleum Gas) with a renewable, low-carbon alternative in household cooking and heating applications.
In the absence of the project, the baseline scenario would involve the unmanaged decay of organic waste, leading to methane emissions, and continued reliance on LPG as fuel for cooking in households. By establishing a controlled anaerobic digestion system and displacing fossil fuel use in domestic energy applications, the project results in significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. These emission reductions will be monitored and verified as per the methodologies listed and are eligible to generate Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) under the VCS Program.
The project was commissioned on 20 January 2024. Based on current projections, the project is expected to achieve a total emission reduction of approximately 395,145 tCO₂e over a 7-year crediting period, with an average annual emission reduction of 56,449 tCO₂e
vcs-5692:
This initiative focuses on the distribution of high-efficiency improved cooking stoves (ICS) across Tanzania. The program aims to replace existing, inefficient stoves with new models that boast superior thermal efficiency. These stoves utilize wood more effectively, ensuring better heat transfer to cookware, thus conserving fuel and reducing emissions of greenhouse gases. By curbing the need for excessive firewood, the project also addresses issues like deforestation, indoor air pollution, and the considerable time people spend gathering wood.
Given that the targeted beneficiaries may not have the means to afford these stoves, the initiative typically involves significant subsidies or outright donations. Project proponents are made aware that the operation of these stoves generates carbon credits, which helps finance the stoves' costs and cover project operational expenses.
Specific details for the initial activities are outlined in Section 1.12 of the document, with information and KML files for expansions into other countries to be supplied in the document upon each activity instance's verification stage.
The introduction of ICS is set to replace traditional open-fire cooking methods, enhancing wood fuel efficiency and thereby saving on fuel and cutting back on greenhouse gas emissions. Without the project, the target population would continue relying on non-renewable wood for their thermal energy needs, a baseline scenario this project aims to improve upon.
For the initial phase, the project plans to distribute 5,000 ICSs; however, the number of units distributed in the future may change depending on the status of implementation and will be updated as appropriate during the registration and verification phase of project activities. The project plans to distribute 2,500 units each in two instances. The projected GHG reduction from the distribution is estimated at 31,866 tCO2e for 5,000 cookstoves.
vcs-5695:
The Siluk Peatlands Conservation Project (SPCP) is dedicated to protecting and restoring 28,506 hectares of peatland within the PT ASK concession in Kapuas Hulu District, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Unlike most Indonesian peatlands, which are typically located in coastal lowlands, the peatlands in the SPCP area are unique as they lie inland, in the upper Kapuas River basin.
Through targeted interventions, SPCP plays a critical role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and tackling climate change by preventing planned deforestation and peatland degradation, as well as through active peatland restoration.
Beyond conservation, SPCP meaningfully engages local communities. The project builds long-term partnerships to promote sustainable natural resource management and foster environmental stewardship. It also generates direct employment through activities such as forest patrolling, ecological monitoring, and restoration—offering alternative livelihoods that reduce dependence on destructive practices.
To further support community development, SPCP provides training and capacity-building programs in sustainable agriculture, fisheries, zero-burning farming techniques, and entrepreneurship. These initiatives aim to improve food security, raise household income, and encourage environmentally friendly practices.
By integrating conservation with socioeconomic development, SPCP empowers communities to become active partners in peatland protection—contributing not only to climate mitigation and biodiversity conservation, but also to a more sustainable and resilient future for the region.
The project also safeguards biodiversity by protecting critical habitats for endangered and native species, including the Bornean orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus) and the Lutung Sentarum (Presbytis chrysomelas cruciger)—a primate endemic to the region and closely associated with peat swamp forests.
vcs-5697:
The proposed agroforestry project spans five Indian states: Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Maharashtra, aiming to uplift tribal farmers and restore degraded lands. In regions marked by low yields, erratic rainfall, and droughts, the project will financially enable farmers to adopt climate-resilient agroforestry, integrating fruit, timber, fodder, bamboo, and endangered/endemic species selected in consultation with local communities.
Designed for local environmental conditions, the multilayer afforestation model (572 trees/ha) enhances biodiversity, soil fertility, and groundwater recharge while preventing erosion. Over its lifetime, the grouped project will sequester an estimated 8,253,286 tCO₂e (post-buffer). Sustainable practices include water-saving irrigation, organic fertilisers, and soil conservation measures.

Focusing on degraded and excess fallow lands through cluster-based development, the project supports livelihoods via free intercropping seeds, supplementary income from plantations, and capacity-building. Annual village-level events will promote activities and offer technical support, health camps, school initiatives, and community programs.

The initiative contributes to multiple SDGs: poverty reduction (1), zero hunger (2), good health (3), gender equality (5), decent work (8), climate action (13), and life on land (15). By combining ecological restoration with income generation, the project strengthens climate resilience, improves living standards, and fosters long-term community engagement.
vcs-5698:
Qingdao Haier Recycling Industry E-waste recovery and utilization Project aims to produce recycled metals and plastics by recycling E-waste. The project is located at No. 68, Huashan Road, Jiangshan Town, Laixi City, Qingdao, Shandong Province, China and is invested and owned by Qingdao Hailuyuan Recycling Technology Co. Ltd. The project processes e-waste to retrieve copper, steel, aluminum, plastic, glass and waste materials. It includes 2 refrigerator disassembly lines, 1 washing machine disassembly lines, 1 air conditioner disassembly line, 1 CRT TV disassembly line and 1 LCD TV disassembly line.
The project reduces GHG emissions by replacing virgin material production with recycling.
vcs-5699:
The Mongolia Afforestation Project (phase II) (hereinafter referred to as the ’project activity')
is implemented in 21 provinces and the capital Ulaanbaatar of Mongolia , and the project
activity aims to increase vegetation coverage in the project area through changing land
cover from non-forest to forest or enhancing stocks in existing forests.
The project started planting in October of 2025, and the project covers 638,215 ha of forest
was established by direct planted on non-forest land in the capital city of Ulaanbaatar and
21 provinces, namely Arkhangai, Bayankhongor, Bayan-Ulgii, Bulgan, Darkhan-Uul,
Dornod, Dornogovi, Dundgovi, Govi-Altai, Govisumber, Khentii, Khovd, Khuvsgul, Orkhon,
Umnugovi, Uvurkhangai, Selenge, Sukhbaatar, Tuv, Uvs, and Zavkhan
vcs-57: The project envisages utilization of the most humid waste biomass (bark and waste water  sludge) with humidity content exceeding 70% at the Arkhangelsk pulp and paper mill and the  respective substantial reduction of the fuel oil consumption by implementation of the fluidised  bed technology of steam generation for technological and heating purposes through two  stages of the technical modernization started in 2000 and 2004. Simultaneously the project  reduces the total amount of waste biomass disposal to the landfill.
vcs-570: The purpose of Guangdong Chaonan Chengtian Wind Power Project (hereafter refers to the proposed project) is to install and operate a 49.5MW grid connected wind farm in Chengtian Town, Chaonan District, Shantou City, Guangdong Province, P. R. China. Upon completion, the electricity generated from the proposed project will be supplied to Guangdong Power Grid, an integral part of the Southern China Power Grid (SCPG). The proposed project is located on the hills of Da¡¯nan Mountain, Chengtian Town, Chaonan District, Shantou City, Guangdong Province, P. R. China. The central geographical coordinates of the proposed project is approximate east longitude of 116¡ã25'49.55''and north latitude of 23¡ã06'05.23''. vcs-5700: The project is located in Akmola Oblast in northern Kazakhstan, which is one of the country's important agricultural areas, mainly used for grain production, especially wheat cultivation. However, due to long-term traditional farming practices, the region faces serious problems such as soil degradation, wind and water erosion, and loss of soil organic matter. Traditional farming practices include continuous cropping systems (such as monoculture of wheat), deep tillage, bare fallow, and monoculture.
vcs-5703: The KwaZulu-Natal Sustainable Landscapes Program (KZNSLP) is a grouped project located in the globally significant Maputaland-Pondoland-Albany biodiversity hotspot of South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal Province. The area has experienced significant ecosystem degradation and soil carbon loss due to unsustainable agricultural practices, commercial forestry impacts, and inadequate wildlife management. The project aims to regenerate 1,000,000 hectares of degraded land by 2065 through the implementation of controlled burning protocols, systematic grazing rotation, strategic wildlife population management, and vegetation restoration. KZNSLP integrates biodiversity conservation with sustainable land management across diverse ecosystems, including forests, grasslands, wetlands, and coastal habitats. The region hosts over 8,100 plant species, with 23.5% being endemic, and provides critical habitat for 14 critically endangered, 36 endangered, and 52 vulnerable species, including the iconic Big Five. Working across various land tenure regimes, including private game reserves, communities, and government protected areas, KZNSLP creates a framework for sustainable landscape management while contributing to South Africa's climate change commitments through collaboration with prominent NGOs such as WildTrust, Peace Parks Foundation, and Conservation Outcomes. The project further builds relations by working with traditional authorities as project entities and government agencies who control large land units in the region.
vcs-5704: The Navigator Company and STX Group have launched a joint restoration and reforestation project in northwest Portugal’s Bragança district, covering 483 hectares in the first phase. The project combines eucalyptus plantations for commercial timber with native species planting to restore the ecosystem and enhance biodiversity. This approach balances economic viability with ecological benefits, supported by income from timber sales and carbon credit revenues. Spanning six municipalities, the initiative aligns with Navigator’s 2030 sustainability agenda and aims to improve biodiversity, fire protection, carbon sequestration, soil health, and water retention. It actively involves local communities, creating jobs and fostering environmental stewardship. The area, previously affected by significant wildfires and dominated by bush vegetation and abandoned plantations, began site preparation in October 2024. Over the 40-year crediting period, the project is expected to sequester approximately 61,540 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, contributing to long-term climate and ecosystem resilience.
vcs-5705:
The agricultural sector is a backbone of Ghana’s countryside, employing a majority of the rural population and serving as a critical foundation for food security and climate resilience. In the Upper West Region—where the Nadowli-Kaleo District is located—agriculture provides livelihoods for approximately 85% of the working population, making it the dominant economic activity1. However, traditional agricultural practices—characterized by inefficient fertilizer use, conventional tillage, and frequent burning—have led to extensive land degradation, biodiversity loss, and diminished resilience against climatic variability2. These challenges are particularly pronounced in the savanna ecosystems of the region, underscoring the urgent need for sustainable agricultural transformation and improved land management practices3.


The Nadowli-Kaleo Climate Smart Agriculture Carbon Project aims to implement improved agricultural land management (ALM) practices to enhance and protect savanna ecosystems in the Nadowli-Kaleo District of the Upper West Region, Ghana. This initiative, involving smallholder farmers across approximately 45,000 hectares, will significantly increase soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration and above-ground woody biomass through optimized nutrient management, improved soil conservation practices, and sustainable vegetation management adapted to the region’s unique ecological context. The project will introduce a combination of practices specifically aligned with Verra’s VM0042 methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management v2.1, including optimized fertilizer application, integration of organic fertilizers such as manure and compost, implementation of precision irrigation techniques, adoption of reduced or conservation tillage practices, and significant emission reductions and removals in shrub burning and tree cutting4.


By optimizing nutrient inputs and adopting improved tillage practices, the project will reduce soil disturbance and erosion, enhance water retention, and improve overall soil health. Precision irrigation ensures efficient water use, thereby supporting sustainable agricultural productivity, even in the context of variable rainfall. Additionally, reducing shrub burning and tree cutting will protect and enhance above-ground woody biomass, providing critical support for biodiversity, hydrological stability, and carbon storage. Before project implementation, agricultural and ecological practices in the Nadowli-Kaleo District were characterized by suboptimal fertilizer use, conventional tillage methods, inefficient irrigation, frequent shrub burning, and unsustainable tree harvesting,collectively contributing to land degradation, soil erosion, reduced agricultural productivity, biodiversity loss, and diminished resilience to climatic stresses.


The project is expected to generate an average of 211,923 tCO₂e/year in verified emission reductions and removals annually, delivering measurable climate benefits while contributing directly to multiple Sustainable Development Goals. It supports SDG 13 (Climate Action) by enhancing carbon sequestration, SDG 15 (Life on Land) by restoring degraded savanna ecosystems, SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) through improved water-use efficiency, and SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) by increasing the share of land under sustainable, resilient agriculture. These outcomes will be achieved through regenerative land management practices, robust community engagement, and science-based monitoring in line with Verra’s VM0042 methodology.
vcs-5706:
The Amau Ganai REDD+ Project is located in the Abau District of Central Province, Papua New Guinea, covering an area of 30,524 ha. The project area was subject to Forest Clearing Authority, which authorized commercial clear-felling of the forest. The Project has replaced traditional logging practices by implementing forest protection measures, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions and protecting the integrity and stability of forest ecosystems.
The Project is estimated to generate GHG emission reductions of 15,265,496 t CO2e over 24 years, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 636,062 t CO2e.
The Project has attached great importance to protecting the rights and interests of the local communities. The establishment of Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes, Benefit Sharing Agreement (BSA) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) ensure the Project gained full understanding and support from the communities.
60%-70% of the carbon revenue is benefiting to the locals with a series of community projects. The project promotes community development by advancing education, healthcare, well-being, capacity-building, infrastructure, etc., which delivers measurable contributions to SDGs 1-8 and 11-15. Also, the Project involves to strengthen PNG’s national emission-reduction commitments under the Paris Agreement.
Beyond climate mitigation, the Project shields the primary forest from logging, secures critical habitat for the endangered flagship species like Goodfellow’s tree-kangaroo (Dendrolagus goodfellowi), thereby significantly enhancing regional biodiversity and strengthening the ecosystem’s resilience to climatic disturbances.
vcs-5707: The project seeks to promote agroforestry through carefully designed tree plantations to capture and store CO2 and enhance resilience to climate change impacts. The project actively engages local communities through employment, skills development, and socio-economic empowerment, with a focus on inclusivity. Cultivating trees in monoculture dominated areas enhances floral diversity and provides habitat to diverse fauna. The trees provide fruits and other parts with medicinal benefits thus contributing to socio-economic betterment of the local farming community. Thus, the project contributes to removing CO2 from the atmosphere, builds resilience of the community to climate change impacts and enhances biodiversity.
vcs-5709:
The Triunfo do Xingu ARR Project is a large-scale ecological restoration initiative covering 10,370 hectares within a designated Recovery Unit — a priority restoration area created by state decree — in the Triunfo do Xingu Environmental Protection Area (APA) in Pará. As part of Brazil’s first forest concession focused on ecological restoration, the project operates under a 40-year state concession. This public–private model restores public forestlands, with carbon credits as the primary revenue.
The area was heavily deforested from 2017 to 2022, largely by cattle ranching with fire. After legal action and the removal of all livestock, the state regained control, enabling restoration at scale. The concession was awarded on March 28, 2025, and the contract signed on July 14, 2025. Restoration is scheduled to begin in the second half of 2026, using full-area planting, enrichment planting, and passive and assisted natural regeneration. In total, 50 native species will be introduced, including 25 zoochorous and 5 threatened species. Selection considers regional occurrence, ecological function, successional stage, supply-chain availability, and carbon sequestration potential.
Classified as an Afforestation, Reforestation, and Restoration (ARR) project, the initiative follows the VM0047 methodology and seeks dual certification under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) and the Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) Standards. Over its first decade, it is expected to remove about 761,000 tCO₂e, averaging 76,000 tCO₂e per year.
Beyond climate mitigation, the project targets gold-level performance across all CCB criteria by delivering durable social and environmental co-benefits: investments in research and basic infrastructure, quality local jobs, programs for youth engagement and gender inclusion, support for land tenure regularization, and actions to strengthen the regional bioeconomy — collectively advancing a long-term, landscape-scale transformation across the region.
vcs-571: The project consists of the implementation of 2.4 MW wind farm near Puerto Baquerizo Moreno on San Cristobal Island one of the Galapagos Islands in Ecuador. The San Cristobal Wind Project is expected to produce 3,316,759 kWh the first year of operation.
vcs-5710:
The Soil Center Carbon Initiative (VCS ID: 5710) is a grouped AFOLU project under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) using methodology VM0042 (v2.1) for Improved Agricultural Land Management (ALM). Open to regenerative producers who are members of The Soil Center in Washington State, the project began on 1 September 2022 with a 20-year crediting period and renewal provisions under VCS v4.7.

The project mitigates greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and enhances soil carbon sequestration through practices such as cover cropping, organic amendments, no/strip tillage, improved water management, rotational grazing, and integrated crop-livestock systems. These measures increase soil organic carbon (SOC), improve input-use efficiency, and reduce emissions from fertilizer and fuel use.

The baseline scenario reflected conventional intensive farming: limited or absent cover crops, high chemical fertilizer inputs, minimal rotation, intensive tillage, and little to no organic amendments—contributing to soil degradation and low carbon retention.

A dual quantification approach is used: (i) SOC is tracked via direct soil sampling and laboratory analysis (Approach 2: Measure and Remeasure), and (ii) emissions from inputs and operations are estimated using default factors and historical records (Approach 3). The project initially covers 39,000 acres, targeting an average annual reduction/removal of ~2,438,383 tCO2e, totaling ~48,767,659 tCO2e over 20 years.

The initiative supports UN Sustainable Development Goals:

SDG 2: Zero Hunger – improved soil fertility and food security

SDG 12: Responsible Consumption/Production – sustainable farming and transparent reporting

SDG 13: Climate Action – verifiable GHG reductions and resilience to climate variability

Carbon Friendly Solutions Pty Ltd acts as Project Proponent, managing administration. The Soil Center, as Project Owner, coordinates implementation, soil monitoring, and delivery with Project Implementation Partners (PIPs)
vcs-5711: This project activity will capture waste CO2 which would have otherwise been emitted into the atmosphere, or atmospheric CO2 which would otherwise be in the atmosphere, and utilize that gas as a feedstock in the production of concrete. These project activities reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sequestering CO2 via the production of concrete. This manufacturing process has the additional benefit of requiring less Portland cement, which further reduces emissions, because the cement production process is highly energy and carbon intensive. The project activity will take place at the location where the concrete is first manufactured (mixed with cement, water, aggregates, etc.).  At its peak, this project activity will result in approximately 366,400 metric tons of CO2 reduced over the crediting period, the average annual emission reductions being 52,342 tCO2eq.
vcs-5712:
Vietnam Electric Vehicle Charging System Grouped Project (“VEVCS”) is an initiative undertaken by UPASSETS CO., LTD. We focus on integrating electric vehicles charging system infrastructures and logistics management platform, aims to reduce the emissions of combusting diesel and petrol fuels from traditional internal combustion engines (ICE), and expand access to convenience charging.

The Grouped Project Activity (GPA) will be submitted following Verra Methodologies VM0038, Methodology for Electric Vehicle Charging Systems, Ver1.0 and generate Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) , this methodology applies to the charging of electric vehicles (EVs) through EV charging systems, including their associated infrastructure, whose greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions are achieved through the displacement of emissions from conventional fossil fuel vehicles used for passenger and freight transportation as a result of the electricity delivered by the project chargers. The usage of electricity powered instead of fossil fuel powered cars lower GHG emissions per distance driven. This is proven in the respective emission reduction (ER) calculations.

Under this GPA, multiple Project Activity Instances (PAIs) will be included as more charging point owners join the program. Under the GPA, all carbon credits accrue under the contractual jurisdiction of UPASSETS CO., LTD.

The first project instance is set to be developed within the boundary of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, but is envisioned to extend to all counties and cities across Vietnam through GPA model.
vcs-5713:
Mongolia Afforestation Project is located in Selenge and Bulgan provinces, Mongolia, which is not part of the jurisdictional REDD+ program. The project aims to improve living conditions for local communities, promote sustainable ecological and economic development, and address environmental challenges caused by climate change through afforestation. The project plans to afforest 364,741 hectares between 2022 and 2030. Over a 50-year crediting period, it is expected to achieve a total GHG emission removal of 75,539,617 tons, with an average annual removal of 1,510,792 tons.
The project utilizes native tree species such as pines (Pinus) and Siberian larch (Larix sibirica), which are highly resistant to cold and drought. These species can quickly integrate into the local ecosystem and generate significant carbon sequestration capacity as well as ecological restoration benefits. To ensure the success of afforestation efforts, the project begins with research on seedling cultivation and planting techniques. Additionally, it includes a series of supportive measures such as pest and disease control, thinning management, the installation of fencing, and regular monitoring. These comprehensive actions are designed to significantly improve the survival rate and overall quality of the afforestation process.
vcs-5714:
Project Tarsier is a reforestation project targeting climate, community, and biodiversity benefits through Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) of deforested and degraded forestlands. Tarsier is focused on working with communities to reforest degraded areas. Communities raise seedlings of native and naturalised tree species (with over sixty native species), then carry out planting, maintenance and protection of areas to be reforested.
Tarsier operates in the Eastern Visayas Region of the Philippines and targets planting up to 5,000 ha of deforested and degraded lands managed by People’s Organisations (POs). POs are groups of individuals established at the barangay (village) level legally empowered and organised to carry out 
activities in government-owned lands under a Community-Based Forest Management Agreement.
vcs-5715: IGL Grouped Waste to CBG Project (hereafter referred to as the IGL grouped project) is methane recovery and utilization project. The project is invested, owned and operated by Indraprastha Gas Limited  and the carbon business development is responsible for EKI Energy Services Limited . Indraprastha Gas Limited is implementing a set of Waste to CBG Project production lines in India. The proposed plant involves treatment of Municipal Organic Waste to produce compressed Biogas (CBG), which shall then be converted to Bio-CNG for subsequent utilization in transport via the CNG filling stations owned by Indraprastha Gas Limited. The residual waste from biogas plant is converted into fermented organic manure (FOM) & Liquid fermented organic Manaure (LFOM) and sold to nearby farmers for agriculture use purpose.
vcs-5716:
The proposed VCS project activity titled “Salvador Biomethane Project” encompasses the gradual/phased implementation and operation of a complete and appropriate infrastructure for promoting efficient collection of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane (CH4)) and its destruction and/or supply/export to consumer(s) (by trucks and through dedicated pipeline) at the Aterro Metropolitano Central (AMC) landfill site. 
The AMC landfill is a very well-managed landfill site located in the municipality of Salvador, capital of the Bahia State (Northeast region of Brazil) and it started its operations in year 1997. This landfill has been operated by the host country project participant Bahia Transferencia e Tratamento de Resíduos S.A. since its commissioning date in 1997. 
It is important to note that the proposed project activity encompasses a new specific and independent area of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) disposal within the AMC landfill, which started to receive MSW in year 2019, and will be the only area of the landfill from where collected LFG will be destroyed/utilized by the project activity (hereby termed “project activity disposal and collection area”).
vcs-5717: The project activity implements Carbicrete, Inc.’s cement-free concrete technology at a large manufacturer of concrete products, based in North America. Carbicrete, a Montreal-based carbon removal company, has developed technology to mineralize waste CO2 during the curing stage into permanent removals and eliminate Portland cement (“PC”) from concrete production.
vcs-5718:
The TARU Odisha Project is a grouped Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) initiative aimed at restoring degraded and underutilized farmlands in Odisha, India. Implemented with local farmers and organizations, the project promotes sustainable agroforestry by planting approximately 16 native tree species selected in consultation with farming households, with the goal of enhancing livelihoods, biodiversity, and climate resilience.
In its first phase, the project will cover 500 hectares in Dhenkanal, Khordha, and Cuttack, establishing approximately 208,500 trees. Over the next three years, it will expand to 15,000 hectares across several districts, targeting the establishment of approximately 6.25 million trees over a 40-year crediting period. The first instance is expected to sequester about 192,556 tCO₂e, translating into nearly 4,814 tCO₂e annually.
Using Verra’s ARR methodology VM0047, the project employs rigorous approaches such as area-based and census-based quantification, control plot matching, and satellite-derived stocking indices to ensure transparent and verifiable carbon removals under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS). Beyond carbon benefits, it incorporates climate-smart agriculture, soil and water conservation, and farmer capacity-building, aiming to strengthen both ecological resilience and community well-being.
Spearheaded by ReNew in partnership with Gram Utthan, the project seeks to transform degraded, fallow, and low-yield croplands into productive tree-based ecosystems that deliver lasting environmental and socioeconomic benefits for local communities and future generations
vcs-572: Maoyingzi landfill is the main municipal-solid-waste (MSW) disposal place of Dalian city in the northeast China,with the daily capacity of receiving 2300 tons waste. There was a large amount of landfill gas (LFG) produced by the decomposition of organic MSW materials in the landfill which is not collected and just vented directly to atmosphere, the un-controlled LFG release impact negatively on the health of the local population by the nauseous odors from the site and lease to risks of flammable and explosive threat on the landfill site. Dalian Maoyingzi LFG Project is a typical application for renewable energy utilization and GHG reduction, which was constructed in two stages, the first stage is to build landfill gas recovery system for flaring, and the second stage is to build LFG power generation station with designed capacity up to 4MW. The negative impact and risks of landfill gas release has been greatly reduced by implementation of Project Activity.
vcs-5720: This project is a combined Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) and Restoration of Wetland Ecosystems (RWE) activity implemented under VM0033 in mangrove areas of the Scarcies River Estuary, Sierra Leone. It involves the planting and assisted natural regeneration of degraded mangrove ecosystems on community land, with the goal of generating verified GHG removals. The project follows a grouped design and applies a community-led, performance-based approach under legally binding lease agreements.
vcs-5722:
The project is an improved forest management initiative that transforms logging activities into forest conservation efforts. Without the project, 169,657 ha of logging area will be logged within 30 years, releasing huge amount of GHG emissions into the atmosphere. With the implementation of project activities, part of the logging area such as watershed area will be protected, which will generate GHG about million ton of GHG emission reductions and GHG emission avoidance through the implementation of Improve Forest Management (IFM) activities from Logging to Protecting Forest (LtPF). Around the project area, there are 16 communities directly related to the project area and approximately 130,000 residents in and around the project area, and the activities of the project aim to contribute to poverty reduction in these poor communities. Projects will be able to generate significant community benefits through positive contributions to gender, indigenous people and community livelihoods and well-being. 
The project is situated within a unique ecosystem in the Nabire district, Papua province. The project serves as a habitat for over 100 species of flora and fauna, among which more than 50 species are globally threatened according to IUCN, and 47 species are protected by P.108 Conservation Regulation from Environment and Agriculture Minister of Indonesia in 2018. These species are categorized as high conservation value species with significant ecological functions. The project holds promise for achieving remarkable biodiversity benefits through the conservation of species and their habitats. 
The project aims to reduce the climate risks and vulnerabilities of biodiversity and communities around the project area. It includes raising community awareness of climate risks and vulnerabilities, promoting agriculture development, and providing better market access for community products to enhance community adaptation strategies in climate-changing.
vcs-5723: The project halts all activities related to timber extraction within the forest concessions that are part of the project area, which are under the ownership of the company Nematsa S.A.C., the entity with legal authority over the management of the granted forest lands. In doing so, the project will conserve the carbon reserves contained in nearly 150,000 hectares of Amazonian forests, recognized for their extraordinary megabiodiversity. As part of its components, the project seeks to maintain and enhance the biological diversity of the area, including populations of wild flora and fauna species threatened with extinction, whose habitats have been disturbed by intensive logging, the opening of thousands of kilometers of skid trails, hundreds of kilometers of forest roads, and numerous log yards. Furthermore, the project has outlined improvements to strengthen its forest control and surveillance mechanisms in order to reduce illegal activities such as illegal logging, poaching, land invasions, and forest fires within the project area. To this end, it has planned the construction of strategic surveillance posts and the installation of signage in high-risk zones, as well as the permanent hiring of forest rangers to establish a routine patrolling system and maintain a continuous presence. These measures aim to reduce the vulnerability of the area, safeguard the ecosystem’s biodiversity, and ensure the identification, documentation, and reporting of actions that threaten the forest heritage of the concession. Additionally, the mechanism includes a satellite monitoring system, using high-resolution imagery to detect alterations in forest biomass, including wildfires, deforestation, illegal settlements, and even unauthorized logging.
vcs-5724:
The IndHemp Agricultural Hemp Rotation – Montana project introduces industrial hemp as a rotational crop into conventional farming systems across central Montana, USA. By integrating hemp into existing rotations of wheat, barley, canola, corn, and alfalfa, the project enhances soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration, improves soil health, and strengthens the long-term sustainability of farmland.

Industrial hemp used in the project complies with U.S. regulations (≤0.3% THC) and is primarily cultivated for fiber and hurd. The crop’s short growing season, high biomass production, and deep rooting system make it particularly suitable for increasing SOC and promoting regenerative agriculture. IndHemp manages cultivation and harvest in collaboration with contracted farmers, while EcoGaia provides technical advisory support and SoilWatch applies advanced remote sensing and modeling for monitoring.

The project applies VM0042: Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management, using Quantification Approach 1 (measure and model) and combining soil sampling, RothC modeling, and satellite imagery. Over a 40-year crediting period (2024–2064), the project is expected to generate an average of 47,545 tCO₂e annually, totaling approximately 1.9 million tCO₂e. Expansion is planned from 192 hectares in 2024 to over 15,000 hectares and 120+ farmers by 2032.

Beyond carbon benefits, the project supports the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by enhancing soil fertility and biodiversity (SDG 15), improving farm productivity and resilience (SDG 2, SDG 12), and contributing to climate change mitigation (SDG 13).

By demonstrating the role of hemp as a viable rotational crop, the project delivers scalable climate, environmental, and agricultural co-benefits while fostering sustainable land management in Montana.
vcs-5725:
In Ghana’s Upper West Region, agriculture employs about 80% of the rural population and is vital for food security and livelihoods. Farming in Wa West and Daffiama-Bussie-Issah Districts is dominated by smallholders using traditional methods such as intensive tillage, inefficient fertilizer use, shrub burning, and unsustainable tree harvesting. These practices drive land degradation, soil fertility decline, biodiversity loss, and increased vulnerability to climate stressors. Farmers face barriers to adopting sustainable practices, including financial constraints, limited technical knowledge, cultural reliance on traditional methods, and restricted access to modern technologies.

Carbon finance provides an opportunity to address these challenges by supporting climate-smart agriculture that boosts soil carbon sequestration, productivity, and resilience while conserving biodiversity. The Improved Agricultural Land Management for Verified Carbon Emission Reduction and Removal in Wa West and Daffiama-Bussie-Issah Districts Ghana Project seeks to improve land management across 91,000 hectares using Verra’s VM0042 methodology. Interventions include optimized nutrient management, conservation tillage, precision irrigation, improved grazing, agroforestry, farmer-managed natural regeneration, and reduced shrub burning and tree harvesting. Field extension teams will ensure training and community engagement.

The project is expected to generate 385,080 tCO₂e reductions annually over 40 years while contributing to SDGs on food security, water efficiency, employment, climate action, and land restoration.
vcs-5727:
AgCoTech Pty Ltd, an Australian company that has engaged in livestock nutrition and emissions reduction initiatives, has developed methane-reducing feed supplement technology known as Emissions Control Block (ECB) for ruminants, particularly cattle and buffalo. AgCoTech's ECB products reduce GHG through both direct CH₄ abatement from enteric fermentation and enhanced productivity, ultimately lowering the greenhouse gas intensity of ruminant meat and milk production. In this project, the application of ECB technology in ruminants such as cattle aims to reduce methane emissions from the enteric fermentation. Additionally, integration of ECB technology with farmer education programs presents an opportunity to enhance productivity and socioeconomic conditions, improve smallholder farmers’ livelihoods, increase household incomes, and reduce labor demands, enabling diversification of income-generating activities and improved access to education while contributing to global methane reduction targets, substantially supporting Kenya’s commitments under the Paris Agreement. 
The project will be implemented in Kenya as AgCoTech has planned the construction of two manufacturing facilities in Konza Technopolis. Each factory will have an annual production capacity of 300,000 ECBs. The emission reduction from the emission control blocks is about 470 kgCO2e for an ECB consumed. The project aims to annually supply the total number of ECB units from its proposed Konza Factories to smallholder farmers and/or farms. As a result, the project activity is expected to generate the total emissions reduction of 1,833,000 tCO2e from 01 July 2026 to 30 June 2033 or 261,857 tCO2e per annum.
vcs-5730:
Mamaland’s mission—Prosperity for Planet and People—guides the MoRe (Mountain Recovery) Malawi ARR Project, a grouped Afforestation/Reforestation/Revegetation initiative targeting deforested and degraded areas within state-owned forest reserves under the authority of the Department of Forestry.  

Malawi lost approximately 31% of its forest cover between 1990 and 2020 and continues to lose an estimated 30,000–40,000 hectares annually, driven by demand for fuelwood, agricultural expansion, and urban growth.  

MoRe Malawi responds to this trend by restoring Miombo ecosystems through assisted natural regeneration (ANR), enrichment, and direct planting of native species, combined with improved forest management. The project’s first implementation area covers 2,000 hectares in Dzalanyama Forest Reserve (Dedza District, Central Region).  

Over its lifetime, MoRe Malawi aims to restore approximately 236,000 hectares of Miombo forest across eligible reserves. The project is expected to deliver robust climate benefits—an estimated 45,387,840 tCO₂e removed—while preventing further biodiversity loss, reducing climate vulnerability, and strengthening local livelihoods.  

MoRe Malawi embeds equitable participation and benefit-sharing with surrounding communities, integrating livelihood co-benefits such as sustainable fuelwood systems, nurseries, and nature-positive value chains. Activities will be supported by transparent governance, clear land-use rights consistent with the public forest estate framework, and a fit-for-purpose MRV system (remote sensing, permanent sample plots, and leakage management) to ensure environmental integrity.  

By restoring Miombo forests at scale and channeling benefits locally, MoRe Malawi advances Malawi’s adaptation and mitigation objectives—translating Prosperity for Planet and People into measurable impact.
vcs-5732:
Mamaland’s mission—Prosperity for Planet and People—guides the MoRe (Mountain Recovery) Malawi REDD Project, a grouped initiative to avoid deforestation and forest degradation across state-owned forest reserves under the authority of the Department of Forestry. Malawi lost approximately 31% of its forest cover between 1990 and 2020 and continues to lose an estimated 30,000–40,000 ha annually, driven by fuelwood demand, agricultural expansion, and urban growth. MoRe Malawi REDD addresses these pressures by conserving standing Miombo forests through community-based forest management and sustainable land-use practices. 

The project’s core strategy is community prosperity and participation. Activities include co-management arrangements with local communities; training and paid stewardship roles; improved forest monitoring and patrolling; and carefully designed energy interventions that reduce wood-fuel dependency (e.g., efficient cookstoves, sustainable charcoal value chains with legal sourcing and efficient kilns, community nurseries and energy woodlots, and alternative household energy where feasible). These measures are complemented by livelihood co-benefits (nursery enterprises, non-timber forest products, and nature-positive value chains) to align conservation with tangible local gains. 

The first implementation cluster covers 8,662 ha across three forest reserves: PAI1 (4,637 ha) in Dzalanyama (Central Region), PAI2 (3,965 ha) in Chimaliro (Northern Region), and PAI3 (60 ha) in Michiru (Southern Region). Over its lifetime, the project aims to conserve approximately 141,000 ha of Miombo forest, avoiding an estimated 10,146,318 tCO₂e. Environmental integrity will be ensured via a fit-for-purpose MRV system (remote sensing, ground verification and leakage management). By protecting Miombo at scale while channeling benefits locally, MoRe Malawi REDD advances national mitigation and adaptation goals—translating Prosperity for Planet and People into measurable impact.

AgCoTech Pty Ltd, an Australian company that has engaged in livestock nutrition and emissions reduction initiatives, has developed methane-reducing feed supplement technology known as Emissions Control Block (ECB) for ruminants, particularly cattle and buffalo. AgCoTech's ECB products reduce GHG through both direct CH₄ abatement from enteric fermentation and enhanced productivity, ultimately lowering the greenhouse gas intensity of ruminant meat and milk production. In this project, the application of ECB technology in ruminants such as cattle aims to reduce methane emissions from the enteric fermentation. 
The project will be implemented in Cambodia as AgCoTech has planned the construction of a manufacturing facility in or nearby Phnom Penh with an annual production capacity of 300,000 ECBs. The project aims to annually supply the total number of ECB units from its proposed Phnom Penh Factory to smallholder farmers and/or farms. As a result, the project activity is expected to generate the total emissions reduction of 848,400tCO2e from 01 July 2026 to 30 June 2033 or 121,200 tCO2e per annum.

vcs-5737: The Beypi Poultry Waste to Energy Project is implemented by Beypi Beypazarı Tarımsal Üretim Pazarlama Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş., one of Türkiye’s leading poultry companies, with the objective of generating renewable energy from poultry manure. Previously, the manure was distributed to farmers as fertilizer; however, under this project, a greenfield renewable energy facility has been established to utilize 96 tons of poultry manure per day. The plant generates 30 tons per hour of saturated steam at 11 bar(g), equivalent to 157,200 tons per year, all of which is used within Beypi’s facilities. The technology is based on a fluidized bed combustion reactor and steam boiler system, supported by NOx reduction, electrostatic filters, wet cyclone scrubbers, multi-stage ash collection, economizers, and continuous emissions monitoring to ensure environmental sustainability and minimize pollution. The project is expected to achieve an emission reduction of 26,019 tCO2e annually and 182,138 tCO2e over a seven-year crediting period. By replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy, the project decreases dependence on imports, prevents soil and water pollution caused by uncontrolled manure disposal, and supports local economic development through job creation, supply chain opportunities, and infrastructure improvements. It contributes to five Sustainable Development Goals: SDG 7 by increasing renewable energy use, SDG 8 by creating productive employment and equal pay opportunities, SDG 9 by advancing sustainable industrial infrastructure, SDG 12 by promoting efficient resource use, and SDG 13 by mitigating climate change through the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.
vcs-574: The Guangdong Chaonan Shalong Wind Power Project (hereafter referred as the Project) is located in Longtian town and Chengtian Town, Chaonan District, Shantou City, Guangdong Province, P. R. China. The objective of the Project is to utilize wind resources for electricity generation. The Project involves the installation of 66 wind turbines with unit capacity of 750 kW, and totals up an installation capacity of 49.5MW. The electricity supplied by the Project is sold to Guangdong Provincial Power Grid, an integral part of the China Southern Power Grid. The Project helps reduce GHG emissions generated from the high-growth, coal-dominated power generation.
vcs-5743:
The Proyecto Tatú: Restoring the Chaco Forest in Argentina is a grouped project located in Argentina's Chaco Region, a unique high-biodiversity dry forest biome. The first project instance is situated in the Semi-arid Chaco subregion, an area historically dominated by valuable and robust Quebracho species.
Decades of extractive logging, agricultural expansion, and overgrazing have left the remaining native forests scarce, degraded, and with extremely limited capacity for natural regeneration. Historical flooding and subsequent evaporation from the Salado River have also resulted in significant soil salinity, further challenging the ecosystem's recovery.
The project's primary objective is to restore these native forests through a multi-faceted approach. This includes enrichment planting with diverse native species (e.g., Algarrobo, Quebracho) and managing natural regeneration through techniques like sprout management and selective thinning. Additionally, the project strategically establishes block plantations of carefully selected exotic species (e.g: Eucalyptus, Almendro, Paraíso) to serve as nurse crops, creating favorable microclimates that facilitate the re-establishment of the native forest ecosystem.
The first Project Activity Instance covers 14,400 hectares within six Forest Management Units in the province of Santiago del Estero. Over its 40-year crediting period, this instance is projected to deliver total GHG removals of 1,849,526 tCO₂e, which corresponds to an average of 46,238 tCO₂e per year.
vcs-5744:
The Stickland Municipal Waste Composting Project is a greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation project that reduces emissions by diverting source-separated organic municipal waste from landfills and processing it using aerobic composting technology.  The project is situated on a dedicated 3.1-hectare composting facility owned and operated by Stickland Compost, surrounded by farmland owned and operated by Stickland Farms.
The project employs Aerated Static Pile (ASP) composting technology, which uses controlled forced aeration, moisture management through a sprinkler watering system, and bio-layer coverage to ensure optimal aerobic decomposition of organic materials. Compost curing and storage are conducted on-site using windrow operations.  Temperature and moisture levels are monitored regularly to meet operational and regulatory targets. The processed waste is screened, cured, and land-applied as high-quality compost for agricultural soil regeneration.
The baseline scenario assumes that, in the absence of the project, incoming organic waste would be disposed of in regional landfills under anaerobic conditions, leading to the release of GHGs. The project prevents these emissions by managing decomposition aerobically, avoiding the creation of methane and other GHGs associated with unmanaged organic waste breakdown.
The project is expected to achieve an average GHG reduction of approximately 40,000 tCO₂e per year over the crediting period, contributing meaningful climate benefits while supporting sustainable waste diversion and soil health in Alberta.
vcs-5745: VATTHANA Cassava Starch Plant Carbon Emission Reduction Project in Laos (hereafter referred as the Project) is operated by VATTHANA  Cassava Starch Plant, located in Donglau Village, Vapi District, Salavan Province, Laos. The project involves the installation of an anaerobic treatment system (black membrane-covered anaerobic digester) for the wastewater treatment of the VATTHANA Cassava Starch plant. The biogas generated during the treatment process is utilized in the thermal boiler. The implementation of the project activity is expected to significantly contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions as well as increase of local employees' income and sustainable industrialization of Laos.

vcs-575: The nitric acid plant at Caojing, licensed by Tecnicas Reunidas (Espindesa)  from Spain, started nitric acid production on 15 July 2006. The production  capacity of the plant is 265,000 t per year (as 100% concentration  equivalent) or 1,200 t/d (68% nitric acid). Generally, this produce is used  as raw material for TDI and crude MDI production.1     The project at hand intends a substantial emission  reduction from the  nitric acid production process at Caojing by installation of a N2O  decomposition catalyst right below the platinum gauze in the ammonia  oxidation reactor as a secondary abatement measure.    With no economic benefit from N2O abatement and the absence of any legal  obligation, the emission reductions will only be realized if the investment  and the ongoing costs for the secondary abatement can be financed by a VCS  project.

The Electric Trucks and Mobile Machinery Project Nigeria (the “Project”) is proposed for registration under the Verra Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Version 4.7 and Program Guide Version 4.4. It is implemented by Sunray Carbon Intralogistics GmbH, with vehicles and mobile machinery owned/operated by Bisedge Limited. The Project is not a Grouped Project and began on January 1, 2024, with continuous deployment of battery electric vehicles (EVs) and electric mobile machinery (EMM), gradually expanding over time.

The Project applies the VCS Methodology VMR0014, Electric and Hybrid Vehicles and Mobile Machinery (AMS-III.C Revision), Version 1.0. Activities cover only battery EVs and EMMs—hybrids, plug-in hybrids, and fuel-cell vehicles are excluded. Current operations include battery electric forklifts and material handling equipment, with future integration of trucks for goods management across Nigeria.

The baseline scenario is the use of comparable fossil fuel–powered units that would provide the same services in the absence of the Project. By replacing these with EVs and EMMs powered by grid electricity, the Project significantly reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Compared with fossil-based units, EVs deliver substantial reductions by using electricity instead of diesel or petrol.

The Project’s geographical scope is nationwide in Nigeria, with EVs and EMMs deployed across multiple locations under a single ownership and operational framework. The estimated annual average reduction is 13,840 tCO₂e, totaling about 138,396 tCO₂e over the 10-year crediting period. These figures are based on initial vehicle deployment projections and may be updated as the fleet expands.

This Carbon Disclosure SA Solar PV Grouped Project 2 consists of commissioning, small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) installations and/or obtaining the rights to pursue carbon reduction from installations in the Republic of South Africa. The PV installations provide a clean, renewable source of electricity. In addition, the PV facilities contribute to electricity supply security in the country, since the national utility, Eskom, struggles to provide consistent electricity due to its aged and failing infrastructure.

The Grouped Project is managed by Carbon Disclosure SA (Pty) Ltd. Carbon Disclosure SA outsources the commissioning of the PV facilities to third parties.

vcs-5755:
The SATROKALA ARR Grouped Project, located in the Ihorombe Region of Madagascar, is designed to restore 6,311.95 hectares of degraded land through multi-species reforestation and agroforestry. The project responds to decades of deforestation, overgrazing, and desertification that have reduced soil fertility and weakened local ecosystems. By planting diverse native and non-native tree species, the project will act as a carbon sink, removing an estimated 1.9 million tCO₂e over its 40-year crediting period (2022–2061), with an average of 47,756 tCO₂e annually.
Beyond climate benefits, the project delivers strong social and biodiversity co-benefits. Approximately 200 full-time jobs will be created, including 40 for women, with training for around 150 people. Livelihood improvements are expected for 1,000 individuals, health services for 5,000 residents, and enhanced education for over 100 children, especially girls.
Biodiversity conservation covers 6,312 hectares, providing habitat benefits for threatened flora and fauna species. Overall, the project integrates carbon sequestration, rural development, and ecological resilience in one long-term program.
vcs-5756:
The El Estero Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the Project) is implemented by Extractora El Estero and involves the installation of a methane capture and biogas utilization system at its palm oil mill, located in Maní, Casanare Department, Colombia.
The Project includes the implementation of an anaerobic digestion system and biogas collection infrastructure designed to capture methane (CH₄) emissions generated during the treatment of Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) in anaerobic lagoons. The captured biogas will be used for on-site electricity generation, supplying the energy demands of the palm oil processing facility. This system displaces fossil fuel-based energy consumption and contributes to the overall reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
The facility is located within Extractora El Estero’s industrial complex in the municipality of Maní, Casanare, where palm oil is extracted and processed. The wastewater treatment system responsible for the methane emissions is fully integrated within the operational boundaries of the site.Under the baseline scenario, prior to project implementation, POME was treated in uncovered anaerobic lagoons without any biogas recovery system. As a result, methane generated through the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter was released directly into the atmosphere, significantly contributing to climate change due to methane’s high global warming potential.
In addition to these emissions, the facility has historically relied on a diesel-based power plant for its electricity needs. Approximately 299,000 gallons of diesel are consumed annually, resulting in the production of approximately 3,531,667 kWh per year. In 2022, a biomass-powered cogeneration system was introduced to complement the plant’s energy supply; however, diesel remains the principal energy source under baseline conditions.
vcs-5758:
The Go Green Jojoba Plantation Project is a large-scale afforestation initiative aimed at establishing a carbon sink in Egypt's Western Desert through the cultivation of jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis) shrubs.

Designed to combat desertification, enhance carbon sequestration, and restore degraded lands, the project follows the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) methodology under the Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) category to transform barren desert into sustainable vegetation cover while contributing to ecological resilience and improving local livelihoods.

The project is located in the El Moghra land in the Western desert in Egypt, a 20,624 acres of desert land where an agricultural transformation is emerging through the Jojoba plantation. Aligned with Egypt’s Vision 2030 and national sustainability initiatives, the project advances desert reclamation, climate resilience, and land restoration.

The Project involves the planting of the Jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis) plant which is a drought resistant shrub that is mostly woody, evergreen and perennial. Jojoba plants are highly resilient to extreme desert conditions, with deep root systems that stabilize soil, improve water retention, and sequester atmospheric carbon. Research underscores the effectiveness of arid land revegetation in climate mitigation, positioning this project as a key contributor to global sustainability efforts.

Through the planting of Jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis) species, the project is expected to generate an estimated ≈ 2,160,677 tCO2e of net GHG emission removals which is equivalent to 379 tCO2e per hectare and an annual average of 54,017 tCO2e for the project lifetime (40 years).
vcs-5759: Leket Israel, the leading food rescue organization in Israel, prevents edible surplus food from being wasted and instead redirects it to people experiencing food insecurity. This project, developed in accordance with Verra Methodology VM0046 v.1, quantifies the climate benefit of diverting food away from waste streams, where it would generate methane and other greenhouse gases, and keeping it within the human supply chain. By measuring avoided food loss and waste, the project highlights the dual impact of Leket’s mission: reducing greenhouse gas emissions while strengthening food security in Israel.
vcs-576: The project envisions the reforestation of grasslands in Colombia. The grasslands show low soil carbon content because of soil degradation and/or climate-edaphic conditions. The A/R project activity proposes to reforest ~ 1,230 ha in the area of Cáceres/Antioquia and ~ 9,640 ha in Cravo Norte/Arauca. The project areas were previously exposed to extensive cattle grazing activities. In addition to cattle grazing, some parts of the Cáceres area was exposed to alluvial gold mining. The project seeks to promote sustainable management of forest resources in a manner that fosters natural regeneration. Since 2002, Asorpar Ltd. has been reforesting land with about 25 native tree species planted in different stand models that allow for natural regeneration of flown in seeds on the reforestation sites. Asorpar Ltd. puts emphasis on promoting mixed stands. This sets their approach apart from other commercial plantation forestry entities active in Colombia. The management of mixed stands is far more challenging than of monocultures. This circumstance is reinforced by the fact that little is known about several tree species planted in the project, particularly with regard to their growth performance and silvicultural management. Hence, the proposed project activity offers a unique opportunity to obtain valuable knowledge about silvicultural management practices for mixed plantation forestry and suitability of native tree species for commercial plantation forestry.

vcs-5763: The Grande Sun Gabon Ogooué-Ivindo REDD+ Project is a developed by Hainan Grande Sun Carbon Energy Technology Co.,LTD, with the objective of promoting forest conservation and the reduction of potential greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions derived from planned deforestation and forest degradation. With a focus on forest preservation, the project's primary land use remains unchanged, barring the reserved area (up to 15% of the total project area) earmarked for future expansion and development of the existing villages and provision of additional and better social services (including the respective facilities and access roads whereto) to the local communities. The project falls under the category of Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) in the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector. The project covers an area of 146,331 hectares and is rich in forest and ecological resources. The Grande Sun Gabon Ogooué-Ivindo REDD+ Project, situated in the Mvoung, Ivindo, and Zadié departments of the Ogooué-Ivindo Province, Gabon.

The Pewma Patagonia Carbon Forestry Project is a grouped afforestation, reforestation, and revegetation (ARR) initiative in Chubut Province, Argentina. It seeks to restore degraded Patagonian steppe ecosystems, historically impacted by overgrazing and fire, through new forest establishment and assisted regeneration of native species. Activities combine Pinus ponderosa plantations on degraded grasslands with enrichment of Nothofagus antarctica (ñire), N. pumilio (lenga), and Austrocedrus chilensis (ciprés de la cordillera). Interventions use low-impact methods, livestock exclusion, and adaptive silviculture to maximize carbon removals, reduce fire risk, and improve biodiversity.

The first Project Activity Instance (PAI) is located in Las Vertientes farm (Lon: -71.427818, Lat: -44.141122). With a total of 2,028 ha, 657.3 ha are eligible under VCS criteria. Within this eligible area, approximately 71% is designated for Pinus ponderosa plantations, 21% for assisted regeneration of Nothofagus species (ñire and lenga), and 8% for enrichment with Austrocedrus chilensis (ciprés de la cordillera). The grouped project spans up to 1.75 million ha across Chubut’s Precordillera and steppe, enabling the inclusion of future PAIs under the same framework.

The project adopts a 100-year crediting period with no harvesting, ensuring permanence. Estimated net removals for the first PAI are ~243,000 tCO₂e, with an annual average of ~2,430 tCO₂e. Beyond carbon, it contributes to soil and water conservation, fire prevention, biodiversity corridors, and local employment, prioritizing rural and indigenous communities. The project seeks dual certification under VCS and CCB standards to guarantee climate, social, and ecological benefits.
vcs-5766:
Soil degradation in Lithuania remains a significant concern due to intensive agricultural practices, especially in regions with sensitive or sloping terrain. Agrokoncernas’s Carbon Farming Initiative aims address the environmental pressures affecting ecosystems and the productivity of farmlands, Agrokoncernas UAB is launching a large-scale initiative to transition over 55,000 hectares of privately managed agricultural land to more sustainable practices over the crediting period of 20 years. The project’s core objective is to adopt land management methods that capture atmospheric carbon dioxide while restoring and enhancing soil health.
The primary sustainable agricultural activities carried out are crop rotations, reduced tillage, organic farming, cover crops and reduced fertilizer use. The project is expected to have a mitigation impact of 209,333 tCO2e per year.
vcs-577: Ayrancilar is a ‘Run-off-River’ type hydroelectric power plant(HEPP) project. Ayrancilar HEPP Project is planned to be implemented by Muradiye Elektrik Üretim A.? and the project site is located on Bendimahi weir in Muradiye province of Van Province, Turkey.   The plant will have an installed capacity of 28.077 MW and generate 112,740 MWh energy annually. According to calculations based on electricity generation estimates, Ayrancilar HEPP project will result in a CO2 reduction of 68,095 tons per year due to use of renewable resources.
vcs-5770: An initiative by Usina Coruripe, which will be certified using the REDD+ methodology, focused on forest conservation efforts. The REDD+ Sertão Veredas project will be developed in the Porto Cajueiro Private Natural Heritage Reserve (RPPN), located in the municipality of Januária, Minas Gerais. The site is part of the Sertão Veredas-Peruaçu Mosaic, a group of preserved territories on the left bank of the São Francisco River aimed at reconciling biodiversity protection with the cultural and social development of communities. There is evidence that the region is under pressure from legal deforestation, which adds value to the project.
vcs-5771: The project aims to improve access to safe and clean drinking water in rural and semi-urban communities of South Africa, where many households still lack reliable water and sanitation infrastructure. By introducing energy-free, gravity-based water filters, the initiative provides a sustainable alternative to boiling water with firewood, reducing deforestation, indoor air pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions. It enhances community health by lowering the incidence of respiratory and waterborne diseases, while saving time and resources for households, especially women and children, thereby fostering healthier, more resilient communities.
vcs-5774:
ReTerra is an impactful strategic partnership and program between Rabobank Brazil, Ruuts by Ovis and Anthesis. It actively promotes the implementation of a set of regenerative practices on agricultural lands at scale in Brazil. 
The objective of the ReTerra program is to closely assist producers in a paradigm shift that will help them transition towards more sustainable use of the land. By implementing improved grazing practices and improved crop and livestock systems (ICL), producers will enhance the water- and mineral cycles, improve soil cover and biodiversity while sequestering carbon in their soils. The adopted framework is based on the GRASS standard and decades of experience in holistic management that allows the monitoring of progress.
vcs-5775: The Hedmenn Strauss Solar PV Grouped Project (the ‘Project’) involves the installation and operation of three grid-tied, ground-mounted solar photovoltaic (PV) systems (‘Project Activity Instances’) on a single industrial site in Pretoria, South Africa. The first Project Activity Instance  began operation in January 2025, while the remaining two are expected to become operational in 2026. The systems are designed to supply clean, renewable electricity directly to on-site industrial operations and associated facilities in the surrounding area. Although grid-connected to comply with national requirements of anti-islanding, no electricity is exported to the national grid. The site covers approximately 7.785 hectares of land zoned for industrial use.
vcs-5779: Community Climate Solutions (CCS) is a pioneering initiative born from two decades of grassroots work in Zambia’s rural communities. It was conceived to address the intertwined crises of environmental degradation and rural poverty, with the ambition to transform subsistence farmers into “ECO₂preneurs.” Operating across nearly 1 million hectares of Miombo woodlands, CCS empowers over 20,000 rural households to remove over 2 million tons of CO₂ annually. Through a best-in-class 60–70% revenue share model, CCS delivers both immediate financial benefits and long-term development outcomes, combining direct cash transfers for climate-positive actions with foundations that build the infrastructure and human capital for lasting livelihoods. Together with Climate Impact Partners, CCS is bringing this transformational project to the voluntary carbon market, ensuring high-quality and high integrity credit generation and deep community impact.
vcs-578: Menge Dam and Hydroelectric Plant are large scale power plant plant with an installed capacity of 85 MW. The average annual electiricty generation is estimated to be 202.56 GWh and will replace the 123,967 tons of CO2 emissions which would have been released by fossil fired power plants. The project contributes to green electricity generation in the country and reduces the dependency on imported fossil energy sources. International environmental and social standards of International Finance Corporation (Performance Standards, Equator Principles) have been followed during the project implementation. The project provides job opportunuties to local communities as well as other social benefits to local schools and educational activities.
vcs-5780:
The KA’AGUY+ Project is a grouped REDD+ initiative designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from under-canopy forest degradation in Paraguay’s native forest remnants located within productive landscapes. Initially focused in the Eastern Region, the project aims to progressively scale up to around 100,000 hectares nationwide, establishing a unified framework for conservation and active forest management.
KA’AGUY+ integrates high-resolution satellite monitoring with stratified field inventories to measure degradation intensity and verify emission reductions with scientific precision. Participating landholders enter conservation agreements and receive direct economic benefits from verified carbon credits generated by maintaining the integrity and carbon stock of their forest areas.
Beyond reducing emissions, KA’AGUY+ enhances biodiversity conservation and supports sustainable rural livelihoods, transforming forest remnants within productive areas into valuable environmental assets. By combining advanced monitoring, local engagement, and transparent benefit-sharing, the project establishes a replicable and high-integrity model of productive conservation, positioning Paraguay as a regional leader in avoided forest degradation.
vcs-5782: The “Electric Mobility Program Morocco” is a grouped project comprising multiple Project Activity Instances (PAIs), each managed by individual participants under contract with the project proponent, Zeroca B.V., which holds overall responsibility. The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through the deployment of battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) and battery-electric mobile machinery (BEMM) across Morocco, replacing fossil fuel-powered units.
vcs-5783:
Green Gold Forestry Peru S.A. (GGF), established in 2008, is committed to the sustainable management and conservation of Amazonian forests in the Loreto Region. Over the years, GGF has evolved from a timber-based model to one focused on forest conservation, ecosystem services, and inclusive community participation.

The Green Gold Loreto 2 (GGL2) Project encompasses 106,575 hectares within GGF’s forest concessions in Loreto, Peru. The project transitions active timber concessions from planned logging to long-term conservation. All baseline logging, including the construction and maintenance of roads, skidding trails, and other infrastructure, has ceased. By halting these operations, the project eliminates emissions from extraction, transport, and collateral damage, while allowing carbon stocks to recover and increase over time in line with the natural accumulation trends of Amazonian forests. 

The project enhances biodiversity recovery and ecosystem integrity, enabling previously logged areas to regenerate naturally. GGL2 also partners with surrounding communities to strengthen conservation efforts and deliver social, environmental, and climate benefits.
vcs-5784:
This project involves the recovery and utilization of Empty Fruit Bunches (EFB), waste from the palm oil industry that was previously left to decompose anaerobically at mill sites or disposed of in landfills, releasing methane into the atmosphere. Instead of being discarded, the EFB is now collected, pressed, shredded, and processed into renewable biomass fuel such as fibers, pellets, or briquettes for use in industrial burners as a replacement for fossil fuels like coal.

The process includes impurity removal, mechanical dewatering using a screw press, drying, pelleting, and cooling before packaging for sale. By transforming EFB into a marketable renewable fuel, the project effectively prevents methane emissions from unmanaged waste decomposition while displacing fossil-based energy in downstream applications.

This initiative promotes sustainable waste management and circular economy practices within the palm oil sector by converting agricultural residue into a productive, low-carbon energy source. Through this, the project delivers measurable greenhouse gas emission reductions and supports Malaysia’s transition toward cleaner, renewable energy systems in line with national climate commitments.
