Prior to the project, the project area was suitable land for forest, there is no forestry management and the coverage by planting trees is low, and there has never been any activity affecting the local ecosystem . By checking the afforestation plan with the forestry bureau of Qianxinan and Anshun, it was confirmed that, a small number of trees have been planted in some project area before the project started, but the coverage by planting trees is low. So considering the low forest coverage, the forestry bureau of Qianxinan and Anshun determined that the project area is suitable for afforestation after investigation, then the local forestry bureau approved the supplementary planting without disturbing the existing trees in January 2019 to increase the vegetative cover.
ccb-3055: The ITAÚBA REDD+ PROJECT aims at protecting forests in one of the regions having the highest deforestation trends in the Amazon Biome, in the municipalities of Itaúba and Marcelândia. Both the municipalities are inside the “Arc of Deforestation” and since the colonization of the municipalities, besides the damage caused to natural ecosystems, several social conflicts have emerged from the dynamics of unsustainable land use, associated with the extensive deforestation and degradation activities. Throughout time, communities with livelihoods based on family-scale agriculture and forest resources were expulsed from the region and gave place to  large scale agricultural and pasture activities.  For the project period, the baseline scenario for the Project Area indicates that the historical patterns of change in land-use would be reproduced: extensive deforestation and systematic conversion from forest to soy crops and pasture areas for cattle ranching, far above the limits stablished by the Brazilian Forest Code. The project activities are designed to avoid the deforestation drivers that would realize the referred baseline in the without project scenario, with the long-term vision of restoring the relation of local communities of rural workers with the forest areas and contribute with the transition to socioeconomic scenario build on bioeconomy principles. With project activity approval, the proponents intend to improve the mechanisms of remote and in loco surveillance, as well as implement activities that will result in other climate, community, and biodiversity benefits.
ccb-3140:
ZhaoQu Afforestation Project (hereafter refer to as “the project”) is located within Zhaotong City and Qujing City, Yunan Province of China. It is an inland province, bordering Guizhou to the eest, Sichuan to the northwest. The province has a total population of 46.9 million. The project aims to plant native species on suitable land for forest  for GHG removal whilst contributing to local sustainable development goals.
36,607 ha (549,105 Mu ) of forest was planted on suitable land for forest in Zhaotong City and Qujing City which used to be poor sustainable ecological environment and karst rocky desertification. Prior to the project, the project area was suitable land for forest, there is no forestry management and the coverage by planting trees is low, and there has never been any activity affecting the local ecosystem . By checking the afforestation plan with the forestry bureau of Zhaotong City and Qujing City, it was confirmed that, a small number of trees have been planted in some project area before the project started, but the coverage by planting trees is low. So considering the low forest coverage, the forestry bureau of Zhaotong City and Qujing City determined that the project area is suitable for afforestation after investigation, then the local forestry bureau approved the supplementary planting without disturbing the existing trees in January 2019 to increase the vegetative cover.
ccb-3141:
The WARG Project is an initiative led by Carbon Credits Consulting SRL and a group of landowners in the state of Acre to protect multiple parcels of precious native forest. The project gives landowners with small and medium sized properties the opportunity to participate in a REDD+ project which will bring biodiversity, community, and climate benefits to their land.
The project areas are in the region known as the Amazon deforestation arc and are located in a region of high conversion rates from original forest habitat to pasture and/or large areas of agricultural crops. 
The Brazilian economy in the south of the Amazonian regions, has been based based on native forest clearing to allow cattle-ranching, often without appropriate management technologies. Considering the infertile soil in the Amazon Forest, its exposure to the weather, and to little improvement in agricultural technology the region is hampered by low productivity, leading to increasing deforestation to ensure profitability. 
The WARG project intends to deliver significant improvements in the area’s monitoring, with remote sensing technology implementation to identify any signs of modification in the Project Area and surroundings, in addition to training staff for field monitoring. The project will also be implementing satellite wildfire detection systems and teams of fire fighters to detect fires early before they reach an unmanageable size.
The project is expected to avoid the emission of 3,620,766 tCO2eq in the first 10 years. The actual project area is 60,000 ha of native forest divided in 22 properties, with an ambitious target for continuous expansion to a total area of 500,000 ha.
Finally, the project has been protecting the Brazilian Big Five which include the giant anteater, the giant armadillo, the maned wolf, the puma, and the jaguar on top of a multitude of other endangered animal and plant species.
ccb-3145: Environmentally and culturally conserve the PANI territory, through the consolidation of its own government, strengthening of traditional knowledge, actions for sustainable development, and monitoring and control of the territory, to improve the quality of life of the communities.
ccb-3155: This is the first Blue Carbon Project of Niger Delta Mangroves. It is a grouped project whose expansion region includes all the mangrove forests present in the Niger Delta in Nigeria. This project is aiming at restoring and sustainably managing the Niger Delta mangroves. Niger Delta mangroves together with the creeks and rivers are a major source of food and livelihood for about 30 million people, which represents more than 17% of Nigeria's population. Other ecosystem services provided by this unique environment are flood control, ground water re-fill, reservoir of biodiversity, fuel wood, cultural values etc. This ecosystem also plays important role in climate change mitigation because of its high blue carbon sequestration potential. Mangroves constitute important nurseries for fishes, crustaceans, sponges, algae and other invertebrates, and also acts as a sink, retaining pollutants from contaminated tidal water. Mangroves are also used as shelter and breeding grounds by small mammals, shore birds, reptiles, and insects. Unfortunately, this unique ecosystem is on the decline and at the verge of been totally lost. Mangrove forests are converted to farmlands and the trees are cut for timber, fuel, house construction and so on. Consequently, many coastal communities in the Niger Delta are losing their lives and primary livelihoods due to increased vulnerability to floods as a result of the disappearance of mangroves which usually serve as defense in times of coastal flooding. They are also now exposed to the high intensity of sunlight and heat waves as the land lay bare of trees to regulate sun rays. There is an urgent need to restore/conserve the mangroves of Niger Delta region. Hence the main objective of the project is sequestration of greenhouse gases (GHGs) through planting activities.
ccb-3166:
The ReforesTerra grouped project aims to recover low-intensity and degraded pasturelands in the Baixo Rio Jamari watershed in the State of Rondônia, Brazil, in the Southern Amazon region. The first project activity instance consists of the reforestation of 2,000 hectares in smallholdings. Available data indicates a potential for reforestation over 20,000 hectares in the watershed.

Through the reforestation of degraded lands in Permanent Protection Areas (PPAs) surrounding water bodies and in Legal Reserves (LRs) in other areas of the engaged landholdings, the grouped project aims to protect water resources and reintroduce native tree species. Additionally, the project is expected to benefit to 600 landholders in the first instance through capacity building and Payment for Ecosystem Services, as well as employing 37 local people full time and 12 other professionals in the region part time, with equal job opportunities for women and men. The first project activity instance will remove 805,304 tCO2e over the 30-year crediting period.
ccb-3179:
The REDD+ project is implemented in the area comprised by 3 natural protected areas, which are the Tumbes National Reserve, Cerros de Amotape National Reserve and El Angolo Hunting Reserve (except the concessioned area: hunting club Coto El Angolo), the same that are located in the regions of Tumbes and Piura.
These regions are located in the noth-eastern part of the Peruvian coast, bounded by the neighbouring country of Ecuador (to the north and east), the Pacific Ocean (to the west) and the Lambayeque region by the south. Both regions have their own specific and variable characteristics throughout and up their territories, since they present part of the Andes Mountain range, high jungle, paramo, equatorial dry forest, tropical valleys, and are an area of permanent interaction between the cold Humboldt Ocean Currents and warm El Niño currents throughout the year.
The project area has an extension of 202,812.54 ha and its aim is to conserve forest in the 3 protected natural areas from the imminent advance of deforestation and degradation.
The project it is proposed to reduce the pressure to change land use in the project area through 3 activities: 1) Support in the implementation of land use plans, 2) Control and surveillance, Forest conservation and restoration, 3) Sustainable intensification of agriculture on existing agricultural land, y 4) Initiatives of aquaculture, tourism and beekeeping activities.
With these actions, the project expects to avoid a total of 5,612,131 tCO2-e according to the baseline scenario projected for the first 10-year period, with an annual average of net emissions of 561,213  tCO2-e. In addition, the project includes benefits for the populations involved as well as for the conservation of biodiversity, where it seeks to contribute to the conservation of forests with high levels of biodiversity with presence of endemic species, species in danger of extinction or with some degree of threat, beyond the benefits of reducing GHG emissions.
ccb-3196: The Paracel ARR Carbon Forestry Project (ID 3196) in northeastern Paraguay combines afforestation, reforestation, and native ecosystem restoration to generate high-quality Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) while promoting biodiversity and social development. The project rehabilitates lands degraded by agriculture and cattle ranching, establishing eucalyptus plantations for kraft pulp alongside the restoration of Cerrado savannas and degraded forests. Paracel manages 195.548 ha, with the first project activity instance (PAI-1) covering 35.764 ha, of which 23.827 ha are eligible. From 2019–2021, 8.382 ha were planted and verified, achieving 192.219 tCO₂e removals after buffer deductions. Over its 50-year crediting period, PAI-1 is expected to remove 7,16 million tCO₂e and issue approximately 2,54 million VCUs. Beyond climate benefits, the project generates more than 1.100 jobs, supports local communities with health, water, and infrastructure initiatives, and actively restores ecosystems, including up to 15.800 ha of savannas and 66.000 ha of degraded forests. By integrating productive forestry with conservation and social investments, Paracel offers a landscape-scale model for sustainable development in Paraguay.
ccb-3210:
The purpose of the REDD+ Bajo Atrato project is to reduce GHG emissions from deforestation and forest degradation activities, envisioning that the efforts of the communities inhabiting and owning the territories where it is located are materialized in actions that lead to forest conservation and the improvement of living conditions. The project is located in the northwest of Colombia, in the Department of Chocó, between the municipalities of Riosucio and Carmen del Darién, in the lower basin of the Atrato River, which is part of the Darién area. In the area of the project’s first instance, the following Afro-descendant communal lands are grouped: the Quiparadó River Basin Community Council, the Curbaradó River Community Council, the Salaquí River Basin Community Council, the Cacarica River Basin Community Council, the Truandó Medio La Teresita Community Council, the Bocas de Taparal Community Council, the Dos Bocas Chintado Community Council, the La Nueva Truandó Community Council, and the Clavellino Community Council.
The actions that will make possible to reduce deforestation and forest degradation in the project area are aligned with the needs and purposes  identified during the first meetings with the communities and while conducting the prior, free and informed consent process. These actions are aimed at achieving four major purposes: strengthening of governance and community management; improvement of community welfare; provision of social and community infrastructure; and boost of sustainable livelihoods and environmental protection, basic sanitation and aqueducts. The lands in the project area include tropical pluvial forests with transition to cold and very humid tropical forests. There, forests, grasslands, secondary vegetation, swampy areas and agroecosystems are found. In these areas, deforestation is associated with wood extraction, agricultural frontier expansion, illicit crop cultivation, and unplanned infrastructure construction.
ccb-3215:
The ASATIQ Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project is located within the area of the Association of Traditional Indigenous Authorities of Querarí (ASATIQ), which is part of the Great Eastern Indigenous Reservation of Vaupés in jurisdiction of the municipality of Mitú, in the department of Vaupés, Colombia. ASATIQ’s territory is located in the Colombian Amazon biome. The objective of the ASATIQ Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions coming mainly from deforestation and degradation of the Amazon Forest.
Potential activities to reduce deforestation include forest protection and monitoring, the intensification and improvement of agricultural productivity in local communities, planting of fruit and timber trees (including those used for firewood), planting of other species used as construction materials, the creation of jobs as an alternative source of income (for example, in forest monitoring) and the improvement of health and education conditions of the communities in order to offer non-extractive work options.
At the same time, actions in the medium and long terms have been defined to support the territory’s self-governance principles, as well as to promote the development of local traditional practices and ancestral education. The proposals made are framed aligned with the general action lines of the ASATIQ Life Plan.
On the other hand, between 40% and 60% of recent IDEAM deforestation early warning bulletins come from the Amazon, and the department of Vaupés appears in the first five ranks of alert. Under these circumstances, the without-project scenario presents an unplanned use of forest resources with extractive logging activities and the expansion of the agricultural frontier through subsistence crops and itinerant mining, which are being developed progressively putting at risk the ecosystem balance of the forests and the cultural traditions of the communities.
The duration of the project is proposed from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2047.
ccb-3216:
The ASATRIZY Vaupés Maloca REDD+ Project proposed to be implemented in the Great Eastern Reservation of Vaupés is in the Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD+) category. Development of the REDD+ project is based on the VM0009 Methodology, v3 of the VCS. This methodology is applicable to this project and is being used for other REDD+ projects in the region. It has also been used by Wildlife Works, having two types of areas of application.  The first, corresponding to the Project Area (PA) and the second to the Project Accounting Area (PAA). The PAA is the area with forest cover, where the project would implement activities to prevent deforestation and whose results would be used to calculate carbon credits.
According to the territory conditions, this is a standalone project that respects ASATRIZY’s autonomy. In the without-project scenario, the forest ecosystems in the department of Vaupés and in particular those in the territory of ASATRIZY are located in life zones of tropical humid forest. This area has been recognized as one of the most biodiverse in the country and the whole continent, being characterized by its endemic species.
The forest monitoring carried out by the Colombian Government and coordinated by IDEAM has shown a national annual deforestation average between 177,764 ha and 219,552 ha for the 2016-2017 period, with the Amazon biome representing 70% of the total deforestation. In addition, between 40% and 60% of recent IDEAM deforestation early warning bulletins come from the Amazon, and the department of Vaupés appears in the first five ranks of alert.
According to this scenario and based on data obtained from the Amazonian Scientific Research Institute (SINCHI) and through field visits carried out by WWC, it was possible to identify the unplanned use of forestry resources as the main driver of deforestation in the project area, consisting of “slash-and-burn” activities in the jungle to expand the chagras.
ccb-3218: The Atrato-Baudó REDD+ Project aims to reduce GHG emissions from deforestation of natural forest. It is expected to achieve this through implementation of community actions framed in conservation, protection and sustainable management of the forest, which lead to improvements in living conditions in the territories. The area of the project’s first instance is located in the Tumbes-Chocó-Magdalena bioregion, in the municipalities of Alto Baudó, Quibdó, Lloró, Bagadó, Tadó, Río Iró (Santa Rita) and Cértegui, in the department of Chocó. The project is designed as a grouped project, initially made up of the collective territories of the following Afro-descendant communities: Community Council of San Isidro, Community Council of Villa Conto and Major Community Council of the Alto Atrato Popular Peasant Organization (COCOMOPOCA).  The project activities are aligned with the community needs and purposes identified during the process of relationship and free and informed prior consent developed with the communities. These actions are aimed at achieving four major purposes, which are: Governance and community management; social and community infrastructure; sustainable livelihoods and environmental protection, basic sanitation and aqueducts. Currently, the forests in the project area include areas of very humid tropical forest with transition to Tropical Rainforest. These ecosystem characteristics potentiate the habitat conditions of both flora and fauna, being cataloged as one of the most biodiverse areas of the country and the continent, characterized by endemism.  Deforestation that occurs in the project area are the result of a combination of complex socioeconomic and historical factors, associated with extractive processes that have directly affected biodiversity and ecosystem services. The project, as an alternative to conversion, aims to maintain carbon stocks through sustainable forest management, promoting improvements in the living conditions of local communities.
ccb-3226:
The Padang Tikar Landscape project is located in the Padang Tikar Landscape of the Batu Ampar subdistrict, Kubu Raya district, West Kalimantan province, Indonesia. The project consists of 10 'Village Forests', covering 76,370 hectares (ha), 58,672.7 ha of which is eligible for the reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD) project. The Village Forest of Padang Tikar is the largest 'Village Forest' permit in Indonesia and is divided
into three types of forest: protected forest (69,299 ha), limited production forest (1,985 ha), and convertible production forest (5,086 ha). The Padang Tikar Landscape project is a microcosm of the country as it has comprehensive forest ecosystems, ranging from inland forests to swamp forests (including mangrove forests and peatlands).
ccb-3241:
Guangdong Huidong Afforestation Project  is located in Huidong County, Huizhou City, Guangdong Province, in the southeast of Guangdong Province and the east of Huizhou City. The project’s aim is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on suitable lands  for forestation, and there has never been any activity affecting the local ecosystem. 
An area of 7,950.86  ha, which belongs to the villagers and the village committees manage the lands on behalf of villagers, have been planted on more than 600 parcels of lands since 2015. All the trees planted in the project zone are native species, including Schima superba, Castanopsis fissa, Elaeocarpus sylvestris, Liquidamba formosana, Camphor tree, Cinnamoummum bumannii, Michelia macclurei, Acacia rachii, Castanopsis hystrix, Casuarina equisetifolia Forst., Pinus elliotti, China fir. No invasive alien species or genetically modified organisms are involved.
The implementation of the project would generate GHG emission removals and improve local environment by planting trees, enhance biodiversity conservation and climate change adaptation, improve soil and water conservation in project zone, strengthening the live skills of local communities and residents by providing their relevant technical skills, training and create more permanent job opportunities for local women and increase income for local communities.
ccb-3280:
The Carpathia Forest Carbon Project aims for the restoration and full protection of forests in the south-eastern Carpathians Mountains in Romania. Through land purchase and conservation agreements, the project seeks to protect primary and secondary forests in five Natura 2000 network sites and regenerate areas affected by clear cuts, spruce monocultures, and degraded riparian habitats along the mountain rivers.
The Carpathia Forest Carbon Project would create GHG emission reductions by avoiding the release of carbon associated with timber harvesting, road building and other forestry operations that would be expected to be carried out in the baseline (business-as-usual) scenario. Thus, the project includes improved forest management (IFM) practices that convert the logged forests to protected forests through conservation management activities with low level of timber removal for ecosystem/habitat enhancement and risk management in the wider Făgăraș Mountains (Natura 2000 designated site), the Piatra Craiului National Park and the Leaota Mountains. 
The broader vision of this project is to establish the foundations of a new National Park that can be recognized as the European Yellowstone Park (in reference to the Yellowstone National Park in the United States), encompassing the Carpathian Mountains; from the Olt Valley in the West to Piatra Craiului Mountain in the East.
The project area involves the lands owned by Fundatia Conservation Carpathia (FCC) as well as those managed by them and owned by their partners Wildland Ltd, Romfor Sustainable Forestry SRL, Almimax Natura, Dante International and Sanatate & Natura. The forest properties to be considered include 36 forest management plans (FMP). The total project area is 23,404 ha, of which 14,541 ha are eligible for the development of the IFM activities.
ccb-3294: The Muskitia Pâsa Klîn Nâka (Muskitia – a source of fresh air) project is a regional community initiative, which seeks certification of actions related to the reduction of carbon emissions due to unplanned deforestation and the conservation of mangrove, broadleaf, and coniferous natural forest in about 5,000, 200,000 and 70,000 ha respectively. The initiative is a grouped project whose expansion region includes all the forests present in Gracias a Dios department (Honduras) that are legally titled to indigenous territorial councils (CTI). The project initially has two instances: the Instance I (West), corresponds to seven Miskitu councils (LAINASTA, KATAINASTA, WATIASTA, Ahuya Yari, TRUKTSINASTA, BAMIASTA, and BATIASTA) characterized for being territories surrounded by other indigenous territories. The Instance II (East) correspond to one Miskitu Council (RAYAKA) and one Pech council (Las Marías), territories bordering communities not inhabited by indigenous.
ccb-3299: The project “Serra do Sudeste” is a grouped project, falling under the Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) category and targeting the following Verra certifications: Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standard (CCB). The Serra do Sudeste Grouped Project aims to restore forest formations that are diminished due to the expansion of other land use practices such as overgrazing on extensive cattle ranches, intensive agriculture and silviculture systems. The grouped project is located in the Pampa biome in Rio Grande do Sul, south of Brazil. Restoration is attained through forestation activities using primarily native species and includes enrichment planting with valuable species as well as assisted natural regeneration. The overarching goal of the project is to create a natural and biodiverse forest that combines carbon capture with a diversity of other economic functions such as apiculture, sustainable production of crops and exploitation of forest products.
ccb-3319:
Tibet Ngari Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as 'the project') is located in Ngari Region, Tibet Autonomous Region, China. The objective of the project is to restore the 'black soil beach' and degraded grassland ecosystem through reseeding native grasses and grazing management, such as rest grazing and grazing prohibition, increase carbon sequestration, and promote local development.
Totally, 373,467.02 ha of degraded grassland in Ngari have been managed sustainably including rest grazing and grazing prohibition by fence building and seeding of local high-quality forage.There are three main restoration measures: rest grazing, grazing prohibition and black soil beach restoration. 
In addition to these main restoration measures, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restores grassland vegetation through grassland management measures to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity, supplemented by daily management measures of other protection projects, such as grassland fire prevention and rodent control, so as to ensure long-term sustainable management of the project area.
ccb-3324: The primary objective of the IPOÁ REDD+ Project is to avoid gross baseline emissions of 2,719,762 tCO2e (averaging 90,659 tCO2e/year), corresponding to 4,200 hectares of avoided deforestation over the 30-year project lifetime (being an average of 140 ha/year). The project operates within private areas totaling 17,386 hectares, 17,329 hectares of which are eligible for REDD+ activities, located in Amazonas State, municipality of Novo Aripuanã. The latter ranks 15th for highest deforestation rates of the municipalities within the Amazon biome according to the Brazilian national deforestation monitoring program (PRODES) as, between 2016 and 2021, it displayed an average deforestation rate of 160km²/year. Long-term, high-impact benefits for communities and biodiversity will be provided by the Ipoá project, which are duly quantified and monitored through the CCB methodological standard. The definition of the actions to be implemented was carried out through a collaborative participatory consultation with community stakeholders. The activities fall into multiple activity scopes including: healthcare, education, occupational health and safety, communication and electrification, employment, and training, within the Community Pillar; fauna and flora research and conservation activities, as well as those addressing high conservation values, in the Biodiversity Pillar; and forest conservation activities articulated under Carbonext’s Forest Integrity Plan in the Climate Pillar. These initiatives will begin as soon as possible to project start in 2022 – 2023, Monitoring Period 1 (“MR1”), and continue along the project lifetime, through MR30 in 2052.
ccb-3334: The Marajó REDD+ Project has been designed for the protection of forests and rich biodiversity in the Amazon. It is part of the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) project category. Specifically, the project is of the “Avoided Unplanned Deforestation & Degradation” (AUDD) project category.
ccb-3336:
Eastern Yan’an Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as ‘The Project’the project”) is located in Yanchang County, Yanchuan County, Yichuan County and Zichang City  in eastern Yan’an City, Shaanxi Province, People’s Republic of China. The project aims to increase carbon sequestration and improve the local ecological environment by means of forest planting activities on degraded lands suffering from severe soil erosion.
The project activities involve the planting of trees and shrubs on 58,423.59 hectares (or 876,354 Mu ) of degraded lands located in Yanchang County, Yanchuan County, Yichuan County and Zichang City under the administration of Yan’an City. The species include Robinia pseudoacacia (black locust), Platycladus orientalis (Oriental thuja or Oriental arborvitae), Pinus tabuliformis (Chinese red pine), Armeniaca sibirica (Siberian apricot) as well as Hippophae rhamnoides (sea-buckthorn). All of them are native species except for Robinia pseudoacacia, which is native to North America; it is not considered as an invasive species in China (refer to Section 5.2 for details). The project area was degraded lands with little vegetation before the project and would continue to be so without the implementation of the project activities. 
The implementation of the project activity will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conditions, increase the forest cover and enhance local biodiversity; the project also generates social benefits including job opportunities and technical skills training for local communities and residents.
ccb-3337:
Central Yan’an Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as 'The Project') is located in Ansai District, Baota District, Fu County, Ganquan County, Huangling County, Luochuan County and Zhidan County in central Yan’an City, Shaanxi Province, People’s Republic of China. The project aims to increase carbon sequestration and improve the local ecological environment by means of forest planting activities on degraded lands suffering from severe soil erosion. 
The project activities involve the planting of trees and shrubs on 67,473.46 hectares (or 1,012,102 Mu ) of degraded lands located in Ansai District, Baota District, Fu County, Ganquan County, Huangling County, Luochuan County and Zhidan County under the administration of Yan’an City. The species include Robinia pseudoacacia (black locust), Platycladus orientalis (Oriental thuja or Oriental arborvitae), Pinus tabuliformis (Chinese red pine), Armeniaca sibirica (Siberian apricot) as well as Hippophae rhamnoides (sea-buckthorn) and Xanthoceras sorbifolium. All of them are native species except for Robinia pseudoacacia, which is native to North America; it is not considered as an invasive species in China (refer to Section 5.2 for details). The project area was degraded lands with little vegetation before the project and would continue to be so without the implementation of the project activities. 
The implementation of the project activity will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conditions, increase the forest cover and enhance local biodiversity; the project also generates social benefits including job opportunities and technical skills training for local communities and residents.
ccb-3338:
Yan’an Wuqi Afforestation Project (hereafter 'The Project') is located in Wuqi County, Yan’an City, Shaanxi Region, China. The project aims to increase the carbon sequestration and to contribute to local sustainable development through planting the trees on the barren land or barren mountain.
45,661.91 ha of forest is to be planted by direct planting on barren land and barren mountain in Wuqi county, there are 4 species selected as designated tree species, they are Robinia pseudoacacia, Armeniaca sibirica, Prunus davidiana and Pinus tabuliformis, the planted trees are all native species. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and improve the Wuqi county’s local environment, about 3,791,500.00 ha enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing them with relevant technical skills and training and increase local biodiversity as a result of establishing a forest of native trees.
ccb-3339:
Yan’an Aerial Seeding Afforestation Project (hereafter 'The Project') is located in Yan’an City, Shaanxi Region, China. The project aims to increase the carbon sequestration and to contribute to local sustainable development through directly aerial seeding on the barren land and barren mountain. 
Aerial seeding is a method of afforestation in which forest seeds or seed pellets are scattered on the woodlands (i.e., sown areas) by aircraft. Planting afforestation by airplane is a modern afforestation method, which has the advantages of high speed, high efficiency, saving labor and great effect. In the sparsely populated, inconvenient transportation, labor shortage of large areas of barren mountains, sand and cutting, afforestation by aerial seeding is an effective way to speed up afforestation.
31,049.40 ha of forest is to be established by direct aerial seeding on barren land and barren mountain in Yan’an city, there are 2 species selected as designated sowing seed species, Platycladus orientalis (Giant cedar) and Pinus tabuliformis (China pine), which are all native species. The implementation of the project will generate GHG emission removals and improve the Yan’an local environment, about 3,703,054.05 ha enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing them with relevant technical skills and training and increase local biodiversity as a result of establishing a forest of native trees.
ccb-3341: The Samkos REDD+ Project (SRP) is an initiative designed to promote climate change mitigation and adaptation, maintain biodiversity and create alternative livelihoods under the United Nations scheme of Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation (REDD+). Phnom Samkos Wildlife Sanctuary and Southern Cardamom National Park are significant protected areas in Cambodia because they maintain an intact and sizeable area of primary evergreen forest in the region. Their landscapes are also home to over 59 IUCN Red Listed globally threatened species such as, the Asian elephant, Malayan sun bear, Asiatic black bear, Siamese crocodile, Irrawaddy dolphin, fishing cat, and the pangolin.
ccb-3343:
The XiCO2e: Mexican Peninsula Forest Project aims to increase carbon removal through Improved Forest Management activities in communal-land properties (ejidos) located in the Yucatán Peninsula in the southeastern state of Quintana Roo, Mexico. The project is developed under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) methodology VM0003 v1.3 - Methodology for Improved Forest Management Through Extension of Rotation Age (IFM ERA).
The Project Area covers 70,246 hectares and is comprised of semi-evergreen tropical forest with broad species diversity, having as its primary target commercial species such as mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla), Spanish cedar (Cedrela odorata), Sapotilla (Manilkara zapota), Fiddlewood (Vitex gaumeri), Tsalam (Lysiloma bahamensis), Ramon (Brosimum alicastrum), Katalox (Swartzia cubensis), Shaving bush tree (Pseudobombax ellipticum), Copperwood (Bursera simaruba), and Chechen (Metopium brownei), among several other tropical commercial species.
The common practice of harvesting in the ejidos consists of selection cuts of tropical species in management units during the established rotation period. The project will extend the rotation cycle by +5, +4, and +2 years. Additionally, the project aims to implement a monitoring procedure to systematize and centralize information related to forest practices. The project is expected to remove 4,599,024 tonnes of CO2e over 30 years, with an annual average of 170,334 tonnes of CO2e.
ccb-3344:
The Last Habitat REDD+ project is located in the Ucayali region, in the central zone of the Peruvian Amazon, one of the regions with the highest rates of deforestation in Peru (31,543.29 ha in 2021). The project area is comprised by two private estates belonging to the project proponent, BAM: the properties of Nuestro Señor Jesucristo with 8,049.87 ha and Selva Maestra with 14,176.13 ha, a total area of 22,226 ha mainly of primary floodable forests.

Located near the city of Pucallpa (Ucayali) and surrounded by deforestation pressures from agriculture, urbanization and others, the project area harbors an extraordinary ecological wealth, being the last habitat or refuge for various species of flora and fauna and a green island of outstanding ecological value. In addition, the are includes several types of valuable forest, among them the aguajales, which are the wetlands with the greatest carbon sequestration capacity in the Amazon, making this an essential ecosystem to conserve.

The Last Habitat REDD+ project is designed under the avoided planned deforestation methodology as this area was originally sold to the project proponent with the authorization to  convert the forested areas in agrarian production lands (camu camu, palm oil, piñon, and cattle ranching). Despite having the legal authorization to carry out traditional productive activities, BAM, with its own resources, has promoted the conservation of these valuable forests and its biodiversity over the years by implementing different strategies and activities such: territorial supervision with technical and legal support, forest surveillance activities, permanent work with communities for improving their capacities in sustainable forestry management, among others. Such conservation efforts will only be feasible and sustainable over time with the support of carbon revenues from the proposed REDD+ project.
ccb-3395:
Carbon Sink Afforestation Project (hereafter refer to as “the project”) in Tongyu County, Jilin Province is located in Tongyu County, Baicheng City, Jilin Province, and is organized and constructed by the Forestry and Grass Bureau of Tongyu County. Tongyu County is located in the western part of Jilin Province, adjacent to Inner Mongolia to the west and Heilongjiang to the north, and is located in the Songnen Plain in the east of the Greater Khingan Mountains.
The project aims to establish forests on barren land to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and contribute to local sustainable development.A total of 3,266.04 ha (48,990.6 Mu[ A Chinese metric unit of area, 1ha equals to 15 Mu.]) of forests were planted in 27 townships (towns and farms) in Tongyu County.
The project aims to bring into play the benefits of afforestation and sink, and at the same time, bring into play the multiple benefits of forests in terms of protecting biodiversity, improving local living environment and natural landscape, and increasing community income. Based on the crediting period of 20 years, a total of 1,175,818 tCO2e is expected to be generated by 2035, with an average annual emission reduction of 58,791 tCO2e.
ccb-3396:
The PlanTogo project aims to establish 120.230 hectares of forest plantations in Maritime , Plateaux and Centrale Regions of Togo, over a period of 10 years (2021 2030). The main forest species to be planted are eucalyptus , khaya and gmelina , the project also considers the planting of other species such as bamboo and cashew .
T he purpose of these plantations is to restore degraded lands in the short term and the sustainable production of goods an services in the medium and long term, while contributing to local development and fight against climate change by sequestering CO2.
The project developer is Sequoia Plantations Togo ( who will implement the plantations under two modalities: i) on their own lands and ii) on communal or smallholders lands to who S PT will provide seedlings and technical assistance. Sequoia Plantations Togo is responsible of project monitoring through the entire crediting period.
SPT is a Grouped Project, and project areas are selected considering the land eligibility requirements of the VCS, that is, on lands where there have been no native ecosystems in the last 10 years and without forest at the beginning of the plantation activities. The areas identified for the first instance are constituted by grasslands and shrublands, and current land use is extensive agriculture or cattle grassing. SPT will allow intercropping in the first years of the plantations.
The reforestation activities proposed by Sequoia Plantations Togo will generate a switch in land covert from non-forest to forest and it will lead to the creation of a carbon stock in biomass and in the soil greater than that existing under current conditions. The Net GHG emission removals expected in 20 years is 1 45 690 569 tCO2e (7 284 528 tCO2e/yr)
ccb-3397: The Kruger to Canyons Rangeland Restoration Project is a grouped project located in the globally significant Kruger to Canyons Biosphere Reserve. The area has lost soil carbon due to unrestricted animal movements and high grazing intensities leading to low productivity and bare ground, while this is exacerbated by unfavorable herd structures. Unrestricted grazing is occurring due to a ‘tragedy of the commons’ where communal areas are over-utilized for livestock grazing and knowledge of sustainable grazing practices have lapsed. The project aims to reverse historic rangeland degradation on communal rangelands by introducing rotational grazing through herding and improved animal husbandry, and removing and reducing Greenhouse Gases in the process. Furthermore, project participants will benefit from improved access to livestock markets.
ccb-3433:
Guiyang Afforestation Project (hereafter refer to as “the project”) is located at Guiyang City.
10,158.2 ha (152,373 Mu ) of forest was planted on suitable land for afforestation in Guiyang City where used to be poorly sustainable in terms of ecological environment and suffer from karst rocky desertification. Prior to the project, the project area was suitable land for forest, there is no forestry management and the coverage by planting trees is low, and there has never been any activity affecting the local ecosystem . By checking the afforestation plan with the Guiyang Forestry Bureau, it was confirmed that a small number of trees have been planted in the project area before the afforestation project. However, the forest coverage rate is relatively low. Therefore, considering this situation, the Guiyang Forestry Bureau determined that the project area is suitable for afforestation after investigation, then the Forestry Bureau approved the supplementary planting without disturbing the existing trees to increase the vegetative cover. The forest farm and Guiyang Forestry Industry Development Co., Ltd implement the afforestation project, and Guiyang Forestry Industry Development Co., Ltd is authorized to apply for carbon sink projects on behalf of the forest farm, and to implement management activities such as monitoring.
The project is to plant without disturbing the existing trees, and only the trees actually planted in the project were monitored. The carbon credit of the original trees in the baseline scenario will not be monitored or counted in the actual net GHG removals by sinks.
ccb-3450:
Located in the department of Meta, Cabuyaro is a municipality whose surface equals to 832 kilometers square, with a population of 5,432 inhabitants, and an altitude of 151 meters above the sea level (DANE, Censo Nacional de Poblacion y Vivienda, 2018). The project is located in Guayabal, a small town in Cabuyaro composed of 204 inhabitants who mainly work the land, growing a variety of crops such as plantain, cassava, papaya, passion fruit, corn, soy, and cacao which are mainly sold in the local market of Villavicencio.
This is a grouped project, the first area to be verified, consists of a total of 2,258 hectares composed of degraded pastures in majority and conservation areas, at the baseline. Of which 1,764 hectares will be established in an agroforestry system, with cacao being the perennial crop planted with other trees for shading purposes (Gliricidia sepium) and boundary purposes (windbreakers -Cariniana pyriformis). This agroforestry system has the goal of increase the soil organic carbon, as well as the aboveground and below ground biomass, and will recover the soil health and fertility through time. Other relevant agricultural practices that will be implemented are proper residue management as crop/tree materials that are periodically pruned are left in the soil for decomposition to build organic matter, processing of the cacao husks to produce organic fertilizer to be applied back in the field, as well as planting cover crops in bare soil areas, irrigation,  and planting boundary trees to prevent erosion and reduce wind damage to the cacao.
The rest of the project area, 491 hectares, corresponds to other uses such as drainage channels, internal roads, and conservation areas which included native forest species, called morichales, riparian zones, and secondary forests. The total project area is divided into two properties, Espejuelos (1,258 hectares) and Primavera (1,000 hectares).
ccb-3452: Sichuan Huili Improved Forest Management Project (hereafter “the project”) is implemented in Huili County, Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province of China by Beijing Hanlinhui Environmental Protection Technology Co. LTD, the geo-coordinate of the project is 101°50'E-102°38'E and 26°2'N～27°12'N. The project includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest and avoids emissions, which will achieve sustainable carbon sequestration at the same time.
ccb-3456: The Fujian Datian Improved Forest Management Project (hereafter “the project”) is implemented in Datian County, Sanming City, Fujian Province of China by Beijing Hanlinhui Environmental Protection Technology Co. LTD. The geographic coordinate of project is 116°38’ ~117°11’ E and 25°47’ ~26°21’ N, the total area is 229400 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
ccb-3479: The Amigos de Calakmul Community Forest Conservation Program (ACAC Program) is focused on protecting the forests and preventing land use change in the Calakmul Biosphere Reserve in Mexico. The program works with local communities called ejidos that reside in the reserve's buffer zone and area of influence. Instead of timber harvesting, participating ejidos receive conservation payments and social program support. Phase 1 of the program covers 10 ejidos and 95,077 hectares. The ejido members in the program area have limited livelihood options, and timber harvesting can be a significant economic activity, both legal and illegal. The Yucatan Peninsula has experienced significant forest and timber harvesting in the area leading to forest degradation, human access, and biodiversity loss. The program also focuses on diversifying income sources and improving livelihoods through productive projects, emphasizing community participation and input gathering. It was developed under the methodology VM0010 under VCS and will also be validated under the CCB.
ccb-3542:
Gansu Xiaolongshan Afforestation Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in the suburbs of Hui County, Liangdang County, Li County of Longnan City, suburbs of Qinzhou District, Maiji District, Qingshui County, Wushan County of Tianshui City, suburbs of Min County, Zhang County of Dingxi City, Gansu Province of China, whose aim is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren or degraded lands. The project is implemented by Gansu Xiaolongshan Forestry Conservation Center. 
3,738.23 ha (56073.4 Mu) of forest is to be planted by direct planting on barren lands in Tianshui City, Longnan City and Dingxi City, including seven suburbs and two counties: Qinzhou District, Maiji District, Qingshui County, Wushan County, Hui County, Liangdang County, Li County, Min County and Zhang County. All the project sites were previously barren lands. There is no natural renewal and afforestation before the project.
The implementation of the project would generate GHG emission removals and improve local environment through growing of the trees, increase income of local residents by offering job opportunities from the project, enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing their relevant technical skills and training, and increase local biodiversity as a result of establishing a forest of native trees (Styphnolobium japonicum, Robinia pseudoacacia, Pinus, Picea)
The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 2,721,683 tCO2e in 60 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 45,361 tCO2e.
ccb-3549: “Community Forest Plantation in India” is a combined Afforestation and sustainable development project carried out by farmers with the help of a project implementer. The associated project implementer is helping farmers to plant trees on the land which is identified as unproductive, and the area is highly water scarce. Farmers retain ownership of the trees, products, and land as well. Farmers received training from the project implementer for plantation and the project implementer (Greenovation) is providing plantation material (saplings, manure) to the farmers and further assistance in maintaining the required survival rate of the plantation. Carbon credits generated from this project will help in maintaining the survival rate of planted trees and support farmers. The total area expected to be covered in the project is around 10,000 hectares. The current plantations have been covered to plant 4,400 hectares in the country.The project participants are using the afforestation approach and planted thousands of trees on the land across the project boundary. In case of the absence of this project activity land would be continued to be less productive land or degraded land. The project will help in mitigating climate change for the next 40 years by sequestrating/removing the carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and creating a carbon pool. The project activity will result in an annual average of 1,40,882 tons of GHG removal and total removal of 56,35,266 tons of CO2 over the 40 years of the period.
ccb-3552:
“Community Forest Initiative in India” is an sustainable afforestation development project carried out by the local farmers with the help of a local NGO. The farmers plant trees on the abandoned wasteland allotted to the communities and retain ownership of the trees, produce, from forestation. Project activity has been planned for helping farmers in developing forest for which they have received plantation material, Irrigation technology and other training received from NGO to establish and maintain the planted forest. NGO empowers the large group of poor communities in West Bengal and Odisha states of India to create & manage the forest on degraded abandoned land to increase forest cover by planting fruit-bearing species. Apart from above, the NGOs helps in managing and sustainably harvesting the NTFPs (Non-Timber Forest Products) for participating farmers. 
The carbon credits from this project activity will also create a new ‘virtual’ cash crop for the participants, who gain all the direct benefits of growing trees and receive benefits based on the GHG benefits created by their efforts (as a result-based payment approach). The maturing trees and conservation activity will provide additional sustainable benefits such as income in form of the carbon payments, climate change mitigation self-resilience and sustainable. . The project will help in mitigating climate change for the next 40 years by sequestrating the carbon from the atmosphere and creating a natural biomass carbon pool. NGO has estimated that this project will result in an annual average of GHG removal of 1,45,278 tonnes/annual and total removals of 58,11,102 tonnes of CO2 for 40 years of project duration.
ccb-3590:
The Jutaituba REDD+ Project is a partnership between the Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Martins Agropecuária, belonging to the Martins Group and aims to promote forest conservation and mitigate climate change by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from changes in land use. In addition to climate benefits, the Project also aims to generate socio-environmental benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and the improvement of the well-being of surrounding communities, while preserving the culture and tradition of local peoples.
The Project Area has 129,417 ha of Amazon rainforest and is located almost entirely in the mesoregion of Marajó, in the State of Pará, covering the cities of Bagre, Portel, Baião and Oeiras do Pará. It is located near BR 422, known as the Transcametá highway, and near the rivers Pacajá, Jacundá and Tocantins. Communities that are directly or indirectly influenced by the Project were identified, either because they provide labor to Fazenda Jutaituba or are geographically close to the Project Area and depend on the forest resources present in the area, such as nuts and medicinal herbs.
The region has great relevance in relation to its biodiversity, being an ecological corridor that makes it possible to connect Conservation Units (UCs) that are nearby. The predominant vegetation is the Dense Ombrophilous Forest with a high density of medium and large trees, as well as woody and epiphytic lianas. It houses at least 24 species of fauna and flora with some degree of threat according to the IUCN Red List, some of which are endemic to the region.
Thus, the Jutaituba REDD+ Project hopes, in addition to climate impacts, to improve the well-being of communities and generate exceptional benefits for local biodiversity.
ccb-3591: The Mayas Project aims to protect and restore a 33,747 hectare area of peat swamp forest in Ketapang District, West Kalimantan Province, Republic of Indonesia. At the time of the project’s intervention the area was in the process of being drained, selectively logged and partially converted to industrial tree plantation in line with a government approved management plan. This would have resulted in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions averaging over 2m tCO2e per year, irreversible loss of globally important biodiversity and a negative impact on the livelihoods and wellbeing of people living around the project area. MPK will fully protect the remaining peat forest areas (now named The Mayas Project) and restore those areas already affected by fire, land clearance and drainage. In parallel the Mayas Project will work in close collaboration with the communities surrounding the area to ensure benefits derived from the project area (no permanent settlements exist within the project area) are used to improve rural livelihoods and wellbeing and to develop greater resilience to climate change. The project will also fully protect the globally important biodiversity of the project area, including a population of Critically Endangered Bornean Orangutan estimated to be between 813 and 1,204 (around 2% of the global population) and significant populations of at least eight other critically endangered or endangered species. At this stage the project is not validated and is not trading carbon. The project remains committed to aligning operations with the Government of Indonesia’s developing legislation on carbon projects.
ccb-3594:
Col La Paz is implementing an Afforestation/Reforestation Project in degraded grasslands in Colombia. The Vichada Department is home to vast tropical grasslands, which have been subject to unsustainable grazing causing ecosystem degradation. La Paz Farm is an extensive forestry plantation with multiple introduced species, mainly planted with Acacia mangium which is undergoing the process of soil regeneration. This productive ecosystem will produce several timber products for construction materials and charcoal to sustainably meet the needs of a growing population. 
La Paz applies practices such as low agrochemical use and regenerative agriculture. It employs a total of 37 workers who benefit from long-term contracts, free meals three times a day, and comfortable accommodation.
The project serves as a biodiversity corridor for many species. Conservation efforts include wildlife protection, spring preservation, and stream conservation. The initiative brings climate benefits by preventing erosion and enhancing carbon sequestration. Col La Paz follows social and environmental policies, aiming for verified emission removals under the Verified Carbon Standard and the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity Standard. 
The estimated annual emissions and removals are 15,705 tCO2e, and the total anticipated emissions and removals are 698,014 tCO2e over 40 years, accounting for future planned harvesting events
ccb-3601: The CAAPII REDD+ PROJECT aims to protect the Amazon Forest present in properties inserted in the municipalities of Paragominas, Ipixuna do Pará and Tomé- Açu in the Pará State, in Brazil. This region has historically high rates of deforestation, especially associated with conflicts of land tenure, and the high value of activities of other land-use such as livestock and soybean production. The illegal exploraration of timber and other illegal activities such as hunting affect the forest, the biodiversity , the climate and consequently the local population as well. The conservation of 33,766.64 hectare of Ombrophilous Dense Forest  with the CAAPII REDD+ Project will reduce more than 14 millions tCO2e of GHG emissions and bring positive impacts to the region with the project activities. The actions have as goals the preservation of the forest, as well as the improvement of the well-being of the communities, biodiversity and climate regulation. A socioeconomic diagnosis on each community involved in the project conducted the design of the project activities in order to encourage the growth of environmental awareness and the sustainable development, aligned with the conservation of the forest and fauna and flora species. With  the approval of the CAAPII REDD+ Project, the forest areas inside the properties can be protected and the project activities can be implemented aiming to bring climate, community, and biodiversity benefits.
ccb-3602:
Udzungwa Corridor Limited will reforest 7500 ha of bracken fern thicket on the Eastern Slopes of the Udzungwa Mountains in Tanzania by planting over 100 native tree species.

The project area is largely fallow farmland on steep slopes with no road access. Natural regeneration in the project area is prevented by a dense thicket of bracken fern, occasional cultivation, and hot fires when the bracken burns. The project is signing 30-year leases with the small holder farmers and village councils that own the project lands. The project covers all the costs associated with tree nursery establishment and tree planting and employs hundreds of local community members in the process. To ensure that the planted trees survive, the project is weeding around the planted seedlings 3 times a year for 3 years, clearing fire breaks around the planted areas, and employing firefighting teams.

The project is a 30-year project and will remove approximately 5,322,834 tCO2e over the project lifetime.

The project will greatly improve the local economy in the participating villages through reliable payments for leased land, creating hundreds of well-paying jobs, the provision of avocado seedlings and improved bean seed outside the planting area and funding village development projects. With 30 years of funding already secured by the project, the economic opportunities created by the project will be much more reliable than farming and thus help communities adapt to uncertain climate conditions. 

The project is located in the Eastern Arc Biodiversity hotspot and will create a forest corridor that will reconnect the Udzungwa Scarp and Kilombero Nature Reserves. The corridor will increase habitat connectivity for the endangered Sanje Mangabey, vulnerable Udzungwa Red Colobus Monkey, and several other endangered and vulnerable species. Additionally, the project is planting vulnerable tree species, thereby directly increasing the population of vulnerable species in the area.
ccb-3630:
Located in the extreme east of the province of Misiones, in San Pedro, the field of native forest where the project is located has 22,878.5 hectares and immersed in the Green Corridor. In this area, controlled logging has been carried out since the 1960s and will decrease as the NIDEPORT project progresses, with harvesting expected to be completed by the end of 2021. The project activity is improved forest management with areas that will be enriched and regenerated by planting more than 250,000 native species individuals annually and others managed to increase forest productivity (bambuacea´s control, and others). 
Although there is not any community, individual or group of people living in the project area, GS1 has been subjected to situations of intrusions and illegal occupations, with burning for planting or deforestation for rudimentary construction, there are numerous cases where the land has been colonized or exploited for agriculture or livestock, where the land is left with high levels of degradation and contamination. 
The project zone, encompassed in an area with population under poverty line, expects to work together with the community identifying risks, HCV areas and needs, in order to implement mitigation actions together. In this line, first meetings with communities have already helped to identify both biodiversity and community´s HCVs, and possible projects regarding housing improvement, health care, among other needs to be identified during the project lifetime.
The climate benefits of the project are defined as the reductions or removals of GHG emissions resulting from forest regeneration, these are expected to reach 3,106,582 tCO2e during the crediting period, averaging 103,553 tCO2e per year.
ccb-3660:
The objective of this project is to reforest degraded mangroves sites in Kwale, Kilifi, and Tana River counties, in Kenya. The project will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem in degraded lands, starting by planting 220 ha in Shirazi, Bodo, Munje, and Funzi Island, in Kwale county.
The main components of the project are to provide a variety of ecosystem services, climate change mitigation, economic considerations, and active participation of the local community. Without the project, carbon stocks in the project area will continue to decline, as the mangrove ecosystems in Kenya suffer a strong degradation process resulting from anthropogenic (e.g., deforestation for wood consumption) and natural causes (e.g., sea tides).
Under this grouped project, degraded mangroves on the Kenyan coast are restored and replanted. In the first project activity up to 196.000 mangroves will be planted. The species selected for this reforestation project are indigenous and local, namely Rhizophora mucronata, Ceriops tagal and Avicennia marina.
The project will monitor soil conditions to measure changes in soil carbon content and maintain soil nutrient levels to improve water quality compared to the baseline scenario. Mangrove restoration will further increase fish populations, improve biodiversity, and provide other important ecosystem services. To measure the positive impact on biodiversity, annual biomonitoring will be conducted using eDNA.
The empowerment of the population is also central to the project. The labour requirement for the project will be fulfilled with local employment. Therefore, most of the budget for labour and an additional 50/50 share of carbon credit revenues will remain in the country. The project will promote a working family model where more than 50% of women can actively participate in the project. People are shown alternative livelihood opportunities that allow them to acquire and grow high-value crops, and invest in beekeeping or ecotourism.
ccb-3664: Huinan County Afforestation Project is located in Huinan county, Tonghua city, Jilin province of China. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren or degraded lands. Prior to the start of the project, the land in the project area was barren, no forest or wetland except some scattered shrub and grass. Under the project, an area of 13,784ha of barren land in Huinan county was planted with trees of native species, mainly including Korean pine, spruce, larch, Fraxinus mandshurica, Juglans mandshurica, etc. The implementation of the project will generate greenhouse gases (GHG) emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conservation and forest cover, enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forests, increase competence and capability of local residents by providing them with relevant technical skills and training, and create more permanent job opportunities for local residents especially women and increase income for local communities.  The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 19,001,754 tCO2e in 60 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 316,696 tCO2e.
ccb-3671:
Project Chaco Vivo will be developed under the Verified Carbon Standard and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standards (VCS – CCBS) as an avoided planned deforestation (APD) REDD+ project. Chaco Vivo will help conserve an area of over 1,800 km2, encompassing over 187,000 hectares (464,000 acres) in Paraguay's Gran Chaco ecosystem. Despite the Gran Chaco’s regional and global significance, the region is one of the most deforested on earth, losing over 1,000 hectares (2,471 acres) of tree cover per day. Project Chaco Vivo will mitigate deforestation pressures in the region and protect this important yet critically threatened ecosystem, which provides habitats to more than 3,400 plant species, 500 bird species, 150 mammals, 120 reptiles, and approximately 100 species of amphibians - including numerous endemic and IUCN red list vulnerable, threatened, and endangered species. 

Chaco Vivo is a People Project at heart with numerous communities living within the Project's Area of Influence (AOI), including Indigenous communities of the Maskoi - an ethnolinguistic group of people of Lengua-Maskoi. The Project Area encompassed by Chaco Vivo is a High Conservation Value Area (HCVA) since it consists of natural habitats of outstanding significance and/or of critical importance due to the special biological, ecological, social, and cultural values. 

Key to Chaco Vivo is a robust social program called the L.I.F.E. Program™ (Land-use Initiatives & Forest Enterprises Program). The L.I.F.E. Program™ will provide a tangible system of socio-economic enrichment programs to improve the livelihoods of marginalized populations. The key objectives of the L.I.F.E. Program™ are to directly impact the U.N. SDGs, but also to foster community engagement, project integration, collaboration, and self-sustaining sustainable enterprise creation for generational impact, or G-Impacts™.
ccb-3700:
The Sichuan Muli REDD+ Project (hereafter referred as “the project”) is located in Muli Tibetan Autonomous County, Sichuan Province, China. The project zone (Including Liangshan State Liangbeiguo Forest Protection Bureau, Liangshan State Leibo key state-owned forest protection Bureau and Liangshan State Yalong River state-owned forest protection Bureau in the Muli area) has a total area of 181,681 ha. The area is characterized for its high biodiversity and subtropical humid mountain forests, but also for the presence of deforestation activities and social conflicts. Deforestation drivers include mining activities, subsistence agriculture andTo achieve the above mentioned objectives, project activities to be developed and implemented include: (i) Development of legal economic alternatives and associated business plans that promote biodiversity protection, (ii) Management and improvement of production systems that str biodiversity conservation, iii) Strengthening land use planning and mechanisms to guarantee food security for the communities, (iii) to contribute to the monitoring and conservation of the biodiversity present in the area of the Muli Tibetan Autonomous County.

Moreover, expected GHG reductions corresponds to an annual average of 234,910 tCO2, so for the lifetime of 20 years it could demonstrate reductions up to 4,698,207 tCO2.
 animal husbandry, and forest fire. Social issues include lack of sanitation, education and health infrastructure and lack of technical guidance regarding sustainable production models.
ccb-3708: The proposed project introduces a reduced tillage technology which integrates tillage, sowing, crop residue retention and fertilizer application simultaneously in Hebei Province, P.R.China. Application of this technology would therefore achieve multiple sustainability goals like improved soil organic carbon stocks, lower GHG flux, reduced irrigation and fertilizer utilization, increased crop yield and enhance the food security of Hebei Province.
ccb-3726:
The growing threats to the forests of the Peruvian Amazon, such as migratory agriculture, land trafficking illegal logging and illegal gold mining, are causing the alarming degradation of forests; the loss and in some cases the disappearance of the most important flora and fauna in the territory; and the general pollution - deterioration of the country’s most valuable ecosystems. Specifically, illegal (gold) mining have caused tragic damage to part of the Peruvian Amazon. Rivers, streams and soils have been contaminated due to this cause to such degree that it will take many years to remediate and recover -to some extent- their initial state. One of the most affected areas in Peru in terms of deforestation, and specifically due to illegal mining, is the buffer zone of the Tambopata National Reserve and the forests located on the right bank (towards Cusco) of the Interoceanic highway in the region of Madre de Dios.

REDD+ Amazon Guardians purpose is to reduce and avoid deforestation within the conservation, reforestation/afforestation, and ecotourism forest concessions located in the buffer zone of the Tambopata National Reserve and adjacent areas which are highly threatened by illegal mining and traffickers who use these areas for illegal crops. REDD+ Amazon Guardians has been designed and developed with the purpose of protecting these valuable forests and their biodiversity, generating environmental services that allow the capture of CO2 and providing opportunities to improve the quality of life for the communities that live and depend on these areas. 

The project is implemented by Bosques Amazonicos SAC (BAM) in partnership with the concessionaire families in the area, grouped in the Federation of Concessionaires of Madre de Dios, FECOMAD.
ccb-3727: The Corridors for Life ARR Grouped Project aims at mitigating climate change through planting of native trees that will remove carbon from the atmosphere, environmental and biodiversity conservation through the formation of ecological corridors that promote connectivity between the remaining forest fragments and protect the soil, and the generation of employment and income through training and acquisition of products and services from local companies of the reforestation chain. With this, the project has the potential over its 50 years lifetime to reforestate 75,000 hectares and remove 29,213,780 tons of CO2e, generate at least 600 jobs, benefit at least 180 women and contribute to the conservation of 8 endangered species according to the IUCN Red List.
ccb-3734: Bosques Cautin is a forest developer operating in Chile, that has traditionally operate a silvicultural model for commercial timber, and now, is expanding its business model to dedicate different areas of forest plantations to carbon sinks. For doing this, is applying an IFM methodology in order to enlarge the rotation age and to create permanent sinks. The project encompasses 15,000 acres of commercial plantations, based on species like eucalyptus globulus, eucalyptus nitens, radiata pine and others.
ccb-3738:
The Triunfo do Xingu Grouped REDD+ Project (hereinafter also referred to as “TdX”) is composed by seven rural properties located in the Municipality of Altamira, in the south region of the State of Pará. According to the geo-referencing data, the total area of the project is established at 10,636.02 ha. This project aims to be registered under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) to avoid unplanned deforestation (AUD), combating the decreased carbon stock in the Brazilian Legal Amazon. 
The crediting period of the project is 30 years. The start date is on August 31, 2022 and, therefore, the crediting period is expected to end on August 30, 2052. The baseline scenario developed is going to be used for the first six years of the project, since, according to VCS requirements, these six years are the maximum period until a baseline scenario reassessment needs to be done. The present analysis, that will be employed in the project validation and future project verifications, is going to be done in a conservative approach, keeping the project consistent.
The TdX aims for the following objectives: environmental benefits through a successful monitoring system; economic benefits resulting in regional development through investments in local communities. To execute the installation of this project and to achieve its objectives the VCU generation is very important. A baseline reduction of 1,565,285.35 tCO2e of GHG is expected over six years, associated with the avoided deforestation of 6,167.07 ha.
ccb-3739:
The Selva de Urundel REDD+ Project, seeks to enforce the protection of the native forest and the biodiversity of the Urundel forest located in the Province of Salta, Department of Oran, in northern Argentina. 
The Project started in January 2021 and is expected to reduce emissions by 3,513,643.40 tCO2eq in the first 10 years through 9,647 hectares of avoided deforestation, at an average of 351,364.34 tCO2eq per year. 
The project is expected to generate emission reductions through the reduction of deforestation and forest cover loss by implementing several activities that include the prevention and control of fires, the control of illegal activities occurring in the property (hunting, logging, grazing), the training and capacity building, as well as the cooperation with different institutions to promote alternative activities in the property including among others ecotourism and scientific research. 
This project is particularly relevant as it aims to preserve a territory which is part of the Yungas Biosphere Reserve, included in UNESCO’s Man and Biosphere Program (MAB) thanks to the arrangement of the Yungas mountain ranges which present a discontinuous and insular distribution that creates conditions for the coexistence of great biological diversity.
ccb-3773: MinFor is a long-term rural sustainable development project primarily concerned with managing forests and forming partnerships with Indigenous Peoples. It reaches a sizable number of recipient households and municipalities in the Philippines' Mindanao Region. The project involved forest protection and conservation in close partnership with the rightful indigenous land owners. Ancestral domains are territories that are declared as territories of tribal groups, and these domains are indiscriminate of political boundaries. These domains are delineated by identifying territorial boundaries acknowledged by tribes members since time immemorial. MinFor aims to achieve sustainable development, social empowerment, conservation and restoration in an equitable partnership with communities.
ccb-3811:
This is a VCS-large scale project class implemented to protect the Chirisa Safari Area in the Midlands province of Zimbabwe. The project area of 144,796 hectares is owned by the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority (ZPWMA) and is leased to Carbon Green Africa (CGA) and Carbon Green Investments (CGI) for the purposes of establishing and running a REDD+ project. The partnership of CGA and CGI, hereinafter Carbon Green, is the project proponent. The main objective of the agreement is to establish a REDD+ project, with the aims of:
●	REDD+ carbon credit generation
●	Contribution to sustainable conservation in Zimbabwe
●	Development of a strategy for invasive species management
●	Fire and roads management
●	Game, water and habitat management
●	Strengthening antipoaching law enforcement
●	Wildlife population management
●	Promoting wildlife tourism and related activities
●	Community livelihoods enhancement 
The project proponent works in partnership with ZPWMA and adjacent communities in 12 wards across the surrounding 3 districts of Gokwe North, Gokwe South and Binga in a REDD+ scheme. Together the protected Safari Area and surrounding communal land make a project zone of 490,710 Ha. The project zone forms part of the last remaining corridor for animal movement and migration. 
The project aims to generate GHG emission reductions through 4 main strategic approaches:
1.	Direct forest and wildlife conservation to stop clearing and cutting of wood and wildlife poaching by implementing standard monitoring activities such as patrols
a.	Training to support law enforcement.
b.	Regular forest monitoring and carbon accounting will be done through aerial (remote sensing) and ground methods.
c.	Biodiversity assessments will be done via aerial methods supported by ground transects-based observations and citizen science. 
2.	Engagement and capacity building with key community and government stakeholders to willfully participate in one climate change mitigation goal
3.	Distribution of performance-based benefits to project zone communities delivered through local institutions 
4.	Implementation of sustainable alternative livelihood activities identified through a robust gender and inter-generationally sensitive participatory rural appraisal process
