a.	Livelihood activities will include both subsistence and entrepreneurial initiatives in the fields such as agriculture, small scale, high-intensive controlled environment growing systems (greenhouses) 
b.	Vocational training on manufacturing of products for export
The baseline (without-project) scenario is unplanned deforestation due to the continual clearing of land for small-scale agricultural expansion and land degradation caused by overgrazing of cattle, driven by increasing populations and decreasing yields. The livelihoods of communities continue to decline, increasing the threat on the already declining biodiversity of the project zone due to erratic weather conditions. 
The project's clear CCB objectives are:
Climate – Avoided emissions of 14,280,937 tCO2e over a 30-year period at an average of 476,031 tCO2e per year, and in the process assist the human and wildlife population of the project zone to adapt to climate change impacts through income diversification, climate smart agricultural techniques, and habitat protection. 
Community - Alleviate poverty for more than 21,000 households, total of more than 90,000 individuals, specifically targeting women, vulnerable, and marginalized people. The project will also improve health, education and general social and infrastructure services within the project zone.
Biodiversity - Enhancement of the population of plant and wildlife species by conserving and maintaining vulnerable, threatened, and endangered species through habitat protection, controlled law enforcement, as well as rehabilitation and wildlife restocking.
ccb-3816:
The project will be developed in the municipality of Apuí, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil - within the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) category. The project will conserve 71,822.56 hectares of native Amazon Rainforest in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to pasture activities, part of which will be designated to Avoiding Unplanned Deforestation (AUD) (56,349.96 ha), other to Avoiding Planned Deforestation (APD) (14,158.28 ha) and the remaining hectares corresponding to water resources (314.32 ha). For the total area (AUD+APD) and by the end of the project, it is estimated a total avoided emissions of 23,452,633.10 tons of Greenhouse Gases (tCO2e). 
The project will follow the CCB Standards, with benefits for Climate, Community, and Biodiversity. As benefits for climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adaptation to the impacts caused by climate change, such as changes in rainfall regime, as the area presents a dense hydrographic network that contributes to the provision and quality of water in the Amazon River basin.
As quantifiable benefits for Communities, the project will implement groundwater collection and distribution systems, installation of solar panels for electricity generation and provision of satellite internet service in  low-income's extractive communities residences. 
The maintenance of forest cover ensures the conservation of biodiversity, the maintenance of ecosystem functioning (e.g., nutrient cycling) and of ecosystem services provisioning (e.g., carbon sequestration) performed by living organisms. It is noteworthy that the project includes a high priority area for biodiversity conservation, in compliance with the vulnerability criteria of the CCB Gold Level, as it presents species classified as Critically Endangered (CR) and Endangered (EN) according to the IUCN.
ccb-3868: Fangchenggang Mangrove Afforestation Project is located in Gangkou District and Fangcheng District of Fangchenggang City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting mangroves in degraded mangrove habitats. The project proponent is Fangchenggang Xinggang Agricultural Development Co., Ltd.The purpose of the project is to restore the degraded local mangrove ecosystem and increase forest cover by planting a variety of species of native mangrove, and establish a healthy local ecological and economic system by involving residents in the implementation of the projects directly. Totally 221.9 ha of mangroves have been planted with 5 native mangrove species (such as Avicennia marina, Kandelia candel, Aegiceras corniculatum, Rhizophora stylosa, Bruguiera gymnorrhiza). The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals, improve the local environment, enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing them with relevant technical skills. In addition, the project has restored the degraded mangrove ecosystem and increased forest coverage, provided a suitable habitat for animals, especially for endangered birds which mainly live in mangroves. The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 111,592 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 2,789.8tCO2e.
ccb-3897:
Mangrove restoration project in Wenchang and Changjiang, Hainan (hereafter as “the project”) is located in coastal areas of Dongge town, Wenjiao Town, Dongjiao Town, Wencheng Town, Puqian town and Jinshan Town of Wenchang city in the Northest Hainan Island, and Zhubijiang estuary of Changjiang Li Autonomous County in the west Hainan Island.
The project is aimed to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on degraded mangrove ecosystem. 352.89 ha of mangrove is to be restored by plantation of mangrove seedlings on intertidal areas where mangroves had been lost in past decades in Wenchang city and Zhubijiang estuary of Changjiang Li Autonomous County which located in Hainan Province.
The project has expanded the mangrove area and improved the quality of mangroves through the artificial afforestation of mangroves on the beach, which will effectively protect the mangrove ecosystem, save and protect the mangrove germplasm resources and rare and endangered wildlife resources. At the same time, the implementation of the project will also improve the ecological functions of mangroves in wind and wave prevention, siltation and beach protection, bank consolidation and embankment protection, disaster prevention and mitigation, and ensure the safety of people's lives and property.
ccb-3913:
The project activity “Creation of Biodiverse Forests for Land Restoration and Community Development” (referred as “the project”) is located in 5 districts in the Maharashtra state of India. The project works with individual farmers and community members across 5 districts of Maharashtra to help them afforest or reforest land that is fallow, unused or deforested thus helping to bring back lost biodiversity and creating green employment and income opportunities for community members. 

Forest plantations on unused or abandoned agricultural land are not only a great mitigation strategy, but also a great adaptation strategy. Biodiverse forests, as compared to traditional agriculture, are extremely resilient to extreme weather events like cyclones, drought, hailstorms and pest attacks. They thus can help provide a reliable source of supplemental income to the agrarian and tribal communities in India that are facing declining yields and income loss due to climate-change induced erratic rainfall and extreme weather events. 

The project involves planting of over over 120 different species of trees, shrubs, grasses and creepers to create small carbon-sequestering pockets of land with about 1000 trees / hectare that can provide a source of fruit, leaf, bark and oilseed harvest for community members, while also bringing back lost soil carbon onto the land and attracting a wide variety of pollinators like birds and bees to the area. Along the boundary of the tree plantation two to three different species of bamboo will be planted that community members can harvest in a sustainable manner for timber. The project is expected to create 30 labour days of rural employment per hectare to plant and maintain the trees every year.
ccb-3919: Henan Luoning Afforestation Project (hereafter referred as “the project”) is located in Luoning County, Luoyang City, Henan Province, China. The project is to establish forest on the barren land and wastelands to generate GHG emission reductions and contribute to local sustainable development. Prior to the project implementation, all the project sites are barren land in the hills and wastelands, without its implementation, all the sites will keep the same circumstances with no natural renewal and reforestation. The project start date is 01-04-2020 when the planting started, and the project covers 23,574.53 ha of forest was established by direct planted on barren land in the hills and wastelands in Luoning County, Luoyang City, Henan Province.
ccb-3923:
ClimeTrek Limited (hereinafter referred as ClimeTrek) and GKF Agroforestry (P) Limited (hereinafter referred as GKF) are proposing a Grouped Agroforestry Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) project in fallows agricultural, and wastelands owned by individual farmers and communities with low plant cover (hereinafter referred as project activity), located in the geographical boundary of India.
The project activity is a grouped project where various horticultural tree species including fruit bearing tree species, commercial tree species and shrubs will be planted. During the first three years, around 31,984 Ha will be planted in the first project instances covering States of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; the potential land available within the project region for future project instances reaches whole of India. All project instances within this grouped project activity will consist of Agroforestry projects across India.
Based on ex-ante estimates the project will sequester around 4.02 million tonnes of CO2e over 30-years (tree/ shrub biomass carbon and soil carbon).
The overall objective grouped project activity is to mitigate climate change while contributing to sustainable environmental management, community development and poverty alleviation of farmers in India. The grouped project activity is to utilize the fallows agricultural and wastelands by establishing agroforestry systems consisting of both forest trees and fruit trees.
The additional trees in the landscape will enhance the wildlife habit value and biodiversity. In addition, the soil water storage capacity will increase, and soil erosion will be reduced. Consequently, the climate change resilience of the land use systems, related to droughts, will be increased.
These activities will significantly contribute to livelihood improvement through creation of employment and improved food and nutrition security. The establishment of forest and fruit trees will increase carbon sinks hence more carbon
ccb-3938: The “carbono rural AR NEA” project aims to support sustainable grazing practices in Northeastern Argentina (NEA). The project will target farmers that apply unsustainable grazing practices in NEA grasslands/pasturelands and encourage their transition to better grazing practices. These changes are expected to improve the productivity and sustainability of grazing systems while enhancing soil organic carbon sequestration and reducing GHG emissions.
ccb-3960: The Belize Maya Forest Carbon Project is partnership between The Nature Conservancy and Belize Maya Forest Trust. The 87,041 hectare Avoided Planned Deforestation project, located in north-west Belize, reduces GHG emissions through the acquisition and protection of forest lands threatened by agricultural conversion.
ccb-4016: The Amazon Biome Conservancy Grouped REDD+ Project (hereinafter also referred to as “ABC”) has as its main objective to contribute to the preservation with the biggest tropical forest of the world in the Brazilian territory, while providing significant improvements in the social interface. The project for this validation process has only one project activity instance located in the Itacoatiara municipality, state of Amazonas near its capital of Manaus. According to the geo-referencing data, the total area of the project is established at 5,140 ha, which is composed of native Amazon Rainforest vegetation, without the existence of secondary vegetation since the land has not been cleared of native ecosystems within the last 10 years before the project start date. The project area consist of the ABC project is equivalent to the 20% of the landowner property area that he could legally suppress, according to the Brazilian forest code (Law 12.651, 2012). This project will be eligible under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) category, using the VM0007 methodology for Avoiding Planned Deforestation (APDD). The crediting period of the project is 30 years. The start date is on 19/11/2022 and the crediting period is expected to end on 18/11/2052. To execute the installation of this project and to achieve its objectives the VCU generation is very important. A reduction of 2,605,773.23 t CO2-e of GHG is expected over the next ten years for the first baseline developed and presented in this Project Description - PD (average of 260,577.32 t CO2-e per year).
ccb-4034: The Agropalma REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Agropalma Group and its purpose is to promote forest conservation, maintenance of carbon stocks and mitigation of climate change through the reduction of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from land use change. In addition to the climate benefits, the Project also intends to generate social benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and improved well-being of the surrounding communities, as well as environmental benefits through actions aimed at the conservation of local flora and fauna. The Project area covers 50,519 hectares of Amazon forest and is located almost entirely in the northeastern mesoregion of Pará State, including the municipalities of Tailândia, Moju, Tomé Açu and Acará. The region has great relevance in relation to its biodiversity, since it is located in the Belém Center of Endemism (CEB), a place with a large concentration of rare and endemic species. The predominant vegetation is Dense Ombrophylous Forest with a high density of medium and large trees, besides woody lianas and epiphytes.
ccb-4042:
The Cauaxi REDD+ Grouped Project (hereafter called GPD) aims to conserve forests in several private properties located in northeast portion of Pará, close to the border with Maranhão. The Cauaxi River, which gives the project its name, is one of the tributaries of the Capim River, located in the central portion of the project's reference region, at Paragominas municipality.
The GPD aims to create positive economic incentives for landowners to conserve rainforests in private areas that are vulnerable to degradation and deforestation, while contributing to net positive climate impacts as well as benefit to traditional communities and conserve biodiversity. By joining BRcarbon (hereafter known as BRC), forest owners can access funds from the carbon voluntary market to develop conservation and monitoring efforts in their forests. A partnership between BRC and landowners will result in the legal protection of forests, forest monitoring using satellite images, biodiversity inventory (including fauna e flora species), and forest biomass inventory in a broad scale, using 
a upscaling approach based on field collection, drone-borne and satellite sensors such as LiDAR (light detection and ranging). In addition, we will involve surveillance of property, wildfire monitoring, fire prevention and fighting, threatened species protection and social activities with traditional communities. 
As a result, BRC expects to enhance the climate impact of carbon projects, helping communities and biodiversity. The Cauaxi REDD+ Grouped Project is part of the company's initiative to promote forest conservation using the financial flows of the carbon market. This project is related to climate-positive impacts caused by the reduction of emissions 
caused by deforestation and avoided degradation (REDD+).
ccb-4046:
The project area is in Nepal which is a home to a plethora of flora and fauna which spread across Terai to the middle to mountain of the country. Around 5962.03 (000 ha) of land was under forest cover in 2020. Forest Act 1993 recognizes two essential kinds (national and private) and five auxiliary kinds of forest beneath national forest (Government Managed, Community Managed, Protected Forests, Leasehold Forest, Religious Forest, and Private Forest). Deforestation, degradation and fragmentation of natural habitat of wildlife are a serious threat to forests of the country which alarm the need for protection of biodiversity. Adopting agroforestry practices is the best possible solution as this system can avail basic needs of an individual and rehabilitate the lost ecosystem. The primary objectives of agroforestry are to produce food, fodder, fuel-wood, and/or timber. There can also be co-benefits such as carbon sequestration, water quality enhancement, soil protection, and biodiversity conservation. 
Agroforestry system in Nepal is a traditional and ancient practice. Farmers in the hills have expanded the number of agroforestry trees on their farmland in response to forest degradation and deforestation, to meet their immediate demand for fodder, fuelwood, and small-sized timber products. The agroforestry systems deliver several forest products, agriculture products and ecosystem services which may enhance social well-being of the local farmers, national and global community. The small and marginal farmers are almost unaware of the scientific importance (economic and environmental aspects) of agroforestry, short- and long-term benefits, and technical requirements. There awareness efforts to educate farmers on the benefits of agroforestry practice in their farmlands.

The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restoration of severely degraded land by replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term. Totally, 125,441.81 ha of degraded grassland has been managed scientifically by including by fence building and reseeding of native species grass.

ccb-4117: The REDD Carbonflor is a multi-activity grouped project, located in Brazil, in the Amazon and Cerrado biomes. ccb-4122:
Siziwang Banner Improved Grassland Management Project aims to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through grass-planting and grazing management in the project zone. ccb-4143:
The project area is located within 6 private properties, located in the municipality of Vila Rica, inthe State of Mato Grosso, Brazil , inserted in an area of transition from Cerrado to Amazon biome. ccb-4155:
The Malawi Bamboo Afforestation Project will distribute seedlings of giant bamboo, Dendrocalamus asper, to individual agricultural homesteads in rural Malawi. The project will also provide educational support and outreach for the long-term care of bamboo clumps. 

The project is located within the political boundary of the Republic of Malawi.

The project will generate GHG emission reductions by sequestering carbon in live above- and belowground biomass. When individual bamboo clumps reach the end of their lifespan, they will be replaced by a new clump, ensuring carbon remains sequestered over the project lifetime.

Smallholder agricultural homesteads are widespread across Malawi. A variety of trees are grown on farms, in gardens, and around homesteads to serve as fuel, timber, and other uses. However, fast-growing giant bamboo is not grown in Malawi at a large scale. 

Estimated annual average GHG emissions reductions: 174,301 tCO2e
Total GHG emission reductions: 5,054,739 tCO2e

ccb-4243: The project activity is an afforestation project on multiple farms of extensive grazing lands. The overreaching goal is to promote innovative afforestation management activities on degraded lands. By combining native and exotic species to produce high-quality wood and other non-woody products and, in the long term, to generate new patches of managed native species forests. The grouped Project is located in Corrientes Province, in the Northeast region of Argentina (host country) and could include areas in the contiguous south of Misiones Province.  In this region, grazing and agriculture lands have different levels of degradation due to a long history of use without sustainable management. The activities proposed in the Project could stop the degradation processes and enhance the regional environmental conditions. For the design of the plantations, specific local conditions are considered to determine where species will be planted to promote facilitation strategies between them. Exotic species have favorable competition conditions over native ones (e.g., in standing flooded areas), but in return, they help native species with their development, protecting them from frosts, wind, and high radiation. Through forest plantation of native and exotic species, the Project sequesters CO2 by generating net anthropogenic removals by sinks that can be measured, monitored, and verified with known tools and approaches, contributing to the country's sustainable development.The initial activity instance comprises 2,331 hectares of degraded grassland generating an estimated average (long-term average) of ≈775.509 tCO2e net GHG emissions reductions and removals, implying a total GHG benefit for the environment of approximately ≈19.387. tCO2e per year for the length of the project (40 years).
ccb-4246: The objective of the project is to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through the sustainable grassland management practices, such as increasing the rotation of grazing between summer and winter pastures, limiting the grazing days on degraded pastures, and replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term, thereby increasing carbon sequestration, and promoting local development. ccb-4254: Tianjun County Sustainable Grassland Management Project is located in Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China. ccb-4255: The Rewilding Maforki grouped project aims to recover low intensity and unproductive grasslands in Port Loko District, in the Northwest Province of Sierra Leone. ccb-4265:
The REDD+ Café Apuí Agroforestry (CAA) project aims to expand the production chain of agroforestry coffee in southeastern Amazonas and avoid deforestation of native forests on rural properties in the municipalities of Apuí, Manicoré and Novo Aripuanã, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. In the absence of the project, forests on the participating properties would be cleared for agricultural activities, especially pastures, for income generation.

REDD+ CAA is a 30-year grouped project that will have periodic membership of new participants over the first ten years. The initial project's participants are 42 family farmers (Project Activity Instances – PAI) that totalize a PA of 3.696 hectares around the town of Apuí (50km) in Amazonas State/Brazil. The project has a defined geographical area within which instances of project activities are located, totalling 19,874 km2. This area is composed of native forests and agricultural areas, mainly planted pastures, in addition to some enclaves of non-forest pioneer formations.

The project is based on long-term (30-yr) agreements with landowners to avoid deforestation in their areas in exchange for performance-based payment for avoided deforestation. In addition to monitoring, reporting, verification, and leakage mitigation activities, VCU revenues will be invested in agroforestry implementation, technical assistance, organic certification processes, administration, and marketing of coffee and other agroforestry products. The project aims to expand agroforestry coffee production using agroecological techniques and trained personnel in organic production promoted since 2012 in the region.

The project intends to generate climate, community and biodiversity benefits under CCB standard. The payment for avoided deforestation, investment in the agroforestry coffee chain, and support for the structuring of new agroforestry product chains offer an alternative sustainable income to producers while maintaining conserved forests.
ccb-4283: The objective of the project is to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through the sustainable grassland management practices, such as increasing the rotation of grazing between summer and winter pastures, limiting the grazing days on degraded pastures, and replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term, thereby increasing carbon sequestration, and promoting local development. The project is located in Aksai Kazakh Autonomous County, Jiuquan City, Gansu Province of China.
ccb-4304:
The Transformational Regenerative Integrated Biodiverse Agriculture for Livelihoods (TRIBAL) Project is a landscape approach that aims to make it viable for small and marginal farmers to live off their land in a sustainable and profitable manner. 
The project will promote agroforestry and sustainable farming practices across within the Araku Valley in Vishakhapatnam District, Andhra Pradesh, India. Planned agroforestry and sustainable farming practices that will be promoted by the project include agroforestry utilizing both fruit and multi-purpose tree species, shade coffee systems, intercropping of pulses and millets, green manuring, mulching and organic composting. These activities will improve the livelihoods and well-being of the tribal landowners by achieving multiple objectives such as improved soil fertility, increased revenue generation, food security, reduced drudgery for women and increased biodiversity. Through this positive impact on climate, communities, and biodiversity the TRIBAL project aims to achieve both VCS and CCB Gold certification. 
This grouped project is being initiated in Paderu and Pedabayalu Mandals of Paderu Division in Vishakhapatnam District, with the intention of expanding to up to 11 Mandals within the Araku Valley landscape in future. The tribal people of this region were traditionally hunters and gatherers, relying on the forest for sustenance. The practice of shifting cultivation came in at the turn of the century. As the- forest began to get depleted, the tribal communities gradually become engaged in agriculture. Now, subsistence agriculture is the primary livelihood for nearly 99% of the tribes within the project region, with over 80% of the landholdings being less than one hectare in size.
ccb-4325:
The Makueni Agroforestry Carbon Project (hereafter, “MACP”) is a carbon project in Kenya being developed together by Eni S.p.A. and Eni Kenya b.v. 
MACP will promote the establishment of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) practices that will generate high-quality carbon credits, through carbon sequestration. MACP will implement a package of SALM practices, by working with a range of participants to implement these sustainable methods across landscapes in Makueni County, Kenya, particularly focusing on smallholder farms. Project activities will contribute to climate change mitigation, adaptation, and food security. The project has been designed as a grouped project and is targeting to be initially implemented in about 40,000 ha across the County of Makueni, with possibility of expansion into other Counties, since this is a grouped project.
The project has a 20-year crediting period and applies the VCS approved Methodology VM0017 Adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management, Version 1.0. The project’s estimated annual average and total net GHG emission reductions/removals are 155,383 and 3,107,663 tCO2e, respectively.
ccb-4329: The Conservation and Restoration of Classified Forests in Côte d’Ivoire project (“CRCF”) is being developed by Eni S.p.A. and Eni Côte d’Ivoire LTD and aims to implement both forest conservation and restoration activities in 14 classified forests for a total area of 156,000 ha spread across the districts of Lagunes and Comoé. The overall project aim is to preserve each classified forest targeted, restore the deforested and degraded areas through reforestation, agroforestry and assisted natural revegetation activities and develop a sustainable management of the forest resources.  The targeted forests have been heavily deforested and degraded over the years. The main direct causes of deforestation and forest degradation are: (i) the significant expansion of extensive slash-and-burn agriculture and monoculture plantations (e.g. cocoa, rubber, palm oil etc.); (ii) the uncontrolled exploitation of forests; iii) population growth and urban expansion; (iv) bushfires (related to agriculture and/or hunting); v) mining, including illegal gold panning; and vi) political and military crisis. To this end, the implementation of the CRCF project is critical to ensure the preservation and restoration of the remaining portions of natural forests, to reduce the greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) from the conversion of natural forest and to restore the biodiversity across the project area. The project will actively involve local communities and will produce significant socio-economic benefits through the creation of alternative livelihoods and economic opportunities. The project is in line and will support the Government’s strategy to reduce the deforestation and related GHG emissions and increase its forest surface. The project has a 30-year crediting period and applies the VCS approved VM0007 REDD+ Methodology Framework (REDD+ MF). The estimated annual average is approximately 273.524 tCO2e and the total net greenhouse gas emission reductions/removals are around 8.205.724 tCO2e.
ccb-4348: The objective of the project is to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through the sustainable grassland management practices, such as increasing the rotation of grazing between summer and winter pastures, limiting the grazing days on degraded pastures, and replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term, thereby increasing carbon sequestration, and promoting local development. Totally, 317,875.91 ha of degraded grassland will be restore in Subei Mongilia Autonomous County, Jiuquan City, Gansu Province, China.
ccb-4369:
Tianzhu Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Tianzhu County, Gansu Province of China. Tianzhu County is located in the northwest of Gansu Province and in the middle of Hexi corridor where the Qinghai Tibet Plateau and  Mongolia Plateau meet. The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by seeding grass and building fence on the degraded grassland, increase carbon  sequestration and contribute to local development by introducing sustainable grazing and management of grassland. The project proponent is Zhejiang Zhongzheng Forestry Development Co., Ltd.
According to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, the grassland in the region has been facing serious degradation and even desertification due to the impact of climate change and human activities. According to the National standard documents of the people's Republic of China and Project Design Report, moderately  degraded areas refer to the total grass yield decreased by 21%-50%compared with that before degradation and the total grass yield decreased by 50% compared with that before degradation is regarded as seriously degraded grasslands.
ccb-4372: The mangrove areas of the Democratic Republic of Congo (fall under the global category grouping of Central African mangrove eco-region. They are found within the Central Congo Province occupying an area of 23,684 hectares.Mangrove forests of DRC are crucial because of its importance in provision of goods and services which are unique to this type of forest such as shoreline protection and being a feeding and breeding ground of commercially important fisheries due to the location of these forests at the tidal estuaries ecosystems of River Congo as well as supporting a wide range of biodiversity. Despite these uses, the DRC Mangrove Forest has seen degradation and deforestation over the years. The threats facing these mangroves include the encroachment of the areas by the nearby communities leading to conversion of forest land to settlement and other land uses that is linked to population increase over the years, coupled with unsustainable harvesting for wood and firewood for varied purposes. Additionally, the loss of mangroves leads to the release o f the carbon stored by the ecosystem back into the atmosphere, thereby accelerating climate change. Through the implementation of the mangrove REDD+ project in the area the project proponents aim to conserve the mangrove areas by addressing the drivers of deforestation leading to a potential emission reduction of 689,274 tCO2e/year. Furthermore, the project proponent also aims to restore the already degraded and deforested area of 1161 ha during the project lifetime that will lead to additional emission reductions of 33,379 tCO2e/yr along with other benefits such as shoreline protection and biodiversity conservation. Thus, this REDD and RWE project is expected to avoid unplanned deforestation and degradation, along with restoration of the already degraded areas on an area of 23,684 ha equating to 21,691,891 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30 year project lifetime with an annual average of 723,063 tCO2e.
ccb-4381: The WSRAFP project serves to preserve natural forest within the West Seram Region of Seram Island, Maluku, Indonesia. The proposed Project intends to engage community in Technology Based Agarwood Silviculture by Afforesting 1000Ha of Agarwood on the longtime degraded grassland and protect and conserve the remaining forest area. The total Project area of 1st phase comprises of 55,000 ha of forest later can be expanded to 85,000 ha. The Project activities aim to improve the standard of living of the community and to reduce deforestation pressures and drivers. The Agarwood farming and forest conservation Project intends to establish activities that simultaneously provide environmental benefits (forest protection, wildlife management, biodiversity conservation) as well as community benefits (enhance local’s source of income, utilization of 20-30% of generated revenues in developing the community and raise their standard of living, improved agricultural practices, local development opportunities).
ccb-4384: The Jaji ARR Project is the first ARR based CCB-VCS project to be developed in Kaduna State, Nigeria and amongst the first CCB-VCS projects of its kind in Nigeria. The goals of the project are; the reforestation of degraded abandoned farmland and the sustainable management of the reforested area for the lifetime of the project in order to sequester emissions, enhance land resources and their ability to support life on land, positive social/community impact for the improvement of livelihoods and conditions of communities around the project area, empowerment of marginalized segments of the rural population and the promotion of biodiversity in the project area and zones.
ccb-4387:
The REDD+ Project Pacha Prometida is a grouped initiative that takes place in indigenous communities San Pedro (located in the Ixiamas municipality), Cachichira and Tres Hermanos (located in the San Buenaventura municipality), in Abel Iturralde province of La Paz Department, in Bolivia. Initially, it seeks to protect 11,500 hectares of primary Amazonian forest, which is strongly threatened by planned agricultural expansion and sugarcane planting activities, through:
• Reducing the threat of deforestation on the forests of the communities Cachichira, San Pedro and Tres Hermanos and, therefore, avoid the issuance of around 4.3 million of tCO2 during the first 20 years of the Project life cycle (on average 215,000 VCUs annually).
• Promoting of the social development actions to improve the quality of life of the families of the communities Cachichira, San Pedro and Tres Hermanos.
• Protecting biological diversity in flora and fauna, especially habitats of endangered wild species, found in the territories of the communities Cachichira, San Pedro and Tres Hermanos.
• Conserving and improving the focal areas where High Conservation Values are found that are identified.
ccb-4391:
The project area is located within 3 private properties, located in the municipalities of Vila Rica, inthe State of Acre, Brazil, inserted in an area Amazon biome. The project aims to avoid unplanned deforestation in a project area of 58,487.50 ha. The REDD+CCB project is expected to avoid predicted deforestation of 10,354,998 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (Dec 01,2022-Nov 30,2052), with an annual average of 345,167 tCO2e.
The objective is to originate- with characteristics of a REDD+CCB initiative, following the Project Cycle of the VM0015 Methodology for Avoided Unplanned Deforestation, v1.1 Methodology. Thus, such VCUs may, in the future, be accounted for in Brazil's Nationally Determined Contributions Emission Reductions efforts, within the framework of the Paris Climate Agreement, as they are negotiated between different parties, within the framework of the voluntary markets for carbon credit negotiations.
Since the proiect will originate from the characteristics of a REDD+ initiative, it will contribute to efforts to reduce deforestation of the Amazon Biome in Brazil, resulting in the preservation of biodiversity in one of the most important tropical forests on the planet and in the restoration and preservation of the conditions of Climate Regulation of the Earth. It is therefore important that the Project is added to the methodological efforts provided for in the CCB Program- so that the VCUs eligible for the validation of the methodological quality are also valued considering the methodological efforts validated by the CCB Program.
The project's social engagement creates a support base to ensure preservation and sustainable use of the forest. Social engagement at all stages is important so the actions to be developed are inclusive and transparent, in processes that allow communities and stakeholders to actively participate to ensure that the project generates legacies with positive social and environmental impacts.
ccb-4394:
The Jatobá project will be developed in the municipality of Boca do Acre, state of Amazonas, Brazil, within the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) category. The project will conserve 94,090.42 hectares of native Amazon rainforests in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to land use conversion activities from forests to pastures aimed at raising livestock. The project area (18,017.19 ha) will be allocated to Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), and it is estimated that at the end of the project the emission of 5,440,804 tons of Greenhouse Gases (GHG) (tCO2e) will have been avoided. 
The project will be developed considering the CCB Standards, with benefits for the Climate, Community and Biodiversity. As benefits to the climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adapting to the impacts caused by climate change.
As benefits to the communities, the project will enable water security and access to information to minimize the impacts caused by climate change in traditional, low-income extractive communities.
It is noteworthy that the project includes a high priority area for biodiversity conservation, as it is located within a Key Biodiversity Area (KBA), harboring species endemic to the Brazilian Amazon and species classified as Vulnerable (VU), Critically Endangered (CR) and Endangered (EN) with extinction according to the IUCN.
ccb-4408: Trees for the Future (TREES) is developing The Lake Victoria Watershed Agroforestry Carbon Project. This project uses VERRA methodology VM0042 with CCB to develop and monitor VCUs with smallholder farmers on 75,000 hectares of land in the counties of Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori and Siaya along the shores of Lake Victoria in Kenya. This project will involve training and implementing sustainable agroforestry practices with farmers to transform mono-cropped land into nature-based carbon sinks with above and below ground biomass and improved soils. Currently this cropland is under low yield cultivation of grain crops and is an area designated by the Kenyan Government as a target region for agroforestry development on cropland. In addition, to creating VCUs, the sustainable agroforestry techniques and extension services provided to farmers will ensure diversification of cropping systems including horticulture crops and fruit and fodder trees. The projects aims to improve nutrition, increase income and resilience, develop the sustainable growing capability of the land, and enhance biodiversity in the region. The restoration effort will generate an estimated 20.7 million Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) and help farmers adapt to the impacts of climate change.
ccb-4411:
Xinzhou Echeng Afforestation Project (hereafter as “the project”) locates in Echeng County, Xinzhou City, Shanxi Province of North China. It aims to address climate change and promote sustainable development in the region. The project involves planting trees on barren mountains to increase carbon sequestration, which can help mitigate the effects of climate change by removing CO2. Aside from the environmental benefits, the project can also have positive economic impacts on the local community by providing employment opportunities for residents and contributing to local economic development. The project was implemented by the project proponent Jingle County Sailing Carbon Sink Development Co. Ltd.
A total of 39,589.87 ha of forest will be planted through direct planting on previously barren lands in Echeng County. The project will cover 6 towns,6 townships and 223 administrative villages. The project sites have not undergone any natural renewal or afforestation prior to the implementation of the project. 
The project is expected to generate GHG emission removals of 19,966,354 tCO2e in 60 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 332,773tCO2e.
ccb-4429:
The REDD + project is implemented in the area made up of 21 native communities: Junín Pablo, Nuevo Loreto, Buenos Aires, Caimito, Nuevo Egipto, Nueva Yarina, Santa Rosa de Dinamarca, Nuevo Paraiso, Santa Marta, Utucuro, Caco Macaya, San José of Pacache, Nuevo Saposoa, Santa Rosa de Aguaytía, Mariscal Cáceres, Yamino, Sinchi Roca II, El Naranajal, Nueva Alianza de Baños, Santa Teresa and Golondrinas, the first 17 communities are located in the Ucayali region and the remaining 4 in the Huánuco region. The project area has an extension of 184,773.74 hectares and its objective is to conserve the forest in the 21 communities from the advance of deforestation and degradation, as well as to conserve biodiversity stocks and improve the living conditions of the population surrounding the project area. .

The project aims to reduce the pressure to change land use in the project area through 4 components: i) Strengthening of governance and management of the territory in native communities, ii) Generation of sustainable inclusive businesses, improving income of the families of the native communities, iii) Maintenance of forest conservation objects, and iv) Strengthening of capacities for the MBC with social inclusion and gender equity.

With these actions, the project expects to avoid a total of 10,394,747.73 tCO2-e according to the base scenario projected for the first 10 years, with an annual average of net emissions of 1,039,474.77 tCO2-e. In addition, the project includes benefits for the populations involved, as well as for the conservation of biodiversity, where it seeks to contribute to the conservation of forests with high levels of biodiversity with the presence of endemic species, species in danger of extinction or with some degree of extinction. of threat, beyond the benefits of reducing GHG emissions.
ccb-4452:
The Asaga Amazonas REDD+ project is located in the state of Amazonas and is comprised of 470504 hectares , near the Apuí Conservation Unit Mosaic and the Campos Amazônicos National Park, as well as being surrounded by other settlement projects, reserves, and indigenous territories and at least one other REDD+ project. This diversity provides a great opportunity for the conservation and socioeconomic development of the region.

The Apuí Conservation Unit Mosaic is composed of nine conservation units, including four state forests (Sucunduri, Aripuanã, do Apuí, and Manicoré), two state parks (Guariba and Sucunduri), two sustainable development reserves (Bararati and Aripuanã), and the Guariba Extractive Reserve. Regarding the Campos Amazônicos National Park, it presents one of the most significant Cerrado enclaves within the Amazon Forest biome. One of the reasons it has great scientific potential is the presence of endemic species.

Due to the high density of biodiversity and the many unique species of flora and fauna, the conservation of this wild habitat is extremely important. Nevertheless, the involved municipalities rank high in deforestation and wildfires, as well as facing pressure from agricultural expansion, illegal logging, mining, construction of hydroelectric plants, roads, and land grabbing. 

The region has a variety of habitats, including upland forests, flooded forests, rocky fields, and savannas, as well as waterfalls and rapids that occur along the rivers, with a great diversity of species and landscapes.
ccb-4455: XINJIANG MAKIT COUNTY WINDBREAK AND SAND FIXATION ECOLOGICAL FOREST CONSTRUCTION BASE PROJECT (here after “the project”) is located in Makit County, Xinjiang Province of China, whose aim is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the desert lands.
ccb-4476: The Grouped Project Sul da Bahia falls under the Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) category and targeting the following Verra certifications: Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standard (CCB). The project aims to restore forest formations that are diminished due to the expansion of other land use practices such as overgrazing on extensive cattle ranches, intensive agriculture and silviculture systems. The grouped project is located in the Atlantic Forest biome in the state of Bahia (Brazil). Restoration is attained through forestation activities using native and non-native species. Project activities also include harvesting and establishing agroforestry systems to diversify and maximize project benefits for all parties and communities involved. The overarching goal of the project is to create a biodiverse forest cover that combines carbon capture, biodiversity and community impacts with a diversity of economic functions such as sustainable production of crops and forest products.
ccb-4480: The Bajo Baudó Mangroves REDD++ Project is in the Pacific region in the department of Chocó, Colombia. It limits to the north with the municipality of Nuquí, to the south with the municipality of Medio Baudó, to the east with the municipality of Atrato and to the west with the Pacific Ocean. The project area is collectively owned by 5 Community Councils, which are Cuevita (R 2701/Dec 21, 2001), Pavasa (R 2695/Dec 21, 2001), Villa María de Purrichá (R 1129/May 23, 2000), Virudó (R 2698/Dec 21, 2001) and San Agustín de Terrón (R 3369/Dec 21, 2000). Although the total titled area for the 5 councils is 73,611 ha, the project area is 62,212 ha, which overlaps 51% with the DMRI Encanto de los Manglares del Bajo Baudó Management District, created through the agreement 008 of 2017. The (DRMI) is a Protected Area category that decentralizes the power of the environmental authority and allows decision-making by the communities that inhabit it. With the management of the area, new models of social and environmental territorial management have been created, however, there are several challenges in terms of governance and conservation of ecosystems. Through the DMRI declaration, sustainable management agreements have been reached with the communities and joint restoration and monitoring actions have been developed with the participation of other key institutional actors. The project area overlaps with two important ecosystems, mangrove forest (19.88% of the total project area), with an estimated average reserve of 800 tCO2e/ha, and Basal humid forest (80.12% of the total project area), with an estimated average reserve of 604 tCO2e/ha. The drivers of deforestation in the baseline have been due to the implementation of coconut crops, subsistence crops, crops for illicit use, and livestock; the drivers of degradation have been selective logging, illegal mining, fishing, and indiscriminate housing. The main objective of the project is: Reduce GHG emissions due to forest degradatio.
ccb-4485: Forest conservation at the BRArbo property, located in the municipalities of Juruá, Jutaí and Carauari, State of Amazonas. Forest conservation will be achieved through a combination of sustainable forest management in an area of 130,641 ha and surveillance in the remaining area of the project, of 543,721 ha. The project will address the needs of local populations and promote biodiversity conservation in the area.
ccb-4490:
Maodeng Pasture Improved Grassland Management Project (hereinafter as “the project”) is located in Xilin Hot City, Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China. The Xilin Hot City geographic coordinates of the project zone are 115 °16′~117°13′E and 43°02′~44°52′N and borders Abaga Banner in the west, Zhenglan Banner in the south, Xiwu Banner and Chifeng City in the east, and Dongwu Banner in the north.
The main objective of the project is to implement sustainable grassland management measures for 10,533.33 hectares of degraded grassland through seeding, grazing prohibition and fertilization. These measures improved grassland productivity, restored vegetation, significantly increased vegetation coverage, improved biodiversity in degraded grasslands, increased the proportion of superior pasture, improved soil fertility, and enhanced the stability of grassland ecosystems.
According to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, due to the impact of climate change and human activities, the grassland in this area has been facing varying degrees of degradation, sandification, and sparse vegetation.
The total scale of the project is 10,533.33 hectares. Strictly ban grazing on all plots within the project area for the first five years after the completion of the project and, after five years, adopt sustainable grassland management methods according to the actual grassland restoration situation, such as rotational grazing in different pastoral areas, limits the time and number of grazing in the project area to protect the natural grassland resources, curb the deterioration of the ecological environment of the natural grassland.
ccb-4497:
The objective of the Amazon Partners (AP) 20 Project is to originate -with the characteristics of a REDD+ initiative (Reduction of Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation), following the Project Cycle of the VM0015 Methodology for Avoided Unplanned Deforestation, v1.1 Methodology. Thus, such Verified Carbon Units (VCU) may, in the future, be accounted for in Brazil's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) Emission Reductions efforts, in the framework of the Paris Climate Agreement, as much as they are negotiated between different parties, within the framework of the voluntary markets for carbon credit negotiations.

The Project will avoid Greenhouse Gas Emissions at the Territory of Indigenous Peoples of the Shawadawa Association, in the municipality of Porto Walter, in the State of Acre, Amazon Biome of the Brazilian Territory. Since AP 20 is originating from the characteristics of a REDD+ initiative, it will contribute to efforts to reduce deforestation of the Amazon Biome in Brazil, resulting in the preservation of biodiversity in one of the most important tropical forest areas on the planet. The Project adds to the methodological efforts provided for in the Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) Program – so that the VCUs eligible for the validation of the methodological quality of the project are also valued considering the methodological efforts validated by the CCB Program. The development of the integrated Amazon Partners 20 Project provides for social engagement to create a support base to ensure the preservation of the forest. Social engagement at all stages of the process is important so that the actions to be developed are inclusive and transparent, in processes that allow nearby communities and other stakeholders in the project to actively participate, closely following to ensure that the project generates legacies with positive social and environmental impacts.
ccb-4513:
The Project aims to protect the native forest socio-ecosystems of the Argentine Gran Chaco ecoregion. The Grouped Project will seek to reduce planned deforestation and unplanned deforestation and degradation pressures by encouraging landowners granted with large-scale agricultural and livestock production deforestation permits to set aside their land for conservation and forest regeneration. It will also implement a combination of environmental and social activities aimed at improving the livelihoods of community members living in the vicinity of the project area as well as the enhancement of the forest and biodiversity.
In Argentina, deforestation has accelerated over the past 40 years as the country's agricultural frontier has expanded, resulting in one of the highest deforestation rates in the world. This expansion of the agricultural frontier is having a major impact on native ecosystems and their biodiversity. At the same time, deforestation and land enclosure have altered the livelihoods of many indigenous and/or peasant communities who use large areas of the Forest for their activities.
For the first Project Activity Instance the project proponent, VISTA Energy, purchased part of the El Chaguaral farm (4.892 hectares) in the current boundary of the agricultural frontier. The former owner of the property had a clearing permit to transform the land for agricultural and livestock purposes. VISTA will not make use of that permit. The activities to achieve this include fencing, hiring responsible field staff to monitor the property, and developing and implementing a biodiversity conservation plan together with an action plan for fire prevention, warning and response will be implemented. Also assisted natural regeneration and enrichment planting activities will be implemented.The initial activity instance is estimated to generate ≈ 983,460 tCO2e net GHG emissions reductions and removals (≈49,173. tCO2 e per year for 20 years)
ccb-4525:
The Republic of the Congo Improved Forest Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “The project”) is located in UFA Djua-Ikié, The Republic of the Congo. It is implemented by Société d’Exploitation Foresrière Yuan Dong (hereinafter referred to as “SEFYD”) as the project proponent. The project is to protect the forest that was planned to be logged.
UFA Djua-Ikié is located in the Souanké and Semé Districts of the Sangha administrative Province. The project is designed to improve forest management in 338,589 ha of native Congolese forests legally designated for logging. By avoiding previously planned logging and implementing improved forest management and conservation activities, this project will increase the carbon stock through protecting the forest.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the forests in the project area were harvested following the guidelines in Timber Harvest Plan approved by the local forestry authority. In order to protect the forest ecosystem, improve the ecological environment, increase carbon sinks, reduce GHG emission reductions and slow down climate change, the project proponent decided to stop the logging and implement this improved forest management project activities from 01-August-2020 to 31-July-2040.
The project is expected to generate approximately 53,140,400 tCO2e during the 20 years’ crediting period, with the annual emission reductions of 2,657,020 tCO2e.
The project’s climate, community and biodiversity objectives:
⚫ Reduce GHG emissions and mitigate climate change; and
⚫ Improve soil and water conservation and contribute to sustainable development; and
⚫ Provide experience of forest management and risk prevention and control for local stakeholders; and
⚫ Improvement of the biodiversity and ecological environment of the project area and its surrounding area; and
⚫ Increase employment opportunities and raise the income level of local residents; and
⚫ Protect the local tree species from being cutting down.
ccb-4539: In Sierra Leone, mangrove forests are under severe threat from the pressures of subsistence-based harvesting for construction material and fuelwood for cooking and smoking fish. The health of mangrove ecosystems is directly tied to the social and economic well-being of local communities that depend on them for sustaining their traditional livelihoods in fishing and shellfish harvesting. Communities further depend on the mangroves for preventing erosion, which threatens coastal villages. Through a community-based and livelihood driven approach, and in collaboration with the Government of Sierra Leone, this grouped project will generate greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals through avoided deforestation and reforestation of mangrove ecosystems in the Bonthe and Moyamba districts, identified as global hotspots for biodiversity and home to some of the most marginalized communities in Sierra Leone. The project will begin with the conservation of 10,624 ha of mangroves on Sherbro Island, expanding in subsequent instances to include conservation activities in a combined total of over 74,000 ha of mangrove forests. Restoration activities will similarly expand from an initial 50 ha to an estimated total of 2,000 ha of degraded mangrove areas that are now threatened by erosion or abandoned due to saltwater intrusion.
ccb-4542:
The Amazônidas REDD+ AUDD Grouped Project (hereafter called GPD) aims to avoid unplanned deforestation in private and public properties at Amazonas State. The scalability area of the GPD was defined based on the Brazil regional division by IBGE of 20171, as the sum of the Tefé, Parintins, Manaus, and Lábrea intermediate geographic regions in the Amazonas state, excluding the immediate geographic regions of Coari, Tefé, and Tabatinga. This region has long been recognized for its alarming rates of deforestation within the Amazon biome, and its forests face an escalated risk of deforestation. Initially, the present GPD is composed of thirty-five properties with 251,706.41 hectares of forest cover, split into four municipalities: Itacoatiara, Itapiranga, Silves and Presidente Figueiredo. The climate benefits brought with this GPD are directed related to the emission reduction of 124,528 tCO2e in average per year, calculated with a 6-year jurisdictional baseline.
The actions involving the implementation of Amazônidas REDD+ AUDD GPD are complementary to the grouped projects developed by brCarbon. Through these projects, in accordance with current federal and state environmental laws, brCarbon seeks to promote integral forest conservation actions in rural properties with remaining vegetation, promote solutions based on nature in its regions of influence, generating co-benefits not only for the climate (reduction and removal of emissions), but also communities and local biodiversity. Furthermore, the Amazônidas REDD+ AUDD GPD aims to create positive economic incentives for landowners to conserve rainforests in areas that are vulnerable to degradation and deforestation, while contributing to net positive climate impacts as well as benefit to traditional communities and conserve biodiversity.
ccb-4552:
The Uákiry REDD+ Grouped Project (hereafter called GPD), aims to avoid unplanned deforestation in private properties at Acre State. The area of deforestation involving three states in the north of Brazil has increased significantly in recent years, where before it was well preserved, the region known by the acronym AMACRO (where the states of Amazonas, Acre and Rondônia are located) has literally become no man's land. The lack of control caused cases of land grabbing and other crimes linked to the expansion of the agricultural frontier to explode. The region came to be known as the new Deforestation Frontier.
Initially the first four project activity instance is composed by four properties with 84,220 ha of forest cover, located in the Iaco River margins, one of Purus River affluents, in the Amazon basin. Through these projects, BrCarbon (hereafter known as BRC) and Yaco2 Gestão e Comércio de Carbono (Yaco2) seeks to promote integral forest conservation actions generating co-benefits not only for the climate (reduction and removal of emissions), but also communities and local biodiversity. At the validation, the climate benefits are directed related with the emission reduction of 215,021 tCO2e in average per year.
By joining BRC forest program, landowners can access funds from the carbon voluntary market to develop conservation and monitoring efforts in their forests. A partnership between BRC and landowners will result in the legal protection of forests, forest monitoring using satellite images, biodiversity inventory (including fauna e flora species), and forest biomass inventory in a broad scale, using an upscaling approach based on field collection, drone-borne and satellite sensors such as LiDAR (light detection and ranging). In addition, we will involve property surveillance, wildfire monitoring, fire prevention and fighting, threatened species protection and long-term social activities with local communities.
ccb-4563:
Allcot Blue Carbon Mangrove Restoration project in Senegal (ABC Mangrove Senegal) is a grouped project for the reforestation and conservation of mangrove ecosystems in Senegal. Through the restoration of at least 7,000 ha of mangroves, the project aims to:
o Strengthen the vegetation cover in the mangrove ecosystems.
o Improve the production and income of vulnerable groups.
o Strengthen the capacity of vulnerable groups to use land resources sustainably.
Involving the local communities since the beginning is one of the most important steps in the project. This includes providing information on all project activities and teaching basic concepts on climate change, and 
carbon sequestration projects. The project promotes a functioning family model where both women and 
men can equally participate in the project. People will show alternative livelihood opportunities that allow them to acquire and grow high-value crops, beekeeping, or ecotourism among other potential possibilities, 
which also reduces pressure on mangrove forests. An improvement of the basic infrastructure for rural communities is targeted as well.
The Project location is the Saloum Delta and the Casamance estuary respectively located in two regions (Fatick and Casamance) and 5 departments (Fatick, Foundiougne, Ziguinchor, Bignona, Oussouye), implemented in bare land, and at the end of the crediting period, the net emissions reductions are 2,241,960 tCO2 e.
ccb-4587:
The Boreal Wildlands Forest Carbon Offset Project creates GHG reductions and removals through the 
purchase and management of 145,173 ha of private forest land, located in the Ontario Boreal shield 
forest, by The Nature Conservancy of Canada (NCC) for the creation of a conservation-based forest 
carbon project.
ccb-4602:
Tropical rain forests with their rich fauna and flora are threatened worldwide from deforestation and forest degradation. In Argentina, deforestation rates are particularly high, caused mainly by conversion of forests to expand soy and beef production. Wintershall Dea AG, VisionNetZero GmbH and Banco de Bosques have joined forces to develop REDD+ carbon projects to conserve large forest patches with a high biodiversity in the Northwestern region of Argentina. 
The project intends to protect and conserve 24,154 hectares that are part of the Yungas forests in northwest Argentina. The main project activity is taking the property off the market to prevent agricultural development and conserve its high carbon values, rich biodiversity, and critical ecosystem functionality by avoiding planned deforestation and forest degradation. Therefore, the project intends a joint certification with CCB Standard.
The project will deliver significant carbon as well as non-carbon benefits by conserving the natural forest ecosystems of the Yungas, one of the most biodiverse natural systems in Argentina and home to nearly 50% of the country's biodiversity. Through the income of carbon revenues, forest areas with high conservation value can be purchased and conserved by donating and integrating them into national or provincial protection systems.
The development of REDD+ carbon projects contribute to climate change mitigation by reducing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) from forest loss and forest degradation. The number of generated credits is estimated based on the comparison of the projected baseline and the effectiveness of the project activities targeting the drivers of deforestation and degradation. In the project area that would be protected, the weighted average of tons of carbon dioxide per hectare (tCO2/ha) is 884 tCO2/ha. On that basis, up to 1.8 Mio. VCUs can be expected within the duration of the project (30 years).
ccb-4646: Since its inception in 1999, over 170,000 participants organized into over 26,000 TIST Small Groups have planted over 25 million trees in Tanzania, India, Kenya, and Uganda - accomplishing GhG sequestration through tree planting, creating a potential long-term income stream, and developing sustainable environments and livelihoods. Kenya 011 is a subset of the TIST project in Kenya and applies to 12,892 Small Groups, 79,089 Participants, 53,357 active Project Areas, and 23,747 hectares.  TIST farmers use a mosaic restoration approach, planting on thousands of individual farms spread across the landscape. The individual farms are found throughout Kenya and concentrated around Mt Kenya.
ccb-4653:
Integrated Management of Peat Forest Ecosystems in Kahayan Hilir District is a peat forest protection and restoration project that proposed by KpSHK to be funded for 25 years through Rimba Collective mechanism. The project is involving 4 HDs in the peatland area in Pulang Pisau Regency which previously had experienced substantial forest and peatland degradation by fire, namely:
1.	Gohong Village Forest of 3,155 ha (based on SK No.587/Menhut-II/2012)
2.	Kelurahan Kalawa Village Forest of 4,230 ha (based on SK No.584/Menhut-II/2012)
3.	Mentaren I Village Forest of 1,835 ha (based on SK No.585/Menhut-II/2012)
4.	Buntoi Village Forest of 7,025 ha (based on SK No.586/Menhut-II/2012)
The project aims to support efforts to protect and improve social forestry management and governance in four village forests: Buntoi Village Forest, Gohong Village Forest, Kalawa Village Forest and Mantaren I Village Forest. The project’s climate, community and biodiversity objectives are summarized below. 
Climate Objective: Reduce emissions from deforestation and forest degradation by improving Village Forest institutional capacity, community-based forest governance and fire prevention and restoring degraded peat swamp forest;
Community Objective: Improved community wellbeing through community economic empowerment and economic development through the development of sustainable agricultural commodities and other sources of income
Biodiversity Objective: Conserve biodiversity by conserving HCV areas, rehabilitating degraded areas of the Village Forest and preventing activities that damage biodiversity in the Village Forest.
The license for the Village Forests has been given to the communities of the four villages by the Indonesian Ministry of Environment and Forestry (MoEF) as part of the national program of Social Forestry – a great innovation and achievement in sustainable forest management in Indonesia much applauded.
ccb-4659: The One Mara Carbon Project (OMCP) is an ecosystem-level conservation initiative that aims to protect ecological resources and provide economic and social co-benefits for communities by incentivizing conservancy formation and grassland restoration in the Maasai Mara landscape in Kenya. The goal of OMCP is to restore the degraded rangelands through improved grazing management and prevent further loss of grasslands by providing alternative livelihoods for communities, build resilient conservancies, ensure biodiversity conservation, and enhance tourism. This region is world-renown for the expansive rangelands where agropastoralists and wildlife co-exist. However, historical land sub-division into small, fenced land parcels and long term extensive grazing by livestock has led to land degradation, including the gradual loss in soil organic carbon (SOC). Communities living within the ecosystem depend on the condition of the grasslands to provide livelihoods that will meet their socio-economic needs. Implementing climate change mitigation measures and halting land degradation are vital to ensuring the longevity of this world-famous conservation area.
ccb-4668: Alxa Left Banner Improved Grassland Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Alashan Left Banner, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. The project is aimed to improve the rotation of grazing animals, limit the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restore degraded land by replanting with grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term. The project proponent is Inner Mongolia Cili Agricultural Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Project Proponent or PP).
ccb-4671: The ANGELIM REDD+ Project protects 21,261.02 hectare of Amazon rainforest from deforestation in Aripuanã, Juína and Castanheira municipalities of Mato Grosso State – Brazil. This project estimates a total GHG emissions reduction of 3,303,261 tons of CO2eq during 40 years of project by avoiding unplanned deforestation of 8,915 ha, with an average annual emissions reduction of 82,582 tons of CO2eq. The project consists of four farms: Continental, União, Recanto do Sinuelo and Cachoeirinha.
ccb-4681:
The YBYRÁ REDD+ Project is a unique REDD+ Project, composed by 74 rural private properties with a project area of 76,481.34 hectare of Amazon rainforest. The project is located in four municipalities: Paragominas, Ipixuna do Pará, Tomé-Açu and Ulianópolis, in the state of Pará, Brazil. The main goals are forest conservation and reduction of GHG emissions of 12,065,803.14 tCO2 in 30 years by avoiding deforestation of 38,317.74 ha in the Project area. 
Pará explores unsustainably the Amazon Forest since its historical occupation. In 2021, almost 25% deforested areas in Brazil were in Pará.  The document known as “Deforestation Arc” presented a list with 52 cities considered priority for prevention, monitoring, and control actions against deforestation  in the Amazonian region (decree nº 6.321/2007 and Ordinance n° 428 (2018) by the Ministry of Environment). The list includes Paragominas and Ulianópolis. 
The deforestation of the amazon forest in the region of the project is due to anthropic activities: timber exploration, pasture for cattle raising and agriculture. The pressure on turning forest into non-forested areas is consequence of the expansion of these economic activities, leading to invasions of private properties. For the project region, the main land use activity is the implementation of pasture for cattle raising. In relation to the social aspects, most of the communities are formed by rural farmers with social vulnerabilities, with presence of food insecurity, low income and lack of job opportunity.
Considering the aspects presented, the Project’s main goals, through conservation of forest areas and combating deforestation of the Amazon Forest, are: 1) To promote adaptations to climate change in the region; 2) To improve the quality of life of the population that lives close to the forest and 3) To conserve biodiversity and ecosystem services, through environmental education actions and foment initiatives to connect forest fragments of the PA.
ccb-4687:
The Tueré REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Brascomp  Compensados do Brasil S.A. and aims to promote forest conservation, maintain carbon stocks and mitigate climate change by reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from land use changes. In addition to  climate benefits, the Project also aims to generate social benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and improving the well-being of surrounding communities, in addition to environmental benefits through actions aimed at the conservation of local fauna and flora.
The Project Area has 135,342 ha of Amazon forest, located in the mesoregion of Marajó, in the municipality of Portel, state of Pará, and is located on the banks of the Anapu and Tueré Rivers. Communities have been identified that are directly or indirectly influenced by the Project, and that are geographically close to the Project Area and depend on its ecosystem services.
ccb-4689: The Ateles REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and AgroSB Agropecuária and aims to promote forest conservation and mitigate climate change by reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from changes in land use. It is made up of a significant part of the Amazon rainforest, located in the municipality of São Félix do Xingú, in the southeast of the state of Pará. The entire project is part of the APA Triunfo do Xingu, a conservation unit with the greatest pressure from deforestation in Brazil, which over the last few decades has suffered major threats to the maintenance of its forest remnants due to large-scale illegal deforestation. Furthermore, the region is of great importance in terms of its biodiversity, as it is located in the Tapajós Endemism Center, a place with a high concentration of rare and endemic species. In addition to climate benefits, the project aims to ensure the conservation and protection of biodiversity and natural resources through mitigating and preventative measures such as strengthening asset surveillance, social inclusion and regional socio-economic development through alternative practices to deforestation and the development and strengthening of value chains, the establishment of a biodiversity conservation program, promoting in situ monitoring of fauna and flora in the Project Area, the development of strategies that seek to bring land security and territorial belonging, as well as the strengthening of local governance, stimulated mainly by the engagement and involvement of stakeholders.
ccb-4690:
The Ningxia 2021-2023 Pengyang Afforestation Project, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region (hereafter as ‘the project’) is located in Pengyang County, Guyuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region of China. The aim of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and to contribute to the local sustainable development by planting the trees and shrubs on the barren mountains and barren land. The project was implemented by Bureau of Natural Resources in Pengyang, who is the proponent of this project (hereafter ‘the project proponent’). The forest is to be established in the project in 10,150 hectares by direct planting various tree and shrub species on barren hills in the selected states. These tree species include Robinia pseudoacacia, Populus hopeiensis, Pinus tabuliformis, Picea, Pinus sylvestris, Red Armeniaca sibirica, Dahurian larch, Salix matsudacernegundo, Acer truncatum, Platycladus orientalis, Pinus bungeana Zucc, Salix matsudana, Chinese Robinia, Robinia, Acer negundoaurea, Ulmus pumila, Armeniaca sibirica, Prunus davidiana, and shrub species involves Shinyleaf Yellowhorn, Hippophae Fructus, Korshinsk Peashrub, Cerasus humilis, Rosa xanthina Lindl and Clove. 
The project is located in the Pengyang County, which covers 12 towns and 3 tree farms, Baiyang Town, Caomiao Town, Chengyang Town, Fengzhuang Town, Gucheng Town, Honghe Town, Jiaocha Town, Luowa Town, Mengyuan Town, Wangwa Town, Xiaocha Town, Xinji Town, Caiyang Town, and Ruhe Tree farm, Caomiao Tree farm, Xiaoyuanzi Tree farm.
The land in the project area was barren mountains and barren land, according to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, there was no natural or secondary forest in the project area. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forest.
The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 3,197,649 tCO2e in 60 years, the average annual emission reduction is 53,294 tCO2e.
ccb-4702: The Chahar Right Rear Banner Improved Grassland Management Project aims to restore degraded grassland ecosystems through grazing management in the project zone. By introducing sustainable grazing practices such as grazing prohibition and grassland-livestock balance, manual restoration measures such as fence building, rodent control, and other sustainable grassland management measures, this project is expected to enhance local carbon sequestration and contribute to the development of local ecosystems. The existing degradation and salinization area accounts for 99.67% of the local grassland. To combat and reverse this degradation, the project proposes to implement improved grassland management across 225,382.93 ha of degraded grassland.
ccb-4714: This project features implementation of rapid rotational grazing practices by dense aggregations of livestock to restore perennial grasses on degraded rangelands across 1.5 million hectares in southern Kenya. These new grazing practices are additional because they differ from the seasonal shifts in grazing activity from wet to dry season ranges and would not be possible without carbon revenues to support governance and monitoring of grazing activities. Rapid rotational grazing will enhance adaptation to climate change by improving soil water holding capacity, increasing surface water availability and providing grass banks as a hedge against drought. Habitat improvement from new grazing practices will restore wildlife corridors between iconic High Conservation Areas such as Serengeti, Kilimanjaro, Nairobi, and Tsavo National Parks and their associated ecosystems and enhance diversity of endemic taxa of plants, birds and insects.
