Second Life is a plastic waste reduction program to recover and recycle ocean, ocean-bound, and land plastic waste. It does this by:
a) Incentivizing the formal and informal waste collectors and recycling agents of islands and remote coastal areas, including municipalities, schools, and volunteers; 
b) Connecting corporate partners with industrial recycling supply chains to ensure reuse and upcycling of plastics recycled, in a fully circular and locally integrated economy; c) Investing in regional recycling initiatives to ensure the increased recycling capacity of materials that would otherwise be disposed of improperly (as defined in PWRM0002) or end up in landfill; and d) Engaging with collectors and communities about waste management and its impacts and teaching them how to mitigate future waste by raising awareness on waste management, collection, and recycling activities. 

The ‘Second Life’ project was initiated by PUR Projet, a Social Enterprise founded in 2008. Operating in 40 countries, PUR Projet specializes in ecosystem regeneration and conservation activities and engaged in sustainable and circular supply chain setup. As an off-spring program of PUR Projet, Second Life benefits from the expertise and support from PUR Projet teams in Thailand for the design, implementation, and monitoring of the project.

Plastic recovery and recycling are done through the Second Life network of aggregators and informal collectors. Each collector willing to join receives a premium per 1 kg of plastics collected of 3,00 THB / kg ($US 0.1) + 2 THB / kg for transport, and 1 THB / kg to the regional collector (aggregator) for monitoring the volumes collected and recycled. This is in addition to the baseline 7 THB / kg of the market price, making previously unprofitable recovery and recycling operations (e.g., on remote islands) now profitable. The project is developed with a longevity of 7 years with the target to cover all Thai areas by 2027, and other SEA countries.
pwrp-2648:
Reciki consists of a systematic approach to tackle the low waste collection rate, high levels of plastic pollution and incipient plastic recovery throughout the locations where it operates- Java and Bali. The model entails implementing material recovery facilities (TPSTs) in selected regencies to enhance the existing local waste management infrastructure, aiming to send zero waste to landfill. The primary plastic waste management is mechanical recycling. The high-value plastic is sorted, baled and sold to large aggregators and/or directly to recyclers, while the hard-to-recycle plastic are repurposed, e.g., into eco-planks and eco-beams. The estimated plastic fraction processed in each facility is on average 19%, of which 60% consists of low-value plastic and 40% high-value plastic. In total, the project expects to recover an average of 15,842 tonnes per year (WCC) across a total of 5 existing and planned facilities. Given the prevalence of the informal waste sector in Indonesia, Reciki provides socially inclusive employment thus improving welfare and social conditions of waste workers (including providing health insurance and basic protective equipment), as well as ensuring strict compliance to anti-child and forced labour policies.

Danone AQUA, as the project proponent, has been incubating Reciki since its inception (May 2020). Reciki now has two facilities implemented: Lamongan since May 2020, and Bali since September 2021. The Reciki- AQUA partnership are among the many initiatives under AQUA’s #BijakBerplastik commitment to ‘recover more plastic than we use’ by 2025. These investments are part of Danone’s broader circular packaging goals, including expansion of reusable packaging (currently, about 70% of AQUA’s business is already fully refillable and circular, through AQUA galon), 50% of our bottles made from recycled content by 2025 and 100% of packaging reusable, recyclable or compostable by 2025.
pwrp-2718:
The Far North Queensland Farm Plastics Project will implement and upscale collection services to remove agricultural waste, specifically composite PE waste, from banana farms in Far North Queensland, Australia. The collection transport service collects plastic waste and delivers it to a suitable end of life destination; being a mechanical recycler or local landfill. Prior to the project start date, there were no efficient or systematic methods of disposal of agricultural waste in Queensland's banana sector, particularly in relation to the recycling of produce-covers, poly-pipe, plastic twine, and other plastic packaging products. This is causing significant issues for farmers, due to high costs of disposal in local landfill facilities as well as increased levies and transportation costs. 

This project will effectively align with existing horticultural activities and will directly reduce the impact of plastic waste entering the Great Barrier Reef, surrounding waterways, landscapes, and the atmosphere of Far North Queensland.
pwrp-2720:
Deekali Plastic Recovery West Africa is a waste reduction program to recover and recycle plastic refuse in different regions of Senegal. The project is developed by Africa Carbon & Commodities (ACC) in coordination with local partners in Senegal.  Located at the most western point of the African continent, Senegal is the gateway to West Africa and as such is key to facilitating the plastic waste reduction program in combatting and finding solutions to the immense amounts of unmanaged plastic refuse in this region.

The goals of the project are:

1. Significantly abate the proliferation of plastic waste in the streets, public places, uncontrolled dumps, landfills, and marine ecosystems in West Africa  
2. Critically reduce the use of virgin plastic by manufacturing companies by providing a market for recycled plastic chips and granules at an affordable price 
3. Create income-generating green jobs in the field of plastic waste recovery and recycling 
4. Educate the population regarding the threat of plastic refuse, its collection and recycling, and alternative solutions to plastic packaging 
5. Create at the household level a plastic waste separation system
pwrp-2783:
An estimated 8 million tons of plastic waste enters our oceans every year. Instead of breaking down, plastic breaks apart into tiny pieces. These fragments end up in the marine food web, posing a major threat to sea life and to human health.

INTERCEPTING PLASTIC WASTE & EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES

The Parley Global Cleanup Network works in collaboration with local groups and governments around the world to remove plastic waste from remote islands, shorelines and waters. It’s never just about cleaning up. Our programs also aim to educate and empower communities, and especially youth, in the movement to end marine plastic pollution.

Utilizing our local Country Coordinators and Parley infrastructure in the Dominican Republic, Maldives and in additional project countries in the future, intercepted material is transported to Parley network facilities for material transformation. The Parley Community Interception program includes full-time employees that collect, transport, sort, and bale plastic material. All employees and stakeholders operate under Parley’s strict Code Of Conduct, focusing on social, economic, and environmental standards.

In the Dominican Republic and Maldives, waste management was largely informal with few formalized institutions. Most formalized institutions did not focus on the sorting of plastics and other recyclable materials, therefore plastics commonly ended up in landfills, incinerators, and the environment.

In order to support a long-term financially-viable recycling model in each country, plastic credits are needed to fund capital and operational expenses. Capital expenses include concept and infrastructure development, general project and country management. Operational expenses include employee salaries and benefits, facilities maintenance, and continued project expansion.
pwrp-2793: In 2017 Starboard, the water sports equipment brand, initiated the world’s first plastic offset program (POP). Starboard know they are guilty of playing a contributing role in the plastic industry but are working towards becoming part of the solution by placing an internal price on plastic-based upon usage. The brand places an internal environmental tax on their profits to fund the program which has grown year on year. The fund pays for the growing team who head out most days of the week to remove plastic from the coastlines in Thailand, the home of Starboard and an area that suffers greatly from plastic pollution.
pwrp-3022: The Project is a post-consumer plastic waste mechanical recycling project owned and operated by IntegriCo Composites Inc. The Project diverts significant quantities of composite plastic waste from landfills across the U.S. for the manufacture of composite timbers that can be used in a variety of applications.
pwrp-3113:
This plastic collection project in Cote d’Ivoire was created by the Conceptos Plásticos company. Conceptos Plásticos is known for the design and manufacture of innovative construction bricks made from plastic waste. They created the Conceptos Plásticos Foundation and developed the WaY (Women and Youth) Methodology. The WaY Methodology establishes a program of support and empowerment for waste pickers.

In the Ivorian cities of Abidjan and Grand Bassam, open dumpsites are proliferating and there is an urgent need to remove plastic waste from the environment. Project participants collect plastic waste from city streets, dumpsites, open land, and beaches. The project also includes a Collection Point where community members and independent plastic collectors are invited to sell their household plastic or plastic collected from the environment. Collected plastic is transported to the Conceptos Plásticos brick manufacturing factory, where it is weighed and recorded. The plastic is formed into durable bricks used to build schools in Cote d’Ivoire. The average amount of plastic waste collected by this project is estimated to be 1,070 tonnes per year. Collected plastic designated unsuitable for plastic brick manufacturing is transported to a controlled landfill.

The project ensures waste pickers are paid above market price for collected materials. Additionally, Conceptos Plásticos Foundation formed a de facto association for female waste pickers to influence the project design and choose redeemable benefits including nutritional kits, cookstoves, and monthly payments to the national health system. Conceptos Plásticos plans to expand the project to include additional waste pickers in Abidjan and other areas in Cote d’Ivoire.
pwrp-3178: Rekart is operating the Waste collection activity in its Northern Railways Division premises and is currently in process of developing it in all other Railway Stations across India. The plastic material of all sorts is collected and transferred to Material Recovery Facility operated by Rekart. The current Project activity is running in Northern Railway premises situated in National Capital Region, India. Rekart innovations Private Limited has installed a Collection model and Material Recovery facility for Indian Railways to collect and deviate the plastic waste from dumping on illegal dumpsites to their proper end destinations i.e Authorized Recyclers and Energy recovery facilities. Rekart started operating its collection and segregation activity from 5th May 2021. Prior to the setup of MRF centre by Rekart, generated waste from railways premises was being dumped with municipal waste or nearest unauthorised dumpsites.
pwrp-3473: Plastic, without doubt, is the miracle commodity that has uses ranging from increasing shelf lives of eatables to medical equipment and automotive. Managing plastic waste requires effective knowledge, not only among those who produce the plastic, but also among those who handle it. The CPCBs annual report says that India has generated an estimated plastic waste of about 34 Lakh tonnes per annum in the year 2019-20 alone, this value has been increasing rapidly for the past decade. Since the documentation of plastic waste is minimal in a country like India, most of the waste generated ends up in the dumping grounds or is left to litter on the roads.
pwrp-3597: The project activity involves collection and mechanical recycling of waste plastics into a high-quality substitute for virgin polymer suitable for use in mainstream products and packaging. pwrp-3647: The program promotes collection, recycling, and reduction of plastic waste. pwrp-3679:
The TerraCycle Global Foundation (“TCGF” or “Foundation”) is registered US 501 (c) 3 charity
with current river waste clean-up operations in Thailand. TCGF was set up in 2018 with grant
from the Pepsico Foundation, to address the extreme volume of waste that flows from
Bangkok’s canals and rivers into the ocean every year. Within the global organization, TCGF
also set up the TerraCycle Thai Foundation (“TCTF” or “Foundation”), which runs the day-to-day
operations in Thailand and includes a Board of Thai citizens. TCTF owns and operates highly
efficient river traps on the tributaries of the Chao Phraya River. The location of these traps
strategically intercepts waste from the canal communities surrounding Bangkok, and also
waste flowing downstream from Northern Thailand.
pwrp-3701:
Kedarnath Shrine is a well-known pilgrimage site in North India situated in the Himalayan hills. It is estimated that annually 1.5 million visitors visit the shrine as part of the sacred Char Dham yatra in the state of Uttarakhand. An estimated min of 110 MT of plastic waste is generated by just the pilgrims/tourists frequenting the track, over a period of just 6 months. The waste generated by commercial establishments is yet unknown. With legacy waste in the environment amounting to more than 400-500 MT the volume of plastic waste is unaccounted for in these difficult terrains
The Nagar panchayat Kedarnath (NP Kedarnath) is a bin-free region (GBPNIHE, 2022), due to which waste generated by consumers and commercial establishments leaks into the environment. With limited door-to-door collection, the waste generated is dumped in the environment, which further leaks into the valleys and rivers
The Clean Kedarnath project, a partnership with the District Administration of Rudraprayag (DAR) and Rapidue Technologies Private Limited (Recykal) addresses the key challenges of plastic waste in the region. Through this project, Recykal intends to enable collection, channelise and process all plastic waste generated in the region to appropriate end destinations. 
These interventions consist of 
1. Enabling waste collection through Digital DRS from source of waste generation (consumer i.e., pilgrims/tourists) while changing consumer behaviour towards waste management
2. Incentivising manual collection of legacy waste or leaked waste in the environment 
3. Setting of up Smart Material Recovery Facilities (SMRF) for collection, sorting, baling and channelising plastic waste to an appropriate end destination 
Consideration of plastic credits has been a key driver to this program for incentivization, making operations sustainable and ultimately diverting plastic waste from landfills, water bodies and mountains in these areas which are considered very sacred by the community at large
pwrp-3704: The Hub for Circular Economy of Plastic Residue Project is a plastic waste recycling project implemented by Modix Plastique Inc. The Project will recycle plastic waste sourced in Canada, with the bulk of the plastic waste coming from Quebec and smaller volumes coming from Ontario and other Canadian provinces. The waste is sourced from local sorting centres, non-profit organisations, agriculture, and other local industry that are outside of the Project’s scope. The plastic waste that arrives on site consists of waste Low Density Polyethylene (LDPE), Linear Low-Density Polyethylene (LLDPE), and trace amounts of Polypropene (PP) that will be recycled into new high-quality LDPE and LLDPE resins. The waste plastics are granted a second life as resins, as they can be used as a raw material by various plastic producers, which displaces virgin plastics. The Project will reduce the amount of plastic that ends up in landfills or the broader environment and will thereby contribute to a cleaner environment.
pwrp-3744:
The project deploys a holistic waste management approach to address irregular low value plastic collection, high marine plastic pollution and under-developed plastic waste management infrastructure across villages in Kerala. The grouped project is a collaboration between rePurpose Global, the project developer, and Green Worms, the project implementer. 

As per the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules 2016, the Kerala state government is entrusted with the preparation and implementation of a SWM policy in coordination with various stakeholders. Since these rules are complex, vague and do not put the implementation onus completely on any one entity, there is sporadic implementation of the rules in the state. The rules postulate that LSGs are tasked with the constitutional responsibility to manage solid waste. However, of the 131,400 tonnes of plastic waste annually generated in Kerala, only 3% gets collected, sorted and sold to recyclers and aggregators. Additionally, with only 47% of the households participating in the formal collection program, uncollected plastics are often openly burned or dumped in public spaces, low lying lands and water bodies. 

Project Hara Kal will thus use plastic credit financing to establish an end-to-end value chain by subsidizing the collection and end-of-life management of close to 497,955 tonnes of uncollected ocean- and nature-bound plastics. The project aims to: 
1. Establish Public Private Partnerships with village administrative bodies - Local Self Government institutions called Panchayats;
2. Engage the services of the collection staff, Haritha Karma Sena in each village or individual project location; and
3. Operate and manage project activities and infrastructures across the waste value chain. This includes sorting and baling activities at GW’s Material Recovery Facilities and transportation of low value recyclable plastic to recyclers and hard to recycle plastics to cement kilns for co-processing.
pwrp-3796: The plastic collection and recycling activity facilitated by Prakash Industries aims to recycle plastic waste and scale up the recycling activities in the city of Madhya Pradesh, India. It has a streamlined process of collecting and sorting of various types of Plastic wastes, to produce recycled plastic products. The production capacity of the project is 27,375 Tonnes/year.
pwrp-3838:
The “Plastic Waste Recycling & Improving Waste Picker Livelihoods in Kenya” project is a grouped plastic waste reduction activity developed and coordinated by TakaTaka Solutions1 Ltd (TTS). This project (hereafter referred to as TTS Plastic Waste Recycling Program, or the TTS PWRP) aims to recover and recycle additional plastic waste throughout the host country of Kenya. The project will both collect and recycle additional plastics.
TTS will source additional plastics from three avenues: informal waste collectors, collection and sorting from commercial and residential clients, and on-site collection from factory clients producing plastic waste. TTS will recycle the collected plastics at its recycling plants equipped to handle additional, “hard-to-recycle” plastics, located near Nairobi, Kenya.

pwrp-3964:
The ASASE Foundation project is a community-based plastic waste collection and recycling project established in Ghana in 2019.  The project involves starting small recycling plants as social enterprises in communities where plastic pollution is most severe, and empowering women entrepreneurs to build their own plastic waste collection businesses as a sustainable source of income and employment.
Networks of waste pickers collect PP, LDPE, HDPE and PET from numerous sources including households, businesses, schools, markets and landfill. The collected waste is transported to ASASE’s collection centres and warehouses for aggregation.  All sorting is conducted in the warehouses, from where it is transferred to ASASE’s Cash It! plants for washing and processing into shred and pellets.
pwrp-4017:
In November 2020 VeryNile started to collaborate with local fishermen along the river Nile undertaking plastic waste collection activities. Prior to the project activity, there was no waste collection along the river Nile ongoing. Source Reuters
The collection area ranges from 10km north of Warraq Island to 10km South of Qursaya Island. Due to the disappearance of fish in the river, this marginalized community of fishermen (30% literacy rate) is suffering from a decrease in revenue and living conditions. “Fishing” for plastic waste tackles not only an environmental problem but also a socio-economic one.
All fishermen working with VeryNile are registered in a database and provided with an ID card verifying them as Nile plastic collectors. (list of fishermen)
VeryNile procures the collected plastic waste from the fishermen and processes it (weighing, sorting and compacting/bailing by plastic waste type) before it gets sent to the mechanical recycling facility of BariQ (clear PET), where it gets pelletized (end-of-life destination #1) and eventually sent to Spain to be transformed into yarns under the SeaQual label which verifies that the plastic was collected from marine environments.
The non-recyclable plastic waste such as MLP/low-value plastics gets sold to CEMEX, a global construction materials company (MLP for waste to energy) where it gets co-processed as an alternative to using fossil-fuel energy (end-of-life destination #2 – 4.1. Plastic Waste Collection Methodology).
All activities were documented manually. Incoming and outgoing materials get weighed (dry) and are documented. Purchasing and sales receipts can be provided. In a joint project with Takatari, VeryNile will establish a digital data collection system (project start 09/2022).

On average ~187 metric tons/year get collected
pwrp-4024: The project undertaken by M/s Badri Cotsyn Pvt. Ltd. manufactures recycled polyester fibre from Waste PET Bottles and Polyester lumps. The Project focuses on collecting and recycling the Post consumer PET waste that is being recovered from many states of India. The Post consumer PET waste includes the wastewater bottles, beverage packing and food packages. This waste is brought into the recycling facility by various collecting agencies, who work inline with Badri group for a singular purpose. The capacity of the project activity is 150Tonnes per day. The by-product of the recycling activity would then be used in the technical textiles and clothing industries. The Recycled polyester fibre having the same properties of PET is highly durable and further recyclable.
pwrp-4054: The plastic collection and recycling activity is facilitated by BLS Ecotech Ltd, located at SP12, RIICO Industrial Area, Keshwana, Kotputli, Dist.: Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. pwrp-4092: The project activity involves collection and mechanical recycling of plastic wastes. The type of waste that is generated at residential, commercial, corporate & overall city level is in mixed form & is very different from what a plastic recycler requires as a raw material for processing.NEPRA develops and operates Material Recovery Facility (MRF) in Public Private Partnership (PPP) model with Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ Municipal Corporation where mixed dry waste is received from ULBs/Municipal Corporation. The waste is sorted into plastic waste (from the mixed solid waste) which then goes into recycling.
pwrp-4093: GemCorp Recycling & Technologies Private Limited is implementing large-scale mechanical recycling projects in India to address the systemic gap in formal recycling infrastructure prevalent in developing economies. These initiatives recycle LDPE, HDPE, PP, and other plastic polymers that would otherwise be landfilled, openly burned, or leak into the environment, reintroducing them into the value chain as high-quality recycled material. By replacing virgin plastic, the projects reduce greenhouse gas emissions, conserve resources, and deliver measurable environmental benefits, while also generating social co-benefits by integrating informal waste reclaimers into structured, safe, and fairly compensated roles. Operating beyond business-as-usual practices in a region with limited recycling infrastructure, GemCorp ensures that all outcomes are additional, quantifiable, and verifiable in alignment with international plastic crediting methodologies.
pwrp-4133:
Pure North Recycling (hereafter called PNR) is a plastic waste reduction and recycling project located in Iceland. PNR's main mandate is collecting plastic waste from land-based sources in an efficient and environmentally conscious way. This is achieved in the following ways:

- Utilizing geothermal energy and hot water for the cleaning and recycling of plastic waste in PNR’s recycling facility in Hveragerði, Iceland.

- Increasing the scale of operations incrementally in order to handle more volume of plastic waste to recycle, which will inevitably result in less plastic being exported out of Iceland.

- Connecting with companies, waste aggregators and other entities, supporting their ambitions to recycle responsibly through the PNR project and presenting a locally integrated circular solution in order to move closer to a sustainable society.
pwrp-4135:
Launched in 2017 by Borealis and Systemiq, Project STOP works with cities to create effective waste management systems that eliminate leakage of plastics into the ocean. Project STOP also aims to create circular systems where the majority of hard-to-recycle waste is recycled into new products and the resulting economic value lowers the financial burden of the waste system on the city, permanently reduce ocean plastic leakage while opening social and economic benefits for communities.
Furthermore, the STOP team supports cities with technical expertise and skills transfer, funding and sustained implementation support. Insights and approaches are shared globally, magnifying impact.
Launched in 2017, our first city partnership is in Muncar, a coastal fishing community located in Banyuwangi, Indonesia. Project STOP has since expanded its reach to the city of Pasuruan in East Java and Jembrana in Bali and is now expanding its program to the entire Banyuwangi Regency.
Project STOP uses a system-enabler approach in which a team of experts in waste management, recycling, financing and education help a city design and implement a low-cost waste management system in which all households and institutions benefit from collection, and plastics are kept out of the environment. The team supports cities with investment, technical expertise, waste system design, project management, skills transfer, behaviour change and recycling/reprocessing valorisation.
Project STOP does not own the waste nor operates collection, sortation, recycling, treatment or landfill business.
pwrp-4181: The Plastic Recycling Activity facilitated and implemented by Aero Fibre Private Limited (Operation now owned by RIbotl Solution Pvt Ltd) aims to recycle plastic waste in the city of Silvassa, Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli & Daman & Diu, India. The project involves mechanical recycling of scrap PET bottles to manufacture PET flakes (Hot Washed) and HDPE Granules. The project activity anticipates recycling of post-consumer PET waste annually, sourced from multiple states across India and produce around 18480 tonnes of PET flakes and 7500 tonnes of HDPE granules annually.
pwrp-4199:
The project concerns the manual collection and management of mismanaged plastic waste from community-coastal and river natural environments in the region of  Batam, one of the islands in the Riau Archipelago, Indonesia.
 
The current situation in Batam is that several areas, especially the coastal slums, do not have access to, or receive, adequate waste management services, causing the locals and households to litter or directly dump household waste into the sea. As a result, excessive debris is accumulating in the open environment, such as under their homes, in neighbourhoods, and in rivers - polluting the environment and causing significant health risks to the families in these communities.

This project encompasses the design, mobilisation and implementation of clean-up activities and waste management activities carried out by formally-hired and trained local community members (“Clean-up Crew”) by the project proponent.

The collection will be undertaken from most community-based sites, i.e. manual collection by the crew member and out into bags for later sorting and weighing. In addition, the plastic waste collection activities will include boat-based methods in the river, river barriers, and household collection in 2023. Moreover, while the non-recyclables will be transported to a sanitary landfill and/or waste-to-energy (e.g. RDF) later in 2023, the recyclables will be sent to a Material Recycling Facility. 

This project will issue Plastic Credits to fund the necessary program investment and daily operational costs, such as setting up proper waste collection infrastructure, waste management and logistics, and decent compensations for the formally-hired workers, such as living wage salary, health insurance, education and training program, and many more.
pwrp-4257: The plastic recycling activity facilitated by PK Industries aims to recycle plastic waste and scale up the recycling activities in the Indore District of Madhya Pradesh, India. It has a streamlined process of sorting & recycling various types of plastic wastes, to produce recycled plastic granules. The recycled goods will then be sold to local traders which are later sold to retailers. The production capacity of the project is 2,400 Tonnes/Year.
pwrp-4431:
GreenCollar is working with experienced Ghanaian NGO, Environment 360 to mobilise the informal waste sector in Ghana by scaling up investment in the infrastructure needed to collect and process plastic waste. The Project aims to incentivise the waste picker community to safely collect PET, HDPE, PP and PET from the environment and deliver it to a 'Pod'. Pods consists of a secure community collection site and processing centre. At each collection site, material is aggregated, sorted, and checked for contaminants, before being sent to a processing centre where HDPE, PET and PP is mechanically recycled. HDPE is then remanufactured onsite. Recycled PET and PP is on sold to local manufacturing organisations. LDPE, due to its low value will be cleaned and dried and sent directly to a local engineered landfill. The Project will scale up this piloted Pod concept, throughout Ghana to increase collection and recycling of plastic waste and drive investment in the recycling infrastructure to support it. The Project aims to deliver a range of social co-benefits, particularly for participating waste pickers. As part of the training program, waste pickers will undergo health and safety programs, financial literary training, and child labour mitigation education. The Project began in March 2023 and will run for seven years with an option to extend.
The Project will scale up this piloted Pod concept, throughout Ghana to increase collection and recycling of plastic waste and drive investment in the recycling infrastructure to support it. 

The Project aims to deliver a range of social co-benefits, particularly for participating waste pickers. As part of the training program, waste pickers will undergo health and safety programs, financial literary training, and child labour mitigation education.

The Project began in March 2023 and will run for seven years with an option to extend.
pwrp-4432:
Upsyde Netherlands has developed an innovative mechanical recycling project to produce durable goods from Hard-to-Recycle plastic waste deploying a patented Waste-to-Part technology. After ten years of research and development, the technology has been scaled up to industrial production. Upsyde's factory, located in Weert, Netherlands, produces pallets, heavy-duty mats, and road plates. 

The project activity was established in 2017 and sources its plastic waste from the Process Losses of Conventional Mechanical Recycling facilities that cannot be efficiently transformed into high-quality post-consumer recycled material. Typically, this Hard-to-Recycle plastic waste would be directed to incineration or landfill due to its low quality and lack of economic viability for recycling. Upsyde's technology addresses this challenge by efficiently transforming the Hard-to-Recycle plastic waste into durable, reusable, and recyclable products. 

By utilizing the Process Losses from Conventional Recycling facilities, Upsyde enhances the efficiency of plastic waste recovery. The mechanical recycling process employed by Upsyde also contributes to a more resource-efficient production process by avoiding the use of virgin plastic. 

Since May 2017, Upsyde has recycled 14.411 tonnes of Hard-to-Recycle plastic waste. The estimated additional amount of plastic waste to be recycled by the project activity from May 2017 to April 2024 is 19.891 tonnes, averaging 2.841 tons per year. 

The project's aim is to scale up production, divert more plastic waste from incineration and landfill, and contribute to a circular economy. The revenue generated from plastic credits will support Upsyde in increasing production volume, developing new products and technologies, transitioning to cleaner energy sources, and potentially investing in equipment and facilities. This will help Upsyde enhance its goal of promoting sustainable plastic waste management.
pwrp-4438: The project has a whole process of collecting, sorting, and recycling materials containing high-density polyethylene (HDPE), low-density polyethylene (LDPE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), and others. Ecopositiva sources plastic waste from formal collectors’ associations, their own collectors' personnel, and collection centers or events for companies established as their clients. Ecopositiva has a fleet of vehicles and partner transporters that bring the material to the recycling plants in Bogotá and Barranquilla, Colombia. Finally, the recycled plastics are sold to third parties to produce shoes, hoses, and bags.
pwrp-4470:
The “Agents of Change: Orchestrating the Recycling Chain” project (AGENTS OF CHANGE) is a proposal to reduce plastic waste in Brazil by including and valuing the recycling chain agents (scrap buyers, waste pickers, and others). The products collected in this project are primarily single-use post-consumer plastic waste (disposable packages) and recycling products that are plastic materials in the form of decontaminated extruded pellets, in addition to ground or flaked byproducts, usually shipped in big bags. For this project, the 2016-2022 timeframe was set to claim 107,040 plastic credits in the first crediting period. This quantity was based on the average amount of collected and recycled waste of 15,291.46 t/year, with 17,380.05 tonnes of plastic waste being collected (2,482.86 t/year on average) and 89,660.19 tonnes of plastic waste being recycled (12,808.60 t/year on average).

The goal of AGENTS OF CHANGE is to increase the collection of plastic waste to be reintroduced in the production chain through mechanical recycling. So, this material’s energetic potential can be recovered through sorting and logistic efficiency, promoting the circular economy and fostering sustainable development. The plastic credits claimed by this project, taking Brazil’s social, economic, and environmental diversity into account, will maximize the demand for recyclable plastic waste, enabling investment in infrastructure for the supply chain, availability of work and safety equipment, and qualification programs for various recycling chain agents, which will lead to greater engagement from these agents and more income from their activities; and they will maximize actions that contribute to providing these professionals with decent work, good health, and well-being, as well as improved environmental quality, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals, preventing this waste from being left in improper places, where it compromises quality of life and biodiversity.
pwrp-4471:
Project Laut Yang Tenang employs a unique, entrepreneur-driven waste management model to check and manage environment-bound plastic pollution in Indonesia. The project promotes recovery of recyclable flexible plastics and channels it to ethical end destinations whilst also creating dignified livelihood opportunities for informal waste collectors. This grouped project is a collaboration between rePurpose Global (rPG), the project developer, and Waste4Change (W4C), the project implementer. 

In Indonesia, a deficient municipal collection system compounded with the lack of sufficient waste sorting facilities and sanitary landfills results in mismanagement of 70% of annual generated waste. In the absence of a sustained formal collection system, the informal sector steps in and is responsible for driving most of the plastic recovery in the country. The project mobilises this existing workforce to recover LDPE and HDPE plastic bags and channel it towards recycling.Through the collection of over 85,000 tons of environment-bound plastic, the project aims to 1) operate and manage project activities and infrastructures across the waste value chain that includes collection activities, pre-treatment at primary processing centers and transportation of recyclable plastic to recyclers; 2) upskill informal waste suppliers by supporting them to improve their operations with improved safety and social compliances; 3) empower private material recovery facility operators via a franchise model to source and manage environment-bound recyclable plastic waste; and 4) identify ethical recyclers for recycling of the collected plastic waste.
pwrp-4491:
The project, Adding value to waste via Recycling - by Jainarain Fabtech Private Limited (JNF), began in 2016, with a vision to work towards a sustainable future and hence are progressive and inventive in their field of work. JNF is a plastics recycling facility located in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, India. They primarily deal with post-consumer PET plastic waste which is recycled into Recycled Polyester Staple Fibre (RPSF), used in the textile industry. 
The PET waste in the environment is diverted through local waste collectors, traders, and aggregators all over India, who are associated with JNF in the plastic waste collection process. The sourced material is channelized to the recycling facility through transporters where it is further sorted, and mechanically recycled into RPSF within the facility as per the Global Recycling Standard (GRS) (Appendix 8.14), the RPSF produced as an end result is sold to textile manufacturing industries. The facility began with a capacity of 60 MT/day and with further modifications and additions, the running total installed capacity was 88MT/day in 2017. Considering the need for increasing the rate of recycling, the facility was upgraded to 120 MT/day on August 23rd, 2021. The company is planning to further expand its capacity by 30MT/day, which will increase the capacity to 150 MT/day in 2023, to manufacture Recycled Polyester Staple Fibre (RPSF) through the recycling of post-consumer PET bottles. The project, on average, has & will recycle to produce 11431 MT of RPSF from PET waste annually.
pwrp-4521: The project pertains to plastic waste collection and recycling. The type of plastic which is collected and recycled is PET. In this project, the PET plastic waste, collected from all over Nepal, is supplied by the balers (plastic waste collectors) exclusively to Ganesha Overseas’s recycling plant in ‘Naval Parasi, Bhairahwa, Nepal’. This PET waste is then processed through mechanical recycling to form the recycled PET flakes and chips. These recycled products are sold to the manufacturers who produce recycled PET fibre which is subsequently used to manufacture various products such as ‘Tote Bags’, ‘T-Shirts’. ‘Upholstery’ etc.
pwrp-4594: UCC Recycling is Mexican plastic recycling company located in Nogales, Mexico. UCC Recycling recovers and recycles a wide variety of plastic materials, focusing on the maquiladora industry which is rapidly growing in Northern Mexico. In Nogales alone, there are over 100 manufacturing plants that employ about 34,000 people, and these industries produce a significant amount of plastic waste. Our company targets these companies, collecting, separating, and eventually mechanically recycling the plastic waste that they produce, so that it can be resold and reused. Prior to our company, most of the plastic waste from the maquiladoras was incinerated, posing numerous risks to local inhabitants and the environment. The plastic material we recycle includes but is not limited to: bottles and small rigid plastics (grades 1-7), MRF film, HDPE natural bottles, mixed bulky rigids, PET thermoforms, HDPE injection bulky rigids, polypropylene rigid plastic, PE retails mix film, LDPE colored film, LDPE furniture mix, agricultural ground cover film, rigid PVC, and flexible PVC. Our business is integral in the transition towards a circular economy, as we secure sustainable raw materials.
pwrp-4610: Project Ekonomia ya Bluu facilitates the recovery and recycling of environment-bound plastic waste in Kenya, while simultaneously benefitting formal and informal waste workers associated with the project activities. Of the total plastic waste generated in Kenya, only 27% gets collected, largely sourced by the informal sector. 8% of this collected waste gets recycled and the remaining 19% usually gets disposed of in unsanitary landfills or dumpsites. This effectively equates to 92% of plastic waste being mismanaged - either openly burnt, dumped on land or in water bodies. It is estimated that plastic packaging such as polypropylene (PP), polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyester make up most of the plastic waste generated in the country. This project will use plastic credit financing to incentivize informal waste pickers, aggregators and community-based organizations to recover mismanaged, recyclable plastic waste from dump and litter sites and channel the same towards recycling. This grouped project is jointly developed and managed by Rintz Industries Limited and rePurpose Global. PP plastic waste is purchased at market rates from waste aggregators working in and around Mombasa dumpsites and brought to the Rintz Primary Processing Center for sorting. The sorted material is then transported to the recycler - Vintz Plastics’ - Material Recovery Facility in Nairobi - where it is processed for recycling. The project intends to collect approximately 112,000 tonnes of plastics and recycle approximately 88,272 tonnes of recyclable plastics, across a 10-year crediting period starting 01 January 2024.
pwrp-4636:
The Company will manufacture Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) material washed chips and Polyester Staple Fibre (PSF) (Solid Fibre & Hollow Fibre). The whole set of equipments will be used to produce solid or conjugated hollow polyester staple fibre with PET bottle flakes recycled as materials, adopting the technology of drawing, crimping, drying, cutting and baling. It consists of main processing line.The company's strategy of recycling plastic waste is an intentional step towards a sustainable future that also seeks to promote the principles of reducing, reusing, and recycling throughout the plastics sector. Fairer prices, health safety training, and appropriate protective gear will be given to the waste pickers and kabadiwalas involved in this intervention. Additionally, the funds generated through this project activity will aid in scaling up the collection and recycling activities in India, which will consequently affect various small-scale waste pickers' ability to network with larger organisations. 
The project plans to recycle about 18,000 tonnes of post-consumer PET trash annually that is gathered from different Indian states
pwrp-4678:
Dodhia Synthetics Ltd. is deeply committed, to addressing the implications of waste through 
its innovative plastic recycling project Located at Block No. 214 Plot No. 1 to 38 Survey No. 
273 near Darbar Hotel in the Vill; Motaborasara region, Ta; Mangrol, Dist; Surat, the 
company has established a state of the art recycling facility.
This facility is solely dedicated to recycling plastic waste with a focus on PET bottles. By 
utilizing cutting edge technology, Dodhia Synthetics Ltd. efficiently transforms discarded 
bottles into quality recycled PET flakes. These flakes are then processed further to produce 
Polyester Partially Oriented Yarn (POY) which finds applications in sectors such as 
beverages, sheets, films and textiles.
The driving force behind this initiative stems from the need to divert bottles away from their 
detrimental fate in landfills. The disposal of PET bottles has become a pressing concern due, 
to their degradation and subsequent adverse environmental impacts. Dodhia Synthetics 
Ltd.’s initiative aims to disrupt this cycle by intercepting bottles from the waste stream and 
reimagining them as resources.
pwrp-4682:
The project represents a capacity addition plan to Wise Plásticos’ mechanical recycling facility in Brazil, that processes High-Density Polyethylene (“HDPE”) and Polypropylene (“PP”) plastic waste. It promotes circularity through the development and production of high-quality recycled polymer resins, which can effectively replace virgin plastics across various segments and applications. Wise has been pioneering a transformation of the plastics recycling market, with strong R&D, technology improvements, continuous capacity increase, and innovative partnerships with the various actors of the value chain. 

To be properly decontaminated, these polyolefins require rigorous sorting and washing processes, and the lack of effective recycling technologies prior to the project implementation – necessary to reach high-end applications, such as consumer goods -, limited the market demand mostly to lower-end applications. As a result of the low value, a significant portion of HDPE and PP plastic waste was sent to landfills or improperly disposed, contributing to the country's low overall recycling rate. To secure reliable, steady, and continuous supply of feedstock, Wise has been defining new models of investments and partnerships with plastic waste suppliers. It also partners with several key stakeholders to secure demand for high-quality recycled plastics, via development of new technology-driven practices and the establishment of transparent long-term commercial relationships. 

From 2019 until 2025, the project implementation results in 101,815 estimated net recycled plastic waste (tonnes), an average amount of recycled waste of 14,545 tonnes/year. Plastic credits are a propitious financial instrument to support scaling up the recycling of plastic waste, and its revenue will be an enabler of Wise’s continuous investments in capacity addition, that will keep raising demand for high-quality recycled resins that can increasingly displace virgin plastics from the market.
pwrp-4688:
ATKASAN was established in 1996 in İzmir,Turkey. ATKASAN operates actively in waste recycling in Turkey's İzmir, Manisa, and Ankara provinces. In 2018, ATKASAN acquired the recycling license. The company collects LDPE, PP, PET, and other specified plastic types, converting LDPE plastics into raw materials to contribute to the economy. The project's aim is to minimize environmental damage through plastic waste collection and recycling, fostering a more sustainable future.

In 2021, the Regulation on the Control of Packaging Waste was enacted by the Turkish Ministry of Environment and Urbanization. However, with the implementation of this regulation, the financial support mechanism for source separation services previously carried out by municipalities and supported by the government has been abolished. As a result, the recycling of recyclable waste has been hindered or even prevented, leading to outcomes such as being taken to landfill sites designated by municipalities, being piled up, buried, or incinerated.

Following the enactment of this regulation, ATKASAN developed a project to integrate waste collection activities with municipalities and also contribute to waste collection by purchasing from chain supermarkets. These collection efforts from supermarkets also aim to raise societal environmental awareness. Additionally, through its project, ATKASAN supported the formation of cooperatives among street collectors. These cooperatives, consisting of Turkish citizens and refugees from different countries such as Syria, Iraq, and Afghanistan who have migrated to Turkey out of necessity, have goals such as improving the living standards of street collectors, increasing their welfare, taking measures to prevent crime and diseases, and contributing to societal harmony.Its efforts also aid in supporting vulnerable groups and increasing societal well-being. ATKASAN seeks to apply for collection and recycling credits for LDPE plastics and collection credits for plastics.
pwrp-4700:
Ganesha Ecosphere Ltd. is at the forefront of addressing the critical issue of plastic waste management through its pioneering plastic recycling project. Situated in a state-of-the-art facility at Gata no. 112, Village Temra, Tehsil Bilaspur, District Rampur, Uttar Pradesh. the company has undertaken a remarkable endeavor. 
This initiative has expanded its recycling capacity significantly, adding 72 Tons Per Day (TPD) to its existing capacity 128 TPD for wash Line, exclusively dedicated to the recycling of plastic waste, with a special emphasis on PET bottles. By harnessing cutting-edge technology, Ganesha Ecosphere Ltd. effectively transforms discarded PET bottles into premium quality recycled PET flakes. These flakes undergo further processing to yield Recycled Polyester Staple Fibre (RPSF), a versatile material applied across various sectors, including textiles, automotive, and construction. 
This project activity finds its roots in the urgent need to divert PET bottles from their detrimental path, diverting them from landfills, where their degradation precipitates severe environmental repercussions. Ganesha Ecosphere Ltd.'s mission is to disrupt this harmful cycle by intercepting PET bottles within the waste stream and reimagining them as valuable resources. In doing so, the company is actively contributing to a more sustainable and environmentally responsible future.
pwrp-4722: RePL - Plastic Waste Reduction Program aims to collect and recycle marine, coastal, and inland plastic waste in the Asian region. H201. operates the program in partnership with waste collection and recycling specialists, local governments, carbon experts, international organizations, NGOs, accounting firms, investment institutions, etc.
pwrp-4726:
Jia Ming Plastic Manufacturing (JMPM) is a plastics collection and recycling company located in the Gabon Special Economic Zone (GSEZ). 
GSEZ is Gabon’s first special economic zone a joint venture between the Government of Gabon and ARISE IIP.  As a pan-african developer of industrial ecosystems, ARISE IIP conceives, finances, develops and exploits industrial zones across Africa. The first industrial zone of the group was developed in 2011 in Gabon and is centered mainly around timber manufacturing. Over 1100 hectares are dedicated the transformation of logs into timber finished products. 
In addition to bringing additional economic value to Gabon, GSEZ is also taking significant steps to improve its environmental footprint: JMPM is one initiative settled in the industrial zone that allows considerable CO2 emissions reduction. 
JMPM activity consists in collecting plastic bottles and recycling them into straps that are then used to package the timber products manufactured in the zone before being exported. This allows for numerous positive externalities:
-	Import substitution: timber industries that were initially importing straps from China are now buying straps in a short circuit, just few meters away from their industry. Those straps were mainly imported from China 
-	Plastic waste reduction: by installing collection points in several areas, JMPM prevents plastics from being dumped open air or incinerated as it is currently practiced in the country. 
-	Circular economy: By producing straps out of waste, JMPM is creating a virtuous circle shifting from a linear economy to a circular one that allows a reduction in oil dependency.
Jia Ming Plastic manufacturing (JMPM) is settled in GSEZ since 2019 and is the only plastic recycling company of  Gabon. Currently, JMPM purchases plastic waste in Libreville from 20 providers and has an average monthly recycling capacity of 22.5 tons of plastic in Gabon, capturing less than 1% of the country's waste.
pwrp-4735:
The project activity recycles plastic waste into usable products for further processing in manufacturing industries and new products that have a wide variety of applications. The quality of the recycled plastic waste is suitable for it to be used as feedstock in the manufacture of recycled products, thereby displacing the use of virgin plastics. The plastic waste is collected through various sources, such as municipal bodies, scrap traders and industries.
The proposed project activity is a capacity addition to an existing recycling activity of 50,000 tonnes/year to 250,000 tonnes/year. The project is implemented and owned by Enviro Recyclean Private Limited. The project activity is located in Indore, Madhya Pradesh.
pwrp-4737:
Unsustainable waste treatment in uncontrolled dumpsites is a growing problem in Mozambique. Agua Pet through its Plastic waste collection and recycling project aims to benefits the local communities by creating employment opportunities at various stages, including waste collection, sorting, processing, and manufacturing of recycled plastic products. The project helps stimulate local economies and provide livelihoods for individuals in the recycling sector.
The Recycling Activity is carried out at Av. Das Indústrias, Maputo, Mozambique. Whereas the plastic waste is collected by the rag pickers from different sources like Dumpsites, Kiosks, Tourism spots. The majority of the plastic waste is being collected from the Hulen Dump yard, Chumen dump yard and from the beaches of Praia da Costa do Sol. Major share of the recycled plastic waste is collected and sorted by the traders and waste aggregators on behalf of Agua Pet Reciclagem Lda. 
The current recycling capacity of project activity is about 24 TPD. The Collection capacity of the project activity is 15 TPD.
pwrp-4738:
Alliance Fibres Limited is a pioneering plastic waste recycling company dedicated to addressing the growing environmental concerns surrounding PET bottles. Located at Block No. 203 & 208, Plot No.1,2,7 & 8, MotaBorasara, Kim, Tal - Mangrol, Dist. Surat, Gujarat (INDIA) – 394110, the mission of the company is to lead the way in sustainable recycling practices. Alliance Fibres specialize in the recycling of PET bottles, transforming them into high-quality Partially Oriented Yarn (POY), Recycled Polyester Staple Fibre (RPSF) and Rope. By doing so, company not only reduces the harmful impact of plastic waste on our environment but also contributes to the development of eco-friendly products.
Alliance Fibres Limited operates an advanced recycling facility equipped with state-of-the-art technology. This facility efficiently transforms PET bottles into POY, RPSF, and Rope. The company is dedicated to sustainability, extending beyond recycling. Their goal is to establish a closed-loop system that minimizes waste and optimizes resource usage. These products have diverse applications in industries like textiles, packaging, and construction, encouraging the adoption of recycled materials and reducing the need for new plastics.
This programme was motivated by the desire to keep bottles out of landfills, where they might otherwise end up doing harm. Due to the breakdown of PET bottles and the associated negative effects on the environment, their disposal has become an urgent issue. The effort by Alliance Fibres Ltd. seeks to break this cycle by removing bottles from the waste stream and repurposing them as resources.
pwrp-4740: VERDE POLYSFY PLASTIC RECYCLING PROJECT  implemented by Verde Polysfy Private Limited (VPPL) is a plastic recycling facility located in Giridih, Jharkhand, India. The project activity receives post-consumer PET plastic waste, which is recycled into Recycled Polyester Staple Fibre (RPSF), to be used in the textile industry. The Polyethylene Terephthalate - PET waste in the environment is diverted through local waste collectors, traders and aggregators in the region, who are associated with VPPL in the plastic waste collection process. The sourced material is channelized to the recycling facility through transporters where it is further sorted, and mechanically recycled into RPSF within the facility. The RPSF produced as an end result is sold to textile manufacturing industries. The facility began with a capacity of 40 MT/day. The project, on an average, has & will recycle to produce 40MT/day of RPSF from PET waste annually.
pwrp-4762: The project is a capacity addition and technology improvement of an existing recycling facility. The plastic waste is sorted in the collection sites and then send to MAYCO’s improved facility in Manizales, Colombia. The main actors of this process are of course the local workers in the recycling plant, as well as the collection companies who provide agricultural, post-industrial, and post-consumption plastic waste to MAYCO.
pwrp-4786:
The ‘Plastic waste recycling by Van Werven, Sweden' project recycles rigid or hard-to-recycle bulky plastic in Sexdrega, Sweden, and began in 2021. This project, hereafter referred to as
“the project”, aims to recover and recycle additional plastic waste throughout the host country of Sweden. Rigid plastics are mainly collected from municipalities (i.e. bulky household material), waste collectors and waste sorting companies for construction as well as building and demolition waste. The plastic is then sorted, washed, grinded and sold as flakes to the European plastics industry instead of being incinerated or sent to landfill. The type of mixed rigid plastics recycled by Van Werven were recycled at a very low rate in the country before the existence of the project. The project recycles bulky plastic items which are currently barely recycled in Sweden due to imitations in recycling capacity.
pwrp-4797: Exxel Polymers inc. (Exxel hereafter) is a Quebec-based company created in 2003 to fill a gap in the market with regards to industrially-sourced plastic waste recovery (historically destined to landfill or incineration) and recycling. The company diverts industrial waste plastics and produces by extrusion a wide range of plastic-based resins. Various types of resins are produced to meet the needs of Exxel’s clients, which will have various  end uses spanning basic commodity-level products through to high engineering-output quality.  Exxel produces a wide range of resins, from commodity resin to engineering resin. For each of the projects entrusted to us, we create a customized, tested, and certified (COA) formulation (compounding). Having started with a 600 ft2 recycling facility in the small town of St-Bruno in the Montérégie region, it then rapidly expanded, relocating to the town of Bromont where it acquired a run-down former printing facility which was subsequently remodelled to Exxels’ business objectives. The 30,000 ft2 facility 5 years later and 75,000 ft2 by 2012 with the installation of a 1st extrusion  line. This expansion was justified considering the amount of recycled plastics which Exxel Polymers has been able to produce thereafter, from just under 2 million kg in 2013 to 8-9 million kg in  2020. A second extrusion line was installed in 2013 and a 3rd one at the end of 2015, marking the start of the Project crediting period in 2016. The project covers the activities from 2016 to december 2022 (Figure 1), a period during which significant changes occurred affecting the recycling capability of the company, including the installation of a 4th extrusion line in 2019 and a 5th one in 2020. These latest 2015 additions have increased the theoretical recycling capacity dramatically, from 470 kg/hr (extrusion line 1) to 1320 kg/hr (extrusion line 3), quasi doubling output of recycled plastic products from 2.8 tons/yr to 5.5 tons/yr for 2016.
pwrp-4805:
The SEArcular project is a plastic waste collection and recycling project established in Surabaya, Indonesia in 2018.  The project empowers coastal communities by providing training, employment and price premiums for the ocean bound plastic they collect.  SEArcular focuses on providing an appropriate end of life for the more difficult to recycle plastic types.  The project’s network of waste pickers, aggregators and suppliers collect HDPE, LDPE, PET, PP, PS and “Other” directly from beaches, waterways, streets, and bins and dumpsters located in public areas and used by individuals/households and businesses.  
SEArcular transports the collected and pre-sorted material to its processing facility in Surabaya where it is washed and processed into flakes and pellets.  The project’s outputs are used by its customers for the production of a diverse range of recycled plastic products, including electronic componentry, luggage items, durable film and reusable poly bags.   
The project currently collects plastic waste in the Surabayan metropolitan area (including 66 km coastline), with its recycling centre located in Driyorejo, Gresik Regency.
Indonesia is the third largest contributor to marine plastic pollution globally.  Conditions prior to the implementation of this project were characterised by high rates of plastic leakage into the environment from both collected and uncollected waste.  Plastic waste in Indonesia is commonly burned, left in dumpsites, or taken to landfill sites operating beyond capacity.  This mismanagement has negative health consequences for large swathes of the Indonesian population.  In addition, there was widespread lack of incentives for coastal communities to collect the ocean bound plastic polluting their neighbourhoods (flexible plastics in particular), creating an urgent need for an empowerment-focused project such as SEArcular's to be established.
pwrp-4864: Plastic waste is a major environmental problem. It pollutes our oceans, landfills, and waterways. It also releases harmful chemicals into the environment. Plastic waste has become an undeniable global crisis, with vast amounts of plastic products entering our environment each day. From single-use plastic bags to bottles and packaging materials, plastic waste poses a significant threat to ecosystems, wildlife, and human health. However, recycling offers a glimmer of hope in mitigating this crisis. This essay explores the importance of plastic waste recycling, its benefits, challenges, and the role it plays in achieving environmental sustainability.
pwrp-4931:
The Green Steps: Towards a Greener Future with Tanrıkulu project is a waste reduction initiative jointly undertaken by Tanrıkulu Group, specifically the companies Tanrıkulu Plastik Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. and Tanrıkulu Geri Dönüşüm ve Atık Değerlendirme Hizmetleri İnşaat Taahhüt Sanayi ve Ticaret LTD. ŞTİ. The project aims to collect and recycle plastic waste collaboratively.

Project activities are carried out in the Kocaeli and Sakarya provinces located in the Marmara Region of Turkey. Tanrıkulu Group operates its operations through 6 different facilities. In Kocaeli, the facilities include the Central facility, Başsikele facility, and Çayırova facility. In Sakarya, the project activities are conducted through the Adapazarı facility, Arifiye facility, and Akyazı facility.

In the scope of the project, various plastic types such as PET (polyethylene terephthalate), HDPE (high-density polyethylene), LDPE (low-density polyethylene), PP (polypropylene), PS (polystyrene), EPS (expanded polystyrene), ABS (acrylonitrile butadiene styrene), and PVC (polyvinyl chloride) are being collected. PET, HDPE, PVC, LDPE, PP, PS and ABS plastics are recycled in Tanrıkulu's mechanical recycling facilities. Tanrıkulu Group provides employment to many people with its collection and recycling activities. Tanrıkulu Group also attaches great importance to the employment of women for gender equality in employment.

Without the existence of the project, the plastic waste materials would still be disposed of in landfills, illegal open dumpsites, or left in the environment. 

The revenue generated from plastic credits is intended to fund capacity expansions. This aims to facilitate the collection and recycling of more plastic waste in the region. Regionally, these activities are crucial from an environmental and sustainability perspective.
pwrp-4933:
Plastic waste is a major environmental problem. It pollutes our oceans, landfills, and waterways. It also releases harmful chemicals into the environment. Plastic waste has become an
undeniable global crisis, with vast amounts of plastic products entering our environment each day. From single-use plastic bags to bottles and packaging materials, plastic waste poses a significant threat to ecosystems, wildlife, and human health. However, recycling offers a glimmer of hope in mitigating this crisis. This essay explores the importance of plastic waste recycling, its benefits, challenges, and the role it plays in achieving environmental sustainability
pwrp-4945:
Situated in the heart of Karaganda, Republic of Kazakhstan, GorKomTrans is greatly improving plastic waste management through its robust collection and recycling initiatives. The organization is a cornerstone of the city's efforts to manage and repurpose Municipal Solid Waste (MSW), with emphasis on improved collection of plastic waste and PET recycling. GorKomTrans is dedicated to refining the plastic waste management process, aiming to drastically reduce plastic pollution and foster positive environmental and community outcomes.
 
GorKomTrans has established an extensive operational network, adeptly handling a vast array of plastic materials. While the organization collects all types of plastic, it places a special focus on the recycling of PET and PET Flex, showcasing its commitment to targeted and impactful recycling processes. Beyond its operational capabilities, GorKomTrans actively engages local businesses and community members, incentivizing participation in its recycling programs. This inclusive approach not only contributes to significant waste reduction but also cultivates a collaborative environment for sustainability.

Specialized sorting and recycling processes are in place, particularly for PET and PET Flex materials, ensuring a streamlined and effective recycling operation. The recent project implementation has marked a notable enhancement in capacity, characterized by the introduction of advanced garbage trucks, sophisticated collection points, and modernized processing facilities. These improvements have significantly amplified the organization's waste management capabilities and environmental impact.

Anticipating the success of its ongoing initiatives, GorKomTrans has laid out a comprehensive strategy to utilize capital generated from Plastic credits. Investments are directed towards expanding the transportation fleet and advancing waste processing technologies.
pwrp-4948:
The main objective of this Plastic waste management project is to achieve social transformation through technology innovation in the waste sector that supports environmental, social and economic sustainability under the pathway of circular economy. The technology innovation, development and implementation includes treating of non-degradable polymer waste by Thermo-Catalytic Depolymerisation Process and generating poly fuel from the plastic waste. This project is represented by WeAct Pty. Ltd. as the project proponent and also the focal point of communication for this pilot project whereas technology and implementation of the project is carried out locally in India under the ownership of “Rudra Environmental Solution (India) Ltd”. The collection and recovery activity are ongoing covering the entire region of Kalyan-Dombivali Municipal Corporation (KDMC), in the state of Maharashtra. 

Project is a great example of circular economy as it is an effective contributor to environmental sustainability by removing plastic waste and then replacing conventional fuel oil in industries with the fuel oil generated from this project that can reasonably reduce carbon footprints. Alongside, it has also contributed to socio-economic development in the region by means of employment generation, community engagement etc.
pwrp-4949: The 'Mr. Green Africa & Removall: Plastic Waste Reduction Project in Kenya' project is a grouped plastic waste reduction activity for collecting and recycling mismanaged plastic waste throughout Kenya. Plastic waste (mostly PP, HDPE and PET) is collected from the environment, from landfills and from commercial entities through a network of informal waste pickers and consumer ecosystems supplying the project’s collection sites. Plastic waste is then transferred to one of the aggregation hubs across the country for being sorted and sent to the project’s mechanical recycling facility in Nairobi, to be transformed into flakes and pellets. The project goal is to fight against plastic pollution and to improve informal waste workers living conditions. Plastic Credits finance will allow the project to expand to new geographies for collection activities and to increase the volumes and types of plastic waste recycled.
pwrp-4954: The Plastic collection and recycling activity facilitated and implemented by Ceprodilic Waste Management aims to collect and recycle plastic waste and scale up the recycling activities at Mutara, Mutimbuzi district, Bujumbura rural province located 20 km north of Bujumbura city, Burundi.
pwrp-4955: The Caribbean Island nation, Haiti, is the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere. Haiti has limited waste management infrastructure, access to clean water. The local population gets much of its drinking water from plastic bottles. As a result, the country is littered with empty plastic bottles polluting its roadways, waterways, informal landfills, towns, and beaches. Sadly, a portion of that plastic waste inevitably finds its way into the ocean. Lavergne’s Haiti project is a plastic waste collection activity that collects those ocean-bound plastics in Haiti. Lavergne Haiti has already made significant strides with 1,200 collectors bringing plastic waste to 77 collection centers throughout the country. In 2020 Lavergne installed a 24-hour wash line that vigorously cleans and shreds the plastic waste collected by the individual waste pickers and collection centers. The plastic is prepared to be shipped and upcycled into recycled pellets in our facility in Canada and Vietnam. Lavergne strives to engage with communities in Haiti to reclaim high quality plastic material, increase the dignity of the people involved, and build good will within the collection community – all in the service of diverting plastic from the environment and driving materials back into a circular economy. Lavergne collects Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET), High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). All three polymers are found in plastic bottles. By recycling OBP, Lavergne is not only preventing plastic pollution but also contributing to the circular economy by reducing the need for virgin plastic. This project is a significant step towards a more sustainable and environmentally friendly future. The plastic waste being recycled is either collected or diverted from environment, landfills, and household and commercial entities.

pwrp-4960:
BIOTREND operates actively in waste collection and sorting of plastic waste in Turkey's Aksaray, Balıkesir, Bergama,İnegöl and Uşak provinces. The project collected waste from mixed municipal
wastes collected other than economically valuable wastes that are separately collected at the source within the provincial boundary is being separated by type at the mechanical separation facility, and the recoverable plastic waste are being sent to licensed companies. The project aims to minimize environmental damage through plastic waste collection and send them for further recycling, fostering a more sustainable future.
The collection of plastic waste was generally disorganized prior to the project's implementation.
The majority of waste generated by people and organizations was frequently dumped in public
trash cans. It was uncommon to see the practice of collecting and storing waste separately from
household garbage. Street collectors rummaged through the trash cans and pulled out some of
the trash that was thrown inside. However, recycling efforts were hampered because these
collected wastes were contaminated with other garbage. Furthermore, the recycled goods made
from such contaminated materials were of poor quality.
pwrp-4988:

reducing the need for virgin plastic.

pwrp-4991: Project Revitalization deals mainly with Collection and Segregation of Plastic waste. The collection of Dry waste is done from two sources- Household and commercial establishments on scheduled days using pickup vans and helpers.The collected waste is taken to the MRF where the dry waste is segregated into Plastic and Non plastic waste. The Plastic waste is Further segregated into Composite, Rigid and Flexible categories. The Plastic waste as per the categories mainly have HDPE, LDPE, PET, FLEXIBLES plastic type. This collected plastic waste is crushed and bailed as per the requirement of the vender and is further sent for recycling where it is made into pellets, flakes to reuse in making new plastic items.
