pwrp-4999: RePL - Plastic Waste Reduction Program aims to recycle inland plastic waste in the Bangladesh region. H201 operates the program in partnership with waste collection and recycling specialists, local governments, carbon experts, international organizations, NGOs, accounting firms, investment institutions, etc., to expand the program and ensure its reliability.
pwrp-5002: The project activity recycles plastic waste into usable products for further processing in manufacturing industries and new products that have a wide variety of applications. The quality of the recycled plastic waste is suitable for it to be used as feedstock in the manufacture of spare parts for the automotive sector, industry of artificial grass, industry of packages thereby displacing the use of virgin plastics. The plastic waste that is recycled consists of mainly pre-consumer and post-industrial waste.The project activity is a capacity addition to an existing recycling activity of 4,276 tonnes/year to a cumulative capacity of 8,500 tonnes/year. The project is implemented and owned by Polibalbino Termoplásticos. The project activity is located in Guarulhos - SP, Brazil.
pwrp-5081:
The Tiê Tiê: Recycling vulnerabilities into opportunities project is a proposal to reduce plastic waste in the southeast of Brazil by mechanical recycling and reinserting this waste into the production chain and by including and valuing vulnerable groups, especially waste pickers, promoting the circular economy and sustainable development in the municipality of Tietê, in São Paulo (SP). 
The project is spearheaded by Reciclagem Tietê and Tiê Plastic (A2 Plastic), interconnected companies whose operations complement each other. Reciclagem Tietê collect, sort, and sell recyclable. Tiê Plastic works in the recycling of plastic waste, which is the subject of this project and can also sort waste.
Reciclagem Tietê also maintains a specific materials reception area for the purchase of all types of recyclable waste, with prices above market value, and is known by the community and waste pickers as a collection point. This initiative values and encourages the work of vulnerable groups, generating income in the Tietê region. In addition, OMA Ativos Ambientais is part of this proposal and is responsible for developing, financing and monitoring this project during the accreditation period, from 2023 to 2033. During this period, it is estimated that 61,650.00 recycled plastic credits will be generated.
The plastic credits claimed in this project, through the recycling activity, will finance investments in the infrastructure of the proposing facility, increasing the mass of recycled plastic, as well as increasing the engagement of the agents in this chain and their income, providing these professionals with decent work, good health and well-being, as well as improving environmental quality, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals - SDG 4, SDG 7, SDG 8, SDG 11 and SDG 12.
pwrp-5103: The project collects and sorts polypropylene and polyethylene waste to produce recycled Flexible Intermediate Bulk Containers and other agro-polymers. The recycled PP has performance parameters similar to virgin PP and therefore makes for a sustainable alternative to single-use plastic. With industry standards in favour of using 100% virgin polymer while manufacturing such FIBCs the amount of virgin plastic going out into the ecosystem is set to increase exponentially. Emmbi will be using upto 35% of recycled PP polymer to produce the FIBCs without losing any of its operating properties. The waste is collected from post-consumer waste, tubs, cups, pouches, used drip line and industrial waste and is sorted, cleaned and then recycled at Emmbi's facility through mechanical recycling. The project activity encourages collection of plastic waste in a structured manner as opposed to the informal waste collection of rag-pickers in India.
pwrp-5204:
The main activity of the Zhangyru Plast project is the mechanical processing of PET packaging waste into secondary raw materials - recyclate, by crushing and grinding plastic materials. This waste arrives at the Zhangyru Plast from waste sorting complexes, recycling collection points and waste collection containers. The activity of the entity LLP Zhangyru Plast for plastic recycling was organized in 2022 in Kazakhstan, Almaty region.
Zhangyru Plast project plans to recycle a total of 56, 429.194 tonnes of plastic over 7 years, an average of 8,061.313 tonnes per year. 
Waste management, especially plastic waste, in the country is problematic. Most of the waste ends up in landfills, which cause serious environmental problems. Landfills, often located near populated areas, overflow, causing soil and water pollution. Plastic waste decomposes slowly, releasing toxic substances and microplastics that enter ecosystems and adversely affect human and animal health. In addition, the practice of creating unauthorised dumps is widespread in the country. These dumps are often spontaneously created, without any control or adherence to sanitary norms, exacerbating the problem of environmental pollution. The implementation of this project is necessary to address these issues and create a more sustainable waste management system in the country.
pwrp-5301: The plastic waste recycling plant implemented by Ravago Recycling Middle East LLC SPC, previously known as DGrade Recycling Factory L.L.C. (DRFLLC) involves mechanical recycling of post-consumer waste PET bottles to manufacture recycled PET flakes and HDPE flakes. These flakes have diverse applications in industries like textiles, packaging, and construction, resulting in the replacement of virgin plastic.
pwrp-5303:
The Roded Recycling Project is a plastic waste collection and recycling project based in Israel. The target plastic waste is agricultural plastic from greenhouse films (LDPE) plastic pipes (HDPE), and other plastic waste (PP) which are commonly used and discarded in the environment. The project activity involves the collection and mechanical recycling of such plastic waste. The recycled product is polyethylene (PE), which is used to manufacture high quality recycled plastic pallets, which displace the need for virgin plastic in the manufacturing process.
In Israel, the agricultural sector produces around 35,000 to 50,000 tonnes of plastic waste annually, only around 7% of which is recycled. The rest is dumped illegally, incinerated or landfilled. The most common products are films, ground coverings, irrigation pipes and bags. Although there is a high recycling potential for PE and PP, much of the waste is contaminated with soil and cannot be recycled at an economic scale.
The use of greenhouse films is common in Israel. The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development estimate that roughly 100km2 is covered by greenhouses. The greenhouse covers are replaced every 2-3 years, with most incinerated or disposed of in the environment. In West Negev alone, roughly 6,000 tonnes of agricultural plastic is used annually. 
The project activity involves collecting eligible types of plastic waste from two primary sources: i) directly from farms, and ii) from illegal open dumpsites. 
The project activity is within the scope of the Verra Plastic Waste Reduction Standard as:
•	The project activity targets the collection and recycling of 66,000 tonnes of plastic waste over the first 7-year crediting period
•	The plastic waste involved is HDPE (type 2), LDPE (type 4) and PP (type 5), which are material types included in the scope of the Plastic Program
•	The activities are supported by approved methodologies (PWRM0001 & PWRM0002)
pwrp-5329:
This project focuses on the collection and recycling of various types of plastic waste in the region of Sulaimaniyah, Iraq. It operates through a single facility located in Sulaimaniyah that handles both the collection and recycling processes. On average, the facility collects 150 tonnes of plastic per month from multiple sources across the city. Workers gather plastic from designated locations, and it is delivered to the facility weekly. Upon arrival, the plastic is segregated by type, washed, and then processed into shreds using specialized equipment.
By transforming plastic waste into shreds, the project helps reduce the demand for virgin resources like fossil fuels, which are the primary raw materials used to produce new plastic. Virgin plastic production relies heavily on petrochemicals derived from crude oil and natural gas, which must be extracted, refined, and processed. These activities are energy-intensive and significantly contribute to greenhouse gas emissions and environmental degradation.
By avoiding the need to extract and process fossil fuels for plastic production, the project helps conserve natural resources and reduce pollution. The environmental benefits include lower carbon emissions, reduced energy consumption, and a smaller ecological footprint compared to the traditional production of new plastic from virgin materials.
Before the implementation of this project, plastic waste in the region was largely unmanaged, accumulating in streets and rivers, contributing to pollution, littering, and landfill waste. When plastic waste ends up in landfills, it takes significant time to decompose, leaching toxic chemicals into the soil and groundwater, which harms local ecosystems and wildlife. Additionally, the breakdown of plastic in landfills generates methane, a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change.
The project’s recycling efforts not only reduce the harmful environmental impact of plastic waste but also create a circular economy by turning waste into valuable products. This approach avoids the use of virgin resources such as crude oil and natural gas, leading to more sustainable production practices. The project seeks to issue Plastic Credits as a means of financing its continued growth. These credits will support scaling operations by funding the purchase of additional machinery and hiring more workers, which will increase both the collection and recycling capacity in the region.
On an annual basis, the project collects and recycles approximately 1,800 metric tonnes of plastic waste.
pwrp-5332:
Re Up Geri Dönüşüm Sanayi Ve Ticaret A.Ş. Repet Şube (hereinafter “Re&Up”) operates in İnegöl, Bursa, pioneering textile recycling efforts by employing advanced recycling technologies. The project, RE&UP Bottle PET Recycled Chips, Flakes & Next-Gen T2T PET Recycled Chips Production (hereinafter “the Project”), focuses on transforming PET bottle waste and PET textile waste into high-quality, sustainable raw materials, namely PET flakes and PET chips.
Through the up cycling of PET waste, the project ensures that plastic materials are returned to the production cycle, fostering a circular economy and contributing to a more sustainable future.
The project employs both mechanical and thermomechanical recycling technologies to process PET flakes and superior PET chips. The recycling process involves sorting of polyester waste, mechanical shredding, melting, filtration, deep vacuum treatment, crystallization, and precision cutting. This results in high-performance granulates suitable for new textile products, extending the lifecycle of PET materials while meeting stringent quality standards.
Re&Up operates as a high-capacity, scaled-up recycling facility. Leveraging innovative and scalable technologies, the recycled materials are made suitable for direct reuse in the textile industry. This facility, aligned with sustainability goals, makes a valuable contribution to recycling efforts.
Re&Up is committed not only to environmental sustainability but also to creating local employment opportunities, particularly for women, to promote social equity in the workforce. The Project’s forward-looking approach aims to expand recycling capacities with revenue from plastic credits , supporting Turkey’s circular economy targets and contributing to regional sustainability efforts.
pwrp-5356: The purpose of this project activity by Repono Green Pvt.Ltd is recycling of plastic wastes through mechanical recycling to give them secondary life. The project activity is a new recycling project of capacity 20 tonnes/day and is located in Pune, Maharashtra, India.The project activity recycles plastic waste which includes thin films, industrial bags, carrier bags and thin food wrappers into recycled plastic sheets / boards which have a wide variety of applications.
pwrp-5422: The Green Wheels Plastic Collection Project is a plastic collection and recycling initiative in Sri Lanka that uses environmentally friendly transport to collect plastic waste and recycle it. This project collects discarded plastic waste from various environmental locations—such as beaches, small trackways, and riverbanks—and transports it via electric bikes (e-bikes) to a central Material Recovery Facility (MRF). At the MRF the plastic will be compacted and transported to a recycling factory for processing into reusable material. This process diverts waste from natural environments and contributes to the production of sustainable materials. The project is situated in a number of locations, mostly in western and southern Sri Lanka, primarily focusing on coastal and riverine areas where plastic accumulation poses significant risks to both marine and terrestrial ecosystems. These locations offer access to large volumes of plastic waste that can be intercepted before entering the ocean. The selected areas in Sri Lanka suffer from inadequate waste management infrastructure, with significant amounts of plastic waste either ending up being dispersed in the natural environment. The general conditions of waste management in the regions reveal a need for improved collection, segregation, and recycling practices. The introduction of using Plastic Credits as credit finance catalyses advancements in local waste management technologies and methodologies, thereby reducing environmental impact and fostering sustainable practices.
pwrp-5428:
Situated at Hollinwood Lane, Calverton, Nottingham NG14 6NR in the United Kingdom, this project tackles the escalating issue of plastic waste through a comprehensive, technology-driven collection and sorting system. By focusing on post-consumer plastics from households and public spaces, the initiative diverts substantial volumes of plastic away from landfills and natural environments, thereby contributing to a more circular economy and reducing the region’s environmental footprint.
Before this project began, much of Calverton’s plastic waste was either mismanaged, partially recycled, or disposed of in landfills, leading to significant environmental harm. To address these challenges, the facility now accepts compressed bales of mixed plastics—often delivered by Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGV) or walking-floor trailers—and processes them through a series of advanced sorting technologies. After being broken down by a bale breaker, the material travels through an eight-paddle ballistic separator, which differentiates two-dimensional (paper, film, card) and three-dimensional (plastics, cans) materials. Overband magnets and eddy currents then remove ferrous and non-ferrous metals before near-infrared optical sorters (Tomra) segregate plastics by polymer type. Once sorted, plastics are baled and sold to downstream processors, who typically wash and extrude the material for re-use.
Since the project’s inception on 25 May 2023, it has successfully collected and processed 52,146.75 tonnes of plastic, showcasing its steadfast commitment to environmental stewardship and sustainable waste management. By actively reducing plastic pollution at this scale, the project not only demonstrates its capacity for meaningful impact, but also highlights the potential for continued growth and positive change in communities across the UK.
To finance ongoing operations and enable further expansion, the project plans to issue Plastic Credits. This mechanism is critical not only for maintaining current collection efforts but also for scaling up to a seven-day schedule, investing in additional machinery, and enhancing site facilities. By securing the necessary funding, the project will be able to process larger quantities of plastic waste, further increasing its environmental and social impact.
Between May 2023 and December 2024 (the monitoring period), the facility collected 52,146.75 tons of plastic. It is projected that from January 2025 to December 2025, and for each subsequent year, the facility will process 70,700 tons of plastic, demonstrating its expanding capacity and dedication to responsible waste management.
pwrp-5447:
The 'Kubik & Removall: turning plastic waste into low-carbon buildings in Ethiopia' project is a grouped plastic waste reduction activity for collecting mismanaged plastic waste throughout Ethiopia. Plastic waste (mostly PP, HDPE, LDPE and PET) is collected from the environment and from dumpsites through a network of informal waste pickers supplying the project's collection centres. Plastic waste is then sorted, weighed and transferred to the facility in Adama, to be upcycled into plastic construction materials such as bricks or beams, or sent to PET recycling partners.
The project goal is to fight plastic pollution and climate change by empowering the informal waste sector. 
Plastic Credits finance will allow the project to increase the volume of plastic waste collected and to set up collection points all around Ethiopia. This will also allow Kubik to increase social benefits to the informal waste picker community, such as providing better wages and enhanced health coverage.
pwrp-5466:
The project activity involves reducing plastic pollution in the recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) industry in Cameroon. Under the project, PET plastic waste is collected from households and businesses through regular curbside collection programs across Douala, Yaoundé, Petcam, Bekoko, Garoua, Muyuka and Bertoua. Across the project area there are designated locations where individuals can drop off the collected plastic waste, which is collected by Ecogreen and transported to the Ecogreen recycling facility.
By implementing these collection methods and using advanced recycling machinery, the rPET project significantly reduces plastic pollution in Cameroon. The process ensures that plastic waste is efficiently collected from urban areas and the environment, sorted, cleaned, and recycled into new products, reducing the amount of plastic that ends up in informal waste dumpsites and making its way to the ocean.
Plastic waste pollution is a significant environmental issue in Cameroon. Urban areas, particularly the economic hub Douala and the capital city Yaoundé, are heavily affected. Ineffective waste management systems contribute to the accumulation of plastic waste in streets, waterways, and open dumps. Plastic waste clogs drainage systems, leading to increased flooding during the rainy season, pollutes water bodies, affecting aquatic life and ecosystems and degradation of plastic waste releases harmful chemicals into the soil and water. In Cameroon, 600,000 tonnes of plastic waste is produced annual, accounting for roughly 10% of the 6,000,000 tonnes of annual municipal waste. In 2017 and 2018, only 1,089.15 and 748.96 tonnes of plastic waste respectively were recycled.
The project aims to collect and recycle an average of 10,862 and 6,662 tonnes of PET per year, and a total of 76,035 and 46,500 over the crediting period.
pwrp-5554: LaoRefuel project launched in 2024 at Vientiane aims to address the growing issue of plastic pollution in Lao PDR. The project focuses on the collection of plastic waste from industrial and commercial facilities, which will then be converted into refuse-derived fuel (RDF). The RDF will be supplied to cement factories to replace fossil fuel, which contributes to the emission reduction by energy recovery. By introducing new machines and equipment to produce RDF from plastic wastes, LaoReFuel will initially collect approximately 50 to 100 metric tonnes of plastic waste per month from industrial sectors, with plans to expand this collection amount as the project growth.
pwrp-5613:
The project, implemented by Agra Smart City Limited (ASCL), aims to improve plastic waste management through the collection, segregation, and recycling of plastic waste at the Material Recovery Facility (MRF) in Kuberpur, Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. The project enhances sustainable waste management practices by targeting high-impact plastics such as HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene) and LDPE (Low-Density Polyethylene), which are collected from municipal solid waste streams.
Plastic waste is collected through a formal, door-to-door municipal collection system, as well as from shops and markets. At the MRF, mixed waste is initially sorted using a trommel machine. Subsequent manual sorting isolates HDPE and LDPE plastics, which are then processed using dust cleaning machines to remove contaminants. The cleaned plastic is shredded into flakes, then extruded into recycled plastic pellets and finished products such as pipes. These recycled products replace virgin plastic materials in applications like irrigation, drainage and construction, contributing to a circular economy and reducing environmental pollution.
pwrp-5693:
This Project Description (PD) contains information about the Plastic waste recycling from PET and PE waste in Azerbaijan Grouped Project 
Grouped Project Description
Project Overview
The proposed Grouped Project aims to address plastic waste management in Azerbaijan by implementing plastic waste collection and recycling initiatives. Specifically, it will focus on collecting and recycling Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) and Polyethylene (PE) plastic waste in Azerbaijan, which currently contributes to landfill waste within the country.
Environmental Impact
This initiative will significantly reduce plastic waste originating from various cities across Azerbaijan. By intercepting plastic waste generated in the main urban centres, the project will prevent its deposition in landfills, thereby mitigating environmental pollution in Azerbaijan
pwrp-5754:
The IGNIS 3R Project, led by IGNIS Environment Initiatives Sdn. Bhd., is a large-scale plastic waste management initiative in Malaysia developed under the Verra Plastic Waste Reduction Program. Operating with approvals from state governments and municipal councils, the Project systematically collects plastic waste from open landfills and directs all volumes to controlled processing through pyrolysis (a thermal process) at IGNIS-owned facilities.

All collected waste is transported to the IGNIS 3R Technology plants located near participating landfills, where it is sorted and utilised exclusively as feedstock for pyrolysis. This intervention reduces reliance on unmanaged landfill disposal and directly mitigates fire hazards. Open landfills in Malaysia are highly prone to methane accumulation and spontaneous combustion, with accumulated plastics acting as a persistent fuel source.

Baseline conditions prior to the Project included open dumping, burning, and uncontrolled degradation of plastics, which contribute to greenhouse gas emissions, leachate generation, and long-term environmental harm. The Project mitigates these impacts by consolidating plastic waste in regulated facilities, delivering verifiable improvements in waste diversion, environmental protection, and safe end-of-life treatment through pyrolysis.

The Project will commence on 27 June 2025 with a fixed crediting period of ten (10) years, ending on 26 June 2035. It is expected to collect and process approximately 42 million tonnes of plastic waste (averaging 4.2 million tonnes annually), with the objective of covering most of Malaysia’s open landfills by 2035 and subsequently expanding operations regionally.
pwrp-5797:
ESA INC. (ESA), based in Tokyo, Japan, has developed the proprietary ESA Method, an innovative mechanical recycling technology designed to process hard-to-recycle composite plastics that are normally excluded from conventional recycling systems. The project focuses on waste streams such as car engine insulation trimmings, toothpaste tubing, semiconductor cover tapes, and multi-layered packaging films. These materials are shredded, cleaned, and extruded into recycled pellets at ESA’s recycling facility, providing high-quality inputs for resin processors and compounders and displacing virgin plastics in industrial applications.
The initial project operations will be implemented at the ESA facility located at 1-2 Shin-yahata, Yuki City, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan (Latitude: 36.269092, Longitude: 139.873580). This facility, hereafter referred to as the “Yuki Plant,” will serve as the first operational site under the ESA PWRS Group Project framework. Additional franchise facilities are planned for inclusion under the same group framework in subsequent phases across Japan. The commencement of operations at the Yuki Plant is scheduled for 1 June 2026.
Prior to the project, the identified composite waste streams were predominantly incinerated for energy recovery or disposed of in landfills, as they could not be processed through Japan’s conventional mechanical recycling infrastructure, which requires clean, mono-material inputs. This practice resulted in the permanent loss of valuable resources and contributed to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from incineration.
The project at Yuki plant is expected to recycle approximately 7,200 ton of plastic waste per year, corresponding to a total 50,400 ton of over seven years.
pwrp-5839:
Naturecycle - Recycling with social impact for flexible packaging is a proposal to reduce post-consumer flexible plastic waste of the LDPE type throughout Brazil by mechanically recycling and reinserting high-quality recycled LDPE into the packaging sector's production chain. Considering the complexity of recycling this plastic waste and the lack of interest among waste pickers in collecting it due to its low value, the aims of this project are to increase the recycling of this plastic waste and its reuse, reduce its inappropriate disposal in the environment and strengthen the socio-environmental projects developed by the recycler, promoting the circular economy and sustainable development in the project's area of influence.
The project is a partnership between Lauro Weber & Cia LTDA (Plastiweber), an innovative, pioneering company specializing in the recovery of flexible plastic waste through recycling. Based in the municipality of Feliz, in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, the company carries out sorting, crushing, washing, drying, mechanical recycling and quality control activities. Since 1997, Plastiweber has been transforming plastic waste into recycled LDPE for packaging, such as film and bubble wrap, and OMA Ativos Ambientais S.A. is responsible for developing, financing and monitoring this project.
pwrp-5921:
Waste Management Control (WMC) was founded in 2019 with the mission to create high-quality waste management centres that protect workers and maximize resource recovery. Under the license from the Ministry of Environment and the EEAA, renewed on June 09th, 2024, and under a commercial registry No. (85408). The first facility was located in the 6th of October City (called 300), fully aligned with environmental and civil defence standards, with a capacity of 400 tons/year. WMC operations focus on plastic waste within Egypt.
WMC collects, sorts, and aggregates post-consumer plastic waste from both formal and informal sources. The company is establishing four state-of-the-art plastic collection and processing warehouses in Ard El-Lewa, 6th of October City (Industrial Zone), New Cairo (5th Settlement), and Bani Swief City. These facilities are designed to serve as formal, licensed recycling hubs in Egypt, addressing the widespread inefficiencies and environmental risks of the informal sector. All warehouses are fully compliant with the Ministry of Environment, Civil Defence, and occupational safety regulations, and are built to meet the highest standards of health, fire safety, and environmental protection.
jnr-2264: This program incorporates incentives related to reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation - REDD+ projects, with a primary objective to value carbon stocks of the state.  The main incentives related to the program include promoting the transition to more productive agricultural systems that reduce the need for expansion and thus avoid further deforestation; including the economic value of standing forests to improve the quality of life of forest-dependent people and increase conservation of forests; and finally, the distribution of benefits for environmental services.
jnr-2574:
The Bago Region is an administrative region in Myanmar that includes the four Districts of Bago, Pyay, Tharrawaddy and Taungoo. The forest areas included in this JNR Baseline include Reserve Forests (including community forests), Protected Public Areas and Protected Area System which are subject to unplanned deforestation and degradation due to subsistence-based activities, illegal over extraction on areas designated as plantations within the Reserve Forests and other illegal drivers. This accounts for 92% of all forests in the Bago Region.  To create a pathway from project crediting to a jurisdictional nested REDD+ program in the future, the Bago Region REDD+ Program has developed a baseline that is validated under JNR and which is also used for a grouped project under the VCS project standards. 
The Program is being implemented by Forest Department of Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation (Forest Department), with support from the Korean Forest Service and Terra Global. This Program will initially be is registering, monitoring and issuing in accordance with the VCS AFOLU standards using this Jurisdictional Baseline which is the same as the baseline developed under VM0006 for the AFOLU grouped project. Technically, this means that the Program is currently applying Option 1 as defined under the JNR Rules and Requirements and will monitor and verify applying the detailed requirements of VM0006 as well as applying the CCB standard for project areas where implementation will be taking place.  Over time, as the Program secures more funding and can expand it areas of implementation, it has a pathway toward JNR Option 2.  This is approach allows the project to apply highly creditable and proven VCS standards and methodologies that allow for the direct crediting and quantification of the social and environmental impact of project activities to be measured under the CCB.
jnr-4648: The Provincial Government of Misiones, Argentina is implementing a jurisdictional REDD+ program with the objective of developing incentives and safeguard systems to protect both public and privately owned native forests in the province.  Misiones is located in the northeast of Argentina and is divided into departments and municipalities. Approximately 97% of the remaining Parana Atlantic Forest is located in Misiones, with over 1.5 million hectares of native forest. Using carbon finance, the Provincial government will enhance the implementation of a REDD+ strategy to reduce deforestation and forest degradation through a variety of measures including regulations and laws, strategic planning, stakeholder consultations, fire control, and measures to reduce illegal logging. The program has developed a provincial Safeguard Information System (SIS), a robust MRV system, and a benefit sharing mechanism.
jnr-5079:
The Chocó Department is an administrative region that is the second jurisdictional level below National Level in Colombia. CODECHOCO, COCOMACIA and Terra Global Capital prepared this Chocó Colombia JNR Baseline Description and FREL. Areas in this JNR Baseline include all forest areas that are subject to unplanned deforestation and degradation due to subsistence-based activities, illegal over extraction of timber, and other illegal drivers. This includes Protected Public Areas, indigenous communities forest lands and afro-Colombian community councils forest areas. This accounts for 80% of all land in the Choco Department. 
The scope of activities in the forward baseline includes emissions from deforestation and degradation, removals from enhancements in forest areas and removals from reforestation/regeneration in areas deforested during the Crediting period. This Program will initially be registering, monitoring and issuing in accordance with the VCS AFOLU standards using this Jurisdictional Baseline which is the same as the baseline developed under VM0006 for the AFOLU grouped project. Technically, this means that the Program is currently applying Option 1 as defined under the JNR Rules and Requirements and will monitor and verify applying the detailed requirements of VM0006 as well as applying the CCB standard for project areas where implementation will be taking place.  Over time, as the Program secures more funding and can expand its areas of implementation, it has a pathway toward JNR Option 2. This approach allows the project to apply highly creditable and proven VCS standards and methodologies that allow for the direct crediting and quantification of the social and environmental impact of project activities to be measured under the CCB.
fcpf-5253: Viet Nam’s ER program is working to increase forest cover and quality and improve forest management and protection through forest sector investments and policy enhancement in agricultural practices. The program supports large-scale integrated forest and land use, addresses the connection between agriculture commodity production and deforestation, supports poverty reduction, and applies innovative financing mechanisms to pay for forest ecosystem services. A participatory forest management approach engages local communities and ethnic minorities in state forest management to ensure their full participation and commitment to the program and its benefits
fcpf-5254: The Zambézia Integrated Landscape Management Program, an ambitious, cross-cutting initiative to promote sustainable rural development in one of Mozambique’s poorest and most populous provinces, is the first of its kind in the country. The project area hosts lush forests, fertile soils, river systems, and an extensive coastline. The ER program focuses on investment activities that will promote conservation and climate-smart agriculture, create sustainable supply chains for cash-crop production, develop multipurpose tree plantations, restore degraded lands, improve the efficiency of charcoal production and consumption, and strengthen the management of protected areas.
fcpf-5255: Ghana’s ER program is an ambitious and unique initiative in Africa—and a global first in the cocoa sector—that is supporting the production of sustainable, climate-smart cocoa beans while reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation. The program addresses landscape management with a focus on sustainable cocoa farming, forest protection, community-based landscape governance, and multistakeholder collaboration; it also promotes other tree crops, agroforestry, and other nature-based livelihoods within the cocoa forest hot spot intervention areas.
fcpf-5256: The Republic of Congo’s ER program addresses both direct and underlying drivers of deforestation and forest degradation in the Sangha and Likouala Departments. The program is among the first in Africa to test REDD+ at scale. Program activities include engaging forest concession holders to reduce the impact of their logging operations and set aside conservation areas. The program is also working to reduce emissions from deforestation in palm oil and mining concessions by avoiding the conversion of forests with high conservation value and adopting reduced-impact mining techniques. The program supports livelihood improvements through smallholder cocoa production, agroforestry systems, and smallholder outgrower schemes, and it provides payments for environmental services for forest protection. Finally, the program includes measures to improve the management of existing protected areas, among others, through the creation of alternative income-generating activities for communities.
fcpf-5257: Building on almost two decades of Nepal’s successful community-based forest management program, the country’s ER program delivers forest conservation results and emission reductions at scale by addressing the pressures and threats to forests across the program area. The program’s interventions include improving the management practices on existing community forests building on traditional and customary practices; localizing forest governance through the transfer of national forests to community and collaborative forest user groups; expanding private sector forestry through improved access to extension services and finance; expanding access to alternative energy with biogas and improved cookstoves; scaling up pro-poor leasehold forestry; improving integrated land use planning to reduce forest conversion associated with advancing infrastructure development; and strengthening the management of protected areas.
fcpf-5258: Madagascar’s ER program builds on the country’s Integrated Agriculture Landscape Program aimed at increasing agricultural productivity and reducing rural poverty while improving soil quality, conserving water resources, and protecting vital forests and biodiversity. The program follows a landscape approach that addresses the direct and indirect causes of deforestation and degradation including important watersheds. The program also reinforces conservation and community forest management and builds on forest-friendly agroforestry value chains, such as vanilla and cloves. The program includes a number of protected areas, reinforcing their important place in the landscapes. The government of Madagascar is finalizing the final steps to ensure effective and secure transfer of funds to beneficiaries.
fcpf-5259: Lao PDR’s ER program addresses the drivers and underlying causes of deforestation and forest degradation through provincial-level activities in six northern provinces. Working across key land-use sectors, the program is providing a strong, strategic, and scalable foundation to promote sustainable agriculture practices, forest management, conservation, and rehabilitation. The program’s programmatic approach combines priority policy actions; improvements in forest management practices and measures to reduce pressure from the agriculture sector, including through integrated spatial planning; and sustainable livelihood development. The program’s benefit-sharing arrangements encourage the participation of local communities, ethnic minority groups, and other stakeholders and provide incentives for greener and more resilient landscape management.
fcpf-5260: Indonesia’s ER program aligns with East Kalimantan’s low-emission development approach, implemented through strategies and action plans that build on the province’s strong leadership in addressing climate change. It is designed to incentivize reduced deforestation and forest degradation in the province through sustainable forest management activities, including forest licensing improvements, strengthening forest management capacity, and promoting community-based planning. The program also focuses on addressing the province’s main drivers of deforestation and forest degradation through improved forest governance, protection and rehabilitation of peatland areas, and support for alternative livelihoods and community forestry. This is Indonesia’s first jurisdictional-level ER program, serving as an example for other subnational governments in the country. View Country Profile
fcpf-5261: Guatemala’s ER program aims to strengthen the management of national protected areas and reinforce forest policy instruments. The program is implementing REDD+ activities focused on expanding existing incentives to increase carbon stocks; promoting sustainable forest management; strengthening the co-management of protected areas, agroforestry systems, and forest plantations; improving governance and law enforcement on forest lands; developing a forest products value chain; and promoting new mechanisms to compensate for the conservation of environmental and ecosystem services.
fcpf-5262: Fiji’s ER program takes an integrated approach to emission reductions and removal through afforestation/reforestation, forest rehabilitation, improved harvesting practices, national and subnational land-use planning, and sustainable forest management. The program emphasizes the enhancement of benefits that extend beyond carbon, such as improvements to the ecosystem, strengthened food security, enhanced land tenure, and conservation of social and cultural values. Local communities will play a key role in program implementation.
fcpf-5263: The Dominican Republic’s national-level ER program focuses on reducing forest emissions and enhancing removals to help local communities and areas important for agricultural production, water supply, and biodiversity. The ER program is strengthening institutional frameworks and policies as well as supporting civil society and government programs that promote sustainable agroforestry and silvopastoral systems, with the aim of improving production on existing plots and stopping the expansion of the country’s agricultural frontier into forest areas. The program also promotes broader, integrated, and sustainable natural resource management through a mix of conservation, restoration, and sustainable production, including for forest products, coffee, and cacao.
fcpf-5266: The Democratic Republic of Congo has selected Mai-Ndombe Province, a hot spot of deforestation in the country, to pilot results-based payments for REDD+ at scale. The direct drivers of deforestation and degradation in the province mirror those at the national level and include slash-and-burn agriculture, fuelwood production, uncontrolled bush fires, artisanal logging, and industrial logging. Existing REDD+ investments underlying the ER program combine different sources of funding, such as the Forest Investment Program, the Central African Forest Initiative, and the Global Environment Facility. The ER program is helping the country to secure long-term public and private finance to provide alternatives to deforestation and reward efforts to mitigate climate change, reduce poverty, and manage natural resources sustainably.
fcpf-5267: Côte d’Ivoire’s ER program combines political commitment and private sector initiatives in one subnational region to promote zero-deforestation agriculture, sustainable management of forests and conservation of classified forests and national parks, agroforestry, agricultural intensification, and capacity building for protected area management and forest monitoring. The ER program is implementing a model for economic development that improves the population’s living conditions and livelihoods while ending deforestation and forest degradation and reducing carbon emissions. It is also developing strong partnerships, including with World Cocoa Foundation members (some of the world’s largest cocoa companies) who have committed to participate in Côte d’Ivoire’s ER program by financing investments up front.
fcpf-5268: The ER program supports Costa Rica’s national REDD+ strategy and its broader ambition to achieve a low-carbon economy in a resilient environment. The program is helping expand the country’s payment for environmental services program and contributing to other key national programs for sustainable forest management, fire management, landscape restoration, and the National Decarbonization Plan. The program is also strengthening the governance of national protected areas, which cover 26 percent of the country’s territory. Marked by a strong social component, the program is working to increase the participation of all stakeholders to address the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation, including Indigenous Peoples and private landowners, enabling emission reductions from an additional 20 percent of the program’s forest area. View Country Profile.
fcpf-5269: The ER program in Chile supports the implementation of the country’s National Strategy for Climate Change and Vegetation Resources (ENCCRV), which aims to decrease the forest-related social, environmental, and economic vulnerability generated by climate change, desertification, land degradation, and loss of vegetation resources. The program focuses on helping Chile address its main drivers of deforestation through strategic activities such as preventive forest fire management and postfire restoration, sustainable forest management, forest and livestock management models, and sustainable use of vegetation resources, complemented with reforestation of priority areas with native species.

acr-ACR1002: Doyon, Limiteds carbon forest offset project, Doyon Tsoo, is located near the rural communities of Circle, Eagle, Stevens Village in Southeast Interior Alaska, and Huslia in Northwest Interior Alaska along the Yukon and Koyukuk River, and the Steese and Taylor Highway. Ts'oo translates to 'spruce tree' in Hans Gwitchin, one of the indigenous languages within the project area that spans across continuous boreal forest located on Doyon, Limited-owned land. As the largest private landowner in Alaska, Doyon, Limited is prioritizing forest health, fuel mitigation, and responsible forest management to create resilient forests over time. The development of an Improved Forest Management carbon project places focus on preserving the pristine forestland in this area of our region while highlighting the ecological and cultural values of our lands and creating in-region economic benefits for current and future generations.
acr-ACR1003: The Anew - Cassidy Forestry Project encompasses an area of approximately193,247 acres situated in central and northern Maine. Rich in ecological diversity, the transitional forests of the project span the northeastern highlands and the Acadian plains and hills. By employing practices of sustainable forestry and maintenance of forest carbon stocking, this project will achieve positive climate impacts.
acr-ACR1004: The Anew - Nova North Forestry Project is comprised of approximately 22,149 acres of forested lands spanning the South Central Nova Scotia Uplands, mainly concentrated in Pictou County. acr-ACR1006: The Challenge Tree Farm IFM project is composed of approximately 8,500 acres of Sierra Nevada mixed conifer/hardwood forest that will be managed for increased carbon sequestration by restricting harvesting to rates less than growth over the project term. This will be achieved by increasing rotation lengths relative to common practice standards in the region and by proactively applying thinning and fuels reduction treatments that accelerate the development of larger diameter trees and reduce catastrophic wildfire risk. The future planned harvest levels are well below the legally allowable levels provided for under the California Forest Practice Rules.

acr-ACR1010: Five orphaned oil and gas wells carrying the official orphaned status/designation at the state level were identified in Adams County, CO as continuously leaking methane from the wellhead. acr-ACR1014: Fielding Environmental (Fielding) is one of only two major refrigerant reclamation and recycling companies in Canada. Refrigerant reclamation and recycling is a core business unit for Fielding and it includes ODS and non-ODS refrigerants that come from various sectors across the country including the automotive sector and the refrigeration and air conditioning sector. Fielding receives refrigerants from authorized wholesalers or directly from contractors and end-users that have collected refrigerant from end-of-life equipment or after equipment retrofits. acr-ACR1031: The Burnett County Timberlands IFM project consists of 95,000 forested acres in northwest Wisconsin. Burnett County manages their forest to optimize and sustain the forests utility via the production of forest products, recreational opportunities, wildlife habitat and watershed protection. The local community is dependent on the forest to generate timber revenues to offset local taxes and fund a portion of the local county government. Carbon revenue will help diversify existing forest-based revenues, providing additional certainty and assistance with county budgeting for the next two decades. With the initiation of an IFM project, forest carbon sequestration and storage has been incorporated as a primary management goal.

acr-ACR1037: The Thompson Family Forest Restoration Project is located in north-central Oregon, approximately 15 miles southeast of Heppner, and includes 9,442 acres. The area primarily consists of pine and fir tree species of younger to medium ages resulting from decades of industrial forest management. The project will achieve GHG removals by enhancing the forest's health and resilience through thinning, harvesting less than annual growth  extending the rotation age, and managing a mix of species that can adapt to climate change. The result of these management actions will increase the forest's capacity to remove and store carbon over time, surpassing common forestry practices, and reduce the risk of stand-replacing wildfires within the project area. The resulting forest will be a mix of larger, older well-spaced healthy and resilient trees that will be adaptable to a changing climate with enhanced habitat for native fish and wildlife species.

acr-ACR1050: The American Refrigerants HFC Reclamation Project - 2023 (the Project) recovers previously used, reclaimed hydrofluorocarbons (HFC) to be used in place of newly produced, virgin HFCs either in new refrigeration or air conditioning equipment or to recharge existing equipment. By eliminating the need for virgin HFC that would otherwise be manufactured to meet the demand, American Refrigerants, Inc. (AR) (the Project Proponent) is ensuring that no additional HFC will leak into the atmosphere, besides what has already been produced. At AR reclamation facility in Bradenton, Florida, recovered refrigerants are received from across the United States, oil and water impurities are removed and the recovered refrigerant are restores to the AHRI 700 Standard for Specification for Fluorocarbon Refrigerants. The reclaimed refrigerants are then sold to distributors, service companies and wholesalers located in the United States.
acr-ACR1052: Located in Northern and Western Maine, the Silva Fortis project encompasses over 37,000 acres of productive New England timberland. With diversified ecological sites throughout the project area, Silva Fortis provides strong impact for buyers looking for more than just a climate solution. The timberland has been managed for multiple uses for generations, with a focus on sustained yield and a healthy forest ecosystem. Implementation of the IFM project will further support the health and productivity of the forest, while increasing carbon storage.
acr-ACR1053: The Rudio Mountain Forest Carbon Project is approximately 17,781 acres of forestland located in the Blue Mountains of eastern Oregon. By committing to maintain forest CO2 stocks through conservation management, the project will provide significant climate benefits through carbon sequestration.
acr-ACR1054: This project is located in the Olympic Peninsula within Clallam County on 4,410 acres. This IFM project will increase forest carbon stocking during the project period beyond local common practice. This will be achieved by expanding voluntary riparian buffers, reducing the intensity of silvicultural practices, and increasing rotation ages via FSC-certified management practices. Management activities will include some precommercial and commercial thinning and even aged management with retention, which will create a mix of mature and young forests with native trees species. These efforts will result in an increase in forest carbon accumulation over the project lifetime. The management regime will also improve overall forest health and resiliency while creating and enhancing habitat for fish and wildlife species. Carbon revenues will replace some forgone timber revenue and support EFMs overarching vision of developing a protected, resilient, and functional working landscape.

acr-ACR259: Homestead Dairy began in 1979 by Floyd and Dan Houin with 110 cows. The dairy grew over time and by 2004 the herd was increased to approximately 1,800 milking cows. As is common practice in the area, manure from the cows were directed to open lagoons where the manure decomposed anaerobically and resulted in large amounts of methane released to the atmosphere. In August 2013 Homestead Dairy completed the construction of two above-ground, complete-mix anaerobic digesters designed to capture and destroy methane in the newly built Homestead Green Energy facility. Methane is currently destroyed in two electric-generator sets or in a backup utility flare.
acr-ACR261: SF6 has been widely used in the magnesium industry for more than 30 years. SF6 is a highly-stable molecule  a major reason why it is such a concern for global warming as it can stay in the atmosphere absorbing solar radiation for 3,200 years. Because of its stability and non-toxicity, the gas is used by magnesium die casters, producers and recyclers to protect the molten metal from reacting with air. Without this protection, molten magnesium will oxidize and form magnesium oxide (MgO) deposits that greatly reduce the quality and strength of the final product. The effective cover gas stabilizes the MgO surface film to form a protective layer that prevents further oxidation. For years, the industry has tried to find alternatives to SF6, which generally gets emitted in the process. US Magnesium has undertaken an effort to convert from SF6 to HFC-134a, itself a greenhouse gas but with a much lower global warming potential.

The rate reduction arises as a result of the adoption of fertilizer Best Management Practices (BMPs) aimed at application of the right fertilizer type at the right time, using the right placement and at the right rate in order to minimize denitrification, leaching and run-off, and volatilization, and thereby increasing fertilizer efficiency. acr-ACR392: The Majestic Meadows Facility digester utilizes manure from Majestic Crossing Dairy in Sheboygan Falls, Wisconsin. The Project consists of one rectangular, in-ground digester, designed by Digested Organics LLC. This system is Digester Organics first fully Integrated Manure Management System (IMMS) that processes 20,000 gallons of manure per day, effectively harvesting energy through biogas generation, concentrating nutrients for more targeted crop use, and reclaiming clean water for farm use and surface water discharge. The system is a modular, scalable, and tunable high-rate anaerobic digester that converts over 90% of the organic matter into biogas with retention times of only 5 days. The digester system has a 100,000-gallon capacity and is operated at mesophilic temperatures. Biogas from the digester is primarily destroyed in a boiler which produces heat to maintain digester temperatures and a backup flare to burn any excess gas.

acr-ACR587: The Anew - North Maine Woods Forestry Project is located on 86,221 acres of Northern Hardwood and Northern Conifer forest in Maines North Woods, an area of more than 10 million acres of timberland, the majority of which is privately owned. The project area has a long history of commercial timber harvesting and the landowner, Tree-Star Timberland, acquired this property as a timberland investment, with the objective of obtaining competitive returns through commercial forest management. Revenues from a carbon project will allow for harvest levels to be reduced meaningfully below the thresholds allowed by the propertys current Forest Management Plan, as carbon payments supplant income that would otherwise be achieved through more intensive commercial timbering. The forest management activities under the carbon project will also foster habitat for rare and threatened species in the area including the Canada Lynx and American Marten.
acr-ACR588: The Anew - Big Six Forestry Project is located on 22,067 acres in the industrial forests of northern Maine. It is owned by Big Six Land and Timber Inc., a for profit company with the intent of generating revenue through a blend of sustainable timber harvesting and maple syrup operations. In recent years, servicing the debt on the propertys mortgage has proven increasingly challenging and the landowners have been forced to consider abandoning the maple syrup operation and adopting a considerably more aggressive commercial harvest strategy across the property in order to generate the requisite revenue. The proceeds associated with the implementation of the carbon project have allowed the owners to avoid the need for near term harvests, other than maple stand improvement thinnings to improve the sugaring operation, and to pursue a management strategy involving zero commercial harvesting for the next several decades.

acr-ACR590: Home to several endangered species, the Anew - Blue Ridge Escarpment Forestry Project protects 5,795 acres of southern hardwood and pine forests in the Blue Ridge mountains of upstate South Carolina. The property is owned by Naturaland Trust, an organization dedicated to protecting the Blue Ridge Region from further development. The properties within their portfolio have historically been managed for a variety of resources, including timber products, and are not subject to any legally binding easements or harvesting constraints. If faced with financial challenges, harvesting would be a lucrative revenue generator to support Naturaland Trusts needs. By providing a continuous source of income for the Trust, the carbon project will provide valuable financial support for the organization, relieving pressures to harvest and ensuring the protection and enhancement of forest stocks on the subject properties for decades to come.
acr-ACR592: The Anew - Doyon Native Community Forest Project is located on 172,737 acres of boreal forest across Alaskas Yukon-Koyukuk and Southeast Fairbanks boroughs, and is the property of Doyon, Ltd, a for-profit corporation owned and managed by Alaska Native shareholders. Forests in the project region have been subject to mining and timbering, which still occur on Doyon lands today. The project supports Doyons mission to be a leading innovator amongst Alaskas Native Corporations and to promote the economic and social well-being of Alaska Natives. Carbon funding will contribute to job opportunities and regional economic growth within the community, investment in sustainability infrastructure (e.g. clean water distribution stations, LEED building construction, restoration of riparian zones), and targeted forest management for cultural use and recreation. acr-ACR981: The Stimson Montana Forest Carbon Project encompasses approximately 115,000 acres of forest land, located in Northwest Montana. The project activity will reduce harvest timber, resulting in an increasing overall stand age, larger trees with greater long-term values, and increasing amount of carbon removal and storage over the project crediting period. Carbon finance will provide revenue to financially support and justify the cost of forest management treatments that create healthier forests more resilient to climate change with reduced risk of insects, disease, and catastrophic wildfire.
acr-ACR982: The Anew - Linkletter Forestry Project is located on about 41,000 acres across 5 counties in central Maine and owned by two family businesses, Linkletter Timberlands LLC and Linkletter & Sons. This land was acquired over the past 30 years, and the ownership has expanded over time as the familys investments in the forest products industry has generated profit. By enrolling this land in a carbon project, the landowners will commit the project area to a management strategy that generates income from carbon credit generation in lieu of commercial timber products.
acr-ACR983: The Shamrock Ranch Sustainable Forestry Project encompasses a total area of 17,050 acres (with forest cover of 13,626 acres), with approximately 80% of the land consisting of forested areas. This project is situated in Mendocino County, Northern California. The property predominately includes Madrone, Black Oak and Oregon White Oak with some mix of Douglas fir, Coastal Oak Woodland, Blue Oak Woodland and Montane Chaparral. The Shamrock Ranch is home to a large, trophy caliber population of the rare Tule Elk, as well as abundant trophy class blacktail deer, large flocks of wild turkeys and great numbers of wild Russian boar. The mission at the ranch is to find a harmonious balance between conservation efforts and business development by making the cash flow break even.
acr-ACR984: The Anew - Eau Claire County Forestry Project is located on 48,547 acres of northern hardwood, aspen, and oak forest in central Wisconsin. The County has practiced intensive commercial timber management across its ownership since 1933 with timbering revenues representing one of the largest sources of annual income for the County. Challenged by funding issues from increasing demand for services and rising operational costs, the County has considered further increasing harvesting to fill the budget gap. Revenue generated from a carbon project will help alleviate these financial pressures and accelerate Eau Claire County toward their goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2050.
acr-ACR988: The Anew - Sawyer County Forestry Project is located on a mixture of northern hardwood, aspen, and conifer forestlands across 105,445 acres. The values and uses of the County Forest have and will continue to contribute significantly to fulfilling many of the regions ecological and socioeconomic needs through uses such as outdoor recreation, hunting, timber harvest, and providing essential wildlife habitat. Escalating operational costs and reduced funding are increasing the reliance on timber harvests to fund County services and demand for forest products remains strong. By cutting less than is currently allowed under their management plan and committing to maintaining forest stocks above current onsite volumes, the project will enhance climate benefits through carbon sequestration as the sale of carbon credits will displace the increased need for additional timber revenues.

car-CAR1009: The Project uses 4 anaerobic digestors (with a combined volume of 20 million gallons) to convert manure from 24,900 dairy cows to methane gas. car-CAR1017: We operate a 70 acre facility in Castleberry Alabama which converts chicken manure and green waste to an organic soil amendment using our proprietary blend of microbes. car-CAR1022: The New Energy One Livestock Project is a centralized digester taking manure from three adjacent dairy farms under common ownership, called Cedar Ridge 1, Cedar Ridge 2, and Cedar Ridge 3 (these dairies, under previous ownership, were known as Rock Creek 1, 2, and 3). The roughly 200-acre set of dairy farms has over 9,000 cows combined, and is located in just outside of Twin Falls, Idaho. car-CAR1033: Sunny Knoll Farms is a 77-acre dairy farm located in Wyoming County, New York and is run as a third generation family farm. The dairy is home to approximately 1,450 milking dairy cows, 150 dry cows, and over 550 heifers housed in three 6-row freestall barns. Manure is scraped from the barn three times daily and gravity flows to the collection pit. Manure and wash water from the milk parlor follows the same path. It has a planned hydraulic retention time of 18 days and is operated at mesophilic temperatures. car-CAR1035: The Scenic View Dairy Methane Reduction Project consists of a digester taking manure from the dairy farm and the swinery across the street called Mushroom Farm. The dairy farm is home to 2,200 milking cows and 1,500 heifers. Mushroom Farm is home to 10,000 swine which also contributes manure to the digester. The biogas control and combustion system was installed and first came online in June 2006. The Project consists of three above-ground, complete mix anaerobic digesters. A flushing system automatically delivers manure and milking center wastewater from the main barns to a manure collection pit. car-CAR1081: Roeslein Alternative Energy of Missouri (RAEM) is converting 14 hog production manure lagoons into Anaerobic Digestion Systems. Each lagoon is connected to 8 barns (with a few exceptions), with each barn holding approximately 1,100 finishing hogs. The project location is in Northwest MO, near Milan, MO. The conversion process entails first placing an impermeable lagoon cover and gas collection system over each lagoon. Each lagoon is approximately 4 acres in size, with 15,000,000 gallons of effluent, mainly a 6-8% solids + water mixture that is the feedstock. Once the lagoons are covered, and in the absence of oxygen, the lagoon will naturally shift to full anaerobic digestion, and produce biogas with the following composition  65% methane, 34.5% CO2, up to 5000 ppm of H2S, and saturated with water at ambient conditions. The project also includes capturing the gas and upgrading the gas to pipeline quality and utilizing as fuel, or flaring to provide up to 100% control.

car-CAR1321: The Remley Family Farm is a 550-acre farm located in Roaring Branch, PA that raises gilts to maturity. They built the first 4,400-head quad barn in 2007 and have since expanded to include a second such barn and a 9,600-head nursery. A below-ground, complete-mix digester system was installed at the beginning of 2018 with the intent to create additional revenue streams for the farm. The 80' digester processes manure from the 8,800 grower gilts as well as thousands of gallons of local, sugar-based food waste to generate biogas for use in an onsite engine generator set. The generator is capable of producing 225 kW. They can also destroy gas in an on-site enclosed flare. Prior to installation of the digester system, manure was stored in deep storage pits below the barns, causing uncontrolled anaerobic breakdown of the manure.

car-CAR1325: El Ejido San Lucas obtuvo su primer autorización para realizar aprovechamiento forestal maderable de sus bosques en 1997. car-CAR1343: The Coastal Headwaters Longleaf Restoration Avoided Conversion Project will initially protect, in conjunction with the associated Improved Forest Management Project, nearly 4,000 acres of forestland from conversion to agriculture and residential development. Going forward, it commits to restoring the Project Area to native longleaf pine ecosystem and timber cultivation, following decades of plantation loblolly pine production. A perpetual conservation easement, which permanently protects and commits the property to longleaf restoration, was transferred to a public agency in late 2018. A global timberland investment management organization, a longtime leader in sustainable forest management, developed and manages the project. It was designed with a consortium of conservation partners to not only maintain important working forests and associated rural employment, but also protect, improve and expand critical local water resources and habitat for species including gopher tortoise.

car-CAR1344: Nuestro proyecto consiste en capturar medio millón de toneladas de CO2 en ciclos de 10 años, mediante la reforestación de 2 millones de árboles de palo de tinte (Haematoxylum campechianum) en 1,000 hectáreas de terrenos degradados. Además de ser nativo de la región, el palo de tinte es una especie de alta densidad y rápido crecimiento, capturando hasta 50 ton CO2 por hectárea por año. El palo de tinte tuvo una importancia mundial en los siglos XVI al XIX, cuando representaba el 40% de la actividad económica de la región. Estamos ubicados en Palizada, Campeche, al suroeste de la Península de Yucatán, en el área de humedales de la Laguna de Términos, una zona muy rica especialmente en especies de aves. Nuestro método de reforestación se basa en un enfoque holístico, con principios de permacultura y agroecología, que permiten al mismo tiempo tener alta productividad, gran captura de carbono y enriquecer el ecosistema. El proyecto incluye más de 300 hectáreas dedicadas a la conservación.

car-CAR1372: The project voluntarily captures and destroys methane from the landfill via a system of gas wells, conveyance piping, and condensate removal equipment, and destroys the gas at either an open flare or an energy generation facility. The wellfield consists of an old cell (Unit 1) that is not eligible for carbon credits since it had prior gas destruction, and two newer cells. Unit 2 is closed and contains 32 vertical wells and 8 horizontal collectors. The Horizonal Expansion (containing multiple cells) is the active fill area and contains 12 vertical wells and 10 horizontal collectors with plans for significant expansion. There are a few collectors on the original Unit 1 which are connected to the gas collection system. Any methane collected from this cell is measured and deducted from the credits claimed by this project. The facility consists of three Caterpillar 3520C Gensets which combust landfill gas to produce up to 4800 kW of electricity that is delivered to the local power grid.

car-CAR1375: El proyecto Carbono Otomí La Florida, se localiza en la región Valle del Mezquital del Estado de Hidalgo, en el municipio de Cardonal y en el ejido La Florida. El proyecto se esta desarrollando en un área con una cobertura principalmente de bosque piñonero (Pinus cembroides), y en menor proporción bosque de encino y matorral desértico rosetófilo. Los dueños forestales son los habitantes de la comunidad denominada La Florida, ubicada en en Cardonal, Hidalgo, esta comunidad esta integrada por una población indígena y originaria de la región, el grupo al que pertenecen es Otomí también conocido como pueblo Hñähñu, los habitantes de La Florida mantienen en uso su lengua originaria. El ejido La Florida realiza un aprovechamiento sustentable de sus recursos forestales, cosecha la semilla del pino piñonero llamada piñón rosa. El proyecto de captura de carbono tiene la directriz de generar beneficios ambientales y económicos que mejoren la calidad de vida de los dueños forestales.

car-CAR1459: CAR1459 is the first project both Listed and Registered under the Soil Enrichment Protocol. The project promotes a range of agricultural management practice changes targeted at increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and reducing net emissions of CO2, CH4, and N2O from farms throughout the continental U.S. Indigo Ag and our partners help farmers to implement climate-smart practices through an integrated system of extension and outreach, modeling, agronomic support, and digital data collection tools. Practice changes target fertilizer use, tillage, crop rotations, cover cropping, and livestock management. Beyond climate benefits, the project will increase farm resilience to weather and climate change, promote diversity of the soil microbiome, and increase rural incomes. This is an aggregated project, with new growers and fields added on a continuous basis. As of 2024 the project includes hundreds of growers managing tens of thousands of fields, covering millions of acres.

car-CAR1465: Pueblos Mancomunados se ubica en la Sierra Norte de Oaxaca y se localiza por sus coordenadas extremas entre 96°07 y 96°49 de Longitud Oeste, y entre 17°36 y 16°59 de Latitud Norte, se encuentra enclavada en el macizo montañoso de la Provincia Geográfica Sierra Madre del Sur, que localmente se conoce como Sierra Norte o Sierra Juárez, la cual se caracteriza por un accidentado relieve. El proyecto de Captura de Carbono Forestal en esta zona busca incentivar el desarrollo de actividades económicas que favorezcan al sector primario con fuertes componentes de mejora social y combate al cambio climático. Con la incorporación de este proyecto y su posterior venta de bonos de carbono se busca servir como vínculo de desarrollo regional en el país dentro de la política forestal, y su vez permite la consolidación de los pequeños productores que pueden acceder a apoyos, mercados y capacitación.

car-CAR1480: Prior to this project, the exhaust from the adipic acid process was directed to a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) unit or a Thermal Reduction Unit (TRU). The SCR destroys NOX to comply with Clean Air Act Title V permit requirements but is ineffective at abating N2O. The TRU destroys both N2O and NOX but is less effective at NOX reduction. To comply with the Title V permit, the SCR was operated historically for a significant portion of the year. Phase I of the project is the installation of an absorption column that will convert NOX to nitric acid via a high-pressure water absorption process. This absorption column will allow the TRU to accept a higher percentage of the flow from the adipic acid plant, resulting in a higher quantity of N2O destroyed. In 2023 Phase II of the project installed a new control device. A second TRU effective at destroying both N2O and NOx was added to provide redundancy and reliability to maintain the highest possible level of N2O destruction.

car-CAR1484: El proyecto se forma por 3 fincas cafetaleras que se ubican en el municipio de Tapachula en el estado de Chiapas, a una altura de entre 1,000 y 1,200 MSNM. La vegetación es de bosque tropical y de pino encino. hasta ahora hay registro de 200 especies de plantas vasculares distribuidas en 120 géneros y 59 familias botánicas. La riqueza de flora y fauna de las fincas es impresionante. Las áreas de actividad de este proyecto se encuentran en los linderos de las propiedades, se conforman básicamente de bosque tropical perennifolio cuya conservación se ve amenazada por la presión de las fincas cafetaleras así como de la expansión de parcelas agrícolas de las comunidades vecinas. También se registra tala clandestina. Para este proyecto estamos considerando 120 has de áreas de actividad de restauración para propiciar el cuidado del ecosistema así como la conservación e incremento de los acervos de carbono.

car-CAR1488: Offset Project Description: The Rosendale Anaerobic Digester Project is an above ground complete mix digester system with four digestion vessels built to capture biogas produced from dairy manure at the Rosendale Dairy. Prior to construction of the digesters, the manure was stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon at the farm. When originally built the biogas produced by the two original digesters was captured then used to generate electricity through an engine generator set (genset). Excess biogas that the genset did not use was combusted in a flare. In 2019, two additional digesters were added and the engine was replaced by a biogas clean up and compression system installed to generate renewable natural gas (RNG). A thermal oxidizer (TOX) was installed to combust off-spec gas and a candlestick flare was also installed to combust gas not processed by the RNG system.

car-CAR1505: El Proyecto forestal de carbono del Ejido Pioneros de Río Xhon - Ha tiene un área de proyecto de 7535.88 ha de extensión y un área de actividad de 969.06 ha, la actividad a desarrollar es Restauración. El ejido se ubica en el municipio de Calakmul, Campeche, limitando al sur con Belice y Guatemala. Los tipos de vegetación presentes en el área del proyecto son selva mediana subperennifolia y selva baja espinosa subperennifolia, así como pastizales cultivados. El ejido tiene un ordenamiento territorial comunitario, y tomado acuerdos para delimitar áreas forestales permanentes, en las cuáles se desarrolla un estudio para incorporar estas áreas al aprovechamiento de materias primas maderables. Actividades económicas como la agricultura y la ganadería representan fuertes presiones sobre los recursos forestales del ejido y el proyecto forestal de carbono se ha diseñado como una medida efectiva para disminuir esas presiones.

car-CAR1506: El Ejido Lázaro Cárdenas Número 2 se localiza en el municipio de Calakmul, Campeche, México; muy cerca de la frontera con Belice y Guatemala. La extensión del área de proyecto es de 3740.77 ha, y tiene un área de actividad de Reforestación de 331.13 ha. Los tipos de vegetación en el área del proyecto son: de selva mediana subperennifolia con formas de vida arbórea, y selva mediana con vegetación arbustiva degradada (acahuales), así como zonas de potreros (principalmente pastizales abandonados). El ejido cuenta con un ordenamiento territorial comunitario y está en proceso de obtener una autorización para el aprovechamiento de materias primas maderables. Actividades económicas como la ganadería extensiva generan una fuerte presión sobre los recursos forestales del ejido, los cuáles son abundantes en especies de flora y fauna. Se considera que el proyecto forestal de carbono ayudará a disminuir esas presiones y a generar beneficios sociales, económicos y ambientales en el ejido.

car-CAR1555: The Brimex Energy project consists of the installation of a new biodigester for the management of pig manure to reduce harmful greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through methane recovery and displacement of carbon intensive grid electricity with renewable biogas energy. The power plant is expected to generate a net amount of 280 kWh of renewable electricity which will be delivered to the national grid. The project activity includes upgraded infrastructure at the farm site including the installation of concrete manure tanks to ensure manure is captured effectively and transport to the biogas power plant site is facilitated and the installation of a solar thermal system, which consists of 40 linear parabolic solar concentrators (Power Trough 110 type) that can provide the biodigester an average temperature of 40 °C through a heat transfer process. In addition, a flare for burning excess biogas and a complementary oxidation lagoon were also installed.

car-CAR1582: The Alliance Dairy Project is a dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon and in long-term solids storage under aerobic conditions prior to project implementation. car-CAR1600: El Ejido Ing. Eugenio Echeverría Castellot No. 2 cuenta con una extensión territorial de 2,564.14 hectáreas, fue fundado hace 30 años cuando llegaron los primeros pobladores, atraídos por la posibilidad de obtener ingresos por la extracción del chicle. Fue renombrado como Ing. Eugenio Echeverría Castellot No. 2, porque durante del período de gobierno de este, se logró la asignación del terreno urbano al ejido. El ejido está formado por 25 ejidatarios, 30 pobladores (aquellos que no han pedido ser integrados como ejidatarios). Su extensión territorial está cubierto principalmente con selva mediana Subperennifolia, que es la vegetación dominante de la región, este tipo de vegetación se desarrolla en suelos rocosos, con pendientes y en hondonadas (Flores, 1974), los árboles dominantes no sobrepasan los 25 metros de altura y solo del 25 al 50% de estos pierden las hojas durante la sequía. Destacan como especies dominantes las siguientes: caoba, ramón, Tzalam, chaca rojo, cedro y yaxnik.
